reviews.comment: Prof is pretty good, I liked his teaching style and he explained things very well. He knows where student struggle and makes sure to cover such topics thoroughly. The exams and hw are very reasonable too

Lectures maybe a bit long at times but if you follow through it is very simple. Since this class rely a lot on consulting to empirically found curves and graphs, and his lecture slides have clear pipeline on how to approach a problem, the exams are very straightforward. Also his homeworks are CONSIDERABLY harder than exam which is super helpful.

Chowdhury has his flaws, but is definitely one of the best  I have had. He is organized and focuses on simple design ideas. If you do the homeworks by yourself you will do well. I recommend him for EMD.
Awesome machine learning class. Had lots of fun doing the project. Take if it's your first entry into machine learning.

Professor was okay, nothing really stood out to me. The exams felt really long and hard to finish, but he does grade pretty leniently. The course overall was tough for me, and I think the material could've been organized better.

Good professor overall. The class was pretty large and there weren't attendance or quiz points, so your grade mainly depends on the exams. He covered a lot of material in a short time, and most of it was explained clearly. You just have to keep up on your own since everything moves fast.
Does not explain material well at all.

I took three classes with Prof. Chowdhury, and he's awesome. He explains stuff in a way that makes sense and keeps things interesting. Each class felt totally different, so it never got boring. Honestly, one of the best professors I've had.

Great professor! Super understanding and supportive, especially during a summer course when things are rushed. His lecture videos were short, clear, and straight to the point, which made the material easy to follow without feeling overwhelming. Very organized and really cares about his student's success.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His lectures can feel like a marathon,long and kinda boring at times. But by the end you realize he's actually managed to drill the stuff into your head. Lots of homework and tests.
Amazing professor. Keeps things organized and gives good feedback. Highly recommend him for EMD.

Dr. Chowdhury is a really good professor. He gets how students think, which makes his class way easier to follow. The way he organizes stuff and keeps a good pace during lectures is super helpful. Plus, he does a ton of example problems in class, which makes it way easier to understand everything. Exams are open book and notes and pretty fair.
What I liked about Chowdhury's class is that he breaks things down in a way that actually makes sense. EMD is tough, but he makes it easier to understand.
Knowledgeable and very understanding professor.

This class is kinda intense. The homework and exams are super long. Dr. Chowdhury's a solid lecturer though. He keeps things pretty organized and uploads notes and practice tests, which helps. Just be ready to grind.

EMD is definitely a demanding course, but having Chowdury as your professor makes a big difference. He explains concepts really well and it's clear he wants students to succeed. The homework can be long and tough, and the course overall isn't easy—but if you stay on top of lectures and do practice problems for exams, you'll definitely do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Excellent professor. He is good at explaining concepts simply. His machine learning class introduces lots of concepts very quickly so sometimes can be tough to follow but he understands this and pretty generous with extensions. He wants students to understand the concepts rather than focus on coding too much. Highly recommended for first ML class.

It is a new class for learning ML and then doing an individual project. The professor keeps the class interesting and engaging. It was his first time teaching it and he did a good job. He know the students by name & gave useful feedback to everyone. Homework and tests are easy. set up Python and you are good for the semester. Will take again.

Pretty tough material with exams being the bulk of the grade. Luckily, exams are graded pretty generously. Homework eats a lot of time but relevant to exams. The class was very interesting! Professor is nice and engaging.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: NIce guy. Go to office hours, he helps you a lot. Tests are tough but fair. Homeworks are really long but he helps. Though the grading can be a bit inconsistent. Recommended for design classes like EMD.
Definitely recommend taking Chowdhury for EMD, his lectures are clear and understandable and he offers videos if you can't make it to class. Exams are easy if you do the homework.
Really enjoyed taking EMD with Professor Chowdhury, he was pretty lenient on Exam Grading, he's definitely my favorite professor at RPI
Decent.
Would recommend for elements of mechanical design and similar courses. Recieves feedback and is always looking to improve lectures. Exams are thorough but open note and very reasonable.
Very caring. Forgiving grading but difficult material.

This is a horribly designed course, but Professor Milanova was very kind and supportive. There have been multiple times when she stayed later than she was supposed to during Office Hours because she was helping us, so I really appreciated that. The homework is challenging, but she gives hints on Submitty, and will help more if you go in person
Class is very hard

Her lectures are theory-heavy. Getting help was at times difficult, mostly due to busy office hours. I ended up needing a tutor, which helped a lot. She was also nice and was willing to give me guidance on assignments even after office hours were completed. I would recommend taking Programming Languages with her.
Very nice and accommodating professor. Class is tough but she is there to help along with the other TAs.

Professor Milanova is truly one of the most infuriating professors I've had in recent years, her teaching style for a coding-based class is nearly entirely theoretical. Problems in the homeworks and exams are sometimes obscure or haven't even been taught yet. She refuses to take any responsibility for the performance of the class.

Idk if it's a problem with the contents she teaches or just her lecture is bad, but overall, progLang with her is the worst class I've ever taken. She releases hws even before enough materials are covered in the lectures and she easily gets stressed when students attempt to argue over her ridiculous hw policy. I wouldn't recommend her.
I took her for MBE. She was super helpful and really wanted you to learn the material. She will help any student at any time and had great lectures
She is soooo amazing. She will go above and beyond to help you understand the material. Make sure to show up to class because she goes over a lot of the material that helps you in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Most of the time, profs are just lecturers and dont focus on their making sure their students are actually learning. Ive taken 3 courses with Milanova during my time at RPI. She is this rare breed who actually cares. If you go to talk with her and ask questions, she will do everything in her power help you succeed. Every prof should strive to be.

Milanova teaches fairly advanced courses dealing with language theory/compilers/etc. The topics tend to be pretty dense and tough, but she knows the subject area incredibly well and is very helpful overall. If you care at all about the subject area, it's pretty hard to not do well in her class(es), although she doesn't offer courses often.

Explanations are usually unclear and not helpful. Lectures were stiff and super boring. Read straight from lengthy PowerPoint presentations. She used LMS Discussion Board instead of Piazza. So of course rarely did people actually use it for questions. Therefore she constantly complained of people sending her emails instead. Find a different prof.

Not helpful. The lectures are boring, slides are unclear, and the worst thing is she never gives us clear solutions to any tests, quizzes, or homework. And if you email her questions she won't reply. Uhhh.
I thought she was a great professor. It's a hard class but if you make the effort, she will help you in any way she can.

Milanova's ok. I usually didn't go to lecture and the lectures didn't seem very helpful (just reading from slides) but the curriculum was pretty straight-forward and well-managed. The course pretty much sticks to the book. Projects are helpful and interesting. Exams are pretty easy but homeworks can be tough.
Very difficult subject matter made more difficult by a professor who teaches off of poorly written, unhelpful powerpoints.

She tries her best, but gets overwhelmed and loses track of what she's doing really easily.  Grading and difficulty varies wildly.  On the bright side, she has a hilarious/adorable accent.  Bring a hip flask to class and take a swig every time she tries to say "push" and it comes out as "poosh".

Not a terribly good teacher.  Tends to teach off of slides, doesn't really stray much from them.  Not really any point in going to class (assuming you can read).  Also, not terribly helpful.  Posts replies such as "Sorry, I don't have time to write all of these down."  in response to requests for answers to the review questions for the final.
Pretty difficult subject matter, with very little clarification from either the text or the professor. I would look for someone else.
Hard to understand.  Tests and assignments can be hard.  Although she makes up for all of that by being a very easy grader.
No Comments

Milanova is new to teaching and it still shows unfortunately. She's not a bad person, but she's very shy and it shows when she's giving lectures. Plus she uses PowerPoint presentations which are upwards of 70 slides. So attention drifts off quickly. Not a horrendous class, but not a good one either.
She is very unclear and difficult to follow during lecture.  Her exams are difficult.  It would be better to take a section of this class that Milanova does not teach.

I have him for inventors studio.. He repeats himself several times over and talks slowly so most of class time is wasted. He doesn't allow phone or computers open during class so the 1-3 in class studio works cannot be completed. He assigns work through the lecture slides so have fun finding what you have to do! Many assignments are given verbally
Very caring professor.  Lot of homework but, isn't difficult at all.  Highly recommend.

Inventor Studio 2 was supposed to be my capstone course. What I got was a poorly organized, low effort, catastrophe that neither taught me new material nor offered me any meaningful chance for growth. Don't expect any of the typical online etiquette you normally get either. By far the most infuriating and disappointing experience I had at RPI.

I don't think any of my assignments were actually read or graded. I just got 95's on everything. IS2 with PD3 has a lot of work. It's not hard work but there is a ton of it. I hated the class because we were not graded on effort.

Inventor's Studio is much better than IED, Ghosh is the man! The minimum grade you can get as long as you complete all the work is a B+. Almost everyone in my semester got an A. He's very experienced with innovation & product design and will give you lots of feedback on considerations you might have missed to help with your projects.

I loved Inventor's Studio 1 with Dr. Ghosh. This is a way better alternative than taking IED by far. The class is very open and creative, motivating you to innovate your own invention and experimenting with it. Lots of group projects and participation in class activities. Easy A if you submit all of your work, & no final exam, just a final project!

Extremely easy class! Weekly readings, group presentation, research paper. Participation matters and is worth 20% of your grade. She's extremely kind and willing to extend deadlines. If you have to take PDII take it with her! I finished all my work (presentation and research paper) by end of October so the rest of the semester I was free.

Professor Hoffman is very enthusiastic and clearly outlines the course. If you show up every day, participate some in class, do all the readings beforehand, and turn in your projects on time, it's pretty easy. She is fairly forgiving with deadlines, and if you start early the work isn't very much.
This teacher was great for the 2-credit PD-Tech course and very manageable and understanding with late work.

PD-TECH2 is such a good class. Professor Hoffman's enthusiasm makes the class even more interesting. She's the best professor I've had. The class goes at an excellent pace. You should definitely take this class.

Dr. Hoffman always had engaging lectures, and I never felt like the coursework was stressful. Getting a decent grade is easy so long as you show up and participate in class. Weekly readings, a group presentation, and a final paper, all of which are graded extremely leniently. Altogether a great professor who teaches the content of PD2 well.

She's literally so nice. Took PD2 with her as a graduation requirement, but had to change majors mid semester. Stayed in the class despite not needing it anymore because it was so fun. She genuinely makes it interesting while not overwhelming you with work. If you wanna take PD2, take it with her.
One of the best professor. Her STSO4100 workload is very appropriate. The professor is also very patient. She gives very fair grade.
She was so nice and understanding when it came to late assignments. She wants you to do well as much as you want yourself to do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I just took with Hoffman this class in the first 6 weeks of the summer semester. She assigns weekly reading assignments and you have one group presentation in the end. Her class was easy if you do the work and participate in class. Overall this class made me think more as an ethical engineer.
PDII wit Hoffman is awesome, she is super nice and very straight forward. If you do what she asks you will get an A no problem. Definitely recommend.

Information was interesting. Lectures were dry. No attendance required. 2 exams consist of 50 MC questions which accounts for your total grade. Questions are clear. Some questions asked aren't in power point slides but said in class. Need to study only a few hours before each exam. Offers optional paper to get 10 points extra credit. She's nice :-)
Tries to keep lectures short. Allows students to come to class if they choose. Posts lectures to LMS. Provides study guides for 2 exams. Offers extra credit paper

PD2 with Hoffman is very easy. No presentations, one easy 2-3 page paper, two exams that can be tricky if you don't study the lecture slides carefully enough, but she give you study guides for each of them. If you don't have an A yet, go to the extra credit session at the end and bump your grade up for no real work. Interesting class though!

I really do think he cares about his students learning, but the lectures are way too notation heavy and the exams are some of the most difficult I have ever taken at RPI. A lot of self-learning is required

Being smart and being a good teacher aren't always the same. Amiri makes some effort to connect with students, but he is meant to teach grad students. He is too smart to teach such an important undergrad class. I really think he cares, he encourages questions and gets excited when they are asked, but I think he should stick to grads and research
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He explains the relevance of the math concepts to machine learning & does examples, but he should make his slides less notation-heavy. Grading in his class is very reasonable. Conceptual understanding is enough. Very open to feedback and appreciates people participating. You have to self-learn some, but he does his best.
Do not take this class

Class slides are abhorent as the material is delivered in a graduate-level research style for what should be a sophomore class. Lectures are formatted poorly with random pop quizzes and no structure. He creates irrelevant homework with AI that's more difficult than the exams. You are better off taking an actual math class.

Trying to follow along during lectures is a nightmare. His explanations along with his notes are unhelpful at best, as everything is exclusively written with utmost mathematical formality and notation, making it incredibly difficult to understand being new to this material. I'd say more but there's a word cap. RPI needs to reevaluate this course.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Amiri knows the material well but he has no business teaching a class. He reads straight off the slides, taken straight from the textbook, gives extremely difficult homework that is worse than exams and never goes over them, pop quizzes that you're sure to fail, and never explains the dense mathematical formula the course requires. Never take.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: The most awful professor!! He graded too low in ML Seminar course. I would never recommend taking his course!!

Amiri needs more practice teaching before conducting a class again. He seems like a smart guy with a ton of research experience, but he has difficulty translating his experience into meaningful lectures. Exam 1 and the final were also incredibly difficult.

He needs to do a revamp of the course before teaching it again. He also needs more TAs.
Get ready to hate yourself after a semester of class with him. Wish I could go back in time and taken anything else

Amiri has a teaching problem, that is he cannot teach at all. His ability to lecture solely depends on if you understand the concept the first time he explains it. His teaching methods are incredibly notation-heavy, but he will never post his notes (so be ready to write down everything). No prep content for exams either. Just use the textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor does not know how to teach a math class. The entire course is straight from the textbook and he doesn't bother going over practice problems in class. He incentivizes going to office hours but is only available once a week for 1 hour.  DO NOT TAKE THIS COURSE. Even Lin is better.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Absolute worst professor in the history of RPI professors. After the final, I walked through the hood in the middle of the road and unfortunately did not get hit. Cant put into words how horrible this class is, makes a math lover hate math.

Design pop quiz that force people come to his terrible as hell lecture, copy and paste stuff from textbook, this dude just keep reading stuff on the textbook, no practice problems that help student learn for the class and does not know how to design a fair test. Definitely one of the worst professor I've ever experienced. Avoid his class ASAP
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor doesn't even know what he's teaching and is very rude when answering student's questions and concerns. Lectures are straight from the textbook and content learned in class doesn't even correspond to homework and test questions. Attendance is not mandatory but pop quizzes are given out randomly.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: I like him, but I have issues with how the course is organized. Solutions are not posted for both assignments and quizzes, and grading feels wildly inconsistent between homework's. It's difficult to learn from what you did wrong, and while he incentivizes office hours as means to do that, not everyone is able to make the time.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Professor Amiri is the worst at RPI. He refuses to give homework or quiz solutions and insists you attend office hours (Friday 4-5pm w/him). His lectures make putting a fork in your eyes seem and sound more enjoyable. Exam 1 was supposed to be "easier than the hw" and was truly a nightmare. Class made up 80% of quizzes and exams.  AVOID.

Terrible experience. Unorganized class and slides are pulled straight the textbook. Doesn't provide any useful course materials such as homework answer keys or practice problems. Lectures are monotone and full of notation that he doesn't bother to explain beforehand. In-class "examples" don't use actual numbers and homework is way too long.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The course was not organized. Overall, it was a very bad experience.

Do not take this class with Amiri if you can help it. Lectures go way too fast and have very few examples. Be prepared to learn from the slides and textbook. I only passed this class because I had already taken linear algebra.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: needs to learn how to teach before teaching important courses

Professor Mohammad goes too fast during his lectures, and when he asks students if they know what he's talking about, no one says yes, and he still continues. The homeworks are way too lengthy and are more complicated than his lectures. His lectures cover mostly proofs, and he rarely gave any in-depth examples.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Class easy, but honestly the TA was better at teaching than the prof. Any time we asked TA, they would thoughtfully answer our question and clear up confusion quickly. The Prof just told us to look at the PDF again, as if we hadn't all already tried that. Thank god this was a lab class, I pity anyone who has him for EMD or other lecture classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is a truly fantastic lecturer, but if you have a question he will answer about 15 other things that are not what you were confused about.
He was Okay just very boring
Cant understand him, gives no feedback on grading, acts as though this class is more important than the others (nothing about the class is important)

Prof Shahsavari was pretty accessible during the MSL in-class lab but whenever my team asked a question, he often responded pretty vaguely and didn't really help identify the problem. However, he kept the class timely and we always finished on time.
He never responded to any of my emails and when I went to ask for help he had me rewatch all the lecture videos and didn't even answer my question.
Great teacher, The Mechanics 1-2 Pilot course is great. While attendance isn't mandatory you should show up to learn properly.

I had him as a professor for Strengths, EMD, &IFE. He really cares about teaching the material and puts a lot of effort into the notes he makes. They are color-coded and wonderfully organized so you have great material outside of class to review. He makes an effort to thoroughly answer questions that students ask in class and outside. Recommend.

One of the best engineering professors at RPI.  Very professional and does not waste time.  He's very clearly aware of the average student's understanding, so he doesn't make the content any harder that it has to be.  Lectures are very well-prepared.  Everything he shows in class is posted on LMS, so you don't really have to take notes in class.
Exams were open textbook so a physical copy of the textbook is necessary. Lectures were great and informative.
Shahsavari does really care about students. The course is difficult though, no matter who teaches. I'd recommend both Shahsavari and the course.

IEA is hard. Youtube helps but the prof really matters. So much better than Korolov he actually goes through each step and makes sure you know how to do a problem before throwing an ICA at you. Attendance is mandatory for ICAs but you can find them all online. Lots of homework but its the same for everyone. He actually cares.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Shahsivari is a caring professor. If needed, he will give you extra time on assignments, but is still strict when it comes to deadlines: late work is always a zero. The homework can some times be heavy, but it does prepare you for exams, with many exam questions coming from homework. It's easy to do well on exams but mess up homework grades.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Uses the full lecture time. Every single minute. Strengths is a pretty hard class he did his best to make the material understandable. A lot of opportunities to save your grade if you do poorly on the exams. He always tries to answer questions.

This was the third class I've had with Shahsavari. He is a good teacher for the mechanical engineering courses but should stay away from the Aero courses. This course was quite difficult and I don't think he personally knew what was going on because the whole course followed Professor Rusak's structure from the previous year. Computer projects hard
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Will go out of his way to help you understand the topics and help you with the projects. Great professor, albeit dry. Make sure to study for the tests and use backtests and you'll be fine if you take him

Great professor, had him for Strengths then Aerospace Structures, and now Aeroelasticity. Get ready to do LOTS of MATLAB coding in HWs and two computational projects that had extra credit if you didn't do well on the exams. Exams are open laptop/book/notes. Really helpful in office hrs! Try to start work early, office gets packed near deadlines.

If you're not following the class I strongly recommend dropping the class early because the professor does not help failing students. I was sick for weeks and tried to catch up but the professor had a severe attitude problem. All he could say was "I covered this in class". Also, I was in his office hour and he consistently asked me if I was done.

Very boring lectures. This professor was not good at conveying material, only went to class because of in-class assignments. I learned everything better by watching videos online on my own. He also never ended early, but would instead spend the entire two hours going over two example problems that could have  been done in 30 mins. Do not recommend.

His lectures take FOREVER, but it's worth it. He goes through everything step by step, and while it is tedious, you will learn. He puts in extra hours if he thinks it's necessary and is available for office hours.

The tests are curved generously. Say the avg. is a 65% with a std of 15, then a score of 80% will get you an A. He does problems in lecture, there's no textbook, and the homework is procedural most of the time. Sometimes a specific homework problem can be challenging, but he's approachable for help.

Second time having Prof. Shahsavari. Lecture notes are useful but it is boring to watch him write everything out in class. Tests are difficult but everything was given a generous curve. He is concerned with student performance and encourages people to come to office hours, which I have found more useful than class itself.

Not particularly exciting, but he describes the material well if you can focus. He gives online homework you have to pay for, but it's helpful and you have unlimited attempts. The tests are difficult but not unexpected. He definitely cares about everyone. He's probably one of the better/best strengths prof. I'll take more classes with him if I can.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: I took Shahsavari for engineering dynamics.  The lectures are not mandatory, however the tests pull from the in class examples along with the optional homework.  If you do the examples in class along with the homework as well, you will get A's on the tests.  If you go to office hours and get to know him, he is helpful in more ways than one.

Strength of Materials is a tough class. Examples he presents are helpful studying for tests and doing hw. Has slight accent but doesn't adversely affect presentation. Very willing to help during office hours and is concerned with each student's performance. Would recommend.

Intro to Engineering is an easy class if you show up to lecture and pay even somewhat attention. He is pretty clear in explaining things, though FYI he does have an accent. Do the back tests and you'll be fine.

Very accessible in office hours and patient with answering questions. The class is a little chaotic with a bunch of mini assignments prior to the labs and exams ("quizzes"), but it's not too bad since the exams are open notes and the basic labs have good instructions.

Nice guy, he's on the younger side so he can relate to his students. Most of your time inside/out of class will be dedicated to lab assignments, but there's a lot of smaller things that factor into your grade. He teaches the basics of ECSE well and if you need something reclarified, he's more than happy to help. Easy to get an A with him in here.

Dr. Patterson is a friendly and helpful professor. However, I feel like he could've been more lenient with extensions. Also, the course felt very hands off. Image processing specifically was the hardest unit. Additionally, some assignments were busywork and a few quiz questions were obscure. Just don't wait till last minute and you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Patterson's a great professor. The class is kind of chaotic and about to go through its millionth redesign, but whenever I need help he's extremely accessible and considerate. Hopefully you have coding experience because you'll need it.
Lab heavy. Make sure you know how to save as a pdf.

knowledgeable person. Understands content. Very good at helping you, even if he doesn't fully understand your problem. Answers your questions with dignity: sees eye to eye with you on your problem. Doesn't get the five because submitting assignments suck. It all has to be PDF, and Gradescope sucks, and Gradescope doesn't perfectly match handouts.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Super nice guy, keeps lectures brief so you get what you need. Keeps it lab heavy so you learn the hands on work but if you ever got lost or confused, he is always willing to help. Can go to office hours for anything, even projects for a club you might need help with. No final, only 5 concept quizzes which are easy if you've been doing your work.

Great lectures, great energy, and amazing person. Although the labs are kinda difficult sometimes, it would be much better if you got a team that actually did their work unlike mine. Suggestions are taken into account, and the tests are not too difficult if you pay attention during lecture.

Not the most engaging lecturer, but a solid professor overall. He clearly cares about students' learning, and gives plenty of opportunities for feedback and improvement. The way he teaches the course (Intro to ECSE) achieves its intended purpose well.
He knows his stuff and always so kind and helpful!
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Patterson is one of the most caring professors in RPI. He goes to lengths to make sure you're learning and make sure the class is forgiving. He makes topics interesting as well through projects. Overall just an awesome guy

Patterson is a good professor, lectures are engaging and on-topic. Patterson talks about ECSE career planning, which was useful for understanding the breadth of ECSE applications. Pick good group members & do omega labs, they are a lot of fun and the second/third ones are graded nicely if you put in the effort. Course is simple and useful.

Overall, Prof. Patterson was great. The class was a lot of work outside with the labs, however doing the labs and attending lectures prepares you well for exams. Also, optimizations on the labs and proof of skills allow for you to raise your grade if you make mistakes and slack off during the semester.

Lectures are optional last I checked, the course is a lot of work outside class but a very solid foundation.
While the course has really too much to grade for the TAs, he really cares about his students and wants the course to be graded fairly.

Professor Patterson was a very knowledgeable and enjoyable professor. I learned a lot throughout the class and it further solidified my love for EE and circuits. Labs are very easy to understand and the option to opt-out of the final was very nice.

Professor Patterson is very understanding and friendly. We had forgot to submit a lab, and he was happy to give us an extension to submit it. Material isn't too challenging apart from Proof of Skills at the start of the semester, which was confusing at first.
Professor Patterson is very approachable and wants students to succeed.

Dr. Patterson is a friendly professor who gives clear lectures, however, he cannot structure a course. ECSE 1010 was extremely confusing, in that the first three weeks are wasted with "Proof of Skills" and labs had unclear or nonexistent instructions and confusing "Proof of Concepts" as the reports. This course is frustrating but isn't too hard.

Patterson was a great teacher and was really understanding. I remember I felt overwhelmed by all the Intro to ECSE work and I emailed him and we figured out how I could get back on track. He was also a good grader and helped you understand a concept you might have trouble with. I also asked for additional material to self-study and he gave me it.

Decent lectures, if sometimes rushed. His grading is far too harsh, especially when 80% of the grade is tests, and seems unaware of the overly high stress this causes students. Not very responsive outside of class, leaves questions unanswered or with unsatisfying answers. Not very flexible. Gives poor study material for the tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The lectures are generally decent, although he sometimes rushes, but outside of class he is often unresponsive or redirects questions without providing clear guidance. 80% of the grade comes from tests. Grading criteria aren't always clear, and feedback is minimal. Doesn't give back exams to study either, because he reuses old questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great lecturer, breaks down and explains concepts very well.  For me i found the lectures a bit slow, but i think he wanted to make sure everyone could follow along.  He regularly “quizzed” us in (not for a grade) class which helped us check if we were learning or not
Best lecturer I've ever had in the CS department. I would absolutely recommend taking any class with him if spots are opened.
Nice guy, great at explaining and breaking down concepts.  Go to class and do any quizzes or practice problems he puts on the board.  Listening in lecture will help you immensely on the exams

Best CS professor I've ever had. He is an amazing lecturer, take him if you have the chance, you won't regret it. However, exams were 100% of the final grade, which is quite scary if you are not good at exams, so be cautious if that is you.

Dr. Anshelevich is a phenomenal lecturer. His ability to break down concepts like dynamic programming in an understandable way (and reinforce these concepts on homework) has made this course one of the more valuable ones I've taken. Despite this, I feel that his tests were unfairly weighted, as even a few mistakes could cost you your entire grade.

Great lecturer, you can literally feel his enthusiasm for the subject in every lecture he gives, and is super willing to answer questions or confusions. Personally not a fan of the grading criteria (35% midterm, 45% final, 20% HW), but I cant deny that the exams were very straightforward and reasonable. All in all, he'll make you appreciate algo.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Best CS professor at RPI. Explains very important material as simply as possible, and provides students with the exact amount of resources needed to succeed - not too little, not too much. His grading and tests are very straightforward, and actually verify that you learned stuff (he doesn't focus on the nitty gritty).

A fantastic lecturer, mostly thanks to his visual style of teaching and his knack for walking through example problems. There's a reason Anshie packed the house for every single one of his lectures (very rare for CS). If I could have him for all of my CS classes, I would.

Lectures were awful. I feel bad for the guy: he obviously is deeply passionate but he frequently went on long, irrelevant tangents. It was easier to read the textbook and skip the lectures. Additionally, our grade was determined by 20 questions: 6 questions on test 1, 6 on test 2, and 8 questions on the final. Homework grade did not factor. Brutal.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Fantastic lecturer. Explains concepts clearly and concisely. Always gives problem examples. Straightforward homeworks that don't break the bank. Exams can have some questionable problems, but are mostly fair.
Feels like I learn a lot from him, and am assessed based off of what I've learned.
Amazing professor. Very clear in lecture and you can tell he really loves the material. He's classes are tough but very rewarding.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Anshie is a great professor, and an amazing lecturer. His courses aren't easy, but if you go to lecture and pay attention he's amazing. He has ample office hours, and is always willing to spend extra time to help a student understand. He has different approaches to areas the textbook doesn't explain well to help people learn in different ways.

Anshie was the best lecturer I've taken at RPI. His lectures were incredibly effective and taught me all the material effectively. He's also a genuinely good guy. The class was not easy, but Anshie prepares you well to succeed.

An amazing professor for Algorithms at RPI. Explains tough concepts in an easy way to understand. His office hours are very helpful. One of the best lecturers I've met. Tests were as difficult as the homework given to us, and are fair. Grading is brutal. Would especially recommend to visual learners. Am excited to take his other algorithms course.

Professor Anshelevich is amazing. He is great at explaining difficult and often abstract concepts in easy to grok ways. He is extremely knowledgeable about the course domain and he imparts numerous insights into every lecture. In CSCI 4020, the class was graded heavily on tests with weekly "partner" homeworks from the textbook problems.

Amazing professor. You'll absolutely learn a lot if you follow him closely during class. Be aware that the tests he gave are very hard(at least for me, lol). The average for the first test i took was like 60.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I took Elliot's class for Intro Algo and he was the best lecturer that I've had. It would be a lie to say that his class is easy, but tests are similar to homework and by no means unfair. They test the how well you can apply the algorithms rather than your ability to regurgitate lines of code, which can be hard if you don't understand concepts.

While Elliot is not the worst professor I've ever had, he is certainly among the worst. He does not give back tests, cannot explain concepts for his life, and when you don't get something, he practically makes fun of you. He curved the class heavily, but still, I feel robbed of my education. I could've learned so much more.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: It was an absolute pleasure to attend Anshelevich's lectures. Algorithms is a tough concept to understand and he explained it amazingly. His tests were extremely difficult and I had to work hard for a B-, but the knowledge I attained from this class is priceless. I wish the 5 point rule did not exist, but still I have the utmost respect for Elliot.
There is no partial credit challenging on exams, and the rule that homework where most of the time is spent can not help you by more than 5 points is frustrating.

He is a fantastic lecturer, and really knows his stuff about algorithms. He's one of the few Algo professors I've had who really did a fantastic job explaining new concepts. His homeworks are short, but tests mean a lot. Really prepare for those and you'll do fine.
Does not have Office Hours so any questions must be answered by TAs during lab with 40 others. Also makes tests significantly harder than what is done in class and in homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Be aware that his tests are much harder than back tests.

Amazing Professor. So inspiring and knowledgable. Tests are hard, and if you f-up 1 test you are pretty screwed since it weights so much, but you'll absolutely learn a lot from his lecture. Hope all professors from RPI cs department could learn from this professor about how to actually give a lecture instead of just reading lecture notes.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: The best teacher I met in RPI. Really smart, knowledgable and well prepared for the classes. He explained difficult concepts and algorithms in a way that's very easy to understand.

I always wondered how this guy had such a high rating on RMP despite teaching a non-trivial course. Now I know.  He makes you engage with the material. He won't teach you Algorithms, he will teach you how to think about Algorithms.  Complaints: The grading TA wrote nonsense in his grading comments. The solutions provided for HWs are terrible.

He is a great lecturer and is very clear and easy to understand. I would highly recommend Prof. Anshelevich for any course. He makes conceptually difficult concepts easy to understand ie dynamic programming.

This is literally the best CS course  I have taken. 4020/6210  are the same. The professor is very knowledgeable and well-prepared. The tests and homeworks are very well-designed and not easy. But the effort is worth it.
Great teacher. He's really enthusiastic about the material. He definitely talks fast, so you have to be awake in order to follow what's going on, but that usually isn't a problem.
Wonderful lecturer.
he is a great teacher!

His lectures are very easy to follow, and he does just enough to make sure we are able to follow him. I'm not sure if this was him or his TA, but I was given a plethora of extra credit points on my homework for using LaTeX. If you take this class specifically with him, beware that he likes incorporating tricks into his problem sets.

He is a really nice, awesome person that I  have never ever meet in RPI !!! During his lecture, you are really immersed into the class! Although HW questions are challenging, the questions are very deep and interesting, which makes me feel that doing math is a very interesting thing.

Banks' class was frustrating. Despite attending office hours and studying past tests, I struggled with the material. Things got worse during an open-book test when Banks accused me of plagiarism for using the same format we'd been taught in class. It was unfair and demotivating.
Fair tests and extra credit given on the homeworks

Professor Banks cares for his students and wants his students to do well in his class. His lectures are engaging and he does a great job explaining the material. The class is test-heavy but most of the test questions are very similar to the hw or lecture examples.
Good lecture notes, and homework solutions are posted after they're due. Exams are fair if you put in the work. Goated professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Banks knows how to lecture and knows how to answer a question from a student.
He is one of the best Professors I've ever had in my life.
Very clear lectures and very helpful in office hours. Class uses Matlab and is test heavy; 40% two midterms, 30% final.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: A very good professor. His homeworks are very long.
Great lecturer. Explains concepts very well. First class I've taken at RPI where you have to use your brain and not rely on a crib sheet.

Took this class fall-25 (my first semester). It was great being able to not show up on Friday mornings. There are 4 tests (no final) and 10 ish quizzes which is kinda a lot but overall she's a good lecturer and easy class.
Her lectures are amazing and if you miss class her notes are still easily understandable. She is a very strict grader and fairly uncompromising on any conflicts you may have.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She is very strict and not very lenient for students. Don't ask her to round anything up, for extra credit, or any other help with conflicts with classes. She will just claim that since her class has no final it's more important. It's cause of her strictness is why I did poor in her class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very good lecturer, nice lady, not too hard class. Focuses on making sure everyone is able to perform the math, which is a positive for many people, however if you grasp it quickly then lectures can be slow. Was significantly more a problem in multi for me, matrix it was really helpful how clear she was. Would take again for sure.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class is an exceptionally awful experience if you have a lot going on. Between my job, circuits, and embedded control, the weekly quizzes and FOUR exams for this class are a bombardment. The homework problems are necessary to do well on the very lengthy exams too. No back exams provided, you need to ask around for them. Good lecturer though

Her lecture notes are really good, and the homework's make sure you understand the material. Tests can seem daunting, but there's a lot of clever shortcuts to the problems that reduces the amount of work you have to do.

The homework are easy but time consuming if done in LATEX(4% bonus). The classes were structured as such that everyone would understand and can easily follow. The problem is the exam (24%*3=84%). No resources, no samples, no crib sheet, very lengthy for 75 minute exam.
Good lecturer, gave good advice on solving problems in lectures. No complaints

Very good at going through examples and showing how the math is done. My only complaint is with the course, as it is very theory and definition heavy (as to be expected in a higher level math course). I advise doing the homework (even though it is optional) to get a better hang on recognizing what the problems ask for.

She seems like a very experienced lecturer/teacher, but she isn't very good at providing a conceptual understanding of what certain concepts actually mean.

She's also a strict grader and gives no opportunity for extra credit. A good class should not be based entirely off tests and quizzes, but that's what she did. Her tests are also way too long.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Her exams are kind of unexpectedly difficult, but her lectures are super clear and concise, and have super readable notes. She kinda grades super hard and doesn't make any exceptions for anyone, so I wouldn't recommend taking her classes if you have a lot of stuff going on.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She gives little time for long exams and only grades on that and quizzes. She drops 2 quizzes which is nice, and no final, but 4 exams total. No homework. Use the TA's during recitation to ask questions. They answer better.

Brown is a decent lecturer, her examples and explanations make sense in class, but she goes a bit fast. The grading is a little tough, her tests are extremely hard, was lectures 1-7 but almost 60-65% was only on lecture 7 topics. The exam was ~10 T/F, 1 select all, and 5 written questions with multiple parts, and she only gave 1 hr and 10 min
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: lectures are helpful but you need to take a decent amount time outside of the class to really understand the topics. The final is optional, there were weekly quizzes during recitation and mandatory two exams, one covering all of multivariable calc and the other matrix algebra.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I thought the lecture slides were really helpful along with examples although sometimes she went through big concepts very quickly. You definitely need to take some time on your own to understand the concepts. If you go to class actually pay attention because Brown will call you out if you aren't.

This class was pretty easy if you understand Calc I concepts. The lectures were a bit boring as she went through a lot of examples slowly, but in the long run that was helpful in understanding the material. I thought the tests were challenging but nothing unexpected.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great lecturer and recitation quizzes are fine but for exams she uploads a practice sheet but doesn't post the answer key nor makes it a complete list of what is on exam, I don't like how deceiving that is. Heard from others that she can also be passive-aggressive though I haven't seen that.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Good lectures, and I genuinely feel like I'm coming away understanding the material. Homework says optional in the syllabus. It is not. DO THE HOMEWORK!! The one exam I skipped a few of the homeworks I did poorly on. Grades are all exams/quizzes, which can be rough, but she's fair/generous with partial credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Extremely clear in the expectations of the course. Exams are very fair and taken straight from the homework. Lectures are to the point and she manages to make very difficult topics understandable. I wish all the professors were as good of lecturers as her.

Dr. Brown is amazing!! No idea why she has low ratings. She's very caring, her explanations are thorough and she provides great examples. She prepares you well for tests/quizzes. Hw wasn't mandatory, but I would recommend doing it because it's good practice + she takes quiz problems from it. Highly recommend Dr. Brown

I highly recommend going to lecture and taking notes (at least filling in her notes sheet), the way she explains things is helpful. The exams are easy as long as you did all the homework since the test questions are the same/sometimes easier hw questions. There weren't any study guides/back exams , however redoing the hw problems is sufficient.

She has the best lectures I've ever taken -- so much so that I'm willing to overlook how unfair the tests feel. If you can get excited for the material and truly want to learn: take the class. If you're just in it for the grade or for the grad requirement: it might be worth it to you to find an easier professor for the class.
Great professor. Uses clear notes and language to teach topics.
this teacher takes horrible notes, you basically need to go in-person .
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I think she is a very good professor. The content taught in class is easy to understand. The test results will be curved.(Generally, if you get 4 out of 6 multiple choice or "true or false" questions correct, you will get a perfect score) If you study hard before the test, you will get a good grade.

Good lecturer overall, very clear and concise. Assigns lots of "optional" homework that you are quizzed on during recitation. Exams were very similar to homework, but the time given to complete them makes them challenging (i.e. 20+ problems in 70 minutes). Willing to give partial credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Took Calculus II with Professor Brown. Would not recommend to people who are not proficient in calc. The grading system is different than the other calculus 2 teachers, such as quizzes being worth more, and just a lot more stricter in certain aspects. It's also very rare that students finish their exams, which are worth a lot of your grade

The notes are really clear and helpful, but the course is too test heavy. 70% is based on exams, and the 30% is based on quizzes. TA sometimes only gives 10 minutes to complete 2 very work extensive problems for the quizzes.

Took for Calc 2 but couldn't put it under that category. Her exams are ridiculously long and tough. Half the people don't even finish the exam. Class is very exam heavy, about 75% of your entire grade, wouldn't take her unless you understand calc very well and can do it really fast
Lectures are extremely slow and boring, but necessary to understand content. Would be better served if recorded and watched at x2 speed.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I took multivar and I dropped. Test is difficult only because no crib sheet is allowed (Other professors might allow crib sheet). I can't memorize all formulas so I dropped. But she definitely have the best lecture notes and she post all lecture notes
Great lecturer, and exams are super easy. No quizzes, and the (fully multiple choice) final is only worth 10% of your final grade.

this is a very good course with a clear and helpful professor.  About one-third of the class covers functional analysis and calculus of variations, which are very interesting and include useful physics applications. the exams are not too difficult if you keep up with the material. Overall, a rewarding course that goes beyond standard calculus.

Dr. Kam is just genuinely a lovely person and professor. Super passionate about teaching and wants you to succeed. Strongly emphasizes application of concepts so everything we learn feels rewarding and useful. Weighs your worst exam lower and best exam higher so one bad test doesn't ruin your grade. If you can take a class with Dr. Kam, do it.
Kam is a great professor; her lectures are easy to understand, and the grading is more than fair for her class.
Amazing professor! Content was manageable and she gave lots of extra credit. Would definitely recommend.

Good prof, exams are fair and very similar to hw/practice exams. Lectures arent good, goes very fast and you'll be lost in 5 minutes. Luckily most topics can be self-learned online easily (specifically Pauls Math Notes). Hw is fair and you're given a lot of time for it. You'll get a good grade but prob wont actually learn the material very well
Kam is the goat. Basically just do the hw, and extra credit. She's a great lecturer pretty funny overall and you can tell she cares abt her students. Lovely woman amazing teacher.

Dr. Kam is a nice person. However, this class is very challenging. She didn't curve, but she made the lowest exam scores count less and gave extra credit. However, I do feel that she was a bit hard to follow in lectures and exams were extremely tough. Office hours were really bad and every TA seemed bothered when I came to ask questions.

Absolute GOAT

Straightforward tests and assignments, easy to understand lectures, and is willing to re-explain topics and break down even simple problems during office hours.

Dr. Kam is a very understanding professor. although lectures are hard (it's diff eq, get over it lol), there are many easy assignments to balance out your grade (unlimited tries on hw, group recitations, back exams are almost exactly the real exams). do not be afraid to go to her office hours!! highly recommend dr. Kam. she's so cool.

Decent lectures, but a bit fast and the lecture notes themselves don't help. Don't take her if you don't plan on going to class.
Tests are very fair, just like the practice and easier than the HW. Grade boost from the homework, extra credit on every test, and grade cut off for an A is 90, easy class to do well in if you try/pay attention in class.

Prof. kam moves verry quickly in lecture and explains what she is doing poorly, if you can usually catch on quickly this isn't a problem, but since i am a little slower it means i get left behind and lost.

Absolutely fantastic for diffeq. Very sweet lady and exceedingly knowledgeable, undoubtedly the best professor teaching this class. Makes each class feel like an adventure, and makes sure that everyone is understanding what happens. The only time I felt lost in the class I felt very comfortable asking her after lecture, and she cleared it up fast.

Amazing person who is very caring towards students. While attendance was not mandatory I would 100% tell you to go to class otherwise the concepts become confusing. Overall, a great professor and class.

MATH 2400 is diffeq.
Fantastic lecturer, everything makes sense. 
However, the exams (and the final) were extremely difficult. Strongly recommend taking another professor; all their exams are pulled from homework or quizzes and are much simpler.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Kam is fantastic. She is very knowledgeable and a very kind professor. She always does her best and it really shows. I really liked her explanations, and she would also drop little jokes and stories here and there to make the class more fun. If you have to take DiffEq, I would definitely recommend it with Kam.

Kam's lecture style is very fast and wasn't the best fit for me. She is a great professor nonetheless, but the HW pretty much taught me the class.
There are quizzes at recitation. 
Exams were difficult but weighted so your best one counted more and your worst one least.

Dr. Kam is a very good lecturer but falls short on every other aspect. The quizzes were fine. However, the homework was usually confusing and the exams were extremely difficult. The final was only 10 multiple choice questions with no partial credit. She also refused to curve any grade even though her class avg was lower than every other professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I love Dr. Kam with my whole heart. She's my favorite professor I've had at this school and she's an amazing lecturer. Although the lectures aren't mandatory, I highly highly recommend going to them. Dr. Kam is so funny and really wants you to succeed. I haven't experienced that from anyone else.
Great Professor

Professor Kam is a really good person and a decent teacher, but there were a few things I didn't like. In my opinion, the exam questions (especially the final) had questions that were much harder and had questions that we basically never talked about in class. Also, there was only a crib sheet allowed on the final and tests take forever to grade.

Extremely good at teaching DiffEqs concepts, never felt like I didn't understand something in the class. HW has random difficulty spikes (spent 8 hours on one assignment), but you don't lose credit for wrong answers. Exams have extremely slow grading, but are fair and mostly cover content emphasized on in lecture. Altogether a fantastic professor.

Elizabeth Kam is by far one of the best math professors on campus. Her lectures are very engaging and she posts her notes for you to see after each class (very easy to follow if you didn't attend). She is a very kind and understanding professor and she is always there for you if you need help with something! Loved having her this semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Most of my peers in other schools would say diff eq is awful. Kam made diff eq extremely fun for me. Absolutely the best class I've taken at RPI and the best professor I've had. Fantastic lectures, notes were easy to understand (though attending helps to understand it more). Just do the homework, do some practice, and exams will be a breeze.

kam was the best lecturer in math department, her class was so easy that you can only read the note to understand, because the attendance was not mandatory. The online homework system was stupid, It will waste you lot of time to correct the form of answer. For her class is easy to get A, if you get good grade in exam.

Her TA sucked. His grading was the biggest reason why I probably didn't do as well as I should've, since his feedback was nonexistent. Other than that, Kam is a fantastic professor. She cares, is accessible, and will answer any question no matter how simple. Her tests reflect the lectures, but her notes are somewhat hard to follow once leaving.
An awesome professor and a great lecturer. Do attend the lectures though, her notes can be hard to understand if you try to understand them outside of class for the first time.

Kam as a professor is amazing, and she has great lectures, but honestly, the TA for her sells the class. He grades (takes off points) extremely harshly and gives off random points, and leaves alot of students confused on what they got wrong, for the average RPI student, leniency is much appreciated, but not offered alot in the class. My opinion ofc

Kam is a great lecturer, but definitely go to lecture, she explains the notes in a way that is easy to comprehend. She makes class entertaining and uses the time well. Exams and quizzes are fair, very similar to hw and class examples.

Dr.Kam is not only the kindest woman I've ever met but her class is also the most straight forward math course I've ever taken! Lecture notes are extremely detailed and organized, exam questions are straight from notes, & quizzes were made optional about 1/2 way into the semester. Just watch out for the eigenvalue HW (mastering sucks not her fault)

Good lectures, although sometimes she uses analogies that make things more confusing. Went over time by 5 minutes or so for about half the lectures. Homeworks were really annoying because of the terrible online software, but she agreed to drop one that nobody could get the answer format right on. Offers bonus questions on exams.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Kam does a thorough job of explaining all concepts and methods. She assigns weekly homeworks and quizzes, but they are fairly light and are always directly related to the lecture material. The textbook for this class is really cheep if you wanted to buy it, but she provides the questions for you on blackboard anyways. Overall a great professor.

Dr. Kam is an amazing professor. She posts her notes after every lecture which are crystal clear. Homeworks are done on Pearson, usually 8-10 shorter problems that are due every 2 weeks (plenty of time to do them). Her exams are very straightforward, usually just iterations of past homework/lecture problems. Extra credit is even available on tests!

Dr. Kam is a great lecturer. She has very clear notes and explains every single step of every single example problem. Tests are exactly what she says they will be, and she wants students to do well. Homework isn't excessive and she does not require a textbook. I don't even feel like I need a book because her explanations are great.
Best math professor.
Really clear on grading criteria, easy to learn.
Dr. Kam is super helpful and thorough in teaching. Never assesses on any information not covered in lecture. Also a very generous grader when it comes to grade breakdown.
She's enthusiastic about teaching and really wants you to succeed.

Dr. Kam is easily the best prof you can have for Diff Eq. A lot of fellow students failed Cramer/switched from his section into Kam. She has very thorough notes and always goes back for questions. She also gave me fist bumps before every exam. Ends up lowering the exam percent of lowest exam and raising highest. Drops lowest 2 HW and quiz grades.
Took differential equations with her. Great professor with great lecture notes. Gave bouns questions on every exam. She doesn't want anyone to fail.

Dr. Kam cares if you understand the material, and is accessible outside of class if you need it. She is funny and explains things well. My only critique is that she goes quite fast sometimes and it's hard to keep up when taking notes. However, she posts her notes after class, so you can go back and fix them. Helpful study guides for tests.

Elizabeth Kam is not only my prof for this class but also my advisor and I believe she is one of the greatest professors I have ever had. The amount of joy and excitement she has for teaching is staggering. She is always able to help a student out and has confidence in everyone to succeed. I am very grateful to have her as a professor :D
Professor Kam genuinely tries to make sure all of her students succeed. One of the best professors at RPI.
Overall, she is a good professor. Her teaching skill is okay, but she is approachable after the class. Test is fair. However, you do need to watch out for which TA you are getting.
Lectures are well-organized, exams aren't difficult, and if you've stopped believing in humanity, Dr. Kam will change that.

The best professor! She is very patient to everyone. The lectures are awesome. It is easy for you to get A if you attend every lectures. The notes are good and useful. You will learn knowledge and get good score!

You don't need to show up as long as you look at the examples and do them. For the quizzes, the TA will go over the weekly material. For exam just do the practice problems until you know how to do them by heart and you'll do great.

Kam is probably one of the easiest Math professors to take, attendance is not mandatory (you can look at her notes online), and she is a pretty fun and bubbly person in lecture. Since she's obviously acquired a PhD in Mathematics, some topics she might breeze by too fast because she does the calculations in her head, but an easy A. Do extra credit!
Nice Teacher!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Dr. Kam is truly an awesome professor. Probably one of the best Ive had. She really cares about your education and your wellbeing, both in/out of school. You can tell she actually cares for her students and will do anything to help you understand the topic. Lectures are straightforward & you can print the notes before class go follow along. 10/10

Great, caring professor with lowkey hilarious asides during her lectures which are very helpful. Tests are straight out of the homework and study guide. Quizzes are straight out of the lecture. Great class, would take again.

Dr. Kam is incredibly intelligent and very kind. Her exams are short and sweet and you're never graded unfairly or on anything you didn't study. Her passion for math and teaching is very clear by how much she explains and how willing she is to help anyone that asks for clarification.

Kam is truly a real gem. She cares about all her students and posts all her lecture notes online, whether you want to print them out before and fill them out with her, or print out her filled-out ones after. Her tests are also remarkably less difficult than other professors, but are accurate in determining your understanding - and have Xtra Cred.
Dr. Kam is the real MVP. She's so funny and her lecture notes are very detailed and understandable. Her tests aren't surprising--if you do your homework and show up to lecture, you will do great.

Kam uses an example-based lecture style to drill in techniques for calc II. Quizzes are literally taken from the 5-6 examples done in lecture, and nothing on the exams are ever a surprise (plus bonus questions!). Super approachable, and she makes hilarious comments during class and then wonders why people laugh. 10/10 would take again
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: Had her for Calculus II, and she's nothing short of the ideal professor.  She's supremely qualified to teach the course (took BC Calc prior) and makes the course very manageable and student-friendly, but that's been said already.  She is a person of immense patience and she puts forth 100% every lecture to engage people in the material.  It works.

Professor Kam was one of the best professors that I had. She is very straightforward and I learned so much following along her lectures. Showing up to lectures, taking down notes, making sure you review the examples and optional homeworks will ensure an A. She made Calc II for me very enjoyable and easy.

Had for Microbiology. She's very passionate about the topic and cares about her students. A little difficult to understand at times, but she's a great professor. We were only graded on exams; however, if you come to class, she will tell you what to focus on. As long as you do the study questions she posts, you'll pass with a B or above just fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She strictly sent course information via email, and she would often exclude students from critical emails. She would still expect the excluded students to submit work at a certain time that she only stated in an email, though. The course was also quite unorganized and unbalanced, as she expected sophomores to know as much as the graduate students.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Shes knowledgeable in her field but I don't think she understands that we're still students
She's a very good lecturer and very passionate about what she teaches! I had her for Microbio, and you can see how much she cares about the subject!

I took Microbio with Dr Barquera and it's clear right off the bat how passionate she is for the subject, which really  does help make learning it easier. She's very accessible outside of class too, and encourages you to ask questions whenever you have them. She does stress in-class participation, but it isn't graded. Definitely recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This woman is completely inept! Insists on holding online classes because of the pandemic but has no idea whatsoever how to use zoom to let kids into the class beforehand. I have missed every lecture so far this semester because of this, which is extremely frustrating considering the class is at 8 am. Quite the disappointment.

Microbiology was a really interesting class. Dr. Barquera is quite knowledgeable about this field. She is an enthusiastic teacher and truly cares about her students. Her lectures are not only engaging, but also show current and relevant information. Anyone interested in biology would definitely like this class!
Microbio was a fun and easy class. The fact that Dr. Barquera is very passionate about the subject material showed through in her teaching.
Tests were in broken english and didn't match lecture material

Prof Cutler did not follow written DSS accommodations and was consistently power tripping over controlling my self and others. Reasonable bathroom breaks are explicitly included in the accommodations, yet during a 6-hour (double-time) exam she still denied them. students relying on DSS support should avoid at all costs.

I took this class fall-25 (my first semester). This class is easy as long as you know what you are doing. No attendance is a bonus. Hot take but anyone complaining got weeded out of the weed out class.
her grading criteria is hilarious because its so unclear. her lectures are alright but i feel like a lot of her homeworks are OD.

It was generally a pleasure to be in her class. If you work hard and always stay on top of the homework you should be okay. Also do go to the lectures and pay attention in them. The lectures are somewhat dry but occasionally they can be quite engaging and they are effective at teaching you. This class will teach you whether or not CS is for you.

Gets incredibly triggered when people ask her about grades. I have never seen a professor actively encourage students to retake a class. Course is too hard for 1000 level and 4 credits. TAs take so much time to get questions answered. Can't even use the bathroom in class without missing late day points. Her class made me want to drop out of college

Make sure you have either taken data structures before taking it with this professor or you have an extremely good grasp of the code for each of them, or you do your own side projects in your free time. This should be a prerequisite before even taking the class. If you do not score above the average in the first exam, drop the course.

Either you love her or you hate her. It's a tough class to do well in, and she assigns a lot of work. She knows what she's talking about, but rarely got through her all of lecture slides. Gives hard & sometimes confusing exams, and homework was harder. But if you can get through this weed-out class with a decent grade, you'll be set up for success.

She's a professor who is very knowledgeable and passionate in the field that she teaches. Her homework are indeed long and a bit difficult, but they are all designed to help students practice stuff taught in class and learn vital programming practices. However, her exams are extremely difficult, yet the grading is fair due to clear criteria.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: She is nice enough, but makes her class extremely difficult. You can never have a breather while taking this class, every week there is a huge homework, and a difficult lab. This class made me hate coding.

Dr. Cutler is clearly passionate and dedicated to the field of Graphics, and I respect that. While the work was tough, grading felt fair. However, I felt she favored students who shared her enthusiasm for graphics and her negative views of AI. As someone new to the field, my quieter learning style seemed to be viewed as minimal participation.

She was a great professor if you want to actually improve. Some students sometimes forget pain and gain. Don't underestimate the professor. Start your hw early, make friends, and work hard. If you try hard she will know it. However, her graders are kinda volatile. I had a grader who really hated me for no reason. Anyway, have fun.

Homeworks are very difficult, mine took on average 20 hours across multiple days and dominated my course schedule. Cutler asks students to write code during lecture, you should either participate or write your own solution in parallel, do not play minesweeper during class. Complete all the practice problems & do the extra credit, start HW on Sat.

Data Structures is a hard class, but with Cutler it was way harder. She has premade lecture notes for class which is fine, but we only finished covering the notes in about 3 lectures all semester. The homework assignments also take way too long. The class should be worth more than 4 credits with Cutler for the amount of time you spend in work.

Be prepared to for possibly 20-40 hours of homework per week. Don't start two days before it's due. 
Go to lectures. They help--especially ones before a break. 
Homework 6 will suck. You'll be better from it. 
Find people to study+review with. 
Don't use ChatGPT as a crutch. 
This is meant to be a hard class, but you'll learn a lot. 
Don't worry
A lot of work but definitely worth it. Learning a lot! CUTLERRR IS THE GOATTTTT!!!!!

An infamously difficult class at RPI. Clearly the weeder class for first year CS students. Took it first semester freshman year, had to retake it (first grade disappeared and didn't impact GPA).
Despite being so painful it is a incredible informative and useful course. Cutler is an especially talented and experienced professor.

dr. cutler is probably one of the best teachers in RPI. she has an answer to every question no matter how niche and the structure of the class is well thought out and organized. tests and homeworks are rough but if you go to office hours she will do her best to help you out. i wish i had a lighter load so i can fully focus on her class this sem.

Data structures is, and should be a very hard class. Her homework's, labs, and exams are very challenging, but I promise you that if you take the time to properly go through them you'll learn so much. Perseverance, patience, time management, and hard work are near essential to succeed in this course. You can do this!

Terrible professor.  Wasn't lenient with grades at all - in fact, she would lower your grade if you requested a regrade for your test and she found a mistake she over looked before. Gave more homework than I did for my next three four-credit classes combined. Values only top 1% of students. Would leave RPI than ever take another course with her.

Data Structures with Prof. Cutler was tough because of the workload and difficulty of tests. I think she is just not suited to teach a lecture to 350+ students at a time, which, to be fair, seems very hard. Every time I went to her 1-on-1 she was very helpful and considerate of my issues. I would consider taking a much smaller class with her.

Cutler was a great professor. The course was very challenging but I gained a lot from it. The homework was time-consuming but helped me to learn the material and each of the assignments were interesting. The tests were very difficult, but Cutler was fair in curving the course. I feel well prepared for the upper-level CS courses.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Incredibly incredibly disrespectful in 1-on-1 encounters. Don't expect her to help you. Completely unfair grader. I have never had a professor verbally torment students for asking questions. Absolutely ridiculous and an embarrassment to the CS department.

She was so consistently disrespectful to me. She was uncompromising when I had COVID and didn't want to take a test with 300 other people. I sent her five emails about the next class and she never responded to me (and still hasn't 3 months later). After the add deadline, she wouldn't let me audit. A poor showing for the CS department.
