People hate on her just because her class is hard, but I thought she and the course were both very fair. She is very strict about deadlines and homework, but that probably prepares you pretty well for the real world. The course material itself isn't hard to understand, but the workload is very tough.

She's extremely smart, and knowledgeable, and sprinkles her own personality into lectures. Honestly, the worst thing about her is how cutthroat she can be. It seems like even if you have a life circumstance like illness, she'll expect that homework in on Thursday regardless.

She is very knowledgable around the class material and reflects that through her lectures. Homework takes up 10-12 hours a week and often describe the objective very vaguely. For a few of them she made some emergency changes to the files without clear notice which caused students' code to break on submitty.
Tough class. It had lots of homework and was very fast paced, and that made me a much better computer scientist.

So hard! I don't know if it's this class that's hard or GSAS that's too easy, but it was the hardest class (I would like to rate 6 out of 5 for difficulty). It was not fun at all, but I must admit that I learned a lot.
What can I say? It's that bad
I overheard her at the union talking about how she wanted to make data structures more difficult because there were "too many CS students." Do with that what you will. Hard pass.

Overall, Professor Cutler is a very knowledgeable individual. However, I find that she did a mediocre job of conveying her knowledge and giving lectures. The homework assignments are lengthy — but given good time management and a strong work ethic — are doable. I averaged ~8 hours per assignment. Tests are not too bad if you review back exams.
This class is a lot of work and you have to manage your time well, you should take it during a semester when the rest of your classes are easy. The exams are also really hard.

Professor Cutler does a well enough job teaching a subject which seeks to strike down most Comp. Sci. majors. She knows the subject material very well, and if you ask questions during class, she will answer. Outside of that, it can be hard to get a hold of her.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Doesn't answer critical questions about homework in a timely manner.

She seems nice at first, but she is an extremely difficult professor and enjoys throwing students into the deep end. The weekly homework assigned are often far beyond necessary or reasonable difficulty and often have mistakes. She rarely gives helpful feedback, and rarely follows her own ridiculous grading standards in her provided code.
Seems nice in lecture but is actually *very* rude. Often can be unnecessarily strict on less important parts of the course. Would not recommend this professor to other students.

Assigments are weekly. One lab done in groups, typically around 2 hours, and one large homework assignment every week. The HW is quite long and takes around 10 hours to complete (a couple of times more), however they are very fun and I enjoyed them a lot. The class is very hard and exam grading is very harsh. In two words: enjoyable suffering
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Cutler appears nice on the surface but in all reality cares little for the success of her students.

Hw is weekly and for me took at least 8 hours (usually many more). Cutler assigns interesting and challenging hw problems and by the end of each one you will probably feel exhausted but also a real sense of accomplishment.

She seems nice in lecture but is actually insanely strict. Exam time limits are not ample. Homeworks can be a bit vague and time consuming. Submitty is slightly buggy/slow. The first lecture taught code that exhibits undefined behavior as if it were correct.

Her lectures are boring and little helpful. Her homework are really hard and will take lots of time to complete. Exams are difficult and the time limit is really intense. Also, the professor is unreasonable since I submitted a regrade request and the professor said there is no need for regrading so I got -1 point on that exam.

Well spoken, introduces material in a clear and concise manner. Very accessible and cares about the success of her students. Very well organized, all materials (past and present) are available online for review outside of class.
Weak course objective, though sometimes inspirational. Obscure instructions.

For a student that got an easy 5 on the AP CSA exam, Data Structures was, by far, the hardest computer science course I have ever taken. The homeworks made me cry, the tests made me question myself. And now looking back at my experience, I have gotten the most out of that class than any other. Taking DS with Cutler is painful, but worth it.
One of the hardest freshman courses at RPI, but make it through the course and you'll know what you're doing when it comes to coding.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Really difficult homework
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Tough Data Structures curriculum. From my understanding, she designs the curriculum for all semesters even though she doesn't teach them all. Not sure if this is true. Tests are very orderly to the point where everyone has an assigned seat. Expect weekly homework assignments that take 10+ hours to complete (minimum).
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: If this is not your required courses to graduate. Please don't take it. You can't learn how to do c++ in this course because c++ is the prerequisit not the main course content.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Took this class as an elective when I was initially really interested and ended up hating it.  Lectures are super dull.  Some of the homeworks are actually really interesting but most are completely asinine or just badly realized.   If you're not a CSCI student, you're better off just learning the same material independently.
The material is challenging but there is no exams so the grading is relatively easy
She is the gatekeeper for computer science majors, if you can't do well here, you should consider changing majors
The most important class I've ever taken. You will either learn the most you've ever learned in your life or you will fail.
Cutler's graphics class is the best class I've taken at RPI. she's a fantastic lecturer and her homeworks are really interesting!

Class is extremely hard. Notes online are more useful than lectures. Hws were extremely hard and it would have been easier to take algorithms first. Normally took at least 20 hours on most (not all) hws. Hardest cs class (took it spring 2013). Tests are long and hard. If you do well on a homework that everyone does well on the curve can hurt you.
Worst professor that I've ever had.
It's hard but helpful, and curved at a good amount

Best class I've taken at RPI. It isn't easy, but the hws (while challenging) are not impossible and actually fun. Tests sometimes are a bit long, but possible...if you know the material. Don't worry, the hws shouldn't take you more than 6 hours if you go to lecture...this stuff about them taking 20 hours is just ridiculous.
Avoid her if you can! Incredibly flawed grade curving system.
Avoid if possible.
Homework and tests are too difficult (homeworks take like 10-20 hours and are assigned almost every week). Also, the curve for the final grade CAN hurt you.
she assigns difficult homework and the tests are challenging, but she's fantastic at teaching the material, and grades with the mindset that her exams are SUPPOSED to be hard (she curves them)
The lectures are 'eh,' but the notes she provides are excellent and the homeworks, while lengthy, are extremely well-designed. You'll definitely know your stuff by the end of this class.

Excellent lecturer, knows the material very well and is extremely helpful. Well organized. Homeworks were hard but doable, labs were fun, but knowing the course material wasn't necessarily sufficient for the exams -- expected ability to solve logic problems as well.

Her teaching style is just reading a PDF that she posts before class. She calls on a student to program the examples, which is boring to listen to. Homeworks are brutal and take 10ish hours on average. Labs are easy and tests aren't TOO bad if you know what you are doing and study the sample test.

Extremely helpful and knowledgeable -- The course isn't the easiest and the homeworks take a lot of time (especially if programming isn't your thing), but you get a lot out of the them. Tests cover a lot, but nothing that hasn't been covered in class, and you can bring notes. Lectures are decent, but you can also read the notes online and be fine.
Gives a lot of work, but it really teaches you well.

She's absolutely one of the best teachers I have ever met. Not only because she's very smart, but also because she has high expectations. Her tests for most people are hard, but if you keep up with class work, you'll think they're easy like me. Her homeworks can be very time consuming, but that's with good intentions. In all, I enjoyed her class.

For people who don't go into the class with more experience than CSCI 1100, the class is very difficult. It requires a lot of time catching up on basic principles that are skipped by most professors, resulting in a struggle to understand what is happening at any given time. The key to success in this case is enlisting the help of the TA's

The tests are fairly difficult and this was my most challenging class for my first semester at RPI. Most of the labs were easy but some were pretty tough. There's one homework project per week; they usually take 5-7 hours but on some weeks take 10-15. Lectures are absurdly boring but the exercises done during lecture are very valuable.

Dr. Culter is very nice, especially if you talk with her one on one, but her assignments are long and nasty. Start them early. Warning: homework #6 is always a killer. Don't think because you were a whiz in high school you'll be able to coast through here. You will learn everything well, especially if you come and participate in class.
Her lectures are long and boring, her homeworks are insanely time consuming. I didn't pay attention in lecture, completed all the homeworks and had a crypt sheet for every test and I got an A-.
One of the better CS teachers, I had her for CSII. The HW could be a little long at times, but the course was taught well and all of the important material was covered.
Her class took up all of my time, but it was wonderful.

Excellent CS2 professor. Lectures are full of valuable information and plenty of examples. If you want to do well, take notes on the in-class examples as they often show up on the tests. Exams are quite long and hard, but they cover the material adequately. Dr. Cutler is very nice and helpful in person.
The tests contained more material than what is appropriate.  The lectures were boring but got the key points across.  The homework assignments were reasonable.
great teacher for my class (advanced computer graphics). knows everything about subject. class assumes a lot from people but most students taking it have a graphics background

She doesn't seem or pretend to care for her students.  Sometimes, he doesn't understand the lectures she gave in class because the lecture notes she uses were recycled from previous professors.  She could at least prepare or read it before class.  IMO, she is a disappointment; the fact that she graduated from MIT.

The best computer science teacher I've had yet. Lectures can sometimes be boring, but she makes the attempt to keep them interesting. I'd say that if you have to take CS2, pray that she's your professor.
Extremely intelligent, however her lectures and exams assume everyone else also has a masters in C++ from MIT. Second time taking the course and somehow did worse with her.
horrible

Professor Cutler is very nice and approchable. She is very helpful when you see her with questions. Lectures are easy to follow. She makes the class as interesting as it can be (for being csci 2) and she seems to enjoy teaching. Homeworks are reasonible, especially if you don't wait till the day they are due to start.
Professor Cutler is not one of the beter professors at RPI. Her lecturs are extremely boring and make people fall asleep. Maybe that is why most of the class does not show up anymore.
Dr. Cutler is incredibly cute however she usually dresses modestly and so we can usually pay attention in class.
No Comments

Dr. Jensen is amazing! When he covers content in class, it can be quite confusing, so definitely read the textbook. The class requires a decent amount of studying, but if you put in the work, you will get a good grade. Dr. Jensen is also really fun, so definitely go to office hours and clear up anything that might be confusing!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Not too bad of class. Overall, the topics were maybe a little more in depth compared to highschool bio. The professor was decent. Exams did require you to try and study, it will take some effort. There is a presentation at the end of the course which can help boost your grade. I only really took it because I needed it for my major.

The course had a familiar, high school–like distribution of exams, quizzes, homework, and projects, none of which were especially difficult. The homework assignments were a bit frequent for my liking, but they were short so I think most people will find the course to be quite well balanced.

I thoroughly enjoyed his lectures and found them engaging. I suppose if you aren't that interested in biology the class itself may end up being boring anyways but Jensen certainly does a good job lecturing. The second unit was disproportionately hard and some of the test questions are very detailed so watch out for the small details.

Dr. Jensen is an incredibly smart teacher and knows what he is talking about. He makes very useful analogies in class that sometimes end up as rambles but nonetheless helped me with the course. Be prepared to read because test questions are extremely detailed. The layout of the exams is what makes this class hard. extremely useful class tho.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He is genuinely passionate about teaching and is extremely approachable. Exams focus on lecture content, not the textbook, so show up and pay attention. Lecture content is genuinely interesting, like a higher quality version of youtube educational videos. Homeworks are mini-essays, but they arent harshly graded.
great professor, makes going to class fun. exams soley based on lecture slides and things he says in class, not textbook. really interesting material and he clearly cares about teaching

Overall very fun! Makes jokes and feels like he genuinely cares about students and everyone around him. Knowledgeable in the subject. Lectures are clear, easily understandable, posted online. Accessible office hours. Textbook use optional. Evenly paced. Interesting homework topics. Exams may contain trick questions. Graded in-class assignments.

Professor Jensen is very knowledgeable and seems to care about his students succeeding. The course was tough overall due to the information covered, but he offered chances for extra credit throughout the semester. If you attend lecture and take good notes then you should be fine for the exams. Funny guy

Funny guy, does his best to make lectures interesting. Teaches in a clear manner and assignments are simple and straightforward. Drops a few attendances, 2 HWs, and lowest exam. Exam questions are not challenging, but sometimes questions are very specific facts from lecture. Runs the class like it is: a bunch of CS students trying to fulfill reqs.

Jensen is a very caring and engaging professor. His lectures are pretty fast paced however he was very good at explaining content. Exams are slightly challenging however all content comes from the lecture slides.
A great professor. Makes lectures fun, very lenient on grading and due dates.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Good Professor, very understanding of any personal issues, class wasn't the hardest and provided good support to all students. Gives a cool dad vibe!

Made me feel comfortable switching my major to neuroscience from a chemE. He is my favourite professor, amazing lectures that are genuinely interesting and he answers questions very clearly, attendance isn't required but he does do in-class questions worth three points so missing a few isn't detrimental. The assignments are so easy but interesting.

Dr. Jensen is a wonderful and kindhearted professor who shows a genuine care for his students. His lectures are engaging, and his blatant passion for biology motivated me to be interested in it as well. He also provides great extra material for practice/review. If you can take him for intro to bio, you definitely should!!!

Diffeq with Belmiro was a hard class. He caringly gave extra credit opportunities to get exam grades up, and tried to reinforce key concepts. He's also a funny lecturer but sometimes I walked out of there with no clue what was going on. Granted, it was his first time teaching this course. Good grades are achievable if you put in some extra work.

Took multi with him in the fall. He does a great job connecting concepts to each other making lectures worth attending. Exams can be tough as they test conceptual knowledge on a higher level, but he gives extra credit opportunities and is fair to students. He's a nice and funny guy too. Take him if you want to learn a lot while working for it.

While Dr. Belmiro is a fantastic lecturer and a very nice person and considerate, his exams are extremely difficult. His biggest flaw is how he perceives the difficulty of the material he is giving out. I am fully confident that if I had taken this class with a different Professor I would have gotten a better grade, but less out of the class.

Calc 2 with him was a pretty good class overall. He explains the theory behind processes, not just application, which can be good or bad depending on how you learn. I enjoyed most lectures, but his tests are quite challenging. If averages are low, he gives EC to boost everyone. He's also a nice guy to talk to in and out of class.

Dr. Galo is an A- professor . His classes are engaging and even fun, which isn't always easy with tough subjects like Diffeq & Multi. I took both with him, and while the exams are definitely challenging, they're kind of fair and cover all material well. If you put in the effort, you'll learn a lot. He also offers a lot of EC if the average is bad

One of the best professors I've had at RPI. Made multi extremely understandable and bridged into lin alg well. Offered extra credit assignments when exam grades got low, very caring about his students and their grades. Also, one of the funniest guys I've ever met. Great professor overall.

Had him for Intro to Diff Eq, first time for him and me. Funny and a decent lecturer, but quite theory heavy over intuitive/practical apps. Rec's always curveballs, TAs run them independently. Low exam avgs b/c he thought we were juniors w/ multivar and linalg instead of 1st/2nd-years w/ calc2, but gives EC assignments to compensate exam avg to 75.
Good professor but definitely one of the hardest graders for multi. Can't slack off or you will fail the exams, and bad. Funny, good lectures, just wish he was an easier grader.
His lectures are informative, hes funny, and i cant stop glazing him. what i say expect for... hes the goat. he wants his students to score well and he does it with aura.

Dr. Galo was a great professor, and I'd recommend him to anyone taking mutivar. He's pretty lenient with grading, and offers a good amount of extra credit. The course is definitely difficult, but he teaches the material pretty well, so as long as you study and don't try to game the system, you'll do fine.

Great professor, knows his stuff, and he teaches extremely well. Can crack great jokes, literally a 67/67. Definitely be prepared for the last exam. He did provide two opportunities to bump up the grade. Very thankful for those.

Belmiro cares about his students and wants to see them succeed. Although his exams were a little tougher than Brown's, he dropped many hints in lectures. He tries to be entertaining and has a slight obsession with 67. If you ask for lenient regrades or extra credit, he gets angry, but he often offers those as a surprise. Great guy.
His lectures are good, but just going to lecture isn't enough to do well on exams. Put in some work outside of class and you'll be fine.

Belmiro is very enthusiastic. Definitely attend all the lectures and office hours if possible- he has his own formulas/confusing notes and will often give hints for upcoming exams. The class is very test heavy and the final is almost all multiple choice with zero partial credit which heavily tanked my overall grade. Learned a lot though!

He's literally a 6.7 out of 6.7 dude! I was on track to finish the semester with a 91% (an A-), but he gave some extra-credit opportunities over the semester, including rounding up final grades (what a Christmas miracle!), that I was able to pull it up to a 93% and get an A. See ya in diffeq!

He always finds a way to make class interesting and fun. His office hours are super helpful so I 100% recommend attending. Although attendence isn't mandatory, going to class is very helpful because oftentimes he gives you advice about what specifically will be on the test. His tests are slightly harder than other professors but they are not bad.

Grading criteria is more forgiving than other Multi professors, but homework feels unnecessarily difficult at times. Exams are tough, but less concept based compared to others. He isn't great at giving a deep understanding of concepts during lectures, so you need to study outside class. Yes, he's funny but that doesn't always make a good professor.

Great professor with interesting lectures that well prepare you for the tests, yet you still need to study a bit outside of class though. Weekly homework except exam weeks. The recitations are a bit annoying, but it's his way of ensuring that students are learning instead of grinding the day before exams.

My grade definitely doesn't reflect his teaching because I had stuff going on in the background and skipped some lectures towards the end. Even then, the class overall is very much study more on your own outside of class. Funny, not the best teacher. No curving, little extra credit(?), 70% of grade is exams. Be ready to self-study, don't skip!

He's nice and cares about his class. Exams are just like the HWs and he gives extra quizzes for more points when the avg is low. He's def not the type to push ppl to fail. If anything, he lk wants everyone to learn/earn. What annoys me is that many ppl dont even study and still expect to pass... when they don't, they blame him like it's his fault.
I love this guy
Nicest professor I had ever

This is by far the worst professor I've ever had at this school, as a senior. he's a nice guy, but the structure for calc 3 is absolutely ridiculous. The weekly quizzes are pointless, the tests are ridiculous and he doesn't really care that 80% of the class cant get above a B-. 70% of the grade being exams is also ridiculous.

Funny. Caring. Understanding. Probably the best professor at RPI. Dude rocks. It is clear he wants his students to success in his class, and goes out of his way to help. Math in general is a hard subject to sit through a whole lecture for, but Professor Belmiro makes it fun. Cannot recommend him enough, I genuinely do not have anything bad to say.

Funny professor who clearly cares for students. Gives challenging exams and TF questions are killer, but good lecturer and explains topics clearly. Feel free to ask questions, he will answer w/o judgement. Will give some sort of extra credit to keep class average reasonable. Set a reminder for weekly take-home quiz!

Professor Galo is extremely nice, and makes class fun. His homework and quizzes are not bad at all, and they are relevant to the exam content. The tests were completely reasonable, there were some difficult questions but nothing you wouldn't expect from a 4000 level class. Just show up, do all the assignments on time and you will do great.

Professor Galo is one of the best professors you will have the experience of taking a class with at RPI. He will push you to your limits at times, and can ask difficult and challenging questions on exams, but nothing unfair or unreasonable. A great guy and great professor, he has truly cooked.

I'm annoyed that missing Exam 2 really hurt my grade, and dr Galo refused to drop it. I completely forgot about it, requested a make-up a month later and he denied.  That felt unfair. But to be honest, he offered plenty of extra credit and the exams were very fair. I didn't always agree with his approach, but he clearly wanted us to succeed.
W prof ong mad aura fr. Goated lectures and fire fits bro cooked w linalg. Exams lowk hard but he gave extra credit !! W vibes

Fantastic at teaching, I'd say I understand the content very well. The course was certainly not easy but he made it very manageable, so your grade reflects your effort. Very funny during lectures so they're never boring but still very clear in his instruction. Exams were challenging but fair, and he tells you the topics of each question beforehand.

Dr. Galo is super caring and always checks in after exams. He loves proofs like Dr. Stevenson! Every test had a proof worth 5–20% and a homework question worth 5–20%. The exams were tough but VERY fair. As a math major I loved the challenge. Likely class average will be a B+. His course is as great as a samba dance!

Can't even lie, this dude's got mad riz. Bro broke down the material so even my sleep-deprived brain could get it. Exam averages were:
Exam 1: 77%
Exam 2: 73%
and really cooked up a Linear Algebra activity for extra credit, which lowkey saved lives.  Hws and quizzes were 40% of your grade! Don't be slacking and then complaining about your grade.
It's hard to get high marks in exams and low class averages.

The exam design is unfair. TF questions are worth 5 points each, but no partial credit is given even with correct steps. This is harsh for students with weaker math skills, missing two makes it impossible to get an A. The calculations are also overly complex and time-consuming, making it hard to finish in time even if you understand the material.

Belmiro does a nice job engaging students. He makes lectures fun by adding in jokes and personal stories while also doing a thorough job explaining content. Exams are on the tougher side but he makes it clear what will be included. He has a slight accent but I find that it actually helps me focus. Grades are based on only quizzes and exams.

I would take all my math classes with him if possible. His lectures are amazing, genuinely funny and kind professor. Completely understanding of students' circumstances, and wants to see everyone succeed. Exams are a little tough and can vary massively in difficulty depending on topic, no final exam.

Belmiro Galo is all in all a pretty good professor, I had him for Calc 2 and was pretty lost at first, it seemed like he reviewed some things quicker if he thought people already knew it, but just talk to the guy about any problems you have and he will try to help you. Very supportive in office hours, and don't be scared to grade challenge on exams

I had Professor Galo for my first semester at RPI and he is definitely one of the most difficult ones I've had. He is a great lecturer and the homework was  fair but his tests were significantly harder than other Calc 1 professor's exams.
Great guy who really tries to make the class fun and engaging. Always accessible during office hours and very helpful. The class average for tests was usually about 70 and they are difficult.

I went into Calc 2 my first semester not knowing what to expect and all I can say is he does live up to the hype. He has well organized lectures and tests + recitations that reflect back exams/achieve questions. My only minor problem with the course is that only 1 back exam was given and that was for the first exam

Took him for Calc 2. I was nervous at first because he's known for hard exams, but many questions (at least 70%) were straight from Achieve, so it wasn't too challenging. I got a good grade and could focus on learning without stressing about grades. Keeping up with the homework made this class very manageable.

Took him for Calc 2. Exams are HORRIBLE in this class. To the point where the averages where Ds and Fs. Also, he was not very good at explaining certain topics. Spent hours studying to barely pass with the skin of my teeth... Do yourself a favor and don't take him unless you have to since other Calc 2 professors have much easier exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Took calc 1 with him he was great, favorite thing was he provided tailored exam practices that were set up similarly to exam he gave (just different numbers), wanted to take calc 2 with him but didn't align with schedule. This semester I saw he teaches Multivar and immediately signed up for it its going great. He explains well. Bonus he's funny.

The content is quite tough, Belmiro is passionate about math and has solid lectures. Recitation had group quizzes. He has a bit of an accent, but is totally understandable.
Tests were difficult but never tedious or annoying with the values given.

Belmiro is a lively lecturer, sometimes goes really fast but you can always ask him to explain things after class. He is good at breaking down concepts. He posts clear notes and always willing to help students. He has 4 midterms, no final and always post practice exams. He's known for giving hard tests in calc1&2 but his exams in multi are easy.

Great professor for MATH4300! Belmiro is clear, organized, and genuinely cares about student success. He literally explains "complex" topics well, makes the material interesting, and is always available for extra help. Highly recommend! The hardest B+ I've gotten and learned a ton!

Belmiro is not a bad professor, just inexperienced. His notes aren't great and the few example problems he does are trivial compared to the hw problems. exams and the point distribution is tough. Since he's new to this class there was only 1 back exam but when asked for more exam prep he said he couldn't do anything about it. He's nice though.

Notes are ok for the homework's but don't prepare you well for the exams. Exams can be challenging and tedious, point distribution between questions is ridiculous, and grading is also incredibly harsh in return. He needs to show more examples in the notes that are closely aligned to what's on the exams, especially for computational problems.

Professor Galo did an amazing job teaching this course. His lectures were engaging and enjoyable and he incorporated a diversity of interesting and useful topics into the material. The homework, quizzes, and tests were well-designed and he consistently demonstrated his desire to improve the quality of his instruction and the course for everyone.
Good professor, flexible, easy going.

He's my favorite professor. He's a very young approachable guy and his lectures are solid. He's always talking about sports or making jokes. Would've given a 5 however he makes his exams pretty tough in comparison to some of the other Calc 1 and 2 professors. His exams are copies of old ones with different functions.
He got through the content easy to understand ways. He's known for writing hard tests but I've had worse. There was no final exam too which was really nice!

I've had him for both MATH-1010 and MATH-1020 and he's been pretty great for both. He provides everything you need in order to succeed such as practice exams and a layout of the exams. He really wants everyone to succeed and even gave extra credit after one of the first exams. He's pretty understanding and is always willing to help if you ask.

Professor Galo is an awesome guy, he's a big sports person and is very friendly, and is very approachable if you need help with anything. Tests can be very difficult, especially the first one of the semester. However, he is a very good lecturer and explains things well.

Professor Galo is a fantastic professor for Calc 2, he is one one of the funniest teachers I have personally had before, and always made lectures entertaining. He is also extremely kind and cares about his students, and is more than willing to help you understand anything you are having trouble with.

Nice dude great lectures and you learn a lot however his tests can be extemely hard for no reason. It can also depend upon which version you get with the different versions for the same exam being two different skill levels

He really cares about students and likes to joke around in lectures. He is also willing to work with you if you don't understand something and when our class average is lower than expected he seemed genuinely disappointed/sad and also offered extra credit.

I really enjoyed this class and thought the professor made lectures both enjoyable and informative. The tests were sometimes more difficult due to harder questions than we had gone over in class, but I did feel that doing homework and practice assignments prepared me well for them.
Professor Galo gives great feedback and is great in lectures. His notes may be hard to read at some times, but he is hilarious and fully attempts to help his students understand the materials

A little bit prone to distraction and side tangents, and sometimes it's difficult to read his notes, but overall, he's a great teacher who knows how to teach material while also keeping the class light-hearted and relaxed.

Belmiro is great. He cares a lot about his students, he strives to form connections, and his lectures are pretty easy to follow. The exams for Calc II were on the harder side, but unlike some professors, he curved his exams or gave us the opportunity to do an extra credit project to get some points back. One of the better Calc II lecturers at RPI.
I love him but I wish he gave me a D- at least, still a very fun and easy teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: It was a fun class. Get to know the professor and the class will be more enjoyable.

almost failed the class, he believed in me and i was able to pull myself back up and pass the class. he was very upset i wasnt in calc 2 with him but unfortunately my major classes interfered. i will definitely try and take him again

Prof. Galo is the best prof at RPI. I currently am taking LA & CV with him. I previously took LA with a different professor, but Galo has taught me more in the past few weeks than in that entire semester. Not to mention, he is engaging, hilarious, and a very kind person. He values our feedback as much as we value his.

With great lectures and an empathetic character, Belmiro is engaging and fun to be around. His lectures do a good job of explaining material and are interesting, but don't always correspond well to the content on homework and texts. He tries to strike a balance between theory and application, but his class would be more cohesive if he just chose 1.

Textbooks were recommended, but not required. 

His lectures were very engaging and chill. He made sure that the material was understandable for both Math and Computer Science majors. Homeworks and quizzes were relevant for the exams. Exams were difficult but fair. Time in his office hours were well-spent. Best linear algebra professor at RPI.
Really cool guy. Often adjusts the difficulty of test based on the performance of previous tests. Posts all lecture notes online but it's easier to understand in person.

Belmiro is an amazing professor. Although at times he can make his tests very heavy to the point where the average grade is very low he provides extra credit to make up for this. He wants all of his students to pass no matter what. If you are looking for a math professor I heavily recommend Belmiro.

Professor Belmiro is truly one of the best lecturers at RPI. He cares for all of his students and their success, while making his lectures fun and engaging despite them being just notes. The problems that he puts on his exams can be very difficult, however they are nothing unlike the examples we go over in class.

Belmiro is a great professor, he's very hard on himself but is still fantastic. His exams are very hard but makes sure his students understand the material before. Go to his office hours, they're helpful and he's very nice to talk to. I was going to take him for Calc 2, but I had a class for my major which overlapped. Recommended to all my friends

Really engaging professor and makes calc topics very easy to understand. He makes lectures very lively and interesting. Balmiro is a pretty young professor too so he understands what we're going through and really wants to help students out. Honestly can't think of anything bad about teaching style or hw/exams. By far my favorite professor at RPI.
Went very easy on us in thermo, I messed up the first exam so I didn't do as well as I should have but very easy to get an A. The exams aren't that hard just make sure you make a great crib sheet

I don't understand the low rating here of Dr. Theo, he is one of the most genuine and knowledgeable professor in his academic domain. He is readily available outside of class and reachable via online, and was very helpful ondata analysis for labs. I would highly recommend him as a professor to take. 12 out of 10.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Good teacher don't know why he gets so much hate, it's people venting their incompetence in thermo.

Theo is late and never prepared for class. He insists on doing ICAs that take half of the class time and are not relevant to future homeworks or exams. The way he designed Heat Transfer is not conducive of learning.

Thermo might be difficult because of its 8:30am start time but Theo is a comprehensive lecturer! He covers everything needed on the homework and exams are pretty similar to homework problems. He also invites students to do research with him at the end of the semester.

I don't get why his ratings are so low on here. His lectures can definitely get boring especially because they're at 8 am, but he's incredibly knowledgeable on thermo. Even though lecture attendance is not mandatory, you will fail if you dont go. He's not super warm and friendly, but he's funny and really wants you to do well in the course.

Only has class at an early time. Seemed to reminice about problems instead of explaining what was going on. I hope they have someone else teach thermodynamics in the future. He's simply too familitar with topics to think they need explaining. seems like a nice guy, had good conversations out of class, simply not passionate for basics

Professor Theos lectures can put you to sleep at times, considering this class is usually at 8am. However, if you reach out to him he is extremely understanding and helpful. If you study enough you will do fine in the class.

Thermodynamics has been the most frustrating class I have taken at RPI, and that says something. Professor was no help in thermo, expecting that before each lecture we would understand the content covered in the assigned reading. He then proceeded to not finish the examples provided in class on top of not going over content covered in the reading.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Theo is a really knowledgeable professor, and cares about his students. Students having academic questions can also go to his two-hour office hour every week. I really learned a lot from his thermodynamics courses. I definitely recommend Professor Theo for his excellent teaching.
He literally does not know how to teach this class. Spending the whole lecture time to just do one example question. Lecture slides are just the copy from textbook.
Does not speak clearly at all. Really hard to listen to for long periods of time. Really take your time studying textbook and lecture "notes" to do well because he wont really teach you much
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Horrible lecturer. His slides are incredibly unhelpful and he does a poor job of explaining the complex topic that thermodynamics is. Expect to teach yourself this class from the text book.
Theo is the worst. He goes over 1 example per lecture and expects students to teach the course to themselves by reading through the textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Unbelievably uncompromising amid the covid situation.

Phenomenal professor, genuinely care about his students and their success. Attend office hours if you're struggling at all and he will straighten it right out for you. If the accent bothers you, try sitting up front so you can read off the slides as he goes through them.

Boring lectures. Reads off the slides and is difficult to understand. Slides are copied from the textbook and he doesnt elaborate on any concepts in class very well. Reading the textbook is crucial for success.
Hard to understand, not very engaging in lectures
Great professor. Lectures can be boring but his tests are different and easier then other Dynamics professors.  No mandatory homework.

A really nice guy, however his classes were often times really difficult to understand. His accent first off is hard to grasp. On days where we had subs, it felt like the sun finally came out and enlightened us. So, yah, he's good but a bit difficult to live through. Take physics I at the same time if you want to understand it better.

Really nice guy. Slightly difficult to understand sometimes. Likes to tell jokes and really cares about the students. Still is a slightly difficult course. Especially being basically the first college course that you'll be taking. Good guy though.
Terrible Professor.  Accent makes him hard to understand, and even when you do understand what he's saying, it makes no sense.  Avoid him at all costs!

you get the idea that he wants to try to help you out, but hardly succeeds at it. his teaching method, diction, notes and explanations are pretty horrible. txtbook helped but not  enough to make up for bad teaching.
Boring, accent makes him hard to understand.  Gets behind in the material.

Lets put it this way, the only time i actually learned something in IEA was when professor simmons came into substitute.  he's sort of hard to understand, but not all that bad.  it doesn't matter though because his lectures make no sense, even if he goes off the pre-made powerpoints.
He is no good. His lectures are hard to understand and if he goes off the ppts nothing gets done. We mostly had to use the TAs to learn anything. IEA itself needs to be restructured.
He's not very good with the english. his lecuters are no good. he likes what he does, but his grading is nitpicky
very easy! w00t
No Comments
Not a very clear lecturer but tries hard to help students, and is helpful when asked or visited in office hours.
Very endearing guy but intensely boring lectures. Content is hard but easy to look up. Quizzes are curved hard.
Charles :D
Excellent course and professor! A must take for CS people interesting in Vision and Deep Learning
A very good teacher. Clear and concise. Willing to help. He's not too serious. Other than the professor, the class was very well done.

Professor Stewart seems like a vey knowledgeable person, but when it comes to homework, he isn't fair in the slightest. He seems to enjoy accusing students of cheating off of each other, even when they didn't do anything.
His class is great.

Great professor for data structures! He did a good job explaining pointers and how to write classes such as vectors and maps in C++. Programming assignments and tests were relevant and fair (and also somewhat easy in my opinion).
Charles is the best professor I've had at RPI. His tests reflect the labs and homeworks. His explanations are clear. He's quick to respond to questions. It is a challenging course but fair.
Prof Stewart is the man. He was quick to respond to emails concerning homework/lab questions (within 12 hrs). Super nice and you will learn so much. Data structures ftw.
Very helpful and easy to understand.  Highly recommended.

Data Structures is a really hard class. He, however, is very helpful if you need help. His homeworks are very time consuming. This course becomes like a black hole consuming all your time even away from other courses so be warned of that.
Really good professor and always kind and helpful

Probably the best CSCI professor I've had at RPI. A really smart guy with a good sense of humor. His lectures were clear and fairly interesting, and he was very willing to provide extra help. The exams were fair and not too difficult.

Tests are moderately difficult, requiring strong on-the-spot problem solving ability. He provides a sample set of problems to review, some of which are modified or copied verbatim on the actual exam. Home-works are challenging, so start them early! TAs are semi-helpful, but very unorganized and harsh graders. Lecture notes are your best friend!
Professor Stewart taught the class clearly and concisely; however the difficulty level was quite high and the homework was quite time-consuming.

PROS: Clear in Lecture, Knows his Stuff, Attempts to be Funny, Curves Tests if Necessary, Gives Good Lecture Notes CONS: Huge jerk if you have to deal with him 1-on-1, doesn't listen if you try and explain something, doesn't communicate well with TA's, puts class "regulations" above common sense, sometimes docks massive points for unclear reasons.
I went to every lecture and understood EVERYTHING! Later when starting the homeworks, i was totally lost. Way to go prof!

He's a good teacher. Explains well but nothing extraordinary. I think he reads this too because he doesnt put the lecture notes online anymore for 2 weeks after the class ends. So you really do have to go to class. Lecture notes are key though, it IS the class, that's all he does.

Two Words: Lecture Notes...  you don't actually have to goto lecture because everything you need is in the notes.  If you actually DO goto lecture, you will most likely be bored out of your mind or driven crazy by his pathetic attempts at humor... baseball jokes get old very quickly...
Chuck Stewart is a really good professor. In class he is very clear and gives out printed notes, which are also posted on his website. The tests are kinda toughish...but he prepares you well enough.

A very good, very structured and caring professor. Probably the best comp sci teacher I had and I took cs2 with him twice. The first time I failed due to my own fault along with dear Motten Hotwick's bad class.

Really interesting guy and great teacher. He makes class interesting, and his tests arent *too* bad. He doesn't expect you to know C++ from the onset, so people like me who had no formal programming (lots of informal though) were fine. Homework gets a little tough... but not too bad. Good class.

This guy is awesome.  His lectures are pretty much just suplimentary and you don't have to go, so for the people that do go he jazzes them up with awesome tangents.  His Napoleon refrences are awesome.  He also brings his kids to class occasionally which is cool.  His projects are challenging andfun

He is pretty decent, but his lectures are pointless. I come in 20 minutes late, take the lecture notes (pile at the back of the room), and leave. Read them on my walk back and still get all A's, without trying too hard. The tests aren't too bad. You can expect an easy A if you keep up with the hw!

First few weeks are straight from CS I, but gets into some pretty complex stuff. He's a great code writer and give you lots of examples. Will show you a lot of cool tricks. Tests are medium difficulty, but he tells you what to expect. Funny, not a nerd. Sox fan. Only buy the Koenig & Moo book.

Starts out slow for those who skipped CS I but soon picks up the pace. The material is though but he covers it thoroughly and clearly. Hands out lecture notes and leaves the stack in the back of the room so you can grab one if you come in late. Amusing and fun to listen to as well.
me no like
Awesome teacher. Lecture notes are very helpful, and assignments are relevant and interesting.
Best. Prof. Ever. Stewart is interesting, intelligent, a truly nice guy, and most importantly, really gives a damn about his undergrad students.
wasn't the best prof i've ever had, but the TAs helped out a lot so I managed a decent grade
Fairly engaging professor. Lecture notes are helpful. Tests are hard.
Best CS professor at RPI by far.
No Comments
This guy is awesome.  He teaches you things and you don't even realize you're being taught.  Excellent coverage of material....and Napoleonic history.
He's an pretty good professor and I think I got alot out of his class. He seems to enjoy Napolean and telling us stories about bathing his children. Quite a strange bird, but I kinda like him.
what a jump from hs comp sci... decent prof, but exams are killers
knows his stuff, tries to be funny but really isn't.  HE LOVES bubble sort.
Very clear and knowledgeable. Not the most exciting teacher, but he tries to be.
He knows his stuff... but if you don't conform to his programming style, forget it.
No Comments
No Comments
Good compsci teacher, very knowledgable

No joke math course. Lectures can be a bit difficult to follow - but there's so much outside help these days, it doesn't matter. Vigilant about prompt grading, and there's grade ballast from homework and discussion. You WILL learn the material, and you won't die doing it, but you will have to work. I'd recommend.

Professor Cunha is a really nice professor and he's very knowledgeable in CFD but he's not very good at teaching. His lectures are very hard to follow. They're mostly math equations without any explanations on how the answer is reached. He assumes it makes sense to all his students. Most of the knowledge I learned in this class came from CFD forums
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Horrible explanations, references a lot of outside material and doesn't explain them. You have to look them up on your own and figure out what it means. Homework includes questions that he doesn't teach or cover and those questions are difficult to answer. Assumes everyone already knows the material and skims over everything.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Well meaning professor but his explanations are kind of incoherent. Hard to keep track of what he's talking about.

Lectures and powerpoints are little helpful. It was to the point where I couldn't get myself out of bed to go to class. Exams contain problems that are 10x harder than the homework and lectures. Little to no partial credit on them as well. If you didn't take Physics I at RPI you are not going to have a fun time here...

Complete unhelpful powerpoints and lectures. It was to the point where I couldn't get myself to get out of bed to go to class. This class is also a ton of work for something worth 4 credits. Exams contained problems that were 10x the difficulty of what was on the HW with little to no partial credit.

Lectures and powerpoints are little helpful. It was to the point where I couldn't get myself out of bed to go to class. Exams contain problems that are 10x harder than the homework and lectures. Little to no partial credit on them as well. If you didn't take Physics I at RPI you are not going to have a fun time here.

Lectures and powerpoints are little helpful. It was to the point where I couldn't get myself out of bed to go to class. Exams contain problems that are 10x harder than the homework and lectures. Little to no partial credit on them as well. If you didn't take Physics I at RPI you are not going to have a fun time here. Really tough weed out class...

Lectures and powerpoints are little helpful. It was to the point where I couldn't get myself out of bed to go to class. Exams contain problems that are 10x harder than the homework and lectures. Little to no partial credit on them as well. If you didn't take Physics I at RPI you are not going to have a fun time here. Really rough weed out class...

Completely unhelpful lectures and powerpoints. It was to the point where I couldn't get myself out of bed to go to class. If you didn't take Physics I at RPI, you are not going to have a fun time here. Exams seemed to have problems with 10x the difficulty with little to no partial credit.  Worst weed out class I've taken here...

Honestly the course is not as bad as everyone makes it seem (esp if you did good in physics 1) theres more work just because the lab reports need to be submitted as hw half the time but theres a lot of opportunity for extra credit to get 100 on the labs.

Phys1200, treat the class as 4 separate vaguely related sections: Lec, Lab, HW, Exam. So understand things conceptually when you do the first 3 because they are all different. Then once you have a conceptual base just do a few back exams and you'll be good. You can skip lecture as long as you do the Pearson quiz the night before.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Although the class often runs overtime, he has always tried to teach in an interesting way. In the lab, he is very patient and helps everywhere. When I failed the second exam, I asked him for a lot of extra office hours; at last, I got an A-. He really helped me a lot.
save yourself.
Not the best lecturer, but helpful and caring during labs. There's tons of extra credit on the quizzes, homework, labs, and exams

Ciolek is not a great lecturer. He often goes extremely long (as in, over double allotted lecture time). The labs are fine and there's no prelabs, but there's a ton of Pearson homework. And accessing the textbook is a pain. When Pearson went down because of the AWS shutdown, he responded to an email for an extension with "Hi, No. Best, Ciolek."

Lectures are much better structured than those in Physics 1, they tend to flow well and the labs help a lot with understanding the course material. Ciolek is a great lecturer, but always goes over the end time sometimes by 30 or 40 minutes. Go to lectures and labs, do the back exams, and you will be fine. The exams also have a lot of extra credit.

His lectures are long and suck. There is a lot of extra credit, but it is not like you learn anything, it is all completion based. Absolute NIGHTMARE to deal with outside of class. He is a pain to email, a pain to talk to, and he is completely inconsiderate of anything that happens outside of RPI. 100% does not care about his students. 2/10, AVOID

Really loves math so his lectures explain a lot of unnecessarily confusing derivations done by math and not concept. It's nice if you can understand it but hell if you can't. Countless integrals/derivatives on lecture, a few in lab, a couple on the homework, 0 on the exam. Just do the back exams to study

The grading was fair (and there was plenty of extra credit), but the lectures were largely unhelpful. He'd consistently go 20+ minutes over the allotted time slot, rambling about something tangentially related or taking forever to get through an example problem. I wouldn't have understood any of the material if not for my lab professor or TAs.

Prof Ciolek is a really good physics professor. Although he may seem intimidating, I went to his office hours and he was really kind and explained topics to me very well. My experience with him for Physics II was nothing short of amazing.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I am a 4.0 student, and somehow Dr. Ciolek would make me feel like the dumbest person in the room whenever he spoke to me. Very condescending towards the woman in his lab sections. I would not take this class again. However, I enjoyed the content and thought the exams were semi-fair, definitely challenging but lots of extra credit opportunities.

Good lecturer but often goes over the time allotted, lecture recordings are helpful in understanding the material of the slides, DONT just read the slides and expect to learn that way. Labs/homework are fair, he provides plenty of extra credit to get you to a basically guaranteed 100 for those. Your crib sheet will make or break your test scores.

He is not the best lecturer. There is just too much content to cover and not enough time. I found his previously recorded lectures to be more helpful than in person lecture. He is a slow speaker and it is hard to be engaged in his lecture. Exams are difficult but Physics 2 at RPI is not as impossible as everyone says! Go to someone's office hours.

Dr. Ciolek was a good professor. Often went over the designated lecture time, but was helpful and taught the content well. Lots of labs and homework that take up a lot of time. Exams aren't easy but plenty of resources are given to help study.

His lectures were pretty boring, he mostly just read from the slides, but the slides themselves are pretty helpful. A LOT of assignments outside of class on top of lab assignments, etc. but there's no other option if you have to take physics II. The tests weren't too bad if you study and use the dozens of back exams they give to you.

Very knowledgeable in course topics and very helpful in answering questions. If you arent used to waking up early, maybe dont take him at 8am as he talks in a very monotone, sleep-inducing voice. Apart from that, he is very good.
Consistently and ruthlessly went over class time, but knew the material enough to give good explanations. Be prepared for superhero jokes.

Most people would find him very boring as you sit there and watch him read the slides, as all the professors do. But, he is actually very nice and puts a lot of effort into the slides to make them less boring. Very knowledgeable, good personality, and explains topics in more detail during lab whenever he shows up. Be ready for superhero references.

The lectures are slow and usually go past the class time but he is pretty good for lab and office hours. He gives out a ton of extra credit. Making a good crib sheet will save your life. This class will be tough if you struggled in Phys 1. Ciolek is great but curriculum is not. 
Save your mental health and grades by taking this class elsewhere.

Ciolek has decent lectures and the labs aren't too bad. I didn't think the class took too much time either. The crib sheet on the tests are super important and doing the back exams, but the tests were fair and not too difficult. Everything besides the tests are pretty much guaranteed to be 100 so the tests pretty much determine your grade.

Very good in office hours, always willing to explain a topic as thoroughly as you ask for. Can be blunt, but rarely ever hostile. Lectures can get a little meandering, and often go past the stated end time. Extremely generous extra credit makes it very difficult to get less than a 100 in all non-exam categories. Crib sheets are critical on exams.

reviews.comment:

The GOAT lecturer

He's an extremely tough grader on exams, either you get it or you don't. The average of the class is near failing yet he has nothing to say about it.

If I could give him a 0, I would but I can't on this website. He's not a good lecturer and does not explain concepts well. He is not a helpful professor, and even when the exam averages are 60s he refuses to curve. His tests are unreasonably hard. It is so demoralizing to keep studying and putting in work for his class when its not paying off.

Professor DiTursi has got to be one of the worst professors I've had. The class average is currently a failing score and he refuses to curve exams. Several students, including myself, have asked him for help and resources, and he told us that since he didn't study for exams in his undergrad, he could be of no help to us. If you can, don't take him.

He is a very bad professor. When we asked him about how to study for the class, he said (verbatim) that he was not the correct person to ask about this and that he had never studied for it as an undergrad. We asked him about online resources & he again said he couldn't help us. He gets answers wrong for homework and labs the TAs have to correct.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is a tough professor who will forego study sessions for refereeing children's football. He doesn't post practice questions, doesn't review content, and if you ask him for help, he will essentially say it is a you problem. The only reason I got through this class was because of the incredible TA Eric. Take this class with someone else if you can.

Dr. Ditursi gets increasingly condescending, gives problems his own TAs can't solve, deletes forum posts or responds rudely, and was completely inconsiderate to students trying to cope with the death of a friend. The current class OVERALL average is almost failing. He is purposely unhelpful, VERY narcissistic, and WILL blame you for struggling.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dan does not care. He misses his office hours, does the minimum and undermines his students. Some students including myself will study 40+ hours for his exam, attend all the lectures and still get a D. He can not teach if his life depended on it and your only hope is resources online or the TA's.

Dr. DiTursi is a great guy and I don't want to judge him bc he teaches a notorious course, his lectures are good but the slides are pm useless when studying. Exams are very rough, with the average grade being in the low 60s, and he didn't post a study guide or practice ?s after the first Exam. The lack of support on Exams is killer in my opinion.

Danon is omnipresent in the nuke department, and all must pass through his gates to graduate. He is challenging yes, but you will learn if you come to class. He's a big "you put the effort in" kind of person and you have to make the first step sometimes. Luckily you'll learn a lot if you stick my that rule. He's a funny guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Fair questions and comments, can offer guidance if you're stuck. Lenient grader (final grades  mostly in the B- to A- range), vicious if he thinks you're not designing or showing new/useful results. Grading was a black box: it's not clear if the written reports were equally weighted, and there was no way to find our grades for oral reports.

Teaches the important topics plus the underlying math. I learned more in this class than anywhere else. Brutal homeworks make sure you know what you're doing & are heavy on math & physics with minimal conceptual stuff. Tests are fair & similar to HW, but brutally difficult and tricky. Very knowledgeable but makes some mistakes in lecture.
He won't fail you, but he sure as heck won't give you an A either!

Expect a good challenge, going way beyond the basics of the course. He's a good lecturer, throwing in jokes every now and then to liven things up. He writes fast and his handwriting is easy to misread. Tests are tricky but fair, and the homeworks will "make your mind rip itself apart" as he put it.

I had Dr. D for NEEP lab, PNR, and Rad Tech, and his homeworks are way harder than any other professor's assignments I've encountered at RPI.  You have to take really good notes in class and work in groups to have a shot, because all the textbooks in the world won't help you.

Hands down the best and toughest class I took at RPI.  Danon is extremely intelligent and seems to know everything.  The homework is hard, and I would form a group immediately.  You should definitely go to all classes or you will get left behind.

He is very good in the area, tries to include parts which are useful to everyone planning to stay in nuclear engineering. His homeworks and exams are fair, just require some thinking. Dont expect to study a night before and get a B or C . Be regular, and the course is well structured.
Slightly boring lecturer so make sure to bring a red bull to class. But his tests, labs, and exams all accurately represent the course material. So cool that he plays basketball too!

literally so goated. his lectures are awesome + the homeworks/lecture exercises were pretty spot on for helping me learn the content for exams. pop quizzes, but not bad. the exams were difficult, but they were doable as long as you did your part in studying. overall just a really great guy - he's really understanding and he grades pretty fairly too
Easy to talk to, nice guy, fair exams

Easy to get a decent grade as exams are only worth 45% of the grade and there's no final. Exams are not that hard, and follow the same structure as the practice tests he gives you. There is a total of 7 pop quizzes throughout the class, but sometimes he will just tell you when they are. Homeworks and labs are manageable. Goated Professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Beware of pop quizzes--Respected

reviews.comment: Probably the best class I took at RPI. Defiantly recommend taking with Goldie and he is really talented at teaching. Start the project early!
Great prof. Teaches well and is very nice.
Goat - enough said.

Goldschmidt is the best lecturer I have had so far. He explains every topic very well no matter how confusing the topic is. If you take Operating Systems with him, as long as you go to lecture (or even just watch the recorded lectures) and just pay attention, you will be prepared for all homeworks. Same for the tests; just write a good crib sheet.

one of RPIs best CS professors. Smart and communicates with students well.

exam heavy. exams were pretty hard. brought my grade down a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Good lecturer. Adds clarifications or corrections to assignments if need be. Exams can be difficult, but fair, and provides prep material beforehand.
Best Prof, get in every course hes teaching!!!!!

Goldschmidt is one of the best profs I have had at RPI. His lectures are clear and concise. He is always understanding and will help any student work through an issue. He is also a great advisor who truly only wants the best for his students. His study guides prepare you for what the exam will be like and you will never be blindsided.
Nice
Reasonable amounts of work. A really nice professor, very approachable. The exam is relatively easy if you spent enough time studying. And do takes student's performance into considerations.
Goldschmidt was the one of the best professor in CS department, he have good arrangement for each lecture. Exams are not so hard if you are willing to spend time review it.
fair and accommodating when it matters.

An absolute wizard in Windows Notepad. Lectures are mostly code examples, which aren't super helpful in the moment, but are useful when doing homeworks. Exams are the downfall of Goldie; Operating Systems is centered around coding, but the exams are mc+write the output of a program. The exams feel like they're testing a different class...

Prof. Goldschmidt cares about his students, and he is very accessible outside class. Unfortunately, I never found his lectures to be clear or very helpful. He did not explain examples well, and many in-class problems actually contained mistakes. This made CSCI 2200 very difficult for me, and I still don't feel I understand some concepts.

Is very clear and concise during lectures, and manages to keep things interesting and funny. Is very understanding of students and doesn't try to make tests and homework overly difficult. One of the best professors I've had.
Perfect Professor I've seen ever

This class is hard, and you should read the textbook and start the homework early. However, from what I heard about the CompOrg professors Goldshmidt is easier. He is a nice professor and extends homework deadlines often, and when a lot of students do poorly in a lab, he allows them to get checked off during office hours.

I like Dr G but his OpSys class could be way more useful.

Won't learn things like how the linux file system works, mounting, devices, POSIX file API. Instead covers decades-deprecated kernel functions in depth.

Tested on trivia, e.g. "trace the output of this 20 line code block which forks and reassigns stdio file descriptors multiple times".

A great professor! I met a weird problem and I posted it on the online discussion board. He responded really fast and he ran the test on his computer, and found maybe somethhing wrong with the online grading, so that he just corrected my score in a very fast speed. Good professor!

Goldie is a chaotic good character. He's a bit disorganized but in an "oh I didn't get the autograder working, here's three extra days on your hw" or "this question on the exam was bad so I gave you all credit" kind of way. Very effective at lectures and the homework and exams are fair and not designed to punish you at all.
This guy really knows his stuff

PROS: Great lecturer, always gives good examples for coding, teaches everything you need to know, clearly outlines the homework and often gives starting points/code to help out, pretty balanced grading, accessible CONS: "90-minute" tests take the entire 3 hour block, amount of lecture content in a week ranges from none to 6 hours

Pretty solid lecturer, does a lot to help out students. That being said only teaches in notepad/vim (i.e. no slides or anything) which can make it kind of hard to study if you don't take good notes at lecture.

Dr. Goldschmidt is a top notch guy. Expect to be graded on your coding ability, and expect to do a lot of coding. Quizzes are extremely difficult but may curve. Dr. Goldschmidt has a lot of office hours, unfortunately everyone and their brother needs to see him so expect to wait (like an hour).
Makes workload heavier than the class reasonably requires, takes over a month to give quiz feedback, doesn't give us timely responses, crams significant amount of work in small timeframe.
Good guy, good class, good job

Highly unprofessional -- pushed back several assignments multiple weeks, and often changed expected program output directly in the test cases but not the problem description. Exam questions were near-exclusively multithreaded programs with no semantic meaning that you had to diagram possible outputs for. Did not assess op sys knowledge at all.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: A ez professor

One of the best classes I've taken. What I've noticed is that it's a very example-driven class and so you'll find most of your learning comes from doing the homework and consulting with example code he writes during class. The tests by comparison are very easy.

A nightmare, this class was. The HWs, projects were super-vague. Little to no sample output provided.  The discussion forum for students, the piazza site, were filled with student questions, but the professor or the TAs responded infrequently & often too late. We had more than a month of no HW then 1 HW & 1 project announced just before the final.

AWESOME Professor. Try to get him for every class. Took FOCs, algorithms, and Net Prog with him. Good assignments and felt like I learned a lot. Took FOCs with Drineas as well and learned the material better with Goldschmidt and did way better in the class. Also felt like I learned a lot in algorithms.

An ok professor, overhyped. Helpful if you approach him but can take a long time to reply. Grading takes ages. Is one of few professors who can compile & run code in class without making a fool of himself. Homeworks are all programming but class is mostly not programming, so homeworks are only marginally helpful.
Great professor with appropriately difficult assignments and projects. Understanding but not a push over.
Useless

The professor seems very intersted in the topic, but is sometimes scattered in class. He's very willing to answer questions in class and gives good feedback on exams, although plan on waiting to get your grade. Other than that, I would definitely recommend him, mainly because you don't get very many good-looking, young profs. at an engineering scho
Very interested in teaching
Not a professor, but an instructor. Makes things interesting. Very helpful. Recommended for SD&D.

This class is heavily weighted on tests and quizzes. His lecture notes are confusing and variables conflict with what the textbook says. The class teaches you some linear algebra which will appear in multi so that's nice. If you can find back exams those are helpful.

Cons: proof heavy, lots of content to be tested on, no crib sheets, tough homework, less rigorous versions of the class are taught by other professors
Pros: Very understanding, grading is fair, incredibly smart and can help in office hours, you will certainly learn linear algebra.

Very much a sink or swim kind of class

3 exams no final so no grade saver. I've heard there's typically a final but we didn't have one. Multiple choice/TF was hard. We had homework so that helped. Explains things in an unclear way. He was an okay teacher.

Proof based class. I like how he not only covers the standard topics of linear algebra, but also introduces elementary applications in graph theory, optimization, machine learning, statistics, stochastic processes, and more. The variety in his lectures makes it enjoyable for both the hardcore pure math enjoyer and the applied mathematician.

Third class with Stevenson, and I can wholeheartedly endorse him as a professor, for any of Multi, Diff, or Lin Alg. I've heard that he started implementing hw in diff eq, but when I had him, your grade was made up entirely of recitations/hw and exams. His grading is fair and pretty straightforward, and he's easy to reach in office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He's a good prof but there is no grade saver in this class... No hw this sem so it was only recitation/exam grades and it dragged down my average. The given crib sheet was helpful but be aware: there's T/F and multi choice on the exams so you kinda have to know the theory stuff. Optional final was worth it, no theory just partial credit math

Great professor who is very approachable and easy to talk to. He has easy exams but be prepared because your grade is all exams and quizzes' with no drop so you have no homework to inflate your grade and you can't bomb a test. Go to office hours and the review sessions by math club, especially if Gabe Weredyk holds them, Best. Undergrad. TA.

Amazing class but also his first time teaching NT; he was just getting a feel for the topic and the student's abilities to learn it, so he'd sometimes overestimate us. Topics covered: divisibility, mod arithmetic, arithmetic functions, primitive roots, cryptology, quadratic residues, Diophantine eqs, elliptic curves, and analytical NT. Proof based.

Stevenson is a great, understanding dude. Very soft spoken so I felt like dozing off in lecture more often than not, but his notes are very to read and you can learn the content pretty easily from them. 

Grade is 100% determined by tests and quizzes though. And he loves proofs and theory. Beware if you suck at either of these things

His lectures are very proof-heavy and very conceptual so if you're less math-inclined you may end up a little lost, but these are usually not covered heavily on exams/quizzes. Usually gives a formula sheet (which is a lifesaver for Diff Eq) and holds office hours 4 days/week so is quite accessible if you need help. Definitely recommend over others.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Stevenson is very chill. The class has two exams (one Multi-var, one Matrix Alg) and one optional final. He also gave our class a massive formula sheet, though I don't think too many people actually needed it. The one bad part was 8am quizzes in recitations. Quizzes are basically copies of practice he uploads; tests are similar.

He was a good lecturer and a very lenient graders. Exams were straightforward and equation sheets were provided, making this class easier to understand. We were graded on 2 tests, weekly quizzes and an optional final (I did not take), ensuring we learned the content throughout the semester. He's a great option if you want a good grade!
Extremely awful

Stevenson's courses tend to be more proof-based (even 2000s) so he may be hard to understand if you are not strong with mathematical concepts. His lecture style is laid back. Homework sets tend to be challenging but office hours are amazing. He will basically explain the solution in detail to you if you ask for help. Extremely forgiving grader.
He's a good teacher who knows the material and it shows. Lots of knowledge, so office hours are very helpful if they're ever needed.
A gooooood professor that gives great lectures
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: lecture notes are very nice IMO. easy to self-teach, but lectures are worth attending. Notes follow the format of theorems + definition --> maybe a visual demo --> example problems. . Exams have 75% in-person portion --> based off of lecture qs, recitation qs, and quiz qs (pretty easy). No hw, but the Recitation wrksht basically serves as it.
Awesome professor. He truly wants his students to succeed. If I could take him for every math class I would.
Good notes, decent lectures, very accommodating. Homework's and exams fairly assess knowledge and understanding of the material. Would recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof Stevenson is dad core without the trauma. He has good lectures, notes, and tests. He is very good at answering student's questions. If you are having trouble, his office hours are very accessible and when I went for homework help, he practically did the question for me. He does focus on theories though but is fair by not testing on them.
He is very nice and passionate about math. Check the homeworks with some friends and study for the tests. The tests follow what he teaches in class very well.

Stevenson is a very nice guy that definitely understands the material of the course, however, his style of teaching was not something I liked very much. He tended to focus more on theoretical material than on practical applications, though this may just be a Diff Eq issue. His tests were more than fair, and Homework was graded nicely even when hard
