Stevenson knows the material he teaches and is great at teaching it. His handwriting is clear and his lecture notes are so organized that many don't come to class and do fine. He is generous with deadlines and extensions and many of his tests are styled similarly to practice or homework questions.

As someone who enjoys math, I found Dr. Stevenson's lectures to be inaccessible. His teaching style seems to be designed for math majors or those who took prior courses with him and this did not pique my interest in the subject. Homework is weighted heavily, but he often gave tedious computational problems or obscure proof problems.

Dr. Stevenson has good lectures that explain concepts well, and has fair tests with no surprises if you paid attention. There were no quizzes but instead there was weekly homework of 5-8 questions, only 3 of which were graded. He is probably the best choice for MVC compared to what I have heard about other professors.

I honestly have no idea why these ratings are good. Professor Stevenson is the worst professor I've had. Lectures were boring, always went past the allotted time, making me late to classes. Homeworks were long but few questions were graded, making half of my work obsolete. DON'T take him. I don't have enough characters to describe how bad he was.

Professor Stevenson is a very fair professor, he is likely to give extensions if you ask in advance and will never hesitate to help you if you need it. He is a very good lecturer and will always answer your questions either in person or over email.
Good

Weekly HW, not difficult if you go to recitation. Unlimited page crib sheet that is not collected on exams. I have seen students bring in literal booklets with a table of contents. Exams are straightforward if you study class examples and hw problems. The questions are almost identical. Easy grader. Not the best at explaining conceptual stuff.

Dr. Stevenson is a friendly professor who cares about his students and gives fair assignments and tests. His lectures, however, focus too much on mathematical theory and proofs rather than applications. He does give good examples, but the content can be hard to follow if you don't understand his definitions, theorems, and proofs.
Dr. Stevenson is a caring and friendly professor. He is very passionate about his field and clearly loves to teach. Lectures can be a bit repetitive, but homeworks and exams are graded fairly.

Prof. Stevenson was an excellent teacher. He was able to convey the material well in his lectures, and his lecture notes are very useful when studying. He doesn't give much homework. Do not miss recitation, and don't forget to do the gradescope portion of his test, and you should do well.

Great lecture notes, easy weekly quizzes, no homework, optional final, and exams that are exactly the back exams. It might seem daunting that the entire grade is just quizzes and exams, but the quizzes are a free 10/10, and 25% of every exam is online. While his lectures can draw on an his voice is a tad monotonous, this class is an easy A.

Stevenson is easy A. Good lecture notes. Class test averages are 20+ points above other classes. Easy tests with an in-person and open notes online portion (you have the weekend to do it). TAs go over quiz content for 30-45 min. before quiz during recitation (quizzes are in the last 15 minutes of recitation and are 2 questions). Opt. HW. No Achieve

Dr. Stevenson is a really nice and chill guy. He usually gives out very smart solutions to simplify problems. His lecture style is a theorem followed by an example question.
Homework is basically plugging in different numbers. Exams are medium difficulty, definitely not hard.
Do your hw and backtests, you will be fine

Professor Stevenson is one of the best math professors that RPI has to offer. For his multivariable calculus and linear algebra course, the tests were really easy but the homework was slightly difficult. However, I felt that this balanced out the overall difficulty of the course. Stevenson is very kind, considerate, and an exceptional teacher.
He is very reasonable and cares about students actually learning.
Professor Stevenson is a great lecturer for Calc II. The only big thing to note is he does not assign homework, you are only graded on quizzes and tests. Take that as you will.
He is a great professor, but his notes are not neat.

I had Dan before he was at RPI, but the man is a great teacher who made me love math. Explanations are clear and direct without a lot of fluff, very easy to understand. Tests are definitely hard but not in an unfair way and occasionally have some fun/rewarding questions.

Took him after seeing the reviews here and thought he would be good... I was used to my calc 1/2 teacher whom made me absolutely adore calc, but Stevenson made me stop liking math. Class was not mandatory, but I always went as it helped follow his notes, but that still didn't help much. No quizzes during recitation, so grade is only based exams/hw

Stevenson is one of the best math instructors I've had. He lectures well and maintains a good balance when it comes to what problems you'll see on homeworks and tests, which usually have 1-2 problems per concept and are a very fair assessment.

Took him for diffeq last semester for Multivar this semester. First time teaching the material at RPI for both semesters btw. Seriously, one of the best professors at RPI. He tends to delve into theory a lot but follows it up with examples that are almost word-for-word similar to HW problems and Tests. You can't go wrong taking his classes. Easy A.
Nice grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Had him for both Calc 2 and Diffeq and he's an incredible teacher. His lectures are a good mix of theory and then a few examples to make the content clear. Posts notes and homework/problem set solutions online so you can check your work. Really accessible and understanding. Probably one of the best math teachers I've ever had.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Does not provide enough examples for material.
Easy class. Tests are short and just like lecture. Quiz in recitation is easy. Homeworks are optional as is attendance to class. Learned calc 2, got easy A.

He is a good professor does a lot of theory, but also does examples and steps for a lot of the problems. he is also really nice and you can tell he cares about his students because he is always available in office hours. even though class is not mandatory I would still go because he tends to not write everything he says down in his notes.

Dan is seriously awesome. He makes Diffeq extremely comfortable and easy no matter what your math background is. As long as you know how to do the HW's and in class examples, the tests will be a lightwork. He is also accessible during office hours and is willing to help you understand the content. Overall, great professor and very straightforward.

Dr. Stevenson is a great professor. He takes his time to make sure that every student is able to understand the content properly and is ready for exams. He is great during office hours and is generally pretty laid back.

He is a nice guy and a decent teacher. He is great in office hours and if you need help on the homework he is always there. He also tries to get to know his students if you put in the effort. His tests are mixes sometimes they are easy sometimes they are hard. I had him for calc II, now for differential equations, next semester I will have him.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Teaching is good but texts are so freaking hard.
He's a laid back professor but is still a great lecturer

Justin Dowdall is an approachable and supportive professor who genuinely cares about his students. His lectures are engaging, and he provides helpful feedback on group work. The course is well organized, grading is clear, and his HCI class prepares you for real-world collaboration.

Professor Dowdall is the most grounded professor that I have met. He meets the student where they are at. He forms a real connection with the students that care; Translates his expertise into genuine advice that he can relay to the student. Taking his class has greatly improved my understanding of HCI concepts and he is definitely a pivotal prof.
I know he had a rough start his first semester but really turned this course around. It's one of the best at RPI now. Really should take it. Just finished and was inspired.
Awesome. Very engaged. Really loved this class.
Good class. Enjoy the idea of UX for the community
Focuses on design and community UX. The course is really interesting I left with a great portfolio piece.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Focuses on UX. Pretty good. Enjoyed the class.

Just finished the course and I can tell you this class is awesome. We did real world work and I think made a huge impact with the project. Dowdall really believes in remaking the course every semester and is really good at teaching design in a approachable way. Really makes you think and write. Highly recommend.
I know that he is new I think. I don't know. I really liked the class. Defiantly a philosophy person.
Cool guy cares about his students and the environment. I would highly recommend. The projects are really fun and pretty easy.
Amazing and interesting class. We did really cool projects.

I get it's not his fault he gets 8am class slots but when you do get that, and you know your class is a writing class at an engineering school, why in gods name do you go crazy over attendance? Seems like a nice guy but I dodged going to class without my grade suffering so idk, others have said he rants over useless/boring stuff.
reviews.rating_tags: So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Seems to work hard to make the material cutting-edge and creative. Was my favorite class. Definitely based in theory. Sometimes lecture was confusing.
It was writing heavy but interesting
8am attendance mandatory yapper
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Dr. Dowdall definitely cares about the material he is teaching and the students in the class, but I think he just didn't have a clear vision of what the class was going to be when he started. Overall the class was very easy, so as long as you put in the effort you will do well. Expect the class to be less UX focused and more humanities focused.

At the end of the semester attendance ended up being weighted as 50% of our final grade. This was super unfair to us because it wasn't even mentioned on the syllabus. Participation was mentioned however, it was only said to be worth 15%. On top of all this, it is an 8:00 am class.

He doesn't seem to know much about what he is teaching and is very unorganized. He also never responds to emails. He calls out attendance at the start of the 8 am lecture for the first 20 minutes. One time I emailed him that I was sick and couldn't make it to class, and he ignored my email and lowered my attendance grade anyway.

Most boring professor I've had and he has no sense of his audience. He always has to go the extra mile to make class annoying and bordering on unbearable. He's trying to emphasize writing, rhetoric, and philosophy in a class of IT students.. this is not the class we signed up for
This class does not live up to its name what so ever. This is more of a class about the issues he finds important when considering politics rather than effectively teaching about UX design.
He claims to be teaching HCI, but the content he covers is not related to HCI at all. I don't even know if he is qualified to teach this course, his profile says he is an environmentalist
A pace so slow it scams your life of time. Left for half a month and made his TA teach when the TA is not prepared to teach. I did not gain any knowledge from Fohtung.

Take a different professor if you can. He was consistently 5–20 minutes late to every class. Midway through the semester, he left to do research with no warning, leaving his lab assistant to take over without direction. We couldn't finish the required material. When he was there he rambled and wrote unreadable notes.

Do not take if you can avoid him, he showed up 20 minutes late to class every single day, switched between slides and unreadable drawings and equations on the chalkboard, and left the country for two weeks without telling anyone (including TA) so we didn't get through the content. Teaching style was just rambling.

Nightmare. No one had a clue what he was talking about, he would spend a minute covering actual information then proceed to draw scribbles and pictures on the board. Impossible to contact, and he literally left halfway through the semester for 2 weeks and gave no notice, his poor TA had to cover for him. Didn't learn anything from this class.
So i took this class and didn't know what to expect. But as the term progressed, Professor Fohtung made me to appreciate science and Engineering. He is so intelligent and smart
i am a better student because of thus dude. Funny and smart
very smart professor.  Very easy to talk to and always willing to help. A very fast pace course, but he knows his stuff. Please take his lectures. He also teaches IEA extremely well.
Wonderful faculty and person
Very rude. Ignoring your email and talking to people as if people owe him money
Very Smart Professor. His insight to physics and materials science is awesome
He is a gem!

I got to TA for Professor El-Shafee and I really enjoyed his course! I took a similar course as an undergraduate student, but I can confidently say that I learned something new during each class. I got to see how much dedication he has for his students, especially those who come in for help. I would take this for credit with him in a heartbeat.
He is a great guy and is pretty funny but he goes through lectures very fast and it is hard to understand him. He is not very helpful outside of class.
Wastes time with memes. Do not solve problems that would help in advanced classes. I learned from friends how to draw proper FBD. Generally a nice person but not the best professor.

Lectures are optional but would recommend going, worth your time. Amazing person inside and out of the classroom, very personable. You can tell he is very passionate about his job and it shows definitely the best strengths prof at rpi.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: When he gets excited he can be hard to understand. Otherwise he is very nice and love the memes at the end of class. The break in the middle of class is life-saving and he lets us out early most days so strengths is cool. I never went to his OH tho and went to Mills instead.

One of the best professors I've had at RPI. Excellent at teaching the content, enjoyable lectures, tough but fair homeworks and exams. Truly understands what students go through and will do anything he can to try and help, including responding to emails at off-hours. His end-of-lecture memes were always great.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Shafee is a charming guy I like his foam block demonstrations and memes but his lectures can be hard to follow. He goes through example problems at Mach 10 and loses most of the class halfway through each lecture. The weekly homework assignments take forever and exams are extremely difficult. Prepare to put a lot of time and effort into his class.

Dr. El-Shafee is a very knowledgeable and kind professor! I'm grateful I had him for Strength of Materials. This class can be very grueling, but Dr. El-Shafee was very helpful during office hours and cared about how you were doing if you reached out. I'm a fan of his memes at the end of class as well. Studying in advance for exams helped me a ton!
He's the goat.
good professor for strength of materials, very helpful during office hours
really knowledgeable, kinda hard class
Omar is probably the best professor you will have at RPI. He is engaging and at times hilarious. Class is by no means easy, but it is my favorite class have taken so far.

Omar is genuinely the best lecturer I ever had. He expertly and clearly explains concepts using his foam beams, both in terms of real-world as well as academically. He will purposefully go on useful or hilarious tangents if people need more time to take notes. If you have a question, he will go back in the slides and explain it in a different way.

For IEA, he was a great teacher. He would explain all concepts thoroughly and efficiently and would pause for questions. If a student still did not understand he would explain in a different way until they did. He would even go back in the slideshow if someone asked. Amazing professor and had fun memes in the slides.

There were many incongruence between expectations and what was evaluated when it came time for exams. His lectures are chaotic and obnoxious especially if its your first class during the day. The classes and homework did not adequately prepare anyone for the tests; I am confident that the only reason I passed this class was because of COVID-19.

Overall, a solid professor for Strengths of Materials, though I don't think I would rate him as highly as some of the other reviews. He definitely does a good job, but, if you prefer a more laid-back lecture style, I would recommend Shahsavari instead.

I love his memes. He's got engineering memes in his lecture slides. He's a good lecturer who can project his voice and is able explain and elaborate well. He's available outside of class often and is very willing to help. There's a problem you'll have to do in class each day to take attendance. Tests and homework are long but you get partial credit

Dr. Omar is the best recommendation for IED. He is very nice and kind, always grade your project, presentation and report with mercy. Also he gives good feedback telling you how to do better next time. He really wants every student to succeed!

This professor is the GOAT! He genuinely cares about his students and wants you to succeed. The exam averages are typically higher in his sections of strengths of materials even though all sections take the same exam. He tries his best to keep lectures interesting by showing real world application, and he prepares his own memes for class.

El-Shafe is an awesome professor- he is funny and loves memes, but he also is the absolute best Strengths teacher you could ever have. He knows his stuff (He is the course head) he is understanding of student difficulties and he is very receptive to questions. He has the soul of a millenial and the experience of a 90yr old. P.S hes got all da memes
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Strengths was tough, but it could have been tougher if I had another professor. El-Shafee explained things well and prepared us for the tests. He also cares about his students. Would highly recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: One of the best professors I have had at RPI. He is very approachable and loves helping out to address questions and concerns. The class is not easy, but if you put in the effort, you can do well.
Dr. Omar is a ball of fun. Greatest lecturer to set foot at RPI.

The man the myth the legend.... We are talking about the wonderful man named Omar. He brightens my 8ams with his use of dank memes. He definitely teaches the material well and tries his best to answer all questions. I love this man.

The most disorganized professor I have ever had. He would have quizzes in the syllabus that he forgot about and would take forever to grade. The hardest class I have ever taken, and he will LIE about what is on exams, don't take his word for what will be tested. He says he won't ask about the specifics but he will, memorize EVERYTHING!!!

If you can avoid having him as a professor, do yourself a favor and avoid it. He is bad at teaching; his lectures are so confusing, you have to self-teach everything, and it's still very hard to get a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Make sure to read the textbook and do back exams since his style of test questions was much harder than I was used to from high school. He is very passionate about biology and is a great person to talk to. The class is definitely hard and the tests are difficult but he ended up giving out many extra credit opportunities at the end. I learned a lot.

grades very tough, and expects you to memorize both his slides and the textbook front to back. lectures are disorganized, he will somehow manage to spend two hours covering 3 subsections of an entire chapter. does provide review sessions and will answer questions, but often times it will be a lot of material in one go.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: It's a terrible experience.
He could not provide your any test corrections and will deduct points if you ask him questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: His course is very difficult, and the score is not very clear and open.
Do not choice this professor
pop inclass, complicated test correction criteria

Rutledge is extremely disorganized in his lectures. I had an extremely hard time following his lectures because they were all over the place. He often goes on long tangents about things he won't even test you on, wasting so much class time. Read the textbook because the lectures make absolutely no sense. I would avoid him if possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: He's very test-heavy and textbook-heavy, but most tests don't have material from the textbook. He rambles during lecture and doesn't actually explain anything but expects that everyone do well on his exams. Most of the class ended retaking the whole class next semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Worst proffesor I had in college. Talks too much but does not focus in the actual topic. The tests are very heavy. He said is about something and it result it's about something completely different. The grades are very very bad. He does not give u extra credit on test questions so be prepared. Office hours are very useless, he does not help AT ALL.

Out of all of my professors, Rutledge is the one who seems to care most about student's success. His passion for the subject material is evident and he wants all his students to care as much as he does. If you participate in class and attend his exam reviews he'll love you and give help on tests. It's a lot of material, some only from the textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: 70% of the grade is 3 exams that he expects the average to be around 60%, he won't tell you what to study or whats on the exams and the lecture slides are worthless. I'd say just study the textbook but he had the class get newest version which was twice as expensive but only used material from the 5th edition for exam and lecture material.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Great professor, very understanding and helpful during office hours. He's amazing.

Dr. Rutledge is a great guy. He will go above and beyond to help students understand. It is obvious that he is very passionate about biology, and he really cares about his students. Make sure you find some study buddies for this class because having a review with them before the exams is very helpful. The exams progressively get more difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr Rutledge is one of the toughest professors I've had so far at RPI, but he's a really good guy who wants you to succeed. His exams are pretty difficult and in-depth, and he doesn't really curve or offer much extra credit, but he's very accessible outside of class and encourages asking questions. I learned quite a lot in every lecture.

Terrible at communication, never answered emails in a timely manner. Exams had a lot of content and were mainly based on the textbook. Before every exam, he would send out a list of topics less than a week prior and revise it multiple times just days before the exam took place. He did give a good amount of extra credit though.

i think dr rutledge does a great job in this class. there is definitely A LOT of information covered (an entire textbook in a semester), but he isn't ignorant to this. he was super accessible outside of lecture periods, and was more than willing to meet to help review for exams. it's a lot of work, but he is absolutely one of the best profs at rpi
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Really liked his class - Truly goes out of his way to ensure his student's success. He tries to give a strong biological foundation for his students. If you put in the work for the class, it should work well for you. BIGGEST TIP:  Don't wait till the last few days before a test to study - study 20-30 min everyday!

Just skip the lecture it doesn't matter. The material on the test is straight out of the textbook and none of the lecture material. Memorize the textbook. Hard tests because of all the information the textbook provides. Only good thing is he allowed test corrections otherwise the majority of the class would be below a C.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Nothing related to the lecture and exam. You have to read through the whole book. Never repeat the answers that he gives in class. Horrible class experiences.

His cell bio is very hard but worth taking it. I thought I would end up with a B+ but there was a curve at the end of the semester, so I got an A-. First test is always the easiest one so try to get as pts if possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Does not Properly lecture in his classes and does not go into detail what is on the test you rely on yourself to memorize the whole textbook to succeed in the course. The only way you can get an excellent grade his class is to either eat and breathe cell biology or go to all of his office hours. don't take if it is not mandatory for your major
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Also took BIOL2120 w/ him. Overall, he is a good professor but great guy. He is always willing to help students and explains things very well; he is very smart. However, he is a tough grader, has fairly tough exams, and can be very disorganized in lecture/teaching. However, talk to him about everything and follow his guidance and you'll succeed! :)

Overall, great professor especially for office hours. Tests can be difficult so DEFINITELY READ THE TEXTBOOK. Lectures may be a bit unorganized/not actually cover the material for the test but definitely very helpful to answer questions related to exam preparation. Very supportive of students and helpful in lab as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: He's the worst lecturer I've had the displeasure of having at RPI. He wants to feel important and like he's preparing us well, when in actuality he goes on and on about concepts not on the test and only mentions actual test material briefly. Incredibly frustrating, boring lecture.

Not very good at grading, waited to put any grades online until finals. This made it very hard to gauge where you are in the class, I didn't appreciate it. Other than that, he knows what he is talking about and is very interested in the subject.

Dr. Rutledge simply loves teaching. this is one of the things we have in common, however,  if he grades you wrongly and you bring it up he will think you're just grovelling for points and completely dismiss any arguments you have, no matter how logical they are. He's right and you are wrong and that's the jist of every argument I have had with him.

Dr. Rutledge gives very tough exams, but he really takes time to prepare you for them. He is extremely generous with his time and even comes in on weekends for study groups. I recommend reading every chapter of the textbook and swinging by his office regularly. He's a very nice guy and I enjoyed his class.
I liked the lab part of the class but Prof. Rutledge wasn't a good lecturer. He didn't seem interested in what he was presenting and his slides weren't that clear either. Tests were fair overall.
Prof. Rutledge is an amazing lab professor. Very helpful, but ask a lot questions to get the most out of the class. He really wants you to succeed.

He didn't know what he was doing, and it was really evident. The averages for the tests went downhill over the semester, even though he said he was trying to make the tests more straightforward. Thankfully though, he came to his senses by the final and let us replace our lowest two test grades with it. Also he handed out A- like candy at the end.

He says that everything is important to know for the test.  He also says that the test will not be specific, but the questions are very specific.  Also, if he emphasizes that something will be on the test, chances are that it won't.  Boring lecturer.  All his slides are pictures, so it is hard to go back through them.  Overall would not recommend.

His lab class was a lot of work but he was great.  He even came in all day on a couple Sunday's to help students learn lab techniques that we didn't have time for in class if they were interested.  He's very approachable and I enjoyed talking to him outside of class.  He really respects people who put in extra time and will give extra credit.
Great teacher. Some TAs grade papers harshly but you can bring yours to Eric for a regrade.

Dr. Rutledge was a great professor! This class was a lot of work (4 papers ranging from 12-25 pages each) but Rutledge was very helpful. He has high expectations and expects you to know every little detail about the lab but if you pay attention when he talks it's not a difficult class. You have to put in some effort but it's not hard to get an A.

Dr. Rutledge actually cares about his students, both their grades and what they get out of his course. He is approachable and kind. Be warned that his papers are highly demanding and the way he words things on rubrics and handouts tends to be unclear. He makes more sense in person so ask for clarification when necessary.

This guy cares about students. Different from other students in the class, I had 0 molecular biology background when I took his lab, and was worried at the beginning. Thanks to Eric who helped me a lot. He made me feel as long as I worked hard, I could do a really good job. This class had a lot of fun, just love it
If you are looking for the best bio 1 teacher at rpi,  this is your man hands down.  Kind, smart, and excited to teach, this guy will go to the end of earth and back for you and your grade

He's extremely friendly and a great guy.  The only problem I had with him is that he taught us what he wanted to teach us, which often involved whatever worm functions he was currently studying.  Because of this, he made his own tests for his section that were often harder than the tests the other sections took.
You will not find another class or teacher where learning is actually easier or more enjoyable. Highly suggested.

Awesome prof. Clearly tells you what is expected and is very helpful! Is more interested in making sure students actually LEARN something than anything else. He is also passionate about the material, which is refreshing. Very straightforward, if he does not know the answer to your question he will tell you.

Amazing professor! He was very clear in class, willing to help is students, and was just a nice guy to talk to.  His Biology lab was easy because he explained everything very well and gave detailed guidlines for his papers which made it easy to write well, and write what he wanted.  DEFINATELY take his Class!!

My favorite class of the semester, even though it was the earliest. Unlike other professors, including the other thermo one, Professor Elahi does not yipyap. He gets straight into the material and lectures at a pace that is very digestible. Exams were on the easy side, which led to a very high class average. I hope he continues to lecture.

This dude sucks. Reads the slides word for word and puts you to sleep. Monotone and does not project his voice. All exams were THREE questions, including the final exam, which was absolutely brutal and did not favor the students' success. Seemed like the final was angled towards how hard can it be rather than showing what you know.

The prompt says to discuss the professor's abilities to which my response is he has none. He fails to teach anything useful and just reads off of the worst lecture slides man has ever seen. The back exams he provided to prepare for the exam was not even remotely close to how evil the actual exam was. A fate I wouldn't wish on my worst enemy.
DO NOT TAKE THIS COURSE with her.

I think Professor Fontaine is a better professor for MITR than HCI - that being said, I liked MITR less than HCI. The courseload for MITR was just too much, but I don't think she chose it to be that way; it's just how she's required to teach it. Overall, she was pretty reasonable, graded fairly, and she appreciates whatever you contribute in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: my favorite professor at rpi
honestly kind of boring as a lecturer but the class projects/work was kind of fun. her assignments were pretty simple but the instructions were sometimes confusing. she grades pretty fairly as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment:
Quizzes are in-person with your group or online open note.
In any given assignment just use exact key words/phrases out of the relevant textbook sections.

A fine lecturer, trying to make class interesting when she could. The only issue was that it seemed like she didn't know what she was talking about. She has industry experience but not enough experience with the topics to be able to teach the class in a way that students get a lot out of it. Give her a few years though and I'm sure she'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Had her for Managing IT Resources, she has very strong political views and contantly pushes her politics onto students. She also is very strict on participation and tracks everytime a student raises their hand and speaks. Her grading schema states that if a student fails the participation grade then they fail the enitre class, which is very harsh.
Great, personable professor with a kind but strict teaching style. You will learn a lot in this class and enjoy every minute of it. 10/10, would take again!

Purely quality over quantity, I'm not sure why some here say the lectures are 'boring'. He's beyond expert level when it comes to the course material, and you never get the sense that he's bored teaching fundamentals. My biggest regret from this semester is skipping a few of his lectures. He has a way of explaining things where you just get it.

Provides a lot of good notes and plenty of backtests, which are similar to the tests. Labs are short and easy. HW is fairly short but sometimes difficult and is similar to the tests. Lectures are boring but teaches the content well.

The lectures were boring, I frequently struggled to stay awake, or sometimes even show up. The lectures were kinda slow and repetitive and he's not tech savvy. But the lecture notes were great, it's just a big PDF of great notes, reasoning, and examples, with important equations highlighted clearly for you to put on your crib sheet. Learned a lot!

One of the best professors I have had at RPI. His handwriting is super neat and notes are very clear. He is very fair with his assessments. He doesn't expect you to know things he hasn't taught you. He also cares about his students. After hearing that the first lab took us 6 hours to complete, he modified ALL of his labs to make them only 2hrs max.

Really good Professor. One of the best Professors I had ever met. Wonderful experience in ECSE2050. His writings through his lectures provided enough time to take notes and his explanation of concepts are clear and brief. I did learn a lot and have a thorough understanding of MOSFET BJT in his lecture. You are not going to regret taking IE with him

The material turned out to be alright, and he managed to teach them coherently most of the time, though he does include some questions that weren't clearly elaborated on. The class was a bit disorganized, though, as there were only 2 mentors and they kept changing their office hours. Overall, my experience in this class was alright, I guess.

Is easy to reach out to, very fair when it comes to grading, and has a more interesting approach with lectures and laboratory experiments that helps students further understand the information taught in the course.

Fields and Waves 1 is a tough course but prof. Schubert definitely made it a great learning experience. His lecture's pace is good and makes sure you have time to copy everything down. We only had 8 homework this semester and it was a good complement for lectures. Plus, his tests are not heavy and grading is fair. Past exams are accessible online.

I enjoyed the lecture. Professor Schubert always wrote everything down in beautiful handwriting, which I respect a lot. The lab was fun and not stressful. He is good in teaching among professors in ECSE department. He also cares about students.

Schubert makes Fields and Waves as painless as possible. He take notes in class so you have time to copy everything down, he allows you to have anything handwritten with you on the exams, his back exams are easily found online, his exam questions and homework questions are often reused, and his labs are incredibly easy. He respects your time

He has confusing and fast pace lectures, and does not care about students' feelnigs on exam date. He makes the test on the first day after spring break and after a class-cancelled day was cancelled. Have no idea what he is thinking about.
Fantastic professor. Learned all of the material very well and in a totally painless way.
Good Professor

by far the easiest class ive taken so far. easy A. some homework assignments but the grading is more like, did you do it? instead of did you do it right. i was surprised when i recieved an A because i didnt attend many lectures and i did miss a few assignments

Lectures are amazing in my opinion, but the course layout is not well made. There were very few assignments outside of tests, and no practice exams or quizzes were available. I hope Dr. Flint makes this easy fix, as I believe his lectures are far more engaging than any professor I have had before. Material is fascinating, but very difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: From a typical A student: Neuron to Behavior is an interesting class, but the professor is completely disconnected from the students' struggles and oblivious to the difficulty. The tests are worth a disproportionate amount, there is a lack of any homework or resources to prepare for the exams, and the class is counterproductive to genuine learning.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Absolutely awful professor. This class is a disaster. Lectures are PAINFULLY boring, useless, and completely disconnected from the exams. The course is almost entirely tests, making it ridiculously easy to fail. Zero concern for students, no real office hours, impossible to reach. Easily the worst professor I've had. Avoid this class at all costs.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Traldi is genuinely the best teacher I've ever had. She makes a point to get to know each and every student in her classes even when they're in massive lecture halls. She is always available outside of class and is so excited to help whenever she can. Traldi is just amazing and she lectures very clearly and posts her lecture notes after class.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Very fair tests with no surprises, explains the “why” of concepts very well, and clearly states what is expected out of the students (such as what the quizzes and tests will be on.)

Exams are a worth 70+% of your grade which sounds bad, but the exams were fair and sometimes similar to homework or quizz problems. She also drops one exam, and gives weekly quizzes which are easy and help prepare for exams.

Although there are so many context need us to remember, she try her best to explain the context in an easy way. And the assignments always give us the comments so that better help us to understand and correct it. Recommend!
She is the best Professor I've ever met. She give clear lecture note and helpful after class to explain. REALLY RECOMMEND

She isn't great at explaining lectures. Exams are hard and not based on the homework or problem solving. She doesn't take responsibility for mistakes on her answer keys and ignores half your emails. Traldi seems nice, but cares very little for the success of her students. Tried to like her in the beginning, but was proven very wrong in the end...

Lectures are boring most of the time, tests are worth 82% of your grade, and the averages on them range from 68/100 - 82/100. I did learn a decent amount from this course, but if you are looking for an easy A, this is not the class, as you have to average high on 4 tests that don't even get curved at the end of it all.

Doctor Traldi is amazing. She will help you learn so much, and has handy tricks and tips for memorizing and understanding everything you need to. If you need to take a class and it's taught by her, do it 100%. She gives fair (and usually decently easy with only a few tricky questions if any) exams and wants to see you succeed (and get a good grade)

Great at the Multi section, a little unorganized in the Matrix section. Tried out a new homework-required grading model, which I appreciated the practice from but could get very tedious and repetitive. Exams weren't too difficult but were very long and are worth most of your grade. Overall great and caring instructor, but class structure is iffy.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great lectures, I never enjoyed math like this before. If you enjoy derivations, she's great. She also gives graded quizzes weekly during lecture, which really pushed me to review constantly and not become rusty before exams.
Test are mainly based on concepts and not actual math. Lectures are very confusing and feel very scattered. Would not take multi with her again.

Dr. Traldi is a kind professor, but this class (MATH4040) was just frustrating. The difficult nature of the course contributed, but half the class was lost. Homework is fair and she is helpful, but exams were challenging, even when they were made to be easy. I thought the class was just presented poorly, though I have heard good things from others.

Super sweet professor and extremely helpful if you go to her office hours. Weekly quizzes which means you actually have to go to lecture but they're a good grade boost. Exams sometimes are more difficult than they need to be which is unfortunate but overall not too bad.

Traldi is a great teacher and if you pay attention in lectures the class is not hard at all. It kinda sucks that almost 70% of the grade is based on exams, but the exams are fair and are true to what she teaches. She gives weekly quizzes that are not hard and help you prepare for exams. Homeworks are easily manageable. I'd recommend her.

Dr.Traldi is such a awesome teacher. She makes her lectures very engaging and she is very helpful during office hours. Although she gives quizzes every week, they are at most 1-2 questions related to the curriculum that REALLY help you boost your grade. If you have the chance, take her class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This course is so hard, traldi is the worst teacher I saw in RPI

Required recitation attendance because of quizzes. If you do all the hw, the quizzes are not too bad. It is hard to revisit her notes after the lecture. If you pay attention in class, it's not too hard to do well. She is very understanding and a great person.

DO NOT TAKE. Exams are worth 70% of the grade and tend to not match the material covered in class/on homework. Professors refused to provide solutions to review problems (and were reluctant to provide those). Grading was extremely slow and little to no feedback was given. Lectures were awful and occasionally had errors that were never fixed.
Good professor for Calculus I & II. Really terriable for high level math course.

She has very clear and precise notes and goes over them in detail. Everything on the quizzes was from the textbook homework which was optional and the tests were very fair. She is a great professor the only thing is if you're a freshman taking multi-var, review calc 2.

Traldi is a very sweet and caring professor and I really enjoyed having her this semester. Her lectures are informative and she uses many examples to explain concepts. The homeworks aren't graded but it is important to do them if you want an A. Overall a great professor and I'm looking forward to taking more classes with her in the future.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Traldi is a fine professor but doesn't really teach for understanding but more so to remember a format. Lectures aren't terrible to listen to but looking at the notes independently is pretty difficult. The text books aren't very much help (at least the matrix algebra one isn't) so I would not recommend paying for it.

Though Traldi's mult required a lot of work, I learned a lot about calculus and linear algebra that weren't taught in other classes. Besides that, she's super kind and works hard to be accessible outside of class. Can't wait to take linear algebra with her in the Spring!

Awesome professor all around that understands that math can only be learned thoroughly with the use of examples. You will find that going to her lectures will flood you with examples of all sorts to ensure you are prepared for tests. 10/10 would take again.
Professor Traldi is the best professor I had by far. She is extremely caring and passionate about the subject she teaches and she teaches it well.
She's really as good as they say. Great explanations, clear notes, fair tests. And she's super sweet.

Very nice and caring professor. Does lots of examples in lectures and gives fair tests. The grading is a bit rough  but she is always accessible outside of class to help. Overall the best math professor I've had!
Professor Traldi is a good teacher with long but good lectures. She does a lot of example problems. All homework is on an online site called Achieve. Exams give partial credit and there is no final
Dr. Traldi is an amazing professor who's sensible in her grading as opposed to rigid and truly cares about her students

Dr. Traldi is a very kind and caring person. Unfortunately, this does not always translate into being a good professor, and she is a great example of this. She provides no review sessions or study material for exams and states what to expect on exams and does something different. In lectures, she has a talent for making very simple topics confusing

She is a very nice person who cares about teaching. But often she makes many mistakes during lecture in which students must correct her (she understands and admits when she is wrong, though). Her lectures also include a lot of material that we are never expected to know on HW/Exams.

A lot of people seem to equate being a great professor to a professor being a nice person. Sure Professor Traldi is nice but she cannot teach at all! It is very disappointing because I heard such great things about her. Her classes are dry, she seems to not even know her lecture material, and she expects you to basically be a math major.
Great professor, lots of office hours.
Nice professor.
Very fair and understanding.

Prof. Traldi is a fantastic teacher who really cares about all her students. I had a very good experience in her class. Her lectures and notes were easy to follow, though class could be a little slow at times. The only thing I didn't like about this course was the homework which often had many problems that were totally unrelated to class material.

One of the best professors at RPI, if not the best in the math department. Lectures are very thorough with a lot of examples to show applications. Dr. Traldi worked so hard to get the class engaged and we did not make it easy, but the time she put in made the lectures and hw so much more enjoyable. Highly recommend! (This is for Linear Algebra)
Wonderful professor

Professor Traldi is probably the best RPI math professor. She genuinely cares about her students and does her best to answer questions outside of class. On top of that, her notes are so clear that you will understand the material after reading it just once.
Loved her lectures and her notes. Lots of homework, but if you do it the exams will be easy

Such a nice person. The math department had just said that they would not be rounding up grades but I had a 89.9 something so I put in the webex chat that I was sad my grade wouldn't be rounded up. She went through my homework assignments and found a few more points for me so that I could get an A- in the class instead of a B+. Such a kind person.
really good and clear lectures, seems like she really cares about her students

Dr. Traldi is one of the kindest professors at RPI. She is so accommodating and helpful. She made a point to learn the names of all her students. On the last day of class, she was able to name everyone in the lecture hall. Her lectures can be a bit dry, however that is to be expected from an hour and a half calc lecture. Overall, a great prof.

Class was 80% exams, lecture notes were not the best as far as examples but they were very thorough on definitions. Be prepared to show every scrap of work you can think of on exams though... there have been many points lost for not showing enough work even when the question was simple enough to do it in your head.
She's very sweet, responds to emails rather quickly, and teaches very thoroughly. You have to study for the tests though because grading is tough

Traldi is wonderful. If you can understand a person with an accent just fine, I highly suggest taking her class. The textbook is only used for homework, practice before a test, and anything you might've missed. You can tell she really loves calculus and wants everyone to enjoy it as she teaches.
Overall great professor. Notes are always very helpful, posts them after the lecture incase you miss it. The tests were fair usually very similar to notes and homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: You can not attend lecture all year and still pass, which indicates how detailed her lecture slides are. If you decide to attend, her accent isn't hard to understand and she will end early, time permitted. She's witty, and funny, often cracking jokes about how her student attendance dwindles throughout the year. She understands and is there to help
Great prof who I would defiantly recommend. Has an accent but it is not bad and doesn't make the class hard to understand. Great lecture notes and will let us our early if we don't have a ton to do.

Great prof all around. Lectures are amazing, lecture notes are as well. Concepts are explained super thoroughly and everything is very easy to understand, only if you're willing to spend the time to learn. Obv calcII is not a breeze, just put the work in and you're good. The resources are there for you!

Professor Traldi is the best professor I had in RPI. She is super nice. If you have any questions, just email her, she will answer your questions soon. Sometimes, she may not see your email because she got lots of email from students, just email her again or go to her office hour. Her office hour is very helpful.

One of the best classes I've taken in the Math Department. We had homework almost every week but if you understood everything in the homework, you are good for the tests. If you have any questions, ask her. She is very generous and is always willing to help her students out. I would 100% recommend this class

She explains her lecture notes very clearly, not just reading off her notes, but actually explaining more of the concept's application & all the related terms and details. She explains in simple language so that we can really understand the terminology and concepts. She's also super nice and cares about her students' wellbeing!

Professor Traldi is a great professor. She's always willing to help her students with any questions they have. Her office hours were very helpful (but there's a lot of stairs). Her lectures could be a little dry at times but she actively engages the lecture hall by asking the students questions. No need to buy the textbook, she posts HW online.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: there was a lot of not mandatory homework but the quizzes were basically homework questions with different numbers. The tests were straight forward and similar to homework. If you go to office hours she is the sweetest lady ever, she will remember your name and will prob be a nice grading your assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I absolutely loved my time in her class. She can be a difficult lecturer, and the homeworks needed dedicated time, but the exams are gentle with extra credit. Cares for her students and had most of our names by the end. Understands student struggles well and does her best to support us. She made a difficult class very accessible to all majors.

She is clearly very knowledgeable on the subject, but her lectures aren't the easiest to follow. Homeworks overall are fair and challenging, occassionally with extra credit. The real kicker are the exams, which are very challenging and go deeper into the content than the hw. The worst part about this class was not being able to prepare for exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Even with a comprehensive crib sheet for the final exam containing thorough notes from every lecture, I felt completely unprepared. Currently a grad student after completing undergrad here, and this has by far been the hardest class to succeed in. Lectures are very hard to follow, no/minimal examples are provided for each topic.

Worst Professor I have seen here yet. Can't understand her writing, her tests do not follow the homework or lectures at all and make zero sense. I did not learn anything in class, only external by reading and studying on my own.

Good professor. Cares about doing well, and about the material. Class was very fun.
Sometimes homework would have problems that would require (or be made much easier) by something that was not covered until lecture after they were assigned, so if doing homework immediately maybe hold off on problems that seem overly hard.

Professor Li: If everyone fail, then everyone fail. I am not gonna curve it. 
Take this as a result for your final grade, and you will get a extremely hard final at the end. 
Do not take any of her classes, unless you really do not care about your GPA.

She clearly did not know what she was talking about and set many of us up for failure. Many I people I know including myself did way worse in her class than we ever had in our lives (even with tough classes some being tougher than this). Never knew who the TA was even though that was who graded everything and she did not care about others success.

Very harsh grader. She did not understand all the material she was teaching and told us so. The first two exams are fine, very fair. However, the final is significantly more difficult than the two exams, and it has nothing to do with the material. Your grade in the course will go down by at least a letter grade due to the final. Take with Stevenson

Professor Li is a good teacher. The pace of her class is rigorous and the courseload is a little bit heavy. Yet you can learn a ton with her. If you are a Maths major student and want to actually learn something, I would definitely recommend her.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Her lectures are hard to follow, and she has pretty bad handwriting. I ended up skipping them all together and learned the material through the textbooks and her homeworks, which are actually really good at getting you to know the course material, which is a big plus. Her tests are very fair and she often offers extra credit on assignments.
Very helpful in office hour. Clear note and great lecture. You can really learn something during the homework, which is not very hard but helps you to understand the lecture.
She is a good professor,
She is a good professor.

Math Analysis is very difficult by nature, but Professor Li did not really help lessen the blow in any way.  Her lectures do not have clear direction, her writing is often illegible, and she tends to talk quietly at the board.  From my experience she also does not consider arguments different from hers, and is therefore is a very tough grader.

He is a great guy and a very enjoyable professor but the way he writes his exams is in a much different way to the homework so regardless of how hard you study the exams are always a little bit foreign.

Professor Fritz was a phenomenal teacher. Assignments were fair, tests covered what he taught, he was always willing to help students in need, and his passion for the subject was clear as day. It wasn't too hard or too easy, but a perfect balance. On top of all this, he's an amazing person who I look forward to taking radiological engineering with.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Totsingan was my professor for the lab of my general chemistry I course. He spoke slowly and was always welcome with the questions. When he explained the lab he made everything very clear and straightforward. The best part was he always responded to emails and they didn't even have to be about the lab. Great Professor!
The best lecturing English. Slowly speaking made me extremely comfortable during the lecture.

Good-heart and understanding the suject/topics very well. Good at delivering knowledge and techniques clearly. He is a great professor and he is willing to teach you everything you need to know if you work with him in labs.
One of the best lecturers I've had. He explains difficult concepts very thoroughly and methodically. A lot of the time I did not even have to read the textbook.

I had Dr. T as my lab instructor for both Chem 1 and 2. He always does a great job of explaining concepts. I always understand what he teaches and he is the reason I am not doing terribly in Chem. He once dedicated a lab session on going over a back exam so that we could do well on it, when he was not required to. He is also very friendly.

He's a great professor, but he also might not be everyone's cup of tea. He plays videos in class, which are entertaining sometimes, and other times a bore. The tests are all MCQ but the questions are kind trivia-ish which gets annoying at times. I really liked him as a professor tho bc he was nice and funny so I'm giving him 5 stars

Optional 4th exam includes content from student presentations, but professor does not upload/provide access to the slides, saying that it will help with engagement/participation... As if students have photographic memory? Or require them to write down everything/take photos, which goes against engagement? I have no words.

Does not care about students' success and seemingly goes to lectures just to keep his paycheck. NEVER replies to emails, no curves/extra credit, mandatory attendance, biweekly quiz/exam - feels like they're trying to give the hardest time to students who just wants a good grade for a required intro class that's completely irrelevant to their major.

If you look up the biology exam #.... on Quizlet you will be able to find about 70% of the questions on the tests and quizzes. The questions are obscure but since you have the questions it is not bad. It is really easy to get a good grade in this class as there are a lot of opportunities to bring up your grade up.

- Quizzes and exams are all multiple choice which leaves a lot of room for overthinking and errors (although I'm not sure what a bio free response would look like). 
- Lectures are almost ALL composed of videos, and he barely teaches at all (also extremely disorganized).
- He is enthusiastic about biology though.
Showed a ton of videos in lectures and barely taught anything. He would show up 2 mins before class in crocs without socks on. He didn't care about teaching at all.

Dr. Farrell is an amazing professor. He's passionate about what he teaches, and makes it clear what he expects from students. Exams are fair, homework is simple, and the lectures will teach you everything you need to succeed.

Really fun class, Farrell is very nice. Reviewing a year after I took it after seeing these reviews, very upsetting that his rating is anywhere near some of the genuinely terrible teachers in the bio department. Makes class interesting if you care at all to learn the material, and easy to do well on tests if you just listen to what he says in class

The quizzes/tests do not reflect what is on the lecture slides, and now he isn't going off the back exams so what's going to be on the tests is pure guesswork. Was visibly disappointed when the class had a high average and made the questions on the next test more obscure to compensate.

Great and funny human being. Lectures also were great, he does lots of videos and slides but his commentary adds to content. Not too difficult either, just memorize slides/video details and you will be golden on assessments. Homeworks are not too challenging either. The final group project is also pretty fun.

Really surprised to see all of the high reviews for Dr. Farrell... To be perfectly honest a majority of the questions came out of nowhere on his quizzes/exams. Best advice I can give is to get back exams as studying the PowerPoints shown in class will not help you. Asked for help with the final for office hours and was given nothing...
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Really awesome professor! I despise biology, but he made the course fun, and a little more bearable. Quizzes and exams were easy as long as you have the back exams and/or go to lecture.

He is a very funny and respectable person however for an introductory biology course, I do not think I would have done well had I not taken AP Bio previous to his class. He likes to test on current events that he mentions briefly. That being said, it is a easy class just requires note taking on what he talks about in lecture.

Dr. Farrell's passion makes even the most dull of topics interesting, to the point where it was disappointing when he ended class early. His lectures covered the material effectively and he made efforts to relate the content to other majors. Exams were fair and assignments encouraged us to think beyond the material while not being too difficult.

His exams and quizzes are very straight-forward if you actually pay attention during lecture. Lots of flexibility with attendance and homework. Exams are typically 50 multiple choice questions. Optional final exam to replace your lowest exam score. Dr. Farrell isn't the sweetest, but he was always willing to help and gave lots of hints for quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Class is not hard, but it is not easy. Quiz and test questions come from obscure moments in a video he showed once in lecture. If it is possible to take someone else do it. Overall he rubbed me the wrong way and I never felt comfortable near him. Beware, he takes his shoes off in class.

Is not helpful or accommodating to mental health issues while himself being neurodivergent, and using it as an excuse to speak poorly of and degrade students. Class is not hard, but it is not worth your time to spend with him.

Farrell seems to not underestand everyone in his class is forced to take BIOL1010. His class consists of watching youtube videos and giving multiple choice tests and quizzes on a bunch of useless biology facts. If you're looking for an easy A, go on right ahead. This class is an absolute waste of everyone's time.

Homework is due at 5 pm the day before class- this is only an issue when I have classes until 5 pm. On a few occasions, I submitted class reflections, only to see them ignored and entered as zeros. After asking about this, I was told that too much time had passed after submission & it could not be fixed- they are worth a large number of points.

Clear as to class expectations. Lectures were seldom unengaging or boring. Clearly wants his students to have a full understanding of the material so they can excel. If you pay attention in lectures, and study good notes you should do well. Quizzes often had some questions that seemingly came out of nowhere but were easy enough to do well overall.
He is very good at teaching this class and shows that he likes to teach it.

Dr. Farrell's passion for the material he teaches will be apparent the moment you enter his room. It reaches a near infectious point (says someone who's switching their focus from cybersecurity to ecology thanks to him). Lectures can be a bit drawn out but attending them is absolutely worthwhile. If you like lakes, he'll be your new best friend!

Prof. Farrell was a very good professor. His communication was clear, and his presentations are a great resource to study from. The material covered in class was also genuinely interesting. My only point of contention is that his quizzes were much harder than expected, and the questions in them were sometimes worded poorly.

BIOL-1010 is a lecture-heavy class, and unfortunately I often found Prof. Farrell's lectures to be boring and drawn-out. He is a nice person and a fair, quick grader, but I wish I had been more engaged in his class. BIOL-1010 is not a hard class, but you really need to know all details in the lecture slides. Anything in them is fair game for exams.

dr. farrell is a really funny and knowledgable guy. his lectures aren't painful to sit through, and you can tell how passionate he is about biology. it really makes a difference. i will say exams and quizzes are way more difficult than i expected. make sure to study all of the details of each powerpoint.

Farrell is super funny and sweet. Lecture wasn't particularly interesting but it was easy to follow. You don't really have to come to class but he has questions on LMS at the end you need a "codeword" for (that he shares in class). Tests and quizzes are harder than expected, be sure to review even the smaller details. Overall easy course.
Farrell is hilarious, but pretty absent minded. It's really a matter of making sure that you're on top of your own work and studying for the tests if needed. The tests/quizzes are TOUGH
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Overall, an amazing professor who puts his all in teaching a subject he very much loves.
Truly loves the class and what he's teaching. Takes in a lot of feedback and gets to know students. Can be energetic at times and excited about topics.

Awesome professor for Bio and non-Bio majors. Very clear and concise lectures, if you give feedback on what you learned in class you receive extra credit for each submission, 1-2 easy group presentations, and tests came straight from the presentation videos and back work. If you ever have to take Biology, go with this professor!

Dr. Farrell is one of my favorite professors at RPI! He's chill, funny, and nice, but also smart and really into the content which makes class enjoyable. Homework is to just read the book and exams are easy if you study. Fun research paper and presentation projects. He really cares about student feedback; if you have a concern, let him know!

Great professor! He is invested in his students and really cares about teaching. He is also easy to talk to, approachable, funny and is willing to help in any way he can. Tests were fair and came directly from powerpoints.
I love him <3
Great guy, great prof. He makes sure everyone, regardless of major, is invested in the material and he does his best at making sure you do well by giving pretty obvious hints as to what to study.

Took his biology course as a comp sci major because of a department requirement. He actually made the course material interesting. Show up, watch the quality videos he shows in class, and either read the powerpoints or listen to his lectures and you'll have an easy time.
His quizzes and exams come right from his lecture slides. Make sure to rewatch the videos he shows in class because some questions come from there too

Farrell is fantastic. His lectures are long, filled with videos, and good class notes are important, but if you get to know him he is a great guy and really cares about what his students think about his performance.

It feels like he is out to get you with everything. If your group isn't all perfect technical writers, you will have to do everything yourself, and everything really is 6 peoples worth of work. Take any other professor who will grade things more reasonably.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Lee is awesome!

Always available outside of class and is also helpful for projects and information that aren't just his assignments. He will go over the homework with you at his office hours. He goes over a back exam as a review before each test and the test is always extremely similar so it's not a difficult class if you study.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Lee is an excellent professor. I took IEA in the spring and despite the difficulty, the lectures were well structured. He knows how to explain problems and work with students so that you understand the content the best. He has an exam review the class before each test and extra office hours before exams as well. I would highly recommend him.
Really helpful, especially during office hours, really took the time to explain. Fair exams/quizzes, easy grader.

Genuinely the best professor I have had at RPI. IEA is not an easy course, but Dr. Lee made it so much better. He is very accessible outside of class, takes care to listen to his students, and genuinely wants everyone to succeed. He does review sessions before exams in class. If you can take IEA with him, DO IT, hands down the best!!

Great Prof. His lectures were clear and if something didn't click you could always rely on his office hours to be helpful. He has plenty of office hours during the semester and even adds some extended office hours before exams. Helpful during in class assignments and has no issue giving people more time to copy notes or go back to a previous slide.
He's really kind, and wants students to succeed! Dr. Lee is so nice!

Probably my favorite professor at RPI. I've taken 3 courses with him so far. He is always accessible outside of class and extremely helpful in office hours. He explains material clearly during lectures, but does rush a bit sometimes. Grading for HW and exams is strict, but he almost always gives partial credit if enough work is shown.
Professor Lee is a great teacher! He is a very positive professor and very helpful. I went to his office hours before the final exam and it was a very chill environment, he was very helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He's absolutely the best teacher ever. If I could take classes with him forever I would, I took biomechanics with him last semester and switched around my whole schedule to have him from programming this semester and is an absolute king. He's fair, honest, and always accessible outside of class, cares about his students and wants them to do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Super chill guy, he won't fail you unless you genuinely skip exams. HW and exams are hard but exams can have +25% curve so good grades quite easy. 6+ hrs work each week

Had him for comp org. He was super chill and laid back all semester. Explained concepts pretty well and always went over HW/Lab/Test solutions in class which not a lot of professors do. Curved exams with low averages and gave extra credit if you did the practice exam. Highly recommend his Comp Org class, it was a lot of fun.

Very chill professor. Gave extra credit on almost every exam for an easy task that helped you study. Prof Slota thouroughly went over every lab and homework assignment. He also highlighted the important slides for exams, which was very helpful because some lectures were confusing.
Had a fun Comp Org lecture and informative homeworks and labs. It is very clear to find information you need and the exams throughout the year were fair assessments of the content we learned.

Took graph theory last year, graph mining this year with Slota. He's by far my favorite CS professor. Great sense of humor, super chill, and lenient. Great lectures, always posted.

He's a little disorganized which is probably not great for core CS classes, but is perfectly fine for electives (tbh ideal because he'll push due dates back sometimes).

Great professor; he was a funny guy, lenient and laid back, gave extra credit, and took time during class to go through exams, hws, and labs. You'll do fairly well in his class as long as you go to his lectures and/or read the slides. There's one group project at the end that was a bit complex but all in all one of the easier cs classes I've taken.
good lecturer with notes; sometimes lectures were hard to understand but fine overall. no tests in this semester, just lots of homework.

Real nice guy, but very disorganized lecturer. His lazy style of teaching often renders his lectures near-incomprehensible, and I got the impression he didn't care much about teaching the class. Spends too much time reading simple HW instructions in class and fooling around. His tests are very easy (probably too easy).

The course itself is abstract and boring since it is about the hardware. Professor Slota did very well making his lecture fun and attractive. He is the very few professors I seen that will go over homework, labs, and exams in his lecture.
He's a good guy; I just think he's a bit disorganized. I took class asynchronously and missed a lot of assignments because there was 0 communication outside lecture videos.

Slota was okay for Comp Org. He didn't seem to really care too much about the course, nor did he seem to be fully aware of what students knew coming in. He was very approachable and helpful though if you asked questions or went to office hours. He wasn't a great teacher, but he doesn't usually teach this class so I guess he did okay.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: The professor is very good. He gives me a ideal grades

The professor doesn't know what he's teaching. He tried to prove the wrong statement in class and a student showed the counter-example, then he tried to cover his mistake by proving in a totally wrong way. The grades are 100% based on tests. And the syllabus first says tests are open book open notes, then he changed that to close books.
The experiments at the end of lecture were epic. She was a decent professor, though her handwriting is diabolical

Her lectures move very quickly and she has a pretty heavy accent that could make it difficult to understand her at times. She is a nice person and does care about her students but her teaching style and speed she moved at made it very difficult to learn and retain information.

Dr. Sharma is very knowledgeable in the course material, but fails to communicate the information to students effectively. Her accent makes it nearly impossible to understand what she is saying, and her handwriting isn't much better. Reading her notes is like deciphering hieroglyphics and she moves on the moment she finishes writing. Labs are good.

She definitely knows what she's talking about, though lectures move very quickly, so it can be hard to keep up at times. The course work isn't super hard, but some of the topics covered in the homework assignments are not in the actual curriculum.

Dr. Sharma is very intelligent and knows what she is talking about, but the lectures can get monotonous and difficult to listen to. The class itself isn't extremely challenging but the sheer amount of work that you have to do per week between ALEKS assignments and lab gets difficult.

This course is super lecture heavy. This is not my preferred method of learning, so it was quite difficult. Lab attendance and mentoring attendance are mandatory; lecture attendance is not. Sharma is sweet but I did not find her to be a good instructor.

Had Dr. Sharma for lab, she is super sweet and caring. You can definitely tell she is here to help students succeed. People say she has a thick accent, but it really is not hard to understand her at all. Plus, she makes sure people are still following along; if you need something to be repeated or did not understand what she said, she will do so!

As someone who struggles to understand accents, there's no issue with her accent as long as you're paying attention. She tries very hard to connect with her students and even took the time to give a motivational speech. She does read off the slides, but all the Chem 1 professors do that.

Sharma is a great teacher who truly cares about her students. It is her first year, so she is trying to improve her lectures and explain everything clearly. She's helpful, funny, and motivating, and her going to office hours makes a big difference. She is very understanding too. Her accent isn't bad, you can understand. 100% take her class again.

She has a very thick accent so many have a hard time understanding her. She has just started to teach a lecture after being lab teacher for a few years.
