She is still getting used to teaching a lecture, this shows as the class was a few lectures behind the other classes. Sometimes she is still teaching something that will be on the test the next day

If you have any questions, Dr. Sharma is very helpful during office hours. If you can't make it, you can send her a message on Webex. She gives out extra credit opportunities in addition to the ones already offered by the course. She also cares enough to stay after her lectures and teach for free. Study the lecture slides, it is college after all!

You will need to lock in because her lectures are quick and she moves through topics so fast you can't even say the word "chemistry" before she's started a new one. You'll also have to hear through the thick accent that she has, and her habit of cold calling people in her lab section.

Not good at teaching the content - assumes you know things that are not taught in the prereq courses. His exam questions do not match the lectures. Machine Learning from Data should be a prereq - do not take this course if you do not have a lot of ML experience. Also judgmental if you ask questions from being confused.

For some reason the class is 95 A and Gittens made multiple errors on a HW problem during office hours. Then he had the audacity to use ChatGPT to solve the problem for him. Apparently, the questions were made by DiTursi and not him, but he did not understand the content at all. He reads of Malik's slides, but doesn't get what is going on in them.

Heavy Homework. 
But it is so easy to lose points on multiple choice questions on quiz and exam. 
There are 13 homework and takes several hours every week. 
Homework will not never stop, especially there will be a homework deadline on you quiz and exam day.

Just glazes over material, left to the students to actually teach themselves. WORK IN A GROUP OR YOU WILL BE CRYING. The homework is hard and long. Tests have unfair multiple choice questions that require regurgitating definitions. Can get partial credit if you talk to him.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: The homeworks were super easy and I very much enjoyed doing them. The lectures were super informative and helpful. He was a joy to listen to, and everyone came to lecture just to watch him light up the room with his incredible personality. I loved how much partial credit he gave to make sure we understood the material. He is truly an inspiration.

This professor was extremely difficult, and did not at all teach but instead just read off the slides. Was nice enough to give you credit for questions you missed if you explained your case, which is something I HIGHLY recommend you do if you have this class with him. He had extra points for attending class because everyone kept skipping.

Professor Gittens, though not the most energetic professor, has engaging lectures for FOCS. IMO he is not best suited for this exact course, but he gets the job done. Very easily accessible via Piazza to answer questions and concerns. Gets to know the students who actually show up to lecture. Grades with partial credit. Tests reflect homework.
GOOD MAN.

Hard class, but Prof Gittens is very assessable in office hours and piazza. There was some extra credit lecture attendance and he would curve some of the lower exams, so grading seems pretty fair overall. This is not an easy class, but Gittens makes it doable.

By far the worst class I've ever taken at RPI. The lectures are so unhelpful, and the examples gone over in class are so simple, yet the homework throws you into the deep end, and makes it extremely difficult to keep up. The tests are abysmal, and the fact that getting just a few multiple choice questions wrong can ruin your whole grade is absurd.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Awful professor. His lectures consisted of slides taken from another professor with little to no explanation or elaboration. The homework assignments took several hours and had very little bearing on your grade. The exams and quizzes were heavily weighted and it was very easy to lose points on multiple choice questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very good professor, know what he is teaching and available after class.
HWs are way too long and given every week, but worth only 10%. Not enough questions on the quizzes/exams. Should give more time and more questions for them since they are worth 90%.
Homeworks are very time consuming yet worth so little to the grade, yet tests have very few questions and are worth about 90% of the grade combined
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Lots of HW problems which even the TAs often can't solve (Don't go to Office Hours until Gittens gives the TAs the solution manual). HW in general is very tedious and there is a lot of it, while only making up 10%.

Exams can be a bit rough as each multiple choice question ends up being roughly 7-8% of the test with no partial credit given.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: FOCS is a tough class so my opinion of Gittens is a bit skewed however he regularly assigns large amounts of homework (even during exam weeks), and chooses needlessly tough questions for hw and exams. The majority of exams and quizzes are after the drop deadline so there isn't a good way to know your progress to see if you need to drop.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: So far Gittens seems like he really does about his students, but he gives way too much difficult hw for it to be worth 10% of our grade. FOCS is kinda flawed since really nobody teaching it can compare to Malik's lecture videos, so it's not really Gittens' fault nobody goes to his lectures anymore. Lowkey feelsbad for him since he actually cares :(
One of the best Professors at RPI. He truly cares that his students learn from his class. He is very helpful during office hours. RPI deserves to have more Professors like him.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Fantastic professor. One of my favorites ever.
He's my favorite

Lectures were nothing more than a copy-paste from the textbook with little to no explanations. You are much better off using the textbook alone and finding the lecture videos from the other professor for this class than trying to learn from him.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Solid professor, very understanding towards student concerns, and is very willing to help. Is extremely quick to respond to e-mails and other messages outside of class.
He is a really good professor which taught me a lot about this course. He provides feedbacks in time. Whenever you have a question, you can always find him on piazza.
A joy to have in class
Very personable, great help.
GOOD MAN

The lectures consist of the Gittens rewriting a few lines from each chapter of the textbook, verbatim. His lectures offer no explanation beyond these few words. Too, gittens does not work through any examples. It is clear Gittens did not come to RPI as a professor and cares little for the students, rather came for research and is forced to teach
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Good Lecturer
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: She gives great notes and releases them after class. The home works make the class seem hard, but the tests are extremely fair and manageable.

For all the people who gave her a bad rating for how she runs her lectures, you need to rethink what a lecture is for. She is very strict towards people who are being disruptive or not paying attention, and if you're one of those people, just don't go to lecture... She explains things very well, and is very respectful if you actually talk to her.

She is a decent professor unless you get on her bad side. She will not hesitate to call anyone out for talking in class (even if you are asking a friend about the material) and God forbid you leave lecture early or try to use the restrooms “too much”. When she talks she generally speaks down to the class and has an extremely passive-aggressive tone

Attendance wasn't mandatory as lecture notes were posted
Weekly quizzes

Wants you to really learn Calculus 2 instead of just worry about exams. However, if all you care about is your grade, the exams are really straightforward, and if you get a hold of a back exam you will be fine. Lectures are not mandatory to attend, and she also posts all her lecture notes after class. She also holds exam reviews.
Great lecturer. Just don't show up late or be disruptive during lecture (easy) or you will get flamed

Kucinski is an amazing professor. As long as you do the work that she posts, both textbook questions and homework questions, they are similar to exam questions. All quiz questions that she gives out usually shows up on the exams too. She is also very easy to get along with as well.

Great teacher who knows her stuff. I skipped Calc 1 (HS credits) and felt behind at first, but caught up easily. Quizzes aren't hard—just do homework and textbook problems for practice. The class is exam-heavy, but if you do well on quizzes and homework, the exams are manageable. The final can save your grade if you struggled on midterms.

Her exams are harder than those given to other calc 2 classes, and I might fail because they count for most of your grade. Others are saying that the class is easy of you read the notes and do the homework, but this isn't true unless you're good at math already. I study a lot and still don't do good on exams. Be prepared to try hard and still fail.
As long as you respect her time and don't disrupt lecture, Dr. Kucinski is a fantastic professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: You need to show up for quizzes on the first lecture of the week (first 15 mins). She does not allow talking or using computers in class, so I typically skip the lecture. The material is easy enough, and simply reading the slides should get you an A.

Gina Kucinski is a great lecturer, pretty easy grader, but for the love of god do not say a word in her class. You can ask questions as long as they aren't stupid, unfortunately the bar is very high and her patience is very low.

Quizzes/Exams are super easy if you study. Notes are provided digitally so even if you miss class it's easy to catch up. Attendance isn't mandatory but quizzes are at the start of class once every week so you just have to show up on those days in case you don't want to go. Content easy to understand & only teaches what will show up on the exam.
This is definitely a difficult class but if you do your work and go to class it's doable. Very much you get what you put into it.
Clear lectures and fair quizzes + exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Kucinski is a great professor for Calc 2, but the class is very difficult. It combines all of a regular Calc 2 class with parts of Calc 3 and Multivar. Tests are fair but you have to study like crazy to do well on them. The class would be a lot easier if there were back exams, however, the lectures are not confusing and very helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Tests are easier than the hw, and the class is organized. Be on time though.

The best thing about her is her clear lecturing style.
Aside from that, I found her to be very passive-aggressive to students, and not great at answering questions. She also was not very accessible outside of class and seemed to delegate all other duties besides lectures to TAs.
Eh. Grade heavy, tough professor, no quizzes, and doesn't have office hours for whatever reason ?
Solid calc teacher but do not speak out of line or use your phone during class because she absolutely will call you out. She is very knowledgeable and can convey topics clearly so I liked her class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She has very clear and precise notes and goes over them in detail. Everything on the weekly quizzes was from the gradebook homework and the quizzes were easy  and helped keep me on track. The exams were the easiest of any calc 2 teacher and were the sole reason I passed the class.

Dr. Kucinski is on top of absolutely everything and knows her stuff. She provided a very up-front and direct style of teaching and communication (which I personally prefer) that made it easy to focus on the lecture. Dr. Kucinski has a very professional disposition that makes her a great professor.

Amazing lectures. She was truly one of the best professors at RPI. Calc 2 was a breeze due to the clear lectures and she would answer any questions clearly. Even if you do not attend lectures the notes are clear enough to understand on your own. The only annoying thing is that Exams make up 76% of your grade.

Gina is one of the best professors at RPI. Her class is organized and fair. She gets right to the point in an easy to understand way. Her backtests are also very relevant and helpful. I highly recommended her for Calc 2.

Very good professor, exams are weighted heavily but as long as you do and understand the homework's you'll be fine. She is a good lecturer and they are worth going to but if you don't she posts notes. She will call you out if you are on your phone or ask a dumb question but other than that she is very nice. Best Calc 2 professor at RPI.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I wish I could take another class with professor Kucinski because she is a great professor! Her lectures and notes are clear and concise. Also, her tests are a good representation of the notes, homeworks, and recitation quizzes. I highly recommend taking her calc 2 class!
Great Professor. I loved the way she taught Calc 1. She does have a lot of rules, but most of those are just basic respect.

Gina is one of the best proffesors I had. She is very caring. Class is very easy and understandable, she explains amazing and you barely will have questions because everything is very very clear. Test grading is very straight foward and they give a bunch of extra points for doing procedure

She constantly complains about how difficult her job is. It gets really annoying. She also does not care at all if something happens to you, she'll give you a 0 on any exam. Other than the fact that attendance isn't taken, she treats us like were in high school. She is a fine professor and teaches everything fine, just some annoying quirks

I had Dr. Kucinski for Calculus 2, and I will say that although harsh at times, she is a very fair grader. Her exams very closely followed the material from the homework and lectures, so if you study the material provided, you will be fine in the class. Lecture is not mandatory, but is helpful. She is definitely one of the best Calc 2 professors.

I had Dr. Kucinski for both Calc 1 and Calc 2. Calc 2 wasn't easy, but it went better than I expected! Dr. Kucinski has very solid notes on her lectures, and I appreciate the way she explains the concepts we're learning. Dr. Kucinski has some of the fairest exams I've taken personally, and I'd use the textbook and lecture slides to prepare.

Kucinski does NOT play she will call you out if you're on your computer or have headphones on. She teaches in an easy to understand way and lecture notes are clear and concise. I'm not a fan of her grading style because I lost points for stuff like "bad formatting" but all in all I enjoyed her class. Wish I had her for calc 2.

Had her for both calc 1 and 2 and was not a fan. She is passive-aggressive with students, often disturbing lectures to call people out on benign things. She will drop your lowest exam but god forbid you're sick because she gives no makeups. This is extremely unfair and encourages sick students to attend exams. Also no back exams.

Great professor; explains topics with care and thoroughness. Tests are extremely easy as long as you do your homework. Very strict on the other hand: doesn't allow electronic devices unless used for note taking, will call you out for any "misbehavior", and has a bit of a sour attitude.

I'm grateful for Dr. Kucinski's teaching style in Calc 1 this semester! As someone who never took Calculus in high school, I liked how slowly she would explain certain topics as she didn't assume everyone knew them. I'd encourage you to go to her lectures and do your best on all the Exams, as 85% of our grades this semester relied on Exam scores.
She definitely knows the material very well, I just wish she did not dock points for the format of your work and just gave you credit if you showed your work.

1)Poorly formatted lecture notes and gives extremely convoluted ways to solve problems.2) Doesn't communicate properly 1 on 1 with students, gives no guidance on exam material.3) No back exams for her class making it much harded to practice for exams while grade being 85% exam based.

Very good lecturer, everything is clear and easy to understand. Exams are also probably some of the easier ones in the math department, especially compared to others. TA was absolutely brutal grading but that is not on her.
Was not understanding at all, although lectures are good. Good professor, not great face to face.
She's a great teacher. She'd be a 5 if the course wasn't so unnecessarily hard. Definitely your best option for calc 2. Except I heard stevenson is a lot easier.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Extremely taxing class, teacher is extremely knowledgeable but her tests and homework are so much harder than the lectures. Very strict, no phones, you get called out for walking in even a minute late. 0/10
i love this lady. she's straight up, tells you wat you need to know and willing and ready to give extra help. She does not, however, tolerate laziness or apathy. come to learn or dont come at all!

Kucinski is a great professor who explains topics in extreme depth and makes sure that all of the questions asked in class are answered thoroughly. She provides a great foundation of knowledge for a topic.

Professor Kucinski is a professor who cares about her class caring. She doesn't put up with talking or laptops being out. However, she explains the material well and cares about her students. If you are looking for a professor who cares about teaching, she is a great one. If you want an easygoing one who cracks jokes... pick someone else.

She's concise, clear, and easy to understand in lectures, and teaches straight from the textbook. While attendance isn't mandatory, I highly recommend going because it improves your understanding immensely. She assigns textbook problems along with the online homework, but they aren't graded, and she'll go over them at the end of class if you ask.
Clear lectures and really good lecture notes. Very harsh on people who disrupt her lecture, though. Tests were very fair if you studied. Lots of online HW.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: clear note and teaches based on textbook so easy to learn
She grades very strictly compared to other teachers. DO NOT take her class.

Really good lectures, if you go to them and do the assigned homework and make an effort to understand it, you will do well. There are 3 exams and each is 25% of the grade, so definitely grind for them. Overall, good class.

You get what you put in. I had credit for the class from a prior institution so I didn't take the class as seriously. She is the best lecturer for math by far. For most math classes your grade is pretty much determined by exams only. If you mess up with her as a professor it's on you as she gives plenty of examples and lectures/explains well.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: She's very meticulous with her explaining and if you can focus and practice you'll do great. If you're tired, however, you are prone to start dozing off because she's not quite monotonous but very calm in tone. Her examples are the best and be sure to follow her requirements: mask up, no laptops(tablets are allowed), noise to a minimum, etc.
She is very to the point. Her lectures were easy to understand and concise. She does not give extra credit.

Great person; however, can be very mundane and monotone during lectures, not very engaging. Lectures generally only run for 80 minutes unlike the usual 110 minutes, very linear progression through course. Quizzes weekly on previous topics. Definitely know how to use the textbook to learn. HW is assigned but not mandatory.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Her lectures were very easy to understand, and her lecture notes were fantastic. I took her class twice. We moved from in person to online half way through the semester, and she was by far the most organized. I don't remember if the textbook was mandatory, but you do need to purchase webassign, because all the HW was administered through there.

Great lectures! Clear, concise, and engaging. I never regretted attending lecture-- even though it was in Eaton. Gives clear expectations on homework and exams, and if you study you'll do well in this class. She seems a little scary, but Professor Kucinski is really nice and genuinely wants her students to succeed. Great class.

Lecture wasn't mandatory and she would post lecture notes online so it was still easy to keep up with the material. A lot of the test questions come from the textbook homework not just the Web Assign homework, so if you want to do well in the class, you have to do the textbook homework. She can be pretty mean if you talk or have your phone out.

Kucinski is really nice! Even though attendance isn't mandatory, she goes over multiple examples and is very thorough. She is especially helpful if you go to her office hours. As long as you complete all the homework assignments (including textbook ones), the class will be an easy A because exam questions are the same/similar.

I first took her class for MATH 2010, but I've made several (possibly unwise) schedule decisions just so I could take more of her classes. She manages to make any material seem easy, and is always great about reviewing concepts you may have forgotten when you need them. 10/10 would take again!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Ms. Gina has the best teaching style you could ask for. Her iPad makes understanding the material easy. However, that's it. Unfortunately, she's often rude to classmates for making mistakes. Also, for some reason, her lectures make me really tired. But, they're only 50 min so just get through it and probably DON'T EVER ASK A QUESTION IN LECTURE.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Super nice and incredibly intelligent. But her lectures are not engaging whatsoever. If you like math and have razor-sharp focus, then by all means take her class. I realized that I would tune out within the first 30 seconds of the class and found more value in skipping class, reading the book myself, and asking questions at office hours.

Fantastic lectures and notes and a soothing voice. I'm taking her again for Calc II. Notes were not posted after lecture in Calc I, however they are being posted in Calc II. Going to lecture is important as she explains things very well. Be sure to be on time as she doesn't like when people are late. Laptops are not allowed unless for note-taking.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Very clear, very organized. Doesn't try and fool you with trick questions and grades on what she teaches. Very easy to talk to and very friendly!
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Best teaches Multi over Calc 1 and 2. If you want to learn the material take her class. Doing the book homework she assigns is your best friend. Asking her for help is no problem, very caring individual.

Very nice teacher, funny, clear lectures. Homeworks are not graded but is almost always must if you want to get a high score on tests (85% of the grade). Quizzes are very easy (15% of grade). Class attendance is VERY important. Sit close and focus for the 80 minute lecture twice a week and you will do much better than in the back. Also, no laptops.
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Not a bad lecturer, although her grading is really tough. Will nickel and dime you for points for small errors. Lots of webassign homework too.
Her lectures are popular, knowledgeable, and inspirational!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures--Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: If you have not taken Calc 1 before DO NOT take her. The class was taught as more of a review. She would breeze through major topics assuming everyone had already taken the class before. This made very easy material very difficult. She does have beautiful notes that were helpful. She will call people out for making any noise in class even coughing.

The best math teacher I've ever had, period! She is clear and concise in lecture, and as long as you can follow along and stay focused in class, you will easily get an A. The only reason I got a B+ was that I didn't go to the mandatory freshman mentoring sessions (RPI thing, not a Kucinski thing)

She is very friendly, unless you're on your phone, on your laptop, wearing earbuds, etc. during her lecture. You're not required to be there, as she posts all lectures online, but she goes through questions with you and breaks them down into steps.
Great professor overall. She is very good at explaining material and answers questions well. Responds to emails quickly and is very friendly.  Would recommend for calc 1 and 2.

Dr. Kucinski is one of my favorite professors at RPI. I had her for calc 1 and I just had to take her class agin for calc 2. Her lectures are incredibly clear and she posts her lecture notes online. She does a bunch of examples in her notes and the examples are often very similar to the problems on her test. Amazing teacher.

Dr.K is an amazing professor and I had her for both Calculus I and, now, Calculus II. It's definitely doable for someone to take her course and do well, but only if you show up to lecture, and do homeworks. The average grade is around a B-/C+, no curves. Most tests are based on quizzes and homeworks. Overall, she helped me improve A LOT in Math.

She is a great and helpful teacher but it feels like she spends way to much times on some simple concepts. Some how her 50 minute classes feel like hours. I would like to see her in  more difficult  content where here teaching style would be more appreciated.

She's a great teacher, and you will learn from her lectures. She gives A LOT of examples. She'll answer questions in class, but with short lectures, it's best to save most of your questions for the recitation. For those taking Calc again, you can skip lectures, or use your phone during them, or go for reinforcement. Just DON'T talk during class.
Her classes are very interesting. Quizzes are mandatory.

Very Clear during lectures and her hand writing is impeccable. She posts the notes online so you can pay attention instead of worrying about copying down mindlessly without completely understanding it. I wish she taught more upper level math courses so that I could have her again because I love her teach style and structure.

One of the better math professors I've had. She posts the notes from class online, so you dont have to worry about writing everything down. You can focus in class on understanding the material. Explains stuff very well.

Chalkboard only so you must attend and be copy thoroughly. Expect 6+ hours per weekly homework. Exams are hard but fair. He's really good at explaining and answering questions. Perfect pacing. He'll sometimes choose a random student to answer an easy question in front of class to get everyone bonus points. Thus attendance and keeping up mandatory.

Prof Henshaw is difficult. He assigns weekly homeworks and you can expect to need over 10 or 15 hours to complete them. He does not share his notes or follow a textbook for this class. You have to go to lecture to learn. If you miss class, you will regret it because he will tell you to get notes from a classmate. Would not recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Writes on chalkboard exclusively, no online notes. Luckily the homeworks follow the book nearly exactly, although there are some things that the book doesn't discuss and he only goes over in class. Material isn't  difficult to understand, but homeworks are time consuming.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: I'm an aero major so the types of problems we approached in class were outside of my comfort zone and most of my friends agree. The homeworks can take a lot of time. I found my TA immensely helpful for these assignments. The tests are reasonable in that they contain similar problems to the homework or lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Lecture is useful and not very hard to understand.

He will NEVER give your grades back. But do not worry, you'll do good in the class anyway. Very casual professor, gets along well with students and is helpful when needed. You'll notice that back exams and exams are pretty similar because he makes them at the absolute last second.

A good professor, I wish he wrote his notes but he is a helpful guy besides that. His explanations are good and the class is fair. I have no idea what my grade is. He hasn't graded a single exam at the time I am writing this.
The GOAT, enough said

GOAT mane professor, Housley is extremely knowledgeable and also a great lecturer. Grading on Exams may take longer than usual, but he is understanding and an all-out great dude. Also great for Propsys and FDL if you can take it with him; he's a super funny and interesting guy outside of lecture.
MANE GOAT, if you can take this guy for your classes

One of the best professors at RPI if you are a MANE student. Had him for aerodynamics, propulsion systems and fluid dynamics lab with clear lectures and open book exams (not quizzes though). He explains concepts in a concise, effective and memorable way; very understanding of a student's circumstances and easy to talk to.

Easily the best prof at RPI. Took him for aerodynamics and again for propulsion systems and not disappointed. As others have said he gives very good lecture notes and the quizzes are generally tame. P.S. Don't blame professors for grades being late, that's the TA's job.

Had fluids lab with him. It's the end of the semester and he did not even grade half of the reports. The quizzes he gives us are based on very random and useless information. I think he has the capacity to be a good professor but he just does not care to try. Would not recommend having him.
Highly recommended for Aerodynamics. Easily one of the clearest and best lecturers here.

I had him for Aerodynamics when he first taught it in Summer 2021.  Very straightforward open-note exams (averages were high 80s or low 90s).  Lectures were well-organized and easy to follow.  Overall, great professor.
Professor Mohamed is one of the best lecturers I have had at RPI! He cares so much about what he is teaching and is very well versed in the subjects. Definitely take this course with him if you can!

Professor Muhammed is definitely one of the best professors I have had at RPI. Class is hard, but he will make it very understandable; tests are very fair, and everything is in the lectures. He cares about the students so much, definitely like a father. If you can take a class with him, do it. Love him so much

The nicest professor I have had at RPI. Extremely empathetic and caring. Has a lot of fun stories from his earlier career too. Lecture slides are busy but he wants you to understand the big picture and actual applications, not just memorize formulas. The first part of the class is hardest, don't be discouraged because it gets better from there.

One of the best professors at RPI! He is an extremely good lecturer and will make everything entertaining. He is also a very nice person and gives really good advice even outside of class, helped me out a lot with career stuff.

Had him for 2 classes, both were excellent. His extensive real-world experience shows in his lectures and adds a lot to the course, especially in prod dev. Grading criteria is confusing but I mostly blame the TA for that. Take a course with him if you can.

Professor Mohamed is one of the real gems of the BME program. He is extremely caring, passionate, and involved in his classes. You can tell that he really loves Biomedical Engineering and even goes off on inspirational tangents to motivate students. He is just great and I wish he could teach all my classes.

Dr. Mohamed is one of the best professors I've ever had in my academic career. I HIGHLY recommend him for any class, every class. I've had him in-person and online, but during the COVID-19 pandemic, he was one of the most caring professors, and completely re-did his class setting to cater to us. 100% the absolute best.

THE NICEST PROFESSOR EVER! Had him for product development and he was so caring. Definitely should talk to him one on one. Grading can be a bit unexpected but he prefers you to be succinct and to the point. Definitely recommend.

From what I understand, the class structure was 'given' to Professor Han, and he was working to improve it, so it was not his fault. As for himself, he gave good lectures and gave fantastic answers to questions. He was very understanding with deadlines and expected work, and overall the class was graded very leniently. VERY knowledgeable as well!

Poor lecturer. Hw grading is brutal (3 attempts, randomized numbers each time, answers must be accurate to 3 decimal points or no credit. Best score is NOT what goes in the gradebook - your most recent attempt does). Never enough time in-class for most labs. At LEAST 6-8 hrs of work a week.

Amazing Professor, and very caring and knowledgeable. His lectures are somewhat hard to follow due to his accent and tech issue throughout the semester (projected a tablet screen via doc-cam...), BUT he is a very approachable and caring professor, and cares that the students learn the material. Taking him again for another course.

EI is a lot of work. All labs and projects are done in groups. Exams are very long and hard. One thing I didn't like was that the exams are graded significantly based on accuracy, so small mistakes can kill you. But overall, Han is a great guy, and I think he did his best to make the class reasonable while staying within the curriculum guidelines.
tough grader but very accessible and cares a lot about his students

He is very difficult and loves to talk, but a really nice guy. He is a good professor and loves it when you ask questions. The design projects are annoying but very beneficial. The exams and homework are graded unfairly, but as long as you do well on the design projects, you will be okay.

Dr. Hedden is a really nice person and an entertaining professor. He's very knowledgeable and is willing to help me in other classes. He definitely cares about his students and likes when people are working hard. I also took his Polymers class over summer and really enjoyed it. Would definitely recommend taking Ron's class

Hedden is the GOAT, he will make an effort to know your name and is very personable, and he encourages help outside of class. He also just knows his stuff, very smart. Overall, really good professor and mentor in the CHME department.
thorough and theory focused

Dr. Hedden is a lecturing professor at RPI so he spends his time with students-not research. He is very accessible by email, and great to talk to in person. He is a real straight shooter and a great professor to ask advice from. I have taken CPDC with him but he teaches a number of classes now and seems very knowledgable across all ChemE

I have absolutely ZERO clue what my overall grade could be with 2 weeks left. He does not use LMS. Additionally, his heavy accent makes lectures extremely difficult to understand (this seems to be a reoccurring trend at this school). I hope RPI reevaluates who it has teaching its students because this is just absurd.
reviews.rating_tags: Hilarious--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Does not use the LMS. CLASS HAD NO SYLLABUS. Lectures are overly broad and indecipherable due to thick accent. Handwritten feedback illegible. A pile of rocks could do a better job at teaching this course.

I saw his ratings that were posted a long time ago so wanted to give him a try, hoping he has improved as I was really interested in Transportation overall. But, boy! I was wrong! It's difficult to keep up with his lecture due to his thick accent. Lectures were not interesting at all. Wouldn't recommend taking his class!

Trans Plan Systems - Jose is a tough professor. Little hard to understand accent. I really wanted to take this class as i love Transportation. However this class was poorly organized. Midterm was a day before Thanskgiving. The class is way too theoretical! Very dry class and you can do better taking other Transport classes not with Jose!
Very Knowledgeable professor.
He made the TA do everything, and then changed the grading breakdown after the final grades were done
Professor was very unclear when it came to class.  He changed the grading policy at the end of the course without notifying the students.  He could learn english and keep students in the know.

Extremely helpful and very interested in helping students.  He did give out a couple of unreasonable tests, but he knows his mistakes and will improve upon them for future years.  It is tough to listen in class with his accent, but he makes up for it by bringing in many guest speakers.
No Comments

Bram is probably my favorite professor at RPI. He's so funny and his energy is just so fun to be around. Intermediate logic is an extremely hard course (at least it was for me) and the grading on the group homeworks is a bit harsh, but overall Bram is just an amazing professor. There are no exams/quizzes, only homework and a final course project.
Bram is a funny guy and a great professor. His lecture slides can tend to get a bit boring, however his energy and jokes make up for it.

Great class with a knowledgeable teacher. The assignments were challenging and there were only 6 major ones, so your grade felt really dependent on those. A lot of the work was group-based. Despite that, I appreciate how the course sparked my interest in Cognitive Science, and I'm considering it for my focus.

Professors Bram and Milanese are so kind. I would be happy to have them again but did not enjoy the class in a content perspective. I thought it would be technology impacts on the world but it's a philosophy/critical thinking class. If you enjoy that I recommend the class, it just isn't my cup of tea. Class was also 5 assignments, all groupwork.

Had Bram for both IFL and critical thinking. Overall engaging lecturer for two interesting and complementary classes. Logic is very challenging, proof related homeworks took me about 10 hours a week and 40% of your grade is distributed between just four 3-6 question quizzes. Would, however, still recommend him for it over Bringsjord.
Love this guy. His lectures are super fun and engaging, I'm lucky to have had him as my professor and my introduction to the world of formal logic!

Bram is a good professor who is passionate about what he teaches. He makes class fun and engaging. However, a large majority of your grade is group projects and it significantly affects your grade if your group mates don't do their part. Bram will try his best to help you if this is the case but he can only do so much.
Bram is a super funny guy. Overall, a great person and teacher. He makes class interesting and it was surprisingly a fun class and I got way more out of it than I was expecting.

Professor Bram is excellent. He has a very deep knowledge of the material, and is clearly extremely passionate about the course and its content. Occasionally he overexplains things, so you may find yourself zoning out. However, altogether he's a superb professor for Logic. Only graded items are homeworks and quizzes, both of which are easy.
He is very responsive, replies quickly to emails and Webex messages. The quizzes are 40 minutes long, which isn't much time for 10+ questions. Overall, he's very nice and enthusiastic.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Bram, as he likes to be called, is an engaging and interesting professor. Very passionate about what he teaches and that shows in his lectures. Often times there are videos or class participation so he is not just talking at you. Weekly quizzes reflect the lectures. I appreciate that he gave us essentially free rein for final project.

Bram is great. The more you participate the more you will learn from him. He does try to work in group activities a lot, but overall they are pretty painless if you put in a decent amount of effort. He tries to get to know his students outside the classroom and seems like a genuinely sweet person (his office hours are great)!

Bram is a very nice professor, who is clearly passionate about the class. There is barely any homework, but there are a couple group projects, including a presentation, and a paper, and he grades fairly. Minds and machines is definitely not just AI, but he makes some of the topics interesting in class and lecture.
He is really nice and gives great lectures
The professor is really nice but the assignments are pretty hard.
Great professor.

Very concise in his lectures and very helpful when it comes to homework and project feedback. Grading is lenient for the class, but it does require some effort. One problem I had is that during lectures, I struggled to keep my attention during lectures both online and in person, and I wish he adopted a more impassioned lecture style like John.

I didn't want to take this course until I saw Bram was the teacher but now I'm so glad that I did. He's a fantastic lecture prof and you don't even feel like you're being lectured at because everything he says is so genuinely interesting
Spend 5 minutes with the guy and you'll want to be a cog sci major.
Professor Bram challenges you to think critically and evaluate things logically. This was framed by the search for sentient robots.
Bram's lectures are engaging and he's always available during office hours or after class. He is well informed of the subject matter.

Bram is one of the best professors I've ever had.  His passion for the topics he teaches is contagious.  He's also just a really interesting guy! Absolutely take one of his classes if you can, and try to get to know him a bit too!  His classes are super interesting and a good break from the norms.
Bram is quite enjoyable to have as a professor. He is very entertaining when explaining new concepts and provides clear criteria for essays.

I've had Bram twice: once for Minds and Machines and once for Intro to Cognitive Science. In both classes he's awesome, entertaining, funny, and teaches interesting course material. Get into a class of his if you can.

Bram's an amazing professor.  Intermediate Logic (PHIL 4140) isn't as fun with him as Minds & Machines or Critical Thinking--it's his first semester teaching it, and Intermediate Logic is mostly about proofs, proofs, proofs rather than logic puzzles or more abstract logic--but I'd recommend any class he teaches.
Professor is good, sometimes hard to pay attention to some of the material. Be prepared to write some essays about topics that are not always the most interesting.
He's definitely one of the most fun professors. I had him my first semester in Minds and Machines and the course was relatively easy. He's interesting, funny, and knowledgeable.
My cognitive thought is that he is dreamy

Bram's awesome, but his Intro to Logic class is too easy. His other classes are more difficult. The question with blue eyed/brown eyed people is not a trick question. The Oracle speaks once and then disappears. You die an excruciating death if you are wrong about your eye's color on boarding. There's no sneakiness to it. It's just a logic question.

He knows what he is talking about. I mostly went to lecture to do the homework in class. The textbook is really helpful and go to the TA for help on homework. If you do practice problems you should do fine on quizzes. His online notes are useful. Going to class is optional, but I would go and do other work while half listening. He uses every minute
Excellent Teacher.  One of the best I've ever had.  Highly recommend for any class.

His teacher is just amazing!!! He is different (in a funny way) and he once let us out to have class outside on a hill. For the final project, he let some of us work on building and programming robots to solve puzzles! I will take as many of his classes to fulfill my Humanities + elective requirements
Bram rocks! Really easy class and he let us go outside for lecture sometimes.  Discussions were enjoyable.  Plus he learned everyone's names in less than two weeks.

This is a very easy class.  If you took discrete math, or had any formal logic proofs in high school, just show up for the lectures which introduce Fitch and you will be fine.  I didn't attend class 90% of the time and I got an A.
Good Professor, very clear and you don't have to go to the lectures, but they would probably help.
Very helpful when material becomes tough...2 extra help sessions brought me from thinking I would have to drop it to getting an A in the course and final exam.

Bram is the BEST teacher in the history of the world.  He has a box, and he gave me A's even though I didn't do jack.  I slept during most of the classes and was wicked annoying.  Also, he's hilarious and awesome.  Take any class he teaches.
Circular! Answered right answer too early, told me I was wrong until the end, where he concluded the same thing I said an hour earlier.
it's so easy... but sooo hard to care. dry dry dry. zzzzzz... i'm bored again.
made class fun and interesting
Funny guy, explains the material well.
Bram is one of the most helpful teachers i've had. He has a great way of explaining concepts and all three of the classes i've had with him have been great.
Interesting lectures, but the subject is such that you won't learn it from them.  Probably not Bram's fault.
first 10 weeks were repeat of hs - only thing i didn't care for was attendance requirement
I hated this class, nothing seemed to make any sense, and it was a logic class. I found the material more difficult to grasp than some of my Engineering classes....unfortunately.
Bram's got a box!!! His class was interesting and fun.
I was expecting to absolutely love the class, but I find it kind of dry - but maybe that's just me.  Be prepared to feel like an outsider if you are not Comp Sci, Comp Sys Eng, or just a plain nerd

By far, one of the most interesting and provocative classes I've ever taken.  Almost nobody in the class can stay quiet for the entire session, because you get so involved.  Oh, and do the reading--it's REALLY interesting.  Lastly, Bram ROCKS.
an excellent prof. we should have more like him, or make copies =P (ask him, he'll debate the copy-a-person thing for hours)
funny professor, good class, very easy if you are naturally smart
Take Logic with him. Easy grades, interesting class.
Bram is da bomb!!!!!!!!
No Comments
nice working on legos with him :o)
A genuine human being. Quite rare to find here at RPI.

Dr Traver is an absolute GEM. Taking a class under this woman is the most enlightening experience, I swear it should be a graduation requirement across the entire school. If it weren't for her, RPI would be a much darker place.

Dr. Traver is a great Social Psych professor. The 5 quizzes throughout the semester were fair. Despite the difficulties of Cengage, the textbook was a good read, and the homework was easy. Come to lectures! Lectures are very engaging and worth your time.

Prof is filled with personal stories and is constantly positive. The quizzes are very do-able and all assignments are super fair and no stress. Prof is basically just forcing you to notice the positives in your life. I recommend you take this class even if you don't have to.

Traver really cares about what she teaches and that shows in lecture. She does get off track and repeat herself a lot which can be tiring. Also, the quizzes are more difficult and scenario based than expected, but most of the class is based on in class activities that you can make up if you miss them, so it was easy to get a good grade.
Pretty easy class, definitely don't underestimate the quizzes, they were much more difficult than expected. Professor Traver is nice, but often brings up a lot of her own stories when lecturing.

Dr. Traver is a terrific professor. Lecture material is useful, homework is interesting and not difficult, occasional quizzes are more than fair, and you get to choose the books you read for the book club. A nice break from a hectic RPI schedule, and teaches you how to truly appreciate the world around you. Take this class!

I loved the course content and I especially loved having Professor Traver. She's incredibly understanding and empathetic. The quizzes are pretty easy because she'll tell you what exactly will be on the quizzes during her lectures. I found the assignments enjoyable and not overwhelming. This class is a nice break from all the other hectic courses!

Dr. Traver is the most outgoing professor you're going to have. She has plenty to say no matter what time of day, some relevant and a lot of personal anecdotes, but all interesting regardless. Positive Psych pretty easy just study for the quizzes and show up to class! Random attendance will kill your grade if you miss it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I took this class in the summer and taking it over the summer enhanced the class experience. She tries to lecture in a way that is not overwhelming, makes it engaging, and makes the material easy to understand by making it personal to each individual. Take this class with professor Traver as it is a must take at RPI.

She teaches lots of communication intensive courses and most are easy A's. If you show up and listen, then there's no problem. She keeps class as enjoyable as possible. Other people don't normally like her too much because of her stories, but I enjoy that she shares and listens unlike other classes and professors. Like I said, easy A.

Her positive psychology is very useless. She always like to tell boring story with her daughter which has no help to class. What's more, she has no sympathy for the students' suffering. Instead, she takes the students' miserable manager as a verbal example. Even her neighbors she likes to gossip in class.
She is a very nice person and cares about her students.

I can't say enough about Professor Traver. She is one of the most passionate and driven professors I've ever had. Professor Traver truly wants to teach and influence her students in a positive way. She is a fantastic resource to have in the school and she is incredibly wise.

I had Dr. Traver for positive psych and she has been the light at the end of the tunnel for a lot of us in the class. She genuinely cares for everyone, whether you care or not. She understands us and works with us. Her assignments and tests are very easy and actually beneficial if you put the effort in. I am looking forward to having her again!

More like an English class than a psychology class. I found myself having to search up a word on every slide. Will say the content of the class is good, the way it's taught is more complicated than it should be, hindering the full potential of learning.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Super easy to pass positive psych. I was not a fan of her teaching style. It seemed like she was never actually prepared for class and she can be kind of preachy. That said, at any time you can shoot her an email or go to her office hours, she's very approachable and will work with you if you are struggling.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Super easy to get an A as long as you do the assignments and look over the slides before the tests. The assignments are very easy and typically don't take much time. The lectures are interesting. It's a material light psych class.

Dr. Traver is great, friendly, and inspirational. While the content of this course (I/O psych) isn't the most interesting for me at least, her lectures make up for it. She frequently uses relevant examples and sometimes tells inspirational stories from her own life. The assignments are very easy, but the quizzes require memorization of the slides.

Prof. Traver's, Positive Psychology is one of the best classes I've taken at RPI. If you truly listen and do the assignments, there is no way you will not enjoy this course. She is a wonderful human being that truly cares about her students and is very lenient with HW extensions. You don't really need the Positive Psych textbook, PPT's are enough.

This was one of my favorite professors at RPI. She really wants every student to learn and succeed. She also genuinely cares about every student's well being and mental health. I looked forward to going to her class every day because she is so positive and her lectures were easy to follow.

She's awesome. Use her study guides and you'll be fine. She tells pretty interesting stories in lecture but attendance isn't mandatory. The exams aren't hard and she is happy when everyone does well on them! Also lots of easy ways to boost your grade.

She gives study guides before each quiz, so if you fill those out using the power points that she posts online or the textbook, you really don't need to come to class. It is very interesting material though, and she tries to have good discussions but most kids don't participate.

I had her for positive psyc.  Very easy psyc course.  No textbook was necessary.  Just do her study guide based off of the lecture notes she posts.  Just don't forget to turn in mini experiments and such, she basically always gives 100% on those experiments.  You don't have to do that well on the tests to still get an A in the course.

Traver is awesome! She is so sweet and always gives real word examples while teaching. If you just study the Power Points, you will most likely get an A. She is an easy grader on essays and projects, even letting you redo it if you didn't do it right. Very big on soft deadlines. Definitely recommend taking a class with her!

The main problem with her Cog Psych class is knowing Too much before you take her class, or studying too much and knowing the material.  If you knowdo either of these 2 things, her quizzes get increasingly difficult.  Poorly worded, ambiguous quizzes.  People who skip class and study the question bank usually get the best letter grade, sadly.
Gives occasional extra credit, easy grader, quizzes aren't very hard.  Pretty easy class overall.
Loved Prof Traver, really easy class

I spent 3 hours of my Sunday before finals completing her extra credit and then was not given my points. Therefore she gave me a B when I should have had a B+. I also had to email her more than 3 times before she responded about being given my points and she has still not added them to my grade. She said "talk to me next semester".

Prof. Traver is not a bad prof, she sometimes has some very useful info. But you can't trust what she says in class, for instance she will tell you if you are busy you can ask her for an extension, and she will typically grant it. That is not true, she very rarely grants extensions and you will most likely waste your time sending her the email.

Professor Traver... where to begin. While she is a very kind lady, she is not meant to be a professor. I took her course, hoping to learn about psychology, and left the semester feeling confused and as though I hadn't learned anything. She didn't have grading rubrics for presentations/papers so you don't know where you stand. Study the powerpoints.
Study the textbook and u'll do fine. She tends to talk about her life often but I can't blame her. It's easier for her to come up with psych examples from her real life experience I guess.

Class is boring but very easy-Powerpoints from lecture are posted to LMS, reading those + skimming the assigned reading is enough to get by. Occasional feminist rants. The course itself is a joke, she makes the occasional useful insight when she's straying from course material.
She's an alright professor. Teaches straight out of the book so buy the book and read it. Should be an easy A/A- if you read. Class averages are usually around 32/40 on the exams.
Boring class, and final poster project reminded me of a 5th grade show and tell on who you're favorite leader was.
Very interesting class. Make sure to keep up with the material and you will do well.

PD II with Traver is all about Feminism. She'll use a lot of samples about herself, and will take any comment/suggestion to heart if you don't say it exactly right. It was supposed to be Leadership, but she makes it clear that's not her goal. Memorize her notes because that is what's on your quiz. Don't plan on getting much out of the class.

Had this professor for Cognitive Psychology. Sometimes gets off track during lectures, but nice and easy to listen to. Very understanding when it comes to the students, I made a scheduling mistake that conflicted with an exam and she allowed me to retake it when most professors would not have done the same. Tests were slightly harder than expected
Lectures were amusing and kept me awake, but I honestly grew tired of all the talk about prejudice and whatnot. This is a class on leadership theory, not the civil rights movement.

She only uses examples that are excessively feminist, and constantly complains about not liking to be told what to do.  Tests are difficult and require reading the textbook and memorizing to get higher than an 85, but everyone gets 100% on the posters, which evens out the class.  Better than the alternative PDII courses, just don't go to class.

Had her for cog. psyc. Her tests were mostly out of the book, so if you don't read then you probably won't get higher than a B+. Easy course, the lectures were right out of the book, and theres no HW, just one presentation, very easy 4000 level course

she's awesome. had her for cognitive psych. her stories are interesting and always tries to relay them to what we're studying (and usually does it sucessfully). she's very nice to talk to if you have personal issues too outside of class.

Horrible lady. Her stories are inchoerent and have nothing to do with the material. Sometimes they are depressing: like the time her friend's dad was shot and her husband went on a month long manhunt to kill the killer.  She talks about last night's American Idol every class.  If she wore a whale suit to class, I wouldn't know the difference.

Hates men. All managerial examples use females as the default. This is incorrect writing and very distracting to the reader, as any good writer knows. That having been said, her biases probably won't affect your grade and the course is easy.
No Comments
Easy to understand. Fair. Interesting. Keeps you awake in class.

Abnormal Psychology is a great course. Professor Traver made the class really informal, but informative. She's the type of professor you want to keep talking with after class is over. The material is interesting and stuff everyone in our society should know about those with psychological disorders.

This PD2 is way better than the STSS one. She has taught this one so much that she forgets what she mentioned in our class and assumes she told us. I'm mainly kept awake in class.  Good class for the lack of homework and only 2 tests and 1 paper and 50 elaborations.

A really nice lady who knows her stuff. The class got boring at times, but she has a decent amount of interesting stories that are quite relevant to the course material. The tests are on exactly what is covered in class, and the grading system in general is very fair.

Stupid class.  I think she's frustrated teaching it, and it comes accross clearly.  Waste of time.  You either know how to work with other or you don't.  You're not going to learn it in a 1 credit class.
she is on a wicked power trip. she is a man hater. the class is easy yet it sucks.
Can't blame her for having to teach a required course.
Worst psych teach i've had. Has serious power trip issues, or as she would call it, serious need for "personal power".
Thickheaded.  She says how women are steriotyped, then stereotypes them herself, and says its ok because its just a 'generalization.'  That's what stereotypes are stupid ****.
Boring material, but a good instructor.

Airhead, plain and simple.  She (along with the entire PD staff) teach a one sided view of how to conduct yourself in the real world.  Her PD2 class is so boring and so easy.  I strongly suggest taking it but get **** before to pass the time.
Understands what PD2 is and makes it great. Worth going to, even. Easy grades -- almost kindergarten at times! Take this version of PD2.
Incoherant at times, useless class
No Comments
a little out of it sometimes, but generally ok
This teacher makes the class interesting!

Didn't explain the slides well AT ALL. Made me redo labs for "finishing too fast". Gave horrible advice on how to do better on exams. She told our class to focus on deep breathing. Oftentimes wasn't helpful at all. Also the test had VERY FEW back questions unlike in previous years where the entire exam were back questions.

Good professor: doesn't rush through lecture slides, understanding, and very friendly. Personally, the lab activities didn't help me with understanding the content but that's a problem with the course itself. I relied heavily on the online textbook and back exams to get a thorough understanding of the content.
Reasonable amount of homework. Okay lecturer. Tests are standardized so it's the same for everyone, just do the back tests.

Aggressively competent in what she teaches. Very on top of things. Fair and accommodating if you are struggling on something or need a little more time. I enjoyed going to her class, which is saying a lot considering it was at 8 am.

I had Wilke for Honors Physics II Spring 2016.  She's underrated.  Very nice, straightforward person. She helped me a lot outside of class.  Very tough grader and expects a lot from her students.  Do the work, and do well.

Wilke really does try her best.  She communicates clearly despite her heavy German accent, and she'll help you if you ask for it. Physics I is a tough class, and you're gonna have some trouble.  Don't blame it on her though; she's doing all she can.  Also, she writes her "m"s weird and has some strange pronunciations, but they're easy to deal with.
8 in the morning makes it tough to stay awake, along with the style of the class.  Long derivations done out in class don't relate much to the homework or exams.

Last year was her first year teaching I-Mech, so I anticipate that in future years, her methods will improve. She taught straight from the textbook, and she writes the letter 'm' and 'n' with one extra hump, but other than that, the class was very easy(with no prior mechanics save physics I) and the hwk can be looked up online if you get stuck.

Don't know how this professor ended up teaching when she can't even solve simple physics problems. She spends too much time on unimportant parts of the lecture and then rushes over the important part. She loves to force people to attend the class for the whole 2 hrs even if you are done with all observations. She's not one to look forward to.
I'm not sure whether it's her or the subject that makes this course so dry.  Taking it at 8:00 AM at Carnegie may have added to the suffering.  She knows what she's talking about though.

So it seems like she's better at Graduate classes.  The class she taught was right out of the book.  You can basically get the same information from reading the book and some outside research.  Homework can be tedious at times, but isn't too hard conceptually.  Same with exams.  The examples are organized, and she does explain them.  Not horrible.

Expect to use your textbook a lot with Wilke's class. Almost everything she puts on the board is out of the book, along with hw and exam problems. She spends most of the time with examples instead of the core material. Read the book before class or else you won't learn much.
She did an excellent job covering the derivation from Jackson. Her final was a little rough, but other than that, she was a great teacher

boring class, but very organized and good notes given. sometimes she does a whole class where you break into groups to solve problems, which is a nice change. exams were hard, but reasonable. homework is reasonable considering its a grad level class.
You have to know German she tends to slip into her mother tongue...
really nice, and tries to help you as much as she can, but she is really really boring.  there is probably a better teacher out there for this class.
good class, very methodical in her teaching. good note-giver. difficult midterm exam. homework is semi-reasonable to difficult.
Terrible avoid at any cost

His quiz are stupid and nonsense
Learn nothing from his class

Very awful professor send notification in the middle of night tell student there will be quiz in the next day without tell ahead of time.
You need to expected that listen to his nonsense lecture for one hour in the early morning and the attendance is require.

Decent Professor for this course. Several things stood out to me, such as how lecture heavy the course is and how exams make up around 75% of the course grade. This Professor, however, does not upload Problem Set answers, refuses to upload back tests, usually holds you for 1.5 hours or more, and does not upload written notes. Would not recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof Chadd goes over slides in lecture and has few iclicker questions which are doable if you pay attention. The problems explained on slides are different than the ones on the hw. Gives out about five hw assignments over the semester but allows limited number of submissions per hw. Three exams and no final. Class before tests are for exam review
Great, easy going professor, easy for A. May be hard to actually get learning about certain things, but ask if you are really interested.

He is very enthusiastic, helpful, entertaining and easy going, he gives great feedback and make sure everybody feels good about what they've made. To be honest, I wish this class is harder, more group projects and homework would be way more helpful. The content of this class feels disappointingly shallow, the history part is interesting tho.
Igor is very enthusiastic, helpful, entertaining, and easy going. The cares passionately about the subject and it shows. Great class overall, would highly recommend.

Took Hacktivism with him in Fall 2015.  He's a unique teacher with a lot of enthusiasm, not to mention a lot of connections with others who are doing very interesting things.  His class can tend toward being overly unstructured but there's a potential to get a lot out of it, especially if you're not accustomed to taking disussion-based classes.

Here's what you do for the entire semester: make a short film. Like 5 minutes. You don't HAVE to go to class, but Igor is awesome so you'll want to go to class. Go to some classes, help people with their videos, and make an okay video and you'll get an A.
I love his video class, and he's awesome.
Great Professor, interesting ideas and keeps class entertained.
extremely interesting chap
cool guy take the course

Igor is the best teacher I had at RPI.  I would venture to say every student, regardless of major, should take a class with him.  I found every othe teacher in the EMAC department to be useless except for Igor.  Keep up the good work, buddy!
Cool teacher, cool guy, great class
No Comments
Igor is one of the coolest professors at RPI!
No Comments

Solid professor. Posts lecture notes and solutions to the homeworks, class activities, and exams. Hosts a review session outside of class before each exam. Exams are comprehensive but fair. The guy himself is pretty chill. Asks students for feedback and is willing to answer questions. Homework assignments are short. Not the best lecturer though.

Micro is a tough class. Your grade is really dependent on how much effort you put into the class. The professor was only accessible if you made an effort to see him. Once you make that effort, he'll help you with whatever you need

Classes are a lecture for the first half and then an activity for the second half. The activities are great practice and really help prepare you for the tests. Tests are very fair and cover the material --he doesn't really try to trick you on the problems. He really cares and will go around the class to make sure students understand the material.
Lecture was clear but about 50% review of previous lecture. Kept lecture interesting and much better than any substitutes that lectured.
No Comments

Nice guy and a pretty good professor, knows the material well but sometimes gets tripped up explaining things in the large lecture hall.  A little hard to understand at first but that gets better, and many stop attending class so it's easier to hear and pay attention after a while.  Tests are fair, and you're allowed to make your own crib sheets.
No Comments
Good professor, very helpful. Explains concepts in a clear manor.
You get a little used to the accent.  Lectures are boring, but if you pay attention, you'll do fine.

I took this class fall-25 (my first semester). He makes the class very easy (87.5/100 or 70/80 is an A). 8 ish quizzes and 3 tests. the quizzes are just homework problems (no number changes) and the tests are the same as back tests (with number changes). No attendance req. Great prof as well.

Prof Holmes is one of the best professors I've had at rpi. He's a great lecturer, is very organized and consistent, and he chose the order of topics quite thoughtfully, for our sake. Grading was largely exams, plus semi-weekly quizzes that were very easy as long as you did at least some of the (optional and ungraded) textbook homework.
Pretty engaging as a lecturer, basically makes it impossible not to get an A in his class.

Professor Holmes is a great lecturer and very engaging. There's very few safety nets in this class- it's 75% tests and 25% homework quizzes, no scaling or grade dropping. He posts all his notes online afterwards. He wrote the textbook he teaches from. Good class.

Mark Holmes is an amazing professor. He makes the class as easy as possible: the quiz's are exact homework problems, and the tests are as straightforward as possible. If you are able to take diffeq with Holmes you should, his lectures are interesting and enjoyable, and if you do the homework (which is not much) you will do very well in the class.

He's very aware of his role as a professor and what it entails. There's no B.S. in his class, and his lectures and tests are only on what's going to help you in the future. He's very down-to-earth and is an excellent teacher.
Honestly a great professor. Easy to learn and the quizzes were good.
There are weekly quizzes, but there is no final exam. The material is hard but he does a good job explaining it.

The grading criteria for this class is very clear; extremely test/quiz heavy. The quizzes are taken directly from the suggested problems list and the tests are extremely similar. Lectures are good; He is very knowledgeable and makes it as easy as possible to get an A(an average of 70/80 or 88% is an A).
This Guy is goated, Wrote the textbook and has a simple syllabus to make your life easier

All the quiz questions are taken from the textbook problems, so if you do the homework, it's easy to do well on quizzes. The lectures are okay, but I found the textbook very helpful for learning content.

Holmes is a very knowledgeable guy. His exams and quizzes are exactly like the back exams and homework problems. Nothing is a surprise. Lectures can be a little boring and he likes to go on the same tangent about covid every other week. My only major issue was that the small lecture hall made cheating on exams and quizzes rampant.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: You can really tell that he cared about teaching the class in an effective way that made sure students understood the material, without pounding them with work or super difficult exams. 10/10, would take again if given the chance.
Very Fair Professor. He wrote the textbook and make everything clear. Although there is no graded HW, he makes up for it by having the quizzes and test just like the optional HW.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great Professor, a must-take for differential equations. Tests are exactly like the quizzes with a few numerical changes, and the quizzes are exactly like the problems assigned.

He is definitely very accomplished and a good teacher. Although I definitely don't like his grading system. He only gives A's, B's, and C's, with no + or - it's really frustrating because instead of getting a B-, you'll get a C, even if you're very close to a B. Because he's older, he gets angry easily and can be intimidating, but he's nice person.

- His lectures are optional but are super helpful
- Fast response time
- Quiz questions are all taken directly from the textbook, and test questions are always comparable in terms of difficulty
- No grade modifiers, no curves, no dropping the lowest score, only quizzes and tests are graded, no final exam
- Anything above 87.5 counts as an A
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Teaches to the textbook, which is great when he's the one who wrote it! Dr. Holmes teaches Diff Eq like it's one of the easiest math courses out there, and with him, it kind of is. Weekly quizzes and three exams which are all fair, no final, and no homework. Is very clear about class expectations. He's sometimes hard to follow in lecture.
Took MATH 1900 w/ him but this man is I think genuinely one of the last few competent professors and advisors at this school. If you're a math major and ur advisor sucks switch to this guy.

Useful stuffs. 
Amazing lectures. 
Easy tests and homework.

Professor Homles's lecture is amazing, he is very knowledgable. 
His textbook is very clear as well, if you read through the textbook, it is easy to follow and refresh your understanding from the lecture. 
Tests and homework are very easy to get full credits as well.
Also, 70/80 is a A in his class.
He is good at explaining the theory behind differential equations and he goes at a pace appropriate for anyone even if they don't have experience with difeq.
Trust me, Prof. Holmes is the goat. If you can do the Homework you can get a 100% on each test. This Prof. response time is literally within minutes of you reaching out.
Altogether a great professor--one of the best at Rensselaer.  He is extraordinarily knowledgeable and excellent at communicating the course material.

Holmes' class is dead easy. His Quizzes are VERBATIM from the suggested problem sheet. No HW's, and optional classes/recitations. And the Exams are the same format as the suggested problems but with different numbers. No modifiers (+/-) but since the A is an 87.5% that's more of a benefit than a curse. Optional final as well.

Holmes has the best approach to teaching I've seen in a long time. He teaches diffeq while convincing us it is actually really easy. He wrote the textbook and its one of the best textbooks I've ever read. If you can, take any math class you can with him. No +/- on grades but quizzes are copy paste textbook problems and exams are more than fair.

Fantastic lecturer, best prof I've had so far, very entertaining in lecture. Explains practical applications to make the theory more understandable. Strange grading system but very advantageous for students. Checks online class forum frequently. Homework not required but strongly recommended; same with recitation attendance. Go to lectures!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Good calc prof, his lectures weren't the most engaging and he often added unnecessary material but he still made it clear what would be on exams. There was no HW requirement so the entire grade was based on weekly quizzes and the 3 midterm tests. He did give non required hw and the quiz questions came directly from those problems (same numbers).
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Holmes is the perfect prof if you want a no surprises course. Weekly quizzes are copy pasted from the recommended problems assigned for each textbook section (optional). Exams are also copy pasted from the textbook but with numbers changed around. The only thing you may not like is that he does not do +/- on grades, it's either an A or B.
Very engaging lectures, funny guy

I am trying to retake the course this summer, which is by the other professor who also teaches 4800 in rpi. Holmes' textbook is written as confusing as possible. Comparing to the 4800 I m having now, the teacher is actually explaining things, and the textbook have a lot of examples. These classes are teaching the same things, but Holmes is not good

He knows his material and is able to relate it to various fields of study so you know why you're taking the class. His lectures are engaging and as long as you show up and pay attention you'll do fine. The quizzes are questions word for word from the homework. Tests are similar to hw questions, but no crib sheet (some diff-eq teachers allow one).

Very clear and concise lectures and gives good examples of everything covered and teaches effectively. If you do the hw and go to recitation and-or office hours, you'll do well in the class. Grading scheme voted on by students allowed a 75+ to be a B with an 87.5+ to be an A.
Extremely straightforward and willing to help you succeed, but only if you show up and do the work. Completing the assigned problems is a must along with attending recitations.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.
