reviews.comment: His lectures are really clean cut and cover everything well (you can tell he wrote the textbook on it) and homework is reasonably challenging. He uses Piazza for everything, gets lecture videos and resources up quickly, announces things well, and does an amazing job responding to questions on there--average response time is 20 minutes.
Great prof. Be sure not to skip the lectures, they are super worth attending. He is a great lecturer and even better at answering your miscellaneous questions.

Quite possibly the worst math professor/instructor I have had in my life. Teaches way too quickly. Typically loses students 10 min into the lecture. I am doing well so far but self taught literally all the material. He seems very intelligent but doesn't process that not everyone has done this material several times before.

Where do I begin? To put it briefly, 1) No way of knowing your grade until the semester is over. 2) Textbook that the homework is from is specifically designed to make as little sense as possible. Ugh

He is nice, but he is the laziest and fakest professor you can imagine. When I was taking his class he was so focused on his own work that he barely took our class seriously. It was very hard to actually learn in his class, but getting an A isn't that hard.

Possibly the best math professor at RPI. The course pace is rapid and the material is complex, but he does such a great job that everyone ends up doing well. No grade modifiers (only A, B, C no - or +) so push for an A! The best part of class was when he connected what we were learning to actual papers and fields of study. Highly, recommend.
Not super accessible out of class. The class itself was fairly interesting and Holmes WANTS you to pass. If you go to class, take notes, and do the homework, then you will do fine on the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: The professor taught Intro to Differential Equations again and last time is 2006 (10 years ago). The greatest part is his lecture, because it is extremely clear with almost all the words he has said written down on the projector. The exams are easy and number of questions is very small (110 min for only around five problems). Class is fast-paced.
Shares a dropbox folder with the class which contains a few textbooks and other interesting/necessary material.  Overall a great class and a great professor.
Really good class. He gives solid lectures and really cares about the material! Hes an energetic guy so be ready for that but overall awesome teacher! go to recitation for sure.

Decent professor for DiffEq. Lectures are straightforward and well-explained as long as you pay attention. Homework (from the book) is not mandatory, but since the quiz questions are taken from the homework it is a good idea to do it. My only complaint is that it can be difficult to know when to do which homeworks.

He is an amazing person and a great professor. You can tell that he truly enjoys his field when he's teaching. Although some of the things he teachers aren't relevant to the test, it gives depth to your learning which helps to remember what he teaches for longer periods of time. He is very fair, and cares about his students.

He replaced my first teacher halfway through the semester after the professor fell ill. Material not always presented in clearest way and he doesn't do examples like our other professor did. Stuff gone over in class also not relevant to homework a lot of the times.
Great teacher, a lot of charisma when lecturing.  You can find 95% of his lecture, word for word, in his book.  If you read his book before hand, the grade will be easier (though not an easy A)

GREAT PROFESSOR. He wrote the book used in class(the book it great by the way). His lectures are always well organized and clear, homeworks can be somewhat difficult but tests are easy if you pay attention. His humor is subtle but its worth listening for, he also pokes fun at pure mathematicians and chemists, as a physics major this was great.
He doesn't go into much detail at all so you don't learn much but the tests are word for word from the quizzes which are from the homework.  I slept thru several lectures and got an A.

The material is diffficult, but having him as a professor makes things so much easier.  He is one of the only professors I've had who can lecture without reading off of slides, notes, etc. in a CLEAR and COMPLETE fashion.  Take a class with him if you can -- you won't regret it.
amazing ... i'd take a course just to have him as my professor again.
Even though he has not taught this class for years, he explains the material like he has been doing this forever.
No Comments
knows his****
Easy in a very hard way. I found his class a pleasent experience.
No Comments
An excellent professor.  Extremely learned in the material.  His work is challenging yet enlightening and far from impossible.  If you have trouble, his door's always open.

Very clear and concise professor. Lectures were pre-recorded and not hard to follow, however he had a makeshift syllabus and took most info from a professor at another college. Nevertheless, his "live lecture" was used primarily for office hours (no mandatory attendance) and the class was only homework based (no exams) which made it a breeze.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Incredibly difficult class. Isaacson helps you through it, though. The material is very thick but very beautiful. His lectures are solid and he is very willing to help you in his office hours -- do him the courtesy of solidly knowing the math vocabulary you need to ask your questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He's pretty good. added a lot of interesting background to stuff. His stories are excellent. But we did not make it nearly as far as one would hope.

Worst teacher thus far. He gives you 5 multiple choice question tests and has no room for partial credit. His lectures were hard to understand, he assigned a ton of homework, and to top it all off, the TA was the worst thing I have even seen. Do not take him for Intro to Diff Eq.

multiple choice tests are awful... 5 questions with no opportunity for partial credit so one small mistake will cost you 20% on a test.  He is not clear while lecturing, giving you all the complicated theory but does not work out or solve any problems like what is on the homework or tests.  Do not take him for Diff Eq!
Multiple choice tests, no partial credit, drop a negative and you are down it an 80 no complaints. Ridiculous amount of homework

does only theoretical examples, never actually plugs in numbers to the equations. skips many steps, does integration in his head rather than write it out on the board. tests are 5 multiple choice questions, no partial credit.

This guy is horrible diff eq teacher, he uses ridiculous theoretical and unclear examples which dont help you understand the material. He assumes everyone in the room is as smart as he is so everyone ends up completely lost.
nice guy, interesting lectures, but the worst prof for intro to differential equations ever. strongly suggest NOT taking this course with him.

Favorite Quotes: "10 greats" : includes Euler, Newton, Maxwell, Gauss, Fourier (borderline), Bernoulli (full family)...; Class is more interactive than other professors; has his own syllabus.. dont bother asking
Excellent teacher. Clear, well put together lectures and reasonable tests. Very helpful both in and out of class. Amusing sense of humor and interesting stories.

Everything went real well...got an "A" in the course...he even asked me if he could photocopy my notes from the course!  Then, he gave me a very medocre letter of rec. for graduate school...seems as though he did not even bother to see what grade I got in the class!!!
really good class. excellent lecturer. he involves students in the lecture. gives good notes. makes it interesting.
wicked nice guy!!

I do not know what he is talking about even after I have read the book in advance. Awful writing and messy ideas. But the exam is not very hard, if you learned  the topic he talked about from reading the text by yourself, and know what the methods are to solve all the review problems. And TA is more helpful and clearer than professor.

Personally, he is not a good professor. Also, he gives a lot of quizzes and iClicker questions. He is really confusing. Just don't choose his courses, please. That would be my every advice for people who's gonna to take multi-var.
Exams are really easy, just do the practice exam. Quizzes are hard. They are usually four questions and there is no partial credit.
I'm sure he does a lot of really cool research.............
bad lecturer

This is the worst professor I've ever taken with at RPI. He's one of those professors that think that can teach but really can't. He has a very messy handwriting. Half of the students don't go to his class because he's teaching style is so poor. Exams are mediocre if you somehow manage to understand his poor lectures. Why is he even a professor?

Professor Herron is frankly a genius and his expectations correspond. He expects you to do outside reading - essential to following lectures and you will teach yourself. Homework is graded and quite challenging, tests are very easy - the two effectively balance one another out. Hope for a good TA because they make your life infinitely better.

By far the worst professor I've had at RPI. His lectures are boring and he doesn't explain anything he's doing, he just expects you to understand it as well as he does. His homeworks are also very long and challenging. Had teach myself differential equations through recitation and the textbook. Avoid him if at all possible.
Avoid at all costs. Very difficult professor. Can't read his handwriting. Wish I took it with another teacher.
Does not make any sense. Worst handwriting possible... Makes a lot of mistakes.. I have to rely on reading the textbook & going to recitation to understand anything at all.
He is the absolute worst professor I have had at RPI so far.
homework is ridiculously  hard. idk how people can give him 4 out of 5 on easiness. he cant teach. alotta mistakes during lectures.
He was a terrible teacher.  I stopped going to lectures entirely once I realized I wasn't learning anything during them.  I had to learn entirely from the book and recitation.
Long, Monotonous lectures consisting of only going over examples of the book. A genius, but cannot teach/explain

His handwriting is horrible and his speech is hard to follow (not due to an accent, but his thoughts are scattered). If you take one of his classes, make sure to use your book and hope you have a good TA.
We learned about meat cleavers. And that's about it.
The nicest professor one could ever have. Very clear in class and never boring. Alwayas available for extra help.

Horrible Multiv. Prof. If you are a geek, have fun in this class or else hit the books and study very hard to get a good grade.  His final is very difficult and his HW's are very very long and challenging.

Don't expect Herron to teach you anything.  Read the book and go to TA sessions.  Herron is useless, can't even read what he writes.  And he goes way too fast through the material.  The tests are pretty easy though.  Unfortunately the homework is incredibly hard.
Worst writing and teaching skills ever.  Would only assign the hardest homework problems possible.  Tests are easy though.
The worst professor i have ever had. Never have i had a professor who cannot teach or write
he makes positively no sense and no effort to make sense.  his exams are east tho.
He trys to act like he wants to help you, but doesn't seem to get that the students don't already understand.

Horrible, horrible, horrible.  He obviously enjoys and knows the material but he thinks we do too.  Didn't even bother going to lecture, as I learned more by just studying the book for the three hours a week.  At least you can use crib sheets.
This man does differential equations for fun and thinks you like to too.  He flies through material at blazing fast speed.  If it wasn't for my TA I would have never passed.
Had him my first semester at college.  Almost made me reconsider being a math major.  Learned everything from the TA.  Herron is a useless man, who experiences occasional fits of uncontrolled anger.

Horrible professor! All he does is derive general equations and never shows how they're used. I learned everything in diff eq through my TA and through reading the book. I really like the topic but Herron ruined the course.

HORRIBLE Prof, I only learned anything in the class because of the TA and also he picked some of the hardest course material.  My TA said he didn't see some of the stuff we are doing in diff eq right now until he was in grad school.
The one redeeming factor in this class was our ability to use crib sheets, and the major portion of our grade that was comprised of homework, which also happened to be very difficult.
I have never failed a class in my life... but I will now thanks to prof Herron... the ****.
Apparently the hardest Diff. Equ. teacher, we hit chapters other teachers wouldnt touch...
He was horrible when I had him
Worst professor I've had at RPI.  Hard to understand, and disliked the fact that I went to office hours as often as I did to try to learn the material.

Professor Jidong is a great professor. He made an arduous and difficult course tolerable. He is clearly an easier teacher than Cutler, but his course is still challenging. He gives clear exam hints while keeping tricky MCQs. The class is taught in a way where self-studying is possible. However, homeworks are time consuming and unrelated to exams.

If you think this professor is bad, the alternative, Cutler, is 100 times worse and that's not an understatement (I retook). Negatives of Xiao: Lectures are hard to understand and he takes attendance by calling on you randomly (3pts, which I lost all 3). Hard to learn if you are taking for the first time, but much much easier overall.

If you think this professor is bad, the alternative, Cutler, is 100 times worse and that's not an overstatement (I retook). Negatives of Xiao: Lectures are hard to understand and he takes attendance by calling on you randomly (3pts of your final grade, I lost all 3). Hard to learn if you are taking for the first time, but much much easier overall.

Easier than Cutler, but still is a very hard course. Homework assignments took around 8 hours each, but were doable. He offered some incentives, but these weren't easy to get. TAs weren't the most helpful either. Despite him giving us hints, exams were challenging with little to no partial credit. He can be harsh and cut throat at times as well.

His DS is easy. Dude spoils everything that will be on the exams, but is bad at lecturing and is hard to understand. Takes mandatory attendance by having his ai voice call on random ppl while 1/3 of the class is always absent. Tanked the zero for attendance bc lecture is that bad

Subpar Lecturer, doesn't spend more than a week teaching basic c++, despite it being the base for the entire class. Has very funny moments in lectures, but always has the notes preloaded and fake printed, leading him to not provide an engaging meaningful lecture, despite requiring attendance, although he does give info on questions on exam.
Avoid like the plague.

Jidong is by no means a bad professor, but Data Structures will always be hard. He always made sure we knew what was coming on tests, and would sometimes borderline tell us the questions. A lot of Homeworks and all of them take a good amount of time to do. He's funny and caring, but his lectures were sometimes useless as understanding him is hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great lecturer, although heavy accent. Otherwise, homework is a part-time job (average 12-15 hours a week for this HW). Visit TAs early on, as they weren't great later on (One of the TAs used ChatGPT right in front of me). Best to have prior experience with C++ syntax before his class, as he doesn't teach it
He's the goat for op sys and also for data structures which I took with him before.

This professor is actually one of the best, and nicest professors I have ever had, and I am in my junior year of college. I had him before in Data Structures and he was good too but taking him again in Operating Systems, he is understanding, his work even though hard he tries to connect it to real world applications, making it fun at time. The Best

Very knowledgeable, bad at lecturing. Tends to mumble, & shows things incorrectly as an example before the correct thing, which is hard to follow. Still, made DS manageable and added comedic elements to lecture to entertain us. Exams could be tricky but all were fair. Very helpful w/ final b/c he gave general idea of every single question.
I like the professor's carefulness of making animation of certain codes, making the notes a lot easier to understand. Love the jokes!

Professor Xiao was a pretty funny professor although I rarely paid attention to class, he is usually really nice when you inform him about like being sick or something. Although he has a accent, his comedy is pretty on task and one of the professors that you would like to definately take again.

Prof. Xiao made what would have been a boring class into one with occasional funny moments to keep the students engaged. The dreaded Presentation Assistants in class created lots of stress on who would get picked to answer the question, so make sure to show up. Otherwise, slightly easier HW (HW6 is a nightmare) and slightly easier tests than Cutler

Jidong Xiao is a great teacher, he's always willing to help his students and is very accessible outside of class. He is very generous with extra credit opportunities and wants everyone to succeed. His lectures are always fun and engaging thanks to his presentation assistants.

Worst lecturer I've seen, accent/mumbler. Lectures almost useless since they are disorganized and he explains things only after students ask 100 questions b/c he cannot explain. Also gave terrible instructions to install C++ software and getting used to compiling (had to go to 3 TAs all gave different answers). He seems nice/smart but bad professor

Jidong is one of the very few professors I've had who cared about my success. He was extremely accessible outside of class and even coded his own animations to illustrate otherwise difficult material; this shows that he actually wants us to do well.

One critique: I don't think English is his first language, so his lectures were hard to follow.
Professor helped outline how to figure out the homework. Good curve at the end of the course.

Favorite overall class I've taken at RPI (in hindsight, in the moment it was stressful) was Data Structures with Jidong. A rare RPI professor who doesn't needlessly deflate your grade. He gave us hints for exams, gave us helpful outlines/strategies for homeworks, and plenty of chances of getting more late days. Overall, top professor. Learned a lot
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: I liked Jidong as a professor mostly because he was pretty nice and considerate. I was sick for a while, I emailed him for an extension. He also made the homework assignments a little easier. On the other hand, he is not a very good lecturer in my opinion. He mumbles quite a bit and has a thick accent. I would definitely take the class with Jidong

After taking the first half of the class with Professor Goldschmidt, whose material was very clear and understandable, I found Professor Xiao's lectures and notes hard to follow and I often left his lectures more confused than when I entered. His exam was relatively easy, but that was only because he told us what every question would be about.

Professor Xiao is genuinely a great person, but not the best professor. Most of each lecture was about the homework assignment of the week, meaning that the test material needed to be self-taught via the notes hosted on GitHub. He was always accessible via the Submitty forum, frequently helping students with assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Xiao is very knowledgeable and teaches well if you pay attention, but he spends most of class time on the homework, meaning most of my learning of lecture material was on my own, making the labs difficult. Overall, he wasn't my personal favorite prof but he is certainly good. The homework and exams are fair, just manage your time well.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Xiao was a very nice professor who actually made data structures much easier then previous years. Ignore the other guy talking about spending 10 hours on homework; that's not much for DS here and it was much worse before he became the prof. DS is hard, but if simply do the work your given and study basics for test (+ crib sheet) you'll be good.
Wonderful, caring professor. One of the best professor in RPI that actually care about students.
He is one the best professors in RPI; nobody teaches better than him for data structures!

The actual goat he making data structures finally passable and not a complete nightmare very chill guy with helpful diagrams during lecture to help you understand lecture topics and also discusses and writes pseudocode for helping you get started on homeworks to make them less time consuming
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Data Structures. yikes. incomprehensible lectures, 10 hour hws and tough exams. this class put me in survival mode and jidong xiao made it worse. the only benefit is that if you make it through this class you are now hirable in CS.

Horrid lectures. It's much more efficient to read the lecture notes outside of class since he doesn't explain the material very well. I'm very concerned for future freshmen if he continues to teach the course in further semesters.
easy A way better than Plum not even comparable

Prof. Xiao isn't the best at teaching however, I really appreciated that he put more emphasis on our future careers, so rather than just giving plain lectures, he also solved many Leetcodes alongside. He also changed the format of hws, again to prepare us for the future. however, his lectures were really hard to pay attention to.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: There will be some negative reviews from this year, but this is the first semester Prof. Xiao is teaching Data Structures. The lectures weren't great at first, but they got so much better by the end. Between this and how he is constantly taking feedback and improving the course, I think it will get better every semester. Don't be scared off!

Data Structures is an intense class, but you have no choice of professor. Xiao's lectures are very hard to follow, he just reads the notes (badly). If you actually want to learn, don't go to lectures, read the lecture notes online, watch lectures from 2020 (see spring23 calendar), go to office hours, make friends, and/or ask questions during lab.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof. Xiao seems rather knowledgeable on DS, but his lectures are very boring and the explanations are sometimes subpar/unclear. He has great demonstrations for certain topics, but, for others, he doesn't really explain comprehensibly. Went to some of his office hours and he was a bit critical/cold, but during lecture he seems alright
He teaches a difficult class, and he does not make it easier. Earnestly, I feel he is very smart and sometimes very forgiving, though this does not shine through in his teaching style and HomeWorks.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: NIce
His class isn't very difficult, but he can be pretty mean.

Dr. Stetler is such a caring professor who puts so much thought and effort into his students. He goes beyond the scope of every class he teaches to ensure students are succeeding whether its job opportunities, career advice, or just overall well-being concerns -- he truly cares. I am grateful to have had the opportunity to be his student here.
He isn't a research professor; he just brags in class every day about mentoring undergrads on their internships.

Great professor for computational bio lab, keeps lectures short and to the point to give students as much time as possible to work on the lab. Always willing to answer questions during the lab. Reasonable with deadlines and grading.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: While I feel this class doesn't require a particularly good professor, I nonetheless feel he is a great professor to have. Grading criteria is reasonable, workload is on-par with a 1 credit class, and the final project/presentation is easy. If you're forced to take BIOL-1010, I highly recommend this class and professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: While a good professor, his lectures didn't always seem 100% relevant to material being tested. He does have a very dry sense of humor, which I appreciated, and I walked into Biostats knowing nothing, and learned a lot. He was very helpful if you needed it.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Lectures were easy to follow and interesting. He is a very kind person. However I don't think grading criteria was clear and I lost points on the last project even though I definitely think that I checked all the boxes on the rubric. but overall a very smooth experience.

While I think it's clear he is here to do research, his class was interesting and pretty easy to follow. The hardest part of the lab work was following his code in R studio but if you have had previous experience with coding it is pretty straightforward and much better than a traditional lab.

Dr. Stetler did not assign more work than should be required by a 1 credit class. The use of real-world data sets made data analysis with R interesting. The design of his course, specifically the final group project, was effective in helping us develop important soft skills and he gave us ample opportunity to build on these skills further.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Very nice professor, his biostatistics class is also highly recommended!
An excellent professor!

Dr. Stetler is nice, but he's really only passionate about lakes and climate change. He reads off the slides and says "I don't know" to most questions, especially in the genetics unit. He gives plenty of time for projects, but make sure to write down the due dates because he does not have the deadlines listed in one clear spot.

dr. stetler is a funny and really nice guy. i only have him for lab this semester, and i've really enjoyed it. i was expecting it to be awful bc they changed my lab section to be computational bio, but he's really made me enjoy data analysis with R.

Gives so much more work than the other professors in Intro to Bio and has really uninspiring lectures. He's a nice guy but take any other professor if you don't want to spend many tedious hours doing busy work.

He was hired a few weeks before my first day of class, so we essentially had to teach him how to be a teacher. I suggest giving him a few years of experience before taking his class. He's nice, but he really likes climate change and group projects. My main issue is that he is too new to teaching, he just got out of grad school.

ENGR 1400 is easier than ENGR 1200 if you have the option to take it. Nothing was too difficult but it was annoying for a 1 credit class. It can be easy to get confused but you'll never be completely lost, especially when you have TAs to help you. I would strongly recommend taking this class (or ENGR 1200) with a friend so you can help each other.

A LOT of work for a 1 credit class. Weekly assignments in increasing complexity + a "quiz" every 3 weeks during lab. Attendance not required when no quiz. Siemens NX is very large, old, difficult, and the TAs are not familiar with it. This all leads up to the grand final(e) gigantic assignment that takes >25 hours and your sanity to complete.

Engineering Graphics and CAD is notorius on RPI campus thanks to this incredible man. I must retake this class to save my GPA - against my greater judgement. The final was an absolute slog - start the final as soon as it is available and pray you can complete it on time.
Just a rude guy, the grading criteria is very vague, and the TAs will yell at you for not doing the assignment to THEIR grading criteria.

Prof Morris doesn't deserve all of the hate he gets. His lectures are videos, but I liked it bc I could go at my own pace and replay things. Make sure to get all the points on regular HW because the ILAs and final are hard. Also start the final as soon as you can, def more work than 1 credit but it is worth it to actually learn a useful skill.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Don't take CAD lightly, especially timewise. Morris is a good teacher as long as you communicate with him and actually do the work, and listen to all the lectures. Just make sure to do the assignment alongside listening to the lectures. CAD is fun as long as you dont procrastinate.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Meh. Extremely easy A but I'm generally against paying tens of thousands of dollars a year to watch youtube tutorials

The class is just frustrating. Morris expects everyone to watch an hour's worth of YouTube tutorials  before each class (and many of them go into much greater detail than is necessary for the assignments). He responds to most questions with "Did you watch the video?" Most of the TAs are helpful though. It's not a difficult A, just an annoying one.
This course is way easier than ENGR 1200 but you still have to deal with Jeff Morris.

Mostly video lectures, definitely better to take ENGR1400 over ENGR1200 if you have the option to. Whenever I needed help and the TAs were all busy he helped me out and was funny about it. Fun guy if he's in a good mood. Just do your work and you're fine.

The CAD part in the beginning semester was a little tricky but the second half of the course was pretty easy. The TAs are always willing to help and figure out any problems you have. If you're a BME definitely take this course over ENGR-1200 it's a lot easier.

His class was pretty easy if you made an attempt to study the videos. He's usually available to ask questions in class and is willing to help you as long as he can tell you've watched the videos. The final was a big issue for a lot of my peers but in my opinion as long as you started early enough then it shouldn't be a problem.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This is a very easy class. I did well in it. I just have a moral objection to paying $50k a year to watch 12 year old YouTube tutorials and only interact with TAs. Morris is helpful a) when he's in the room (which is not often) and b) when the question wasn't covered in the 5 YouTube tutorials he posted.

Jeff is very knowledgeable about CAD, and always helped me understand where I was messing up on modeling (albeit with a slight condescending attitude). I know a lot of people don't like him, but he means well. Show up, attempt every model/drawing, and for your own sanity start the final the day he assigns it (you get 30 days)

There is no lecture, only videos online which has its benefits but can be very annoying. The workload throughout the year isn't necessarily bad but for a one credit class is absolutely insane. The worst is the final. DO NOT WAIT. START IT THE DAY HE RELEASES IT. PLEASE. It is a MASSIVE step up in terms of difficulty, and workload. just take 1400

Very knowledgeable, 90% of the class was fine, but the final is awful. Huge jump from the level of difficulty from the rest of the class. Relatively helpful, but has a sense of an ego due to his extensive knowledge of the program he created. The TAs are fantastic and are greats helps on all the assignments.

Could have a clearer syllabus. Not in class for full time. Looks like a bother, but is not. Helpful. Virtual office hours. Grades using TAs. Attendance mandatory for TA grading. Knowledgeable with software used in course. Video lectures, from previous years and slightly outdated. Easy class. Homework for only 1/3rd of semester. No quizzes or exams.

All if the lectures are online and are hard to understand. The TAs help a lot, but he is not frequently in the class often. He does not have a lot of interaction with the students in this class, and it seems like a bother to answer questions from the students.

He doesn't give lectures and sometimes isn't in the room. The material is posted in video format so that he doesn't have to teach it every year. The videos don't cover all the material either. If it wasn't for tutoring at the Folsom Library I wouldn't of passed this class.

Very good knowledge of software we use bc he created it, but he's not always in class. Assignments take much longer than a 1 credit class should. You only have to show up physically once every 3 weeks & there is no final which is nice, but all lectures are videos you must watch online. Gives good advice in class so long as you watched his lectures.

Don't know why he has so many bad ratings, this class is much better than I expected. It's true that there are no lectures, but you don't really need them. His online videos walk you through everything and if you're stuck, he or the TAs will help. I'm constantly impressed by his knowledge of NX and he's got pretty funny dry humor. Chill guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Morris is nice but this is such a heavy 1 credit class, should be worth at least 2 or 3 compared to other classes here. In-labs are not great and the homeworks take forever. start the final asap

For Engineering Communications, the class is easy enough that his lecture style isn't going to force you to study CAD for 5 hours each week. Every lecture is a video, and he expects you to watch them all. He comes off as someone who doesn't care, but I think he does. If you show some effort, he's a genuinely nice person. TAs aren't very helpful.

For those who rated him low, I can see where they're coming from. But this is kinda how the real world works. The online instructions he gave were reasonably clear. Just find the help you need, and there's always a way.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Morris is a very interesting character. All you do is watch the prerecorded lectures and submit the assignments on time to get an A. If you try to ask him a question in person he is very knowledgeable but sometimes he gets mad because "it was in the lecture videos." Overall, class was much more work than 1 credit.

Always very helpful to me and answered my questions. Assignments have very clear grading criteria and I would recommend watching the recorded lectures, as most of the content came straight out of them in my experience. Was very understanding when I transferred in at the beginning of the semester and gave me enough time to catch up to the class.

I'm switching majors so it's kind of sad to say I won't be taking this class anymore, however the professor and TAs are very helpful during the hours you go in, they won't scold you for the stuff you don't know so please just ask for help. The grading rubrics are pretty clear aswell.

this guy is definitely a strange bird out of RPIs faculty but he genuinely does care about the success of his students, but it can be difficult to notice since he oversees like 50 sections. even still, he surprised me when he actually remembered the names of me and many others in my class. the class is decent to understand if you watch the videos

It's a reversed classroom so all of the lectures are online and you just follow along with the assignments given. There are in class "labs" every three weeks where you only have about an hour to do an assignment but you get the entire library of videos to use while doing them. If you ever have trouble with an assignment he knows how to fix it

Morris teaches through video lectures that can sometimes take an hour or two to watch fully, however you can submit everything online so you don't have to go to class except for ILAs. The actual 3D models do take a lot of work, however if you work together with other people they can be completed in a reasonable amount of time.

Be prepared to spend hours building models and watching lecture videos. I took both 1200 and 1400. I loved both and learned a lot. If you don't know how to ask for help you will have a hard time, but I found him accessible and friendly. Just show that you've given an effort before asking. I used my knowledge in a future internship! Very satisfied.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I had Dr. Morris for both CAD and Comms. Lecture videos are useful and give you the info you need to do the whole course. Despite his reputation, he showed up to every session, and is extremely helpful if you ask him a question. CAD is a work-intensive class, but Dr. Morris is a great resource to help you get through it.

This class was essentially self taught through lecture videos, which granted were helpful, the only time you would ever see Jeff Morris was when he would take the first 5 minutes of class to speed run the entire assignment that took you a week to finish just to vanish like a fart in the wind.

You follow videos online each week, then the class is for the TAs to grade/help with anything. The videos have the answer to literally any question. Sit by the door so the TAs grade you first and you can leave within 10 minutes. Prof. knowns the answer to EVERY question. There aren't any tricks. If you watch the videos, you can do the HW/quizzes
Hes a nice guy just know that all the learning will be through his youtube videos

If you're a woman, he's a little bit of a misogynist but not actually. He's really nice and if you have a problem, he'll often just fix it for you. The cad part of the class is the only truly difficult part but if you get in the groove of things, it's not bad at all. It's really the TA's running the class but Dr. Morris is always around somewhere.

Its a 1 credit course with a 4 credit workload. The professor only teaches through videos, but everything in the videos is taught well. He is very helpful in class in checking work before submission, so recommend doing that. Most assignment are difficult, and usually get harder as the course goes on. Its a different style of teaching for me.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I got lucky, he was in every class. He'll help you if you ask and tbh it was very helpful. The class itself is interesting but don't take 1200 unless you have to. NX sucks but it gets better (kinda). The TAs pretty much ran the class even though Dr Morris was literally there. At least TRY to watch the lectures and START THE FINAL PROJECT ASAP

I understand why many people don't love him, but I think he's great. As someone who took 1400 and 1200, the content wasn't too bad. If you have him when 1400 isn't going on at the same time, chances that he's there is high. He does run FEA office hours during class sometimes, so he might be occupied on occasion.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: All the lectures are online and you might never actually see Jeff. The ILAs are tough and stressful. He takes a while to grade. If he does show up to class, you can ask him any cad question and he will know how to help. Start the final project early and if you have questions, ask them. Everything builds so make sure you understand the basics.

What a joke of a professor. Was in class once, maybe for 5 minutes and never saw him again. We were only assigned videos to watch and work to do. Was rude in emails asking for assistance and the TA's ran the class. The way this class was structured was to make it the easiest for this man never to care about his students or to teach the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: It seemed like he didn't really want to teach, he prerecorded all his lectures and had you go through them for the homework. I will say he knows his stuff (because he wrote the software) and will help you if you ask. He can be condescending at times. As long as you get the homework done, you can be out of the class within 10 mins.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Saying that I had Dr. Morris for my CAD class might be an overstatement because he almost never actually showed up to our class. There are a lot of sections of CAD, so I understand that he might have to miss sometimes for some of his higher level classes, but his presence was rare. The grading in this class is also very harsh.

Morris gets a lot of crap but if you go to the classes (literally any of them doesn't have to be yours) you can easily get 100 on all the assignments. Siemens NX is extremely aggravating but by the end of the course its pretty easy to get the hang of.

Look if you asked him to help you with whatever CAD project you had, he'd straight up do it for you. The TAs were hit or miss so sometimes Jeff is all you have. Only thing is when he doesn't show up to class you're kinda done for. Just don't procrastinate and you'll be fine in CAD.

A few pieces of for when taking this class is 1) to join his office hours he will help you fix any of your problems 2) Look for the undergraduate TA because they are the ones that will actually know what they are doing. 3) if you do not need to take this class do not take it will save you a headache.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: This class is definitely a lot of out of class work but if you watch and follow along with the lecture videos every week, you can easily grasp the content. Plus the TAs will always check your homework for you and help if you go to class so there's really no way to get bad grades on them.

I love this man. He always shows up to class, helping everyone (mostly white guys). If you become his TA, expect to do absolutely no work, as Morris completely does all of it. If you want an easy one-credit class, this is the way to go. (He gives plenty of extra credit opportunities if you meet him during his office hours). Woohoo Dr. Morris!!

I love this man. He always shows up to class, helping everyone (mostly white guys). If you become his TA, expect to do absolutely no work, as Morris completely does all of it. If you want an easy one-credit class, this is the way to go. (He gives plenty of extra credit opportunities if you meet him during his office hours). Woohoo Dr. Morris!!!

Morris was present for only the first class, just to read the syllabus. The TA's will be actually teaching and administrating the class. All lecture content is youtube vids by Morris. Grading is harsh. It's a good course, teaches you to teach yourself which is good, but I can't give much kudos to Morris. Work is much more than 1 credit class.

He only came to the first day of class and I've only seen him a handful of times around campus since then. I didn't mind the format of the course, you just have to hold yourself accountable and actually watch the lecture videos because that's where he explains everything. Hopefully you get good TA's or have helpful friends.

Dr. Morris teaches CAD using a flipped classroom model with prerecorded lecture videos. While some in-lab assignments can be challenging and NX is not ideal, ENGR-1200 is a great course that also teaches you time management and independence.  If you watch the videos and ask the TAs for help, you will find that Dr. Morris's presence is not critical.
He just DO NOT teach. I did not see him once in the whole semester. The officer hours are now turn to online. Tough grader and never knows where you loss the point.

Good ol' Jeff here teaches through a lecture series he recorded years ago and has not once shown up to class. He also schedules office hours at the same time as class and is rude if you try to use them. Assignments are also barely relevant to "lecture" material. All in all the only thing I learned from CAD is dealing with frustration.

Can't tell you what his face looks like. Even the final was graded by the TA. He knows his stuff, but does not teach it. He never showed up to class after the first day and left everything to his TAs. 1 credit class but 2-3 credits of work. Everyone was upset, disappointed, or both when showing up to class. Could be great, but sadly does not teach.

Can count on one hand the number of times I've seen Dr. Morris all semester. Class run by TAs, grading criteria not always clear. Lectures to be watched before class, highly recommended to watch for CAD and skip for everything else. Attendance not required but helpful to get work checked over. Have heard mixed results from attending office hours.

Morris will show up on the first day and then never again (unless you find him at hockey games).TAs grade everything; the class can be hard, and even they don't know what they're doing. Now everyone's confused. The class is entirely taught with outdated videos. It was a waste of time for me, so beware of this class if it's required for your major.
He never once showed up to class, and the entire course is run by the TAs. I went to his office hours once and he was extremely rude.
Almost hated as much as Shirley Ann jackson

He didn't teach Engineering Communications, the TAs did. Showed up to the first class for half an hour, never saw him in person again. Content was taught through old youtube videos using an outdated version of NX. CAD part of the course was way too much work, but it was a breeze once we got to word/excel/labview. Take this course instead of 1200.
Refused to round up a grade that was extremely close to the next letter grade. Threatened to decrease my grade when I asked him to regrade an assignment.

Man literally does not show up to class. There are video lectures that were made in like 2008 that use outdated software. Office hours are during class for some reason. Do not let Box grade your assignments. Have the TAs grade it instead.

Has the absolute worse grading metric, volume, since he contributed to the software that he teaches he expects everyone to use the features the exact same way he would when even the TA's don't even know the right answer. I've had four separate assignments where the TA's had no idea what the problem was. He hasn't even taught in years, just videos
the class is almost entirely taught by TAs and requires much more work than one would expect for a 1 credit course
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Morris does not teach. He just shows up the first day and then leaves you in the hands of the TAs. I was lucky to have a few very helpful TAs, so I did fine in the class. Just whatever you do, avoid Morris's office hours if at all possible. He will do everything possible to make you feel like an idiot.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Morris never showed up to class. During office hours, he was very condescending and offered little help. Grades harshly (even though guidelines aren't clear) and requires every assignment to be done in a very specific way (which he does not tell you; you're expected to just figure it out) even if a different way would also be right. TA's ran class.

Doesnt show up to his own class. The entire class is taught by his poor TA's who are doing their best and will try to help you but some things they just don't know. In which case you can either take the L and lose the points or go to his office hours where he will be outright aggressive, mean and rude towards you for simply trying to pass his class

This guy is an absolute scummy person. He belittles you with every chance he gets. If you ever want to feel bad about yourself, go to his office hours. Apparently, he's the only one who knows NX in this school so he made the CAD assignments for IFE, thank god they were easy. It sucks that freshmen are forced to take CAD with this tool.

This has to be the worst professor at the school. You will never know what you are doing wrong unless you explicitly ask the poor TA's. This guy does nothing for you and hates students. The whole class is a series of YouTube videos recorded in 2018 on a different version of the cad program we used. ***AVOID AT ALL COSTS***
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I would give him a zero if I could. He makes this one credit class more work than my major-specific courses. He is lazy and rude. I once asked for an extension on an assignment days before it was due, and he told me that if I'm too stupid to not be able to do it in an hour then I have bigger problems. Has not been teaching on campus in seven years.
Unclear grading criteria and unnecessary amount of work for a 1 credit class. Try to avoid this class if you can.

Knows his information, but if you ask for help, he treats you like you're an idiot for not knowing something briefly mentioned in the lecture video. I asked for help once and he talked down to the person before me, to me, and to the person after me. I've talked to other people and they experienced the same. Way too much work for a 1 credit class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He never shows up to class and expects you to learn via youtube video only, which can be difficult for first time CAD students. He gives grades without explaining why you got the grade you did. I have worked with CAD for years, and I find myself struggling in his class because of his unknown grading criteria. Do not take this class.

You never going to see him in the class except the first day. The class is taught by recorded lectures. TAs did all the grading. However, he is quite helpful in office hours. It is a one credit course, but time consuming at the beginning cuz CAD. Beside CAD, other projects are straightforward.

I honestly couldn't have a lower opinion on this guy. His "lectures" are a series of prerecorded YouTube videos. You'll never see him again after the first day of class. Total joke of a professor. I have had many great professors at this school, and it's a shame that he is a part of the faculty.
You will literally never see this man and for some reason if you need to contact him he will be sure to be extra rude and not understanding.

Assignments other than CAD are extremely easy but CAD with NX is ridiculously confusing and the explanation videos are long. Apparently you can get a lot of passes on late work and incomplete assignments if you visit the professor but office hours clash with regular class time and he doesnt reply quickly to email

I personally loved Morris for Engineering Communications. The other ratings are right, he shows up the first day of class and you will only see your TA's in class afterwards. I used to skip class and just go to his office hours, and he'll help me finish 3 projects in a day. If you watch the videos and still don't understand, he helps!

Be sure to WATCH THE VIDEOS he posts on LMS!! I loved Professor Morris! If you feel like there's a subject that you do not understand in class/the , definitely go to his office hours. He makes it his duty to help his students get all of the assistance they need. 10/10 would recommend. I would love to take his class again if I could.

You will see Jeff Morris once during this course- the 5 TAs are your graders. This class is rough and is mostly online cuz it is a 1 credit course with the work of a 4 credit class. NX-12 is the used program and honestly it super sucks- bit this class is kinda required :/. Expect lots of work and try to make buddies with CAD experienced peoples.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Morris doesnt even teach the class he just shows up on the first day to tell you what you have to do for the course and thats the last time you'll see for the semester. Only a 1 credit hour class but requires probably about 2 hours of video watching and 2-3 hours of work each week

This man is never in class. He can't even be called a professor since he doesn't teach. Watch the broken videos to learn the skills that you need to complete assignments in class and you'll do well. You've got to be lucky with TAs as well since sometimes, even they don't know what they're doing.

Not what I thought it was going to be. I thought it was going to be mostly in lab assignments that were guided by him. Instead, he shows up the first session and lets you know that the class is based purely of his pre-recorded lectures which are long and boring. Had to get help from friends often. He is available for help but can be cocky.

My interaction with Professor Morris was pretty much watching the videos he made for class. To that extent, they're well laid out and edited, but the class isn't the best. Since the majority of your interaction is with TAs, you don't see Morris much. However, it's not a difficult class at all.

Jeff is an awesome professor!  He's fairly tough for CAD grading but he is the best IED teacher ever!  Jeff is clear and cuts the bull that permeates this class.  My friends always complained about cryptic assignments and annoying questions, but Jeff is just helpful, polite, and reasonable.  Great professor!

I can only comment on Morris concerning the video lectures he provided for a 1-credit class and from the one time that I attended his (busy) office hours for extra help. His expectations are clear and he provides all the information you need. To get an A just watch his videos, do your work, and be nice to the TAs. Good engineering professor.
Had his videos for an engr communications class. I had to go to his office hours once and he was quick and helpful.  Young guy, solid pick for leading any class.
well it's CAD. you can't go wrong with that. Easy explanation, easy grading, easy A

Had Jeff for IED. I didn't realize how lucky I was until after speaking with people in other IED sections. He's acts in this course like a true engr supervisor and will give you a feeling for the real world. He checks up on your design and makes sure you're on track, but then LEAVES YOUR TEAM ALONE to do your work. Would recommend him to anyone.

My opinion of this man couldn't be lower. Useless video lectures explained nothing and had nothing to do with the assignments. The non-CAD portion of the class was a waste and clearly ad-libbed at the last minute. The TAs tried their hardest but couldn't salvage the class from Mr. Morris' incompetence and vagueness.

So he went to class the first day and that's because he just happened to be around. Guy's totally a d***. I went to office hours once and he cut them short to go to his other job... DJing the hockey games. I didn't look at the video lectures for many reasons: his annoying clicker, the uselessness, and the time spent watching. Befriend a TA.

Video lectures meant he never showed up in class. The CAD segment of the class was obscenely hard in NX(bad software), many of the videos were of little/no help, if not for tons of help from a friend I would've failed. The rest of the class was easy & pointless, the TAs weren't necessarily more helpful than other students in the class.
The NX segment of his class sucks. It's insanely difficult to understand, but after that the rest of the class is a walk in the park.

I only saw him once when he was trouble shooting my computer during the "Word" part of class. Pretty much the TAs are the only ones who do anything. I liked the CAD part of the class, but totally disliked the part prior to labview. The videos for word are useless. All the talk about are making pizzas

Prof. Morris's video lectures were almost entirely useless. CAD cannot be taught be throwing bunches of random features at the viewer and requesting that s/he turn them into a part. Prof. Morris also does not know proper drawing style, dimensioning rules, etc. His drawings are among the worst I have ever seen- worse than freshmen in my high school.
doesn't actually exist.
This class was a joke.  It may have been a lot of work for a 1 credit class but none of it was hard and you had to try to not get a 100 in this class.

Everything but the last few projects are easy, but those last projects are harder, and the final is nearly impossible.  The videos either explain something twenty times or none, but are useful (mostly).  I guess it really does depend on your TA's though, because he isn't really responsible for your grade at all.

Eh, well, the videos were...not exactly the best way to teach CAD, in my humble opinion.  However, I did all my work and got the A.  Helpful in his optional live lectures; bring specific questions to that and he'll help you out.  Simple philosophy: Do your work.  In reality though, not the easiest to follow through; hard work for a 1-credit class.
No Comments
No Comments
No Comments

Completely ridiculous amount of work for a 1 CREDIT course...At least its  not that hard, once you sit and watch his boring lectures, which have the potential to put you to sleep more than once. Just hope you get good TA's, mine pretty much did the work for me, and gave me perfect scores on labs that weren't perfect.        = )

The class was taught entirely using video lectures, which basically meant you never actually saw him unless you sought him out.  Otherwise you have to trust the TAs, and since this year we switched over to NX, they didn't really know what they were doing.  He could have been hibernating all semester, for all I know.

She is extremely caring and always puts you and your learning as her top priority. I always felt motivated to learn in this class, and this class is one of very few I have ever looked forward to going to. Genuinely one of the best teachers I've ever had.
She cares a lot about each student and wants to do what she can to support everyone academically and outside of class. She makes class fun and interactive so we fully grasp the material.
Truly cares about every student

She is one of the most passionate and dedicated teachers I have ever had. The class requires a lot of effort for homework, studying, projects, etc. But it is definitely worth it to take a class with her if you get the chance.

Yue Laoshi is a very generous grader. At the beginning of the semester, she explicitly stated that demonstrated effort will lead to a good grade. She gives plentiful extra credit opportunities, worth 10%, as long as you do the work. She gives good feedback and is clearly passionate about sharing Chinese culture! The get-togethers she hosts are fun.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Prof. Yue, in her time at RPI, fostered a caring environment for any and all students that showed interest in the subject material. She is very knowledgeable when it comes to characters and etymological history, and often incorporates anecdotes relating to the subject material in lectures. Very personable and fair when it comes to grading.

Great teacher! Clear about expectations outlined by the syllabus she hands out on the first day. There is a lot of work but reasonable. Her grading is fair and based on your effort. Her classes teach you discipline, you can't procrastinate. One of the best professors I've had at RPI. I would highly recommend taking one of her classes.

Prof. Yue is one of the most considerate professors I've had. Although her feedback may seem harsh at times, she is truly trying to help you do your best in understanding the content. Overall, I would recommend taking any class she teaches.

One of my absolute favorite professors at this school. She puts in so much work in and out of class to make sure that it's a comfortable environment for everyone by doing things like organizing mentoring hours and class lunches. She really pushes her students, which means a surprising amount of work, but she makes it very hard to not learn Chinese.

Very sweet and understanding. Clear about expectations. Surprisingly, a lot of work but reasonable. I'm a heritage speaker, so the class was mostly easy for me apart from presentations. Her grading is fair and based on your effort, though. Her classes teach you discipline -> can't procrastinate. One of the best profs I've had so far at RPI.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Yue Laoshi is hands down one of the best professors I've ever had! Mandarin is naturally a challenging language, but she makes it engaging, manageable, and even fun to learn. She's incredibly accessible, always willing to give extra help, and truly cares about her students' progress. You can tell she has a real passion for teaching.

Professor Yue is very good at attracting students' interest in learning. Her lectures are full of fun and students behave actively on class. The grading is also very kind and fair for everyone, and the workload is generally ok. I really love taking her teaching style.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: She is a really kind teacher. You can feel that she is really care about your situation. Responding to all your questions and trying all the ways to make the course interesting. She let me know that learning a new language is not a so difficult.

Yue Laoshi has immense care and personal investment in her students. You end up caring a lot about her feedback since its so genuine, but ultimately she understands wherever you are. If you take any of her classes just follow along with the syllabus and put the work in, it will be rewarded.
I've taken this professor for many classes and she is very good
I really loved Yue Laoshi's class. I learned so much from her and she is very passionate about her job.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Best professor I've had at RPI even though I am a cs/math major. Provides good feedback and really wants students to succeed. It is very clear what we need to do if we want an A. You also can learn a lot of skills outside of just the Chinese language, such as planning, not procrastinating and communication skills

Yue laoshi is an amazing professor! I've had her for three classes now and each time, I look forward to going to class. She's very knowledgeable, her lectures are fascinating, and she genuinely cares about her students. Would recommend taking any of her classes!

Yue laoshi is extremely passionate about teaching and genuinely wants her students to perform well in her class and learn not just textbook but also authentic Chinese. She makes her grading criteria extremely clear and hands out a syllabus with a detailed breakdown on deadlines for the entire semester at the beginning of the semester.

The Laoshi is an amazing teacher that really cares about your personal development while making sure that you have a comfortable experience in the meantime. She leaves a lot of room when grading assignments/projects and also offers  opportunities to gain extra credit! This course also allows students to sign up for mentoring which is very helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: She is kind, caring, and always think for student. However some says it causes too much redundent voice ( like, keep reminding things too often ). But I even liked that part as well, so it is up to you to take it or not.

Yue laoshi's class is tough and you're definitely gonna have to put some work to pass the class. However, your effort is very rewarding. One of those classes that you finish and you feel like you actually learned something.
Yue Laoshi is an ama

Yue Laoshi is a very caring professor. Everything that you need to do is made very clear from day one of class, where a comprehensive syllabus is provided. Your grade is very much about how much effort you put in, not your fluency. It is clear that she wants students to succeed. There is a lot of content, but it is presented gradually.

As a senior, I can definitely say she is the best teacher I had in RPI. Really cares about her students and very supportive. She fostered an incredible sense of community among students, it truly felt like a collaborative environment where everyone kept growing together. You have to put in effort, but in the end, you will have a solid foundation.

Yue Laoshi is a very kind, understanding professor and her classroom environments are very fun. In her class, everyone knows each other and it's a nice little community where no one feels awkward or out of place. You definitely need to put in some effort, but the assignments are very doable and you leave the class feeling accomplished.

Yue Laoshi is a great professor to have. One of the few professors at RPI that actually cares about student learning and the material that they teach! She is so compassionate and understanding, always trying to bring a positive and uplifting attitude to class. The workload may be high, but she's always willing to work with you and you have makeups.
Great teacher, just a lot of homework
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Amazing professor. The requirements for the class are very clear. Cares more about effort than your knowledge of Chinese. If you put in the work she WILL see it and it will not matter if you know less than other people, she will greatly appreciate it and you will get a good grade.

Prof.Yue is an amazing professor. There is nothing about Chinese culture she does not know about. The content itself is not difficult, but there will be a lot of work. She gives you the syllabus and it tells you the work you will have to turn in for the entire semester and the deadlines. If you miss them, there is an opportunity to make up for it.
I love Yue Laoshi. She was excellent. The class is work-heavy, but if you put the effort in, you will see that learning Mandarin Chinese is easier than you think!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I had a hard time in her class. She sometimes was very rude and didn't allow students to explain themselves if there was miscommunication. I tried my best, but she made it impossible for me to receive an A. She likes to brag during class that kids like her, but that is subjective, and I don't know how that is relevant to the class material.

The best Chinese professor I could have ever asked for. Very passionate and understanding. Will always go the extra step if she sees that you are also passionate about the language. Gives a lot of opportunities to learn and grow. You get as much out of this class as you put into it, but attendance is mandatory.
Yue Laoshi is an amazing teacher that really cares about her students and their progress! There is a good amount of homework for the class, but it is very doable.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Yue laoshi was a great professor who guided me through the beginning stages of learning Chinese. I took this class during the accelerated summer semester, which added to the rigor of the already fast-paced schedule of memorizing words and grammar structures, but I always felt that I had the educational support required to succeed.

Professor Yue is a very caring and thoughtful professor. This class has a lot of assignments, but if you manage your time well you will get a good grade. I would recommend her to anyone looking to learn Chinese!

I love Yue Laoshi! She is very involved with students and is one of the clearest teachers at RPI. The work outside of class is fairly easy to do good on (70-85), but if you want to really master it (85-100), you need to put in work.

Our class loves Yue Laoshi; she brightens our day and always comes to class with great enthusiasm. She teaches us in a fun way, and she goes above and beyond to help us learn the material. She is a fantastic professor who cares about not only our grades but also our happiness. She is very intelligent and knowledgeable. Definitely take her class!
I've had professor Yue for Chinese 1 through 3. She's by far the best professor at RPI and one of the few that care about their students

You can tell Professor Yue truly cares for her students. She expects a very reasonable amount of effort from her students but with the way she encourages and helps the students, its usually no problem. I never thought I could have so much fun taking a foreign language class so if you are interested at all, I highly recommend taking her class.

Professor Yue is the only professor that I've come across at RPI that really does care about her students. She listens to feedback from students to make the course as fair, effective and enjoyable as possible

Anyone who's taken her class can see how much she wants you to succeed in not just learning but internalizing the Chinese language. She is always prepared for the day's lesson, and always ready to happily answer your questions. There is a lot of work for this class, but it is definitely manageable and ultimately worthwhile.

Yue Laoshi stresses learning in her class, and while she may often correct your grammar or tone, she does it because she wishes for you to be better at the language. Her grading metrics are clearly defined, and while she stresses focus in the class, she is willing to tell stories in both Chinese and English, as well as learn English from us.

Very good at giving feedback, after every word she will make you practice it so that you can pronounce it correctly. Professor Yue is also very supportive and only wants to see you succeed and be able to speak Mandarin well.

Yue laoshi is an amazing professor who I admire very much. She is incredibly caring and hardworking. She prepares for many hours outside of class to make sure we have the best learning experience. I appreciate her dedication to her students; she wants us to become native speakers, and she is willing to support us throughout!

Professor Yùe is an outstanding educator. Her knowledge of Chinese etymology, history and culture is extensive and accurate, and she is so meticulous and thorough in her explanations. She carefully reiterates important concerts in various ways, such that certainly that no student has ever left the classroom with any misunderstanding or confusion.

A rare professor. If you want to learn Chinese, don't miss Professor Yue. She cares about her students and sets you up to succeed in the language. I was surprised by how much I learned in a couple of months. Challenging but rewarding. Take a class with Professor Yue.

Laoshi Yue is easily the best teacher I've ever had the pleasure of having. I took Chinese I with her my freshman year and from the very beginning, she is clear with her expectations. Chinese is a difficult class that will require lots of time outside of class studying, but she is willing to listen to students input and work one on one with any.
Shes very nice and very supportive.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I really loved the class! Fair warning: THIS IS NOT AN EASY A. While Yue is very clear on what you can do to get an A, I wouldn't say it was easy. You really do have to go to class and do all of the work. Make sure to start early on projects and sign up for mentoring hours early in the semester. The class is taught primarily in Chinese.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I took Chinese 2, 3, 4, 5, and an independent study with Prof. Yue. She is accomodating (within reason.) If you do the work (which there is a lot of,) you will probably get an A. You'll get out of the class what you put into it. I found the projects helpful, but the workbook HW seemed like busywork, I don't feel like I learned anything from them.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Professor Yue is probably the best professor I've had at RPI. She clearly puts effort into her classes and even makes online classes engaging and fun.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Yue laoshi is very knowledgeable and always willing to help and provide feedback. At first, you might feel embarassed every time she corrects your pronunciation or grammar, but it's always with the intention of helping you improve. As long as you keep up with the work and frequently participate in class, you'll have no problem getting an A.

A great professor that really cares about her students. She'll do everything to make sure all students are following along and puts a lot of effort into her class. Since it's a language class, there's a lot of work. However, the pacing is good and if you start work early, you won't struggle. In this class, you'll actually learn Chinese well.
Good lecturer but tended to repeat the same thing over and over in class. And her english is sometimes difficult to understand.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Professor Yue is awesome! She pays attention to all her students and takes the time to understand us not only as students, but as individuals. My favorite part of learning in her class is how interesting she makes it (i.e. if we have trouble recognizing a character, she'll tell us a story to help us remember the character itself and its meaning).

As a professor, she is one of the best I have ever had. Not only does she truly care for the students and what they are able to take away from her class, but she does see the effort that the students put into her class. She tries to help clean up students' pronunciation whenever possible, so that the students speak as authentic Chinese as they can.

Best. Language Class. Ever. If you've heard that Chinese is super hard to learn and are worried about taking this class, don't be. Yue Laoshi is an amazing professor and you can really tell that she cares about teaching. If you're looking for an easy A, this isn't the class for you but if you want to learn Chinese, there isn't a better class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Yue Laoshi is a great instructor. Fully recommend. If you put in the work, she respects you. Even if you don't, she will still push you but it is only because she cares about her students. A wonderful instructor.

Amazing professor. Yue Lao shi cares about all of her students. You can tell just by being around her that she wants every student to succeed. The workload is what you make of it. If you don't understand something she will gladly go back and review. She takes a lot of time to go beyond the textbook but the quizzes/tests are based on the textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I absolutely loved her teaching style and class time. Most people wanted to be in class all the time because we enjoyed learning without feeling too much pain from homework or stress from the material. I honestly wish that all classes were run the same way because Chinese I has sparked my love for love for learning all over again.

Professor Yue is the most dedicated professors to a course that I have ever been taught by in my four years at RPI. She provides excellent feedback and teaches the material excellently. Class time is very productive and stimulating. She also provides opportunities for students to practice the language outside of the classroom with native speakers.

Yue laoshi was excellent, showing a great wealth of knowledge way beyond what was expected. She know the entire history and origin of every single character and had great background and cultural information for many of the topics covered. She was also very aware of the difficulties in learning a new language and was very patient and understanding.

This course is quite time intensive but that is expected of a language course. The course was very enjoyable and the students really got to interact with each other. Professor Yue was always ready to enthusiastically help any student and answer any questions about the course or other subjects related to the course.

Professor Yue did a fantastic job ensuring that all students were familiar with a given topic and set of words before moving on. She doesn't just teach content but the reasoning and understanding behind the content. She is always trying to find ways to improve the classroom experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Yue Laoshi singlehandedly helped me discover what I'm passionate about, and she's made my time at RPI invaluable. She is incredibly caring and will do everything she can to help you succeed. I've never met another professor who cares about her students as much as Yue Laoshi, and I don't think I ever will. I highly recommend her classes.

Yue Lao shi cares so much about her students. She truly loves teaching. She always does her best to make herself available for students, and when she helps you she does so in the kindest way possible. She understands that her students top priority is not her class but their major work, and she's always considerate of that.

Yue Laoshi is hands down one of the best professors at RPI. I have taken Chinese 2-5 with Yue Laoshi and can say the class is always fun, interesting, and interactive--you get to learn so much culture beyond just the language. Additionally, the class size is small so you get to know your class and amazing prof. I would highly recommend this class!

I've never met another professor who has put in as much effort at Prof. Yue. She is a very caring prof who gives it her all so that her students can get the most out of class and do well. She is always there to help you with anything you need. Lots of work (presentations, dialogue performances, quizzes and workbook HW) but you'll learn for sure.

I learned a lot in this class. I do have prior experience with Mandarin because I speak it at home. Even so, however, I came into the class without the ability to read or write any Chinese characters.
