After finishing this class, I can now say that I can confidently recognize and write nearly all of the characters I learned in class.

Yue Laoshi has an amazing ability to instill in her students a high regard for and robust understanding of the Chinese language and culture. She takes care to address the learning needs of each and every student and is always accessible. Class is fun, so going to class does not feel mandatory despite the attendance policy. The work is manageable.
Meh

Yue laoshi's class is clear and although attendance is mandatory class is fun to attend. There is a fair amount of work, but if properly paced the workload actually seems rather light and learning is not difficult as Yue laoshi does her best to answer any and all questions. She's also very accessible through office hours and email. Would recommend.

Yue Laoshi is one of the best professors that I have had at RPI. She genuinely cares about her students and you can tell that she absolutely loves teaching. The class is not hard, per se, but very homework intensive. You have to study a lot and put a bit of time in to the course. If you think this will be an easy A, don't take a class with her.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Caring

reviews.comment: There are only a few professors who really care about their students in RPI, and Yue Laoshi is definitely one of them. To me, she's like a family member because cares about everyone in her class. She makes sure that all students are at the same pace. I got a B in her class because her class is relatively challenging. Overall she is a great teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Yue Laoshi is the singular best teacher I have had here at RPI. While her course can be challenging and intense, she is committed to going above and beyond for her students, and will go any lengths to inspire and encourage those in her class. She approaches each student as an individual, addressing their specific needs and deficiencies, and pushing

Excellent professor. As a senior, with six years of college semesters behind me, I have never had a college professor that cared so much about their students. She constantly puts effort into trying to accommodate for students, gives constructive and helpful feedback, and makes everyone feel included.

There are few language teachers like Yue Laoshi. She is very caring and accessible to students if they need help in class. Gives plenty of extra credit to encourage learning. Class structure is ideal and the syllabus is concise and clear.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: God-tier language teacher. If you're trying to learn, you'll get a lot our of this class.

Yue laoshi is a professor who really cares about her students. She is an exceptional teacher and always keeps her class interesting and engaging. I always look forward to class because of the enthusiasm she brings on a daily basis. It seems like all of her students are always hard workers because of the environment she sets.

Professor Yue is by far one of the best professors I have taken a class with here. She makes class interesting and makes you want to learn more from her. She often tells jokes and stories about a certain character to help students understand it more. Although the homework and projects may seem like a lot, it won't be if you properly space it out.

Yue is the best professor I've ever had. When it comes to teaching Chinese, she is enthusiastic and overqualified. The environment of the class during lectures is lively and joyous, unlike other language classes. Active participation is expected and advised, and errors made during class are not mistakes but enjoyable learning experiences.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: One of the best professors hands down. Very experienced teacher. Extremely nice. Especially great for first-time learners. Some ppl say a lot of homework, but only true if you let it pile up (only 2 hrs/wk avg). Most important thing is GENUINE effort/motivation. You'll learn a TON of Chinese stress-free, and love doing it, & should be a natural A.
Amazing professor who cares a lot about her students and their success. Definitely among the top professors I've ever had.

Professor Yue is a very supportive and caring teacher. Chinese is a very tough language to learn and Yue makes a point patient and enthusiastic every single day. She offers individual feedback to each student and shows them specific mistakes and how to solve them. Overall I genuinely enjoyed her class, she made learning Chinese fun.

She really takes the time to make sure every student has what they need to succeed. The class is by no means an easy one and requires a lot of work, but as a student, you have everything you need to do well in the class if you are willing to put in the work. The most important thing in any of her classes is being involved and showing that you care
If you do the all the work, you'll do well. She's a great teacher who really cares about her students.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Yue is personal and cares about each of her students. She focuses on providing opportunities for her students to improve their Mandarin outside of the classroom such as in Conversation Corner. She is interesting during class and does a great job going above and beyond, teaching not only what, but also why.

Yue is one of the best profs at RPI. She genuinely tries to make learning a fun experience for everyone, which is a pleasant change from most RPI profs. She's super sweet, however, you will get out of her class what you decide to put into it. It can be an easy A if you do the work or it can be an incredibly easy D if you miss more than 2 classes.

Prof. Yue is the type that expects a lot out of you and at the same time gives you've everything you need to meet those expectations. If you are planning on taking Chinese at RPI, don't expect an easy A, but expect to be able to get an A with the right effort. Definitely one of my fav professors so far.

What separates her from the rest of the professors at this school is her passion and ability to inspire her students. Her class had a steady stream of hw and quizzes every week, which was an appropriate work load and kept me engaged in learning. If you are considering taking any Chinese class with her, i highly recommend it!

Seems strict at first, but if you put in the effort, it's very easy to do well in her class.  Going to class is mandatory, and you will fail class if you don't, however, participation is a huge part of your grade and as long as you at try to contribute you'll get 90-100% easy. Has dialogue and culture presentations so you aren't just taking tests .
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Prof Yue is an excellent professor. You can tell she is very dedicated to her work and she genuinely wants her students to learn and excel in the Chinese language. B/c of that, expect to work a bit to get a good grade, but learning the material isn't too hard since she's is great at teaching and she's always eager to help students if they need it

Prof Yue is enthusiastic about teaching language and she does a good job incorporating Chinese culture into the class. She's often available to help students when they need it and is very approachable.

Professor Yue does an outstanding job at breaking down the foreign language learning process into a way that is easy for students to learn. By easy to learn, I mean that I was never without direction in the course. Learning a new language can be overwhelming and discouraging, and Professor Yue was always available to explain material in a new way.

Excellent professor overall. Very passionate about you actually learning Chinese. A lot of focus on speaking with proper tones. Expects a lot from her students, but not too much. Is very reasonable and knows that for most students this is not their major or even their minor.

Yue Laoshi is a really great professor. She cares a lot about her students and tries her best to meet everyone's needs while still moving through the material at a good pace. Expect to have to work hard, but you'll be rewarded for your effort. I hope to take more courses with her in the future.
Great professor, great course. There's a decent bit of work in the course, but it's fair for the content. Just wish I wasn't swamped with other courses this semester.

This was a great course. It was a much needed break from the technical work at RPI.  This class is by no means an easy A you do have to work for it, but it's not back breaking work. Lecture is very interactive and fun you learn a lot about the culture and plenty of Chinese jokes. Professor Yue is so dedicated to helping her students.

She keeps the course very interesting. We learn something new nearly everyday. There hasn't been a boring moment in her class. She's very knowledgeable in her field of expertise and provides clear easy to understand feedback to students.
It's a jam packed class in with a great teacher who wants to see her students succeed. Stay on schedule and do well on the quizzes and you will be fine.
Very considerate to every students. She makes a language class, which is supposed to be hard, easy and fun.

Great and fun professor, goes out of her way to be available to help. She wants to give you an A, just study for the quizzes and you're golden. I don't think I got below a 90 on anything I handed in on time.
Professor Yue is phenomenal.

Chinese is definitely a tough language to learn, but Professor Yue puts a ton of work into making it possible for you, and clearly tries to support each student.  Plus she's super nice, though you are expected to do work.

Yue Laoshi is a wonderful Professor that truly loves teaching, and her love for teaching is what really makes her so great. She cares so much about her students and wants to see everyone succeed. She is a very understanding woman too and is very easy to talk with. If you are struggling at all, talk to her and she will help any possible way she can.
Yue Laoshi is a great teacher. She is very clear about what she expects out of you, and very helpful. She can be a little harsh at times, but overall, her courses are relatively straight-forward.
She's just everything you need to learn chinese

Dr.Klein's lectures are interesting because the content is interesting and he tends to tie the concepts to real world medical or scientific examples. His exams are difficult because the short response can be on topics that are barely covered and grading for those is tough. There is a lot of extra credit to raise your grade. Do back exams!

Wasn't the biggest fan of him for BIOL2120, but he's great for BIOL4740. He's a very lenient grader (unlike the TAs for BIOL2120) and provides thoughtful feedback on lab reports/project papers. He's not the best at responding to emails, but he is very accessible in person.

Very tough class and the material is hard to grasp so go to the mentors for help. Attendance isn't mandatory however it's easier to grasp the material if you go. DO the extra credit!! Drawing out the processes from the textbook is very helpful. DON'T memorize the notes you have to understand the processes.

Lectures are 2 hours straight with no breaks. He reads directly off slides, puts in no effort to engage, and assigns all auto-graded HW on day one. This allows him to do no work outside of the classroom. Tests are overly detailed with averages in the 50s. Extra credit exists just to boost grades. He's often late, and mentor support is inconsistent.

Professor Klein reads directly from the slides and that's it. The class is extremely difficult. Tests cover over 200 detailed slides, many of which aren't even on the exam, and grading is harsh. He lectures for two hours without breaks, making it hard to focus. He's also terrible at responding to emails and relies on extra credit to boost grades.

The exams had questions that didn't pertain to anything even touched that much during the lectures. The lectures were too much material in a short amount of time. Very tough grader and the class was unnecessarily hard for a subject that isn't even that difficult.

Micheal Klein outs himself as never once being invited to a party by writing in his syllabus that the quizzes are "from 6AM to midnight on Wednesdays" and by some miracle of incompetence meaning that they are meant to be done on Tuesday, even though every other assignment IS due on Wednesdays.

Dr.Klein knows his stuff but is an awful professor. He rambles during lectures and if you are not specific in the free response section of his exam you'll never get higher than a 65 on his tests. He also sets up review sessions but never checks to see if the mentors can make it so about 50% there is no mentor to help you prepare for your exams.

Dr. Klein is a respectable scientist, but he is not the greatest professor. He tends to forget that it is a course designed for first-year biology majors. He wasted the majority of lecture time rambling about irrelevant information, which made his exams more challenging than necessary. You also must memorize over 200 slides per exam to do well.
Dr.Klein is a very tough grader and if you don't write the answer he wants then you will get no points on the open ended parts of his exam.

exams ar every hard and does not understand the level the students are at. So he has to give back multiple points on the exams because questions are too hard. he does have extra credit tho so thats good
bad communicator and very hard exams

Cell and molec bio is a weed out class, so it's hard by design. Dr. Klein teaches the material well, though, and you can come into lecture for the online tests so you can ask him questions. Very smart guy. Labs were a lot of fun but the reports were long. Extra credit was offered both for the AEFIS survey and for posting on the discussion board.

He isn't an "exciting" lecturer, but he is organized and clear. Reserved but extremely nice & caring towards his students. I had him during covid (online) and he did little cute things for class like starting all his lectures with a montage of frogs, or listening to jazz during exams on WebEx.Grading is clear. Exam content is from the PowerPoints.

This class is much harder than Intro to Biology, so be prepared to actually study. There is a lot of homework for this course, pre- and post-class. Dr. Klein has a clear understanding of what his students' background knowledge is, so don't be afraid to ask "dumb" questions because he will happily answer them.
BIOL 2120 with Dr. Klein was much harder than taking it with other professors. Tests and quizzes are extremely tough.

She seems nice at first but is actually extremely rude. Class is easy, but I honestly did not understand the point of playing a tedious game for 60% of class time that she claimed would help us "stick" to the course content.

She is very passionate about a subject I cannot care less about. Be prepared for lengthy readings and lectures with tedious discussion and classmates that believe they are much smarter than they are. That said, the class is very easy to do well in. Just try to keep your sanity as you sit through the class.
Incredibly easy class, she lowered the required number of assignments multiple times over the semester. Class was also very boring.
Throughout the year made the changed the syllabus to make the class easier and massively decreased the amount of work required. (went from 16 down to 9 essays and from 3 to 2 revised essays).

Prof. Tyrol gave interesting lectures with class discussions, and graded very fairly imo. She was very clear about rubrics and very accessible to help you understand material and improve your work. That being said, do pay close attention to your final paper--it is your biggest grade, will be graded the strictest, and you can always get her help.

This professor loves yelling at students and is always angry. I have never met a professor who shouts more than she does in a 2 hour period. She once yelled at a student for asking for a tissue. She knows her stuff and has a passion for the class, but I just wish she had a better attitude.

While the course was very easy the professor has the worst attitude ever. Someone will ask a simple question and she will find a way to yell at them. She yelled at a poor girl in my class for using the bathroom. The textbooks are free though which is nice. The class itself is also very easy but I would not take another course with this professor.

I only had Dr. Tyrol for lecture and a TA for recitation, so I can only speak on that, but I found her lectures to be interesting and she really cares about what she is teaching. In terms of workload, if you space out the assignments and plan when to do journal entries and start the final paper, this class is a breeze.

Engaging lectures. Frequently changed the syllabus. Added in-class assignments on the last two days, not outlined in the syllabus (DO NOT SKIP). Altered attendance policy mid-semester. Wouldn't recommend her section—opt for a TA, as they grade more fairly. I had a great experience with my TA, but Tyrol is reportedly a tough grader.

I thought it was an overall good class! A lot of reading and a large essay as a final but not bad if you get a head start on your work! Dr. Tyrol gave several really interesting lectures but some of them were just plain boring!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Took Sociology with Dr. T this summer. Very fun lectures, participation is critical so make sure you do the assigned readings(textbook is free)& stay active during classes. She doesnt reply emails often, make sure u book appointments w her in person, she's very accesible. DO NOT use chatgpt for anything, she will catch you and you won't learn!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: made me waste 100 dollars

Local History was a super fun class and Dr. Tyrol did a great job making the course as their first time teaching it! Not a lot of homework, except for an archives trip and field trip for the final paper. Not much going on in lecture though you get extra credit if you participate.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Tyrol is really well educated and the topics she chooses to teach are very engaging. She summarizes articles very well and does a good job at looking at multiple perspectives. She's really kind and cares about her students. She will sometimes alter the coursework schedule and/or let students have the day off to give them extra time to work.

Dr. Tyrol was a very nice and caring professor - she made the class very easy and it was a very interesting class. I learned a lot about the way artificial intelligence works, and even though some of the reading was long it was very informative and intriguing.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Tyrol cares about her students and will adjust the curriculum and workload of the class to accommodate you. She constantly asks for input about her lectures and is very open-minded. The class is very easy, just read and bring some ideas to the discussions (the whole class is discussion-based). One final essay as a final.

Prof Szczesniak is so kind and he answered so many of my questions. This class is so fun and not at all stressful. Just show up, try, and take the super easy online quizzes and you'll be fine. You are also allowed to stop going to class once you finish your project, which is super helpful when the end of the semester gets busy.

John is a funny guy who wants to share his passion for machining. The class is easy and you'll likely finish your project with a month remaining. The instruction manual is confusing but John and the TAs are happy to answer questions. It's a chill 1 credit class.

Prof. John is an incredible machinist and amazing at teaching how to machine safely. He is very smart and very reasonable and very understanding. If you read the manual provided, and follow safety protocols, you will pass SO easily. And if you get stuck, ask the TAs or him for help, and you will pass just as easily.
Key: read manual, don't be dumb!

Extremely knowledgeable of every single tool inside of the lab. Amazing and sarcastic personality, is extremely funny, and you come out of the class with true knowledge of various tools. Don't be afraid to ask him questions, and there's more than ample amount of open hours provided.
John is a really funny guy who's always around to lend you a hand if you're stuck or need help fixing a problem. The class is really easy if you show up, and a lot of fun!

John is very knowledgeable on all things Processes, but sometimes his sarcasm and dry humor can rub you the wrong way. The course was restructured this semester, but the course material wasn't fully updated, leading to confusion on what was expected of us. Very time consuming class for a 1 credit pass/fail, but you will learn a lot.
John is my favorite prof at RPI so far. He has a strong personality --- expect him to be quippy --- but his class is an easy A and absolutely rules.

Great Course with a great professor. It is a major change of pace from the typical lectures in most courses, and instead, learning how to use the heavy machines in base engineering. The professor is very funny, and also informative of what your supposed to do.
The class is easy and the lab manual tells you everything you need to know. Just read it a bit beforehand and ask questions when you need help. The TA's are very nice.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: easy class

You have to be a real muppet to fail this class. Also, nothing the negative comments say is true coming from someone who asked him a crap ton of questions. If you are also in IED, you can go ask him for advice on how to do things and he will give you fantastic ideas and let you use his machines to complete it. Overall very knowledgeable guy.

He is such an awesome guy -- pretty much an overgrown child who likes making things and I mean that in the nicest way possible. He'll let you use anything in the shop and just finish your project and you'll get an A. If the TAs don't know what to do, he always does.

I personally didn't care for this class, but as long as you actually read the manual and try things before you ask him for help, he's super helpful. He can be a little intimidating, but just remember you aren't the first or last person to ask him for help. Do your labs and finish your project on time and you will be fine.
He was extremely knowledgeable and respected by his students

John's class was my favorite class last semester. He sends out a manual at the beginning of the semester to help with the machines, schedules of the other labs, and more. You only have to attend class until your project is completed and when you are scheduled for the welding and plastics labs.  TAs and John are very fun and helpful.

John has some hilarious stories and does everything he can to help you learn on your own, especially letting you make mistakes and making you find answers in the lab manual. Passing his class is easy, just show up and participate every week and put effort into your lab report. You also learn a lot from helping your partner.

This was a Pass/No Credit class and was extremely easy. John grades the projects lightly. He comes off rude when you ask for help but just ask the TAs. Read the manual though because all the answers are there.

John is friendly, full of stories and cracks witty jokes to lighten up the class. He is always ready to help if you get stumped, however the year's project instructions are pretty easy and detailed in the manual. Make sure to complete the training video/test in the beginning of the year, he becomes a stickler about it later on.

I really enjoyed professor John's classes. He always had good stories to tell and plenty of knowledge to share with others. He was always willing to help students whenever they got stuck with the projects, but keep an eye on the safety course at the beginning; I forgot and he made me go back to the dorm and do it.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Hilarious

reviews.comment: This is THE machine shopman. He can be callous and rough, however, he has got your best interests at heart. He can seem intimidating but will help you in a moments notice (e.g lathe difficulties). However, GET YO LABS DONE. For engr processes, if you don't finish the Cannon Barrel Project, the two labs, the report AND the final - he will fail you.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Perfectly fits the trope of experienced machinist. He is funny, and very intelligent in the sphere of machining. Highly reccomend if you can get him. He grades by if your final project looks vaguely like what its supposed tofrom 10ft away.

Just read the manual and you will be fine. He wont answer some questions because he wants you to learn and figure it out on your own. If you are really struggling though he will help you. Really hard to fail.

John was really funny for Engineering Processes. He is very helpful but loves to mock you if you ask a question the lab manual answers. His manual is very long but very easy to follow. Class is easy if you get everything done on time. Very hard to fail. Don't even need to go to your assigned lab meeting unless your have a specific lab that day.

Was not helpful at all. Anytime you ask a question, he refuses to answer it directly and will refer you to the class manual. Become friends with your TA's, because they will provide any help that you need.

Interested in safety first, but challenges you to learn on your own; does not feed you answers.  It can be tough to ask questions because he expects you to know what you're asking (not just.. help what do I do next).
Good guy and always helpful when you need, though a bit sarcastic if you are asking a stupid question.

John isn't a bad guy, but he's quite a bit nicer to girls than to guys.  If you're a guy, he'll probably make you feel dumb at least once during the class.  He expects people to at least have common sense and be safe, so do that.  Processes is pretty easy though, as long as you remember your safety glasses and your instructions every class.

Had him for processes. I only talked to him a few times because I soon realized that he was not very helpful and a bit of a stuck up brat. He expects you to know the answer to every question, even if you are the one asking, otherwise he'll try to make you look stupid.

Worst professor I have ever had. He constantly made fun of my accent and questions. I was the first one in my section to finish the project but still was made fun of. The TA's are amazing. Anything you need they can help you

Great hands on guy. Yeah he yells a bit, and **** a lot, but you can't deny that he's good at what he does-machining. Suck it up. The final is just from the lab manual, and you surely can get a lab report somewhere. And yeah, it's pass/fail.

He's a suck up for girls. If you are a girl, he'll know your name within the first week, if you are a guy you're lucky if he knows it in 2 years. Watched a female TA of his ram a .500" endmill at 3200rpm into a piece of aluminum stock and sheared the mill clean off. John smiled at her and yelled at me. I was just watching...

Very unhelpful. Questions will be answered with a question or an unclear "sure, you *can* do that" which just means you're doing it wrong. Obviously knows everything there is to know and decides not to actually help the students in Processes. Good luck if you don't walk in already knowing how to use all the equipment.

I had John for processes and now I'm a TA for him. When he isn't around, it's because he's fixing things, or helping people in the other labs. If you can't figure it out from the manual, the TA's have the answers, or else John does. Don't be stupid and you won't get yelled at. John knows practically everything about machining.
Very easy going.  Don't see him often.  You get most of your questions answered by TAs.
John is incredibly helpful.

This guy is useless and a complete ****.  He doesn't teach.  He simply gets paid to do nothing.  Very unhelpful if you have a question.  With the amount of time he spends chillin behind the plastic glass wall or chatting with Ta's, I am surprised not one of the untrained students he is to look after hasn't killed them self on a machine yet.

Extremely flexible.  if you didnt like your class time, you could come into the shop during open hours and do your project then.  extremely nice guy too... only he is a little protective of his machines (understandable, they're really expensive).
No Comments

Didn't have him for processes, but he was VERY helpful in IED.  He had a lot of helpful ideas and he was willing to take the time to help us work on our project or fix problems.  He is very knowledgable and even though he is often quite busy, it's worth the wait for the help and advice he gives you.

so mean. if u do something wrong, he comes up to u and gives u a disgusted stare and says what are u doing? it feels like kindergarten, when the teacher disapproves of u. makes u feel so bad! the manual is so long and ur expected to find it urself. he doesnt tell u anything and expects u to know everything.

Don't down John, He's a great guy if u get to know him a little bit and a lasting relationship has gotten me a TA job and a URP.  The class itself is a cake walk if u put in the time and itll priceless for IED.  Nothings worse than and IED kid coming in not having seen a lathe before.  Anyway Johns the man.

This guy just sucks, that's all there is to it. If you haven't had shop before, good luck. He doesn't teach at all in class (you're expected to know what to do from the lab manual) and don't expect any help from him. As said, if you need help, go to the TAs, although most of them aren't much better.

I don't know what this guy does all day. He certainly doesn't bother to help anyone in his class, just leaves it to the TA's, who aren't much better. Good luck if you don't have much experience in a shop.

Yea, he's a jerk.  Don't bother asking him any questions, he won't answer them.  Just go to the TA's, they'll help you out if you have a problem.  Remember it's a pass/fail course so your project doesn't have to be "perfect."  Just do it and don't worry about the minor details and you'll be fine.
The guy is an ass.  He is so full of himself and acts very unprofessional.  Not very helpful at all.  Needs to start hanging with people his age.
Awesome.  Don't break his machines.  He will beat the crap out of you.
Very helpful during both processes and IED.  He knows what he is doing and ensures a factor of safety in the shop.  Highly recommmended
Very competent and definitely knows his stuff.
This guy was just full of himself.  I needed no helo in the shop, I have used the machines before, but he seemed to laugh at people who did need help, not a nice thing to do.

While everyone else is correct that he is cool, note that I missed the one plastic lab which his underlings told me not to worry about and yet he ruthlessly flunked me.  Perhaps because the course is considered a joke.

John is awesome.  One of smartest and friendliest people on campus.  I wish he could teach all of my classes.  (he probably knows enough about engineering to acutally teach most any class here)  Seriously, if you need help with anything at all, go to him.  John you ROCK!
Great guy, if you put in the effort he's great to learn from. Highly recommended class, and a lot of fun.

Dealt with John in Processes and IED.  He enjoys making fun of you if you don't know what you're doing in processes but if you need help making something for IED later on he's going to be your best friend, seriously.  Extremely helpful for IED, period.

This class rocks and John is awesome.  Always very helpful, especially if you show that you're making an effort to follow the instructions and get it right.  Be stupid and get treated as such.  Be intelligent and you'll love the whole class.
Cool guy, the class is lots of fun! Make a cannon, it rules!
Take this class even if you dont have to.  You learn a lot and have fun.  My cannon actually fired a .036 musket ball.
awesome prof!  lots of fun! :)  and cannon rules!
No Comments
John is da man. Period. And Catapults ROCK!
Does he actually live in the machine shop? And if not, does he teach anything else? It's all about the canon!!!

Mr. Machine shop, knows every single thing there is to know about anything that has to do with metal.  Read the lab manual, because he will enjoy belittling you if you don't know something thats in it. Easy class. (CATAPULT!)

Amazing great prof. FOAM was in 3 sections: 1) perturbation-many pages of algebra but interesting 2) modeling-easy, watch kramer fumble with python for a few lectures 3) nightmare. Few HWs but very long each. Up to 75% bonus credit on some! Just awesome though, he's the best prof i've had at RPI

The lectures were virtually incomprehensible in the latter half of the course without being a math major or having a significant 4000-level math background like FOAM. The professor definitely made things seem harder than they were by doing expansive derivations that virtually none could follow along with.

difficult but rewarding. lecture notes are the best i've ever seen and the practice exams are immaculate. diffeq had 3 different back exams for each exam, each exercising the concepts from a different angle. even if you skip every lecture, you can get over 100% as long as you read the lecture notes and work hard to fully understand back exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Really great professor, he is very helpful and his classes are very interesting. However, FOAM with him is probably the hardest course I've ever taken at RPI. Homeworks take sooo long, however there aren't too many of them. You will get a lot out of this class though. I would strongly recommend, but not for the faint of heart.

Good teacher, class isn't as hard as others say most just dont go to class. If you go and understand the equations, you'll be fine. Lots of extra credit on tests and through weekly quizzes.  Does tend to ramble but he lets you know so you can tune out. Very helpful during office hours and does post back exams which are helpful for studying.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Avoid unless you have to take diffeq in this semester and its the only professor's class you can get into. Kam is so much better, take her. The grade is all exams, so if you don't do well on exams or have test anxiety this class will be very stressful. He also tailors the lectures towards math major when I'm sure 95% of the class aren't them.

He tends to delve into the deep analysis problems a little too much, and while this is helpful for math majors, it might not be for everybody and can get mundane. Going over examples of problems that would be on the test I feel would be more helpful.

Dr. Kramer is definitely better than most people think, although his lectures can get boring. While your grade is entirely based on the exams, he gives several extra credit opportunities, including weekly quizzes on a homework problem. Be prepared to think through the modeling problems he emphasizes! He also tries to know his students by name.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dont. Take. Kramer. IF you didn't get into Kam's diff eqs, drop it and take Multivar. Tests were 100% of the grade. The tests (1,2,3) averages were 67, 62, 47 with deviations of 24, 26, 26. Final was optional which was an avg of 60/135. The positive reviews for this guy are literally just sabotage, so here are the actual facts. GPA ANCHOR, trust me
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I think that Dr. Kramer is an underrated teacher. He has a sense of humor and is an EXTREMELY generous grader. I am aware that one's grade relies entirely on test scores, however, given that he is generous on partial credit and 20-35% extra credit is available for each test, a score less than satisfactory is entirely one's own doing. Pay attention.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
It's a hard class, but Kramer makes it easy to do well (given you work your ass off).  Kramer's lectures were clear and concise.  The only grade in the course is the tests and maybe some quizzes.  Lots of extra credit but don't expect to earn much of it.  keep up with the notes and homework

Took this class with AP calc BC credit and did well.

Loved Prof. Kramer.  Although this is a tricky class, Kramer's teaching methods were very clear and concise.  Lots of extra credit on the tests but don't expect to rely on it carrying your grade.  If you study hard and take notes during lectures it's not too hard to get A's on tests.
He knows his stuff. So he is great at answering questions, but that also means he goes very fast in lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Avoid Diffeq with Kramer if you can. Lectures were fine for the most part, but he would do very few example problems and instead say "you can zone out for the next 15 minutes, you don't need to know this." You have to be very self-sufficient to succeed in this class, with lots of independent learning. Was unnecessarily hard. Exam 2  worst one.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Exams are pretty much the only grades that you are going to get in this class and that can either be very beneficial or detrimental depending on if you understand the course content very well.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: AVOID AT ALL COST. I have to take this class to graduate, but this class is killing me. He gives five homework for a semester, and it takes at least two days to complete each one. His homework is not actually relevant to his lecture notes, so you have to know a lot about complex variables outside the class to get an A or B.

Lectures were smooth and enjoyable. Applying them for the assignments will probably be more challenging. His class is an A for one of two kinds of people: the bright and the hard working. If you are neither don't expect an A.
Do not take his class if you are graduate student. He gives Cs to graduate students. Very bad grader.

Dude managed to take off points even though I had the right answers with the right work. He's a horrible grader. Do not take his classes because the grading is unfair. He single handedly ruined my academic career.

One of the more difficult DiffEq professors I'd imagine. Lectures are a bit confusing. His background is mathematical modeling, so his tests are extremely difficult. However, every test has a possibility of getting at least a 125/100 with all the extra credit. Plus, his recitation quizzes add 1% to your final grade for every one you get right.

The lectures are extensive, thorough, but boring. It took all I had to stay engaged. He's very smart and very helpful during office hours, but the lectures are hard to sit through and he rambles a bit. Tests 1 and 3 were pretty similar to back exams in difficulty, but test 2 came out of nowhere, so there's a little inconsistency.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Worst math professor ever in my entire life! Patrice exam will nothing like the real exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He has boring lectures with already filled paragraphs long lecture notes which are very difficult to follow during lectures. Exam questions are far different than practice exams and it is almost impossible to get extra points unless you're on top of the materials. There are no TA hours to help you either just office hours.
The practice final exam is nothing like the actual exam. He is smart, but not really good at explaining the questions.

Not an ez A class, but also hard to pass, in terms of he is giving lots of bonus but meaningless. He won't really help you when you have no idea about the homework. The practice exam is easy, and the actual exam is really another world. But, you do learn stuff from his class. Of course, most depend on yourself.
Lectures often contain topics that are not important for tests. Tests end up covering material he barely goes over.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Very intelligent man but he doesn't know how to be a teacher. If you're only looking to get your math requirements, avoid him. Otherwise, you'll be placed in a class with an extremely high bar that requires mostly self-learning/motivation to succeed. Extremely disappointed with my experience. Ruined my GPA and wasted my time.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: A lot of homework with really huge extra credit which is no way to get. The hardest course

By far the most awful math experience of my life. I know I know, it sounds like I just had a bad time. There is no curve, your grade depends primarily on the tests, and the tests feel like they're written in another language. If you get above a 70% you're doing better than the vast majority. Wish I could go back in time and stop myself.

This was the worst math experience I've ever had. Not only were his lectures terribly boring and useless, his tests were insanely hard and lacked the ability to accurately assess my knowledge of the subjects at hand. He would also ramble about things we didn't need to know during class which wasted time he could have use to better explain the topic

Probably the best lecturer I've had. He teaches the material extremely well, going beyond the sequential and formulaic methods and really giving good understanding. He has optional homework which helps gain extra credit and the tests are easy A if you know how to do the math. If you are mathematically strong, he will be easy and you will learn a lot

A little awkward, and boring lectures, but not too hard to do well on the exams. Exams are similar to the back tests. Goes into details for the people that care about the subject, and doesn't require that knowledge for the people that don't care too much.

I found Kramer's lectures to be SO BORING. Could not stay awake in class. He is so smart, but he sometimes goes on and on about things that we don't need to know, and he admits that we don't need to know that! I did not do well on his test and that's what your final grade is based on. He's smart, but I wasn't convinced he should be teaching a class

Not many homeworks but they were super hard. The last homework of the semester had a median score in the 30's. Tests were very hard but had a lot of bonus points as a safety net for students who really understood what was going on. Even though it was difficult it was a really good class. Id take another class with him if I had the opportunity.
He's tough but you will learn a lot from him. Going to office hours can really help and he's a cool nice guy. But getting an A is tough and questionably possible.

One of the smartest people I've ever met and a great teacher. If you go to lecture and pay attention, you will learn Diff Eq. Otherwise you will not do well. Felt like I had actually learned by the end of the class, which is very rare among other professors for this course. He's kinda awkward but super nice and his tests have a lot of extra credit.
He is extremely smart and extremely good at teaching. He made hard things so easy to understand.

Quite monotonous and thorough. I called it "DiffEq for math majors." His tests aren't linear, but studying his back exams can help. His tests are a bit difficult and LONG, so study a lot. Optional final brought me from a B- to an A in the class. Lots of extra credit on tests! By the end, I felt like I understood the material quite well.
Good Professor!
Great class, great professor. The homework problems were particularly helpful.

He did a good job teaching the material, which is something that most of the people teaching 2000-level math courses at RPI have a problem with. However, his tests never resembled the back tests he claimed they would, or any of the material in the class or homeworks for that matter.
Dr. Kramer is an excellent teacher who knows his stuff.  Made diff. eq. enjoyable, which is no small task.
Great Professor, very helpful and fair, responds to emails very quickly and explains things very well. Also very realistic.
Nice guy extremly smart extremly hard to pass.
Fabulous teacher.  Really presented the material in an organized manner that was easy to understand.  Always more than willing to give help, anytime.  Deffinitly take a course by him.
No Comments
Excellent professor and lecturer.  Work is ridiculously hard compared to examples and class materials

One of the smartest people on the campus, more likely in all of New York. Could teach applied math to a monkey, though that is often what you feel like once you start work on the homework. O and if it's due in 2 weeks, you start NOW. Tough but great.
Excellent teacher and lecturer.  Knows the material very well.  Also a nice guy.
His homeworks are ridiculous.  He is extremely anal.  Knows the material very well but you better study because the tests will kill you.
Boring lectures.

Not the most engaging lecturer, but I found the course to be mostly straightforward, and exams were relatively easy. The homeworks are pretty important, so take your time with them. I did Alpha Labs, and I thought that they were extremely easy, but you do get to do some cool stuff.

Ok lecturer who was nice/easy to understand. Pacing could be an issue, with too much time on easy content and not enough on harder stuff. Answer keys were often wrong, requiring grade challenges. Exams and HW were straightforward but very tedious. Labs didn't always align with lecture. Do Omega labs; not much harder and free points on the final.

Native speaker of English. Understands the teaching topic very well. Was never mean to the class, never saw her get angry. Sometimes ends lecture early if she gets through the content early. Have no complaints about her. Definitely one of the better EE professors at RPI.

Prof Kelly is awesome--she's a great lecturer and her assignments are fair in my opinion. Definitely choose which set of labs you do wisely; I would not recommend doing omega lab C since the final exam problem it equated too was way easier.

Dr. Kelly is new, it's her first time teaching CoCO. She's really nice and answers questions asked on Webex quickly and efficiently. Lectures are a little boring but it's not honestly her fault, she's just going through the content she was given and makes honest improvements. She gives good and fair tests, much better than back exams.
standard middle of the road professor. Lectures can be quite boring, since she does many examples of the same concept, however it can be great for review. Overall 5/10 professor.
I feel bad, Kuzmin is kind, smart, and passionate but painfully boring and gets shafted with the most tedious classes. Like the prof, hate the lectures and tests.

I've had dr. kuzmin 3 times now, comp org, prog lang, and now db systems. He's a genuine, respectful, knowledgeable professor. Specifically for DB, i thought the exams were lengthy (esp exam 1) but honestly fair in terms of content. But the time it has taken to get things back like hw grades, exam grades, is outrageous. Lots of extra credit tho...

We had 5 hw's in this class and an extra credit hw. The final was today and we have had 2 hw's graded. I cannot emphasize enough that this is the worst class I have ever taken at RPI. Furthermore, the exams are much harder than whatever prep material he gives you, that is even if you have prep material at all. Never take a Kuzmin class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Enjoyable if you are in no other classes, however, the exams are unfair and hard to complete, and the grades are NOT put in in a timely manner at all. It has been over a month and we still can't see how we are doing past BEFORE THE FIRST EXAM. Do not recommend taking any classes with Kuzmin.

First exam half of it was algebraic operations. Mind you those questions are WAYYY harder than previous exams, more thought needed and harder to extract certain properties. Dont even get me started with finding the keys. The relations and FD's were almost double the size from literally last semesters exams every SINGLE question just took more time.

This class is like the SAT's. The problems themselves are easy and a child could do them. The most difficult part is not dropping dead of boredom while doing them. The tests and homeworks legitimately test your attention span more than your knowledge of the subject.

Poor lectures and does not give any exceptions even for sickness. His tests are poorly written and rely on the fact that you're given infinite crib sheets to make up for how badly the content is taught and tested.

Seems like a nice guy but he's really bad at lecturing; I almost fell asleep multiple times. I got above a 100 in the course thanks to a HW counting as extra credit b/c we fell behind schedule.

Exams were much harder than the practice material, but got graded generously. The TAs came in clutch.

Overall just a crappy experience and painful class.

I didnt find the class or exams hard, and with extra credit i had over a 100 in the class, so people complaining about the final are dramatic.  However kuzmin delivers terrible lectures, he is mostly rambling and repeating things multiple times. Seems like a nice guy but the lectures are unhelpful
Final was 20+ pages in 3 hours - less than 10 mins a page of which 95% was free response.......
Hardest final ever

During lecture, Kuzmin talks a lot, almost too much sometimes. It's even seen on the slides where there is just multiple slides that say the same thing in a different way. This year especially the exams were increasingly more difficult than previous exams, and even when people complained about the length, somehow the exams were even longer.
What a joke:

homework took many hours to implement, debug, and also infer and guess the hidden test cases
60% requirement on tests/exam to final made me fail course.
Lecture very hard to understand while quizzes impossible to do with lecture material alone.
The practice exam I receive before each tests was very different and also much easier than actual exam.s
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This has been a very stressful course :(

Way too much homework, and the grading criteria is very - very challenging. It seems as if it is certain that I will not be getting a good grade in this class.

Tough because of his HWs (in this class), which take forever to complete and are hard to get full points on. Tests are way easier then everyones says, short on time but if you understand the material not hard (not memorization based). Kuzmin is very very kind and easy to reach, but just not a good lecturer (especially in large classes, it seems)
anyone who rates this man higher than 1 star is LYING!!! do not believe them!!!!!

NEVER EVER TAKE ANY COURSE WITH PROF KUZMIN. He makes everything so necessarily complicated and always picks the hardest problems for tests!!! This class was extremely unbearable, and I actually tried to enjoy the course content. everything is a trick question or an impossible question. he does not care about your grade at any cost! worst prof here

Kuzmin is incompetent and should be fired. Expect large homework loads, to be unprepared for the material on the test, boring lectures, lagging course material, and weekly quizzes with trick questions that aren't on the slides.
Useless class, no important concept but unnecessarily long and hard exams, terrible class.

This was the most frustrating class I've ever taken at this school so far. His lectures are at least a week behind the schedule, meaning we have to review lectures not covered in class in order to complete homework on time. The quizzes given are unreasonable (though the TAs are very helpful, unlike Kuzmin), but the homework is not terribly hard.
Very hard tests and a lot of homework with little time to complete
I think this course may be my lowest grade

To preface: the professors are nice - however, the course itself is very tough. Rough tests and lots of homework. The hw themselves are a ton of work and the grading for them is insanely rough. If possible, avoid this class.....

A dry lecturer but is very knowledgeable about the topics so if you go to class and pay attention you will certainly learn enough to do well in the class. I've had very few professors who care as much as him. Only downsides are that the homework and exams are often on the long side and grades are not updated in a timely manner.

Prof. Kuzmin is a great teacher. He is one of the rare teachers at RPI that can actually teach without being boring. The only reason the class was empty was because it was 8 AM; otherwise, it could have been more full. But the class was really unorganized. Many of the HW weren't assigned on time and weren't graded for a month or even more.

One of the worst professors ever! DO NOT TAKE HIM! (unless you are ready to unalive yourself!!) Class isn't structured at all, doesn't care about students, exams make no sense (picks questions from somewhere and dumps it), unrealistic/delusional.

never really went for lectures except the ones where we had quizzes. tests weren't too bad. homeworks were pretty intense but nothing took took long. 

prof Kuzmin is very very good at debugging. he can almost find a bug in almost any program.

Okay lectures and notes, very caring. Occasionally assigns too much work but the amount of late days given can offset it. Exams aren't easy, but are fair and allows unlimited crib sheets. Assignments can be released late, but deadlines are extended to compensate.
Lecture is useless, show up because he gives extra credit because he realizes that showing up to lecture is a waste of time otherwise. Just a terrible experience overall.

Dr. Kuzmin is genuinely helpful in one-on-one encounters, but he was not well-suited to the task of teaching this course. He was constantly behind, both in lectures and assigning homework, to the point where the last homework was made extra credit (and it was painful to complete). Moreover, his tests were poorly designed and weighted improperly.

Really disorganized professor. Failed to upload the first homework for a whole month, then gave insanely challenging labs on some weeks, and super easy ones on others. Very poor lecturer as well - often just talks non-stop for an hour fifty. Highly recommend not taking a class with him.
I Envy those who werent required to take a class with him.

Kuzmin is a nice guy, I have noting to say that goes against that. But He had no clue how to manage this class. Our 2 hour labs were previous semester's week long assignment. The content in hw/lab were covered 2 weeks prior. Not to mention that the first homework was a month late and the schedule never adjusted well.
Cool guy but legit has almost zero common sense.
Although prof Kuzmin is not the best lecturer, his homeworks are informative and interesting. The exams are a bit tough tho... Stop coping y'all give him time and you will understand his class.

Will change quiz policy without telling students. For example, if a quiz is opened on submitty at 9:30 you would expect to be able to work on it until 10 (30 mins), but you have to submit by 9:55 to get credit even though the quiz says there is 5 minutes remaining. Anything submitted after 9:55 is a zero, no points deducted per minute. Ridiculous

Dr. Kuzmin is by far the worst professor I've ever had. He often lies in the syllabus and it seems like he's making up the curriculum as he goes. N/A

He is one of the most understanding professors I've had at RPI. He will always be lenient on missing/later work if you have a personal situation. The course content is difficult and the exams aren't very fair but every year he finds a way to fix the grades at the end of the semester.

Professor Kuzmin is a very kind person, he just lacks an understanding of what his students know in his course. There were multiple times when I spent time before a lab to complete it and the TAs would not understand how to approach the problems. Grades had to be heavily inflated at the end of the semester with extra credit.

He's a very nice guy do not get me wrong but his class is super disorganized and difficult and well no-one understands anything, I got a B+ so i must understand like 88% of the material right? Nope I learnt basically nothing. Everything is super difficult, no-one gets anything and his lectures are bad. You NEED to do the extra credit!!!
The only class where I felt despair not from my lack of understanding, but from the insurmountable workload. Having homework, an exam, and a final project due on the same week should be a crime.

I believe prof Kuzmin cares and understands the content he teaches, but this class was plagued by logistical problems, and as somebody who learns most from DOING rather than listening (Dr. Kuzmin gives long lectures), only getting 4/7 homeworks, missing 3 or 4 labs, and getting our final project late, all due to clerical errors, really screwed me.
too hard
He used exams to make this course more difficult. His lecture was just reading power points , but attendance was mandatory.
Never ever take this course by Kuzmin

everything written before me is true and he never responds to emails himself

reviews.comment: Lectures can be a tad dull at times, and HW and exams can sometimes be longer and harder than I think he intends, but he's one of the most caring and kind profs I've ever seen. Always nice to talk to, very knowledgeable and happy when people engage with the lecture material. Also, infinite crib sheets and insanely good course eval incentives.

Kuzmin edited the homework by changing the copies from few semesters ago. He changed only some requirements, but the workload was doubled or even tripled! Just do meaningless job. Also, he likes to skip classes for stupid reasons.

Dr. Kuzmin's lectures are often uninteresting and unclear. My class was also blindsided by a few extremely difficult assignments and tests.

Despite these issues, Dr. Kuzmin is BY FAR the most caring professor I've met at RPI. He works with students on deadlines and is generous with extra credit. He is also a genuine and friendly person.

I think overall Professor Kuzmin is a good professor, his lectures are not the best but he is very caring. Just do some self-studying after the lecture and study for the exam. He's pretty lenient, especially if he realizes that an assignment he gives out is too difficult.

Prof. Kuzmin is easily the most caring prof I have ever seen and he really listens to the students. The homework assignments are not to be shrugged off but you'll do just fine if you pay attention in the lectures. Beware of exam 2 but I feel that may have just been a freak chance for this semester only. Overall, 10/10

Professor Kuzmin is very knowledgeable about Computer Organization, but he is a very poor lecturer and tends to repeat the same things over again in class. He doesn't really know how much his students know, and this has caused situations where a massive curve needed to be applied so the class wasn't all failing exams. Take it with a diff prof

Kuzmin's lectures are not the best which leads to problems with the hws, but he really cares about his students and is always accessible during his office hours and is eager to help. He also will push back the deadlines if he realizes that people are having trouble meeting them which is good.

reviews.comment: Principles of Software was one of the best software classes I took at Rensselaer. Kuzmin is a great guy, the lectures are long and the class is tough, yes, but the work we were doing actually felt meaningful. The homeworks solidified lecture content, and the material felt very useful; they were also just enjoyable. Can't recommend him enough!

I'm not going to sugar coat this: Kuzmin's classes are tough. However, he knows that and makes every effort to help his students. I think what sets apart those who like Kuzmin and those who didn't is that those who liked him went to his Office Hours. The guy knows his stuff, and he will go out of his way to help those who care to learn it well.

Kuzmin clearly cares about his students, however I feel like he loses sight of his position as the professor. He will often put material on labs or exams that he views as easy but is challenging for the vast majority of students. That being said, he was very open to feedback and comments, and made many accommodations to help our grades.

Kuzmin is willing to make up for mistakes and listen to students, but this is set off by how horrifically incompetent he is as a professor. He gives out absurdly difficult assignments at very strange timing, to the point where I wonder if he even reads his own syllabus. If you need to take Comp Org, just wait until spring.

He made Comp Org a "trainwreck class." You learn next to nothing from his lectures. His assignments are terribly balanced, and graded pedantically. The schedule may as well not exist since he either cancels every office hours or misses lectures.
You learn everything from the textbook and whatever unreasonable assignments he puts on your head.

Avoid this class at all costs, take in the spring with a different professor. He grades you in homework + labs on material that you will learn a week later in class. Be prepared to look literally everything up in this class. Lectures are dull. All around do not recommend this professor. He's a nice guy, just a poor lecturer.

Professor Kuzmin is extremely unclear with his expectations for students. He also gives out assignments that aren't relevant to learning the course material (read: busywork), and grades students on their knowledge of concepts that were barely touched upon in class.

Database systems is an interesting class and it's clear that this professor knows what he's talking about. The lecture exercises for the course are incredibly annoying and the homeworks fall out of sync with the lecture contents past HW 4 which makes them more difficult to complete and stay on top of the lecture material.

Overall, Prof. Kuzmin is great. He has a great passion for his teachings and really cares about students' feelings. he also gives students options to choose their preferred curve. Definitely would like to take his class again.

As an instructor, he is very nice. He is open to any extra credit/ review session request and trying to be as helpful as he can, I got over 100%. As a teacher, he needs to focus more on his teaching quality. He is lacking the ability to control the pace of the class (going off tangent/ fly through the material). And he needs to improve "his" PPT.

This professor is easily the worst professor I have had at RPI so far, he will take slides that were written by the textbook company and then fly though them with almost no context given. Expect to search up everything and essentially learn by yourself. This material is interesting but is clearly taught by the wrong person. I dont know why I pay.

I've had Professor Kuzmin for Comp Org (CSCI 2500) in Spring 2020 which was not a great experience, but I can honestly say he's greatly improved and his lectures are less dry. He really cares about his students and truly strives to be helpful and fair to his students. Regardless of what the topic is, Professor Kuzmin tries his best to teach!

reviews.comment: I've had Kuzmin for the past 3 semesters (CompOrg, PSoft, and ProgLang).He has improved so much, and I think he's really found his stride with ProgLang. He does not lecture but handles course management/organization, super nice and flexible, always willing to extend due dates or clarify. He's a nice guy and explains well one-on-one.

reviews.comment: So I previously submitted a bad rating, but since then I've had Professor Kuzmin for 2 additional classes, and I actually really like him. I think the first class was poorly organized, but it was his first time teaching it. In the other two classes I've had with him since, I think they were taught very well :) He is a caring teacher.
Lectures aren't great, homeworks can be annoying and the quizes people averaged 50%s on. That being said, he is trying harder than a lot of profs and he will help you if you give him the chance.

Many of the complaints are valid. That being said, Kuzmin is clearly trying his best as a lecturer even if he falls short. Class was heavily curved at the end.

Won't give practice exams and won't accept any criticism about his teaching methods. He gives absolutely no indication in class when something he is lecturing on will be on tests.

Tests every 2 weeks, laughably hard. The last exam had to be curved so sharply that the minimum d was a 22! He gave us an 8 page test in 50 minutes. He then told all of us that we didn't study hard enough and said he could finish it in 12 minutes. He explains how to do the labs and the homework in the lecture AFTER we had to do it ourselves. RUN.
The worst professor. Lots of difficult homework. He think he teaches very well and give us hard quizzes. However, I think he is wrong!

He spends lots of time on stuff you dont need to know and rushes through things that are on the test and doesnt teach the programming you need to know. AVOID AT ALL COSTS!

TERRIBLE teacher. Quizzes are super hard and irrelavant to the homework or labs. Does not teach and only reads the powerpoint. Blows through the material quickly and expects you to have it mastered the next day. If you take him expect most of your education to come from youtube or google. Kuzmin is definetly on here rating himself the 5 stars.

Terrible. I don't understand anything he talks about in lecture. Quizzes are ridiculous difficult. nothing similar to the past quizzes and homework.
Great professor and is teaching the class very well.

Professor Kuzmin is one of my all time favorite professors. While the lecture was dull (comp org just sucks.. not his fault), he was always willing to help and I learned a lot by going to his office hours and receiving help. I have also had the pleasure of working alongside him as a mentor and he truly loves his job and it shows.

Kuzmin was okay for Comp Org. He really seemed to enjoy the course, unlike the rest of the class. He was very enthusiastic and excited to answer peoples' questions, and he did a good job answering them. He had to pick up the class half way through, so for a late start, he did a pretty good job. Comp Org itself is not a great course though.

He's a great guy who is just trying his hardest. The lecture exercises are easy, the labs are not too tough, and the homework are doable. Exams suck but they get curved like crazy so its okay!!!!! Great dude!!!
Do not take this professor's course!!! Trust me! Too much homework, and too difficult for an introduction course.

You don't have to go to lecture at all to pass CS1. Just read the note packet, do the lecture exercises, and use stack overflow to help you with the homework. Be careful because weird things can pop up on tests.

I register for Rate my Professor just to let others know do not take course with this prof. His lecture note is not helpful AT ALL. You'd better youtube and look for online courses instead of reading through his notes and slides. Lots of homework. His exams are hard. The average for our Final Exam was terrible.
The worst professor ever
Highly underrated professor. Makes clear slides and easy exams.

I think he gets a lot of bad rep for someone who also is teaching 10 different classes. Honestly he does his best, he could be better but he has more on his plate than most students. Very understanding when you talk to him, provides materials, wasn't a hard class. Study the homeworks and you'll be fine.

Great professor. Very clear in grading criteria and exam material. Easy to talk to and he explains topics well. He might not be the best lecturer but he does his best, ICAs are important in the class and he does in class exercises. Exams reflect homeworks, ICAs and class exercises. Gives opportunity for extra points through surveys.

At first I would not recommend him. However he does care about the students, I've talked with him one on one multiple times over the semester and he genuinely is a nice guy, his grading is more than fair and gives opportunities for extra credit. He did become a great lecturer. He posts slides, video recordings, and practice questions before exams.

Overall a solid professor. Was very flexible despite issues with lecture location early in semester. Provided plenty of transparency with exam content and seems like he wants us to succeed. There is some difficult understanding him, however he is willing to explain anything you ask. Not a bad option.

reviews.comment: If you have the option to not take this professor, don't. If you have to take him in this class, don't go. You'll be better off on your own. The worst lecturer I have had at RPI. Poor slides and a poor lecturer. You will not understand the material in class and will have to learn the material via YouTube. You will fall asleep in his class.

First day of class told every student there was no point in going to class. Then randomly decided to start hosting lectures however most lectures are just proofs. Surprised when students had low first exam score, however posted over 50 problems for the exam with no solutions because it took "too much time" to give the solutions.
Posts a bunch of practice problems
Tells us not to come to class & acts surprised when exam scores are low. Posts 18 pages of practice problems

Refuses to teach, literally told us to not come to class, refused to offer solutions to exam practices, and heavily relied on the TAs to do everything. Lecture slides were unhelpful and often included examples that weren't relevant of the content. He just doesn't do his job.
did not teach read off of the lecture slides and gave examples that had nothing to do with the lecture slides do not take him

He teaches at a whisper and his notes are lowkey hard to read but the exams are very fair and look just like the homework. ICA at the end of every lecture and they are graded based on correctness but usually he takes too long with lecture so just shows the ICA process and answer and lets us go.  
Not an outstanding professor but not bad either.

His notes are very detail and often have examples that are useful for studying for exams. He does a good job introducing new topics/ concepts,he provides good background information and motivating factors for new concepts. His grading is very fair, you will do well as long as you demonstrate that you understand the applicable course concepts.

Professor Panneerselvam is one of the better professors I have had at RPI. He is knowledgeable about what he is teaching, and most importantly seems to enjoy teaching it. I had him for 3 separate classes now and have enjoyed all of them. Courses are hard because they are generally new concepts for engineers here. Would highly recommend.

Although his lectures could be a bit more clear, he does provide extensive content (example problems w solutions, HW solutions) that you can use pretty effectively to do well on the exams. Kid below me probably just had a rough semester and chose to take it out on Dr. Paneerselvam. He is genuinely a really caring guy and wants students to succeed.

He cannot lecture to save his life, doesnt like to do hand written notes. Is far too softspoken when lecturing making it hard to understand him. does not like to do more than 1 example in class when it should merit many more. Syllabus and what he says in class conflict many times. I am actively avoiding taking a class taught by him ever again.

Professor Zhang is really nice but seems to lack skills as a lecturer. Almost every other lecture, she would make a mistake in her example solution, which would derail her work for the entire example and would take an extra half hour to correct. She often had trouble understanding questions and couldn't answer (when they weren't that confusing).

Avoid if you can, I can't tell if its the difficulty of the material, or if its her, but this class was nasty. This class is supposed to be learning NX-12 Nastran Stress simulation software, but the heavily weighted tests have nothing to do with it - there is a lot of material in this class that is nonrelevant to engineering.

Goes very fast with powerpoint slides, easily fall back on notetaking. Exams are difficult! Exam 1 no calculator nor crib sheet and Exam 2 1 crib sheet that is given, but useless.

I had her for strengths of materials last semester, and I felt like I learned what I needed to in lectures without a problem.  She has a slight accent, but it's very easy to understand her.  I thought the tests were fair.  All things considered, I think she's a good professor.

reviews.comment: She seems to teach well but her tests are just the hardest thing ever and her grading doesn't get any better. Stayed on par with the rest of the class but still got a low grade. Take Strengths with another professor if you can!
WORST PROFESSOR EVER...no partial credit on tests...the material covered is simple just her grading style doesn't make any sense
great professor. very helpful. she really spends time with you whenever you need extra help.
she is absolutely the worst professor or teacher i have ever had. cute though, wouldnt mind taking her to dinner, but thats it.

Have her for strengths, too. Really does care about getting students to learn, but doesn't always know a good way to explain the material in a way that's not somewhat confusing. I'd say better than most teachers, mostly due to genuine student interest, but could still use a lot of work.
Awesome teacher. Retook IEA to get better grade and succeeded. In great part due to Prof Zhang explaining stuff better than Professor Henry Scarton did the first time around.
No Comments
I'm not sure if she's bad at explaining the material or if the material is just hard to explain in general but either way this class has required me to teach myself.

Extremely helpful and caring. I was frequently at her office hours and she gave great feedback. She is clear about what will be on exams and quizzes and provides a lot of back work. She clearly wants her students to succeed. I will miss taking her class.
Fantastic professor. Very knowledgeable, understanding and flexible.
Dr. Snover is an angel sent from heaven to grace this school and make it a more tolerable place
Best professor at this school.
Amazing all around
Dr. Snover is wonderful. She cares about everyone's success and understanding of the course. It's a hard class but she does her best to simplify it and there's a ton of extra credit towards the end.
Good lecturer, and gives ridiculous amounts of bonus points on tests. Made orgo I very manageable even at the fast pace.
She is awesome, the only reason I got an A in both orgo I and II

Dr. Snover is hands down one of the best professors at RPI. She truly cares about her students, is incredibly understanding, offers LOTS of extra credit, explains material clearly, and her exams and quizzes closely match past ones she provides. She's approachable, easy to talk to, and made this class a breeze compared to the gen chem series!
You will get an A. She wants the best for all her students. Incredible professor, knows her stuff. I don't know her personally but people say she's the sweetest ever.

Aside from the fact that the class is difficult, Margarita is a queen. She's so sweet and responds to emails fast. I would often complete other work during orgo lectures but when I did pay attention, she was very detail-oriented. The exams and quizzes are hard but manageable, same with the homework. Chapter 6 is when it's time to lock in.

Dr. Snover is a wonderful, caring professor who truly wants the best for her students. She gives an absurd amount of extra credit on exams and quizzes, provides assistance with lab reports, and always allows students to make up exams without asking any questions. She is the antithesis of Dr. Ma, which made Orgo much more enjoyable than Gen Chem.

Dr. Snover and the way she formats the course is the only reason why organic chemistry is even tolerable and passable at RPI. Such a kind and sweet soul, and I loved both semesters I had her for organic 1 and 2.
