reviews.comment: She is the most caring professor I've met. She will reschedule tests and quizzes when needed, and will straight up give you answers and processes when you ask during a test or quiz. She just cares that you're learning something and understand the material, not if you test well. Orgo with her made it fun, and entirely less stressful than chem 1
Excellent professor in every possible way. Very accessible inside and outside of class, motivating and encouraging students to succeed. Very detailed-oriented, easy to understand lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She is a wonderful lady. The lectures can be pretty dry and most students stop going as the course is so easy through achieve. She will also legit just tell you the answers on quizzes and tests sometimes. 10/10 would recommend, she's so accommodating and nice.

Amazing prof who gives wonderful feedback if you go to her with questions. She makes sure that you understand whats happening and really wants you to succeed. She gives a ton of crib sheets for tests and quizzes to you basically dont have to memorize anything. In her class, organic chemistry felt more fun rather than stressful.
Love this professor. So kind and helpful.

Dr. Snover is one of the nicest professors I've ever meet. I took her class during my freshman year. She was willing to listen to your concerns and more than ready to answer your questions regarding the lecture or the lab during office hours(might be pack with people).
Dr. Snover is very kind and is very helpful during office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Snover is an excellent professor. Her lectures are clear and very helpful in understanding the material. Tests can be challenging, but if you understand the back exams and hw it should be no problem. Would take again.
She gives out a lot of extra credit on quizzes and tests.

She is a very sweet and caring professor. Orgo itself is a lot of work but she makes it doable with always being there to answer questions and her office hours are very helpful. The online homework gets annoying so just get Chegg. Overall, much better compared to previous teachers of Orgo.
She is very sweet, the type of lady who probably bakes amazing chocolate chip cookies. Definitely available to ask questions, but the lectures are boring.

I took both Orgo I and II with Dr. Snover.  Orgo II was much more challenging than Orgo I. You have to study hard and not fall behind. Her exams were hard and long, especially the mechanism problems.  Her lectures are organized and thorough, with many examples. She made me want to go to class and as a result I love organic chemistry.

Took Orgo 2  with a different professor prior year and dropped because they were so awful. So glad they switched her to be the professor for this class. Solid professor, through and through. Always nice and approachable. Tests/quizzes were fair and often had bonus questions. Orgo is hard and annoying, but it was bearable with Dr. Snover.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Not a very good lecturer, but a nice woman. She has a slight accent, but is usually comprehendible. Orgo. I and II with her were both challenging.

She is friendly, professional, clear, easy to talk to/ask questions of. Orgo Lab I & II were my favorite subjects. She explains chemistry quite well and makes it easy and the labs fun. Extremely helpful. Will help you with experiments and give you hints for the homework problems and guide you through mechanisms from Professor Moore's class.

The course uses ALEKS and the resources provided can usually teach you the content you need to know if lecture wasn't enough. Pair your studying with back exams, you will do fine. Overall, V^2 is very clear in the way he explains, especially in comparison to other faculty who don't tend to cover the content in time for the exam. Very caring.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Unorganized lectures that aren't always the easiest to follow. However, exams are fair and not too hard as long as you do the homework thoroughly. Very hard class if you do not do the homework and give time to learn all the concepts. Lots of online homework each week.
Very nice guy but very unorganized, can't answer certain questions asked in class, textbook reading very necessary because lecture is useless

Speaks English natively. has a good understanding of content. Very good person as an individual: not a bad bone in his body. Wants you to succeed. Homeworks suck; they're very long, and you have to get the questions right. Overall class was harder than AP Chem. Class average on tests were in the 60s.

Cares a lot about his students but his lectures are unorganized. Makes a good effort to engage the class and make the lectures entertaining, but he often goes super deep into one topic and then realizes he's running out of time, so he flies through the rest of the slides. For that reason, lectures aren't very helpful.  Exams are fair.

He did not understand what was going on his his lectures sometimes and would fly by everything really fast. He would constantly tell us students are his first priority, but then tell us to use AI for help instead of going to him and show up late to lecture.

He only writes on the chalk board. Exams make up 100% of your grade and they're quite unfair. Lecture material is hardly covered in the exams and most of the questions he gives on exams were never covered in lectures. I attended every lecture and took notes and they were not helpful in the slightest on the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His lectures were uniformative and exams were way too difficult for the things that he was NOT teaching us properly
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He must have some sort of ego problem because he spent roughly half the 40 minute intro lecture kicking people out. I watched him pan across the room looking for people who even moved their mouths wrong. His lecture was unintelligible, his research looks really cool, but I think Id rather bathe in acid than ever ask him about it. Stay far far away.

Was a guest speaker for my class and spent more time ego tripping and kicking people out for “talking” than actually teaching anything. He kicked a girl out for trying to ask a question and when she protested he said “I don't care, I said no talking, get out of my class”. I'd steer clear of this guy if possible.

This professor needs the entire lecture hall to be completely silent and if its not, he will kick students out of class. He was a guest lecturer for MANE 1060, which is an introductory engineering exposure class. There is no possible reason to have such a harsh classroom environment, let alone in a 300 person lecture hall for an intro class.
This guy genuinely was on something. He kicked me out for "talking" when I did not say a single thing. He was even a guest speaker and was extremely rude to students.

Toxic professor that has been kicking people out of class for literally saying 1 word or because he thinks they are talking when they are not. Only having him for one lecture, but I can tell that any more time with him would be a nightmare.

nice guy bad grading structure, lms is the most barren one I've ever seen quote from syllabus 
"The raw numerical grade is the minimum of the sum of all homework grades and the sum of all exam grades: 100% exams grade, if exams grade is lower than homework grade 100% homework grade, if homework grade is lower than exams grade"

Very confusing professor, we are currently two weeks away from our first exam and I still have no idea what's going to be on it. Our grades are either our homework grade or test grade, but he takes the lower one.  None of his notes are posted online and he only writes notes on a chalkboard. Python is on every homework. Avoid this man at all costs
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Doesn't teach well. Leaves you to figure out everything on your own. Grades very harshly over material he doesn't explain. Operates based on "Figure out what you need and make sure it's there." Very disorganized; finish things as soon as possible because otherwise it will all pile on. There is always more to be done, no clear end goal.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Disorganized/unclear objectives for projects/hard to reach outside class/grades on arbitrary criteria/gave groups of 5 2 wks to write an 80pg CDR over Thanksgiving due to poor planning ruining break/unengaging lectures/joins remote 3 classes before CDR due when needed most/not funny nor nice/made the semester miserable for all/not fit to teach
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Too difficult

The structure of this class was confusing. There was no guidelines for grading of the homework or exams. We didn't use numbers in calculating anything and it was quite conceptual. He also tried teaching us Python to help with the homeworks but it only made it more confusing. All the other professors had different content that was much easier.

The most confusing grader I have ever seen. Graded either on HW or tests, whichever was WORSE. I can appreciate at the bare minimum that he exposed the class to a bunch of concepts that were useful and not covered by other professors. However, material comes from his head and is written on a chalk board with no hope of recovering lecture notes.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Probably deserves mercy since this is the first class he's taught but he didn't give me or my capstone group any so RIP. He opened the first class with some basics on space vehicle design but the rest of the semester was spent grilling each group and not providing any advice on how to improve. He seems like he wants students to struggle. Don't take

Lectures are mostly reading off slides. He tells you a lot of what will be on the exam at review sessions, class average tends to be low anyway because the tests are sort of unrelated to the actual problems in class.

he livestreams and posts all of his lectures, so attendance isn't "mandatory", but there's a 5% participation grade from answering echopoll questions in lecture. very clear about what is on his exams, and they follow the same pattern every year, so do the back exams
Very helpful during office hours. Lecture content best fits what comes on exams. His review sessions are the ones to attend.

Overall good professor however if you go to office hours and asked questions he'd be a little condescending and expect you to know everything. Go to the exam reviews because he'll tell you a lot of hints on the test. Lots of homework so definitely try to plan out your homework schedule ahead of time.

Fantastic Chemistry prof. Lectures are fun and very useful, but fast with a lot heavy material. If you pay attention and try to understand logically, will be a breeze. Attendance is very important. EXTREMELY helpful during OH explains material super well. Labs are super fun. Homework helps a lot Ask as many questions as you need he will answer.

Very knowledgeable in what he teaches, but lectures are incredibly fast paced. Will often begin the next lecture if he finishes early. Expects you to have a good understanding of chemistry prior to taking the class and will rarely answer questions during lecture. Exams are multiple choice but require deep genuine understanding of the material.

If you're taking Chem 1100, take it with Dr. Ma.  Ma writes exams and he is an extremely tough grader, so make sure to study harder than you think you need to.  All 3 Chem professors teach well, but try to get Ma or Korenowski.  Attendance matters a lot.

Although Chem 1 is an RPI course that has too much busywork quite often (especially with topics many students don't care about), Dr. Ma is the best professor to have access to for this intro class. He goes fast in lectures, but I admire how passionate he is in when reviewing content. Utilize the cybermentoring office hours as well, they're helpful!

Ma's Lectures are always extremely direct and to the point. It is extremely fast paced but he tends to not go off topic and his office hours are quite helpful. Chem is all round a very tough course so no matter who you pick it'll be hard but for me Ma was extremely helpful in learning the material. He makes the test so attend his review sessions
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Chem 1100 is the classic weedout class, with tons of homework and tough exams. Given the choice between Korenowski, Tysoe, and Ma, I'd take Ma any day of the week (Tysoe > Korenowski though). If you can't stomach the 8 AM lectures, at least attend his review sessions. He writes the exams and drops hints like crazy. Good lecturer and cool guy!

Take Chem 1 with Ma! You're doing yourself a disservice if you don't. He does talk fast sometimes but is totally willing to answer questions or talk during office hours. HE WRITES THE EXAMS so sometimes he will directly tell you if something is on the test in class. Also, go to his exam review sessions, they cover everything you need to know.

It does not matter how well you can pay attention in lecture, you will have to learn everything on your own. Add that to the insane amount of homework for homework for lecture AND lab and you have a course that pretends like you don't have any other classes. It's absolutely criminal that it's only 4 credits. This is an 8 credit work load.
Knowledgeable bout what he is teaching

Dr Ma is a pretty good professor! He's good at explaining harder topics and is accessible outside of class if you have questions. I will say he is not the most tech-savvy person out there, however. He's the Chem 1 lecturer who mainly writes the exams, so if you go to his review sessions, he'll probably tell you the kind of questions to expect.

Dr. Ma is a good professor when it comes to teaching and conveying topics that can be difficult to understand. However the tests are made to be very difficult and he takes no responsibility for the averages (even if the exam average is an F). Office hours can be helpful but have to go from the get-go or else he gets upset and lets you know it.

Dr. Ma is a great professor for CHEM-1100!  His lectures are extremely fast-paced and engaging and he tries to make jokes about whether or not he will put something on an exam. If you take CHEM-1100 with him, be ready to take quick notes, read the textbook, and spend a good amount of time on homework. Definitely attend his exam reviews too!

If Ma is available for Chem I, take Ma. Writes the exams so knows what to teach. If you put in the effort, A is very easy to get because of the abundance of test review sessions and mentoring opportunities. Nice guy in office hours. Lectures are extremely fast, highly suggest pre-reading and taking light notes before lecture. Lectures required.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I do not recommend taking Dr. Ma for chemistry 2. The best thing about his teaching is that he is clearly very knowledgeable no the content but he is unable to actually relay that to students. His lectures are incredibly fast paced and boring and do not prepare you for the tests.

Terrible professor, worst teacher Ive ever had. Calls students stupid. Will not give points back on exams despite having questions with more people getting it wrong than right. Some of the exams had a failing class average with no curve. Has no idea of student's understanding of material and seems to enjoy giving exams that people do very poorly on

A super nice guy. He lectures at a fast pace. All of the lecture slides where posted online. His reviews are key, he breaks down reviews to the topic of each question which helps focus on what to study. If you are a freshman I advise taking him for chemistry.

I strongly recommend Dr Ma's lectures, not because it's great, but it's the most helpful strategy for your exams since he made it. I don't like him personally since he always makes things way too difficult.

Dr. Ma is the chemistry professor who writes the tests, so I would suggest getting him if at all possible. Yes, his lectures are early, but you will get a much higher grade if you attend the lectures in person rather than over Webex. Pay attention, and don't be afraid to ask questions or go to his office hours.
Really hard tests
He covered all the material and his review lectures are super helpful, only negative is that he lectures very fast so taking notes can be difficult.

Ma is very knowledgeable in the field of Chemistry, which seems to be his biggest downfall. He lacks the empathy for the majority that struggle with chem. Lecture attendance isn't mandatory but he speeds through 90+ lecture slides expecting complete understanding from students instantly. He creates the tests and makes sure to make it very difficult

Took AP Chem senior year of high school with an A in the class and a 4 on the exam, and I hated and struggled with this class, getting poor grades while actually trying. Seemed like half the things we were supposed to know weren't in the textbook, and I learned more from google than the class. COVID isn't an excuse, this class was real garbage.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This professor made me want to find whoever invented Chemistry and hurl them off the Golden State Bridge. This man gave us an 1hr 15 mins to finish an exam w/ an absurd amount of questions. No one was finishing on time, so much so that Dr. Ma had to increase the time on 2 separate occasions! 3 surveys were made about the difficulty of the exams.

Ma's really nice and helpful. You can get away with an A in the class if you do well on the labs & hw and get Bs on the tests. But, you do have to actually work for your grade. If you don't understand something, ask for help EARLY. Physically showing up isn't necessary. You don't REALLY need a textbook but for some people, it can a difference.

Dr. Ma is a good professor to have. He goes over a lot of content during lectures, but the pace never felt rushed. He streamed the lectures live online which was nice (i.e. staying in bed for an 8 AM). For Chem 1100, he is the preference. His review sessions are very helpful. He tries to make lecture fun and enteraining. A nice guy!
Quick lectures but they are extremely helpful especially while studying for exams. He also always holds test reviews that are vital to attend before taking the exams.

He's a good lecturer, although he tends to go through powerpoints at light speed. He also does his best to make lectures funny which is good. Tests are usually hard since he puts tricky questions (wording, hard question in general) and the tests were at 8am.

I had him for Chem 1 and Chem 2. He's a great guy. He loves to be tricky on exams, but he genuinely cares about his students and is a good lecturer. You gotta work for a high grade, especially in Chem 2.

From day 1 when he stood up and declared that in classical physics waves don't carry momentum I knew this guy didn't really know what he was talking about. He is a nice guy but not a rigorous explainer. People tend to think he's funny, I think he's just silly. He often just fails to teach material declaring it too hard. He's kind of a ridged grader

Going to lectures is a part of the grade, plus they really help. Dr. Ma really knows what he is teaching and explains everything very well. He's funny and makes lectures interesting. You do have to put in a good amount of work to get a good grade.

Dr. Ma is a great lecture-style professor. I had him for chem I and class was a breeze. He posts all of his lectures and review sessions online, and offers a tremendous amount of resources to study for tests.

I had Ma for chem I and chem II.  You do not have to read the textbook, but you HAVE to go to lecture and take notes.  His course is not that difficult, but you do have to do a lot of back tests to prepare and do well on his exams.  He is a great professor and I don't really have any complaints

He wore a Hawaiian shirt and brought inflated beach balls to lecture one time and let us throw them around the room. Enough said. Dr. Ma is great.  He presents the lecture material clearly and goes at a reasonable pace, though I'm not gonna lie, those lectures are long. Go to his review session before tests, they help a lot.
Dr. Ma is fantastic and hilarious. The class isn't too terribly difficult, but requires a lot of studying for exams.

Funny guy. Is very clear and explains material well. Lectures can be a bit long, but they're not too boring, and very helpful. Tests are 20 multiple choice questions, so a  few mistakes and your down to a B pretty quickly, but other than that, they're not that hard.

Dr. Ma is a funny guy. The curve is built into the letter grade criteria. Final MIGHT replace your lowest exam score. It happened in my year, but the previous students I've asked have said that he doesn't cut you any slack beside the aforementioned built-in curve. I was able to get an A with only Chem I experience in HS.

Ma is one of the nicest professors I've had so far. He is in charge of Chem 1 and has a deep understanding of the material. Also there's small experiments at the beginning of some classes. He encourages students to come to office hours where he occasionally gives out test hints. He doesn't curve and the tests can be tricky, but manageable.
Very clear and not boring at all. Best chem1 professor!
PRAISE MA!  An almighty god of chemistry and science, Ma fights the troubles students have with an Iron (Fe) fist.  Ma saves the day every time with his brilliance in Chem 1.
Very hard tests and final. Very nice teacher. Keep up with lab because that can help you grade a lot.
His lectures are not boring; he makes funny comments :) He's really nice, and he's tests are not impossible! Awesome Professor~~~

Dr.Ma is very helpful and patient. His encouragement throughout the year really helped guide me towards a successful end. He supplements the info learned during lecture with Korenowski very nicely. You just have to make sure to take the time to go meet him outside of class.

Overall he's a solid professor. He explains topics well and makes sure to provide numerous examples. He isn't very timely with uploading his slides so I wouldn't recommend skipping, but I have no other complaints.

Zeghal gets the content done, but lectures were incredibly slow and monotone. Many times delved deeper than necessary, not enough time for in-class assignments (1-2 per lecture). ICAs aren't checked for accuracy (might depend on TA). 
Hws aren't easy 100s as difficulty is higher than lecture examples. Office hours after lecture for only an hour.

He is very lecture heavy. He is a very harsh grader with many points taken off for not putting labels on answers and work. There is a lot of homework with much of it being harder than the topics covered in class. He often skims over topics that are harder to understand and spends time on things that are easier to understand.

Zeghal lectures painfully slow, even for simple things like manipulating basic vectors. This can be painful, but he teaches you everything you need to know and finishes the lectures, so I can't ding him for that. Besides that, he's a fine professor, and I would argue he's just as good as any other IEA profs.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I thought Dr. Zeghal was an excellent instructor for IEA! He provided back exams with problems very similar to the exams. IEA is a difficult course but he explained the content in a more understandable way! I would definitely recommend

I thought he was great. Teaches very well. He occasionally emphasizes a thing unnecessarily, but not often. I got a B in the class but I understand and remember all the material better than any other class. He has review sessions and back exams that are super helpful. Only complaint is he didn't answer my email one time. My favorite class so far.

He teaches, and that's about the best thing I have to say about him. He responds to emails once in a blue moon, even talking to him about it after class doesn't help that issue. He's typically extremely late with uploading lecture slides and is often difficult to understand because of his mumbly speech.

Oftentimes doesn't upload lecture slides until over 3 weeks have passed, making studying examples absurdly challenging. Almost never responds to emails. Emphasizes information on slides that don't matter and/or are obvious and understood to everyone in class while briefly skimming over the most important things that will be on tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures are slow, repetitive, and often lack information that will be present on homework or tests. Problems practiced in class are generally helpful for understanding a new concept, but fail to prepare you for the large difficulty spike of exam problems. I tried many times to reach out to the professor when sick but would receive no response.

This is a good professor for a difficult course. Everything that is needed to know for tests is taught well and thoroughly. Yes, he teaches on the slower side, but for me, it was a nice change of pace compared to most courses at RPI. HW is harder than tests, but doesn't take too long to complete. Overall, a good professor
His lectures were sometimes unclear, but if you ask him questions, he is very knowledgeable and will help you through the problem.

Professor Zeghal was a very solid teacher for IEA. If you put in the work, his lectures will be more than enough to prepare you for the exams. He's not very enthusiastic but I didn't find that to be a bad thing. I actually liked it, almost like an organic chemistry tutor vibe. Would rec for IEA.

Your experience with Dr. Zeghal is proportional to the effort you put into the class. Ask questions during lectures and reach out to him during office hours, and you'll find him to be very knowledgeable and eager to help. His lectures help to prepare for the exams, but they can be very slow. Homeworks are much more difficult than the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Zeghal is a great lecturer and prepares for exams well.  IEA is a tough course, but he explains the material in a comprehensive way.

IEA itself is a bit of a learning curve but this professor does not make it easy to get over the curve. In class he mostly mumbles and keeps skipping things "for the sake of time". When asked a question, he will go off on a tangent and leave your question mostly unanswered. I ended up going to the TAs or upperclassmen for help.
I found IEA to be a hard class but Professor Zeghal is a good lecturer and is helpful during office hours.

IEA is a tough class, but he cares enough to provide examples to work in class for credit. For these problems, he does not just assume the TA's have got everything and will go out of his way to explain problems crystal clear. He gets a bad rap on this site I'm assuming from people who didn't do well. Just go to class and don't be afraid to ask.

Professor Zeghal did give slow lectures at times, but he always got through all the necessary content on time regardless. Everything was clearly laid out and plenty of examples where given to help us students prepare for tests. He also would regularly schedule extra office hours if students where having a hard time with concepts.

Dr. Zeghal effectively teaches IEA, however, his lectures are extremely slow and boring. There isn't too much homework, but be sure to check your answers! There were frequent grading errors on exams, and the rubrics were completely incomprehensible, even to the TAs. Don't expect your exam to be graded promptly either!

IEA is a tough class, but professor Zeghal did a great job to make it interesting. This became one of my favorite classes of my freshman year, despite it being the hardest. Professor Zeghal was so helpful in and out of lecture, and he had tons of office hours. Just make sure to pay attention in lecture, it is very important if you want to pass.
Honestly not a fan, I'll put it this way, I'm retaking the class with a different professor

Crystal clear lecturer with solid powerpoints. The content is relatively difficult for a first year course, but the in-class assignments and the 1 hr long homeworks usually help keep you attentive. Back exams are also readily available and help a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Great, comprehensive lectures. For the difficulty of the material, he did a great job teaching it. In-class assignments were a great help in understanding the concepts, and the homework was abundant but not busy work. It really helped. No more than 1.5 hours of HW between classes and that was rare. Use the back exams. They're life-savers.

Dr. Zeghal's lectures were very clear and incredibly helpful. A lot of people were not fond of his lecture style, but I found it to be very comprehensive. The online homework was helpful in practicing, and therefore learning, the material. The class itself was not an easy A, but with a hard work that grade can be achieved. Use back exams to study!
Repeats simple concepts and solutions rather than explaining harder ones that will be on homework and exams
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Not an easy A but cared about his students. If you went to him for help he was more than willing to figure things out with you. I wish he'd sent the power points out before or after class so that we'd had access to them to study from. His lecture style was fast paced, he sort of expected you
He cared about all his students and made sure that everyone was doing fine. His lectures were great and his review sessions before tests were super beneficial.

Not an easy A for sure but if you're willing to study a bit and pay attention in class, you should have no problems. Go to every class: Zeghal is a great lecturer and genuinely wants to help students that don't understand. For every problem on the test, we covered similar examples in class. Just bring a blanket to class, he keeps the room ice cold.
Very good professor, the online homework can be difficult, but he does a good job with tests and reviews questions very closely related to the exam q's. Would recommend
Very helpful during lectures and test were easy.

Good professor; knows the material well and is very good at communicating it. The material itself was hard for me to grasp, but I feel his teaching helped make it a lot easier. Plus his accent is cool.
His notes for lecture are very straightforward and make sense. Ask questions; he happily answers. Both of his sections had the highest averages for the tests this year. Overall, he's wonderful!

Helpful and Interesting, lays out all the material in the easiest way to understand. People complains about him going to fast, if you ask him to slow down he is more than willing too. However, on review days he sometimes goes to slow! His accent is easy to understand and amusing.Great experience for my first collegiate engineering course.

He is a good teacher, can be boring at times sitting for 2 hours in a lecture. Has an accent but i got used to it after about one lecture and had no trouble understanding him. Wants you to succeed. Post his lectures online and everything else about this course is constant between all professors. Shows lots of example problems during lecture.
Overall pretty good professor for this class. Only downside is all the homework he gives :-( 10 homework problems can take you 6 hours. Still I would reccomend this class with him
He is a pretty good teacher. He went too slow for me though, and teaches stuff you do not actually need
Class was more unorganized than anything else.  His lectures were less than helpful.  As an IEA professor he is great.

I was stuck with Professor Zeghal for IEA, which was a bit unfortunate for everybody involved since, from what I understand, he's not really a first-year studies kind of professor.  It was very intense at the beginning of the semester, but as the semester progressed everything began to get easier, and I credit Professor Zeghal.

Prof. Zeghal is an overall excellent professor for this class. His examples cover the most important material and his review sessions are a great guide for studying for the tests. In class though, he can tend to get too caught up in derivations. However, he can usually help settle any difficulties that you have in his office hours.
Boring class, but he is helpful at office hours.  Lectures are clear and easy to follow.  He also tells you what's on the tests, and has review sessions before.  Take strengths with him.

His voice puts you to sleep, doesnt try to make the subject more exciting, but he tries to be helpful, keeps repeating to us his office hours, and looks you square in the eye when ur answering one of his questions... did i mention he kinda looks like zoolander?

Good IEA professor. Willing to help students and actually cares about making them understand what's going on. TA's suck at grading...every test I had to get points back, but regrading sessions were held (long lines).
It was a pleassure to be in his class. Very helpfull! Gives great, long reviews before every exam! Has nice acentt.
Boring boring class.  He doesn't make it any more interesting but at least he's a pretty easy teacher.  Do your homework and tests and you can pretty much sleep through class.

There were four grades for this class, three assignments worth 25% each, and participation. Nideffer loves AI. Feedback given to us months after assignments were submitted was almost certainly AI generated and were unhelpful. His lectures consisted of listing games that have stories and showing videos made for 12 year olds.
Took digital imaging with him. Don't take any of his classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Lacks the knowledge and background to teach a course on the history of games, which becomes immediately apparent based on the confused lectures and lack of knowledge on game development.

Be wary of the heavy usage of generative AI to teach the course if that is something that personally conflicts with your beliefs.
Great lecturer and very flexible in terms of the instructions in the assignments, allowing for greater creativity. He encourages participation and makes it come easier even to those more shy.

The content of AIM is really outdated, you don't learn anything that will be useful or that you haven't already learned in high school. It's a shame, it's a waste of time. The good thing is that it's an easy A.
Very irresponsible as an online course instructor - does not give lectures at all. Only posted links to online tutotials which are generally not well presented, some of which are dated.

Arts for Interactive Media is a gem with professor Nideffer. The course is not a large amount of work, you can get away with only really working on the weekend. This class was one of the most fun I've had due to the sheer creative freedom I was able to experience. Top recommend.
The strat with Neti Embedded Control is to completely ignore him and just ask the TAs if you need anything. Thankfully, he doesn't do the lectures for this course.

Never again. We are literally weeks behind according to his own syllabus and you learn nothing from lecture. No example problems, just formulas and derivations. Take this class with Oakes or get her notes from a student who took it with her. This class is unbearable
Goes on tangents. Gloats about his time at GE. Gives participation points but it mostly goes to the same 2-3 people and honestly isn't useful at all. Exams were easy - reproduction of lecture slides.

ECSE 2340 is basically Wilt's class. Wilt designed it all, Neti clearly doesn't know what's going on. Does not answer questions at all, gets confused quickly. Nice man, but if he wasn't in the room nothing would've changed.

I had professor Neti as a lab instructor for Embedded Control and he didn't seem like he knew what he was doing. He aight

Terrible/Doesn't explain complex topics, slides don't help much either. Halfway through the semester. Want to drop the course and take it next semester, but he's teaching it again.

Cares about students and likes when they ask questions. Test questions are variations of (or the exact same as) the practice problems. He's def better in EES than in signals because his field is power

Gives lectures with one airpod in. Doesn't explain things very well either. He's not clear about expectations, and homework is usually very behind. Very disorganized. Gives a lot of extra credit for answering bonus questions in class, but he won't let you finish answering them before he blurts out the answer. Would never voluntarily take his class

Brilliant man, incompetent professor with incredibly poor communication. No grading scale in the syllabus, and lectures make even simple topics hard to follow, often twisting and turning through various derivations that are never used again. Lists and example problems are all that is needed in this class, but you wont get them from Neti's lectures.
Don't Bother. For the sake of your sanity take it with any other professor.
he touched me after class whem I complained about his style.

Neti is literally the worst professor I have ever had. He drones on in lectures, asking rhetorical questions and interrupting students who answer them. His homework run about a month behind the lecture such that you have had no practice on the contents of the exam by the time you take the exam. Exams are worth 80% of your grade, very mean grader.

Though his lectures are a bit unclear, the homework and tests are not that hard. You can learn a lot of things from his lecture. And if you go to ask him questions, he will answer thoroughly and patiently.

Questions he asks are so irrelevant that they are either basic questions from Calc 2, or something oversimplified. If you start to answer, he WILL interrupt you with the answer to the question and then go on a tangent. Never goes through an example and just gives you solutions, he will not do a problem in class. Retired and teaches as a "hobby".

By far the worst Professor I have ever had. His lectures are awful.. how does someone learn math by just looking at slides??? This class might actually be worse than data structures and that is saying something. I wish we had HAMEEEEED ��

reviews.comment: His notes are entirely handwritten and almost no words at all (just diagrams and equations) It was first time teaching elasticity, pretty sure he's usually supposed to be teaching aerolab. I recommend anyway, He explained everything very well and was lenient with grading.

I had Prof. Koratkar for Aerospace Structures Lab. It was a great experience. He offered very informative lectures related to the lab content. Although the Lab appears to last for 3 hours, it usually takes 1 hour. Prof. Koratkar is very accessible outside of lab hours, and is willing to explain concepts related to the lab content. I truly recommend
Professor Koratkar is very friendly, smart and professional. The lecturing is clear and easy to follow, while Professor Koratkar is open for questions both in and out of the classes.
Professor Koratkar is very knowledgeable and professional.  You'll only use about 30 minutes of the lab block.  5 lab reports are your only grades.

This lab class could have benefitted significantly from a lab manual. Koratkar knows what he is doing but expects you to already be as learned in the subject as he is. You literally show up and do the lab and then have to answer 7 report questions with nothing but your computer and lots of these questions have no clear answer. No office hrs either.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: professional, smart, very logical, relatively good teacher, "knows what to do"

Doesn't make class any longer than it needs to be.  You will only go for an hour of the 3 hour block.  Lab reports always ask questions that aren't explained in class, but he is available and willing to give help.  Doesn't give a lot of partial credit, either you get the answer or you don't.

Niemiec is a very tough grader, but he is very honest and transparent. Grades are well-explained, due dates are very clear. He gives great lectures and answers questions well, is clearly very knowledgeable. He did aim the tests to be ~50% average, but knew ahead of time the final grades had to be curved. Imo, great teacher, hard grader.

Niemiec's exams & projects were difficult, but his HWs were straightforward. He scheduled exams once he covered their material and allowed students to vote for when the exams would be. If you wanted to know an assignment/exam's grading process, you'd have to go to office hours. Overall, he was a good, timely professor who was disorganized at times.

Very knowledgeable and passionate in MODCON, and does a good job lecturing, but none of the work you get graded comes with a rubric so you have no idea what you did wrong and how to correct yourself down the line, which makes it impossible to learn from your mistakes. Exams are tough and class is graded very harsh but grade cutoffs are adjusted.

Niemiec accused the class of cheating because several students actually did cheat. I thought his lectures were informative. I just wish he had been more organized. IMO, the projects and homeworks were reasonable. Exams were hard given the time alotted, but still doable. He also gave us a chance to retake 2 midterms. The class was heavily curved.

His personality is definitely a little on the prickly side. But overall the class wasn't that bad. Very challenging exams definitely. But he presented the material well in lectures that were never too boring. There was also a very generous final exam policy and curve at the end.

The tests are very, very difficult. In addition, the lecture material he presents makes it very difficult to understand how what we're doing in class applies to real life.  Fairly forgiving with homework grades, though.  He is also quite condescending sometimes and assumes everyone wants to watch him play with matlab for a whole lecture.

Would not take a class with him again. You can tell that he wants you to know he's smarter than you and will be incredibly condescending. Exams are written to be much harder than the content taught in class (if you can even follow) and graded harshly. The homework's and project won't save your grade either as they're also graded rigorously.

reviews.comment: Genuinely the worst professor I've ever had at RPI. Lectures are all handwritten and are extremely hard to follow. Very tough grader and gives no partial credit. Does not post homework solutions anywhere so he can reuse them, so no way of checking why you got a bad homework grade. Spent countless hours on this course for nothing in return.

This course was the worst experience of my entire time as a student and has been the cause of lots of late nights and burnout. Lectures are confusing and exams ambush with things never introduced in the course before, leading to averages in the 40-50s. Communication w/ prof is frustrating. Avoid if you actually want to learn controls engineering!
Do not take for ModCon!! So far the test averages have been in the 40s as the exams barely reflect the homework and lectures. The projects are harshly graded while having little to no guidelines.
He makes this class even harder. The open-note exams don't reflect the homework or the material covered in class. The projects make no sense, and good luck if you don't know MATLAB.

He is top 3 worst prof don't take MODCON w him unless you enjoy spending hours on MODCON to figure out what the exams are even about. His lectures don't even make sense, and his handwriting is chicken scratch. I highly suggest taking the class w a different prof.
totally buns
absolute buns

Accuses class of cheating multiple times. Do not take his modcon class. He has accused a third of his class of cheating on test 1 and the project. Do not take if you do not want to be accused of cheating constantly and also drained mentally.

If you have free time and want to spend it teaching yourself three levels above what lecture covers to do well on the exams that a you thing. Objectively, he's a decent enough guy but the way he teaches this course makes it very difficult to get a good grade. ( first two exam averages were in the 50s).

Maybe the worst exams ever written? Great lecturer, great office hours, etc. But the proff does not know how to actually write a exam. The exams are always barely related to what you do on the homeworks. The lectures and homeworks barely help for studying for exams. Test averages are almost always very very low.

Exams are almost the whole grade, very difficult, and required knowledge is not entirely covered by weekly homework or lecture. There is no extra material/exams to prepare and study with, and no way to have expectations. Professor is sometimes rude and condescending when dealing with students. You will spend hours daily and always feel unprepared.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: For an 8:30 am class, very engaging lectures and helpful review at the beginning. But I was NOT prepared for the difficulty of his exams even with open notes. He does kind of make up for it by replacing a past exam grade if your final (optional) grade is better. Otherwise, very knowledgeable.Tip: take FEA and work on MATLAB beforehand

Professor Niemiec ran a very fair and structured Aeroelasticity course. As with many engineering classes, the course was test heavy. However, they were very fair exams. His lectures were all directly related to the exams and we were never tested on anything we did not go over, or did not take notes on. Very fair professor.

GOOD LUCK! This class was a nightmare and a waste of time. Class was set up as 75% exams and 25% HW but there were only 5 hw assignments so each one is worth 5% of your grade and he grades them rigorously. Only upside is that your final replaces your worst exam (which you're gonna need). He grades on a curve at the end which might save you.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Nevo is a great professor. Though some find his grading strict, I think he is a fair grader. His instructions can sometimes be unclear, but he's happy to clarify if you ask. He doesn't take attendance, but he gives pop quizzes frequently. However, he does drop your 3 lowest quiz grades. He allows a double-sided reference sheet for every exam.

Boring lectures. I've fallen asleep more than once in them. The pop quizzes come out of nowhere, but they're not weighted heavily. He's quite thorough in class, and super easy to access during office hours.

He also gives a ton of extra credit- I ended the class with a 103. Just make sure to show up because he's a stickler about attendance.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Saggi is a very quiet guy and sometimes you don't understand what he's saying but he means well he is a super nice guy when you have a one on one conversation with him and he's always willing to help when you go to his office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Beware of pop quizzes--Caring

reviews.comment: Mr. Nevo means well, but this class is in rough state. No engagement—it feels like he's talking to a brick wall. reviews.comment: Made me retake my final the next semester. Can be difficult just have to pay attention 24/7
Great person, but the lectures follow the slides closely. The multiple-choice tests are tough, so definitely lean on the back exams—they're the best way to prep.

This class is very easy if you do the homework and read over the slides before tests. Look at the back exams because some of the questions are the same questions on the test. You will have to do a group presentation at the end of the semester so choose your group wisely.

honestly idk y is professor's rating so low. She is a wonderful professor and even though the lectures are a bit long, they are really interesting. There would be an amount of homework but they wont take long. boil-1010 is a basic course with lots content, so it's really not the professor's problem and she's doing great.

Wonderful person, but not a great lecturer. The 2 HOUR lecture is her reading directly off the slides and having you watch videos. I just can't pay attention like that. The homework assignments are busywork at best, but usually pretty easy. She posts all the slides, which the exams are all based on, so as long as you just study you'll be fine.

Super nice Prof! Don't be afraid to email her.

That said, I couldn't pay attention to lecture. She plays videos in class and talks slowly. To be fair, she did do a poll in the beginning and most people said they learned best through videos, it just didn't work for me. 

I got a B+ because I was bad at remembering assignments, the class is easy.

Hw assignments are easy. Review her slides before the test and memorize them and you'll be good (I'm not good at memorizing but her lectures r great and interesting so it makes it easy). Tests are online and multiple choice, but must be taken in class (system shows if u are not in class). Final is optional and replaces lowest test score.
Tests were most of the grade and they were really easy.

Lecture is intensely boring. Unless you learn super well from videos you won't learn much. She clearly doesn't have a deep understanding of her own lectures and basically just reads off the slide. Youre better off staying home and reviewing the slides on your own.

While Prof. seems to do her best to be accommodating, questions on her exams can often be overly specific, poorly worded, even to the point where the correct interpretation of what the question actually says results in the wrong answer. Additionally Prof. is an uninteresting lecturer, and slow talker--you'll learn more from the videos than from her

She isn't awful but if you cant learn from videos don't take the class she doesn't really explain anything. If you aren't good at memorizing stuff don't take this course it's all memorization and a lot of work. The really good thing is that her final is optional and will replace the lowest test. Homework is all busy work and kind of annoying.

Pay attention, the previous reviews are all from 10 years ago. She just started teaching again and shes way better than she was before. Literally just watch the videos she shows again before the test and you'll get an A. Pretty engaging lectures too, because she tries really hard to appeal to CS majors who are forced to take bio.
Awful teacher. Didn't know what she was doing, and the course material was abysmally boring.

Try to get a different bio teacher if you can. She basically reads of the slides, but I guess thats ok, as it's a canned course.  But she doesn't seem to very interested in teaching...  she definitely belongs in research.
OMG.  Makes things up as she goes. I can read your powerpoint just as good, ma'am!  Boring, unenthusiastic. Shouldn't be teaching.

Worst. Class. Ever. The work is mindless and tedious, rather reminiscent of elementary/middle school, and there's tons of it. I spent more time on this ridiculous class than most of my real classes combined. I have gotten no benefit out of taking it, only frustration. This class in only here to mess up my GPA.
Doesn't teach, just reads the powerpoints and makes the TA's do the rest.
Does not explain many concepts. The pop quizzes are also hard.

His lecture style of presenting concepts and equations then applying them to example textbook problems worked very well. He also provided lots of practice problems via optional homework assignments which was very good prep for exams. There were pop quizzes throughout the semester but they were straightforward and graded leniently. Great professor!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Great guy, smart professor, good lecturer. Provided plenty of (ungraded) homework, in-class examples, with easy-to-understand lectures. I really have zero complaints about him!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: I believe this is his first year at RPI? Regardless, I quite liked the style of his class. Some content for the first hour, then 3 examples for the next. There are optional hw to do on your own time to prepare for exams. There are 10 pop quizzes but they're graded very leniently and not hard.

Great prof, lectures were great, starting with a few derivations and moves onto examples afterwards. There is optional homework assigned every lecture with the solution posted with it to help one study, in class quizzes occasionally, exams were fair and if you studied the homework and examples, you would surely do well.

The semester started rough, but the professor was open to criticism and feedback and made positive changes to the way the class was operating. He was very willing to review exams and offer valuable advice on how to study. Most importantly, he was flexible with exam makeups, which a lot of RPI professors do not usually allow. Great class experience!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Beware of pop quizzes--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great Professor. This was his first year teaching, but he crushed it! Very available outside of class time for extra help, and is readily available if you need concepts in class explained beyond what is covered in class. Tests are challenging but fair, and are very representative of the (optional) homework material given.

reviews.comment: Dr. Amjad was a great professor throughout the whole semester. His first few days started off kind of rocky, but after that he rocketed to being the best professor of the semester. Incoherently rambles, then wonders why people arent responding in class
Uninspiring, very mechanical (follow what I say) attitude. Throws tantrums like others have said. Please avoid her class.

throws tantrums
goes overtime constantly

CSCI 1100 not 1200. Once got upset with the class for looking at their laptops instead of paying attention to her (computer science class). Consistently begs for participation and throws a tantrum when nobody answers. No grading scheme or rubric, removed random points on homework for no reason. Argued with student who brought it up and walked out.

She cold-calls, which wouldn't be a problem if you knew what she was saying.  She also doesn't know your name and will never learn it out of principle.

She'll always post assignments late, but keep the same deadline. Lectures are extremely confusing. She will (and has) move the lecture online but won't notify students till 5 min AFTER class already started and will punish you for being late. I'd often pray omw to lecture that I was hit by a campus truck so I'd no longer have to take her class.

Regularly posted homework assignments late, keeping the same deadline (so less than the syllabus-given 7 days to work) and claimed it was for our benefit. Literally in what world is a shorter deadline for an assignment that takes 5-10 hours better? I did not go to lecture and ended up doing better than most of my friends who did. Cold call in class
It's true she cold-calls, but it's mostly okay so long as you pay attention. She doesn't have much patience for those who aren't, though.

Didn't care about helping students. Lectures were very confusing, disorganized and stress inducing due to cold calls. How did she make a cold call without knowing names you ask? She described your clothing and liked to call on isolated students. Strict on timing despite never posting the homework on time. Every time I saw her teaching I left.

This professor co-taught CS 1 and my friend and I made a point to go to the other professor's lectures. She was unwilling to help students + got agitated when given feedback despite asking for said feedback. Students were given less time to complete homeworks, she claimed the homework was open for less time to "make students less stressed."

Straight up horrible. She makes no sense in her lectures, the accent doesn't bother me, but when it's to the point where she pronounces 8 out of 10 words in a sentence straight up wrong all the time, it's not English anymore... Never met anyone with such a strong accent before. There was no way for me to input anything she was teaching.

Worst professor I've had. Grading sucks, can get a C in the course and still fail regardless if your test average is too low. She canceled office hours more times than she held them and is hard to follow in lecture. AVOID HER AT ALL COSTS

(Actually for CSCI1100, wasn't a selectable option)
Just a really bad professor. You can't understand her during lectures, she doesn't seem to ever want to help anyone, and she's just not good at teaching. She would get angry when people weren't participating but didn't understand that it's not gonna happen in an 150 person class.

Her main ideology is that "I'm the professor, so what I say goes". She would repeat the instructions for assignments multiple times, but each time, details would change. We had to ask repeatedly to get a straight answer. She threatened to lower everybody's grade multiple times. She posted assignments at the last minute on the discussion forum.

reviews.comment: Take this class, not with this prof. no syllabi, no rubric, no nothing.

Professor Keshan utilized lecture time more effectively than Professor Xiao did when teaching CSCI-1200, though her reliance on forcing students to participate often made lectures stressful for students with anxiety. This professor single handedly de-railed the entire Data Structures course by three units because she wanted to teach us some arbitrary form of a tree (Red Black Tree) only to not even teach it properly and then test us on it. 

She tries really hard to be a good professor but lacks the experience for being a professor.
my life was already on a downhill trend and then I had neha as a professor

Dr. Keshan is kind and her explanations make a lot of sense for the topics she teaches. Provided non-functional AI docs and files from the previous semester, forcing us to start over. She was dismissive when asked for help. Grading was frustratingly based on hidden criteria not listed in the rubric.

This was the worst Capstone class ever. She graded on things not on the rubric while other professors did, so we would get grilled every presentation no matter what. reviews.comment: Overall, a very rude and mean professor. As a professor in capstone, she is very self-centered, pursuing her own personal gain, and does not consider others' feelings in the group. She approved our final presentation without acknowledging the rubric, and thus our group received a low grade. Despite being a PE for a while, she was unaware as well.

Very involved and can be mean at times. For my capstone group, she approved our slides for presenting despite the fact that there were a few major sections of the presentation rubric missing. We were not aware of the rubric and despite being a PE for multiple semesters, it seems she was unaware as well.

Rahmi is a very caring professor that understands that the courses he teaches is difficult and has very good office hours and online presence to ask questions and advice. He is very flexible with exam dates, homework due dates, basically anything that can be moved will probably be moved if you ask nicely enough.

He is a very funny guy and overall a really good professor. He focuses a lot more on his research than his class, but the class was still very good despite that. Definitely be prepared to study a lot for the exams and you will do well.
His test is insanely difficult, trust me do not take his strength.

Compared to other professors in this course, HE IS THE WORST PROFESSOR. I took his class this summer. He tries to make students feel embarrassed and uncomfortable in his class. His notes are an absolute disaster, and the lecture slides are not human-readable. Opt for classes taught by Kristin Mills or Omar El-Shafee instead of him.

FANTASTIC lecturer, the best I've ever had. He makes you care about and gain intuition for the material. Very funny and personable. Incredibly tough grader. Unless you study, expect to feel lost. Test averages very low but he curves everything. His slides are a bit confusing and don't always have all info.

reviews.comment: He failed to explain the content of the course thoroughly due to his weak math and physics background, which makes this course unnecessarily difficult.
He is the man. Strengths isn't my favorite subject but he keeps the lectures interesting and teaches it well. He knows his stuff

Wasted a lot of time on joking instead of really focusing on the materials. Go to class without preparation. Never able to solve the problem in the textbook. Extremely weak in basic math, physics and chemistry.

Strongly recommend he go back to high school and learn some basic physics chemistry and engineering stuff. Guess he bought his PhD degree. He pretends he is good but God he has no idea what he is teaching. His lecture is no help at all for his own exams. How does he manage to keep his job?
Very though class
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Rahmi is a pleasure to be taught by. He is quite fair and honest. Also, he is completely willing to help if you're willing to ask for it. His accent is super dope too which is a nice touch. Reading the textbook really helps on the quizzes.

Rahmi was a great professor. He explains course material very well. He is very helpful during office hours. Thermodynamics itself is a tough subject and the low averages in the class are reflections of thermodynamics subject's ambiguity itself. I would take this class with Rahmi again!
My favorite professor at RPI so far. Made everything easy to understand and is always willing to help if you're willing to put in the effort.
A good introduction to polymers. I took the course years ago and ended up in polymer research. I learned a lot from this course.

I took Rahmi for Strength of Materials and he is clearly the best teacher for that class. All of the sections are hard for this class and the average for our class was 15+ points higher than the other sections. He's great in his office hours and will go out of his way to help you learn if you seek him out. Amazing person and professor.

Rahmi is a really great guy who genuinely cares for his students. He goes above and beyond for his students and wants them to do well. He explains topics much better if you see him one-on-one by making an appointment to see him in his office. Not to mention, his jokes are great, you will be very entertained.

Great guy, really humorous, would like to see his student success. Really helpful outside the class. However, sometimes, his lectures are not clear.  And he is really a poor organizer. Change his syllabus over and over again.
Rahmi will make sure you know the information if you put in the effort. He takes the time to understand students' problems and truly wants to see his students succeed.
He is the top dog. A really nice and amusing professor that helps cut the tedium of thermodynamics with his brand of Turkish swagger.
Greatest professor i have ever had. Truly he deserves praise akin to the praise received by ghandi or MLK.

He was a nice guy and everything, but this class sucked.  The test averages were like 50/100 and even though he curved them, it was very frustrating.  Expected us to do all of the already-worked out book examples on top of the assigned homework 2+ hours of homework a week.
his exams do not test material covered in course
Tried to make this course work, but in the end it was a horrible failure resulting in test averages below 50 and a lot of unhappy students. He is a decent guy, but he should not be teaching.
No Comments

Was his first time teaching the course. He dealt with issues in class in a fairly mature matter but his organization of the course was not so bright (Double-length homework due BEFORE Thanksgiving and test immediately AFTER?)
No Comments
A victim of bad course organization. Knew his stuff, but didn't always teach what ended up being on the tests written by the course coordinator. If you talk a lot in class he will like you.

A good guy who really wants to see his students do well.  His lectures can get boring and sometimes he doesn't seem to know what he's talking about, though.  Hard grader overall.  Unpredictable with some of the questions on the quizzes.

He is one of the best professors I had at RPI. He went over everything that is in the book and warned us that we need to read and understand the book. Was very helpful out of class. I think the course could be changed a little but overall it was a good start to polymers.

Very boring class - prof. is one of the more boring lecturers I've had. However, he's nice when asking questions face to face and will give points back on tests. MUST read the book to do well on the tests. Test questions tend to be ambiguous and random, so write as much as possible. Not much HW.
The worst class I've taken.  Don't expect to learn anything, but be expected to get tested on information that is random and not in the book/notes. Simply put a waste of time.
All he said was read the book, but when you wrote what was in the book to answer his test questions, you didn't get the right answer.

Rhami is a terrible professor. His test questions are vague, and rarely pertain directly to what he lectures on. Even though there are multiple answers to each question, he only accepts one, and thus most people get bad grades.

besides the fact that broken english and little dances fail to describe what polymers are, he doesn't write test questions that ask for anything in particular and then looks for one specific answer and fails you on it, even if it pertains.
The undisputed GOAT. She's awesome. Lectures were a little long and in-depth, but the class provides a lot of resources for students to pass despite how workload heavy it is.

Professor Oakes is phenomenal-- her lectures could be boring (but 2010 can be boring if you already have solid understanding) but she was always incredibly accessible outside of class; often she would respond to questions well outside of hours, and was always willing to help even out of office hours. Makes me very excited for signals with her.

Best professor at RPI. She live streams every lecture and posts them on LMS so you can watch them again later. Posts all the notes, back exams, and anything else you need. Gives you a lot of make up opportunities if you didn't do well on something. Her lectures are so thorough so you understand everything. And so caring, take her if you can
If you fail Circuits with Oakes, YOU wanted to fail. If you care even a little bit, Oakes will do her best to help you. Absolutely nothing bad to say. Amazing
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Oakes is an amazing professor! She always available to help on projects and assignments. She made Robotics I a great class and an interesting field that I want to pursue in. Take any class you can with her and everything will be fine.
One of the only good profs at RPI

Oakes is great, gives a lot of information on the topics she's teaching which sometimes can be overwhelming but in my opinion it's better to have more information than less. Her back exams always help a lot when preparing for tests and she live streams all her classes and is sure to record them.

She's amazing. Everything you'd ever need for the class is posted online. That includes recorded lectures, homework + solutions, back exams, literally everything. She explains everything so well and can make it easy to understand. Really recommend.

Best professor at RPI hands down. She really cares about students learning rather than what grade you end up getting in the course. Dr Oakes makes her lectures seem like she is discovering and deriving the material right then and there, making everything super understandable. Very accessible outside of class too.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Oakes is one of the best professors I have had at RPI by far. She really cares about whether you understand the material more than the letter grade you receive. She is almost always available to answer questions, and will let you retake exams that you did poorly on, and goes over every exam during recitation. She's the best.

Professor Oakes is a very good lecturer, and circuits in general are organized well. The content is clearly presented, and the content on the tests always matches what we learned in class. Alpha Labs were not overly difficult, and grading on labs and tests was usually fairly generous. Overall, if you put effort into the class, you will be good.

I really liked this class and this professor. She is flexible with students, even live streaming her lectures and uploading recordings for those who can't make it to class. She definitely assumes that you have taken a more advanced linear algebra class than Multi, but overall not having done that didn't really affect my grade. The project was fun.
Simply amazing. Great lectures filled with practice problems, which are very similar to what comes on test. Clear and concise, no fluff, straight to the point as every course should be.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: highly recommend

She doesn't normally teaches circuits but she did a great job, the lecture consists pretty much exclusively of practice problems and a few group assignments. So if that style doesn't work well for you the videos on the course website might help. 
Very accessible at her office hours and very quick to respond to inquiries. HW is tough but completion
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This is the best professor I ever met during college. She's a very kind and helpful lady with rich teaching experience.  If you miss something in class, everything covered would go to piazza including the recordings of entire class. The policy of taking home exam portion is also great. Just go for this professor if you want the best outcome.

Extremely considerate and willing to help with any questions you may have about the material. She has a recitation period every week, will schedule other appointments, and responds very quickly to online questions. There's a lot of material covered in this course, but grading is easy. Median has to be close to an A-.

Actually meant for ECSE-2410, but great professor all the same! Shows how to derive seemingly complex topics, allots 2hrs where you can ask questions about course material, and records the lectures so you don't even need to attend class. Would give 10/5 if I could!

This review is actually for robotics 1.

One of the best profs at RPI. They will solve all your doubts and queries. A great depth of knowledge in the field. Leninat Grader. Their in-class lectures were difficult to follow because they spoke softly. Easy to understand notes but difficult to follow their handwriting.
Awesome professor! She is willing to answer my stupid question anytime, until I fully understand what is going on.

Professor Oakes was the only reason that IED was remotely tolerable. In a class where expectations are vague and ill defined, Oakes was able to provide clear, grounded information, and helping to point my team in the right direction. Furthermore, she provides effective constructive criticism, and all of her feedback on reports was fair and useful.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: One of the best professors I ever had and actually cares for the understanding of her students. AMAZING lectures. Just make sure to study homework problems and the practice exam while knowing the concept itself

Professor Tumuklu is one of the best professors at RPI. The class is challenging and sometimes confusing, but he brings passion and energy to every lecture. He uses humor, welcomes feedback, answers questions thoroughly, and connects the material to real-world applications.

The goat. He is extremely engaging and funny in lecture and actually made me want to come to class every day. Super knowledgeable in fluids and lectures are theory based so it can be hard to follow at times but he does try his best to adapt to what students want. Tough but fair class. Bonus points may be given for participation in lectures
Awesome professor. Very helpful at office hours and after class. Made lectures fun even when deriving equations. Would definitely recommend.
He is a nice guy and helps when you need. Extremely knowledgeable and approachable. He gives real life examples. Everything is planned but be prepared worked hard. He hates Ponzi schemes.
Bad lecturer. I had to relearn many topics by myself to do well in later classes. Spends too much time on ideas instead of solving practical problems to explain things.

I thought he was pretty good overall. I actually kind of enjoyed going to his lectures which tend to be entertaining. The hardest part for me was how much he stresses the concepts. Tests were up to 40% concept questions, so you basically have to memorize the facts on the lecture slides in addition to learning the scary math. His HWs help though.

Pretty good lecturer, although lecture notes aren't great. 82.5% of our grades was based off of 3 equally-weighted midterms and final exam, with lowest test score dropped (so final was technically optional), and the remaining 17.5% across 8 homework assignments. 0 late credit on HW, but solutions were released immediately. Tough class, fair grades

It was fun to be in his lectures. He's theory oriented in lecture which can get hard at times. Very hard class! That said, Professor Tumuklu was generous in his final grades. Exams were tough and heavy, but not unfair. Overall I was happy to be in his class, but be prepared to work for it.

Professor Tumuklu is dedicated to his students' success and is easily accessible for help. His lecture delivery could use s. While it's only his second year teaching, he is actively seeking ways to engage his students. He's clearly passionate, and I'm confident he'll continue to grow into an excellent instructor.

I have mixed feelings about him. Fluids is pretty tough, but I went to many office hours for hw and it really helped me understand what was going on during lecture and learn about him as a person, and he is actually quite nice and funny. He is probably the most self-aware prof too when it comes to understanding the limits of his students.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: As the others mention, he is extremely knowledgeable about fluid mechanics but not the best teacher. He is a funny/nice guy, he always seemed very stressed out and sad that people weren't paying attention in lecture, but he taught in a way that was very conceptual and often made things way more difficult to understand than they needed to be

Prof Tumuklu is very knowledgeable in fluid mechanics but he's a bad teacher. After we requested more examples, he said he would do them but kept deriving equations instead. Homeworks are hard and barely related to the lectures/textbook examples.

I took Prof. Onkar's class on FEM for fluid dynamics. The course has a clear roadmap starting from the basics of FEM to Non linear problems. You need to be decent with python to do the assignments and projects. No exams but projects and assignments are heavy and can take up a day. Make use of office hours to make the most out of the course.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He is very knowledgeable about using Python for problem-solving, but he had a lot of trouble getting his point across. Compared to other professors teaching the same course, he barely does quiz preparation. It is also frustrating that this course is so disorganized.

I originally had him as my Numerical Methods teacher but switched to another because I couldn't handle his teaching style. He tried his best to explain concepts but sometimes just ended up reading off lecture slides without elaboration. He's accessible in office hours and emails which helped. He looked out for students but I wouldn't take him again
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This class is all back work. If you have the tests/homework from the previous two years, this class will be easy for you even if you don't know whats going on. He is helpful at office hours though and if I wasn't a senior, I may have put more effort into the class. Class notes are pretty helpful for understanding the backtests.
Very helpful outside of class and is willing to help you with homework. Tests were somewhat tricky, but redoing the homework for practice makes such a difference.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Olsen's only saving grace was that he could explain things well during office hours. However, lectures are useless, and his handwriting is unreadable. Exams typically had various mistakes, which would be haphazardly corrected on the board midway through the exam. The homework did not align well with the exam questions.
exams were confusing and important information was changed on them halfway through

Wastes much of his lecture time on anecdotes / untestable material. He doesn't show enough examples to learn the material. His handwriting is also terrible which doesn't help. In addition, 3 out of the 4 exams we were given had multiple errors on them, and corrections were made haphazardly during the exam in order to make the problems solvable.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: During lectures it is difficult to get a firm grasp on the concept being taught (a combination of his bad handwriting and quickly going through example problems), however if you go to his office hours I find he is extremely helpful and knowledgeable about the topics covered. If you take charge of learning the material, he will help you.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: lenient grader (becuase of his own mistakes), but does not teach a single thing.
