Olson is quite possibly the worst educator I have ever met. Thermodynamics is an incredibly difficult class, and it doesn't help that Olson REFUSES to teach it. I learned nothing from lectures, his notes were riddled with mistakes and he had typos and missing information on 2 of his tests. AVOID THIS PROF

Doesn't actually teach the content, so often need to use other resources to know what's going on. The hw doesn't relate to exams, and he has a huge ego. He isn't much of a teacher. He never explains topics, just gives you the equations and expects you to already know the material and how he got to his answers.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Bro does not teach, nor wants to teach. Lecture consists of 3 or 4 power point slides about global warming and nothing else useful. I learned everything through chegg.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: A small man with a fragile ego. Some students (myself included) let him believe he was an expert in the field because they felt bad for him. You can tell there is pain behind his eyes. Sadly, he projects this pain onto his students rather than looking inwards. Side note, his book is also unreadable.

Great professor that prioritizes communication and the success of his students. Most of the course material is very easy to understand, but please note that the class is very group and presentation heavy - just like in the real world. Overall, I had a fantastic experience with this Professor, and would highly recommend you take MGMT 1100 with him!

Prof O wants you to do well and is reasonable. It is important to participate in his class. Homework is usually assigned readings which you discuss in class. There are PS Challenges to work on with your assigned group every week. Quizzes are m.c. (25-30 q's) but you need to thoroughly review the notes. He also has a few extra credit opportunities.

Prof. O is the type of professor where you could really learn life long lessons from a conversation outside of class. His classes were lecture heavy, information heavy, and quizzes were difficult. However, if you participate in class, contribute to group work (P.S. Challenges), he will see that and look out for you. Highly recommend this guy

Prof O. is very organized and have a clear agenda with how he runs each class. Quizzes are multiple choice, but they are still tough so pay attention in class and do the assigned readings. He does not grade participation, but it is a participation heavy class. Be prepared to work with a group for activities and a final project.

Hes a great professor who is always accessible to answer any questions. Wants his students to do their best so if you do the work, you should do pretty well in the class. Quizzes were pretty tough but overall I would recommend the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Olson is one of the worst professors I've had at RPI. During his lectures he never solves out problems which leaves students at a disadvantage and also is not useful for the homework's. He also never proofreads his exams beforehand and likes to add in missing information/change information during the exams. Get ready to self-study.

Olson is probably a great professor for nuclear classes, but he certainly should not be allowed to teach an INTRO Thermo class. He does not do ANY problem solving in lecture, he rambles trying to get students to understand the "big picture" of Thermo but makes 0 sense, and he doesn't even proofread his exams (expect actually impossible questions)

I passed the class, so he managed to teach me a bit.  But almost all learning came from doing homework, not from his lectures.  In his lectures, he showed not only his huge ego but also gave very little actual information about thermodynamics.  Textbook required not only for tables of info but also to actually learn anything.

AVOID AT ALL COSTS - the lecture slides are almost entirely irrelevant to hw/exams and he makes sure to never explain anything fully or properly. He rambles constantly about engineering as a whole but never about thermo. ALL exams including the final have had serious typos and mistakes and overall he seems to have no regards for his students.

Take ANYONE else. Lectures are packed with misinformation that can and will cause you to get wrong answers on exams. Allergic to doing examples. Homeworks/quizzes are nothing like lecture. Multiple hour+ rambles into nowhere. Endless errors on exams. If you're unfortunate enough to have him for Thermo, expect to cling to the textbook for dear life.

AVOID AT ALL COSTS. Simply cannot teach. Readings are usually irrelevant to his lectures. Shows hardly any example problems. So many errors in lectures that if he does convey a point, you are left wondering whether it is accurate. Doesn't accept criticism, and grades harshly if you deviate from "his" method on exams, which are RIDDLED WITH ERRORS!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: WHY IS HE TEACHING THERMO? I can never read his notes, which is very irrelevant to exams. Try another professor if you have any other choices...

The professor has made mistakes on almost every exam, including the Final Exam. His notes are difficult to read and contain some mistakes. There were a few errors with due dates too. He is better at explaining course material at office hours. During lectures he can get off-topic and talks about sustainable energy and other semi-related topics.

everyone is review bombed him because of his thermo class this year, but much of his shortcomings this year were not all his fault. the exams this year were missing key variables in order to solve the problems, but in respect to the actual course and how he taught it, i dont know how it would be done better. in his office hours he was very helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: He understands the material well and gave a lot of opportunities for students to do well. The exams were difficult but he gave points for getting the basics down even if you didn't get the question completely right. With that said, he took lecture notes using a mousepad and you could barely make out his handwriting...
Messed up 3 exams, the back and practice exams don't help, take thermo with any other professor if you can, even if you have to wait.
Very vague in his explanations and very messy hand writing

Don't take for thermo try someone else. His lectures almost never have anything to do with test material. Never even did a practice problem he just rambles on about engineering stuff not related to course material. Almost all of the learning is done through homework by teaching yourself as his lectures don't help.

I both love and hate Olson as a lecturer. His lectures are very interesting and engaging. However, they're irrelevant to the homework/exam content 70% of the time. Expect most lectures to be rambly and opinionated, mainly covering engineering as a whole. If you like fun lectures and can teach yourself the material, pick Olson. Otherwise, don't.

He really wanted students to learn to problem-solve as opposed to just memorizing course content. Lectures weren't always super helpful with homework, so some reading in the textbook helped a lot with unfamiliar content, but I thought they were pretty engaging and to the point most of the time.

Lectures can deviate greatly from homework and exams but are interesting and intended to make you understand fundamental and real-world applications of Thermodynamics. Most of the learning is from homework.

The reading is not required but is recommended for people who would normally rely on lectures for course content.
One of the greatest classes I've taken is PropSys. Frequent his office hours for amazing homework help and life philosophy lessons. Very knowledgeable, hope to take another of his classes.
Very well spoken professor who seems to enjoy what he is doing, the course wasn't particularly hard but he made it very interesting. One of the best professors I have had.

Professor Oehlschlaeger is incredibly caring and easy-going.  Lectures are very well prepared and informative.  Exams are straightforward.  Homework is graded on effort rather than correctness.  Overall, he's probably the best professor I've had at RPI.
One of the best professors in RPI, you should have no problem with the test if you understand the examples in his lecture notes and he is quite generous in grading

Great professor, always makes lectures interesting. Passionate about the subject and always talks about the industry applications to what we are learning - got me inspired to pursue aero while taking his class as meche!

I had him for summer arch TF1. He's a chill professor who's very approachable. He's pretty young (30ish). He lectures well and grades fairly easily. 3 tests are your only grades. He'll spend some time to answer your questions and explain things if need. He's not too pushy so he won't demand class interaction. Great guy, in and out of class.

Excellent professor on all fronts. Lectures are well prepared derivations, tests are challenging but fair, optional homeworks are definitely recommended. Matt is very helpful outside of the classroom as well. I would definitely recommend taking any course that he is teaching because it will be well done.

Matt is easily the best professor I've had at RPI. His lectures were clear and effective, and his enthusiasm for the material helped inspire the class to actually care about it. Tests were fair, as was his grading system. Overall just a wonderful person.

Matt is the greatest professor at this university. He is clear in what he expects and has realistic expectations. He knows what it is like being a student and teaches for you to do well. His lectures are really helpful and he makes difficult material easy to understand. Two thumbs up!

Probably the best teacher I've had.  He's very realistic about how easily students forget things between semesters and he'll brush up on topics to keep everyone current.  In class work was very relevant and engaging.

Great professor, one of the best on campus.  Material was difficult, but the notes he gives in class are superb and he answers emails promptly.  I definitely recommend this professor for any class he's teaching.  One of the few professors that realizes that students have other classes besides his.
This guy is definitely up there on the best teacher list.  He knows that school is important, but knows that life is more important.  Real helpful at office hours, cant say anything bad about him.

This guy is a great teacher.  He is smart, the material for the class was fast paced, but he understands that undergrads will be behind the grads and makes up for it in the grades later.  If he is a choice for a professor, choose him.
One of the worst professors I've taken. Extremely unclear assignments and tough grader.

Actually, I think Gina is a very responsible professor although very strict. She is very helpful and resourceful, and she concerns students. Her marketing classes are awesome. I really enjoyed her class.

She is arrogant and does not listen to an opinion that is not 100% in line with hers.  Grades hard, and belittles students for sharing their opinions.  She thinks she knows everything because she has a PhD, when in fact she has no real world experience.
No Comments
I found her lectures easy to follow and the assignment expectations very clear.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: She's a very kind and understanding professor who cared about her students. Not the easiest A since it is a writing heavy course, but doable. I also wish she had a policy for excused absences, since I had to force myself to go to class when I was feeling unwell a few times. Course topics were a bit dry, but I still found them somewhat interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: She is a very kind and understanding professor. The course is heavily dependent upon two essays and she is a lenient grader, just use office hours to your advantage. I didn't find the course topics too interesting, but is an overall easy course to fulfill an elective.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Peterson-McCann is such a sweetheart. She's clearly passionate about her job, and you can tell the effort she makes to curate her lessons. There is a strict attendance policy, but it is fair bc class is mainly discussion. She's a fair grader, and it's always accurate with rubric/syllabus. Gives excellent feedback on your work and is very kind
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Peterson-McCann is honestly such a sweetheart. She's very passionate about what she teaches and carefully curates every reading/lecture to be interesting. She has a pretty strict attendance policy but does not make attending class seem like a chore. She's a fair grader, very accurate to her syllabus and rubrics and gives great feedback.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Very nice professor. She was very lenient with late submissions, graded closely with the syllabus, and is clearly passionate about what she teaches. If you want an enjoyable, easy class, she's a good professor to have. She is fairly strict with her attendance policy. Every unexcused absence past a threshold is a whole letter grade reduction.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: he runs the course for the first half of the semester which is generally pretty easy content. lectures are long and definitely dull at times, but they're easily understood. he's accessible outside class and hw/exam questions come directly from the textbook. grade weights are wack: 20% hw, 30% midterm exam, 50% final exam
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He rarely responds to emails and provides very little feedback on homework or presentations. Graded work was not returned; only a final letter grade was posted on SIS. The class is all about readings which can be a little bit dry.

He is easy to reach outside of class, and genuinely cares about your success. He grades things very fairly, but weighs exams way too heavily. Our final was worth 50%, and our midterm 30%. Attendance was not mandatory, but you should still go, as his lectures are where he covers all of the material step-by-step.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is super inaccessible outside of class, which was super frustrating, because no matter how hard I tried, I could never get an in-person meeting. He promised that he would continue to be avaliable after we had a professor switch, but that was not the case. He didn't have any clear reasoning on grading our design projects, which kinda sucked.

He's a really solid lecturer and seems to really care about students he has. MEEBal was wonderful with him and he made it easy to transition into, especially as a budding cheme. Isn't great about office hours and isn't very good at responding to emails though.

He rushed through problems in class & moved on even if students didn't understand. Very inaccessible outside of class -he didn't respond to a single email & cancelled his office hours last minute. Exams were difficult & counted for most of the grade. Since he curved grades at the end, you didn't know your grade all semester, until it was finalized.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: MEEBAL was very hard, but he wanted to make sure everyone understood the material. Often went too fast when solving problems, but took class feedback and was accessible outside of class.

Prof. Karande is the best professor I've had at RPI. He genuinely cares and wants to make absolutely sure that his students understand the material. He tries not to overwhelm, even though MEEBAL can be an overwhelming course.

Dr. Karande is probably the best professor I've had at RPI thus far. He really cares about making sure his students understand the concepts he teaches. He thoroughly goes through problem solving methods to the point that one example will give you a complete understanding of how to solve any problem of that nature. Great professor!!
PK is my favorite professor so far at RPI. He's extremely helpful if you go to his office hours or if you ask questions in class. Funny guy, great professor.
This class is wery wery interesting. I absolutely love this guy!
Use his office hours esp. for the design projects. He definitely appreciates kids he sees putting in effort, and reciprocates equally.

Design projects are hard but turn out to be fun if you have a good group. He is awesome if you get to know him and his test are straight forward as long as you go to class and understand what you do in class. i really liked him

Professor Plotka is a good professor. The class moves quickly between topics, with languages like MySQL and JavaScript covered briefly. Grading can take some time, and many assignments are graded automatically. Overall, the course is manageable if you stay on top of the material.

He takes attendance so you need to go everyday which seems juvenile for a capstone level class. For the first half of the semester it seemed like he just made up stuff for us to do like debate each other or present a random topic to the class.

If you don't pay attention, the Labs become hard, and then you fall behind/use AI for the work. My work method was setting aside 4-5 hours over the weekend + Monday to work on and finish the labs, and any info not covered was googled. Overall, an intriguing class and my favorite of that semester

Nice guy & knowledgeable, but not great at teaching. Covered a ton of concepts at a shallow level, which made me feel constantly lost. Assignments are still manageable b/c he gives examples to help, but to learn anything fully, you have to do it alone. Read rubrics carefully, lots of details to remember. Don't procrastinate labs, ask for help too.

Very solid class. However, you will definitely need to set aside 4-5 hours per lab assignment each week or half-week to complete. Heavily used Google and a bit of AI to complete this assignment(AI was for questions related to material ONLY). Pay attention, take notes, complete labs, and Do Your Work. Other than that, enjoyable class ngl.

Fake class. I finished every lab perfectly, I got 20 points deducted because I put in wrong link. No explanation about grading, never replies to emails. Don't work on group projects too much, they don't decide your grades. Read the instructions carefully, make sure on every things, double-check. Learned nothing from him, just stressed.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very knowledgeable and likable guy. He's always accessible outside of class for help. Only complaints were that assignments took forever to be graded (sometimes up to 3 weeks) and you could have up to 5 assignments due on the same day. There was one day where we had a case study, a lab, a group project writeup, and a quiz all on the same day.

prepare for plotka to move deadlines to earlier dates without warning and not provide groups for projects until 3 days before they are due (when we should have had groups from day 1). i have had weekends where 3+ labs and projects were assigned due monday. expects you to already know everything in an intro course so get ready to teach yourself

Plotka is very knowledgeable but he also demands a lot sometimes. He really wants people to participate and also sometimes speak up on things they really don't know anything about. The course content is interesting but we also move very fast and there's a lot, so be sure to keep up and do all your assignments.
Very knowledgeable professor who is able to clearly explain concepts to all levels of students. He is a bit of a strict grader but always strives for student improvement.
Class is a free A if you are putting in your time. Quizzes are open note so you don't even need to study and group project is fun
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Plotka is a little hard to follow at times but he truly wants the best for everyone and is always available on Discord or after class to explain things. He makes it all clear if you're brave enough to admit that you're lost which is fair in a lot of intro level courses.

Professor Plotka is a wonderful professor. He is knowledgeable in what he teaches, approachable, friendly, and an overall excellent professor. He is also very flexible with deadlines and grading, offering a generous amount of time for any assignment.
So many labs and the material for them is expected to be learned on your own
Did not give any feedback for the submitted section work and give a really bad grade on the final report. Didn't really learn anything. If possible, DON'T take his course (guess not possible)
Great professor, well respected, always gives clear grading criteria and projects.

What an amazing professor. He's willing to bring in outside lecturers and really teaches you practical things you use in industry. He makes you work in teams and do a lot of technical projects and presentations. He prepared by so much for my co-op and is really helpful in helping students apply for interships. He really cares a lot.

Professor Plotka is an extremely knowledgeable and respected professor, and it is an exciting opportunity just to take one of his classes. The class wasn't the easiest, but I learned a ton. He also really cares about his students, and is really accessible during office hours.

Profesor Plotka is my favorite professor at RPI. He grades fairly, and his classes are entertaining. Plotka actually got my group together to tell the other members he could see that they were not pulling their weight. He continued to intervene to help us work better together as a group, this is a skill I needed help with.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Plotka teaches the majority of the core ITWS classes and he's absolutely wonderful. His classes are definitely tough, but you learn so much. He is also really accessible during office hours if you ever need him. His classes involve a lot of group work, presentations, and labs so be ready to work hard. Overall, he's a great guy, would recommend.
Amazing teacher. Classes are well structured. Always willing to help. Literally always
He is an amazing man.

I had Professor Ji for Computer Vision (CV) and it was one of the most difficult classes I have taken at RPI. You need a good mathematics (Linear Algebra) and programming (python or Matlab) background. Overall, Professor Ji is very respected in the CV community and extremely insightful. Only take CV if you have an interest in the subject!
As a student of this course, although this teacher is very strict, he is a good teacher like never before.

The course was 'Introduction to Deep Learning' and it was very demanding. There were lots of homeworks and programming assignments. The difficulty level was between medium and high. However, professor is helpful if you reach out to him and discuss your issues. You have to work hard and give time to this course.
He will let you know life is full of dangers.
homework isnt so easy but labs and tests are open book so it's easy to do well.
not good
The only words: "Life is not easy!"
No Comments

Prof Ji was simply this most unprofessional teacher I have ever had.  Although I attended every lecture and made sure to keep good notes he found it necessary to call me a "loser" and "disrespectful to him and my father" during the last class.

The comments about his anti-American attitudes are spot-on.  To quote him directly, "There are over one billion of us!"  The context of that statement was the final lecture of the Spring '05 class, where he chided the class for being lazy, and also engaged one student in particular simply because he was sitting with his feet up.  Weird.
EXTREMELY Anti-American; insults students in front of entire class using derrogatory terms for asking questions. In the process of filing a complaint against this guy...he's the real LOSER!
Aweful!  Hates Americans. Rants about how bad americans are constantly.  Call you and idiot and says you will never get into grad school because your inferior.

More than once I have seen him lose his temper and fly off the handle, (never at me) many times simply because a student asked a question or didn't understand. His last lecture ended with him yelling at all of us and telling us we were terrible students. Way to leave a last impression.
he says 'ok' and 'right' every other word and doesn't like to accept the fact that we don't know what he thinks he taught us when we say we don't know the information. then he quizes us anyways.

Ok, I'm sick of him say ok, ok? Coherency, politeness, and a desire to teach are obviously no longer requirements for professors. He prefers lecturing on how students don't know the material than actually teaching it. He expects that every student should already have a phd.

Cannot speak english. Is easily distracted and upset during class. Demeans American students (basically says we are slackers and will never get into grad school/get a job) Very vague, better to just read the book and go to studio, lecture is worthless.
Has a hatred for American students.
Looked like he hated teaching, yells at students.  Once saw him call a guy stupid in front of everyone in lab.

Jerk with a capital J.  They just let anyone lecture these days.  Not nice to students at all.  Would be better suited as a corrections officer.  He cares more about students behaving in class rather than learning.  Complete jerk
Good explanations, sometimes hard to understand his accent.
Funny guy
Very hard, unclear class.  He's very tough on students (verbally + academically)
No Comments
Good professor!!! Recommend!!!
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Good professor, tried to let everyone focused and participated, but failed all the time; has a think accent as posted before, but it was understandable. Some pop-up quizzes and you can drop one. Better than other Accounting for DC professors.

Prof. Wu is a nice guy who knows what he's talking about, and the accounting class I took with him is easy.  He has a thick accent and isn't always clear, but I can't complain about his class.  He does try to get the class to participate, but it usually doesn't work.  The material just isn't engaging enough, I think.

Super easy A for humanities reqs. dont show up to lecture ever, just do the hws/quizzes/tests once a month ish (all online open book/internet). If you do show up to lecture she is a good lecturer however.

Econ inquiry is an easy A. All the work and exams are online. Homeworks and quizzes have unlimited attempts. There's two 500 word essays (topic of your choice) that are graded very leniently. Prof Greene's lectures are to the point and functional. Most people skip the lectures. Highly recommend this class if you're looking for a light workload.
Very easy course. Required to pay for pearson MyLab to complete assignments, but I never went to lecture after the first one and finished the course with an A.
intro to econ is the easiest inquiry class and is basically online. you dont need to go to lectures at all and the hws/quizzes have a cumulative due date. exams are online and the final is optional.

Prof. Greene was really knowledgeable on Econ, and her lectures were easy to follow. I ended up skipping lectures in the second half of the semester because I got too busy with other classes, but it was very manageable. HW, quizzes, and tests are all on Pearson. HW and quizzes have unlimited attempts. 2 short essays on whatever you want.
Easy A no need to go to lecture

Never went to class after the first day, got an A, two 500-1000 word papers on literally anything. Couldn't tell you how lectures went, but I took this class for my HASS requirement first year and 100% recommend you do too if you want to get it over with. So easy, amazing class, basically online.

Prof. Greene is kind & her personal research seems interesting, but the course overall was not. She teaches fine but I zoned out every class after the 1st one, & by the end 20ish people showed up. Definitely do take b/c HW and quizzes allow unlimited attempts. Tests are take-home and papers are graded on completion. Easy to do well & low effort.
Don't come. Lecture sucks, mandatory reading, confusing class pace, foggy syllabus, blindly chosen textbook and waste of time.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Attendance wasn't mandatory. All lectures online. Homework and 3 tests on Pearson due at the end of each month or so. 2 500-word papers about basically anything you want. HW and quizzes have unlimited retries. Definitely an easy A if that's what you're looking for. This style worked for me and I still think I learned the material pretty well.
Her class was very easy but very boring. I really liked economics in high school but sitting through lectures in this class was painful.

REALLY BORING LECTURES. Granted I'm not interested in economics and took this course for my inquiry, but I can't understate how easy it is for your attention to drift when you're in her class. You'll learn a fair amount if you're actually interested in the topic however.

Granted I was never a big fan of economics before taking the class, the lectures were hard to sit through and weren't very engaging. She seemed like a cool person and she definitely knows what she is talking about. But the lecture material wasn't reflected in the tests, which I learned the hard way.

P.S. Goes by Dr.Greene

Econ 1200 is a really light load. There were 2 essays graded on completion, and the 2 tests (and optional final) were all open note. However, Dr. Greene is also an incredibly boring lecturer. I would recommend this class if you have already taken some form of economics, and you want an easy inquiry without ever showing up.

I had Professor Parrales in Spring 2023 and I really liked the class. Everything including the exams were online. She's also empathetic and understanding if you ever get a chance to speak to her. The exams are pretty similar to the homework too. I didn't find the content too challenging and overall, the class was great.

The class was great and overall well taught. However, attendance wasn't mandatory and 100% of the material was posted online. Because of this, my 300 kid lecture turned into 30 kids by the end of the semester. The class is an easy A and a good elective to add to a rigorous schedule. Overall, the professor was kind and clearly loves economics.
This class is a lot of "listen to lecture, do homework on this textbook homework platform". Really easy and the lectures are of fairly good quality.
lecture is a little dry, test and hw are not that hard

I can't speak for her in-person class, but I would advise against her online class. Her class is entirely prerecorded lectures from 2015, using a different textbook. There are homeworks that ask about things she's never even mentioned in her lectures. If you don't mind cheating though, it's pretty easy.

I would rather die than hear her voice at 8 am. You basically don't ever have to show up for class except for the exam as long as you follow what she posts on LMS and the online homework. She's very clear about what you have to do and the tests are basically identical to the online homework questions.
The curve is really good

You don't need to show up to one lecture, just do the online homework and show up for the final and you can get a A in the class. She tends to go off on random tangents in lecture and most sessions are ran by TAs
Terrible lecturer. Unless you love econ this class is extremely boring.

Prof. Parrales is fine. Took her for ECON-1200 back when it was cross-listed as IHSS-1200. I think it's tough to teach the intro material because it is very, very DRY. I think she did her best all things considered. However, her lecture style is not for everyone. That said, if you pay attention, and/or read the textbook, you should be fine.

You don't need to attend class, and the exams are pretty hard because the backtests do not help. There is no curve and the two tests are worth 40%. The work you do for the class does not really help for the exam either, but you could easily make a B if you do the hw and journals. The way she explains is hard to understand and gets messy quick.

There's no extra credit in this class any longer. If you want an A, which is 94, you need to do well not only on the homework, but also on the test. First, you need to get at least 95 on your homework which means you are already loss 2 point on your final grade. Second, get average 92 on both of your exams, which is much harder than back tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This professor is fair and pretty easy. Lectures can get boring though if you are not very interested in the subject. If you mess something up, she is very understanding, and gives you multiple opportunities to succeed. Beyond accepting some late work, there is extra credit available, and an optional final. Good choice for your HASS class.

Her lectures are not clear at all, especially because of the extremely blurry notes she writes every class. Don't expect to learn much from her notes and during her lectures. You definitely need to study the past exams on LMS hard in order to score higher on the exams!
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--EXTRA CREDIT--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Lectures are extremely unclear and she says to read the book but that didnt seem to help much. Took the class in Fall 2017 and the only way to do decently on tests was to grind 3-4 back exams and memory dump on the test.

She gets a lot of heat from students sometimes, but I can't complain. She made the course criteria very clear and taught everything clearly. She's a good lecturer, the tests are very fair, and she gives a lot of material for you to study from. Can I say I like economics? No, but Dr.P was a good professor. Not the best, but not bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: This course, unfortunately, suffers similarly to her ECON 1200 course, but without lecture videos. Lectures are drawn out and seemingly helpful only on a few occasions. The backwork she provides is somewhat similar, but encourages memorization of answers, because her teaching style does not promote learning of the material.
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I'm no ECON major, but there's really too much to dedicate to this course given that it's introductory and only meets twice a week. Her lecture style is obviously directed towards those who already understand economics. Even if you show up, her online materials are more helpful (I guess) but lengthy at best, just like her lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Show up, take some light notes. Do the back tests she gives you. Get A, simple as that.
Show up and listen, or just sleep. Read the textbook and then do the backtests she gives(which have similar questions as test). Get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Her voice makes me sleepy, but the A was easy. Goes for ECON1200 too.
It was easy if you showed up to class or read the textbook or watched her online videos.  Lectures were boring but covered the material.  Tests were all multiple choice.
Grades depended on 4 tests (2 micro, 2 macro). Final can replace your whole grade, so you will either need to do well on the 4 tests, or focus on the final. The tests are fairly difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: One of the best teachers I've had at RPI. The lecture videos were great. She provides the tools you need to get an A.
Easiest class I've taken since preschool
Read the book or watch video lectures. Do back tests. Easy A.  Her lectures aren't especially helpful but the course is easy enough.
She puts all content to LMS lecture. But always late and she cannot clarify the knowledge very clearly. Too many tests, with 2.5 each question and 94 for A.
You do most of the work yourself but as long as it gets done it's a super easy class.

I wasn't really interested in ECON-1200 but Parrales makes the class very clear. She records lectures online which is extremely convenient and makes it so that one good night of studying will have you earning A's on the tests. Great personality, great professor. ECON was much less painful than it could have been thanks to her.

Lectures rarely last longer than an hour.  She requires you to watch recorded lectures of her to learn the material which can be annoying but allow you to study at your own rate.  Tests were of moderate difficulty but very passable if you study.  Her voice can sometimes be annoying.  Often rewords powerpoint slides in answer to questions.

The tests were difficult if you had no previous economics background. She is very knowledgeable of the material but power points may not be the best presentation method. The final can count as your entire grade if it is better than your test averages.
Class is boring. Stopped going after the 3rd week. Can learn everything without her

Friendliest and most accommodating professor I have had during my tenure as a student here. It was her first time teaching Money & Banking and she didn't always have all the answers at her fingertips, but you could tell she put in a lot of work to know what she was saying and deliver it well. If there was a tough question, she always followed up.
Awesome teacher. Homework/projects/ etc are all online and nearly impossible to fail.
she is a really amazing teacher. Does everything in her power to help you out, and the class is insanely easy.
Outstanding intro to economics professor.  All course material is online, meaning tests can be taken online at home with classmates and all the resources you want, and she has no problem with it.

Overall good professor. Usually only holds the class for about an hour and leaves the rest of the time for studying. Uses old exams. Keeps lectures entertaining with videos and activities. Good amount of homework, but it really helps you study for the exams.

Doesn't teach from the text, but uses videos as supplemental material.  Very good at explaining concepts if the text was somehow too difficult.  Material is easy, exams are mixed.  Extra credit available.  The exams are no longer open book or open notes.

This teacher is obviously teaching straight from the text book.  She lacks any intuition or common-sense regarding economics, i.e. she uses material from "The Onion" to depict current evens, oblivious to the fact that its a satire.  I feel like i've lost intelligence from being in this class.

Really, she looks like Sarah Palin. And is definitely past her prime. She has her degree in Wood Forestry, not Economics. She no longer gives open book tests, but is still a horrible teacher. Wear plaid and eat pancakes for an A.

One of the easiest classes I have ever taken. The tests are open note and open book, plus there is significant amount of extra credit offered, but you probably won't even need to take advantage of it. If you even try in the least you will get an A.
This class has open book and open note tests, and she tells you in class what in her notes will be on the tests.
Pretty good looking professor. In her mid twenties. Blonde. VERY easy on the eyes =) Gives extra credit. Easy A. Easy B for the dumbasses
The class was the easiest I've taken at RPI, but I wasn't bored. The material was fairly interesting. Parrales explains it well. She's easy on the eyes, too.
Amazing professor, genuinely interesting class, lenient grader. Highly recommend
Incredible! Her class is so accessible and way more interesting than I was expecting- I highly recommend! Very lenient grader and very kind

Communications with Reina was genuinely so interesting. As far as HASS classes go, this was the most engaging one I have taken and she was really lax when it came to the material. Her class really made me glad I took the media pathway, especially with engaging assignments and really interesting lectures if you like this sort of thing.
One of the best COMM and Writing professor. She is trying to keep the class active and she has good explanations and examples of the course material.
Good at explaining and encourages participation.
Easy to understand.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Weina is the best professor I have ever met, she is caring and makes the class atmosphere perfect. Definitely take her class if you want to enjoy university.

Fantastic educator, the videos are great. He's difficult and the class is hard, but is accessible in office hours and always willing to help. Exams are unreasonably hard, on one notable occasion there was a question worth ~15% on a topic that he said wouldn't be on the exam. However, I stress, other than exams he's great.

So brilliant of a man that he does not understand that his Engineering Probability class is difficult. No nonsense in the best possible way: does not ramble, does not waste time, does not go on unrelated tangents. With laser precision he teaches, answers questions, and leaves (often early). If you want to learn something, get him for you class.

Prof Radke is definitely standing on the front lines against grade inflation. I wouldn't be surprised if more people get F's than A's in this class (exam averages ranged from 61 to 71 with 2-5 percentage points added as a curve at the course's end, and the average RPI EE student isn't exactly lazy or bad at math either). But a good prof overall.
Has "Probability Bites" videos that supplements well with his great lectures. Tests and homework is a bit tough, but completely fair to how well he teaches.

Dr. Radke is the best professor I've had in my educational career. His lectures are fantastic, the classes are perfectly structured and paced, he's one of the most accessible/helpful professors outside of class, and the homeworks are incredibly interesting. But above all, it's clear that he truly loves teaching and cares about the students.

Good guy. Does not go out of his way to make simple concepts difficult like some other people. Instead elucidates on all complex one's with simple epiphanies of understanding. Go to his classes. Not only would you learn but you would obtain clear knowledge about the field. Always helps his students. Class extremely well structured.
Best professor I had in RPI. He knows how to teach! Super friendly as well!

Amazing professor. One of the best I've at RPI simply for his dedication to the students, material, and field. He creates his own homework problems with fun premises and he is always available to help online through Piazza. Quality professor and quality man. Also: he has great shirts.
Excellent professor.  Explains material thoroughly and answers questions well.  Very available for out of class help and responsive to e-mail and WebCT.  Some of the homeworks were tricky.
Great professor - knows his stuff and is able to teach it well.  Uses as many illustrative examples and demos as possible.  Always takes time to clarify or explain if you are lost.

I took three COMM courses with Professor Tack and she is the reason I pursued COMD as a dual major after taking Intro to Graphic Design. She gives excellent feedback and will make sure you leave her classes with extensive design knowledge. I highly encourage anyone who is interested in a future design career to take at least one course with her!

After taking all her classes, I finally feel comfortable writing a review. She is an incredible professor and I now feel confident in my skills as a designer (after coming into RPI with no experience). Amazing feedback both in and outside of class. With that said, Graphic Design is not an easy field. Do not take her courses if you want an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She cares about your participation and effort so if you give both, you will get a good grade in her class.

This class was the reason I decided to declare my Graphic Design minor. It is mainly used to provide feedback on the students' work to be worked on for the next class. The professor is very approachable and accessible after class, although I always found it easy to discuss anything in class. I highly suggest taking any class with Sara Tack!

If you enjoy expressing yourself, this class is great.The professor's grading is highly subjective. Even if you follow the project outline, they may grade based on unstated personal criteria, leading to negative feedback and unfair treatment. The outline encourages creativity, but grading doesn't reflect that.

Took Intro to Graphic Design with her. I absolutely loved her. Very knowledgeable and gives excellent feedback. Projects have clear guidelines for grading but not for specific content so requires some creativity. She's very willing to help you with projects and with other non-course stuff too. Definitely recommend.
An excellent professor!! She always provides me with excellent advice and ways to improve my pieces in critique. Best teacher for the start of the graphic design
not recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Amazing professor!! She places a high value on the creative progress of every student, regardless of their major. She motivates me to strive for improvement as an artist and venture beyond my comfort zone. She is also incredibly skilled at providing constructive feedback that helps her students grow and improve.

Prof. Tack has a wealth of knowledge to offer and a consistent dedication to making sure we get the most out of our courses - like organizing field trips to local design studios, and bringing in guest lecturers. By offering diligent and individualized attention to every student's work, I felt that she was fully committed to helping us succeed.
Extremely hard as an intro level design course. Reviews and feedback are always are mostly negative.

The hardest part was that class was at 8:00. I woke up at 6:00 for class once. You must have work printed out and posted on the board before class starts. The large-scale printing assignment was the most frustrating because of this, esp. dealing with the VCC plotter. Listen to feedback and integrate it for a good final grade. Adobe is fun to use
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Probably one of the best design professors at RPI, though she is extremely tough. She makes you work for your grade, though you come out of every class with a vast amount of design knowledge.

She's an excellent teacher,the best design teacher in RPI. BUT she is tough. Classes are usually at 8am and if you get there more than 5 min late you get points off. You have to work hard in this class but you learn a lot and it pays off in the end. At first she seems like she's super anal but she means well.
Very friendly and easy to talk to. Good designer and teacher.
I took her color theory class and I felt I learned a lot about color.  She has a very casual way of teaching.  Also she has constant he responsive feedback that is very useful.

I had the privilege of being a TA for him. He's perhaps the most caring professor at RPI. He takes the time to learn his students' names, their interests, and what they may need help with in the course. He's incredibly friendly and accessible. I WISH I had Professor Uchida when I took the equivalent course back in undergrad.

Professor Uchida has a knack for IEA, and it shows in his lectures. He is easygoing most of the times and is pretty funny. However, he does have a temper at times, and will let you know when you asked something silly. You will need to attend all lectures since there's ICPs, and tests are weighed heavily (75%)
He's professor I've ever had
IEA is a tough course, but he made this class very enjoyable and understandable. He is one of the most caring professors I've had at RPI.

If you ever take IEA and have to take it in the spring, please take it with him. He is absolutely amazing and will help you with anything you are struggling with. IEA is a difficult course but he really shows that he wants his students to succeed. His office hours are super useful too.

Amazing IEA professor and one of the best professors I have had at RPI. He gives you extensions on homework assignments and opens his office hours to schedule them whenever you need them. Go to his office hours early in the semester even if you don't need too much help because he likes to see people who are putting effort into his class.

I received a hard earned A- after a very challenging final but this class is absolutely worth taking. Uchida replies emails in a very timely manner and also sets his office hour 24/7. This class could be challenging, need TA's help during class, but all these could be overcame with office hours. 10/10 would take again.

Professor Uchida is what made me stay at RPI. IEA is so unbearably hard, but this man made it go by not as bad as it could have. The most caring professor I've ever had. He cares, 95% of professors don't. Will go out of his way to help is students get the best grade as possible and helps the students (me) struggling get through the semester. 10/10
Dude is very nice and actually cares about his students. He is sometimes difficult to understand because he has every accent under the sun. Best teacher I've had here so far.
Very good professor, cares a lot. If he sees you working hard in class and sees you show your work as he walks around, it won't go unnoticed. He is a very good professor and IEA is easier with him
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --So many papers--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: One of *the* best professors at RPI by a long shot. He's very nice and actually cares about his students. He's approachable and tries to make sure that everyone understands the material. The class material can be difficult but the way he taught made things a lot easier. I 100% would recommend taking his section if you can.
Do not take this professor for IEA. Other professors will let you use crib sheets, he will not, and you will only find this out after the add deadline.

He is such a great professor. Unlike the administration here, he actually cares and wants to see you succeed. Just ask for help if you are struggling and he will help you out. Best professor I have had so far.

Easily the best professor I've had during my time at RPI. Incredibly engaging during lectures, doesn't waste time, and is so helpful with learning the material. He is very accessible outside of class, responds to emails quickly, and clearly cares that students learn the material. I looked forward to every class.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He is really good at teaching. If you pay attention to his class, the course will be really easy for you. He will reply the email as soon as possible , especially before big test. You will love IEA, if you take his class.

The homework is a lot harder than the lectures and the tests. As long as you do a couple back exams before the tests and do the example problems during lecture, you will do fine. Shun is a good teacher who cares about his students and will give you points back on practically anything on the tests if you explain yourself. He is cheerful and lectures
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Good at teaching in general Wants you to do well and gives multiple opportunities to do so Understanding Interesting accent, easy to understand, but interesting Funny guy
Best lectures I've had at RPI

Liked his lectures and lowkey sense of humor. Exams were fair. Between the homework and recitations it was a decent amount of work (6 hours of lecture & recitation + ~5 hours of HW a week + exam studying). Watch out at the end because it ramps up in difficulty suddenly cause they tacked on 2 weeks of stress (literally).
No BS, cares for student success, very open. Communicate with him and he'll do his best to accommodate for you. Don't be scared to ask questions in his class.

This guy is only capable of teaching IEA level class. He would demean student's academic knowledge and report writing by reiterating his background in Physics. The grading is very random, it's totally up to his personal taste. The fact that people getting a good grade DOES NOT mean he is a good lecturer.

Prof. Taylor cares very much, and is one of the best lecturers I have ever had. IEA is a very tough class for most people and he understands that and WILL help you and encourage you and offer aid constantly, but you have to put in the work. 
He had frequent in-class assignments for attendance, but those could be made up. Homework was important!

This man single handedly ruined my aerospace journey. From his inconsistency in the amount of detail that he uses for his slides to the severe LACK of communication for his project details. Lectures are so confusing as he likes to go on so many rants about meaningless topics which have no connection. On top of that having terrible grading skills.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Professor Taylor is an extremely passionate and engaging lecturer. He has a strict no-phone policy during his lectures but it's to help his students in the long run. Amazing office hours and although the tests and homework may be difficult, it is clear he will support students as much as he can if they put in the effort.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Incredibly precise when solving questions in class, and makes sure to show all work necessary. Hands down one of the most knowledgeable and caring professors I have had here at RPI.

Very tough class, but Taylor is absolutely your best choice for IEA, his lectures are clear and he's very enthusiastic, he really wants his students to do well. The class is hard (and the homework is harder!) but if you pay attention, do the back exams, and get help when you need it, you should do well
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Very good lectures, very clear, very passionate. Great professor!
Great teacher, great office hours

Aerodynamics with Professor Taylor was easily the best class I have taken at RPI. Lectures are more of a discussion rather than a lecture, making it easy to get in depth in to complex topics. He does a great job of making sure you understand the most important concepts that you will need in the industry. He's also hilarious.

Absolutely love Keith Taylor. Probably my fav lecturer I've had at RPI so far. He really cares and you can tell. His lectures are incredibly engaging and thorough and you actually feel like you've learned something important by the end of his class. Show up to lecture, do all the homework and study for the tests and you'll pass, not an easy class.
Taylor is fantastic for IEA and is so understanding and intelligent! He calls things as they are and is one of the few professors who actually remembers what it was like to be a college freshman.
I loved this class, he presented the material in a way that just made sense to me. He genuinely cared and made sure everyone passed, AS LONG AS YOU GO TO HIM IF YOU'RE STRUGGLING.

He truly cares about his students and wants everyone who deserves it to succeed. The course content is was pretty challenging for me as I felt like it was all mostly theoretical. I went to his office hours and he took the time to explain each and every step in a way I understood. Very accommodating, patient, and one of the best professors at RPI.

He definitely cares about his students and is very helpful at office hours. However it is hard to get help at office hours with how many people go. I do not like his lecture slides and find his process of solving questions overcomplicated. However he emphasizes on using his method which is why I did so poorly.

Professor Taylor is genuinely one of the best professors I have ever had. He went out of his way to help me in IEA and took the time to work with me when I was struggling. His lectures explained the content well. He will go out of his way to make sure his students pass.

Professor Taylor is legitimately one of the best teachers I've ever had. He is very accommodating for all students, and his office hours are incredibly useful. If you can handle some corny jokes, some mild sarcasm, and some VERY emphatic repetition of important concepts, his class is the place to be in for IEA.

He is extremely clear with what he needs student to learn, as well as very attentive to students when doing in class assignments. He repeats the important stuff over and over until it gets in your head.

While prof Taylor was one of the hardest profs I have had, he is also the best teacher of any course he is a part of. He grades hard but it is clear that he just wants you to succeed. If you do the work, ask questions, and show up to office hours with problems he will ensure that you pass.

Professor Taylor often uses his paranoia to award students points, and he will deduct points from students for adding attachments to their emails. His ppt was very chaotic, and his teaching method was too. I could hardly learn anything in the two-hour class. He even needs chegg to explain some topics, but he does not allow students to use chegg.

Professor Taylor's Engineering Dynamics is - in all honesty - much more difficult than other professors' classes you could take, but it was definitely worth it. He teaches you notation strategies and methods of problem solving that make classes requiring 3D problem solving and multiple reference frames way easier. 100% recommend prof. Taylor.
JUST AVOID. Can't say too much details.

Do not take this class with him. He is a fine professor for other classes but in this one he is incredibly confusing and insists on using this terrible notation that is unlike anything in the textbook so you're solely dependent on his notes which are rarely helpful. He makes the class much more difficult than it needs to be. Take a different prof.

I would not take the course again, and he needlessly punishes honest students for what cheaters do. He spends way too much time caught up on chegg use instead of teaching. Graded by few tests and grading criteria is never clear.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: At first, he seems really funny and nice, and he is, he answers questions in lecture just fine. However, the number of mistakes in lecture notes is really problematic. His tests are either NOTHING like the back exams or have errors in them. And don't expect him to be helpful in an exam either if you ask for help. He is nice and approachable in gen

Professor Taylor is a great professor. He is funny, intelligent. He often makes jokes during class. He constantly improve the way he teach the concept. His pacing of the lecture is good. He would often stay a little late to help the student with in-class activities.
He makes everything very easy to understand, often tells jokes during class and is very understanding.
Really great professor who cares about his students and knows a lot about the subject. Very fair grader and reasonable with excuses/absences.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Very helpful. Loved his class. Always seems to care about the students and the materials; very helpful when asking questions. Good, well-paced lectures and easy-to-follow in-class assignments. Definitely come to class or you will quickly get behind.
Talking to my friends that were taking IEA with other professors made me feel lucky to have Taylor. He is very nice and helpful during office hours and his lectures were great.

Don't get me wrong, he's a very clear lecturer in terms of concepts- it's just his exam/class answer keys are constantly riddled with mistakes, and it's hard to keep up with his numerical errors. His exam q's are HARD and points get taken off easily with significant figures, ect. but he's caring and knows his physics stuff. NOT an easy A, but hey.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Taylor is a very good lecturer and his office hours are very helpful.

reviews.comment: Prof. Taylor is definitely the best lecturer for IEA. He is clear and concise, and is able to ask any question asked of him. He is also very accessible in office hours, or if you want to make an appointment with him.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: Prof. Taylor was excellent as an IEA lecturer. He structured the class so in-class assignments were integral; he didn't just turn his back on us when we did them either- he would work through any issue we had and would lift us up when we got down on ourselves. The man is definitely your best bet for IEA in my view.
Had Keith for IEA and Dynamics. Guy looks like a goon but hes a good professor. Study his back exams and in class example problems and the exams arent too bad.
Keith Taylor is the man. IEA was a tough class but he was as clear and understandable as possible. He is also very helpful during office hours and he's so funny. You won't use your book much.

I had professor Taylor for IEA. This class is my favorite class so far because of him. His lecture is clear and easy to understand. He is also a pretty funny lecturer to keep you awake. You pretty much get full credit for the in-class-assignment grade as long as you attend ever lecture. He is super caring and his office hour is supper helpful

I had professor Taylor for thermals and fluids. he is a good teacher. his tests are kind of difficult because he doesnt let you use crib sheets but he makes them pretty straightforward. As long as you study the lectures you should be ok.  He seems to care about the students and is a nice person.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: Overall great professor. He goes through every topic at a good pace and explains things very well. As long as you attend lectures you'll do fine.

Yes, I failed the class. But I recognize that it is only the fault of my own. He's the best you can get for IEA, and he has office hours for a very long time. MAKE USE OF THAT! It will be easy to fall behind in this class because of its very fast pace, but if you work hard, you'll do well. His lectures are clear and thorough.
Helpful teacher. Taught effectively. Nice guy. No complaints.

Could not ask for a better professor. As long as you put in some effort into this class, you'll do fine. He is insanely good at explaining material so MAKE SURE TO GO TO LECTURES, especially since there are in-class assignments. Professor Tathagata makes difficult concepts easy to grasp. An amazing professor who genuinely cares for his students.

Prof. Bhaduri is a great professor, who gave interesting lectures. Strength of Materials was very, very, hard, but he did try his best to help, and the materials posted on LMS were invaluable for my final.
Also, was very understanding when I had to miss a test, which was very nice as things were very awful that week for me.

He is understandable and draws excellent diagrams during lectures which really help visualize the concepts and problems covered. The class and exam structure makes it difficult to do well, and although he is not very entertaining or engaging during his lectures, he is a solid professor and will teach you the material if you don't fall asleep.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Bhaduri is a good Strengths professor, especially considering the difficulty of the class. The tests and homework are rigorous but fair, and the lectures are helpful. Sometimes Bhaduri forgets the difficulty of the class and can also be quite monotone. El-Shafee would be a better pick but both professors teach the class well.

Dude has lot's of office hours available and really takes his time to help students outside of class. Not much to say other than he's a great guy and you'll definitely laugh at least once in his class.

He is really great at making a difficult course easy. This is one of the first courses engineers take at RPI, and a lot have trouble with it, but Bhaduri goes out of his way to make sure we were prepared for exams and keeping us interested in the subject. I would definitely take his classes again.

The lectures count for 5% of the grade. New materials are introduced in each lecture, and it's a very fast-paced class. Four tests count for 80%. It's very hard to understand prof Bhaduri sometimes, but if you go to his office during office hours, he will help you a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Overall, I thought that he knew a lot about the subject he was teaching. It is a hard class and going to lecture made the difference. The test's are difficult, just study back exams. No extra credit

Overall a great lecturer and very knowledgeable in the subject area. Sometimes can move slightly too fast or skip steps when explaining, but is good with answering questions (if he sees your hand). Provides tips for how to study for exams, and I found his office hours very helpful, which I would recommend if you are struggling with the homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Bhaduri is a great lecturer and clearly understands the course material. He's compassionate and understands students' usual challenges/wrongdoings, occasionally giving hints to ICAs. He provides interesting real-life-application scenarios and wants everyone to succeed.

I had a very positive experience with Prof. Bhaduri in his Intro to Engineering Analysis class in the Fall 2024 Semester. He is very knowledgeable in his field and provided students with clear, well-structured lectures that provided us all of the content needed for our exams. Be sure to attend his lectures to complete the In-Class Assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He is a very smart professor and understands the material very well, almost to well to leave behind some steps he thinks are common sense. The test's are quite difficult and go to every single lecture. It counts towards your grade and will help you so much

He's a great lecturer for a notoriously difficult class, and I highly recommend him if you're a visual learner. It's worth noting that he doesn't write the tests or the grading rubrics - those are done by the course coordinator who oversees iea.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I found it very hard to stay focused during Prof. Bhaduri's lectures, even if you could tell he was knowledgeable on the course material. Small mistakes on exams and written homework assignments would be punished more than in other classes.
Bhaduri is very knowledgeable about the course material and lectures in an accessible manner. He's very good at answering questions and provides helpful tips for solving the in-class assignments.

He's a real nice prof - lectures are well-structured, and his explanations are in-depth. Despite the difficulty of the class, he is very encouraging and helpful; he seems to genuinely want his students to succeed.
Professor Bhaduri is a welcoming professor and is very nice, he cares about his student and has good office hours, he usually responds quickly on Webex too. We love him
We love Professor bhaduri

Professor is Very knowledgeable on Course content and subject matter concepts, But forgets his class is very difficult for a lot of people. Overall a good lecturer but sometimes there is confusions in his explanations due to many circumstances.

He's clearly very knowledgeable on the subject, his lectures are necessary for passing the class however he goes on tangents of higher-level concepts often and he covers things so quickly that it's hard to keep up with him. If you can keep up, he's a great professor!
Also, he welcomes questions but will make you feel like an idiot if you ask any.

Dr. Kruger has excellent lectures in which he clearly explains concepts and does many practice problems with us, he's a funny guy and has a great attitude. The class itself is hard, but he makes it manageable and gives very fair questions on assessments. Anybody who rated him low for this class likely skipped lecture, which is crucial to succeed.

If you're going to take this class, you MUST attend lecture. Good luck trying to get resources outside of class. All the handouts he gives you must go to class to get them because he doesn't post them anywhere. He uses WebEx to communicate to his class lol. There's no homework and your only grades are online quizzes and exams.

reviews.comment: Terrible, 'know-it-all' attitude, not easy to approach

Extremely frustrating to try and get an A in this class. In my opinion if you get A's on tests, quizzes, and HWs and you study for the final and don't get lobotomized before taking it you shouldn't fail the final but idk. That being said I enjoyed the class a lot, I signed up for another class of his and I'm excited to take it.

Do not take programming with Kruger. Take it with Lee in the spring. The exam content is way more difficult than what's covered in class. Kruger is hard to understand, mumbling and rambling, making this class 10x harder. The homework is confusing, requiring hours of work. Office hours with the TA was the only thing that helped.

Tbh the worst class with the worst professors you could take. Before the final I was doing fine and had a good B. The final had material that he said would not be on it, and created difficult problems way out of our scope. Dropped my grade to a D+.
Professor showed an astounding lack of understanding, both empathetic and academic. If you have the misfortune of registering for this course with this professor: reconsider.

MAU is tough to begin with and Prof Kruger's lectures are kinda confusing. Homework is optional but I recommend doing it if you want to do well. He's always making jokes though and they make going through the content a little easier.

Programming for BME with Kruger wasn't so good. Exams were fair enough, but the grading was quite harsh. Homeworks took minimum 4.5 hours and were composed of coding various matrix operations (pretty boring).

1: unilaterally lengthened class by 30 minutes (8:00-10:05 instead of 8:30-10:05)

reviews.comment: He doesn't want students to know the average score because it is too low!

reviews.comment: Generally strick with students' manners( sometimes not very responsive to me due to my questions...) and not very accessible. inaccessible, very irresponsible in homework and exam grading, some times unreasonablely getting angry with students' posts on piazza. Only one good thing his teaching pace is not very fast to keep up with and homework is more concentrated on problem solving rather than conducting many reports ,which is more accepatable and productive for sophomor
Don't do it. He is one of the worst professors I've had at this college. Extremely tough grader later on. Does not care about students. Avoid this professor if you care for your GPA.

This professor for this class refused to post notes, would ofyen not answer questions, and did not adjust the grading for the class nearly enough to make up for the amount of Fs in the class. reviews.comment: Type of professor who thinks his class is the only class. Test one is very easy whereas later tests become much more difficult. He doesn't offer many resources to help study the material, students often have to just redo homework problems to prepare for exams.
IEA wasnt that hard of a class, but Kruger is an extremely dry lecturer. Basically reads the powerpoint word for word. Also MasteringEngineering homework sucks

Good professor for IEA. Our section was the highest scoring in each exam (F'17). All IEA exams, grading criteria, and lecture material is the same for all sections. Is very clear and takes his time when going through example problems in class. He is also helpful during the in-class assignments.

He isn't the worst professor in the world: he explains concepts quite well and paces the class appropriately. I just personally find some of his comments and mannerisms rude. He constantly puts down dual majors, pre-med BME students, Biomaterials and Biomechanics students for not choosing Imaging/Instrumentation, and students with a low GPA.
