reviews.comment: weird grading rules, hard to understand

Don't want to say too much about this professor. It's the first time for him to teach this course this semester, so I'm not sure about what does it feels like in the past. The knowledge in the class is not too difficult but this professor makes you feel worse than it should be. Also with horrible handwriting, which is beautiful but hard for reading

He is very strict in class - no cell phones, no talking, etc (we are going back to middle school). Additionally, he constantly deletes student input regarding the exams from Piazza. Gives us a one-week notice before exams and is unwilling to tell us what will be on them. No back-work. No reviews. By the way, tests are 40% each. Lowest is dropped.

Grade distribution (Fall 2017): - 80% is your 2 best out of 3 exams. He does not answer questions during exams. He does not tell you exam averages - 10% is Piazza Participation - 10% is from 10 HW assignments. 5 are incredibly easy, 5 are difficult without a TA or backwork No crib sheets on exams even though the other section get one.
He has no idea about what is gonna have in test. Also mean. Class is extremely boring.
Very neat hand writing. nic man

This was his first time teaching the course and he seemed out of touch with the class. He used another teacher's powerpoints and tended to simply click through them during lecture rather than explain and do problems out himself. Much better if you ask him questions directly.

Unlike other profs at RPI I've had thus far, Kruger actually cares about whether you understand the material and gives time to students who need it despite  having hundreds of students. Taking his IEA class, which is a tough course, but it's totally manageable if you get this professor. He's a great guy.

Some reviews make this class sound awful, but it's really not that bad. The setup was a bit disorganized and sometimes unclear, but you'll still come out of the class knowing the material well. Labs were fun, the reports fair, and group projects tough but manageable. The professor was kind and often gave extra time for assignments.

Proceed with caution. Her disorganization permeates every aspect of the course; don't expect consistent expectations. Her office is in complete disarray and the condescending tone when asking for help is just wonderful. Grading is harsh, but not in a way that pushes you to grow;  almost like you're being penalized for not reading her mind.

She'll treat you like a child but grades on a warpath to prove getting an A is impossible. Her group assignments are the worst thing, more-so because she cares more about ABET than content. Her exams feature abstract questions that are hard to grasp what she's actually looking for, while seeming suspiciously easy. Boring lectures that are scattered

Dr. Bennett is unorganized and can be condescending. Took forever to grade anything, and was harsh with grades. Lectures were always disorganized. Lab content was interesting, but not utilized well. Would constantly change assignment deliverables during the semester. Never thought I'd have a professor who spoke to me like I was a kindergartener.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: A very tough grader, takes off points for reasons you will never know why. Completely unorganized, assignments thrown wherever; syllabus is a mess. Teaches the class as if you are children. Exams are open-note but that does not mean they are easy.

This class isn't overly difficult but can seem so with little experience. Do the homework and labs to improve problem-solving, as they'll help on exams. The course mainly covers Python, with real algorithms introduced in the last few weeks. The teacher is knowledgeable and overall good.

She's willing to help and answer questions. HWs can be long, me and students I know agree that it's easy to run out of time on tests. To do well on tests, you NEED to know what is happening within your code. Exams are on paper. Lectures notes imo are helpful. Textbook available but definitely not needed to do well. Think of CS as puzzles/riddles.

Really good at explaining stuff. Tool topics I already knew and phrased them in ways that I hadn't thought of before (ways that were better and more efficient than my original understanding) and put in lots of time into answering class questions. I also liked how for every test, she went over a back exam as a final preparation on the day of.
i am a comp sci major and i thought i was good at coding until i took this class. i had 100s in all my coding classes in high school. this class makes me want to change my major.

I disliked that Comp Sci 1 tests were on paper. I also disliked that course materials were on Submitty instead of Blackboard. She is very slow to grade and even slower to update overall grades. It's also hard to interpret grades because, instead of a simple percentage, you're given a confusing rainbow color-coded chart called rainbow grades.

I came to this class with zero programming experience and learnt so much. Prof. Mushtaque gave good lectures and answered every question. I got a lot of help during her office hours. Tests are the most difficult part of the course.
Amazing Lectures. Explains everything in-depth. Tests are difficult and homeworks take a lot of time.

- I didn't even know her name, that's how engaging she is as a professor.
- She does actually teach the content, just not super well and not in an engaging manor.
- The exams for this course are awful just as a heads up, although I don't think that reflects on her as a professor.

Encourages questions but then is quite snappy when people ask them, giving off the impression you don't want to ask anything. Lectures are just walking through the notes which you can do by yourself. HW assignments aren't hard but take forever because you need to code the output to be exactly what it says which is often ambiguous. Exams are fair.

Professor Mushtaque gave good lectures and explained things well imo, though the difficulty curve in the class was very steep. You can get TAs to help and there are labs where you can ask TAs for plenty of help, but be prepared to spend +10 hours on a single assignment by the end of the semester. 
Tests and other work was fine, though!
She pauses a lot during lecture to see if anyone has any questions and her lectures are pretty understandable.

Explains clearly and takes questions. The lectures are well organized and everything is done fairly on time. There is a lot of time spent on homework and the tests are difficult but that's just how the class is, it will not be better with a different professor.

This will be the best professor for CS1 you'll find there no better, trust me bro. The homeworks are the same regardless of the professor, however her tests are much more similar to what is covered in class. If you check the other CS1 reviews you'll know immediately what I'm talking about.
not the easiest to understand but her lectures make sure you understand the material. The test were pretty difficult logic wise, but the amount of questions was fair to the time given.
uzma pls teach data structures

Uzma teaches clearly and she's willing to repeat concepts. She writes code in class which is better for understanding. Not every HW is complex, but they took 3-15 hours depending on the week. Tests aren't bad if you do the HW yourself. All assignments & tests are same for everyone regardless of the professor, so pick the best lecturer (Uzma).

reviews.comment: She's really great, loved taking her class, everything was explained very clearly, always provided examples.
Very good lecturer who shares her experiences

For an intro computer science class it's too hard for non-cs majors and too easy for people with coding experience. Her lectures are fine, the structure of notes is nice, and the homework is pretty easy if you can manage your time. The hardest part was one-liners on tests. You get out of it what you put in.

Overall, it's just OK and unhelpful. She has a bit of an accent however, when she's teaching the lessons, she moves on too fast without properly or fully in details, explaining what's going on. If you come to this class, be prepared to spend all of your time in doing assignments, labs and homework.
Great lecturer; explains things thoroughly and willing to answer as many questions as you have. As long as you don't underestimate the course you will do just fine.

Class is more about you than the prof. She is a good lecturer and very clear in class but if you already know python you dont need to go to class. I got an A- and never went, the hard parts are the exams which are on paper and Homework 8 which took me like 20 hours.

reviews.comment: It's awful to write python by hand. But that's how the tests are taken. If you can't take lots of extra time in exercise, there's no way to get an A
Exams are the hardest part about this course. Work load is heavy but manageable if you decide to start every assignment early. Use office hours throughout the semester.
Best professor I have ever had. Excellent lectures, extremely clear and very helpful outside and inside the class.

Professor Mushtaque is a friendly and knowledgeable CS1 instructor. Her lectures are clear and the tests are challenging but fair. Most of the labs and lecture exercises are straightforward and quick, however, some of the homework can be time-consuming and challenging. CS1 is a great course and as long as you don't procrastinate, it's not too hard.

The class can be difficult for those coding for the first time. Labs are standard, tests are a bit hard, and homework can get very difficult, especially toward the end. The best way to get by this class is through Uzma's office hours, she helped me a bit with the last homework. She tries her best to answer questions too. Overall, she's just okay.

Extremely clear and well-prepared lectures. For first-time programmers, this is a very hard introductory course, with difficult, sometimes nitpicky tests, a pretty fast pace, and weekly homework and labs. (No HWs if there's a test). If it's not difficult, it's a time-consuming course, with HWs nearing ~10 hrs by the end. Time management is key.
I learnt a lot in this course. Best Python programming class. Professor is very helpful and the lectures are fun.

reviews.comment: I loved her teaching style. Was helpful in office hours.
Well-paced for a introductory-level course

reviews.comment: I suck at Computer Science and this professor didn't help by giving advanced material.
Absolutely terrible. Hated every second of this class.

Professor Mushtaque is really clear in her lectures. The homeworks and labs are difficult, but doable with some grit and perseverance. Overall, great course, just requires you to step outside of your comfort zone and actually think hard.

horrible. supposed to be an intro class, and it is definitely not taught that way. this was my first time coding, and let's just say it was a disaster! my TA was amazing, and is the only reason i passed this class or learned anything at all. he deserves double whatever he's being paid. avoid this class if you can.

I thought her lectures were okay and an average prof. No matter who you choose, you'll need to self-teach and practice a lot. reviews.comment: Worst class ever taken. His lectures are not helpful. Exam and homework are difficult. Yes, you might be able to get an A if you completely know the stuff. However, if you are an average student, be prepared to get a C. And you can easily fail the class :).

Prof. Xu definitely knows his stuff, but his english is sometimes difficult to understand. Surprisingly you can still learn if you pay attention, as he tries his best explain all his calculations and the intuition behind the subject matter. Homework is sporadically given, exams seem to be clear cut. No official t-book, so you better come to class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment:
Small class. Starts with just lectures and pivots to being a project based class with presentations and a final paper.
He is direct with his feedback but wants to see students succeed.
Computational social choice is Lirong's home field. He is clearly passionate about the course.
It is unique course offering with a lot of interesting applications.

Possibly my favorite course at RPI and possibly my favorite professor.
I think the curriculum & homework is based on UC Berkeley's version of the course.
Homeworks are mainly based on writing functions to control a Pacman agent. Very engaging. Topics are useful for anyone hoping to build a background in reinforcement learning and AI generally.

The professor is nice, but his handwriting is terrible. His exams are littered with mistakes that they are forced to regrade. His teaching methods are poor, as many students need to consult outside lectures to properly learn. He is aware of this and has made it clear he will give 0's to anyone that uses methods taught outside the class.
Beware of the average exam score element to the course. Overall the professor is a very strong lecturer and the assignments in the class do a really good job of reinforcing the material covered.
Coding assignments are given every 2 weeks and there is no final. Go to classes, figure out the material and the test will be a breeze.
Great professor with a very thorough understanding of the material. Could stand to work on the organization of his lectures, but this was the first time he offered the class.
Just started taking his class. He seems fairly engaging.
She is a super great teacher and while the content can be difficult, it all clicks if you just practice a lot!! Make sure to do the homework and re-do in class questions and you'll succeed.

This class is lowkey insanely difficult, but a lot more manageable if you go to Dr. Wang's lectures and actually pay attention. She's really funny and wants you to do well, and she's consistently the best professor for MAU. After failing the first exam, I locked in with her lectures and ended up doing really well. That can be you too!!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She's probably the best for MAU and explains the content in a way that's easy to understand. She is pretty mom-like and wants the best for her students. Super understanding.

Wang's lectures are excellent and she understands the material and communicates it clearly. Attendance isn't mandatory, but it's probably the most helpful preparing for tests compared to the textbook. She is strict in lectures, she would walk around the room seeing if people were doing work or yell at people for having computers out.

If you have to take MAU, let it be with Wang. She knows the material, and will make sure you do too with clear lectures, telling you exactly what will be on exams. She gives off a persona of a really serious mom but when she breaks character it's really entertaining. She is just great and made MAU enjoyable.

Lectures are very clear, in-depth, and well-paced. She seems intimidating, but she's your typical Asian parent who does care about you. She expects you to put in a lot of effort in the work, so her exams can be challenging and require higher level thinking but definitely fair. Her office hours are casual yet productive, and she is really helpful.

The difficulty curve is like a roller coaster, everyone got an A in the first exam and 1/6 got a fail after the final. My grade was around B before the final and I Got a D even though I prepared for the exam. Just avoid her class, not even a single point of curve.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
The Professor knows the course material well and her lectures are easy to understand. 

However, it is almost impossible to receive A in her course. The exams are complicated and the general grades in her course in lower than other professors teaching this course.
Dr. Wang is a very knowledgeable professor. If you attend lecture, you will have a very good understanding of the material and know what to expect on exams.

Grade is 20% quizzes, 10% project, 70% exams with the final worth 35% so make sure you're a good test taker. HW is not graded but important for exam prep. Both midterms had exam averages in the 60s. So, you definitely need to put in the work if you want a good grade. She can come off as rude but probably just trying to commiserate with us.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Probably the best option for professors of this course. Good lecturer with lots of examples to help, and provides back work for exams. Be ready to do the "optional" homework and study frequently. You must attend lecture to receive a copy of the handwritten notes
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr Wang is a good lecturer, with clear notes and plenty of examples to go along with the material. Very frequent quizzes in class with less than a week's notice (usually around 3-4 days). Tests and exams seemed much harder than lecture material, and make up almost your entire grade. If you do bad on the exams, you do bad in the course.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great professor! She cares a lot about her students and if you reach out she is extremely willing to help. The material is very new for some which is why so many students struggle with the class. She is also a fair grader and will curve the class if everyone is doing really poorly.

Dr. Wang is an excellent professor who cares deeply about her students. She will make an extra effort to help you if you ask. There is a lot of material, just how MAU is and she goes over each kind of problem you may seem in extreme detail. The lectures can be difficult to follow but, the notes are essential.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Caring

reviews.comment: Definitely has a strong grudge against phone usage in class and will call you out, but incredibly helpful during office hours. You get a strong foundation in application statistics with her.
Professor Wang delivers great lectures and explanations but her course entails a lot of work.

Definitely the worst transition to online learning of any Professor Ive had. In a 4 credit hour class she managed to pack 5-9 hours of lecture material into a week depending on the content for said week. Sometimes less is more, and in this case it definitely wouldve been. The book is the way to go for online learning - lectures are horrible.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: DR. Wang has taught me all of the fundamentals of statistics, I appreciate her as a professor. Although she is not an easy A, there are no textbooks or required homework, just weekly quizzes, a project, and exams. She goes over examples in class so as long as you put in the work to understand those concepts, you will do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: She is very nice and really cares for each of her students. However, she really makes you put in the work for MAU. If you actually try and put in the effort, you can manage to get an A. I don't recommend her if you're looking for an easy A. That being said, you'll know the material inside and out by the end.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Wang was the best professor that I've had at RPI. She cares for he students (in both MAU and Biomechanics) and her lectures are easy to follow. She makes sure to prepare you for exams through numerous in class examples and optional homeworks. Her classes are not an easy A however, but if you do your work and pay attention you will succeed

Taking MAU with Wang is a great choice. No surprises on tests or quizzes, so if you do the homework and look over your notes, you'll be fine. She does lots of examples in class and understands when material is confusing to many students.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This is the worst teacher Ive taken for MAU. She is the rudest professor Ive seen! Does not offer help to students.

They g0t n0 chin and n0 chill. They post class notes that are more understandable than the lectures. They expect you to answer exam questions that take too much time in only 80 minutes. They grade on a curve and have 5% extra credit quizzes, but don't rely on it. The TA gives no feedback on graded work. Overall, don't take this class.

She's very knowledgeable of the course domain and is a nice person. However, her lectures were very monotone and consisted of a PowerPoint, example problems that looked like she prepared in about 30 minutes before class, despite teaching this course many times. She would simply recite material incohesively as it came to her reading off the slides.

Professor Yazici starts from the fundamentals of set theory, which is an unintuitive way to learn probability. Her lectures can also be monotonous, as probability math isn't inherently an interesting topic.  She does practice problems in class and posts lots of supplemental materials. It gets a lot better once you understand whats happening.

She requires attendance in this class but gives the most boring and useless lectures. She will also make comments if you aren't paying attention and is very passive aggressive to anyone who asks a question in class. She decided we did too well on our first exam so she made the second one almost impossible to drop the average. Do not take with her.
Please do not take any course with her unless you have to

Please attempt to avoid this prof if you can. Does not lecture well and is hard to keep up as she will NOT wait when done writing on a slide. Exam 1 followed the content very well; however, the following exam was a bunch of random questions stuffed into a 15 page packet that was expected to be done in 80 minutes? The RMP rating says all.

Engineering Probability (ECSE 2500)

Lecture, HW, and Exams lined up until the drop deadline passed, at which point only the exams became much more difficult. She asked the class "how exam 2 went" and the class spontaneously laughed instead of anyone answering the question. It was a 15 page exam over 80 minutes. 40% of our grade is to be the final.

Bad attitude, boring unengaging lectures yet requires attendance (wastes 1.5 hours of your day), inaccurate review sessions to what's on the test, singles people out and embarrasses them in front of class. Why is she still teaching?

The lectures for this class were insufficient and did not cover the material asked on the homework, quizzes, and exams. Attendance is counted, despite the time being better spent self-studying. This professor will not hesitate to delay the class and interrupt lectures for multiple minutes in order to scold individual students.
Avoid this professor for ECSE 2410, Kimberly is much better. Lectures doesn't cover the homework and quiz. Mandatory quiz on each week.
Be self-sufficient if you want to take the course. Otherwise you are doomed.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Assigns homework without covering the material first, useless lecture notes. Would avoid taking her class if possible (for me it wasn't).
Just don't take her courses. Her course is not worth to attend at all. Take about nothing you needed for homework. By taking her course, all you need to do is self-taught and it's hard.
Bad performance, don't take her course!!
This professor knows nothing, and can't make anything clear.
Generally incompetent.  She's unable to understand and/or listen to students' problems and does not exhibit interest in helping them.

She covered all the material, but did not really go into depth on any of the subjects.  I learned most of the material from the labs and homeworks (and  from image processing, which I'm also taking).  No exams, other than one take home.  I had her for PEA as well, and I really didn't have  a problem (it's not as hard as people make it out to be).

Let's get one thing straight...she is NOT a good professor.  Her lectures move way to fast to keep notes on, which would be more of a problem if her lectures contained any worthwhile content whatsoever.  I don't doubt she knows the material, she just cannot teach it for the life of her.  She just lacks clarity and is just way too disorganized.
No Comments

Horible teacher, she is completely worthless for learning and very unhelpful in office hours.  Her exams are imposible, in fact she told us not to study material that she decided to include for 25% of the final. Another 25% of the final, which was open book, according to the book "the difficultly of this material is out of the scope of this course"

If you want a free A, I suggest you take his courses. There are no exams, HW, quizzes, or any type of assessment. Just go to class, take notes, and hand them in and you'll get an A. I literally used his class as a study hall.

Honestly by far one of my favorite professors at RPI, he is someone who truly loves both teachings, as well as the content that he teaches, and that shines through in all of his classes, making it a much more enjoyable learning experience

"I will give you guys the best lecture you've ever had!" No textbooks, no quizzes, just notes and a course paper at the end. Yingrui does have a nice insight into so-called empirical science, but it could be hard to understand his idea considering his disorganized lecture, contagious laughter, and tendency to value his own work above yours.

I am in Gauge Theory of Higher Cognition and he started off by saying what we are graded on: Notes. Just notes. Nothing else. He does not teach from a textbook, everything is his own research or work and some stuff that came from others in the field. A very very sweet man. Accent can be difficult at times but you get used to it. Would recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Yingrui teaches several nearly identical courses, both in subject matter and student requirements.  The latter are quite breezy: a couple term papers and hardly an exam in sight.  If you don't mind the professor's accent, contagious laughter, or tendency to value his own work above yours, you can still learn a lot.

Professor Yan is a great professor who cares about his student. He may be strict sometimes, but he cares about his students' learning and is understanding. He is very kind and approachable to the class. I had a great time in his class.

Dr. Yan is an excellent professor whose classes are very much what you make of them. If you want to coast and get a B, that's possible — but if you choose to engage, sit up front, ask questions, attend office hours, and even do research with him at DIAL, you'll get so much more out of it. He became my most impactful mentor at RPI.

I've taken two courses with Dr. Yan and enjoyed both. Dr. Yan explains all the course topics well and is very responsive to any questions you may have, either through email or in person.  Most content on exams or HWs was well-discussed via lectures. As long as you pay attention in class, the course materials should be relatively easy to understand.

Lectures do not align well with homework assignments and practice problems. Aware of student struggles but does not provide accessible office hours for students (cancelled office hours several times). Tells students to drop the class because he did not provide the proper teaching of the subject. Inconsiderate to those with limited coding background
Deadlines are very lax, grade basically completely dependent on ability to speak the language. If you are learning what she teaches in class, you're perfect. otherwise you'll struggle. She's good tho

Took the immersive AI class over summer arch. She is a great professor to have; so kind, understanding and lenient. Lectures are immerse and dynamic (quiz games). If you have any issues or questions, talk to her and she'll understand. Assignments are not difficult. Studio 2 lab puts you in scenes and scenarios that you'd encounter in China.

Zhou Laoshi is a great Chinese teacher. She is a native speaker and her teaching is clear. She assigns lots of homework, but can lenient with due dates. She has also been very encouraging to me. One warning: semester-long projects.

He's a good professor but if you don't vibe with him the lectures are hard to bear through. I also don't personally feel like his office hours were super helpful but if you just need to hear the same thing a couple times to understand they're good for that. ( I also might just be bad at math)

I loved the guy. He did his best to be funny and make his lectures interesting, and he would try to get people involved and asking questions cause he wanted the class to do well. Syllabus seems harsh but he gives tons of extra credit, practice problems (which often show up on the test), and homework is really instructive.

Lvov is a funny and interesting guy but his lectures do little to prepare you to solve actual problems. He follows the textbook almost exactly so you end up just reading the entire book to understand what's going on. He does offer a lot of extra credit though, so it's easy to get good grades in his course if you do read the textbook.

Lvov is a nice person and knows the material, but we were months behind other professors. Did not cover laplace transforms, fourier series, or PDEs. His lectures can be confusing, but the tests are extremely easy if you study from the website. Some homeworks are very difficult or were not covered in lecture, saved by the TA, but most are not hard.

Yuri is an interesting professor, he is a very kind man but he also is not a good teacher. His lectures are boring/unhelpful so I never went and still learned all of the course meterial. I was able to do this becasue my TA was great so I learned a lot through the reciataitions and by doing the homeworks. Exams are predictable with lots extra credit

He's a good person and knows the material he's teaching, but unfortunately it's hard to understand because of his russian accent and his handwriting (some letters are written really similarly). He's also pretty helpful if you email him questions about anything (be specific though). Just study for the tests using his website and you'll be fine.

Impressively bad.

Edit: F24's course with Dr. Lvov ended up like an entire month behind *every other professor*. I'm sorry but students deserve at minimum to have access to materials explicitly stated to be taught in the curriculum.

I had this professor for MATH4400 and he was one of the worst professors I have had. His lectures have you confused and he does not explain what he is doing. His note are handwritten and barely legible. He always says to visit his "website" for all information, yet it is poorly made and has nothing he claims. Zero back exams. Horrible experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Worst professor at RPI. Notes are in sharpie and uploaded into a 300+ page pdf with no organization. His handwriting is impossible to read. He grades super hard on exams and refuses to rescore, even if he made a mistake while grading. He's condescending and rude in office hours and never responds to emails. AVOID HIM AT ALL COSTS!

Professor Lvov falls into a specific type: he is clearly brilliant and has a deep understanding of advanced mathematics, but is ineffective at conveying it to non-experts. His lectures often moved quickly through tough material, focusing on derivations over examples. Can be a great resource when supplemented with recitation and textbook reading.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Yuri isn't the worst professor you could have. That being said, he's nowhere close to the best. I learned 90% of the course from my TA and the textbook. During my semester with him, the tests were average but he was SUCH an easy grader. My understanding of the material is probably a C, but I got an A from trying every problem on the test. No HW.

Don't take this professor. If you can take Prof. Kam as a lecturer do so. His lectures are super unprofessional and disorganized... You will mainly have to teach yourself from the textbook. There is no homework, only quizzes, and exams. He messes up multiple times when problem-solving and doesn't explain the process.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: No graded assignments. The grade is an average of exams, cumulative recitation quiz grade, and the final. The lectures, however, are terribly explained, disorganized, and not at all informative. You will end up teaching yourself from the textbook. He is also very unreasonable, and hard to work/communicate with over email.

Hard homeworks/exams but easy grader (does not curve at all so don't try to convince him). Did not like the way he taught the class (curses time to time). About 3/4 of the class dropped about a week in, only stuck through it cause of credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I would not recommend this professor. He does not clearly explain material and goes so slow you are lucky if you make it to the second half of the course. We started the linear algebra half of the class with 2 weeks left in the semester. There is so much material we didn't cover. The tests are either super easy or hard but scaled ridiculously high

Prof. Lvov is a gem - he makes oftentimes difficult material more accessible and easier to understand with his lectures, & the structure of the course/the path followed through the course material made digesting everything straightforward. Of all the math courses I took at RPI, I found his among the easiest to attend, understand, & learn from.

Lvov is not as bad as a lot of people says he is. He does a decent job teaching, and he will answer pretty much any question no matter how dumb it may be. He tells jokes during lectures, some are funny, and some don't make any sense, and most are offensive, but he kept me awake. There's a lot of extra credit available if you're willing to do it.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: If you aim to pass the course and get a not bad grade, he might be the best choice ever in RPI for this course! Because his way of calculation of the final grades are kind to everyone. However, if you are in Math department or you really needs those knowledge, please avoid him. He skips a lot of course material and wastes time during lectures.

Lvov knows the material, but he can't teach it. The only way I learn how to do the homework is by reading the textbook. I study a lot and I still can't understand the type of responses he wants on the exams. Not easy to do well. No matlab experience? goodluck. I DO NOT recommend.

Pretty good. Clear lectures, likes questions, but slow so misses important material (diffeq is EVERYWHERE@rpi). Encourages questions. Homework sets optional and very comprehensive/gr8 review. Tests and quizzes pretty easy, forgiving grading system. Jokes vary wildly in quality. VERY knowledgeable, though. If interested you can get a lot out of him.

Despite being a very nice man, he is not that great when it comes to teaching. Sometimes his writing is hard to understand or he skips some steps... etc I would advice going to his class from time to time but you will be just fine by doing the optional homework problems. It's an easy A if you know how yo use the formulas..

Horrible at giving lectures, he has no organization at all in teaching. Handwriting is hard to tell, and usually, he is not available outside of class. You may want to buy him a microphone because his voice is so low that you often can't hear what he says.

It isn't too hard to get a decent grade in his class, you can do a final project for 10% extra credit. But the professor has a pretty heavy accent and his notes are so hard to understand. Which require you to spend extra time to figure things out yourself. He also provides very few resources for you to study and review.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I took differential equations with Lvov last semester.  As many have said, he's very Russian.  He has a slight accent, but he's easy to understand.  He tells a lot of dumb jokes and gives a lot of extra credit.  I didn't have any mandatory homework in the class I took.  Attendance was mostly optional, but for a few days he tried to take attendance.

Worst c;ass I've taken thus far at RPI. It's hard to do well in a class where the prof. verbally informs me he doesn't enjoy teaching it. As an aeronautical engineer, I got absolutely nothing out of this class except useless math theory which I won't use again. Homework takes forever and he doesn't teach the Matlab portion, the most important part.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: He's actually a really good professor, he answers any questions in class and explains things well. His homework answers online are wrong but other than that I can't complain. He's really funny and very Russian but not hard to understand. If you do the online homework and go to lecture the exams are really easy.

Lectures are confusing, not very helpful, very russian. He has a course website with everything you need for the class. Do the problem on that site and you will get an A. Get the book, do the problems, follow the proofs and put them on your crib sheet.
For spring 2015, gave 26 free points on exams. However, the exams were kind of tough. He is a not a good lecturer, but you can find all the information online and do fine
He's pretty funny, easy tests and quizzes, will do well if you take notes and then supplement with the textbook for exams

Professor Lvov isn't the best instructor for Diff Eq. He tries to be funny and makes jokes very often, but his lectures aren't very clear. He often makes mistakes and is ambiguous as towards what he's trying to show. To his defense, he does encourage students to ask questions and attend his office hours. Exams and quizzes are easy as well.

Don't listen to people who tell you to avoid him. He's a great professor, his accent isn't bad, and he loves jokes.  His exams are four 25 point questions and one 20 point question that is extra credit. He wants you to ask questions, and he wants you to get an A.  And honestly it's worth it just for the jokes. Take him if you can.
the exam is very easy.

Lvov is bad news. Hardly does anything to help his students. (No lecture notes, hw solutions, practice tests, or test solutions posted) Makes mistakes constantly. Horrible at operating Matlab. Loses focus or gets confused and harasses his students to fix the issue for him. Test ?'s are not like the homework ?'s at all. I'd recommend any1 b4 Lvov.

He is terrible during lectures. Spends most lecture talking to the board. Some jokes once in  a while. Constantly makes mistakes when doing examples, which are literally copied from his notes. Learned the class's material from the TA, who also wasn't notified of exam material, some of which were stuff he spoke softly to the board. Self-Study+GoToTA

Lvov knows math, that's for sure, but he has a poor way of communicating the ideas to students.  Diffeq is tough if you don't have a math mind, and although he covers the "what" in lecture, he doesn't even begin to address the "why".  He's also difficult to deal with (told the TA nothing about the final, making it harder to study)

He is funny, knowledgeable and supportive. He's been teaching NC for roughly 10 yrs. His English's surely improved to a good level. It's harsh in the syllabus and the grade of the first homework. But after that he is very generous on grading(2 of 4 questions already told before exam). He likes proofing.  He is the best professors I've ever met.

Don't know what the other raters here are talking about. Just finished his class and I intend to take his other courses too. He gives you several textbooks to read, tells you where to find the current material. Gives great EC. He wants students to ask questions because he wants them to know the material. HW was rough but you learn so much from it.

The only prof worth taking NC from.  He actually cares that you learn the material.  The HW are hard and time consuming, but worthwhile.  Definitely not busy work.  Tests are just right, not easy, not impossible, but require a great deal of though.  There are enough bonus points to keep you afloat though.

This is the absolute worte professor.  He complains if you don't ask enough questions.  His selection in textbooks is terrible as it shows no example that are worthwhile.  He teaches nothing about matlab which every homework is based on, its ridic that if you have no background in matlab you are screwed.

This professor subbed for two days of the Numerical Computing section taught by Kapila. Me and my friend found him very interesting and motivating. He was very interested that people understood everything he went over and strongly encouraged asking questions. Slightly wishing I had been in his section.

Homework amounts to plug'n'chug.  Tests amount to Monte-Carlo regurgitation of notes.   He states he's "too lazy" to put course notes online -- instead you must refer to those from previous years which are in a 200 page, unindexed, PDF of his horrid writing.  The course material itself is interesting to me, but this professor does a half-arsed jo
Terrible teacher...I would rather take it with Giladi in the spring

Tough grader, boring lecturer.  His syllabus states that if you fail any homework, exam or quiz you will fail the course.  This is simply him showing his inability to use the English well.  He's trying to say that if you're consistantly failing your homeworks, you'll probably fail the course.

This professor taught the absolute worst class that I ever took. His policy was simply that if you failed anything, ranging from a homework to an exam, you automatically failed the course. He was harsh in his grading as well.

I was homeless until I took Abrar's class. On the first day of class he told us, "mediocrity is not a virtue", so I decided to simply lock in and buy 13 single-family homes. I keep my old companions (the sewer rats) as my tenants and overcharge them on rent. I continue to take his class and fail it every time, but maybe one year I'll pass.

I was a Bulawayo street urchin, mugging folks with sharpened cheddar. I tried to rob Abrar while he ironed bread. He fixed my stance and whispered, "Mediocrity is no virtue." He gave me a card: *Abrar: I Know Things*. We flew to America in a sock balloon. I've failed every class since, but my cheese-holding posture is now world-class.

My grade was changed from an A- (hard fought) to a D- because I was unfortunately selected in his raffle for “Grade Reduction”. I spoke with the dean but realized that the real lesson came from randomness; life isn't linear, mediocrity is not a virtue. Fortunately Dr. Zaki took pity on me and, instead of failing the class, dropped my GPA to a 1.3.

audited argo 350 cause my hg was taking it and somehow got entered into roulette system. thought nothing of it till i checked lms and found out i somehow had an F for multi. professors notes? you guessed it. arcosanti field trip makes up for it tho

I was born in Zimbabwe. I was poor and delinquent, committing petty crimes and hanging with the wrong crowd. Abrar came across me while traveling across Zimbabwe. I tried to mug him with a knife but he corrected my stance and said "mediocrity is not a virtue." I came with him to America and have taken classes with him ever since. I haven't passed.

In lecture, Professor Zaki with a colleague from the math department shared an intriguing theory from Egyptology. In the Old Kingdom, the Giza pyramid complex was constructed, consisting of the Great Pyramid, Khafre, and Menkaure. Some speculate their layout mirrors Orion's Belt as seen then, by the design of its builders. Truly fascinating stuff!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Wow. This has been..... quite the experience. Lets just say I dropped the class in the last week of classes. Lets just say.... to be concise..... This was the best class I have ever taken. The only reason I dropped the class was because I decided to study underwater basket weaving. Not to say that I did or didnt. Thank you.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: I was very excited to take ARGO 350 with him as an ecology major hoping to learn to about argonauts. Unfortunately I only read the class code and the class was actually on Arcology. Still fascinating, as he is one of the world's premier arcologists.

Prof Zaki saved my life once, drove my friend who is in active labor to the hospital while her deadbeat bf was busy gaming on Discord, and saved 5 disabled children from an orphanage fire. He's involved in cutting-edge research in Texas, where he aims to provide Texans with free, state-wide public transportation fueled by green energy. He's 6'7 btw

Professor Zaki was, without a doubt, the most challenging professor I have ever had. I spent 30 hours a week on his class, attended class and office hours, and even before this have maintained a 4.0 gpa. Alas, I was failed in this class but would do it all over again just to experience the man again. As he often said, "mediocrity is not a virtue".
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: this is the greatest professor of all time

Prof. Zaki (though he likes to go by Abrar) is an amazing lecturer, and he always has great anecdotes. I loved taking Network Science with him, he made a difficult subject clear, and his stories about Zimbabwe were hilarious. He can definitely come off as harsh ("mediocrity is not a virtue") but he really cares about his students.

Every class, he draws a student's name from a cowboy hat for a pop quiz. If you answer incorrectly, he enters you into the roulette system where you could get an F. After each draw, he states, "mediocrity is not a virtue". As you can see, the odds were not in my favor. Some dedicated guy I know got an Incomplete. AVOID roulette system if possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If I had 100 lives, I would take Zaki's class in every single one of them. The course changed who I am as a student, as a friend, as a son, and as a father. Every night I dream about joining his team in Texas and every morning I wake up sad because I don't have Zaki's lecture anymore. This class chewed me up and spit me out a better man. Take it.

brooo this dude was out of his mind “mediocrity is a virtue” like ??? tf does that even mean 💀 and like he'd say it at the beginning of every class too. also like i'm seriously boutta crash out cuz why does every slide need a lobster bro??? 😭 lectures lowk go hard tho

What a brilliant man, and mmmmm ahh oooooo just sublime. What an absolutely splendid class, oooo but over too soon, my days are now sooo lugubrious ohh noooo. But ahh the memories, mmm what a time, the most heavenly class. Undeniably money for old rope, but those recursion slides mmmmm wowwwwweeee.

Professor Zaki is one of the truly most inspirational human beings I have ever met. I got a D- in his class and nearly failed. Despite this, the amount of knowledge that I have received is beyond the caliber of anything else.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Prof Zaki is delightful to have as a professor. He is always clear about his expectations and is so humble for a guy of his caliber. A passionate lecturer who often talks about his time doing research in Texas. So accessible outside of class, but I don't know how I feel about his college in the math department...

Prof. Zaki is one of the best professors I've ever had. Lots of people complain that the class is too difficult but they just won't put in the work. I've never had a professor who clearly puts so much effort into his lectures. As he says “mediocrity is not a virtue” and this is reflected in his course. Take this course if it's the last thing you do

Prof. Zaki is an incredible man. Inspirational. As you can see, I nearly failed his class. But I would do it a thousand times over. The life advice I've gotten from Abrar, as he likes to be called, cannot be measured by a single letter. One time, in the middle of class, Abrar went on a tangent about a life-changing experience in Zimbabwe.
an absolute g
For CAOS. He is a great guy! You can easily reach out to him on discussion forum, and do care about students.

[CSCI 2800] He is difficult. The topics aren't that hard, but the lectures are impossible. Cares, clearly, but honestly maybe shouldn't be a lecturer yet. Most classwork isn't too bad, but in lecture he just reads off the slides. One occasion he read a slide twice because he tabbed out and back, and didn't seem to realize.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Accessible Outside Class

Monotone lecturer. Very knowledgeable but not good at conveying it. Labs often have nothing to do with what is being taught.

At the start of the class, he teaches you C by giving you a week to do a whole 50-course introduction to programming course that happens to use C. Each section of this course has unskippable videos too.

Does good curves.

The most boring professor I've ever had. The topics of the class are actually kind of interesting but Professor Zarif just reads off the slides. I'm pretty sure most of the resources are from another professor. I had to teach myself the material and went to ALAC. Trying to learn MIPS from his slides was hell. Make sure you look at back exams.

Pros: test is fair and do curve the exam and the final grade, have extra 2 percent credit for doing submitty poll question for every class. 
Cons: lecture is boring, only reading ppts, i feel like it is kind of wasting time for getting up at 8am and listen to his lectures, just do the back exam and you dont need to actually listen to his lecture
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Terrible lecturer. Class is structured horribly. You won't learn anything but he curves the grades at the end.

Not a good professor, his teaching in lectures was really boring reading of the slides so I stopped attending after the first few classes.  The class was always disorganized and confusing.  I taught myself everything and got an A without too much struggle but that wasn't the case for most, wouldn't recommend in general

Impossible to pay attention to, makes the content way more boring than it needs to be. He only reads from the slides and does not explain anything well at all. Combined with it being a tough class to begin with, it is a very bad combination.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The lectures are oddly paced and generally it feels like there's no proper lesson plan. Not rare for lab assignments to be completely unrelated to what's been covered in recent lectures. Just feels very unplanned.
Worst lectures I have ever witnessed. Incredibly boring and bloated with useless and unrelated information.

Yet another professor that's paid by textbook companies to charge every student $70 to be able to complete homework.
Also has no idea what he's assigning - see mandatory 1000+ problem week 1 assignment.
Exams are horrible. Pray for a huge curve.
Labs can take from 10 minutes to 4 hours.
Lectures are very monotonous. Homeworks & Labs are busy work.

Shows a general lack of enthusiasm for teaching his class, and does not respect his students. Assigns regular busywork and does not give labs, tests, and homeworks that accurately reflect the level of material that was taught. Monotone lecturer, hard to stay engaged.

You will not learn anything in class, you will not learn anything from the textbook, you will not receive study materials related to the tests whatsoever, then when everyone fails on account of the test being completely unrelated to things even mentioned in class, he will curve it till a 50% is passing. Also worst and longest HW's I've had so far.
Lectures are boring. Homeworks are tedius.

I disagree with other comments. The lectures were boring however the tests were very fair and almost the same as the example exam provided by the professor. He did a HUGE curve even though he shouldn't have and 85 people out 100 got an A. I don't know why everyone is complaining much. This is college you need to work hard to get good grades!

Aside from his poor lecture style, Masoud made many questionable-at-best choices with the structure of this course, like assigning a homework on MIPS only after we took an exam on MIPS. He also barely answers students' concerns on the discussion forum, and he fails to follow his own syllabus on many counts, such as the number of late days we have.

Awful. Worst experience I have ever had. He breaks several institute rules and fails to prepare his students for exams. He is also an extremely inconsiderate person and does not care about students success.

One of the worst professors of all time, labs are either almost impossible or the easiest thing ever. The syllabus has two different rubrics for course grades, he never answers students questions on discussion boards. Homework's are given out randomly, and he does not let you use late days despite giving you five. Take this course with anyone else.

Masoud explains the content pretty decently but hes kinda quiet. Lectures are recorded so you don't have to go to class. The course content kinda sucks and the tests are miserable. The homeworks and labs are also sometimes annoying. No curve, but no final either. Seems like everyone is collectively doing bad in this class lol
There are so many tedious homework in this course. Such as you need to finish at least 200-300 questions in zybooks weekly. Addtionally, there so many high repetitive homework.

One of the worst professors at RPI—barely understandable, just reads off slides, and assigns longer, harder work right before long weekends or Thanksgiving. Claims attendance is mandatory however doesn't account for it in syllabus and only takes it before breaks. She also barely understands students' questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: As a CSE, I took this course with Prof. Huang as an elective: It's equation hell with a professor who speedruns lectures in a quiet, boring voice, and she refuses to post lecture notes online or use any sort of electronics in her class to help her TAs grade. Go to rpistudygroup for old notes, they are similar; and actually read the textbook.

I feel sleepier during her lectures than I do going to bed at night. Besides that, she's not much work and her tests are fair. All you need to do well is have every equation from lecture on your crib sheet, problems are just plugging in values. She's not great at teaching the concepts, just how to solve the problems, so I didn't actually learn much

For Microelectronics Technology, Dr. Huang tends to read from the powerpoint slides a lot, so the material gets pretty boring. But she is available after hours and is willing to go the extra mile for you. I like that she makes it a point to put all her notes, homeworks, class assignments, backwork, etc. online. She is a fair grader.
reviews.rating_tags: SO MANY PAPERS--Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: No Comments

Uses powerpoint lectures.  Everything online, which is nice.  Tends to teach details without giving the big picture, but that's just the nature of the class.  Slight accent but not difficult to understand.  Kinda sexy.
Goated dude, so sad he is retiring :(

Overall a good prof. All of the physics lectures are the same for all sections but he showed the stats for which exam questions were the hardest/could appear again on the final. He cared about us understanding the fundamentals. He appreciates class participation. There are class activities which makes attendance essentially mandatory.

Very sweet man who is passionate about physics. You definitely do need to show up to class (there are graded in class activities no matter who your professor is). He is great about exam review, and gives a ton of practice problems during class. I recommend just paying attention, and he is more than willing to answer questions or review hard topics.

He's great! His english wasn't always the best, but he is so clear in his explanations of things it wasn't an issue for me. He is so sweet and wants everyone to do well, so he reviews sample questions each class about the last lecture's content. I always thought the test reviews were super helpful as well. Definitely ask him for help if you need!

I loved professor Zhang! His lectures were easy to understand and our section consistently did better than other sections on exams. At the beginning of class, he often reviewed questions from past exams (pertaining to the previous lecture) which turned out to be super helpful. As long as you study back exams, this course isn't difficult.

He is insanely passionate, you can see his face light up when he gets to a topic he likes. He is extremely accommodating and understanding and although work can sometimes be hard he wants to help you. He is great at adding interesting tidbits to the course without veering away from the textbook too much. So it's still easy to catch up if you miss.

Though he does not speak very good English, his mind is clear. This course is very easy to pass and get A as long as you review all the points taught in class. By the way mastering physics is so awful !

Most lectures come straight from the text, but it can feel like something is lost in translation between the book and the chalkboard.  Use Griffiths as your primary resource but come to class to ask questions and take the quizzes.  Prof Zhang is super helpful during office hours if you find the lectures muddled or are confused about something.
Physics was not my strongest subject. Although he is hard to understand at times, he is very helpful. If you email him with questions or concerns about your grade he is willing to help.
Very kind, flexible and responsive. Class is useful and doesn't make the class more difficult than it needs ot be.

Professor Eleish is great! Very responsive and caring for students, understanding RPI coursework challenges. I took Data Science and Analytics with him. The courses are very laid back, promoting students to learn through exploration, rather than strict grading criteria. He was very helpful advising outside of class, guiding my career aspirations.

Great professor, 99 overall rating. Had him for Data Science and Data Analytics and I really enjoyed both of his classes. Most meaningful class content I've had, everything I learned in his class I applied at work. Love how it's more applied CS compared to the more theoretical courses at RPI. Very caring professor as well, wants to see you succeed.

Very low-stress class but still interesting. Only had a few assignments and no tests. Dr. Eleish's lectures can get a little monotone sometimes, but I think he'll get better w/ practice. If you care about Data Science you'll learn, and if you don't care you'll still get a good grade. You get what you put into it. Some professors can learn from him.

goated professor, one of the few who really cares. I didn't take it for Data Analytics but rather Data Science (CSCI 4350) and it was a very relaxed course. The class is structured where there is a few group projects that are intriguing and some individual work. No exams or final and I still feel like I learnt more here than in some other classes.
Good professor, easy classes, and useful assigments/projects

Honestly one of the best professors at this school especially for Computer Science/Information Technology and Web Science (ITWS). For Data Science and Data Analytics he is very laid back and gives extensions whenever needed. The projects for both classes are pretty easy and all the assignments are easy to understand/complete. 100% recommend!
Had a great time in the class. He was always willing to help with any task. If you find anything difficult (including requiring extensions), reach out to him.
this guy is pretty good. gives good lectures and always responds to emails ASAP. very chill and very open in class for questions.

Absolute goat, keeps his classes chill af. If you genuinely enjoy the subject his classes are fun, probably one of the only professors I bother paying attention to. He likes to be on top of technology and discusses new things in class which is good for this field.

Tough accent but interesting lectures. The lectures only take 1 hour, and the rest is a class activity. Most class activities and past tests are available on rpistudygroup. This guy curved all our grades down with no prior warning because I guess he made the class too easy and had to normalize.

Definitely one of the best professors I have ever met. He makes clear points in class, and his homework & quiz are easy if you go to classes or read PDF yourself. The only imperfect thing is his accent that may lead to a bit of understanding problem. BTW, he replies your email ASAP and the feedback is always helpful.
he never showed up to lecture and when he did, he was hard to understand
Not easy to understand him because of his accent, but he is a great professor. Homeworks, studios, and quizzes are easy. He's there to answer your questions after the class, and is helpful.
Prof is nice and generous!! Exams are pretty easy. Projects are a bit timeconsuming.
professor is pretty nice. HW and Exam are not hard. But the project need some time. If you have a good TA it will be OK. great course for VLSI.
Prof zhang is pretty good. Nice lecture. He explain the concepts very clearly and easy to understand. Exam are easy to handle if you take notes on class.
Prof Zhang is really nice. HW and exam paper is not hard if you read lectures. The content is instructive and matched well with industry.
Boring but capable lecturer, though his accent made it really hard to process what he was saying and notes were cryptic. Tries to avoid out-of-classroom interaction. Very generous curver.
Good professor and class is fairly easy as long as you write down the examples he gives in lecture. Labs are easy (TA's will help a lot). Homework is time consuming but not too hard.

Very difficult to understand, although it can be amusing at times, especially when he attempts to say "bubble".  The homeworks take way too long, but the tests aren't that bad.  The class is average...
Helpful, nice guy.  Accent is strong, but easy to get used to.  Class is quite easy.

Really strong accent. Don't know how to teach. The class is always boring. Bring a pillow, have a good sleep...He wants to help but I don't get what comes out of his mouth. This guy needs to practice his English.
Very cool!

Prof Zhang's accent makes it really hard to understand and follow the lectures.. the contents not too exciting either, but with help from the TAs and reading the lecture slides and text book the class is really pretty easy. Make K maps for everything!!

Listening to this guy talk is hilarious.  If you are making a circuit for a cerror phone...  Use the bobble...  if we want to count to tweolve...  it is in the middowl... having said this, he is poor at answering questions because he usually can't understand the question.  the class isn't too bad
strong accent, hard to understand
I couldn't understand a thing he said from day one, may as well have been teaching myself COCO =/
Hard to understand, but very helpful and easy going
very boring, uses powerpoint, class isnt very hard tho, just do the work and u will do fine
Very helpful
He is very friendly, and he will help you to the best of his ability.  You just have to listen hard to get past the language barrier.
No Comments
Great guy, very smart, can be hard to understand during lecture though.
Very friendly on the side and very smart, difficult accent

He is well educated on the topic he is teaching, but he doesn't care much about students success. It's important you pay attention in class and take good notes. I would recommend taking the class with friends who you can rely on. The class average was with a 50%

You could tell this class is probably not where he wants to be.  If you're stuck on any concepts, it's better to find a friend to help than pursue him.  If the material is easy for you, he's fine, but his way of explaining things can leave you in the dark more often than not.
Worst Professor I have EVER come in contact with. Refused to go any deeper than "study harder" for advice on how to do better.

The math portion of tests very closely matched the homework given.  Some multiple choice word questions were ambiguous.  He is very uncompromising with regards to his way of thinking and becomes verbally nasty when asked questions about test material.  I got an A, but I still wanted to punch him in the face.

He doesnt care about students, or teaching. You can email him a million times and even if its about how he gave you the wrong final grade (an F) which caused you to be on probation he will not answer.

He is a smart guy but he can't teach and doesn't try to explain the material. Lectures didn't fit with the book whatsoever and homeworks made nothing clear.  The book was terrible and didn't match the material we were expected to know at all. His tests are not complex, though he will murder you with the grading. I did well in his class despite him.

tons of office hours visits ended in anger, with no progress made on the subject matter. notes were handwritten, but at such a low contrast, that they were often illegible, along with his handwriting. Although he appears to know what hes talking about on the subject matter, it seems like he has no ability to convey that knowledge to his students

His exams are designed to match his lectures, where as the homework was from the text. He never really went over the text in class, as a result things were very disjointed. He does post lectures online, but they are difficult to follow.

This is the first bad teacher I've had at RPI. He does not even understand his own labs. He does not care about his students. Occasionally, he just walks out of the class during labs.. He teaches lectures via powerpoint & has VERY quick slide changes. If you want to read the slide, expect to take your laptop to class (lectures off LMS). Horrible.
His lectures were a borefest.  90% of the time I had no clue what he was talking about.  I asked for advice for taking the final and he told me to switch to management.
Doesn't seem to care much about his students.  Labs were somewhat ambiguous and he was very unclear about what he wanted initially.  Lots of problems with the execution of the labs.

Personally, he is not a bad professor, but he is not quite that helpful when I ask him questions during class. Still, he selects great TAs that can explain things well, so I thought it was a pretty good class. But by the pace of the class, he could only skim through most of the concepts, so I suggest you to read the textbook.

Adams' voice is a lullaby.  Expect to sleep through his lectures (you will not be missing much).  If you want help, ask your TA or someone else.  I feel like Adams was not really prepared to teach physics I, seeing as his name was only added to the course the week before classes started.
Not very helpful. Rate of teaching is too fast to comprehend.
Adams is a horrible writer. The lab book used is very vague and the information in it is not well organized.

Didn't explain things well, didn't make it clear what exactly was supposed to go in lab reports. We didn't have to set up the labs, and it was a game to figure out how to use the equipment, then later what the point of the lab was in order to write the report. I didn't learn anything useful.

I wouldn't say that the course was absolutely atrocious, but the fact that Adams' lab manual was not thorough and his lectures also did not help, the course proved difficult. Additionally, I don't want to harshly label Professor Adams as an idiot, but his competency level was not what I expected from a seasoned physicist like him.
engage students more!

I really liked the class, and Dr. Adams was very helpful.  Also, the TA's were amazing, particularly Brian Moziak, who also helped me tremendously.  This also reflects well on Dr. Adams, showing that he knows how to pick good TA's.

Professor Adams was not helpful at all. When I would ask him a question he would just make me feel dumb instead of trying to answer it, responding with things like "didn't you read the book?". Lab instructions were poorly written and usually very unclear. A little more effort on the professor's part would have saved all us students a big headache.

For Ex-Phys, you don't interact with the professor that much.  He's pretty reasonable, my only problem is that he isn't direct in answering questions and wasn't too clear with explaining error analysis.  Other than that, I have no qualms with him whatsoever.  The course itself is a lot of work, but that doesn't have much ofanything to do with Adams
Professor Adams is knowledgable, but his teaching abilities seem marginal at best.  In particular, he did a poor job explaining error analysis in the lecture sessions in the beginning of the year.
Since it's Ex Phys, there wasn't much interaction with the professor. When there was, it was brief.
adams is ok. his voice will put you to sleep during lecture as he reads from the powerpoint. he doesnt seem to be too competent in physics. he's not a bad teacher, but by no means good.
Didn't really seem into it.  Lectures were boring and what's worse: uninformative.

For X-Phys you don't really need to use the professor that much. I just use the TA's since I know them. From what I understand he tends to over explain things a tad. The point of this class is to figure things out on your own anyway.

BAD. The first few weeks of the semester we just lectures, which consisted of him rambling on for an hour. I kept taking out my notebook to take notes but he never made any points. Then we had labs, which were impossible. He did try to help but had no clue what he was doing.

Bring a strong cup of coffee to stay awake.  He reads directly off the powerpoints, which makes me doubt how much he knows about the subject.  He reeks of incompetence.  The class was easy, but not at all enjoyable.  Avoid if you can.
Nice guy nice teacher at least hespokeenglish well
borin, kinda goofy, but hey he is a physics guy...
Easy to listen to during lecture. Explains problems well.
Neutral, doesn't explain things very well.
gary adams is the WORST professor i have ever had.....he's also a big JERK

This guy sucks.  He sucks at giving lectures and physics 1 is just terrible because the tests are so messed up (curves of 20+ points).  Tell the idiots that got a 5 on the ap physics not to take this class and ruin everyone else.
Clarifies Bedrosian's lecture notes.
No Comments
i got a lower score on the evaluation test given at the end of the semester, then the one at  begining of the semester.

Despite getting a relatively low grade in the class, I really feel like I learned the topic. DBS is pretty comprehensive and Dr Adali seems like she's made an effort to seriously streamline the course so that exams and homework test your knowledge of the topics rather than act as busywork. Strongly reccomend.

Great professor! Class easy as long as you attend lectures and take notes. Super helpful and knowledgeable. Highly recommend - teaches topics for real-life applications (job interviews, etc.). As long as you put in effort, you will do good.
she is very tough grader and alway make people lower grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: So accessible! She would always respond in less than < 5min to pms on webex teams, even late night and outside of office hours. Lectures were clear and homeworks are fair.

Professor Adali is an amazing professor. I really enjoyed this class, but I wish I had taken it not online since I would enjoy lectures more. Still, she works hard to give notes/lectures/examples and used the online format to her advantage in interacting with students. Always available outside class and super understanding when I talked to her.
Lovely professor
Good class, Great Professor.

Professor Adali's lectures are helpful. She is nice to everyone she meets. If YOU ask her questions face to face or on the piazza, or even by emailing her, she would reply to you with words easy to understand. I took the course in fall 2017. The tests were not heavy but you should review all the materials she posts on website.

Phenomenal teacher! If you have any background in coding at all, you can honestly just skip lecture most of the time, but if you're not so well versed in coding, she does a pretty decent job in explaining everything. I mainly went to class once a week to chat with her about the new Rick and Morty episode (they will show up in class quite a bit).

She is a rather poor lecturer; luckily Professor Turner had lectures which ran parallel to hers, earlier in the day, and covered the same content (same course). Id avoid her; she is a bit annoying and tends to be quite poor at illustrating concepts. Im very glad this course is over. Be prepared for poor instructions on assignments and esoteric..
She's one of the nicest and funniest professors. CS1 with her was an easy A for someone with no prior experience.
Her lectures are very clear. If you have any question the TAs are very helpful. She also gives a lot of extra credit. Just do the work and its an easy A.
Many bugs in homework that I have to wait for them to be fixed.

Sibel Adali is a great teacher.  I had her for CS1 and she really helps you understand new topics.  She has a site set up where her and her TAs will answer nearly all questions students have. The class isn't an easy A, because the nature of the class itself requires time and energy, but she gives several late days and decent partial credit.
Excellent instructor

Such a great professor! Really enjoys working with students. Makes assignments fun by making them about student interests. Lectures are a little boring. It can be hard to pay attention, especially with your computer right in front of you. It doesn't really matter if you skip class, all the notes are online. You should try to go though!

She's just great especially if you get to know her personally. The labs are mandatory but the lecture isn't because the notes are recorded and  online. Tests are straightforward and there's tons of help if you don't understand the work.
love her teaching style. She give enough time to do homework and review when they are hard. Offers extra credit sometimes but not often. Classes are engaging.

She's very engaging and uses good example problems to keep students interested. Gives three late days for no points off during the semester. Homework and labs can be really tricky, there're frequently lots of kids in office hours the day before an assignment is due, but they are graded generously. Hw grade counteracts my low (70's) test average.

Sibel Adali is not only the most adorable woman I've ever met but is literally the best professor I've had. People who posted bad things about her are just bitter because it's a difficult subject and requires a lot of work to do well. She makes classes interesting and is in NO way hard to understand. Everybody I've ever encountered loves her.
She taught the comp sci 1 class with Stewart the first semester it was offered in python (fall 2012). I preferred the days she taught because she explained things better.
She was very helpful and I loved her teaching style!

One of the better CS profs. Looking at older comments, I get the idea she's come a long way. She really knows her stuff and puts a lot of work into the class. She is very nice and helpful in office hours. The class is challenging, but fair, and certainly not impossible. The average on exam 1 was 83, exam 2: 85, final: 77.
I enjoyed her class

I think she teaches well.  She really knows her stuff. Her accent might lose some people, but if you pay attention, and take notes you will pass the course.  Her tests are open note and book.  I think she's great!
Completely worthless...waste of time...not at all easy to understand..neither does she make it easy...tests and homeworks are impossible to crack...take another course instead!!

I understand why people don't like her... her tests are difficult, the homeworks can be long, and the projects both difficult and long. However, I felt that she was one of the better instructors I've had at RPI. She could explain things more clearly, but at least she took an interest in the course. Overall, I thought she was great.
Projects were difficult

She was helpful during office hours, her tests were on the notes and the book, so go to class. I have no idea why she has gotten such bad ratings, she was actually one of the better CSCI teachers because she would actually explain the material in office hours rather than tell you 'go read the book' or 'think about it'
Projects were much harder than everything else in the class. Exams and homeworks were fairly straightforward. Lectures were pretty dry. Slight accent, but little difficulty understanding.

She admitted she was bad at programming and using a database. Her practice test answers were almost always wrong. She always left the country before a test. The course wiki was never up. Her lectures were unhelpful after the first test. She seemed to get lost a lot in her own examples. Don't expect to learn much practical info from this class.
Very intelligent...very helpful..Willing to help those who show interest in learning.  The class was difficult, but at the same time very satisfying and worthwhile.  Plus she's kinda cute! :)

Boo!!!  RAISED cutoffs 5 points after initial ones were posted!  Very misleading/secretive about grading process; you have to live, breathe, and eat Database Systems in order to get an A in one of her courses.

Database Systems is not as hard as she makes it out to be.  Weekly quizzes are very hard, even though they are open book.  Homeworks border on annoying, where you really don't learn anything because the problem lies in some stupid slide she put up and talked about for a minute.  Avoid.
One of the best classes I ever took. Adali was very helpful during office hours.
her teaching sucks

This guy is really easy and is pretty helpful. The guy who wrote that hes strict is a moron. So he wants you to raise your hand. Its basic classroom etiquette. Plus he tries to find outside material that is interesting.

awesome guy and easy as hell

AWESOME

very helpful! definitely the best teacher for this class.
