cool professor who really knows his stuff, seems like a better professor than some of the other professors who teach IEA, from what some of my friends who were in other sections said.

loved this class!

reviews.comment:
Avoid Agarwal at all costs. First, there are NO partial credits on an exam question if you get it wrong. Lets say you used the correct formula but plugged in the wrong numbers or made a silly mistake. Thats 0 points for that question. 

The majority of the students are doing poorly in BMED 4430 (Biomedical Instrumentation), but she does not curve.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Argarwal is a wonderfully spectacular instructor. It is easy to get an A+ in this course since she is forgiving and gives great feedback. She definitely did not intimidate students by reminding us that she has the power to fail us and prevent moving forward in the curriculum or from graduating. Also TAs came well prepared every time for lab!

Dr. Agarwal is a good lecturer, I will give her that. With that being said, she will smile as she hands you a failing grade. She grades very objectively, so take it seriously when other people say she is HARSH when grading. I found her feedback fairly unhelpful as well.

To be honest, she is extremely nice and personable and that is noticeable if you talk one on one with her or in a small group, although she may appear to be a tad rude in the lecture. If you need help in the lab, she's there for you no matter what. But she is a TOUGH grader. Ask TAs for help in the first few labs because she grades the rest herself
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The class is boring. The labs are cool but it sucks if you don't get the lab you want. Grading is harsh but at least it's consistent. Try to coordinate with friends if you want to get your first pick of the labs

The grading criteria in BME lab is insane. It took my group (3 competent people, in my opinion) 4+ hours to write each lab and then another 2+ hours just formatting. We barely got C's. None of us know anyone that ever got an A on their labs. Get to know the TA's and see if you can get them to look at your labs ahead of time. They will save you.

Dr. Agarwal's grading criteria for BME Lab is harsh. Don't be surprised if your lab reports are returned all marked up. On one hand, this means she cares. On the other hand, it means you get a lot of points taken off for anal reasons. Make sure you are never seen with your phone/laptop in class or in lab. She will find you and she will fail you...
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Dr. Agarwal is very caring and willing to go the extra mile to help you but her Biomedical Engineering Lab course was a lot of work and the grading criteria was unclear. Lab reports are graded very harshly - make sure you take note of any lab report writing tips in class or you will probably fail a lab report or two
Lot of work and too much information scattered in slides.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: The best professor I have seen at RPI.

Systems and Synthetic Biology: He was very helpful in explaining all of the concepts and was very friendly and great at explaining concepts at his office hours

She made MAU slightly more tolerable, and she will take all the time in the world to explain something if you don't understand it. Her lectures are slightly discombobulated at times, so just keep asking questions.

Of the MAU professors whose lectures I have gone to (her, Shenogin and the german guy) she is the only one that lectures via ipad notes and then shares those notes afterward so I definitely recommend her, especially if you skip lectures.

Dr. Agca Aktunc is one of my favorite lecturers at RPI. She is extremely knowledgable, especially in statistics and data science. MAU is a math & theory heavy course, but she explains all the concepts very in-depth and clearly. She is kind, polite and always willing to help students, all of her office hours I have been to were extremely effective.

Probably one of my absolute favorite professors at rpi. He is nice and open to all sorts of ideas and input. Unlike most professors he is willing to iterate and design his class in order for students to succeed. There was a lot of discussions in his class but he made students feel welcome to state their opinion.

reviews.comment: This course was writing intensive. There was a large project worth most of the class grade that included investigating something related to the environment (that was as specific as he got). There were also weekly "journals" due to reflect on the things you learned in the course. Overall boring lectures, but an easy course.
He is a truly passionate teacher, and always a ton of fun to listen to.  I just wish I was more interested / better at what he teaches.

A good professor if you are at college to learn. The course was work intensive, but definitely inspired thought and creativity. Required text was Lessig's Code 2.0, which is cheap for the hard copy and better yet, free online.

Lectures are absolutely terrible; it's as though he does not know when to stop talking and when to allow discussion to continue in class. Possibly one of the most boring classes I've ever taken and it had the chance to be something wonderful.

Good prof, provided you actually care about the subject matter (or like to read, or write, or learn, or do much of anything). If deep/convoluted thoughts aren't your thing, though, you might want to find a different professor. If you like going "Huh?/Whoa..." then Social Dimensions of Engineering is the class for you.
P&E sucks.. it's a lot of work, especially if you get stuck in a crappy group.  Atsushi is ok, but the lectures are pretty boring.

Social Dimensions of Engineering -- very interesting course.  Though it was my humanities, I probably learned more about engineering in this course than any of my other first year courses.  Atsushi, (he encouraged us to call him by his first name), always involved everyone in the conversations.

Great Prof. Knows his stuff. Tons of work, but you learn alot too. He is opened to all kinds of diffrent opinions too!

Watch out he assigns a lot of work and just when you think your done he assigns some more. I thought this prof was very good. Though he tends to take very left-wing stances and I am very conservative I found this lead to great debates in class. He was very open to people who didn't share his view and welcomed disent.

he is japanese and has a mullet! he is that screwed up, his views are completely utopian and the grading is retarded. a kid in my section failed a paper because he used the term "man-hours", as in hours of labor. The professor said it was gender

I thought he was one of the best teachers I had at RPI

The grading system for this class is definitely messed up: a) Effort definitely DOES NOT translate into good grades, and c) I got an A in the course even though I got a B or a C on pretty much everything I did.
Horrible class no matter which u take of his, if possible stay out, classes are completly left wing, lack relisticness, and are always too much work.

Too much work. The class is full of over-acheiving freshmen and it seems no matter how hard I try I can't figure out what him and his colleagues are looking for when it comes to grading criteria.

I had Akera for and I can tell you that while his outward appearance might be left-wing, you have to have him as your section leader to learn his true colors.  He's a really bad lecturer, however in a smaller group he's more accepting of right-wing views.
I hated his class.  Way too much work.  The whole course was a way for him to talk about his left-wing political views, and I learned nothing.  Way too much work for a freshman level IT class.

He was a great teacher, and enthusiastic, glad i had Jill Fisher as a section leader though, she was even better.  Atsushi was very organized in lecture, and this was one of my favorite classes at RPI

This is by far the most one-sided teacher I have ever had.  He is a complete hippy that has no respect for normal people's comments.  If you are going to try and engage students in discussion you must respect both sides of an argument.
intro to sts, lot of reading articles and writing involved, prof is kind of out there, but he's very nice. enthusiastic and knowledgeable about his field.  really emphasizes participation
It was wonderful to watch optimization and experience in optimization together.

This is one of the wonderful course, that I took during my educational career at MSU.  The course works are well organized, and the professor was  awesome in teaching that makes enthusiastic period while taking the course. I can recommend anyone who is willing to take this course.

The lecture is wonderful, and it is definitely one of the most useful courses I've ever taken in graduate school.  It also has a beautiful textbook coming with this course.  Engineering students must take it! It is really helpful for your career.
Prof. Messac is fantastic. The best teacher I have seen. You can learn a lot from this his class.

AWESOME !! He is THE best professor in the department Challenging course, but I highly recommend it. Dr. Messac is the best in his field and is very intelligent in the subject. He is always willing to help. I have learned a lot in his class. His lectures are great!

Had him for split level optimization at Mississippi State.I was a little nervous at first since optimization is a specialty of his, but the course was taught in a very manageable fashion. There was a steady stream of HW, but it's all very useful. He'd always help after class if you got stuck on something (start HW early!) Good Teacher; Good Course

As the message below this one states "He is not as bad as they say" HE IS WORSE!!!!. The only way he could have gotten a positive review is if he wrote it himself. THIS GUY IS TERRIBLE! I get more from the course by not attending and just reading the book, BECAUSE THAT IS ALL MESSAC CAN DO.

Also, the hw isnt too bad if you keep up on it and it helps on the tests.
The worst professor I have ever had.  All the man can do is read word for word from the awful text he requires and yank his own chain.  He is his own greatest hero.

best TA ever!!!

ochem lab sucks, especially with moore as the professor. but akshar made this lab so much fun, especially coming from javier the first semester, i learned so much more with akshar. best TA i've ever had at RPI and probably will never be topped. if you miss out of the experience of having akshar as a TA you've missed out on an amazing experience.

Akshar is the best OChem TA there is! I had him my first semester in OChem lab and I miss him so much this semester. Even though he is no longer my TA I go to him all the time for help. I know he's done TAing after his second year in grad school but he is just so so so awesome!

Very interesting class but the only way to do well on exams is to get the back exams from the union. He isn't very accessible outside of class and overall, the course structure was disorganized. He would often not give directions for bigger projects until the last minute.

One of the most engaging lecturers I have had. His class is very interesting and builds on itself in a way that makes sense. Quizzes are difficult and typically had averages of 50-60s. Exams have a lot of content but as long as you start early they are pretty straightforward. Very test heavy grading but does give extra credit for participation.

Interesting class. Exams were difficult but very close to back exams from the union. Assignments in the syllabus were mentioned but specific instructions were not given to us until very close to the deadline. He will cold call and grill your responses. Nice and willing to reschedule quizzes and exams. Just a lot of disorganization.

He was a great lecturer with understandable slides. The exams were fair but you definitely needed to study a lot for them. We had extra credit but you need a 95 for an A. TA review sessions were extremely helpful and Rojas was helpful in office hours. Grades took a long time to be put into LMS but overall biomaterials is a good course- just study!
The course was obviously going to be heavy, but this teacher made it very simple and had us understand all of the material. He was very caring and this class is very manageable for 4-credits

Dr. Rojas is a good professor. Not a lot of homework. Definitely cares about his students and is very approachable. He rushes through lectures but the slide material is good and easy to review. He is sometimes unclear about content for assignments/quizzes. Tests were difficult but awesome TA review sessions and forgiving grading helped a ton.

Professor Rojas is new to the school in Fall 2024, and I had him for bioengineering and material science. If you have Anderson for your capstone group, I would strongly advise trying to find a different prof or a substitute class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Mark Anderson was an awful Capstone PE. He refused to answer questions directly, but got angry when things didn't go his way. He lectured us about things he doesn't understand, like mechanical engineering. He lied to us about the previous status of the project, then literally made us keep working on it after our final presentation was over.

Tbh, one of the most underrate person at RPI. He teaches you how to think like a real engineer and had helped us tremendously in our project. The grade received was awful, but he was not one giving us the final grades, don't blame him.

He is incredibly rude, interrupts you constantly so that you can never justify anything you do, treats women like they're hysterical, and makes team members cry. He will never give you direct feedback. It always feels like he's taking you on a long journey about how he's right and you're wrong. I hate the thought of going to class every time.

Mr. Anderson is the worst teacher I have ever met. He gives you hard time during lectures and always tells you he doesn't care about the problem you encountered rather than helping you. Takes forever for him to go through your presentation because he always tells you where you are wrong. Don't take his class if not necessary.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Mr. Anderson is impatient and always tells you that you are wrong. He criticizes you without knowing the whole story and focuses on details that should not matter. In addition, he speaks so fast and it is hard for you to concentrate for the whole class to get everything he says, and he seems to be proud of that. Do not take his class if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Anderson is not a good person. This man refuses to give positive feedback about ANYTHING and will make your group members cry. He wastes class time lecturing the group about why he's right and you're wrong. He treats group members like children. My entire experience at RPI is tainted because of Mark Anderson.
Worst professor at RPI.

I had a great RPI experience, not a single bad professor, until Mark. Most of the feedback you receive from him is negative and sometimes rude. He forces you to do some work of the project, and the next class he claims that he never did . If you have the chance to drop the class just do.  Kept saying for the group that we will get an incomplete

Anderson will always say why what your doing is bad so your not allowed to do it but won't tell you what you should do instead resulting in a continuous cycle of failed proposals and nothing accomplished. If you get anderson I would highly recommend dropping the course and taking it the next semester. Trust me it's worth it.

If you are looking for a good grade, you just have to read, take notes (open note quizzes), raise your hand in class, and attempt all the criteria in the assignments. Do your best to make time for the class and get the most out of it. She can be kind of eccentric at times, but she always goes deep into the concepts she is teaching.

This class was incredibly difficult with some very strange theories that are taken for fact. The distribution of reading assignments was skewed and some days you had to read a five page essay about feminism and the next you would have to read an entire book. Half the class glazed over while she was talking.

Dr Anicca definitely knows what she's talking about! She's a great professor and very easy to reach out to. I loved her Women's Writing class, and although it was a lot of work, it was very rewarding!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Do not take this course unless you absolutely need it to graduate. The professor is unorganized, unpunctual, and expects too much of her students for what her class is. This is an art history class. She is very opinionated and often interjects politics into her lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Mary Anne is difficult to rate. She is very knowledgeable, and is always willing to talk and give feedback. She cares about her field and wants others to feel the same. She can, however, be very disorganized and distractable. I wish I could grade her higher. She is, however, very lenient with grades, especially if you submit decent work.

Grades based off 3 papers and attendance, as of now (last days of finals) she still hasn't graded anything. Rushed assigning us papers at the end of the semester because she didn't plan out due dates. Lectures are awful with everyone sitting on their phone behind their computers. So many easier inquiry classes don't take it.

do not take this class

No

Prof. is such a sweetheart, I loved taking this course and it really changed how I consume media for good, there is a lot of news analysis during class and it is mostly based around current events. She did require us to memorize some key facts about culture & history, however I liked the fact that she allowed us to be creative/open-minded and pick our own topics to present.
She is a very thoughtful professor and cares about students. Although her exams are hard, you should be fine if you put emphasis on her syllabus. She grades everybody kindly.

Prof.Staniszewski is a really nice person! I like her. I don't think her lectures are boring, but when she explains stuff, it's really confusing. Her exams are not hard (lots of memorization -dates/paintings- for this course). She's always energetic and active! overall i like this course and the professor.

Professor Staniszewski was the best teacher I had at RPI. Her concepts are really interesting and she knows art theory/history inside and out. She literally wrote the book(s) on it! The classes I took with her were eye-opening and just so wonderful. She requires a lot of memorization but there's a lot of discussion and analysis too. She's fabulous!

I gave this class countless opportunities to shine, and it passed up each one. The course material is actually interesting, but is not presented well. At all. Professor S. is a good professor- she professes and all that- but as a teacher I find her to be IMPOSSIBLE.

If you wished you went to a liberal arts school, you'll enjoy her, but she's too tied up in the pretentious "Art" ideals to actually teach stuff that will be useful in real life (unless you plan on being a fine artist or a teacher).
Rarely starts class earlier than 20 min in. Enjoyable personality especially outside of the class period. Do take notes. A lot of memorization. Essentially an art history course

controversial and partisan, some people think shes a b*tch, but i love her, even though I dont agree with her social-political beleifs nor her aesthetics. She has written, researched and added plenty to her feild and she gives out mutual respect when it is deserved. only treats adults like adults.

Course totally not anything like described. Turned into a boring tedious art history course centered around a horrible book that was written by her (of course). SHe is 1 of 2 reasons why I changed my major.

He's wildly different in normal classes from the studio, we didn't have any homework this semester. He would spend the entire class time lecturing, asking us questions, and giving very good life advice. Sometimes it was hard to stay awake, but that's just how soft-spoken he is.
Professor Titus is an inspiration to me and will be for many years to come. He cares about each and every one of his infant architects.

This man is a walking talking architecture model, and you will become one too because of how many freaking models he made me do. I hate even looking at glue now it reminds me of the countless all-nighters this man cost me. Also he does shrummies.
Fantastic professor. Inspiring. Eccentric, a kind of arcane, mythic figure or illusory enigma...

Prof Titus is a gifted designer, painter, and educator. Expect to be constantly challenged in studio, but also expect to mature as a thinker and produce profound work. Anthony puts a student's interests and education first -- which is all too rare. Seriously and genuinely committed to architectural education. A transformer of minds.

A fantastic studio professor. Is both extremely committed to and extremely knowledgeable of the subject matter. Wants you to do well. Is willing to come in on a Saturday to help you with your work. Only major complaint is sometimes he's not the clearest with what he wants for an assignment. But he knows this, and will try to re-explain if you ask.
One of the best Prof at RPI. You will learn despite the hard topic she will cover. At the end of the day, you feel rewarded for the class that you took.

Great teacher. Her lectures are very clear and she is precise in her teaching. Professor Maniatty is very knowledgable in the courses she teaches.

People say they don't like the lecture style. This is one of the best lecture courses I've had at RPI. Professor Maniatty always comes to class prepared and makes the most of lecture time. She has handwritten lecture notes that she posts after and goes through completely in class. She accurately explains theory and presents releva example problems.

The exams are very similar to the practice exams she posts online. Homeworks are graded based off the fact that you did it. So as long as you have an answer you can get a 10/10 all all homeworks. Memorize the practice exam and go through the homeworks and this class is easy.

I took EMD as a senior. It seems that everyone who did poorly was incapable of working hard-doing HW. Class instruction was dull, clear (at least to me), and very relevent to the tests. Test ?'s were very similar to HW and class examples. I never did her worksheets, but you will fail if you don't understand the HW. Was very helpful in office hours.
this class sucks
The class was sooo terrible! She has no empathy towards students or understanding of student's learning styles, so she ends up being a terrible teacher.
STAY AWAY FROM HER CLASS!! SHE IS BORING AND DULL. HER LECTURES ARE TERRIBLE AND HER TESTS WILL DEFINITELY OWN YOU. MAKE SURE YOU SUCK UP TO HER

Be prepared 90% of the homework you will have to teach yourself as she teaches it the day it is due or after. Her tests are absolutely horrible, bordering on sadistic. There is also only 1 crib sheet for every test (including the final).  Learn to love the book as you will write in it a lot in order to put everything relevant to the test somewhere.

Prof. Maniatty is very passionate about the subject.  Explained the topics well, but there were still a few instances of not fully understanding a topic before doing the homework. Tests are similar to the practice exams but for some reason seemed to get more complicated than the practice exam in a sadistic sort of way.  The worksheets have no value

Previous ratings on this professor are far too critical. Professor Maniatty is quite good at teaching this course. Her notes are very clear and she posts all of them online. Go to class and pay attention, this class will not be very difficult. Plus, all of her tests are alike. Best of all, you will really learn the material from this professor.

Classes are long, and she sometimes starts writing stuff where you don't know where it came from.  However, her tests are extremely easy because she never changes problems from previous years.  All homework and worksheet solutions can be found from previous years, and all of the problems are identical.

This professor is absolutely brutal.  She made me want to get out of Mechanical Engineering.  I pray to God that the rest of my ME courses/profs at RPI are not as horrific as her.  Please find employment elsewhere, lady.
Pretty bad teacher.   From what i hear you can find allot better people to do the job

Don't bother asking for help.. ever.  Consider yourself alone in this course, basically you are going to teach yourself in this class.  Asking her for help is like asking the devil for candy... not going to happen.  Just give up the teaching thing and be that great engineer that hides from the world in pile of paperwork.

Her class is incredibly boring.  Lots of notes to copy, some of which she seems to make up on the fly and is incorrect.  Very poor social skills; often she will pause and just stare at the students for a while.  Clears her throat in possibly the most annoyiing way possible.  Vicious grader - only scale is that she will make the highest grade a 100.
No Comments

Maniatty shouldn't be a professor... she doesn't have what it takes to teach college students... she needs to just be a mechanical engineer and that's it.  I go to her office hours, I work hard, and she did nothing for me.  Plus that she's extremely cold and unfriendly.
incredibly boring... did not learn a thing from lectures

Her lectures are awful and boring. She has given out incorrect info. Everygroup did somethign wrong and all did it the same way... We want to put her as a source of error on our reports. She says there's no curve and the TA this semester is brutal at grading lab reports (worth 50% of grade).
Pretty boring class ... but she is smart & the tests aren't that bad if you're not a complete idiot ... I like her
This class isn't fun, but it's not her fault.  Everyone one says she's an awful lecturer, I disagree.  She just need to do some example problems.
she sucks all life out of the material.  tests are not easy.

Someone PLEASE nominate her for "What Not to Wear"! No fashion sense whatsoever, its funny, she tries to dress up for the first day. You have to be self motivated to do well in her class, 'cause she doesnt collect most hw.  I dropped the course.
Exams are fair, problems similar to the homework.  She is helpful at office hours. Not easy, but reasonable.  She is not an exciting lecturer, but gives the important info clearly.
She looks really passive, but don't let her fool you, she really DOESN'T have a personality.  oh and her tests suck.

Everyone knows him and everyone likes him. An incredibly smart person with SO MUCH experience. Can tell you everything about anything. Also funny and easygoing and does not expect unrealistic things from students. Would always recommend taking a class with him.
A hard course but extra credit up to 10% could be applied if you manage to get a license for some kind of engineering tools. Test requires lots of calculation and most people could only barely finish
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Quiz every week, plus he very soft spoken- sit close. A lot of times he dosnt know what hes doin.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Best professor I've ever had. Great stories,sometimes relevant to class. I wouldn't say the course is easy, but it is highly math based so if you learn the rules you can do most problems. Exams are very close to past years and he goes over a back exam in class. Does not get caught up in covering all mtl as long, just teaches what he can well.

I had this class a couple years ago. Now I am in a graduate program at another institution, and have a much better appreciation for Anderson's knowledge of the subject, and his rigor as to how things are really done. This is an excellent first course in spaceflight mechanics.

Very interesting class. The instructor has great stories (best part of the class is when he gets side tracked and tells one of his stories about a satellite screw up). This really should be split into two courses (too much material)
A very tough class, but he did much better than the prior instructor. He likes his math and emphasizes understanding. He needs to do more examples. Too little time and too much material
My favorite prof. He is very clear in his teaching. Keeps the class interesting by telling us the practical use of the material. Do the homework, study for tests, you should do fine.

I've taken three classes from this guy so far.  Best professor I've had -- by a long shot.  Makes everything interesting and has some amazing stories.  Worked in the field -- so he's not strictly academic.  Absolutely brilliant, great at teaching, and always VERY helpful with any problems a student may have.
This guy is the best IEA teacher. Very clear with the examples and really cares about the students.

Incredibly thorough. Does a lot of problems in class. Shows you multiple ways to do each problem, and generally lets you use the method that you are most comfortable with. He won't tell you exactly whats on the tests like some other profs would. very helpful in office hours, but be prepared to spend time if you ask him a question.

Find a way to do the problems that makes sense to you- not necessarily the method he uses. Be prepared to spend about an hour if you ask him for help with a problem. The course itself is setup a bit strangely. Uses "interesting" terminology.
Very good professor. Works problems and tells why and how thing done in real world. He was clear and willing to help.

He's tough but he works out detailed problems in class, so you can learn how to do it out, not just theory.  You will learn the material with him better than with anyone else.  Very helpful in office hours.

Really interesting class. The professor always tried to relate material to real world experience, but this caused him to deviate from the book some what. The course really needs to be be split in to two courses which cover a year
No Comments
Excellent professor. Taught how to solve problems in general, not with tricks. He should write his own book because what he does is so different than how the book does it (Better).

Probably the best professor I have ever had. Made a difficult subject clear and interesting. My expericence with his undergraduate research was also great. He shows much more interest in the students than other professors at RPI.
Explains everything very clearly. Great teacher and very helpful.
he explanes everything verywell, starting with the derivations and going from there. very streight forward, very clear. he is the best teacher for dynamics and has an honest love of the subject.
Very clear and relates material to real life application and experience. Probably the best professor I have ever had at RPI
Really good professor, if you like professors that do examples all during class, pick him.  He's a really reasonable guy and speaks english!

Made the subject very easy to understand.  Taught general cases that worked for every situation and helped set up homework problems in class.  Some classes got boring because it was the same method every time.  Not his fault though -- he taught with great clarity.
Teaches General Cases, one of the best teachers I've ever had
Explains the material and derivations verry clearly. Uses general formulas to make problem solving much easier than Prof. Scarton's methods. Excellent professor.

Do not take this class with another professor if Anderson is an option. His inthusasm in and out of class is contagious. He gets you intersted in the material and is willing to work with you until you get it. Young, Enthusastic, Organized, Helpful, Understanding. GREAT PROFESSOR!!!
Great Professor!!!! He works very hard to make material clear and understandable.
He explains everything clearly and puts it into a real world prespective.
Great professor. He explains the subjsct thouroughly and makes it seem easy. Much much better than Scarton.

Very good Professor. Probably the best I have ever had. He works very hard to make a difficult subject uderstandable. Bashes the book. He is willing to spend as much time as it takes to help a student
Great guy.  Very thorough and makes mincemeat of the book.  A little flaky, but very intelligent.  He was understanding about the tough course load too.  Whatever you do, don't get Scarton.

biggest goon ever... he is just plain uninteresting... it is impossible to sit in his class and learn because you are too busy thinking about how much you cant stand being in the same room with the guy... says the same thing over and over and over and OVER AND OVER... terrible professor
This guy is a ROBOT...talks and thinks like one. Not very helpful unless you speak "robot" language also. Take Dymanics with a different teacher (or at a different school bc Scarton sucks too)
One of the best in his field.  Very helpful.  Makes a very hard class clear and easy to understand.
Professor Anderson is one of the best you'll come by at RPI. He is gifted as a teacher and will make an effort far beyond what is required of him.
Very Clear, and explains things well. Exactly opposite of Scarton
He's the best there is!
Excellent Professor - Brilliant in getting the material through to us
Really Clear & Fair workload
Quite possibly the worst prof I've had in 4 years of Aero/Mech.

A really awesome teacher, he makes dynamics lots of fun and loves feedback. Always there to help if you have questions, even if it's on homework due right then.  He loves students to do well and encourages them. Only teaches in the fall at the moment.

Eventhough this class is one of the most challenging for engineering majors, with professor anderson it's the most interesting class, you learn a lot with him, and from him. I can say that he is by far the best dynamics professor. BTW Scarton is the worst
Probably one of the best engineering professors i've had. Plus, a graduate of UC Berkeley!!!!!
One of the best professors I've had, although I'd recommend him more for dynamics than EMD.
Really cool prof. He's cynical to the point of hilarity
good dude
No Comments

Best professor at RPI. He is super funny and actually engaging. He genuinely cares about what he does and his textbook is free!!!!!!! Attendance is not mandatory but highly required due to the pop quizzes but they're so easy as long as you read the short textbook pages. He is amazing and genuinely a caring kind professor w/ dad jokes.
He is a really good teacher, one of the best classes I took. It helped me a lot with my public speaking skills.

--took 2340--
Excellent professor. Very kind and honest, earned a ton from him-- he takes this job more like coaching for success and it works really well. Not too hard, and a very enjoyable class. 10/10 would take again, he's one of my favorite professors here.

Prof Hiland is my favorite professor at this school. I took Intro to Comm Theory and Speech Communication with him.  He is first of all very knowledgeable on the subjects but is also really open to discussing and debating with students. He makes sure that his students are actually learning, and every assignment is useful. 100% recommend.

He insists we call him "AL," and he's the funniest dude at RPI. His lectures are good for Public Speaking, and he will actually help you become a better speaker if you put in the effort. He grades based on your capabilities, so he will grade fairly with everyone. Only downside is that there are pop quizzes based on a textbook, but are always easy.

Dr. Allard is so kind and awesome. She definitely is under appreciated in the Business department. Class is relatively easy if you show up and do what is asked. One exam ( study!!!), and a final group project are the bulk of the grade. She will be generous, but don't take advantage of that fact. Not a ton of assignments but each is weighted heavy

This class gives the appearance that it's going to be easy, then your whole class bombs both the quiz and exam because it is simply impossible to study for. You'll be asked to buy a textbook that you won't want to read, but that's the only way to even get some of the exam information. Forcing it for a 2 credit class.

I had PD3 over summer arch. Follow the readings and lecture slides to pass the quizzes. There is a writing assignment but she'll give you full points as long as you follow the rubrics given. You'll have a couple representations but she is a lenient grader. She's quick to provide written feedback on papers and is very approachable.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Group projects--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: She is a saint. Only thing that made IED tolerable. Always excited to teach, very engaging and helpful.

The only thing that made PD1 even more of a joke that it was to begin with was the fact that she takes it so seriously! It's like student orientation all over again with all the activities, except this time you get graded for it.
I agree with the poster below.
She does her best with the material. I only wish she didn't take it as seriously as she does. She has to realize that we all think the material is pretty ridiculous.
Excellent teacher, very involved with her students.  You should have fun taking a class with her.
The class is really boring but it's easy to get an A if you do the reading and take notes.  She's a nice person but the material just isn't very interesting.

Tajer is great in explaining the material. The class is fast paced. There are weekly assignments. Calculators are not allowed in the exams, but you can have crib sheets. He is also nice and care genuinely. Provides extensive material (course notes and slides).

Tajer's a nice professor, but his lectures aren't the greatest, mainly because he doesn't go too into depth with any of the material, especially some of the math, and the class moves at a pretty quick pace, meaning you'll need to learn most of it on your own. The class isn't easy, but it is definitely doable, asnd it is curved (70 was a B).

ECSE 2500 with Professor Tajer was an unenjoyable experience. His lectures are difficult to follow along with, and he breezes through harder math topics without much useful feedback when students raise a hand. It is very difficult to get a hold of him outside of class time. His exams are harsh with a short time limit and no calculator or crib sheet
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He seems like a very nice and good person but speaks very softly. Primarily reads his lecture slides with little to no additions, so the lecture feels kind of useless. The exams were much harder than hws/ example problems; the average for exam 1 was 40%. And with each exam weighing 40% of your grade, you need to do well on them.
Homework is hard and exams are even harder. Questions on exams are totally novel, which are all created by the professor.

Professor Tajer is very clear and detailed with helpful feedback. At the end of each exams and of the course he provides indepth feedback and potential future paths. His tests and homework are more than just memorization of the concept but rather analysis and applying what has been found.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Excessive amounts of work are expected to be done on the homework. Lectures do not prepare you for the questions that are asked. Questions asked on Piazza are usually not answered usefully.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Dr. Tajer's lecture are clear and understandable. He is able to make the purely new and complex materials easier to make sense although it is a very tough course. He gives good feedback, after 1st midterm he said we are strongly recommended to attend lectures according to the statistics he made about our grades. He kept inspiring us to improve.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: He's fine... I guess. His lectures are mediocre and often lack details needed for the homework. In my opinion his feedback needs improvement. He often answers questions with "We went over it in lecture" to the point I wonder why he even bothers responding. I feel he could condense the 2 homework assignments a week into one longer one. Overall okay.

I think that the professor is the one who made this course as great as it was. While it was very challenging, the professor was not only gracious in evaluation, but also very accessible and very good at explaining the concepts.

wrote aggressive emails to the entire class. used the projecting device to project her notes to class. it was hard to read. did not like explaining things again. got upset for minuscule things. rebukes students who are even a minute late. refused to provide solutions to exams or even for past homework. avoid.

We dont have anonymous midterm evaluations so we cant voice our concerns during the semester. I honestly regret taking this class with her as my free elective. She needs to take a class on passive-aggressive behavior (its no longer microaggression). Save your happiness and choose another elective.

One of the most disrespectful professors I have ever encountered at RPI. I'm really upset with how she treats students (extremely unprofessional over email). Sending her an email only results in an out-front aggressive response back to you. She does not create a welcoming learning environment in the Risk Analytics class. Do not take as elective!

Gupta is the absolute worst. She is someone who shouldn't teach. No slides, just scratchy notes written on chalkboard/projector. No examples ever gone over in class but expects you to be able to do everything. Class is weeks behind because she is extremely disorganized. Does not explain a single thing. If you don't need to take a class w her DON'T.

I am a BA student and I need to take financial modeling for fnce requirement. However, this prof talked in class that those BA students who dropped the class 'do a good thing' because it is better for QFRA students. I will never give her any respect.
Exams were hard, with no review material provided. Class was confusing and mess

Gupta is a good professor. She does not come from a business background so there are few practical examples. She is very organized and seems to have every minute of every lecture planned. The RM exams are difficult. She applied a curve to the final which pushed me to an A. The two projects are a bit vague, but going to her office helped.
Talks constantly throughout slides, does not respond well to questions.  Inconsistent grading methods.  Takes attendance by using busy work sheets every class.

Don't be fooled by the "bad" icon.  I took MAU in Sp2007 with her, and it wasn't nearly as bad as these comments claim. MAU, will be a hard and annoying class, but she made it less of this than my friends w/ Malaviya experienced.  Gupta has much better organization and made sure you knew how to use the Minitab software. If she is a choice, take it.
sHE IS VERY BRILLIANT

It's true she doesn't always clarify stuff in class very well, but this class is so easy that you can figure it out yourself or with friends. Tests, homework, and quizzes are all reasonable if you pay a minor amount of attention. She was very accommodating when I had to miss class and a test because of sickness.

Worst professor that I've dealt with at RPI.  She gave awful lectures that made no sense, and when someone asked her to clarfiy examples, she pretty much yelled at them and told them to read the text and understand it for themself.  Work load and exams much harder than in other MAU sections. Don't expect an A with this woman.
Horrible.  She is unclear and just talks during the slides and assumes that you understand what is going on.  She doesn't explain any of the topics and her examples are terrible.

What he said.  This woman has no concept of teaching to the students.  She just speaks through all the slideshows she manages to come up with and thinks the material makes sense since it makes sense to her.  Her in class examples are worthless and she gives you a pretty needless attitude most of the time. Just read the book during class and smile.
She has a way of making the simplest thing look like the hardest problem of your life, when you take MAU stay clear if you want to pass.
horrible intructor, you best bet is to not go to class and read the book.  All she does is confuse you

Too much theory, and not enough hands on work. Never wanted to give, or work through examples. Piled on the course work, projects leading right into an exam. Too much overlapping of assignments. Handouts were terrible, could not read. Felt that I could have learned better without going to class.
No Comments
Extremely difficult to learn from.  Hw was ridiculous and the online program hw was given on was very buggy.
She is extremly difficult and just cannot teach.  She gives huge amounts of hw, more than any other professor in the course and relys on a faulty computer system to grade them.
Used real world examples and insight not just textbook cases.  Definitely the real deal not just an academic...

Awesome guy. I'd take a class with him again in a heartbeat. Even though the class was at 8 am I had no trouble paying attention to this guy. Grades everything fairly and distributes grade percentages evenly between tests, projects, etc.

This guy is legit. Real-world examples. Spontaneous yet relevant examples. Fair grader (this is a good thing). Tests are based on in-class discussion and PowerPoint. He ends class earlier frequently too. Just wonderful.
Fair, reasonable.  Knows stuff.  Good use of outside material / cases / discussion.
Doesn't hod your hand, but is fair.  Knows his stuff.
Great Professor. Uses real life cases to justify text book lessons. Tests are easy, BACK TESTS are key!!

One of those teachers where you'll never understand his justification for grading on the projects, or maybe I do (The Hockey players get A's for goofing off, and the rest of the class gets C's to make it look even).
Test are based off the text book, not a bad class, fun teacher.

Lectures were full of errors and he spent more time deriving complex equations than explaining theory. Office hours were profoundly unhelpful, as he was condescending and dismissive. Tests were very difficult and unrelated to the lectures. He should not be allowed to teach anymore. Text-to-speech of the textbooks would do a better job.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: My guide to getting an A in funflight: Try doing the homework on your own. It's okay to refer to the online answer guide, but be sure you're not using it as a crutch.  Back tests are available and super useful from the APO office and there's a few online if you look hard enough.  Go to office hours to ask for clarifications.

Took Fun Flight with him last semester. The tests are pretty tough the average was always in the D range. Just pay attention in class and make sure you understand all the homework don't just copy it from the answer key. Go to his office hours if you don't understand certain material, he is actually really helpful and a nice guy.

Overall, Professor Amitay was very good for Fun. Flight. Tests are difficult and you must write EXACTLY what he mentioned in class to get full credit. Luckily, he curves the class average to a B. Otherwise, the average would be around a C-D+. Homework was pretty straightforward if you read the book beforehand. He is very helpful to talk to.
He really knows what he's talking about

Idk what that other kid is talking about but this is not a very well taught class. It feels like physics classes from high school in the sense that you just get equations without a real intuitive understanding. He assigns problem from the book that end up having problems that lack either correct answers,and assumptions that don't make sense forsome

Best professor ever! He teaches really well so if you pay attention and do the homework you're going to do well in funflight. His notes are ten times better than the textbook. He condenses material but his explanations cover everything you need to know. He's very approachable for help in funflight.

His class lacks the freedom of a good design course.  He purports to let the design be up to the student, however that's a lie.  Frequently our design was dictated by what might get him more research funding.  Also, Miki never has a clue what progress (or lack thereof) his undergrads have made.  Very close-minded about projects for a researcher.
Amitay was a good professor for IEA. The subject material was hard to grasp at times, but he always walked around asking you personally if you understood what was going on.
The best place to get an A. He himself also doesn't know the subject very well!
Great guy, offered guidance where needed, and was eager to learn what the students had to contribute.
He gave me an A, which is all that matters
Very easy to learn from.
No Comments
It's only IED but she taught the PD1 parts of it. I like that she takes the time to learn everyone's name, it gives a nice personal touch and makes it seem like she cares for students to do well

Professor Youmans is one of the most understanding and kind professors I have ever had the pleasure of meeting. If you have a choice between two professors to take a class with the other professor's skills and ratings are irrelevant. Take it with Professor Youmans and you will be happy you did.
Prof Youmans was amazing for PD3! She understands the material well and teaches it in a fun manner.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: She is a lovely person, but her lecturing ability left a little to be desired.  Her lectures were always under time, which was nice, but I would have liked a little more in-depth explanation.  When I went to her office hours, she was very cordial and patient, which is her most redeeming quality.  Her tests were variable in difficulty as well.

Aminian  is a nice person, but she isn't a very good professor. She really just reads the textbook for an hour. Regardless, calc 2 is easy and her tests are simple. just go to recitation and skip the lectures.

I thought she was very nice but her lectures were dry. Most of differential equations was explaining how to get the formulas you needed. Let you have equation sheets. Overall I thought the class was good.

Probably the worst math professor I've ever had. She's nice and everything but she does a horrible job teaching. She speaks very softly and her lectures are very dry. Don't bother going to the lectures cuz she'll just confuse you. She doesn't help much in office hours. I never went to class, just for the tests which were not bad.

I'm fairly certain she only taught the course because Prof. Reubenfield died a month before semester started. Regardless, I regret ever having gone to her class. It's boring, dry, she can't teach basic concepts (her description of a function was two circles with arrows pointing from one to the other). Avoid unless you already know the material.
most boring professor ever

Professor Aminian teaches lectures very thoroughly. She goes through every step painstakingly slow. But, if you want to learn, she certainly provides you with a wealth of information. Calculus tests are extremely easy, mandatory (for a good grade) weekly quizzes are bothersome.

My friend just posted a review of her and I agree. She's probably a nice person, but her training in CS is very limited and I find it hard to believe she has a Ph.D. Fortunately, the other RPI profs more than make up for her.

I can understand where the previous opinions are coming from, but this professor is not that bad. Yes, she isn't very clear sometimes, but you should still try to understand/learn the material before you judge her. You can be more in control of your grade in this class than you think, especially since the exams are easy. Just put in some effort!

Very unclear. On the first day, for example, she wrote on the chalkboard in something only somewhat larger than normal handwriting, so I couldn't read it even from the third row with my glasses on. She went on to fix this issue, but there were still consistent problems with her class.

Her lectures are usless, she takes the most round about and confusing method to explain concepts. She only used book examples. If we didn't have a quiz nearly every lecture, i don't think anyone would attend.

Consistently leaves out important exam pertinent information, completely skipped over propellor theory just giving us notes, and refused to let me see my quiz that was clearly unfairly graded. His TA Nate Karwic is also probably the worst TA I have ever encountered by a mile. Highly recommend taking this class with Hously.

Great professor inside and outside of classroom. Reads emails and answers them thoroughly if you have questions about exam topics. Exams are based on lecture materials and sometimes taken directly from lecture notes. Obviously everyone's experience is different but many people in my grade, me included, always found him approachable.

Lectures are always amazing, so you should attend. Exams are homework heavy, don't cheat and go to office hours for homework questions and you will be good. Very reasonable grading policy and very understanding professor.

Great guy, very knowledgeable about the source material but always humble. Actively works with students to line up office hours with their schedules and arrange review sessions. Always willing to answer any questions about source material. Can sometimes get sidetracked during lecture, but never fails to cover all of the material in depth.

Hirsa is a great professor, he takes the time to make sure the students understand what is going on in the class and encourages people to learn. I've had him for PropSys & Aerodynamics and would take more of his classes if I could. Extremely knowledgeable, and very accessible and willing to help outside of class time.

I do not understand all of the heat he is getting. His lectures are very interesting and I feel like he is one of the few professors I have had that really care about the subject matter. He seems very nice and approachable although I have not had to approach him that much.

Professor Hirsa is one of the worst professors I have ever had. He spends the entire lecture rambling about subjects at best tangentially related to what will be expected on HW and tests. He also "does proofs" in a rushed and useless way instead of examples. Take any other professor.
The worst professor to work with. He changes the goal for his research students and burden them. He is incapable of attracting new students.

Hirsa's lectures are often confusing because he doesn't know how to deliver the material and he often gets sidetracked. His tests are very straightforward. If you do the homework (without copying/cheating), review the lecture notes, and sometimes  consult the textbook for clarification (it happens) then a good grade is easy to get.

Prof. Hirsa was a decent professor for Aerodynamics 1. Lecture notes are useful but lectures themselves are a bit dull. He is very accessible outside of class and is very concerned with his students' performance. Tests are very fair and are based off of the notes. Homework does a good job of assessing subject material.

Prof. Hirsa is a very motivated guy. He likes to teach but at the same time expects you to figure out more after class. His tests can be trivial but not necessarily hard. Overall he knows his stuff pretty good and definitely helpful.
Great teacher, can relate the material to the real-world. Tests are very difficult! Grades fairly though.
he is the man. I really enjoyed every single thing ..
Amir you are my bald jesus.

Had him for Thermal and Fluids 1. Great professor for the subject. He knows his stuff, and really cares for his students, and does his best to make sure everyone is on the same page. Generous grader. Overall one of the best professor's i've ever had at RPI. Cheers Amir!

(thermo 2 lab) He's scatterbrained, nervous, and rushed in his explanations. In short, not a great teacher. He relies on handouts in class instead of a textbook, so you have to go to class.  His quizzes pick out very precise things, so you have to memorize even the unimportant stuff.  His exams were not too hard.  get someone else if possible.

Very eager. I found him not that personable/helpful out of class. His 'Q&A' sessions are useless. Tries to get too many topics in one semester. Tests can be obscure but not brutal. Seems to be a fair grader. Whatever book he assigns for the class, put it on your shelf and get Elements of Gas Turbines by Mattingly. That is THE book for prop sys.

I have no idea how someone thought he was a jerk. Very approachable. One of the friendliest, best, and hardest working professors ive had. At RPI its rare to find a professor in the engineering field who really cares about the undergrad teaching part but he really does and he is a good prof.  Hard class, but it is rocket science what do you expect?
too anxious
His class was ok, but he's kind of a jerk out of class.
[Incompressible Flow] Very good professor and lecturer, but the class is HARD, especially the final exam. He'll fit a lot of topics into one semester so make sure you don't fall behind.
he can explain to u very clearly but he's damn painstaking..that's the problem..

Grade is composed of 4 tests, each one counts 25%. Tests are online and open notes- yet the time constraint makes it very tricky. Make sure to attend lectures and read the chapters ahead of time. Plus, Estrella is very interesting- I enjoyed listening to his stories from working at the Federal Reserve.
caring
This guys is the man. Really successful economist, ask him about what he did with his life before RPI. Class is tough. Get ready to grind and make sure you read the textbook.
Attending macro requires a lot of caffeine, but Estrella is extremely knowledgable so you get a lot out of it. The tests are pretty easy too.

This guy is ridiculously boring. He does not post his lectures online claiming that they are based on the book. He refers you to the Mankiw website where you can find student presentations which are generally more helpful. Exams are multiple choice and can be vague but overall are not hard.
One of the Best Professors, very clear about what he teach
Boring as hell, but a good professor.

Hands out packets every class so you're just filling in missing information not full notes. He's very thorough when lecturing, really cares about his students, has a good sense of humor and grades fairly. The tests are difficult, but it's a difficult class. Class is def mandatory though. He knows EVERYONE, and also doesn't put announcements on LMS.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: Aram is a great guy and really cares about the success of each one of his students. He will accommodate your schedule for office hours and is very helpful when you go to them.  You must show up to class bc he knows everyone's name and will know if you are absent.  He is very clear and will teach the class at whatever pace works best for the student

Intelligent and accomplished professor. Tries and succeeds at making the class interesting by adding a few cool demos. Tough grading criteria, but if you really want to learn thermals and fluids, take his class.  Truly wants his students to succeed.

He is one of the nicest guys you'll meet and he always tries to engage the students and be funny. He made thermals interesting. It was a little rough at the beginning because he was brand new but once he got into it his lectures were pretty good. He is fair and will not give you ridiculous tests. I enjoyed the class.
Such a great class!
tough course, excellent professor

Extremely prepared for class and organized during lecture.  Goes the full 2 hrs with no break (EVER).  Attendance optional.  Homeworks can be a bit tricky and no matter how much you think about them will not always get the right answers.  Tests were way harder than the homeworks.  Course was tricky, but professor was very fair and did a great job.
Extremely competent teacher, very clear and helpful. But the material was pretty difficult for an intro-level course.
is very helpful when you ask for it. the class was harder than expected. he spoke clearly and enjoys the subject he teaches very much.

This was a pretty tough course,  but worthwhile. The professor was  actually pretty clear and helpful,  his notes were very good, and he  always made time to meet with  students and help them. The homeworks  were tough but very instructive. I learnt a lot from the course,  and would recommend it, but be  warned that it's a lot of work.

Avoid this professor! Nearly half the class dropped right before the drop deadline. He may know his stuff, but he is a TERRIBLE teacher. He also didn't really seem to pay attention or care if people cheat on exams discreetly... so... take that as you will...
He is the best teacher I've ever seen. He is nice and explains things very well!

Definitely the best out there. This guy explains the material REALLY well, and he was patient to make sure that the students understand. Really helpful, in class and in tests. he is one of the rare occasions that'll make you enjoy undergrad at rpi.
Very clear in explaning concepts. Very patient as well. More importantly, very knowledgeable. He's the best prof i have had, both in my home university as well as in RPI.
I had him for Thermals and Fluids. He explains everything really well and is really helpful outside of class
The best prof in RPI. he really helps people in understanding a problem. go ask him questions during an exam and he'll answer

I had him for Dynamics. Assad is the man! Very clear in explanation of new concepts, and deriving formulas. He's pretty neat, and has a bit of an accent, but he speaks very good english, and was probably one of the most articulate professor's i've had here. He has a heart, and curves the final grades generously (at least he did for me).
Nice guy, comes around and makes sure u know how to do the in-class questions
Go to class. Go to office hours. Likes it when students participate in lecture. Go to extra help when available.

Easily one of the best professors at RPI. Truly cares about his students, if the lecture isn't going well, he will back track and go over material again. He will spend as much time as you need in office hours.  Tough course, people fail, he tries to make sure that doesn't happen.

Strength of materials is a difficult class, no matter what professor you have.  Attary does his best to help you.  His sections score the highest on the exams.  Ask questions in class, if you don't understand something, ASK IT!  Strengths builds on previous material.

His section had the highest average with a 52100. Decided not to curve the second test and instead told the class to "just do good on the final." Instead of explaining examples during lectures he likes to force students to solve them and then laughs when they struggle.  If attendance wasn't a grade no one would bother going.
His sections always scored significantly higher on the exams, which says it all.
He is endorsing grammarly solid lad, 10/10
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Inspirational--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Audrey is great! She's fun and nice and quirky. Her assignments don't really have clear-cut criteria for grading, but it's easy to figure out what she wants and cater your work to her expectations. Turn in a first draft and she'll tell you exactly what to do to get an A. Just use Helvetica and you'll be fine. The class talks are really interesting.
She is very tough with grading and sometimes ambiguous with her feedback in class. But if you see her during office hours she is very helpful, and it will help your final grade. Great professor!
Awesome Professor. Gives really good feedback for future projects and jobs outside of the classroom.

Her critiques are harsh, which isn't necessarily a bad thing, but when combined with the arbitrariness of everything she says, her (typography) class can become disorienting and frustrating. Work that otherwise looks impressive she dismisses, while simultaneously applauding obviously rushed and ameuter work as if it's avant garde.

Great professor -- teaches visual design the way it goes in design schools (tough critique, minimal direction), so can be a surprise to some students who aren't used to that.  Really challenges your use of software and design principles.  For the best results, take it seriously when she says you should physically sketch things on paper first.
I learned alot in Typography but her playing favorites every class was sickening!
She lacks the mathematical skills required to compute grades correctly. Very knowledgable about design; completely incompetent in her duties as a Professor.

definately has favorites, if you aren't one you will hear every little detail wrong with your project while her favorites hear nothing but omg how far you've come, wow that just looks wonderful. she never emails you back and sometimes claims that the emails were lost, and her office hours are so not compatible with students time.
No Comments

Horrible professor. Not everyone's papers should look exactly the same. Definetly has favorites, they can do the****tiest work, but still get more praise than the best projects. During "design studios" she grades your projects, and says she doesn't have time to speak with you. grrrr

She is the worst professor I've ever had. She has rediculous design principles, her critiques are terrible and miss the mark, and she has no clue how to use the software she should be teaching. I dropped the class because I was actually getting dumber.
You have no idea where you stand with her. She'll give the impression that you're doing great in the class, but then zing you at the end if she doesn't like you.
She has her favorites and seems to cater to them - anyone else has to wait for her time and attention. Totally frustrating at times.
Very good designer and professor, has ease in getting point across.
Audrey is a very talented designer and is a wonderful and helpful professor.
No Comments
No Comments
No Comments

Great professor. I have now taken her for 3 classes specifically because she teaches them. She leads an open discussion in the class and manages to maintain kindness while questioning your inner logic. She is a great PDII professor, but if you can, take her for other classes. They are filled with other engaged students and her style works better.

Took her class during the fall of 2023. Such an amazing PDII prof. She cares about your education and is very engaging in class. Not too much reading and there is one paper and presentation that makes up most of the grade. She comes off extremely strong which I liked but I know some of my peers did not.

Hirsa is one of the few professors that care about your education. She makes the classroom a fun and engaging environment. She does make you think a little harder than surface level but it is worth it.

Hirsa was nice but her PD2 is definitely the hardest one. The grading of the papers, done by the worst TA I've had, was very unfair. Weekly discussion board assignments get old very quickly and aren't helpful, just busy work. However, the in-class discussions in this class were amazing and honestly very valuable.

This lady deserves a better class than PDII offers her. I love her style of teaching, involving everyone in discussion during class. She's incredibly fair and lenient on grading. Put in decent amount of work and you'll get a good grade. She likes to probe what you know so be prepared to explain yourself. Overall an awesome class.
He rounds down grades even on the cutoff.
Pretty good lecturer
Take his courses if you really want to learn things.

The absolute worst lecturer I've ever had. He is the king at rambling while bringing in no context about the problem, and if you attempt to ask a question; he appears to take offense to it, as though it is blatantly obvious what he's talking about. He is, without a doubt, brilliant, and extremely talented. But he is horrific at teaching.
If you take this course, expect your grade to be a C+. But hey, you will learn a ton regardless!

Occasionally accidentally condescending but a good lecturer. Exams are hard and Kapila does not believe in curving exam scores, even when the median score is a 53. Hard class but potentially very rewarding.

Kapila is one of the best professors that I have had. You can tell that he genuinely cares about his students and will put forth the effort to make sure that you learn the material. He will go out of his way to help you. He is also one of the most difficult professors that I have had, but that ensures that you know the material inside and out.

Kapila loves to talk low and rapid fire his lectures. His hand writing is so awful that he manages to make his x's, y's and z's look identical. Rather than focusing on doing examples that are relevant to the homeworks/tests, he gives general proofs that can easily be looked up. The class is largely self taught and tests are way harder than practice

Took Num Comp with him over the summer, and it was one of the better classes I've taken at rpi. He was always very well prepared and well spoken, and posted typeset notes online after every lecture. 10/10 would recommend
Boring, quiet speaker. Notes are dense class moves fast. Homeworks take a while and come from his head. Use office hours and read the notes or book. Stay on top of it and you will pass
Good pace in lectures, incomplete notes, read textbook for homework. Do homework carefully or lose points for no reason

He's a clear and motivated lecturer, and he sometimes banters (well) with students.  It can get a bit dry by the second hour of class, but the material tends to be pretty interesting. He produces and distributes LaTeX versions of his lecture notes, and they're better than the textbook.  Review these and the homework solutions to succeed on tests.

I had already taken BC Calculus (The AP equivalent to this class), so I knew most of the material already. Kapila is an insanely hard grader! He did not curve any of our tests, even when the class average was below a 60%. That being said, If you really pay attention and complete the practice exams he gives you, you can do really well in this class.
Kapila is a wonderful professor who will do his utmost to make sure you learn. He offers plenty of extra credit but his tests are HARD. You will learn whether or not you want to.

The teaching style of this professor is very intuitive. He expects students to show the same intuition during the exam. If you want to do well in the class, you must understand all the material thoroughly. Read all the notes he gives and understand them.

Teaches the material well but is dependent on a particular learning style in order to be clear. Test and homework was challenging but accurately reflected the material needed. Expects a high quality of work from students and those that don't put in the time won't do well. Best thing to happen to Num Comp.

His material was hard and lectures were such a bore, but I can say that I learned a lot.  Not only that but his tests were nearly exactly the same as the tests from previous years, all he did was change some numbers.  Again, hard but will learn a lot and get a good grade if you prepare.

He goes through information a bit too fast and does not seem to teach. Use the textbook to learn the lessons. Try to read his handwriting in class, but it is a bit sloppy. Test questions can be anything. Do the sample tests, and review the homework. You will need to work in groups for matlab.

I began the semester with high regard for him. It fell with the weeks, realizing his overly methodical and unintuitive lectures left me confused often. The book is key, and I certainly recommend looking at other books to gain more insight on a topic when you're attempting to do the homework that often does not totally correspond to the book.
Very hard and bad for average clac I class. he does theory more than examples. good for math and physics majors, not for average engineer. hard tests and does not prepare enough examples
As per below, avoid at all costs.
HE"S SO MEAN! he likes to pick on sleeping kids in class and he grades really harsh!!!

Avoid this guy at all costs.  He is the kind of guy that would drop a nuke on a small town....Overkill...Calc 1, which I received in A at a state university, has turned into my arch nemesis.  His exams are 40% no partial credit, then the rest is impossible.  Class average on exams floats around 60-63%, which is a D by the way.  Take Dr. Blue

Excellent professor. He runs a very strict class, but in the end you really learn the material. He always takes time to help his students IF you seek him out. His class is a lot of work, but it will teach the material very well and give you a sense of accomplishment upon completion of his class (if you do the assigned work. The TA is another story.

Kapila's an awesome professor with good English.  He's very difficult, but he will explain things clearly and concisely.  He's very fair with homework and grading, but tests are tough.  It takes effort, but you'll walk out of his class knowing the topic inside and out.  I reccomend him if you're not taking math for easy A's and you want to learn.
The most polished prof ever. Thoroughly enjoying his class.
The hardest class I have ever taken. Kapila is a good professor; he explains the material well and is generally fair. However, the grading is so tough it'll make you cry.
No Comments

I have an A in every Math class I have taken before and after Calc 2 with him.  I got a C in his class because his homeworks are impossible and so are his tests.  No way will you get a curve either.  Do not take this man ever.

This guy is a fantastic prof.  The only thing I could complain about is the hair on his knuckles (you can see it on the overhead projector!) Seriously, he is very knowledgable and very clear in his explanations.  He demands quality work from his students, which some professors overlook.

His Maple labs are great.. you really learn how to use the software, and apply the concepts.  Calc 2 maple quizzes are a joke compared to this guy's labs. His final's kind of hard, but overall I learned a lot from his class, even though I already knew calc well coming into the class.
The best professor ever.  He knows how to teach.  And he cares a lot about it and knows his stuff.

Tests are easy, homework is hard, but they all make you think.  An A in Calc I is nice, but a B in Calc I special is nicer because I know that I actually learned more than most people.  A great teacher even if it is sometimes difficult.  Take this professor if you want to challenge yourself.
Impossible homework, hard quizes, and even harder tests.  Avoid at all costs, my class was full at the beginning and at the final we had a quarter of the original people in it.

The class was at 8am and everyday he would come in turn on the overhead and start writing. Sitting in the dark listening to someone monotone on about math and poor examples, what else can you do than fall asleep.The HW and test are also nearly impossible
Homework is impossible and it is weighted more than tests, avoid at all costs.
Excellent professor. Speaks English better than 99% of the population. Clear and concise.

I took him for Calc I and again for Calc II. Have to admit though if you're looking for an easy A...wrong prof. But if you really want to learn and are willing to put in some work this is it. He is a great prof !
So much homework!!!! I'm dying!!! He goes obsurdly fast too
very smart and very helpful if you attend his office hours, which i strongly suggest doing if you don't understand what was covered in class
Fairly difficult, he does not make it easy to pull an A.  He allows for students to excel if they put in the effort.

Numb comp sucks, especially when you are an undergrad AERO in a class full of grad students and math majors.  But Kapila is probably the best thing to happen to the class, and does the best anyone can probbaly do to make it tolerable
very difficult, but extremely intelligent and an awesome teacher. he forces you to think a lot.

A very strange, yet funny professor.  He is a strange little indian man with a british accent, walks around with a cowboy hat, and loves to torture students, while feigning ignorance.  If you ask him if he knows how to do something, he'll simply say no.
his class forces one to think for themselves on problems.
His lecture notes are better than the course textbook.  More practice problems would have been helpful.  Some of the homework problems required detailed knowledge of Maple.
Cool Accent, could help out a little more

He really cannot explain anything about numerical computing.  He transcribes his notes onto the projector, but doesnt really explain them.  He grades rather harsh and does not curve the course in any manner.
No Comments
Kapila = Genius
Utter genius...you come out of his class with an IQ five points higher

SLOWEST GRADER. Expect to get Exam 1 back on the day of Exam 2, 1 month at the EARLIEST. With that being said he's very fair and lenient. He relies a lot on the textbook. His lectures aren't v engaging, I would get distracted often. Beware bc sometimes he throws a crazy curveball on exams and it destroys you.
Once again the grading pace killed me.

This is probably the easiest cheme class you'll take at rpi. Baysal's lectures are fairly difficult to focus on but that was likely a me problem. The homework is easy and the best way to understand the concepts. He takes forever to grade the exams but he's a really fair grader. Also make good crib sheets, they help a lot.

He's very accommodating and knows transport well, the issue is he essentially teaches directly out of the textbook. By the end of the year, he started just reading off a pdf version of the textbook. The nice thing is he gives online tests and an optional final. It's hard to get deeper understanding of the material.

Depends entirely on textbook (just scrolls through it during lecture). The exam questions always were completely different than anything covered during class, and he will literally tell you to "go through it yourself" during lecture. One of the questions on our final exam was from one of these "don't feel like teaching it myself" sections.

Very knowledgeable professor. The Aspen program is fun to use and very logical. Get ready to work in groups, on almost everything. Lecture is boring but covers everything you need to ace the class.
