Great preparation for CRD. Not all aspects of the program that is distributed by RPI work properly. Nothing is graded until the semester ends.

Really nice guy, knows his stuff when it comes to Aspen Plus.  I learned to use the program well enough, which was the goal.  He's not very good at giving guidelines for assignments though.  We didn't get the syllabus until halfway through the course.

I love this professor. He is really funny, and I go to all of his office hours and this helps me do well on all his homework. The homework takes a while, but they directly relate to the exam, and he is always available for questions. He is so enthusiastic and truly cares. He wants everyone to understand the material and enjoy it as much as he does.

Would never take again. As difficult as CS1 very bad homeworks, very bad, that take forever and the tests are extremely difficult. Lectures are not helpful, doesn't explain concepts well, and acts like cares for students difficulties but really does not. Avoid if possible.

Took this professor for both ISYE 4600 and ISYE 4960. I did a lot better in ISYE 4600 because the content is easier. His lectures last the entirety of the hour and fifty minutes if not more. The homeworks are long. But he is a fair grader and wants to see his students do well. He gives a lot of bonus points and extra credit to help you succeed.

Professor is a complete and utter mess. I did not receive a single grade back until the end of October for the fall semester. Assignments are extremely unclear and will leave you wondering what he wants with the assignment. Half of time spent completing the assignments is deciphering what he wants. Syllabus says TBD on how we are being graded.
He is very knowledgeable and relates what you are learning to industry. He is very good at making visual aids for students and is always excited to teach.

Awful, awful professor. Failed to update grades for months at a time, leaving us completely blind to how we were doing all semester. Misgendered me constantly, despite being corrected often. Assigned ludicrous homeworks and then complained that his TAs were overworked (from all the grading) when we asked for even a shred of quality control.

EMD was super tough. He was obviously very knowledgeable about the subject but went through his 60-slide lectures way too fast. Refuses to answer questions during class, and will end the WebEx as soon as he's done without taking time for questions. Terrible at communicating through email, which is the only way we could contact him.

horrible horrible. I dont usually leave reviews but had to leave this one . Even if you understand all the information perfectly during lectures, dont worry because he will make the exams a race so youll still do badly anyways .
Lecture slides are a mess and EXTREMELY difficult to follow. Isn't clear during lectures either. Exams are a race to finish.

Lecture notes are a mess and hard to follow. Exams are poorly formatted making them even more difficult. Professor Bagepalli also actively deters students from attending office hours or asking the TAs for help, leaving us with nothing but his chaotic lecture slides.
Very thorough and clear lectures. Useful topics and he really cares about his students. Listen to him when he tells you to take notes
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Probably the worst professor I have had. The slides are extremely unorganized and the homeworks are unclear. If a question is asked during class, he will get annoyed at the student for not understanding the first time and doesn't like answering questions before or after class. I found strength of materials to be a breeze, but this is really bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The whole class is just him lecturing, and very hard to pay attention to. The slides are basically everything in the class, but are hard to follow and pretty messy. The homeworks are reasonable, but expect to have to study everything yourself.
B2 is a great professor. It is very apparent he cares about his students. His lectures are easy to understand and are paced appropriately. On top of it all, he is quite a character!

Tests are races, with performance depending more on how much practice the student has as opposed to understanding of material.  While tests are overly punishing, homework and solutions provided by the course are effective at teaching course material.  Lectures are repetitive with error-prone examples.  Attendance dropped as the semester proceeded.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Great guy with lots of experience. It's an easy class, but you learn a lot.
So good

Unlike most professors, Ballinger actually has relevant experience. He teaches through real world examples, has a good sense of humor, and is extremely inspirational. It is impossible to do poorly in his class if you put the slightest bit of effort in. Most classes are extremely fun so attending isn't even a chore.

Barb is the kindest professor I had during my time at RPI. Not only was she a great professor, but she also did a wonderful job of running the writing center, COMM+D. I learned a lot about communication & rhetoric and how to improve my writing in an environment that was incredibly comfortable and welcoming.

She cares about her students and wants them to do well. She is very lenient with deadlines and grades pretty easily. I learned enough about writing for me to get by at RPI, and I would definitely take a class with her again
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Caring

reviews.comment: There were only three papers we wrote the whole semester, and she gave plenty of time. She kept pushing deadlines back because she was late with giving feedback, haha

Professor Lewis is one of the best professors I had classes with in RPI.  She is willing to spend  time to discuss with each student after class individually.  Her class was appropriately paced and well designed that  not only helped students learn writing but also encourage them to think about their future development in career and academics.
She is a nice person. But it is hard to know what she really wants. She will negate your work in the afternoon even the presentation is tomorrow. Be ready to work big projects again and again.

Makes the course unnecessarily drag on forever. Makes you fill in tons of feedback forms for simple presentations. Course content is boring, and not challenging at all. She looks tired at times, and continues lecturing for the sake of filling class time, which makes her repeat everything uncountable times.  It is not worth the easy credits!
Shes so bad i cannot express how bad. She might be great in 05 but anymore. Shes very anal with everything she does. Thought it would be easy until I received my grades.
Great speech comp/presentation class. Brea is brilliant and will get you thinking (whether you like it or not) Not a push over. Doesn't give up on students. Loved her and the class.

She's a very good teacher that really tries to make us nerds appreciate communication and writing. And as much as RPI students hate to admit it, we need to be good writers. And Brea makes sure we get to that level. She definitely makes us work and it isn't a cake walk, but it is a class that is definitely worth taking.
She's definitely capable of becoming unclear. Sometimes the assignments are guessing games, and it sucks when you guess wrong.  Helpful course though.
doesn't take too much bull, but an enjoyable class.

Brea's fun and friendly. Some people are bored by the class, but if you're interested in writing or language it's not bad. It's usually at 8 a.m., but it's more interesting than the other option for a writing requirement.
very thorough
This class is a lot of work and a lot of writing.  She is a horrible grader.  That is all.
She's a terrible grader.
Boring class...but a real nice lady.  Easy grader
Great class!  not the easiest, but well worth the effort
Lots of papers to write, otherwise pretty easy
No Comments
Great teacher....boring class.
No Comments
No Comments
Good teacher, easy to understand, great class.
Do yourself a favor, dont mess up your gpa really really hard
No Comments
Head of the Dept for a while, kinda looked like a little weasel, very accessible to students, always around to help but that doesn't mean I learned a damn thing.

EP is great. They're a fair professor and do a fantastic job with an intro class for non-majors. The assignments are interesting and fun, and we're given adequate time to do them. Your enjoyment may vary depending on the group you're assigned, but I promise this class is a lot of fun if you put the effort into it.

EP is an excellent professor and Digital Filmmaking was one of my favorite classes! The projects and in-class exercises were fun, collaborative, and a great learning experience. I liked that we received feedback on our work in class.

EP really cares about their students and has been someone I can reach out to even after graduating.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great professor! Learned a lot in their class

ARTS-1030 is a fun class, but to succeed you will need to put in effort. Scripting, filming, and editing is a time consuming process. This is not a HASS class where you can coast with no work.

Prof. Press is very knowledgeable in her field, though her feedback and rubric requirements can often be vague, leading to some unexpectedly low grades.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: EP is quite knowledgeable about video production and does everything she can to help you with your production. IHSS-1030 is a communication-intensive course, so be prepared to write a lot! As long as you show up to class and do the homework, EP's class should be an easy A. Just be sure to put effort into all of the group projects!
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--So many papers

reviews.comment: Vague and subjective grading system and criteria, somewhat unhelpful when approached for help, TA was horribly unhelpful and graded arbitrarily harshly

Pros:
Nice professor
Fun class
Small class

Cons:
Instructions and grading requirements on many assignments are vague and at times very subjective 
No grading rubrics were provided
Feedback is unhelpful, many times correcting formatting rather than anything of substance
Inconsistent with how far in advance some assignments are posted
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Press is super knowledgable about video, audio, writing, and everything else involved in broadcast/journalism. She was very down to earth and was there to help you through the process. Her class was a lot of fun. Make sure you study for your tests and do the projects assigned.

Doesn't teach you how to use R despite the labs being the largest portion of your grade. Homework and given back exams do not prepare you for the exams. Her instructions often leave you scratching your head figuring out what she wants you to do. While not common, she has lashed out at students and her TA. Never take a class with her.
The lecture is very clear. She always gives clear instructions and if you read through the lab notebooks, it is very easy to follow. Easy to get above 95 for her tests.

Class is a combination of using R for coding and pen/paper math. Grade consists of weekly labs, bi-weekly homework, two group projects, and two exams. Overall Prof Bennett is fairly solid. Gives clear instructions, notes are easy to understand, and the work is challenging but not extremely hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--Caring

reviews.comment: She's a decent professor along with Professor Erickson, the class definitely requires for you to be there and put effort from the beginning. Most assignments and exams are cumulative, so you should have a good understanding of previous topics and continue with that. Put in work and you should do fine, I found the TA Karan extremely helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Seems she genuinely wants students to learn the material, but it would help if she prepared before each lecture. She often seems to have forgotten key points she's trying to convey, and the discontinuity of thought as she tries to piece things together at the board ends up more confusing than helpful. Also be ready to come up with your own project

She doesn't really explain things all that well and she doesn't do enough examples. I think it also would have been helpful if she'd stuck to the textbook a little more which would have made it more useful.
She makes mistakes an nearly every slide. She also goes through things too quickly.

Terrible professor.  You can see she has put some time into preparing slides for this class but is absolutely awful at teaching any of it.  She needs to prepare before class, not let her voice die down in the middle of a sentence, and use lots and lots of examples in class.  Also, I thought the grading system was terrible.  Avoid her if you can.
No Comments

plenty of examples in class - if only she had worked out the examples ahead of time there would be fewer small mistakes that students have to point out to her - the in-class tests were relatively easy and the final was moderately challenging - overall, a pretty decent prof
Cute

Rude and not accommodating of students learning challenges. at times - doesn't understand what she is asking of students and then penalizing them due to her lack of knowledge for what's she's requiring. Would not take again. Hope to never have her again.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: My first grade I got back was in late October and my grade was okay 2.8/3. The next grade was give back on December 1st after all my assignments were submitted she then says I'm doing it wrong and there's no chance to go back and fix my assignments, they then offer extra credit to redo the assignment and fix things… and I get 0 points for that

Grading was that of an English class rather than based upon understanding of concepts. Assignments were not graded in a timely manner and students were told that they should "be keeping track of [their] own grade." The lecture given felt as through they did not serve a purpose as assignments did not line up with lecture content whatsoever.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Nice, engaging, pretty funny. I really enjoyed the lectures and his teaching style made them really interesting. Would definitely recommend for intro to cog sci and I imagine his linguistics courses are the same.

If you pay attention in class and like to raise your hand, you will have a great time in his class. If not, you'll probably still have a good time. He is very understanding and remembers all his students' faces. I sometimes zone out in class but he uploads all the lectures so I could still understand most of the material.
Just an awesome guy. I would recommend any class taught by him.

Ben is def the best professor I've had here. The course content is pretty interesting, and the activities and videos are really engaging. He is really nice and there are few assignments but they are very doable. He grades pretty leniently and really cares about his students. Def recommend taking a class with him at some point while you're at RPI

I've taken both linguistics and cog sci with him in the past, easily best rpi prof (which tbf doesnt say much or really anything at all but he's still pretty good), he mogs everyone else, now if he's teaching a class w/ something else it might not be a 5/5 experience but he himself is a 5/5 prof, pretty lenient, good teacher, mostly light on work
Very engaging

Professor Ben, as he likes to be called, gave interesting lectures that often included videos and class participation to make it interesting. Biweekly quizzes reflect the lecture material. Gave us essentially free rein for final project topic. Easily approachable and understanding about DSS accommodations and in general.
Very kind, understanding, in-touch, and passionate. Very interesting lectures, assignments and tests were not very difficult but still engaging and interesting.
Super nice prof, very lenient with grading, only things you have to do are a few essay-like assignments and 2 quizzes every week

Very caring and easy-going.  Very well-prepared, fun lectures.  Doesn't waste your time.  You only have to write a couple very short papers throughout the semester and take open-note quizzes based on the lectures.  As long as you show up to class and pay attention, you'll have no problem getting an A.

weissman is my GUY. he is a great professor and i recommend everyone tries to take at least one of his classes. he cares about the content and about his students a great deal. he is extremely accessible out of class if you ever need help understanding a concept that he talked about. overall 11/10, great guy, great prof
This class is pretty easy, its a few essays and short homework quizzes

He’s a wonderful professor who really cares about his students. I did take his class when it was online due to covid but I have to imagine he’s the same way in person. Lecture slides are posted online and you can review the slides if you miss class and get pretty much the same info you would’ve gotten if you went in person.
Great prof. Very kind and fun. Personally, I definitely could have done better in this course.
Great professor, clearly loves linguistics, and is a great guy.

Dr. Weissmann is honestly one of the best professors I've met. He is hilarious and he made the class fun for all majors. I also loved how he discussed real life applications based on what we were learning. The class does require some work though, yet if you actually put effort in, you'll get an A.

Ben is great. Tests are online on open-book, made available at midnight on test day, you can start it whenever you want, but once you start you have 2 hours to complete. I always looked forward to class because the material was interesting and Ben is a fun guy, you should definitely take his class.

Prof Blanchet is a legend. His course is so structured, even though the concepts were tough to understand he made it simple. Lots of homework but if you can do the homework don't worry about the exam.
Amazing person..
He gives really meaningful lectures and homework, showing respect for students' work.
His homeworks are difficult, but if you work through them, it makes the tests much easier. He is very helpful at office hours.

This professor very clearly explains all the concepts. His homework requires thinking. Tests are similar to homework. Make sure that you understand homework problems thoroughly. He is very helpful during his office hours. It is also pleasant to attend his office hours.

For an engineering class, Blanchet was good.  He can be boring, but overall he is approachable, helpful, and very knowledgeable.  I had him for MSL lab, I'd recommend getting him for EMD too if it's between him and Maniatty.  A nice guy, though the MSL quizzes were rather hard.
His notes are great.  The material he teaches is fairly difficult but if you show up to class, have a decent background, and a brain.  Very easy to understand.  Always there for extra help.
No Comments
i guess he's cool ... and pretty hot
No Comments
He is very boring. SKIP CLASS and show up for test. He seems like a dick in class but e is actually pretty cool
Good guy. Good biker.  Not super exciting, but a really nice guy.
Get a tutor and skip class!  He says "uh" so many times.  Smart guy, not a great teacher.  HW is HARD, but 50% of the grade. (which is good) Only 2 tests, one is the final, but not cumulative. :)

Pretty good prof. although sometimes gets caught in side tracks.  Very understanding and willing to help outside of class.  Although sometimes seeming a bit spaced out, he always makes sure that you know what's going on.
Great Class.  Great Prof.
Great teacher. Very difficult homework, but very willing to help outside of class.
horrible.
Good. Highly interested in what he teaches but can ramble. Took during summer. Workload was hard but doable. Usually 2 writing assignments a week.

Blaise Farina is an absolutely wonderful teachers who is ready and willing to help his students succeed. He provides great feedback and sparks great discussion in each class. I would highly recommend him.
His classes will not be easy.  If you just want an easy A, find another professor.  However, he is a great guy and he wants to see his students succeed.
He was a super friendly guy but the class didn't really know what he wanted from us in terms of the essays. Lecture was dull. He did not make me a better writer.

Took his Ethics course to fulfill my obligation to humanities.  He rewards cohesive arguments and well-discussed material EVEN IF you disagree with him.  He's interested in training your thought processes, your logical presentation and firm bases for discussion.  For the STEM heavy population of RPI, this is a paradigm shifting class.

Class material is interesting and will make you think, but the grading scheme is awful. As others said, he admits upfront that he grades on length because "it's the only real way he can tell you're trying." Very much the opposite of the way I was taught to write. Not very responsive with grades and how to improve papers either.

Had him for Moral Development. Class was all over the place, and the grade in the class is determined on two 20 page essays, in which your grade is really subjectively defined. The lecture was tedious because of its sporadic nature, and his gimmicks to appear "different" are obtrusive to learning. Take a 4000 Psych instead, it'll be easier.

Prof. Puka is a thoughtful man who really cares about what he teaches. I have taken classes by him for two years, and he certainly provides interesting ideas. His classes will change your viewpoints and life, if you let them. I would HIGHLY suggest taking his Ethics or Anarchy classes. (Note: There is a lot of reading.)
One of the best professor I have ever met. He makes the subject crystal clear with a lot of humorous stories. And he's a very nice person.

Think 'personal growth'. His classes aren't to 'teach' and the grades are a necessary annoyance. I rarely read or took notes (though I wish I had), and sometimes I daydreamed during class; yet I consider them the most important I have taken. The papers weren't fluff, but opportunities to debate my own morality. In no small way, they changed my life

Only take his courses if you know how to fluff a paper. His grades are mainly based on participation in class and how long of a paper you can write. So basically his grades are based on quantity, not quality (took this course w/ a friend and turned in the same paper, except one was fluffed a few pages, longer got the higher grade)

Along with Zenzen, the best professor that I've had at RPI.  Extremely intelligent and passionate about what he is teaching.  You'll learn alot, not only about philosophy, but about life in general.  The only reason you wouldn't want to take his classes is if you're easily offended or hold unreasonable beliefs.
He is one of the most brilliant professors Ive ever had the privilege to learn from. He is a truly good person, and a very good teacher.

He is definitely one of my favorite professors.  He will explain something from 3 different perspectives.  I second a previous reviewer's comments on his compassion.  If you take a Psych class, make it one of his.  Let me rephrase:  take Bill's Psych class!

Great class. The class periods are very entertaining and often he drops nuggets of information useful in interacting with the world (not just the field).  Often people confuse his examples with pushing an opinion. They then argue the point as wrong and get frustrated - if you can't understand metaphorical and hypothetical speaking, you'll struggle.
Puka is the man! By far the best class I have ever taken!
He has a lot of ideas however he refuses to listen to the classes points of view, interesting lectures if you don't happen to dissagree for the moment.
He is the best teacher at RPI, and made my 4 years bearable.
One of the best professors at RPI. This was one of the few courses I enjoyed at RPI.  Highly recommended.  The man is awesome!

A great philosophy professor.  He has an excellent rapport with the class and his lectures are entertaining and funny.  You have a lot of freedom in the class (we were free to make any syllabus we wanted).
Very good, funny, and entertaining. He doesn't assign much work but attendence is mandatory--the lectures are good enough to go anyway.
Take any class Puka teaches. He'll work with you, he's entertaining, and by far one of the smartest men on campus.

Awesome! Best professor I've had at RPI. He assigns a reasonable number of papers of reasonable length and lets you have a lot of freedom. His lectures are more like a cool talk show than lectures! Lots of reading assigned but if you miss some you're ok.
Really interesting professor.  Also one of the most compssionate people I've met.
Awesome professor, illustrates every concept eloquently and extremely clearly.  I recommend his Ethics class to anyone.
No Comments
Puka roxorz
Worst professor I've ever had

She was my advisor several years ago and was nice when talking on the phone. However, she doesn't read your emails or responded to just half of it. I swear she is a drunk. 

All her feedback and comments as well as email replies are lazy, soulless, ambiguous and the list can go on. She also has zero empathy for any problem you might have
STAY AWAY

Avoid if you can, I noticed most of the good reviews about this professor came about 15 years ago. This professor needs to realize that students are paying thousands of dollars to learn, not to have to pay thousands more for tutoring. Do not expect a kind response if you email her that you are running late on an assignment.

Ask a question why you get marked down and she only reiterates the directions(mind you, they were followed exactly). She doesn't like when in a project you solve for a value asked for and the process you used is different than what she thought, even though it's still right and didn't say what so ever how to solve. Beware, this should be criminal

Has unclear of unstated expectations, refuses to help students when asked. Her feedback is unkind and unnecessarily harsh when providing feedback. Won't actually explain the problems or instructions, instead cutting and pasting the original directions while implying students are too lazy and stupid to understand.

I just started her class. We have to use MML and have to complete 65 questions (with 5 parts each on a lot of them) that are ungraded before we can even access the actual graded homework. Stupidest thing ever. Fortunately I work full time and have a group project for the entirety of my other class. Absolutely ridiculous.

She is at Excelsior now and she is the worst. She is horrible with communicating her expectations and when you ask for more guidance she blows you off. She is a really strict grader even on the smallest assignments. Her expectations for her students is 40 hrs a week dedicated to her class.. So goodluck having a job. I would not recommend this class
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: She is knowledgeable, but she does not like to teach.  Often will not answer questions and simply tells  you to look in the textbook. Does not respond to emails or phone calls in a timely manner. Avoid if possible.

Empire State College has a tendency of hiring professors who are either fired from other institutions or are really cheap.  She is one of those professors who cant find job anywhere else.  She is very disrespectful, never replies to student emails and when asked to talk over the phone she always declines.  She DOES NOT offer any assistance at all.

I found her course very frustrating.  She would not get back to me in a timely manner at all, over a week would go by without getting a response email after sending multiple emails.  I did not find her helpful at all when trying to learn and she did not try and help me succeed at all even after asking for help.
Very difficult class and the professor did not provide assistance when asked prior to grading assignments.  Professor graded all assignments harshly with vague feedback.

Says another review: "good teacher for students who have already had a Calc BC background and just need a review of that material before starting higher level math classes." Umm, classes aren't for review, they're for LEARNING. You can't teach a class expecting students ALREADY know everything there is to learn! It's sad she hasn't been fired yet.

Definitely the worst class I've ever taken.  She is not very helpful, and her quizzes do not prepare her students for upcoming exams.  She always confuses herself when solving examples in class, and leaves the students even more confused.  Study at least a week prior to her exams.  With that being said, I do not recommend this professor at all.
Excellent Professor.She put all her notes online and her classes are easy to follow. Exams are not hard, and you do not need too much extra reading for her class.

Irritating and frustrating professor. She was NOT a good lecturer, and she seemed to decide that showing up to class wasn't important until the department told her to! Her graduate TA taught a ton of the lectures. Tests are unnecessarily difficult. She tries to trick you and grades harshly. She doesn't even have office hours in person. Avoid her.

Taking 5 classes as a freshmen with any other teacher I would have recieved a 4.0 her class dragged my gpa down the entire semester until the point where I rallied 10 or 15 pissed of student to complain to the department head. If these other rating were true, they no longer are. It is not a challenge, it is a waste of time. You will not learn.

When she did show up to class, which she decided not to about 6 times over the semester, her notes were colorful and appear as though they would be helpful but in reality she jumps back and forth writing unintelligible notes on top of her other ones. Her tests are unreasonable and do not reflect notes or homework, and she is generally unkind.

Lecture notes are very much unclear to the point of unreadability. Does one example usually for each new concept in class, then expects you to use the book pretty much as your professor. Says things like "e of stuff is the same as the derivative of e of stuff." Just tell me some actual math.

She makes a lot of mistakes while teaching. She is very unorganized and a lot of times the class has to correct her. Her level of helpfulness extends to telling her class that they should get help from their math mentors and go to tutoring. Tests are unneccesairly difficult compared to the homework. Unless youre bright you will not get an A.
Excellent professor. If you try, you will succeed.
good teacher

Prof. Blue is very nice, yet somewhat disorganized. Lectures are sometimes boring, especially if you have seen the material. Exams are not too challenging. She is a good teacher for students who have already had a Calc BC background and just need a review of that material before starting higher level math classes.

Professor Blue is fantastic. She is amusing and gives extremely detailed notes. There are a lot of quizzes, but she gives you resources that will make you well prepared. She is by far my favorite professor.
not bad pretty easy and straightforward diffy q
Excellent Professor. She explains things extremely clearly and puts all of her notes online. Her exams are very straight forward too.
Very helpful and very clear examples. The class was quite useful as far as being applicable in the real world.

Great professor for calculus 2. Her online notes are color coated and she relaly makes sure that you understand the material. I went to her for extra help and I pulled up my test grade 3 letter grades. I recommend her for anyone that likes detailed notes and doesn't mind attending lecture. STUDY FOR NPC QUIZZES!
Yall.....lol her favorite word
I took her calculus and differential equations classes. She is an incredible instructor.
Outstanding professor.  Cared about her students like her own kids.  Fun, interesting, outstanding at explaining material.  Get her if you can!!

Considering that she is teaching calculus one (possibly the most uninteresting classes) she does a wonderful job of keeping things fresh and fun. Clicker questions are something to look forward to with her, rather than something inconvenient and to be dreaded.
Kind and enthusiastic, and strong mannered. Very outgoing.

Great professor.  Direct in what she wanted, but very clear and concise in the way she taught Calculus 1.  If you cared, you did well.  Easily approachable and very helpful lectures.  Non-mandatory homework which was never collected.  Nice jokes and wisecracks too! Awesome overall.
Awesome class. Got an A...as long as you go to class, then you're set. REally.
really great prof..has office hours from 9-11pm the night before the test in McNeil.. right when you figure out you need help...laid back biker chick...cant get better than that

she skims down the material to get rid of the unecessary details which is fine for a bit but then Cal II arrives and you dont know anything. Nice teacher, easy to work with and you end up with a better grade then you think
Shes pretty cool.... She tries really hard to put calc into understandable terms and is pretty fair with her grading.... Tests are SO EASY!!! Good Luck!
Jennifer Blue is the best. She's very cool, and her method of teaching is very effective.
No Comments

All teachers should be like Jen Blue. She's very down to Earth and approachable. She also likes to "cut the crap". She is very practical and her tests are fair. She doesn't play the demoralizing "I gotcha game". She's easy IF you've taken Calc I before, but not so much if you haven't.
She is really awesome. I did really bad on all the tests and did really well on the final and i got a b overall. but she is also very helpful in and out of class
Very good teacher.  Went into calc 1 with no previous clac classes from HS.  Clear to understand.
She is the coolest teacher at RPI.....she actually has a personality!! wow, what a concept. Definitely try to get her; she kicks ass!!

GREAT PROF!...LOVED her class.  VERY HELPFUL...begs for you to come to office hours.  I have one word for her: STUFF!  (ull understand if u take her class)  GET THIS PROF IF YOU CAN.  Final took 30 mins!...
Professor Blue is very helpful and will work with you on anything and everything you ask her for.
Great teacher

A very fair teacher who explains the subject well. She doesnt try to trick you on tests, but instead just wants to make sure you know the material. Easy and a great refresher course if you have already taken calculus before.

Jen Blue is awesome.  She cancels class all the time and her exams take 20 minutes, if that.  She is very straightforward and teaches you exactly what you need to know- nothing more, nothing less.  And she's young and crazy, so her lectures are definitely an experience.

SHES AWESOME! SHE KICKS ASS SOOO BAD!!!! hard professor but always comprehensible....unlike the rest of the professors at rpi. finally a professor who makes sense and teaches the topic in a straightforward manner.

Great professor from Texas!! Finally someone who says "y'all!" I miss southerners, so it's nice to have a redneck somewhere. She knows her math, and understands we don't care about trivial terms and whatnot. Engineers don't need the mathemeticia

Very easy professor, teaches the essentials and no more, often cancels class and recitation, tests are easy as well. Doesn't prepare you as well for further classes as I'd like, the downside to the easy class.
very good teacher, explains material well, makes up easy tests, overall a good teacher
Made things  very easy to understand and very straight forward
Very nice teacher, makes lecture interesting, tests take you 1/2 the time to finish (while getting an A), nuff said.
very easy!!! and clear, cancels class often which is great! she also isnt strict w/ her stuff
Very easy teacher, the final took me about 35 minutes to finish.
If you don't get an A in her Calc class there is something wrong with you.  Best calc teacher!
Best Calc Professor
I love this professor, really good guy.
Very nice professor! He is very nice answering questions!

Malaviya really knows what he is talking about when it comes to MAU but doesn't present in the most effective manner. He zooms through lectures very fast making notes hard to copy down and rarely pauses for questions. He often mocks you if you do not understand something and try to talk to him during office hours. The class also doesn't get curved.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Extremely rude and dismissive when I came in to ask questions. Questioned if I even care about my grades, even when I came in to ask clarifying questions. Is overall a difficult human being to communicate with on a one to one level.

Really nice guy.  Cares about his students.  Difficult to understand accent at first but it isn't bad after a few days.  He is the go to professor for MAU.  Make sure he knows your name.  That definitely helps when he gives you the grade.
Prof. Malaviya is a sweet and brilliant man. Great teacher and very willing to help you outside of class, he even helped me find a job! Homework's not too bad but the take-home final was tough.
Best professor i have ever had. period.
Bimal is the man! Boring as heck to hear lecture, but he's very thorough. Very helpful in office hours.
He's the best teahcer of this class hands down!
Not only are his lectures pretty good, with plenty of examples, but he's SO nice. I showed up to an exam without my book or notes, and he let me leave to get them and gave me extra time at the end.

He has a really mumbly and quiet voice, but if you actually pay attention, his lectures are clear, logical and helpful. Office hours were also a big help. What sucks is when he's out of town (often), because his TA's generally are terrible at explaining the material.

Prof. Malaviya really cares about his students.  He takes the time to write out notes and examples rather than using Power Point.  He also goes through lots of examples in Minitab so you'll be prepared to answer test questions quickly.  Great for answering questions.  The key to success is going to class.

i dont know what you pple are talking abt, but he's an awesome professor! brilliant man! very easy going and diligent. definitely helps with the understanding of difficult materials and knows how to grade fairly!
Tests are easy, but he is really hard to understand.  Lectures are very boring.  He is helpful if you ask him questions after class or during office hours.  TAs are good too.

Professor Malaviya is rather poor in expalining things, and worse at presenting them. The class is easy, but Professor Malaviya seems to find a grading  scheme to make sure that it follows the "normal distribution"...that means you will probably get a B in MAU.

Thanks for the comments about the final grading, I am in MAU now and didnt realize that he did that.   If you can get past the mumbling (pay attention to what he writes) the lectures are actually quite clear and progress in a logical sequence. He is an extremely nice guy and very willing to help out.

Good: Professor Malaviya knows how to do mau.... Bad: Prof. Malavuya can't explain how to do mau, he mumbles, he gives the same incomprehensable explanations in office hours as he does in class. Finally he believes that grades should follow a normal distribution. Yes he curved down...That means my 89 was a C.

He made the minimum A grade a 95 without any warning that the final grade cutoff would be adjusted -- of course I was in the low 90's and got a B.  Anyway, noone could understand him in class, the subject was just naturally easy once you figured out what you were doing.  So, everyone spent all lecture playing games on their laptops.
He was really fast in trying to get through class with as much information as possible.  Provided very thourough class with useful information.
He is a really nice guy but my god i cant understand a thing he says.
Very nice caring professor. One of the best I haver had

I LOVE PROF. MALAVIYA!He is the best professor and person I've ever met.More professors and people should be like him.He is so personable and I just love his amazing personality.I just want to give him a big hug everytime I see him.I aspire to be more like him in my personal/professional life. His friendly personality is inspiring. He's the best!!!
Awful mumbling indian professor who only confuses you more when you ask him something IF you can either a) hear him, or b) understand him.

Taking MAU with him for the 3rd time now.  He was abysmmal the first two times. This year he's teaching basics he never taught and giving new notes I don't remeber him giving. Also, either I'm getting used to his heavy accent, or he's worked on his english. Last year I would have rated him a 1.
VERY hard to understand, doesn't present material in a clear manner... seems nice enough, but i wish i had picked a better teacher
He is extremely difficult to understand.
...still waiting for that email
nice guys..really helpful..
looks like a confused chimp most of the time, but will do your work for you if you go to office hours
Impossible to understand. Seemed confused most of the time.

doesn't help students understand the material. he gave me half the answers to the microquizes while i was taking them. i've learned more of the course while taking hte open book test than from his lectures. the homeworks on "ilearn" are nearly i

Heard he used to be pretty good ... That's changed!  MAU stinks to begin with (unless you like statistics anyhow) but he makes it worse.  He tries sometimes but he's usually pretty unclear.  Seems like somethings not quite right upstairs?
doesnt return your emails.
he is aweosme if u dont take mau with him u r an idiot ... hes such a nice person
Does not cover course material well.  If he doesn't agree with the course coordinator he just doesn't cover the topic.  Did not cover the material at a level that prepared us for the tests

was alright... ease of class made up for his lesser points

She is one of the best professors I have ever had. I had her for two semesters ( biocomp and tissue engineering), I wish she offered more classes. She is very smart and her resume is impressive ! She puts so much enthusiasm into teaching. Her classes are NOT easy. You have to work very hard for your grade and ATTEND to class.

Dr. Bizios was my advisor.  This woman was so passionate about how her students acheived, she yelled at me (yes, yelled at me) for not attending Grad School.  For whatever reason, I think she was right.  And even though I've learned through the school of experience about the medical device industry, I could have benefited more from an MS or PhD.
She isn't the most approachable professor (putting it nicely)...and she tends to be very defensive if you question her.  The class is really interesting to sit through, but her exams are REALLY HARD.

Test questions tend to be broad and ambiguous; in addition, there is no pre-defined rubric and points seem to be assigned randomly. MUST attend lecture to do well on the exams. Professor does care about the student but views most questions as personal attacks, and can come off as slightly arrogant. Grades are based on standard deviations.
Expects alot from students.  Tests are very hard, but class is entertaining.  Don't miss class, as everything is based off of lectures.
Terrible! Never shows up, just reads overheads.  If it's not on the overhead, she can't help you.  Tests very hard, with very low averages.  Don't take a class with Rena!!
She teaches only the stuff you'll need to know for the test.  She can be harsh sometimes, but I think she teaches well.  She expects a lot, especially in TBI.

She just copies quations from the book.  She doesn't seems to know anything except what's on her overheads.  Takes off points for no writing all cancellations in equations.  Seems satisfied with very low averages on tests.  Only showed up to teach for about 60% of the class times.  Not recommended.
She was only in class 60% of the time, replaced by some old guy.  Her notes were simply copied straight from the book.  Tests were ridiculously hard.

Her notes are just copies that she uses over every year.  It was very difficult for me to follow what she was talking about relative to the notes.  I thought it was a waste of my time to even go to class.
Fun
Great professor.  Very nice and helpful.  Liked the many example problems that were done in class.  Fair tests.

The amount of examples that she did in class and posted on the website clarified the course significantly.  She was very helpful when I brought her questions about the grading of an exam, and I got 4 more points.
Do not take a class with this professor.  She is a self involved lazy teacher.
i like her..she is cool beans
cares little about material/students

Professor Sikdar's a really nice guy.  He doesn't do a lot to make the material interesting, so it can be easy to fall asleep.  Other than that, he understands what he's teaching and has no problem elaborating.  Great personality and cares about students more than other professors I've encountered.
Biplab is one of the nicest professors I've ever had! I definately recommend him.
His accent is a little thick but tends to be rather clear. His pacing can be amusing and he understands the material and teaches it well.
I love Biplab.  He is the funniest guy in the whole world.  I don't know where he gets those jokes but they are pure GOLD.
HORRIBLE at teaching! Needs to learn English and make the slides more interesting and better.  I see other small college websites teaching CANOS and they teach very diligently and clear.
great professor.  Explains material very well in class.  For CANOS don't bring your laptop (NERDS!!)  and you will do well

We started out the semester with another professor, and Biplab blew him out of the water.  He explains concepts very thoroughly, and was very helpful in answering questions.  His accent isn't bad if you pay attention.  Plus his constant moving around is very amusing.
He is a good teacher and, yeah, likes to teach, but the class is horrible.  Always willing to help and answer quesitons.  He has no problem answering "dumb" questions either.

When Prof. Sikdar speaks, it's like a locomotive train.  If you don't pay attention early on, it's really hard to get back on track.  He goes so fast at times.  His accent doesn't help either.  He is a great person but I'm sorry, I can't understand him when he teaches hard to understand concepts.
Biplab is the best professor to have.  He is incredible.
Clear, interesting, and most of all -- interested in teaching.  Don't find that much here at RPI
Best professor on campus.  Extremely clear and helpful.  Great personality.
Pretty good at explaining stuff.  The class still sucks, but he is willing to help you try to understand.  A little bit of an accent, but still easy to understand, and funny too.

Professor Foley is absolutely terrible. He is incredibly unorganized and is very unclear about assignments. He will grade extremely hard and will grade based off of rubrics that are not provided to the class at all. His lectures are barley even lectures and just turn into mindless rambling. Avoid at all costs.

Terrible professor. Doesn't understand the projects he assigns and then deducts points for things his pin head doesnt hear during your presentation. unaccountable and has a very surface level knowledge of all subjects. Attending his office hours is like trying to ask questions to a monkey.

He was not a great lecturer, I never paid attention to the lectures. You have to read the textbook. The most useful thing was his workbook problem videos. I spent most of my time with the TA, who was great. Lots of homework, but test are mostly what's graded. Tests are not super similar to homework. You have to go to lectures to turn in CPE.
Just no. It gets extremely frustrating especially when you take his course not knowing the way he teaches

Prof. Foley is a pretty boring lecturer. Material can be learned straight out of the book and isnt too hard. A lot of busy work and one homework assignment per week. Make sure you use ExcelOM to save yourself a bunch of time on the work. Exams are open book, notes, laptop.

He is not a good professor. But if you watch all of the video's he posts before exams, and make sure you submit all of the class exercises and all of the homework you'll do decent in the class. Avoid him if possible, but you know what you're getting when you take a class with him.

Foley was a decent professor for IED. He graded fairly and was helpful in the lab when working on our main project. He has a strange sense of humor and tries his best to keep his lectures interesting. Overall not a bad choice for IED.

Always talking about something interesting, he is super knowledgeable. But he doesn't really teach much. Stopped going to lectures because even if I went I had to read through the online material to learn anyways. Not a tough class though. Great guy, just a lot of homework. If you do what you're supposed to do you'll get like a B+

He will make you work for your grade. You are drilled with work after work. So, if you slack off for half a week, you'll be behind. He is accessible outside of class. Still a reasonable professor, expects a lot from you, and will keep you on your toes with work. You'll definitely come out learning something.

DON'T DON'T DON'T TAKE HIS CLASS UNLESS YOU WANT TO CHALLENGE YOURSELF REALLY BAD. HE MIGHT KNOW WHAT HE IS DOING, HE MIGHT NOT. NO MATTER WHAT, HE DOESN'T MAKE SENSE IN THE CLASS AND IS NOT A VERY NICE PROFESSOR TO STUDENTS. I TOOK IED AND OR FROM HIM. BOTH WERE AWEFUL EXPERIENCES:(
The only reason I did alright was because of the textbook.  Awful professor but if you are an IME, there is no way to avoid him.  Good luck!

He doesn't grade fairly nor does he offer help. He goes on tangents throughout all of class on topics that have no relevance to the course. He does not go through example problems and his lecture slides are not helpful when studying.  His exams are way too difficult because he does not teach clearly enough. Take MAU with a different professor.

Maybe people at RPI are just used to bad professors.  I can't comprehend why anyone would rate him highly.  This man is the worst educator I have ever encountered in my entire life.  Every negative comment I've read about him has been far more accurate than the positives.  Avoid this man at all costs.  His arrogance is only matched by his ignorance
Useless with any help at all
Rants a lot during class, somewhat tough grader. A little awkward, laughs at his own jokes. Pushes you really hard to do well.

he is a really bad teacher who doesnt know anything and pretend that he is the smartest person in the whole world. he doesn't care about his students and talk about his stupid cars all the time which are like bmw 1 series and Volkswagen beetle...

At first I though he was unreasonably hard.  He is a really good guy and will push you beyond your comfort zone.  As long as he sees that you go don't just do the minimum you will do very well in his classes.  Very strange sense of humor and funny laugh.  Ended up being one of my best experiences with a professor.

Very difficult, grades favorites higher. Tries to push you beyond your goal. Sleeps and eats sandwiches. You must talk to him and show him that your doing work otherwise you will not do well. your project must show engineering process otherwise you will do poorly. Our project worked but he didnt like how it looked gave us a D-.

Relates course material to real life situations on a regular basis.  Willing to help you outside of class during office hours or through e-mail if it is obvious that you made an effort to find the answer on your own. Any bad reviews about this professor are from people upset that they couldn't find back tests to cheat off.

Girls - get ready for him to hit on you in a weird, old guy fashion. Guys - try to refrain yourself from punching him in the face whenever he's the only one maniacally laughing at his own jokes... He's more interested in himself than the class. Get another professor if possible.

He often went on rants in the middle of class.  His test are very hard, but he will help you if you ask.  If you put in the work you'll be fine.  Stick with him though.  Don't just give up on the first test if you do badly.

Worthless. Claims students are getting dumber by the year, yet has no regard to his own substandard teaching. Has no interest in helping students understand the material. Worst professor I have ever had.

Nice guy. Doesn't go out of his way to help students at all. Has barely anything on LMS; no practice problems or backtests. Worst thing about him is the lack of answers on the in class problems. How am I supposed to know if I'm right? Useless.

Great professor.  He is a bit full of himself, but if you go out of your way and do crazy interesting things, he will reward you for it.  He says it's all about the process, and it truly is - if you fail, but your process succeeds, then you will get a decent grade.

He is awful to have for a professor. He doesn't know how to teach and all he does is read slides for 2 hours. He does not grade fairly and he is useless in office hours. He thinks he knows everything. If you are a good looking girl however, be sure to be aware he will be rather creepy towards you but will give you good grades based on likes.
Great Professor in my opinion. Does go off topic some times but he is easy to understand and has been a really fun professor. He is very knowlegable in economics and project mangment.

procrastinators beware..his homeworks can take hours if you want 90+ and are usually due the same day as  tests, he offers flexibilty on tests, has really high standards for his students, insightful but sometimes rather boastful of his ego which can/will get annoying

Foley is one of those professors that makes sure you know he's a Ph.D and PE at every possibility by flaunting his credentials to secure his superiority over his students.  Shame he doesn't spend more time trying to teach design instead, or the class might not have come down to a last ditch effort to find something that impresses him to get an A.

Ok professor.  If he likes you, you'll prolly get an A.  Can go off onto some weird tangents when us tart talking to him.  He's very knowledgeable though.  Sometimes i get the impression that he doesn't care about students, like he's sometimes  short with me when I go to see him in his office to ask a few questions, but that just be the way he is.

The guy's kind of a pain in the ass.  But he does know what he's talking about (most of the time).  The class really isn't engineering design, it's "make the project that pleases foley the most" design.
Totally self absorbed.  Likes to talk and waste your group's building time with theory that's not applicable at all.  Take any other IED professor over him.

Homeworks were hard but very helpful in preparing for the tests. Tests were fair and the material on the tests was exactly what he taught. Interesting lectures even if it was 8am. You could get help always if you wanted by going to the office hours.

Homeworks were byfar the hardest part of the class.Homework questions would be very involved, while the tests were as simple as possible.There was never any "catch" on the tests; everything came straight from back tests or the book and the tests were open book/open notes.Lectures fairly interesting.

If you do the assigned work in his class, Foley will respect you and give you an A. Everyone that hates him probably did a****ty job on their notebook and such and thus got ripped apart by Foleys grading.  He is knowledgable in many respects, and is a very nice guy. Is vague about due dates however

Falls alseep and doesn't appear to pay much attention during presentations.  His lectures are somewhat scattered.  Is vague with instructions, doesn't always answer questions clearly.  Not that bad though, could be a lot worse.

This man is very unhelpful in class, and has an awesome tendancy to fall asleep during presentations. Stpent most of the class eating turkey sandwiches instead of doing something productive. Don't take IED from this man.
all around bad experience...he wasn't helpfull and at the end of the IED he still didn't know anyone's name.  Try to get any other professor for this class.

Foley is an absolute idiot.  He doesn't know his left elbow from an Op-Amp.  Teaches erroneous information, useless information, and denies class discusion in a course where it is a must.  He has the worst jokes on the planet, and he is the only one actually laughing, very annoying.  Horrendous!
he may be crazy, but he's all around a nice guy. easy class too :)
IDIOT.  the man is only concerned w/ himself.
Very unhelpful especially to EE's and has a very vague grading system. Didnt find helpful at all
No Comments

Although vauge and mean at the front of the room, if you talk to him individually you see just what it is that he's after.  He sees more ability in you than he lets on and pushes you to it.  Great for that and cares about his students and their work.
No Comments

Has no ability to describe what he wants. IED is a very difficult course to start with, when you have no idea what he wants or when, the course becomes impossible. Assignments and project requirements are given roughly 2 day before they are due. Horrible.
seems a little strict and unusual at first but if you take the time to get to know him he's actually not such a bad guy
Vague about what he wants, I was confused even after going to office hours. He does seem to care about students however
No Comments
Prof. takes too long to respond to emails.  Very vague project requirements.  Students must rely on themselves.
he definately puts you in your place. frank and straightforward...great teach.
horrible.

had him 3 times... hated him at first. but ask him for help or just go talk to him for a bit. he's actually a good guy and really does care about his students. he definitely makes you do better than you ever thought you could. he really helped me a lot.
this man truly IS evil
Seemed questionable at first but eventually proved to be a good teacher.  Very helpful, really cares.

Failed me on a loophole clause in the syllubus, the next time I took the course the syllubus was changed to fit the situation.  Actually had the **** to tell me I needed therapy without any grounds.  Inconsistent and has no practical experience
No Comments

implimentation of the team based groups was a total waste of effort on our part.  Not a single  ball-testing-machine  became what could even remotely resemble a functioning product.  Foley did nothing to help up work together.
Again, he's very rought on your ego... but it's well worth it when you look back at the end.  He makes you do more than you think you could.
he was SO mean at the beginning but it turned out to be the best thing because our project rocked in the end... and mostly because he was so critical to begin with
talk to him face to face, you'll thank yourself for it
Felt like I was in kindergarten during his Wednesday IED lectures
No Comments
He gave great advice on our project, and was genuinely excited about the class.
No Comments
what a class... but Foley is a terrific instructor.

Very cool guy that loves what he does, has VERY long lecture slides but explains everything super well in class. Test grading is very specific on what words you use in your free response, so go to post-exam reviews to ask for regrades when possible. Textbook not required but I find it easier to read the textbook while reviewing slides.

One of my favorite biology professors at RPI. I highly recommend taking his Microbiology lab, you learn so much from Dr. Bonocora and he truly cares about you succeeding in his classes. Very understanding and fair. Just put in the work and you will do fine in his classes

Dr. Bonocora is an extremely caring professor. He grades fairly, gives points back if a bunch of students missed something, and grants extensions whenever necessary. He also gives fairly interesting lectures and will meet with you if you have questions or need help. Overall a great prof!

Dr. Bonocora is great, but he wasn't my lab professor, despite my having signed up for his lab course. As a person, he is wonderful and really understanding. But his grading - or maybe it was the TA's grading - is really unnecessarily tough. Every week, I thought I was failing this course because grades wouldn't come in until 3 weeks later.

Great prof who loves the material. His tests can get really specific into how pathways work but as long as you know the material on the slides, youll be good. He makes it clear that reading the textbook is not necessary. The only things he tests on are the things he puts on his slides.
Solid teacher. Only complaint was how specific the information on the tests were
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Bonocora is great! He's nice, funny, overall a great guy. The class itself is about average difficulty, though I took it as a senior so the class was very easy. Simple homeworks about every other week, two short essays, a few tests, and NO final! Each class is just a lecture, you don't NEED to show up. I didn't touch the textbook.
He mumbles, so at first it is hard to understand his lectures. He is very knowledgeable though, and available outside of class for help.

Dr. Bonocora teaches the lab portion of Cell Bio, and he's wonderful! He's incredibly smart and very supportive. If you go to his office hours before major assignments are due he will look over your work and give suggestions. He's totally chill.
She genuinely wants students to learn. HT is not an easy course, but it's not hard to succeed with her a professor.

Outstanding instructor and lecturer, extremely knowledgeable and caring for her students. She will get to know almost everyone's name in the class, especially those who participate in lecture. Tests are very fair, but there is an unbelievable amount of fairly difficult homework. Overall worth the difficulty and time, I learned a lot in this class.

Overall Prof. Borca isn't a terrible lecturer, but she's not great either. For a three credit class, expect about four homework assignments and two quizzes per week. You will be doing heat transfer homework of some kind almost every night. Most of the homework is done on Wiley Plus as well, so TAs/Prof don't grade the HW. (so no partial credit)

Prof. Borca taught this class using a more involved approach than most classes and, as a result, the material was more thoroughly explained. Lectures were clear and informative, and contained both lecture material and worked examples, which were both helpful. Class was very time intensive, but if you put the work in, you will get an A
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Heat Transfer is difficult, but the prof makes it infinitely better. The most important thing I can say is that it's obvious she cares about her students and their ability to learn the material. Easily accessible outside of class as well- answers emails super quickly!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Group projects

reviews.comment: As far as lecture goes, she's pretty average. Not very helpful in office hours. Projects are frustrating since she doesn't clearly define the deliverables.

Heat transfer is HARD and Professor Diana is a hard professor too. However, she is very knowledgeable about the material and really cares for all of her students. Homeworks and projects are very rigorous but they are designed as if you were in the industry. You will be frustrated but if you can crank out the work and work with TA's, you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: She is the best professor I have had at RPI. She actually cares about her students and actually want them to succeed. She sent two students home one class to go rest after they pullled an allnighter.

Most of your grade is the project. The project is a great experience and requires intuition, assumptions and decision making skills in the field of heat transfer. It is supposed to simulate industry. It also requires a lot of communication, creativity, and initial assumptions that you may not be comfortable making. Great experience overall.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Fantastic professor and fantastic course. Hard work, but nothing will prepare you for industry better. Take any opportunity you can get to be taught by Prof. Borca-Tasciuc; she is simply the best of the best.

Awesome, would recommend her to anyone. She is a ton of work but genuinely cares about her students' success and is a great teacher. So far, she's the only professor I've had that's made an effort to learn her students' names.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: It was definitely lecture heavy with lots of expected prior knowledge. Aside from the difficulty of material we were learning, the project required at least 4 hours a week and sometimes required 20+ hours for milestones. The take-home exam was the hardest test I ever took. Overall, though, she is incredibly helpful and teaches thoroughly.
Very good at explaining material. If you put in the effort you will succeed.

GREAT! Tests are open-book, notes, laptop + are easy! She gives out extra credit every class! Clear communicator, organized + receptive to feedback! That said, be prepared for a quiz + challenging homework EVERY class (drops lowest of each) + that the final was hard, but honestly she's one of the best teachers at RPI! In fact, I'm taking her again!
She is awesome! Tests are easy, final was a bit harder than the rest of the exams, but she does everything she can to help you succeed. I absolutely recommend her.

Prof Borja is a cool guy who is very interested in physics and it's applications. The in-class lab work is very simple to follow, and the lectures are reading off of slides. My issue with the class is that he does not prepare the class very much for the exams, which are a majority of the grade. Other professors cover more back exam Qs.

As a new teacher, Dr. Borja is an overall super chill and sweet dude and I had a solid time in Physics. Alas it was 8:00am but he made the best of it and I respect it. It felt like having a new high school teacher who you just gotta like.

Professor Borja is very enthusiastic about physics, making his lecture blocks very easy to sit through, even at 8AM.  Gave good preparation for tests. The only issue, which I assume is not his fault, is that the lecture slides are made by a different professor. If he crafted his own lectures, I think he could go from a 4 to a 5. (Taken Fall '22)
Prof Borton is awesome.  He makes you think, and in big ways.  Out of all the professors at RPI, he's in the top 3 in my book.  Take his course!!
This guys loves to push his beliefs in class. Not that bad to get a good grade... but you will want to take a swan dive off the CII stairwell listening to his boring lectures are

I can't believe this guy has been teaching at RPI as long as he has.  I have never seen a professor trying to push his own personal agenda like this guy has.  Whenever you ask a question which challenges his personal agenda he quickly changes the subject.  Miserable teacher-an embarrasment to RPI!

An old-school loon. Cares about sig figs but doesn't allow calculators! Very one sided towards solar energy. He'll just ask you back any question you ask him.The worst is that he is soooo full of himself.

This professor made an intro 1000 level course feel like an 4000 advanced one. Readings were 50+ pages and extremely uninteresting. Participation was required every class, but you only got the credit depending on if he found your responses “worthy.” Grading was very strict, with expectations far too high for a freshman course.

I had Bucky first semester of my freshman year, and he truly ruined my first semester experience, along with the other freshmen in my class. He insisted on teaching a 1000 level class at the 4000 level, and graded like we were PhD students. While he is very knowledgeable in his field, he cannot teach to inexperienced students.

I had Bucky for his first semester teaching. This is a communication-intensive course, and it is no less than what that demands: reading and writing. Bucky's approach to teaching and grading is hilarious and constructive, but some feel it is offensive and targeted. You'll have no problem getting an A if you know what this class asks of you.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Don't let his intro algo reputation stop you from taking this course. He is so much more engaging and entertaining in crypto. You can really tell that he loves this stuff and wants you to as well. Can be a tad confusing at times but is always willing to try to explain again. Super caring and nice too. He's so incredibly Bulent Yener its awesome.

Literally the highlight of my schedule. He's absolutely an enthusiastic teacher. Classwork is appropriately difficult but not too hard, tests are a bit harder but nowhere near the level FOCS or something. Great class to take to brighten up an otherwise heavy semester.
Very knowledgable but sometimes confusing. Has english accent. Ran a very organized class.
god gives his toughest soldiers his strongest battles. and this one was too tough for me.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures were meh, most people stopped showing up pretty quickly. Homeworks and labs are kinda difficult and will take a few hours, but are well put together and are what I learned from. Midterm was 30% of the grade, final was 40%. Back exams are easily available on google, but someone snitched after the midterm, so he made the final a nightmare :(

He teaches the class in a poor and disorganized manner. His handwriting is very hard to read. He could easily be replaced by distributing copies of the textbook and relevant practice problems to students and providing a list of required chapters to read: then the quality of the class would skyrocket.
Rude towards the students and just overall a lazy professor that does not care about teaching.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Bulent Yener is a thoroughly confusing man. His verbal lectures are difficult to follow at best, and his handwritten notes are virtually illegible. Regard Yener not as a teacher but as a guide. Use his resources to follow the pace of the class, then teach yourself from Google. Don't expect any support from him; you will only be disappointed.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I have different opinions about the 70% rule because I think it is fair to put all the students under the same standard. But two exams increases uncertainty.

I am sure Yener is very knowledgeable, but unfortunately translating that into a way that the students can understand is his weakness. 70% of our grade was composed of two tests! That is absolutely ridiculous, it really only takes for you to have one bad night or lack of sleep for your whole semester of work to be drained in the toilet.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
It is fundamentally impossible to describe the emotions this man evokes.
Two exams worth 70% combined which is awful, lectures are not very helpful, but is a fairly nice guy. Final was insanely difficult. He's the most Bulent Yener I've ever seen.
Also he uses a fountain pen.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Yener is like a coin. It's like flipping a coin, he's like an anomaly, if he wakes up on the wrong side of the bed its war.  Research should be done on what Yener is thinking, a day in the life of Yener is needed.
Worst professor ever. Bad handwriting, uses a bad textbook, makes two tests worth 70% of your final grade, and is super rude. Don't take him.
Get ready to read bruh, you never gonna understand his lecture. The explanations in the lecture is HORRIBLE. just don't take his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: There are two exams worth 70% of your grade, the prof does not explain anything, and instructions for most assignments are extremely unclear.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Lectures are dry and provide little benefit compared to just going over the slides yourself. Yener would often suggest watching the online videos instead of covering various topics in class. Too bad the videos are just as bad (and often worse) than the in-person lectures. Unreasonable workload towards the end, assigned exam on top of project.

Although many people will complain about his lectures, especially his handwriting, most I've heard negative things from tended not to even attend the lecture and just look at the notes posted online. He goes into great detail about examples and step by step methods, and shows a great passion for the course.
Professor Yener is very responsible, instead of reading slides he prepared for every lecture with hand-written notes, which encouraged you to attend the class in person.

Python skills make labs easier, and back work really helps midterms. Lectures aren't bad, but handwritten notes are hard to understand without attending. Poor criticism handling as he tried to take down ALL notes due to an inflammatory post on his bad handwriting and notes. I feel for him but he's uninterested in improving based on our feedback.

Seems like he dosen't care about any of his students doing well in the class. When we complained that his lecture notes were impossible to read he took them down online saying "if you guys don't like them then I won't post them". His test reviews are awful indications of the exams and he ignores anyone trying to point out his faults.
Lectures were like reading chicken scratch. Had to constanly use the textbook to fufill my learning. Yener is alright but just does not teach well
great professor, easy exam

I am in algo currently trying to prepare for a quiz we have at the end of class despite the fact that he has completely abnegated his responsibility to teach the material. I got a 6/15 on the last quiz and I do not know what I did wrong, or how to improve. His teaching style fosters an environment that discourages understanding the material.
Worst Professor! Incredibly rude and had a rude Post doc. Lacks basic courtesy towards students

Professor Yener is without a doubt the worst professor I've encountered since I've been in college. For lectures he just copies directly out of the low quality textbook onto the document camera. The labs typically don't really work that well for teaching you the material. 3 test dictate 80% of the your grade. Luckily he will curve at the end.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: took crypto 1 with yener and algorithm, he is one of the worse prof i had for cs courses. He did not communicate with student at all, no responses in piazza and email, he said he had a busy schedule but he was busy the entire semester. No explanantion of test and homeworks, always delayed posting lecture slides for more than a week

Very scatterbrained, will do things like accidentally schedule a test on Thanksgiving. Lectures are dry. Homeworks vary from moderately easy to somewhat hard. Final project is long but fun/rewarding. Tests are insanely hard and tend to assign disproportionate point values to things that were barely mentioned, while not testing on major concepts.
Took crypto with him first semester as a freshman... was both the toughest and the most enjoyable course I had. If the thought of cracking RSA on exams doesn't scare you off, you'll fit right in.

Nao was totally awesome. I think art is a hard subject that is very controversial, so if you're a sheltered freak, living under a rock with super conservative parents, she will blow your mind. cognitive dissonance from real learning makes you wanna hate her but she's the most caring person ever. she cared about me. bigtime
Facebook-based class interaction, movies in class, and encourages free and creative thinking...  A breath of fresh air for this engineering school environment.

It appears as if many of the RPI students who gave Nao ridiculously harsh criticism are afraid of themselves and being free thinkers.  Nao excels at getting students to think outside the norm and she challenges us to look at ourselves in new ways.  She is wonderful!

Nao is the coolest. If you can take a class with her, do it! She has done a lot of really interesting work, and is very helpful if you have any questions. Just look up "Nanookie of the North" on YouTube. It explains Nao to a "T".

She is a little weak in the music arena but strong in film performance and fine art, but as a capstone teacher she is varied enough. as long as shes not restricting media thats not "creative enough" or is too "corporate" for her tastes, i think shes all around totally cool.

She studied at the San Francisco Art institute, I think she critique's bad work harshly, but usually the work presented is clearly mediocre, and therefore deserves the critism. RPI students are just living in a bubble and she tends to pop it with clear explanations of what the real world is like.

nao is smart and knows how to be an artist and teaches that expertly. she's creative, her work is great, and the work she shows is great as well. she's sometimes disorganized but you can learn a lot by examining how she's fashioned her own arts career.
great
"Precisely what's wrong with the EMAC department."
dumb b*tch.  can't teach.  won't learn anything.  waste of time and money.  and she has a knack of picking horrible TAs.
She seems to have her own agenda but is a nice person.  MAybe not the best teacher, maybe a little stange, but if you really wanted to get something out of her course you could.

The worst part of this is that she's incredibly stupid.  She's teaching a class that she has no knowledge of, regardless of the fact that she's spent (and wasted) her life in the same field.  She knows nothing.  By far the worst class I've taken, ever.
