Absolutely, without a doubt, the worst professor I've ever had, period.  A trained monkey could do her job.  She offers no incentive to get involved with the class.  Why she gets paid, I have no idea.  The class is easy as hell, but it's intolerable.

Absolutely horrid, she doesn't teach she just shows movies and wants you to agree with her not that it matters. If you can get Igor Vamos to teach, he guest taught once and I learned more in a day than all year in her class.
Joke of a class.  A waste of 4 credits.  Take it if it's required, but try something more intense if you're allowed to skip it.
Tough but fair
Excellent professor, very kind, ask for research projects

Probably one of the most disorganized classes I've taken. I never knew what was going on. There seemed to be little communication between the professor and the TA, and the students were consistently out of the loop. I didn't get most of my grades back. He is very quiet and hard to understand, but tests were easy and quizzes were graded leaniently.
Very intelligent with regards to mathematics, but cannot teach to save his life.
WONDERFUL PROFESSOR
Complex Variables was a freaking nightmare. He made it super difficult in 6 weeks and there was way too much homework. DO NOT TAKE IT WITH THIS DR.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Multivariable Calculus is rough, but Boudjelka makes it less horrible. His lectures are rough and super theory heavy, but you will learn the material. The tests are GREAT super super fair and straight forward. HW can be 'fun'. Of all the multi teachers at RPI, I'd definitly reccomend Boudjelka.

Very interesting man. Unbelievably intelligent. Pretty hard to get down all he is saying in lecture, he moves quick. If you go to recitation and do your best to pay attention in class you will get an A with ease. He's super accessible and very willing to help if you ask. Just study what he tells you for the tests and you will get an A

Excellent professor- very intelligent and truly does care about students. The class is an easy grade (tests are easy if you are prepared) and you will learn a lot if you pay attention in lectures and do the suggested homework problems. Boudjelkha is always willing to help those struggling as well. Definitely take this class.

Not the best teacher, however he does give many examples. Homework is where I've learned most of the material. He is, fortunately, an easy grader and his tests have are predictable. Although he is not the best teacher, he is certainly brilliant and is to be respected. He is also pretty funny, but his humor is often hidden behind his thick accent.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Figure out all the homework and go to the class before tests and you can get an A. You do not even need to take the final

He clearly has the subject mastered, but teaches in a manner that skips basic definitions and basic concepts. The end result is page after page of notes that are ultimately meaningless to students. I recommend skipping the lectures and reading the textbook instead. Go to recitation and ALAC to learn the subject material.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: I'm not going to talk about the tests because I've not taken one yet. But one thing I know for sure is that I don't learn anything from this class. The lecture is boring, and all he does is giving theorems and proofs to those theorems. There is no concrete example of how to use those theorems in lectures.

Bojangles is one of the most intelligent and enthusiastic professors Ive had at RPI. But he sucks at teaching. Going to class is not usually helpful and may make you feel very overwhelmed and confused. Not to worry!! Make sure you do the homework and study solely from the back tests and you will do just fine.
Has a heavy accent, which wasn't too bad to understand. His handwriting, however, is very small and hard to read.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Bojangles is a genius but he's a really bad professor. He doesn't take a breath for you to actually understand what he's saying or for you to write down his messy notes. You will good grade if you study the back tests but you won't actually learn anything. Show up early to tests. Lecture attendance is unnecessary and may confuse you more.
If you do your homework and use back tests you will be good. He was very good in office hours.
His  heavy accent and lack of a current course website don't stop him from being the REAL MVP  You can also call him Bojangles
very good professor, really nice to student, and easy to get A

Class is easy. Professor is hard to understand sometimes in class because he moves very quickly but is very helpful in office hours. Don't really need to go to lectures but I recommend it because he will try to get to know students who go to class.  Homework can be long if you want to actually put effort in. Tests are the same as back tests.
Lectures are pretty useless.  Just be hopeful that your TA is good.
Go to class. Do the homework. Succeed.
Is good teacher like It
An overall good professor his lectures are a bit hard to understand due to his accent but he teaches all concepts clearly.

He seems nice enough but isn't a very good teacher. He speaks quietly and constantly and writes constantly, rarely pausing to explain unless asked to, and then his explanations aren't very good. DiffEq was extremely easy anyway, though, as he basically gives you the exam questions. I think he tries to be a good prof but comes up short. Hard accent.

Teaches you to do PDEs hella fast, also Fourier transforms and wall heat. Says very profound a lot, would recommend. Course is approachable for illiterate students, I can't read and I did fine. Happy to talk to you at office hours, very thick accent, being fluent in Arabic before attending class is recommended.

Don't need to go to lecture, but make sure you go to his lecture before every exam, those review sessions are golden in terms of studying for an exam because you encounter every scenario you can see on an exam. Other than that, don't bother copying proofs that he writes in class, you'll never see them on a test

Ignore all of these lazy cynics complaining about how horrible Boudjelkha is. Pay attention in lecture, go to recitation if the TA is worth it, and do the homework. He practically gives you the test questions the class before. It's a shame that a good guy and a better teacher gets slammed here by the ones still whining about his accent.

All of the negative comments are very un just. This is one of the most caring professors I have encountered in my college career. He basically tells you exactly what is going to be on the test, and will go through any problem step by step in his office hours. His biggest down fall is his lectures are fairly boring, usually non stop note taking.
Easy A, but you might not actually learn anything.  Lectures are terrible and completely optional.

I managed to get an A in his DiffEQ class without ever going to lecture, but ACalc was different. Not that going to lecture helps much either, since he's incomprehensible. The homeworks alone don't fully prepare you for the exams and he uses weird notation. Lectures are like a game, you try to sort through the mumbling and extract what's important.
If you are failing his Diffeq class, you shouldn't be at RPI.

Boudjelkha is one of the smartest people I've ever met.  He knows a ton about math, and if you go to lectures, he'll give you some good shortcuts for solving problems.  He's a bit tough to understand, but he posts his lecture notes online and tells you exactly what's going to be on the tests, so it's pretty easy to do well in his classes.

I have to say that the poor ratings he gets mostly are due to his accent. If you go find him during his office hours, he is extremely helpful and friendly. I mean you cant do anything about the accent. But a nice professor overall.
Bad teacher. Class was boring and useless. Homeworks were unrelated to class. Tests were poorly done.
Class consisted of him mumbling while he wrote constantly. He never paused. A brutally boring class.

This class is as easy as you make it. Boudjelkha is hard to understand but he has a grad TA reteach the 3 weekly lectures in an hour. Skip class and just go to those. The format of the tests is the same year to year. Buy a cramster account and learn the hw as you copy it. Easy A.
If you copy down what he puts on the projectors, you'll do fine.  However, he misinterprets most questions you'll ask him, and does a very poor job of explaining/elaborating on what he did.

Awesome guy. A little hard to follow in lecture but if you take notes and look at them later you can see what he did. Super willing to help you if you go in a talk to him during office hours. Tests and quizzes are a breeze as long as you do some amount of studying. Overall an easy A.

One of the easiest A's I got at RPI.  Pro tips for success: 1.  Take good notes in lecture, but exclude the proofs, you don't need those. 2. Go to the Wednesday night review sessions and/or ALAC tutoring if you need help. 3. Do ALL of the homework and don't start the night before it's due. 4. Back tests are your friend.  5. The final is optional!

Math itself is a language, so english shouldn't be a problem. In his original country, he was really recognised as a genius due to his research theories. However, his exams were extremely difficults to solve when he used to teach in his original country. If he's not well recognised in USA, it means that there's a problem in math students level.
He isn't as bad as everyone says, just pay attention in class and his accent won't seem that bad. Very willing to help students and does plenty of examples to make sure students get the concepts.

Really easy class. Do all the homeworks from cramster or rpistudygroup because pretty much none of the problems you do will show up on the tests. The tests are a piece of cake. 4 problems and the back tests are almost identical. I'd recommend going to class because his methods for solving problems are more understandable than the book.
He is my favorite professor at RPI thus far.
easy grader, interested in students achievments, office hours are helpful (esp for maple projects) ive never gotten such a high math grade before

Great class and completely straight forward.  He gives you the equations you need to know right away and then gives you more than enough examples.  One of the easiest graders around and a nice guy overall.  One downside is his accent can be hard to cut through but the material is not too complicated.

His class was an easy A, though I did learn quite a bit.  He lectures are a bit on the theory side, though when possible he explains the physical meaning or gives an example where it is useful; alot of what doesn't make sense is clarified by the homework.  He prepares students for exams very well.  Simply, he wants students to do well.
Excellent Professor. He is a little dry, but he explains things well with lots of examples.

His lectures were hard to understand, partly because of his accent and low speaking volume. I ended up skipping most of them, but by doing the homework and going to recitation I managed to learn the material. Diff EQ is a pretty dull subject, so I don't really blame him for not being very interesting.
Keeps it simple and shows you exactly what you need to know for tests.  It may seem unclear at first, but the homeworks help to clear anything up and usually end up being harder than the test itself.

He is a very smart person. He tries his best to communicate, but that is usually not enough. His exams are very straightforward and with just a little preparation an A is easy to achieve, BUT I highly suggest back exams and pray for a good TA. Try Drop In Tutoring or his online notes. I did not go to class after 2nd exam and still got an A.
very easy tests
Do not go to lecture.  Pray that you get a good TA.  Go to recitation.

Soft spoken and has a thick accent, either sit close or hope he wears a microphone.  Other than that, very knowledgeable, focuses more on pure math than application (doesn't give any word problems).  Very easy grader: if you do the Diff Eq right but screw up arithmetic or calculus you won't lose much, just show you know the process.
Decent teacher. Writes out proofs for everything and gives plenty of examples. Not big on the conceptual side or giving you that nice feeling of understanding. Pretty fair grader.

He isn't that hard to understand , nor is it terribly difficult to read his handwriting. He more or less tells you what will be on tests. He is a really nice guy and if you talk to him about your grade and let him know you care, you will do better. Go talk to him at least once study, go to class, and do the homework, and you should get an A
Very easy test if you know the form of the solution. He is very passionate about teaching and thinks that some forms of solving differential equations are "like magic"

This guy is quite possibly the funniest professor I have ever had-- honestly just listen to the stuff he says, its hilarious.  He's also incredibly smart-- one time a kid challenged an "assumption" he wrote down and Prof. B responded with a 3 page proof off the top of his head, impressive. Watch schmidts videos and do the homework,you will befine

I agree with the some of the previous comments on this forum. This guy is not fair guy. Some people say he is an easy grader and nice. But he is NOT. He is nice to only certain type of people and if he doesnt like you, he will make sure he take it off your exams.
Tells you exactly what is going to be on each exam- makes the class relatively easy.

His approach to teaching mathematics is geared toward mathematics majors. His tests can be hard due to the limited number of points. (20 point tests translate to 5% for each point...) Good professor overall.

Trust me, take Diff EQ with this guy. He is by far the easiest grader I have ever seen. He goes through proofs in lecture, but you dont need to learn them. Instead, follow the tons of examples he puts up, cause the homework and tests are exactly like these.
easy stuff but lectures make it seem more complicated than it really is

DO NOT GO TO LECTURE. YOU WILL KICK YOURSELF FOR WASTING 50 MINUTES OF YOUR LIFE EVERYTIME YOU GO. Easy grader though, the final is optional. Id take him compared to the other professors but just know its pointless for you to go to lecture. Read the book and watch David Schmidts online videos, it got me through well.
Great Professor, a little hard to understand but i learned a lot in his class, easy grader, buy you still have to learn everething

His accent and complex explanation of subject matter make the subject much more difficult than it actually is.  He uses complex proofs during class that use notation and ideas out of students' understanding. Very boring. Homework is fairly understandable, some complexities. Tests are extremely straightforward, and final is optional. Not recommended

He is a kind and friendly person. When you have questions, he is always glad to help. When teaching, usually he not only tell the practical part, but the proof and principle as well. But...it is sometimes really hard to get a clear understanding of what he is talking about...
No Comments

He is not a nice profesosor, not an understanding professor. iHe treats you depending who you are, if you appear to be quiet and hide, he dont care about you. But you if those people who see aggressive, he will be nice to you. But he dont require final exams in his class, its optional which is good

He's very hard to understand, and he writes very small, so lectures aren't that useful, unless these things aren't a problem for you.  If you're good at reading the text for most of your info and then asking some questions to clarify, then you'll be fine.  The material isn't that hard.  It's similar to Multivariable Calc.

Boudjelkha teaches math how it should be taught, with examples. In his lectures he'll show hundreds of different situations for each type of problem. Understanding him is tough at times, but if you just follow his math everything becomes clear. Exams are easy and homeworks are easy if you don't suck. Check out Schmidt videos for anything else.

This professor will go much out of his way to help students learn. He is very reasonable and he will always tell you exactly what is going to be on the test. He is not the greatest at giving lectures, but this isn't the only part of a teacher's job. If you go to his office hours and try to do well, you will.

Lectures are bad, just does a bunch of proofs.  Do the HW and listen during both recitations to do well.  He grades easily and teaches different stuff than the other professors.  Not a hard class, just a chore to get through.
you cant understand a thing he's saying, skips steps when he does proofs/examples.  watch schmidt videos if you wish to survive this class

Cant understand anything he says but if you watch Schmidt videos you will do good on his tests except the last one which you have to read the book. I got a B by never going to class, copying all the homeworks, and studying the night before the test.

This guy is not nearly as bad as everyone makes him out to be and neither is his accent. He likes to do the proofs in class, but you don't need to take those down; make sure that you pay attention and copy down his examples, though. His tests are not hard, and he is very willing to help you if you ask him. He wants to see all of his students suceed

What made me go to class all semester is the guilt I would have if I didn't go. He sounds he's on Nyquill, and his accent is terrible. Does all proofs, and like one example, and skips steps there. Doesn't even answer questions. Example: girl: "where did u get that equation?" Mr.B "We took it out of the sky." Worst professor ever, even for RPI.
bojangles is the man! he might not make much sense in class, but he's a very easy grader, and if you go talk to him, he'll help you out ;-)

Lectures are useless. He talks about what he's writing down (proofs), but not in english, and he stands in front of the projector so you can't see what he's writing down. He's not helpful at all. He grades his tests incredibly easy because he knows that you learned more from one of Schmidt's online videos than you ever did from all his lectures.

This guy is the worst professor I have ever had.  He does not speak clearly and should be fired from his job at the first possible moment! Fact is he may be passing, but you come outta that class with nowing about as much as you went in with, which sucks when you go into other harder courses where you actually need the material. DONT TAKE HIS CLASS

If you like hearing the professor, lectures in English, or legible notes this professor is NOT, I REPEAT NOT, for you.  I think I could learn more about Diff Eq from watching teletubbies than I did from sitting through the horrible lectures.  If you do get stuck with him, try to get a good TA.
No Comments

what can we say about this man...he has his own group on facebook, he's a freedom fighter (look it up on google) he has the thickest accent known to made and understanding him is a chore. One of the easiest graders ever. Shout out to Sharath for getting me an A in the class.
only does the proofs on the board and the material he does in class is VERY HARD.  The test are easier though, but if you don't know how to do any of the problems your screwed.
cant understand a damned thing he sais, bores you to death and does not do anywhere near a good job of teaching material

Whether you call him Bubba J, Bajorkabork, Boudie, or anything else, the fact remains that you will hate this guy by the end of the semester.  A thick accent and horrible English skills make Bubba impossible to understand, and if you were like me and not blessed with an amazing TA you will fail this class if you can't read the text without sleeping

Dear lord, don't take diffEQ from him.  Too many proofs, impossible to follow, doesn't answer questions.  I went to every class and was still lost most of the time.  Easy grader. I got an A but that's because my TA Pablo was totally the man, and he's not TAing anymore so you have no hope.

Mohamed's notes were pretty hard to follow and the lectures were boring. However, he tells you what are on the tests and it's pretty straight forward stuff that just takes some memorization. He's also willing to explain stuff to you, which can be a big help. I got an A in the class w/o taking the final, since I got a B and C in Calc I and II.

Pay attention in his class.  Write down everything he writes on the overheads durring lecture.  If you do this and put in some effort you will do fine in his class.   He is one of my favorite professors here...but i don't think i could get to know him because his english is not that great.
Look at this. Just follow the formula; don't worry about the rest. We've proved it; just use the formula. We have example number...um....3. It's so simple. Just follow the formula.

Difficult material. He tends to skip steps, leaves students wondering. Starts class right when he walks in (come early if you're going to classes) goes a little late. Thick accent. Fair tests. Tests are on Mondays. I recommend getting a Friday TA section, if possible.
we call him Mr. Bojangles, but he doesnt dance. somehow i got an A.

oh my god.... worst teacher ever.  assumes that people care about the proofs only and not actually how to do anything.  doesn't help that you can hardly understand him.  grr.  super easy exams though.
One time this chick asked him to go over a solution, and he gave her a blank stare for a while and then said "moving on" and continued to the next problem.  Awesomest prof ever!
hard to understand. real easy grader just do the homework. onoy tests the basics
This man gave me a gift that noone else on earth could -- The Wronskian. and i love him for it. He just really needs to shower

hard accent but once you get used to it you'll love him.... you'll feel utterly lost at times but dont worry he'll answer everything eventually... grades very nicely become friends with him and you'll ace the class
Very thick accent, very confusing lectures. He has good notes you can download and is lenient with grading, as long as you talk to him.
No Comments

The most confusing professor I've ever had. Most of the lectures are spent doing mind numbing derevations of every concept covered. The differing test forms he gives out significantly vary in difficulty. The last test was extremely difficult. Get a good TA or be a math major or you're doomed.

A terrible teacher who can't communicate with students.  A very smart man, but he is not good at teaching.  His thick accent makes him difficult to understand.  He is also bad at answering questions, (he just stares back at you), or interacting with other humans in general.
just use his notes and u will do fine the book sucks
HAS TERRIBLE ENGLISH.  the only words i can understand are 'the wronskian'.  he also chooses not to bathe so be prepared if you need to talk to him one on one.  grades pretty leniently.
he's spastic, u can't follow him
Its hard to follow the lectures, but if you write everything down and do the homework, you should have no problem acing the tests.

Mohammed isn't that great.  Very unclear about his steps to solve problems, almost has a belittling response to some students questions.  His accent makes it difficult to understand what is going on, and despite being culturally respectful, it makes the learning process more difficult. $40K matters.
No Comments

Too bad I didn't understand a word he was saying. The TA's for his class are awesome though. If you skip his class and take his tests it isn't too bad - be prepared for his homework though, and make sure to do it!! it really helps reinforce the topics
very difficult to understand

Hard to understand. The only reason I did well was because my TA was awesome. Tests can be hard but he grades leniently. Hope for a good TA or you're screwed. Also, his version of diffeq is drastically different from any other prof's.
Wise professor that comes up with amazing ways of solving simple calculus problems (math tricks).  Just study his lecture notes and go to his lectures and you'll get that A.  Trust me.
Starts class early and runs late.  Hard to understand in lectiures. Giving a 9am exam the morning after spring break.
Seemed to know his stuff and was willing to give extra help.

His section of Differential Equations was the easiest of all that RPI offers -- 80% of his students recieved A's, and it's not because he's a great teacher, it's because of TA Jay (who rocks) and the way he grades.  He is completely incomprehensible, btw.

he's an awesome teacher. Talk about someone who is a genius and willing to help his students whenever possible. As for his accent, in this diverse world we need to understand each other, and we cannot make accents a barrier.

He's a nice professor and is always willing to help but his accent can make things a little difficult to understand. A good chunk of the students would skip out on his lecture and not bother to come until test time. He's new this year (2003).

Class activities and homework and useless and confusing.  I have gained no knowledge on how to right professionally.  The course itself is fine, but she completely disregarded the set syllabus and turned the class into something it should never be.  She also expects your life to revolve around this class.

Unclear with assignments, there will be a small acknowledgement about part of the tremendous amount of hw, but you would need to be a mind reader to know what was due. Acts as if her class is the most important class at RPI. Grading is based on foggy premises highlighted after the essay has been graded. Classwork is dry and has no function.
Absolutely a horrible teacher. If you value your grade or your education, get somebody else.

Professor Miller is clearly passionate about art, but I occasionally felt like there were two different courses being taught at once. She's definitely a film professor, but as long as you take the class somewhat seriously, you'll do fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed Docs, and I enjoyed having Professor Miller. She's quite lax about grading as long as you show that you care and put in effort, and she wants to see all her students unlock their creativity and find their passion within the realm of documentary filmmaking. Pretty easy A, and some pretty interesting content to boot!

Took her documentary class, and kinda slept my way through it. She gives good feedback, so if you take this class seriously (unlike most of the class) you'd actually learn. Just show up to class and you're good.

Burt can be confusing, and contradictory, but he is also motivating and inspiring. You will do things to appease him, and focus much more on concept than on design details.You will have to work on a project with an empathetic or environmental focus. Inventor's was stressful, difficult, and fun. And has changed the way I see myself and the world.

Inventor's Studio is all about the creative process, and this is no easy thing to learn, let alone teach, and Burt does a great job if you listen to him. Some people have difficulty learning this because they are too narrow-minded and focus on the destination and not the journey. My advice is to keep an open mind and you will succeed.

I took Swersey's new class "Creativity, Innovation and Entrep." It was an interesting class, but very disorganized. His philosophy and his speeches sometimes conflict and are hypocritical. Puts down innovative ideas that aren't philanthropic. He  sometimes alienates students by thinking that his meaning of "innovation" is only right. Easy A doe

Burt genuinely cares about helping his students to reach their potential. Advice: go to his office hours, actually try some of the creative exercises, and don't feel self conscious about doing something out of your comfort zone.  If you approach this course with the intent to learn and become creative, you will.

Burt is an amazing teacher. He demands a lot of work and is a bit disorganized but will push you to your creative limits to create something to change the world. The best teacher I've had overall at RPI. He doesn't just teach innovation, he inspires it.

Warning: If you can't deal with a vague, unstructured and highly demanding class, don't sign up for a class with Burt. It's very frustrating. That said, you can learn a lot from him if you can put up with him.

Burt does a lot of good for RPI, and for the world beyond, by challenging people to think outside the box and push themselves to the brink. His classes are generally extremely disorganized, and he often asks for you to work beyond what is reasonable for any course. But if you don't get too frustrated, you'll find him to be extremely insightful.

Burt is a vision and an inspiration to all those who want to make a difference in this world. He WILL drive you absolutely crazy at times, but at the end you will realize the value of his dedication to pushing everyone in new directions. Don't be afraid to take chances and be ready to commit yourself to this class.

This is not a typical class: if you are a motivated person who wants to make a big impact on the world Burt can help you get there. Yes it is a lot of work, and Burt will push you, but it is because we are capable of doing so much more than we realize. This class changed my life.
Nice, vague, disorganized

Single best professor I've had at RPI. Can lead you down a rabbit hole if you cannot extract meaning from his words/assignments. Unparalleled vision for innovation. He pushes students harder then most students care to work but the results can be amazing. I ended up with a patent as a result. To get the "A" you need to show interest and initiative.

Wow. What a class. Stretches you to the limit but for good reason. Felt like I learned more than any other class at RPI. Those who didnt enjoy the class arent flexible enough! Its not your typical engineering class with clear goals...its much more, and if you participate you may create something amazing.

He was either very vague as to what he wanted or wanted way more than could be completed in the time allocated.  He thinks that this is the only class students are taking and expects them to invest all their time in  it.  Make sure to decide on a project you want to work on or else risk having a torturous semester.

this guy is out there in the ether. he doesnt ever have class planned out, and is always scattered. He is always brining in expert guests to replace the need for him to teach himself. the class gives you sweet opportunities if you want to take them, but swersey thinks that his class is the only thing that matters in your life, it can get really old

His classes are the MOST difficult, frustrating, and painful that you will ever find at this school. You will be emotionally and physically stretched past your limits. However, along the way you may learn crucial life lessons that cost people jobs and relationships. Take at your own risk (and only if your other courses are <11 credits and easy).

Has had no official training as a teacher, thus has no idea how to teach or even guide students.  Under no circumstances should you take any class with this professor.  He simply doesn't live in the real world (we call it Swerseyland).  He will make unreasonable demands of your time and energy, and will then criticize your best work next class...

Worst professor I have ever had. If you get stuck in his IED section, then get out! It's not worth taking his course. He teaches based on the principle of "my way or the highway." If he tells you to make a car with 3 wheels, next time you see him that car better have 3 wheels. Extremely hard to understand. No accent, just ridiculous. Immature! Fail

Unfortunately we figured him out too late in the semester. The key is to fully write up your report, then delete half and hand it in. When he asks you to resubmit, give him the full original for a A/B grade. If you give him the full originally, you'll fail and still have to resubmit it.

Terrible at describing what he wants.  Would advise only taking in Inventor Studio if you already have an idea or product you want to develop, having him give you very vague problems to solve (Fix global warming) is awful.

Nice guy, worst prof ive ever had.  Never actually explains what he wants.  Contradicts himself constantly.  Rambles for hrs about things that dont apply to the class.  Often tells students they are wrong with no factual basis for it.  Absolutly cannot handle being dissagreed with.  Ruined the class for me.

Burt Swersey is a nice guy at heart, and a very smart guy as well.  However, that in no way translates to him being a good professor.  He doesn't make it clear at all what he is looking for, and when he does attempt to say what he wants, it is usually unreasonable.  Overall, this was the worst class i have ever taken.  I DON'T reccomend this class.

Good guy with good intentions, but way too vague. He definitely needs to have a structured lesson plan, with a timeline, and he needs to stick to it. He's easy to get on your good side, though. If you show some initiative and be a leader in your group (IED or Inventor's) he'll like you.
Robert Ingalls of engineering.
Seems like a nice guy but it's very difficult to understand what he wants in the assignments. Also, occasionally talks about random and unnecessary things in class.
Prof. Swersery cares about what you learn. He more concerned about building a solid foundation so that you will exceed in the real world. He is a really good man..
If you want to do well in IED, DO WHAT SWERSEY suggests!! and have a good notebook.  All grade is based on his opion of you and your notebook.

For this course, the only way to get an A is to document everything you did in the notebook & list down all the new things u learned from the beginning to the end of the course(Very2 important). Recipe for A in his class.

He's garnered a lot of experience over his career and I think he truely wants to share that with us for our benefit.  But despite how long he's been teaching, he doesn't seem to have developed a steady lesson plan to do that.  Very vauge requirements, inconsistent, and prone to playing favorites.
helps you develop your ideas to actually be patentable and commericially feasible
Confusing lectures and requirements.  Not recommended.

He really makes you want to do well.  I thought he was a very nice person and did his job well.  He will always push you to do better no matter how well you may be doing.  He cares about how much you improve and how much effort you give.  The end result is not always important to him.  Great Guy.
NOT GOOD for PDI majors...  Swersey thinks he knows a lot about everything, especially patents.  He's really just an old, confused man that needs a one way ticket to the home.
No Comments
Do not sign anything he gives you. Be wary of any legal/patent advice he gives you.

Swersey is the true american idol. He totally kicks ass. He is very helpful when you are stuck with sumthin. If you do your work, there is no way you can get lower than a B. All you have to do is try. It's all about the learning!
He's a nice guy, but he's just exceedingly vague. Take an easygoing art teacher and put him at RPI. You've got Swersy.
Not recommended for engineers...  Horrible.
With any luck the guy retires like he should have years ago.  Avoid him and his rambling lectures as best you can.  Horrible professor, but a decent guy.
Bad for engineering.
Possibly the worst professor on campus.

It's about learning folks.  He wants you to learn more than you possibly can.  He emphasizes learning at all costs, not success, not finishing the project.  He changes his mind often, just disregard most of his suggestions and do what you think is right.
Unless you are a mechanical engineer, Swersey will not know what is going on (or where he is) when you talk to him.

Professors like Swersey ruin RPI's reputation and discourage its students from the field of engineering.  A conversation with a rock makes more sense and is more productive than with Swersey.  I wish there was a -1,000 rating for Helpfulness and Clarity.

Very helpful when approached for advice. Following his advice had successful results.He is accused of being vague, but the course is designed to be open ended to enhance the learning process.Such a nice guy.Honestly a very good teacher if given a chance.

He really tries to help us. If you do your work and do what he says, you will do fine. If he gives you a suggestion, ask him if that is really what he wants you to do, then document it. If he changes his mind about it, show him your documentation.
Horrible teacher. Very unclear, makes class extremely frustrating. His classes are a total waste of time. He may mean well, but he should not be teaching.. he isnt even a professor!

Hes a wacky harmless guy.He likes people who make as much sense as he does-minimal.If you make the slightest effort to think outside the box youll do fine.Dont go into his class with a well defined idea of what you want to do...he will make you change it.
Very nice dude who really means well
I think Professor Swersey is a very good teacher.  He helps the learning process but does not do it for you.  I had a very good semester with him!

Changes his mind at least twice in the same coversation. never gives clear direction. he picks his favorite students at the beginning of the semester and exhibits favortism towards these students. one of the worst profs i've had.
worst Prof i ever had!  need to get his act together and not change his mind every 10 seconds.  should not be teaching senior capstone at all!
seemed like he always meant well, but unfortunately it didnt always come out that way, due to this everyone is expecting a grade lower than they think they really deserve
Wanted one thing on monday and something different on thursday, extremely unclear.
completely out of his mind.  Makes inane suggestions and changes what he wants from you on a daily basis.  Impossible to please.
No Comments
Swersey is awesome!  He rocks, and he only means well!!!
Those who can, do.  Those who can't, teach

Goes back on his word, senile, can't make a clear point, can't gather his thoughts, can't stick to a single idea for more than a minute, very unrealistic.  Claims he's searching for creativity when in reality he wants you to create what he's thinking.

never keeps on the same track. Always switches ideas from day to day. If you do somethign he suggests, he later comes back and says  no no not liek that ..keeps you working till the last minute redesigining and redesigning instead of sticking to one soln.
BS doesn't stand for Burt Swersey
This man is not living in the same reality as everyone else. Too Ecentric, and wtf is up with that hat??!
This guy is way out of the loop in terms of engineering and life in general

I took his Hawaiian Philosophy & Political Science courses which I dont see listed anymore. But nonetheless, Bruce is one of the most passionate professors I ever had. He is funny & shamelessly himself. He aint afraid to tell it how it is either. He has a unique/unconventional way of teaching which was different yet refreshing. Heavy on group work

Bruce is a phenomenal professor and teacher. His lectures are very thoughtful. If you ask questions and pay attention in class he visibly appreciates it. Focuses on concepts, but you get a good dose of hw problems too.

Professor Watson is one of the best professors I've had. His lectures are super interesting and he really puts forward the effort to make sure you know the material.  Tests are pretty straight forward, just stuff from the class notes. The homework can be a little difficult, but he always leaves time in class so you can ask questions.
Fantastic
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Prof. Watson is a great guy, I learned a ton in his Geochemistry course. He really wants you to learn, and it shows. If you attend class, think about the material and ask him questions, you'll do fine on exams. Remember, if you have any questions, just go see him - you'll be glad you did!
No Comments
No Comments

he was okay. i feel like he doesn't do that much as a professor because he's rly busy with RCC so he's out of class a lot. his lectures are solid though. labs can be time-consuming but are fun. i actually really liked this class.
very biased around certain people, especially girls. kinda weird.

i thought the class was ok. my main issue was that dr. callahan didn't really do a good job at answering people's questions - he would just be like "well what do you think" or tell you to figure it out yourself. besides that, it wasn't too bad. group project is fun but takes up a decent amount of time throughout the semester. labs kind of annoying

Dr. Callahan is very personable and cares about his students. His teaching style is very hands-off, though. He will lecture on some topics, but not code. He may provide a resource or two, but when it comes to any code, he does not teach it. The class was fun when I got what was happening, but if you do not like learning on your own, beware.

Professor Callahan is one of the best professors I've had. He cares a lot about his students and if something is not working he's willing to change an assignment to fit the needs of his students. His classes are usually filled with laughs and jokes and a very fun atmosphere. 11/10

Horrible professor. He does not give clear feedback or guidance for coding assignments. He is also a pain in the ass to work with. The class overall is easy but the tests include many curveball questions. I would definitely not recommend taking any class with him.
Very fun and enthusiastic professor. Only a few assignments in this course but all are very doable

Dr Callahan has an interactive teaching style and encourages group projects which makes learning fun and engaging. He is also flexible and lenient with students which makes it easier to learn and understand the course material. He was very knowledgeable on subject matters. Overall, I would highly recommend Brian Callahan as a professor.
Dr. Callahan is a really good professor, always reachable in office hour time, give good feedbacks. Lectures are easy to understand, gives reasonable deadline push, cares about students' feedbacks.
learned a lot about logic & other subjects too

Intro to Logic Based AI was great last semester.  Bringsjord is one of the most brilliant profs at rpi. The hyprslate software is definitely better than anything else I have seen for logic / discrete mathematics.

You definitely need to put in the independent work to benefit

The lectures can be interesting and thought-provoking. However, the class is graded through the Hyperslate program, which he does not spend time to guide through during lectures. Tests are graded generously; however, prepare to self-learn if you want to do well in that class. Best to avoid this class if you're taking it as a laid-back elective.
very good

Whole class is based on his self-developed online software which he does not take the time to teach about. All homework on said software is required- you will fail the class if you don't finish them. Tests are given the same format, grading is pretty generous. Can be a good class with some background in logic, but don't take for an easy grade.
He is a great lecturer, and is very lenient with deadlines, a lot of the homework assignment deadlines were extended.
Intro to Logic with him is pretty easy. He uses a weird program but other than that its pretty easy. The lectures are entertaining but not always that helpful, but overall a pretty solid class.

Selmer really is a caring professor, let alone possibly one of the most intelligent people on campus. He is willing to help a lot on homework problems (which are all on his $100 online software, similar to mastering). Homework problems aren't too difficult, and all the answers are on reddit. Tests are randomized per person but problems are not hard

Good guy generally but if you are looking for an easy A in a HASS course I would not recommend this. Unless you are a CS and are familiar with computational logic, this class is an unnecessary headache. His lectures are unrelated to all the homework and tests he assigns. You pay $100 for his software that he does not explain and expects you to know
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Selmer is a great professor. "Are Humans Rational?" is an easy A while being non-traditional. The course itself is easy, but if you take the material and give it thought, it is challenging and engaging. Selmer, like the course, is different, interesting, and ultimately a softie. He truly cares about students and spreading logic and rationality.

Actually I took both this course &the other one based on the Stanford software that Bringsjord is competing against. All I can say is that from the AI point of view HyperGrader and HyperSlate are cool. They get sluggish when hit hard, but the AI in them is really something. This isn't really an intro to logic. It's an intro to logic & AI.

This is an easy-A professor. He grades all the course materials very generously or even not mindfully. For example, at the beginning of the exam 3. He said everyone will get an A FOR THIS EXAM (only this exam, not the whole course). You must finish all the homework questions in hypergrader, or you will get a F in the homework part .

This class introduced me to something I'd never heard about despite stuyding a lot of comp sci before getting to RPI -- logic programming. Bringsjord has unique knowledge of the connection between formal logic and programming, and that was really helpful. Really knows his stuff when it comes to comp sci and logic intersecting.

Intro to Logic is a great class to take with a difficult courseload. It's very easy to get an A while not trying at all (although you will be very confused the whole way through). However I would still recommend trying your best, since Bringsjord is world famous in this field and is a really interesting professor (albeit strange at times).
Great prof, famous but humble.

It's kinda cool taking a class with a famous AI guru, but his views on AI & logic are kinda tough on stat-based AI.  Lots of students get by without knowing what they're doing, but Bringsjord knows they're faking it, cause of his AI grading technology.
Great professor.  Extremely knowledgeable and helpful.

About the only thing I think is missing in Bringsjord's platform for teaching intro logic (and its really intro to *mathematical* logic, which he's pretty clear about, actually) is an automatic grading technology.  That would allow students to get instant analysis of their graphical proofs.  But basically I think this is a world-class course.

Personally, I think Bringsjord makes some of the material super hard so that he can find students with the potential to do research, while in the end he's pretty easy grade-wise.  So, if you just stick it out, your grade should be great, but it's really, really hard to nail all the problems.

I found some of the problems to be ridiculously hard. I'm not sure how some of my classmates got some of these problems, which are very mathematical in nature.  But I learned a lot, including that I probably shouldn't try to be a logician.  But Bringsjord is a great guy, and you can get a high grade even if like me you can't figure it all out.

The material Bringsjord teaches, at the level he teaches it at, can be downright impossible for mere mortals (students who don't plan to be logicians) to understand.  But if you seek him out and ask for help, he gives it with cheerfulness, and you can grasp a lot of it.  And then in the end he really doesn't grade that tough.

Before I got to my Analysis class as a math major I really didn't see the value of Bringsjord does, because it's really an intro to mathematical logic.  But what I'd learned about proofs  in his class saved my butt.

Bringsjord is a dynamite logic teacher, and his logics are cool, but the bottom line is that it's all very computational, and even specifically AI based.  If you want just old school paper and pencil stuff, stay away from this class.  But if you want to know how the heck he and his lab @ RPI built smart gadgets, this course unlocks the secrets.

If you want to study logic taught by a teacher just using someone else's logic book and courseware, don't go with Bringsjord.  He has his own novel approach to teaching mathematical logic, which is based on graphs, rather than linear sequences of symbols.  It's kind of cool taking the course from a prof famous in AI, & he uses logic for AI.

Some of the extra credit logic problems are so darn difficult that I'd estimate about 2% of the class understand them.  Despite some  ridiculously difficult proofs (which Bringsjord openly says only make sense at a place where students are technical), he's more than fair as a grader.
Well, Beingsjord is probably a genius, but he's very opinionated.  He basically condemns all current math education, and claims that his approachsoftware will revolutionize learning logic & math.
Intro to Logic is very easy but a bit dry. He is very responsive to emails and a really smart guy. The entire class is just a few homeworks.
class is too advanced to be called an introductory course
Very knowledgeable in his field, but seems to find it hard to teach those who are new to philosophy and logic. Great reference is you are already into logic, but not as helpful for beginners.

Bringsjord is very fun.  His stories are great, and he teaches in a way that makes the time pass quickly.  His courses are easy enough to get A's, yet you learn everything you are supposed to and have fun doing it.

The content of ModCon is not too bad, but the class is very dense and fast paced. ModCon is not a class you can learn the night before the exam, and if you fall behind or miss too many assignments you may reach the point of no return. 
Attend class, do the homeworks on time and ensure you understand the material, test out of the final.

Professor Cagliari is a great lecturer, who is comprehensive and cares about improving the course and helping you. Nothing in this course is really that hard, it is just all extremely time-consuming. Start homeworks as soon as possible, and pace yourself during exams to avoid running out of time like I did! Oh, and be sure to test out of the final!

Cagliari is great at explaining concepts and procedures but lectures are incredibly dense despite being two hours long. His assignments are very time consuming but definitely prepare you for exams. He is a very competent professor and holds incredibly high expectations for his students, but falling behind at all in his course may be unrecoverable.

Modcon is just a hard class. It's an entire field of engineering condensed into three credits. Cagliari does the best anyone could do with that situation. His lectures are content-heavy, but his delivery is excellent. He prioritizes making us learn instead of giving out A's for participation. Office hours are invaluable, he's very knowledgeable.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: ModCon by itself is a hard class. He teaches like we've been behind since day 1. Maybe I couldn't keep up, but he seems to leave out a lot of stuff when teaching too. GET READY TO STRUGGLE. This class will take up all your time. Grades won't update until like 2nd to last week and there is no curve. DO EVERYTHING YOU CAN TO TEST OUT OF FINAL.

One of the best Professors I've had at RPI, though the class is very difficult. He breaks down concepts into manageable chunks and explains things well. The crux is that mod con is 5lbs of content shoved into a 2 lb bag. Extremely time consuming class, but he will teach the information as best as you could ask for.

3 Credit class with 6 credits worth of work. Professor is a good guy but very strict when it comes to grading. He is also the only professor offered and tests are graded very harshly with no curve administered in possibly the hardest class at RPI. Be prepared to use 10+ pages of paper for each weekly homework assignment.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Only instructor for ModCon so buckle up...

Amaing prof! His lectures are extremely clear and easy to review after class. His office hours are helpful, and he gives out study guides before every exam. I had a great time in ModCon, even though the homeworks were uber difficult and took hours on end

Luiz is an superb guy stuck teaching the hardest MANE class if not the hardest class at RPI. It's is a lot of work but it is so worth because the exams are literally just that. It kills me that he doesn't make more jokes in class cause if he does, he would be a lot more personable. I don't think Modcon would be as clear if another prof taught it.

9 credits worth of work for a 3-credit class. Professor's teaching style and courseload needs a serious overhaul. The "project" is already decided, you can't do something based on your own interests. Very disappointing way to learn, and a complete lack of understanding of how this could be helpful in the real world.
Hardest engineering course at RPI

The lectures during the summer were long and he used the entire 2 hours 5 minutes of class time, sometimes even more. The homework also took way longer that it should have for a 3 credit course. That being said, the lectures were clear and well organized, and he did a good job of connecting the content that we were learning to previous lectures.

Averages on tests were in the 60s, but no curve administrated. For a 3-credit class it was a ridiculous workload, lectures were EXTREMELY BORINGGGGGG. 2 hours of yap followed by an in-class assignment that would be given with 5 minutes left but would take 45 and go well beyond the 2 hour mark.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This course was a LOT of work, but it definitely paid off to keep up with it.  The lectures were very high-quality and Professor Cagliari's notes were well-organized.  He was very helpful outside of class and understanding about extending certain deadlines.

Would not recommend taking MANE 4500 with Cagliari.  This class does not build a good intuition for control theory nor does it teach a wide variety of useful methods.  It instead focuses on laboriously utilizing needlessly complicated/outdated methods to solve what should be simple problems for a small corner of control theory.
Very kind professor. Definitely eccentric, but cares about her students and their well-being. A lot of reading assignments, but nothing too challenging.

She's overall pretty nice, but sometimes can seem a little condescending. While I didn't love the scope of the class, I can appreciate that she was passionate about what she teaches. This class was easy to get an A in if you go to class and do all the work.

The homework is heavy the first two weeks then lightens up to one assignment every two weeks. You get put in a group by the second/third week and are with them for the rest of the semester. If you do the work then you will get an amazing grade, and she only has one pop quiz. She is very passionate about what she teaches, and it shows.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Her class is structured in a very unique way that allows students to explore a variety of sustainability topics from different perspectives without doing much homework aside from reading. There are lots of class discussions, but participation is never mandatory. There is also a lot of work done in assigned groups, including the final project.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I had no issue with Dr. Cardinal, but she seemed to have a bit too picky and was harsh at times. She denied taking reports from students just because they were not stapled properly... Also, was not very considerate of students missing class due to not feeling well or having a broken leg... Class is an easy A if you do the work though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Lots of assigned reading, but you can generally skim the material and get the point. Classes are structured as debates, participation is encouraged but not mandatory. Overall good professor, was easy to communicate with and made grading clear and understandable.
Professor is very involved with the students in discussion, goes above a beyond to make classes fun and interactive. Very easy grader if you take the time and do the work.

Dr. Cardinal is very knowledgeable teacher and clearly is very passionate about what she teaches. Most assignments in this class are very easy, and the longer assignments have very specific grading criteria which she is strict about. The professor does make some class blocks more interesting through nature walks and exploring the city.

I took Sustainability Debates to see if I was interested in a Sustainability a minor and this class helped me want to do that. Dr Cardinal is nice and respectful of all opinions, through is a bit strict with some things. It's a lot of reading, though especially in the beginning, and the final is a group project.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Dr. Cardinal is a wonderful professor and passionate in her field. Classes are interesting and engaging and she is always open to new ideas from students' perspectives. Everything for the course was very clearly laid out in the syllabus. I would highly recommend taking a course with her.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Cardinal is a joyful teacher, with lively lectures, a respectful attention to inclusion and social justice causes, and a careful adherence to principled education. Plenty of jokes in class, an infectious intellectual curiosity and a classroom atmosphere that doesn't put you to sleep.

Very understanding teacher, grades fairly and gives chances for extra credit. Attendance is mandatory, as HW is handed in in person (printed or handwritten.) Class revolves around a lot of interesting discussions, just make sure you do the reading so you can participate! I learned so much, and was inspired to minor in sustainability.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Great professor. The homework and labs were tedious, but you get exactly what you registered for. Interesting course, and her lectures were well done. Diverse assignments, i.e. journals, brochure, energy audit, earthquake analysis, mars rock analysis, etc. Lots of group work in lecture (not graded). Tests require a lot of memorization.

She's a great lecturer, she's super passionate about geology, and she really cares about her students. As long as you go to class and stay on top of homework deadlines, it's not difficult to get a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I had Dr. Cadieux for my spring 2023 semester and I enjoyed the class. The exams were a bit challenging but as long as you paid attention and obviously studied, it should be okay. She's very knowledgeable and kind and I always found her lectures engaging. The labs weren't bad either, I found them more tedious than challenging. I liked the class.

Dr. Cadieux is always incredibly nice and reasonable with grading. This class was super lecture and reading heavy, but she always tries to make the material engaging. Overall, really cool class and great professor

Took this class for my science requirement. She has very engaging and clear lectures and seems very passionate. The textbook used was online, and no purchase was required. Exams were tough but fair and we had ample opportunities to improve our grades. She was also friendly and tied learned concepts to everyday experiences. Would recommend.
Bad handwriting, unhelpful office hours. Took this course in spring 2023 but review was taken down despite not violating guidelines, just gonna leave it as this

Professor Piper is really good at teaching math. He is really knowledgeable. If you go to lecture and take notes, you will learn the material. Homework is weekly and consists of 3 textbook problems. His tests are straightforward, if you work through his study guides you will be well prepared.
Very good professor, his second and third exams were harder. His 2010 was relatively good A. He even gave curve in final grade at the end and my friend and I went from A- to A.

The textbook was required for homework but you don't need to buy it. Grading is test heavy but he teaches everything you need to know. Prof. Piper hits every you need to know but doesn't explain concepts well and his handwriting is terrible.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: One of the best professors I've ever had. He makes difficult concepts seem trivial and helps build a genuine passion for the subject. I have never felt more interested in what I was learning in a class.
Awesome dude. He produces study guides before each quiz and exam. Be sure to do the assigned practice problems before the exams and you're golden.

Professor Piper does an EXCELLENT job teaching Number Theory. The quizzes and tests are very fair and he includes a study guide to help study for them. It should be noted that tests (3 exams and final) account for 80% of the grade so it is the majority of the grade depends on a few items.

I've had Professor Piper for 3 different classes MT4020/4090/MP4400. Lectures are not mandatory, but highly recommended since he does a GREAT job really explaining the material, but will also clarify in-detail if something doesn't make sense. He's also a bit silly. HW/tests are 100% fair, and provides study guides too. Office hours are a bit short.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Piper is really intelligent and knows his stuff, but his lectures can be really overwhelming. He kind of just gets up there and starts spitting out knowledge, so it can be hard to keep up. He's pretty lazy though so he grades pretty easy. The labs are really easy, and his homeworks are fair. Overall, he's okay and would recommend.
The class is really good. I can understand it very clearly.
Tough to understand. Would not recommend taking again.

Piper's tests are very reasonable but you need to go to class to know what to expect on the tests. If you do the book work and write down the examples from class he says are important, you will have seen every problem on the tests.
Nice guy but very mono-toned. Difficult to stay awake but I already took calc in high school so it wasn't too bad.

In high school, I used to be terrible at Calculus and hated the subject. After attending his lectures, Calculus finally made sense and I actually liked it. The tests are very straightforward and he even tells you exactly what will be on the test. He teaches at a nice pace with plenty of examples. A very good professor!
Very good teach, a bit boring, but easily understood. Tests arent too hard, and his class is worth going to.
piper makes everything harder than it needs to be. however, he is a nice enough guy and calculus isn't inherently difficult, so it doesn't really matter who your professor is.
Prof. Piper is definitely one of my favorite professors at RPI. He really challenges you, but the workload is reasonable and he's available for help if needed.
Good teacher, the material is hard the way he teaches it.

Decent teacher but lectures were very boring. He wasn't the best at explaining the why's and how's of concepts which led to issues in clarity, although the TA helped with that during office hours. Overall, not too bad but not nearly my favorite.

I'm surprised people rate Piper as boring, his Calc II class is my favorite class this semester.  His voice takes a little getting used to, but he is a very good calculus teacher.  The class moves fast and is not very easy, but it is good.
I had BP for 3 classes while at RPI.  He is one of the best professors I had in college.
His lectures are REALLY boring...his voice is monotonous.

One of my best classes, I have credit for the course already, but I do feel like I am gaining from the class. He speaks clearly, gives several examples and its a quick and dry, but easy to get through class.
good
very very dry. nice guy, means well, but sometimes is hard to follow...lectures very boring, but what math lectures arent?
This guy sucks... changed the textbook mid-semester, along with class format.  horrible teacher for this class
No Comments

Great professor! I used to have so much trouble with calc and now it's a breeze. He explains it well, and follows it up with examples. It's obvious that he's taught this class for many years and that he knows what confuses students and what doesn't. Great prof!

Piper is a great guy, BUT he talks to the board constantly. He is very structured and quizes you before the start of (almost) every class. Goes at a fast pace and difficult to understand many a times. Looks into his book instead of interacting with class.
good professor, a little boring, but teaches well. i had no problems with tests, though i actually went to lecture
I wasn't able to learn much from him.  Maybe he's good if you're already a great mathematician.
Great Prof, definitely recommend to take his class. Give out bonus points, but you do have to do(look over) a lot of suggested problems to prepare for test.
good prof, a litle boring, but good.
teaching method good, personality good
Math Analysis was the worst class I took at RPI
good man .. but BORING
Excellent and very caring teacher.  The required workload was not excessive, but he provided many optional problems to enhance your understanding.
Don't slack off.  Ever.  He's a great guy, and will help you when you need it, but you are expected to pull your own weight and then some.
Prof Piper is a really good teacher who is available for help often.

Believe it or not, with a drop-out of 47% it was less than the other section of this course.  Also had him for MATH4020 which was a more interesting course and as such had a drop-out of less than 10%.  Very clear and always willing to help.
No Comments
Best Math Professor out there
Great guy and very willing to help.  Definately one of the best in the math dept.
Great Prof.  Extraordinarilly flexible and helpful.   Horrible puns, though.
Hard grader but makes you learn stuff

There couldn't be anybody better than Dr. Carroll to teach Structures. Her engaging lecture style made concepts much simpler than when introduced in ENGR 2530, and was easy to follow. Exams and homeworks were fair, and never due at the same time as a lab. Credentials were easy quizzes to test basic knowledge and boost your grade. Optional Final.

Dr Carroll is a very kind and understanding professor. Although she teaches the class a bit slower than I like, I still like her teaching style. She is a bit harsh of a grader on homework and is very strict about any kind of plagiarism. Her office hours are also very helpful.

An awesome professor, extremely kind and only wants to help you succeed. Very personable and makes you want to go to lectures for the vibe she brings. Exams are reasonable, and she does not throw curveballs. Her office hours are a great way for you to get help, and she does her very best to try only after you tried yourself.

Prof Campbell is amazing for Studio B! She cares so much about harm reduction and her students. Her lectures are in-depth but understandable and she's flexible with deadlines and participation. And she would occasionally bring snacks to class!
Excellent class and excellent professor. Fair grading, and solid discussions.
Excellent professor, I've taken History of Drugs and Bioethics with her,both classes were great.
Her class is hard, but she's a great teacher-really knows her stuff. I agree with the person who said her style reminds them of a high school teacher, but it's nice in my opinion nonetheless.

Professor Campbell is amazing.  She is a legal historian and specializes in drug history.  She teaches sort of like your high school history teacher may have taught, but it's nice.  She loves when people share their opinions, and the class is interesting.
Sometimes grading out of the momentary feeling. Educational and well prepared lectures are recommended. Easy course testing materials as well as the homeworks.
Amazing professor and course. You will love the lectures and course both. He is very easy-going and respects his students.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Best RPI MANE Professor.
This class was very challenging but I enjoyed it because he is such a good professor. Very funny and easy to understand despite the complex subject matter
Great professor who can explain the heavy staffs in clearest possible manner
one of the best professors ever met in RPI
Had him for Fracture Mechanics and fatigue of materials. He knows his stuff, explains it well, and obviously cares about the students. Is surprisingly easy to meet with. Highly recommend.
This guy knows his s**t, and he can explain it very well. Excellent use of diagrams and examples in class. He can be pretty funny too.

I like him. He didn't use powerpoints during lecture so I had to pay attention to what he was writing down and the examples he did. He explains concepts quite clearly and is actually a pretty entertaining guy.

One of the few professors at RPI that knows his stuff and can also explain it. Ask him any materials science question and he'll have an answer. He jokes around in class a lot and is a generally nice guy.
No Comments

Professor Century did a great job teaching this course. Despite being a bit unengaging, his lectures covered the topics well and he made efforts to enhance them through guest speakers. The course expectations were more than fair and he gave extra credit. The communication intensive aspect was well executed through a balance of writing and speaking.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: As long as you show up, do the work, and study a little for the midterm and final you will be fine. The homework is easy and can often be completed without reading the full article. Very kind, easy to communicate with and a great pianist. It was nice that he would play during class.

History of Western Music. Professor Century is far too qualified to be teaching music here tbh (he studied under Nadia Boulanger) but that's all the more reason to take one of his classes. He plays these ridiculous pieces of music in the middle of class on the piano and it's enthralling. Not a free A and attendance is mandatory but worth it.

Prof. Century certainly made the class much more interesting than I thought it would be. His mixture of teaching with video, text, and music makes the material feel more real. Though most of the EMPAC performances he made us attend had questionable/weird taste, he is happy to help anyone that displays interest in the course material.

Prof. Century.  He's the head of the music department, and teaches the new media theory classes too I believe.  He interesting, and steers clear of 'boring' material.  Occasionally he go into tangents, or long-winded talks, but bearable, and will teach any material well.

His delivery is a little dry, but Professor Century is a very smart guy. He really explains the various art movements very succinctly, and if you can get him onto a tangent, you'll find he can provoke lots of really interesting (and relevant) discussion and debate from the students.

He taught History of Western Music very well. Was thorough and detailed. Not good at keeping the class awake though. Easy grader, its an easy A if you do the reviews on time and read the textbook before quizzes. Students interested in the course can get an easy A.
Take this course if you can. Always something to learn.  Helpful and enthusiastic guy. Not a dynamic entertainer, but something to stick with you long after it's over ... in a GOOD way.
He has a monotonous voice during lecture but if he is helpful!
The class is pretty boring and useless, but Century is pretty easy and always willing to help.  It's not his fault the course sucks, he tried his best.
Very easy class and he gets very excited about what he presents. He tries very hard to make sure everyone understands the material but he is PAINFULLY, PAINFULLY BORING.
Very test heavy remember that, nice guy but there's tests and hw thats it lol
He is an excellent professor who cares about his students' success.

Prof McDermott is nice but the lecture may be boring. He does do class activities but not for every class. Grades are based on quizzes which are fine if you study the notes and understand the homework questions. He likes to use simple examples to explain course concepts but he sometimes gets off topic.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great professor but Operations is so boring, the only thing you need to be aware of is the exams since they are 80% of the grade. They arent too hard if you put in the time studying and you will have probably like 1-2 hours of HW a week max
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Mr. McDermott was amazing! I really enjoyed his lectures and how he explained the content while being funny here and there to keep us engaged. If you pay attention and do all your work you should be fine in this course.

He gives straightforward lectures, fair homework, and easy exams. His lectures are pretty interesting as long as you pay attention to. He goes off topic sometimes, but I don't really mind. He gives good feedback and has an easygoing personality. Overall I really like his class. Recommend.

There is a lot to learn from McDermott and his professional experience. If you study a few hours the 2 days before the test (especially the notes) you should do just fine. There is very little homework and the subject matter is very practical for anyone who is considering going into business. Overall a great learning experience.
The course material is super boring as the other guy posted. Its hard to stay awake most of the time but he tries to keep you up. Its not the best class.
the material was boring but it wasn't his fault. he tried to make it fun with activties but most lectures were 90 mins of trying to stay awake. classic case of a nice guy stuck teaching a lame topic.

Although as some students pointed out. He focuses on supercomputer history and so forth and the assignments might be a bit different but I found everything super interesting. I loved working with MPI/CUDA too and it did get a bit heavy in the end but overall learned a lot and it was worth it.

- Gives generous grades
- Talks a lot about different supercomputers (kinda like history) instead of focusing more on CUDA/MPI stuff
- Doesn't respond to discussion threads/emails
It's 2023 and this man still never responds to email or discussion forum

- 5 homeworks, 4 of which are done alone, and 1 which can be done in a group.
- 1 group project worth 30%
- 26 lecture summaries * 350 words
Only would take again because I can PNC.
Don't work with lazy people for group project. 
He doesn't respond to emails or discussion forum.
Homeworks generally easy, don't start late.
No late days.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--So many papers

reviews.comment: Writeups are a significant portion of the course grade; they tend to be all-or-nothing with vague requirements and little feedback until far along in the course. Lectures suck horribly, but you sorta have to go to get access to the supercomps/have all the info you need for the writeups. Homeworks were mediocre. Only CS class I've ever dropped.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--SO MANY PAPERS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Slides in comic sans, perpetually late, never answers email

While the homework can be difficult and the lectures can be a bit dry, it is wonderful to have a professor teaching about something they are genuinely passionate about. Not easy by any means, but he is a very helpful person should you ever need it.
Terrible professor. Frustrating assignments, and very little indication of what students are expected to know for quizzes.

I've never experienced true rage until I entered this course. After taking it, I realized it wasn't a course on computer science but rather a course on perspective. I always felt that the current topic/homework was the hardest/most unfair thing ever until I experienced the next one. By the end of the course, I was at my wit's end. Don't take it.
Very smart, very knowledgeable about the material, very passionate, and a pretty bad professor. Assignments are ambiguous and quizzes are pretty bad. That said, you could do a lot worse.

The professor might as well have not tried to teach the course. His lectures are copied straight from another university's computer science website, and he does a terrible job of even trying to explain that. If you enjoy computer science at all, spare yourself and don't take computer science with Chris Carothers.

Terrible professor! His class is extremely difficult and he literally reads off of his powerpoint which includes some of the worst written things ever. He also never responds to emails, literally none of my three emails to him were answered. Don't take comp org with him.
Not the easiest of instructors but he knows his stuff and teaches well. Looking for an easy A, go elsewhere. Want to learn, he's the guy.
very hard, very boring, do not take comp org with him!

Do not take this professor for 6:00pm-8:00pm class. I could not focus on his lectures which were powerpoint slides loaded with typos. You would be much better off just studying the book instead of going to the lecture. I found the two exams very difficult and failed both of them. The other half of the grade was homework which I got 100% on with sup
Comp Org with him not an easy class but you come out of there learning something.  If you just want the grade take it with someone else. If you want to learn, he's the guy.

Terrible professor, lectures straight off of horribly typed slides. The homeworks do reinforce the material that SHOULD BE taught, but they're hard as hell. He rarely responds to his email, is very unresponsive to the class, and you have to pin him down at office hours to really get him to explain things sometimes.
No Comments

Terrible professor.  Doesn't really teach, only reads from the text.  Has typos in everything, annoying as hell to read anything he types up.  Quite frankly, with him as your professor, save yourself the time of going to class, just read the text, you won't miss anything
