VERY UNHELPFUL, ANY TIME I ASKED FOR HELP HE BLEW ME OFF, VERY RUDE PERSON
When I had Chris C as a professor for Comp Org I thought he was the hardest professor EVER.  However, I've come to learn that he was one of the best.
Clearly one of the most attractive professors at the school.  Classes are good with lots of options to learn more about topics you enjoy.
Clear explainations and VERY helpful outside of class... But course work is HARD compare to other prof for the same course.
Good teacher and enthusiastic, but the class was hard as hell.
No Comments

Class notes not all that useful, but if you READ THE TEXT.  He picked a REALLY good book for this course and if it seems like he's just reading stuff straight from it, it's the best way it can be explained.  Liberal with extensions.

His PhD should be revoked.  While it may be easy for him to simply copy his assignments from everywhere else, when he forgets to friggin' change the email address from cmu.edu to rpi.edu, he gets his PhD taken away.  That anecdote says a lot, trust me.

If lumberjacks could read then he might be a good professor.  He completely reads from powerpoint slides (which he got online from the publisher).  He had no idea how to explain concepts, he is just all around a bad teacher.
No Comments
Hard course!!  good teacher, sometimes rambles on and on but tries to keep it interesting
Really good prof, you get an email from him nearly every other day.  Explains material well and cares about students.

Dr. Letchford teaches Applied Hydrology better than Fluid Mechanics. Tough grader and not the best with feedback, but is easy to reach out to on Webex. Take the final project and exams seriously and ask lots of questions during class and office hours. Some extra credit is available in the form of RCAs and other assignments. Use the back exams.

Dr. Letchford sets you up to fail. Lectures are okay, but he offers almost no study materials for exams, and he grades too harshly without any helpful feedback. Easy to reach out to on Webex but won't answer simple questions, and is quite snarky. Refusal to release Final Exam grades is completely unacceptable. Completely unprofessional.

You would ask him a question on webex and he either wouldn't answer or answer in the most convoluted way possible. He also has a habit of randomly calling on students with a varying range of questions, he would ask questions that was like "what is the density of water" to "explain why pumps matter." also the harshest grader I have ever had

Dr. Letchford is kind, but the way class was taught wasn't the best. Our final grades revealed for this semester were lower than we expected as he never told us how we did on our final exams. He also made all HW and exams, but used no textbook. I do feel that his lectures with asking us questions on the spot made me more confident in the material.

His class is tough but if you put in the work, you'll understand the material. After the final, grades were posted without exam scores, and our grades were much lower than expected, straying from the syllabus. Extra credit seemed ineffective and his explanations were snarky and left the class confused about how are grades were actually calculated.

It's been about 4 days, and he still hasn't released the grades for the final test, despite having posted the final grades for the class as a whole. The homework and tests were written solely by him, which means that sometimes there will be no definitive answer. He is very accommodating during office hours, but outside of that, he's not the best.

Last minute removed a policy written in the syllabus that drops our lowest homework grade because, in his opinion, it probably would not make any difference for anyone. Unfair. Why have the policy in the first place if this were true? Refused to post our final exam grades final grades. He is the dean of CEE and seems to be abusing that power.

Prof. Letchford's entire class and coursework were very disorganized, and at many points he contradicted himself in regards to homework's, labs, and grading. The instructions for the labs were very unclear, and therefore nearly impossible to do well on. He also refused to publish our final exam grades, even after many students requested him to.

Letchford's teaching is a failure. He has incomprehensible lecture notes and exam material that doesn't match the content covered in class; his grading is excessively harsh, making success nearly impossible, and his refusal to release our final exam grades shows a lack of accountability. He should be removed from his position.
This class was the reason I changed to business

Unreasonably harsh,unfair. Tests= understand physics in the scope of fluids so if u aren't strong physics, math be prepared to get screwed. thought he was nice but a harsh professor tilhe refused to accept my revision bcusI mistakenly submitted the template first. dissapointed bcus I had liked him. Doesnt care for students. Don't take if possible.

As a person, he is very nice and caring. As a professor, he is very tough and leaves you confused. Do not miss lecture! The only way to "study" for exams are the very difficult homework questions that are tough enough on their own. Active Webex, yet is sometimes helpful. Generous office hours. Lab reports will take you several hours. Good luck!

You think you know what you're doing, until you get to the exam. Exam review and homework do not prepare you at all for the exam. I went to office hours every week and somehow almost failed the first exam. The average was a 54 and there was no curve. Be prepared to be confused. Picks favorites and is not helpful. Doesn't care about your grades.

Used back exams to get thru the class. bad lectures and there are A LOT of reports (labs or group projects). Expect to not have a social life this semester as 3-4 assignments are due Sundays and Tuesdays.
do not use textbooks and grade tough, but fun classes and you can learn stuff
Teaching style doesnt work at all.
exam are 65% worth of the class. dident use the book at all
he mentions the textbook in the syllabus but never used really, nice guy but tougher grader
goes up note which very hard to follow, TA for the class dont help at all
very hard tests
Letchford is a beast super nice guy his class is just super hard
tough grader, nice guy but class is too hard

Nice person, but one of the worst professors I have had. He was an insanely tough grader and I did not learn well from his teaching style. He has a bad habit of calling people out and putting them on the spot every 5 seconds.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Personally, his teaching style doesn't work for me. He doesn't post notes online so you have to write down everything in class, but it might not make sense by the time you have time to actually go over it. Also, he mentions a textbook in the syllabus, but it doesn't really makes sense with the way he teaches. REALLY TOUGH GRADER
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Had him for Intro to Structures, great guy and good professor.  He moves very quickly and he's tough, you need to work very hard in order to get an A.  If you need help, he's there.
great professor

Had him for both Intro to Structural and the Hydraulics portion of Hydrology/Hydraulics. Excellent Professor! I rate him one of the best at RPI. Super hard tests. Hard grader on HW too. Class moves quickly so pay attention.

Letchford's a good professor and all, but he randomly calls on people for answers in lecture. That probably doesn't bother most people, but it scares the daylights out of me. The tests are hard too, by the way.

Great lecturer, very clear to understand.  Likes to randomly ask people questions during lecture, and tries to get to know everyone individually.  Tests are incredibly difficult, the average for ours was 60%.  Not very helpful at office hours, and the lack of textbook makes figuring out problems difficult.
Awesome professor.  Makes you pay attention by asking random students questions during class, so you actually learn stuff.  Hard tests, but only one of them. He also has a cool accent.

The grades are never curved. He rarely uses the textbook. And he is not the best at explaining concepts. He also has some aversion to using numbers. How do you possibly give examples of problems based solely in math and not give numbers? Oh, and he grades up, not down, so test scores will be way lower than expected.
Always very prepared for Class and ready to answer questions. Great to talk to and especially helpful in office hours/ discussions outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Assigns lots of homework but grades very slowly. Currently we have 3 ungraded homeworks and the next was assigned. Going to class is basically useless he does not explain content too well. Figure out how to do the homework based on textbook and youtube videos and use the homeworks to study for the tests. Very tough grader, no leniency on tests.

He tries his best to be helpful. Going to office hours really helps. Financial computation is very tricky, and is very work intensive. Sometimes I don't understand what he is talking about. He always gives the solutions to the homework promptly, and guides us well for the exams. He makes sure all students have solutions to the class given problems.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: He is very helpful, provides a lot of material. The correct solutions to homeworks are always provided which helps for the exam.  Sometimes has a hard time getting his point across. Financial computation is a hard course, but I had no issues with the professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Very good lectures, but class is hard.

Branden and I go way back and the guy really knows his stuff.  Can't recommend him enough for one on one work.  The work assigned for his classes (I have taken MBE and Malware) isn't just busy work and it really does help you understand the subject on the whole.

Few instructors at RPI are as passionate about teaching as Professor Clark. He really gets into the details of what he is talking about when he explains all the techniques and security exploits in the class. He also got a few guest speakers in from world class security companies. Definitely want to take before you graduate.
great dude

By far my hardest class all semester. Completely flunked the first exam but did better on the second, third, and final. If you have Professor Wetzel, be ready to teach yourself for the exams. Labs are somewhat helpful, but when I took them right after lectures, they just made things more confusing. Definitely a weed-out class at RPI.

This class is already extremely difficult, and he somehow makes it worse. The slides he uses gives basically no help compared to those of other professors and he provides less material to prepare for exams than other professors. Basically, good luck trying to get a decent grade in this course. I studied countless hours and still almost failed.

Avoid this professor if you want to understand the material. As previous students stated, he doesn't explain things and just points at the slides. I went into the class enjoying physics and now I hate the subject.
Avoid him he just reads off the lecture slides and doesn't really explain anything.

My main critique is less Professor Wetzel himself, and more the poor structure of the course itself. That being said, choose another professor. Wetzel often does not explain concepts well, and can sometimes be very rude and not understanding. Relying on outside resources or prior knowledge for this class is more helpful than the lecture slides.

Underrated in my opinion, he's funny, and his lectures are pretty fun. The tests are pretty brutal, but that is not entirely the professor's fault as it seems to be standardized tests that all physics 1 students take.

Horrible lecturer, nothing he says sticks. He reads off the pre-made slides, doesn't explain anything covered in the course, and will not help you prepare for the brutal exams whatsoever. Also, he straight up just gets things wrong and expects you to use his faulty formulas. Please take any course but his. Your gpa and mental health will thank you.
other reviews arent huge fans of him, but i thought wetzel was a pretty fun prof. he doesnt remarkably standout but hes helpful when you need help and makes jokes from time to time

Anyone rating this professor higher than a 1 aren't in their right mind, he literally (as the rating below me states) reads off the slides which the physics department does NOT make any easier.. the structure of the course is sloppy and the professor does not make everything any better. Please pick West instead or Kim.
He doesn't go over any problems in class and he just points and reads off the board all of class.
not good at all, avoid at all costs

This professor simply can not teach the material well. Everyone who I know who received a good grade in his class learned the entire material through the textbook. I ended up retaking the class with professor Kim, who was a far better at explaining the knowledge (my new grade reflecting that). This is not a hard class if you have the right teacher

This professor wasn't great at all, I truly dont recommend taking a class with him if you can. He didn't explain the material well and was occasionally rude. For this class I think that its best to take it with professor Kim.

Professor Wetzel is a fine person, though the PHYS-1100 course is structured terribly. He was very kind and understanding when working with me regarding missed assignments, and many of his lectures were only tolerable thanks to his sense of humor, as the slides the department provides are far from useful.
Lectures are boring, but practice exams given before tests are very helpful and similar to the actual test.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I really liked Professor Wetzel this semester. He does try to help you even if sometimes he doesn't explain everything well, but his lecture slides were always pretty easy to understand. And he is very lenient and understanding with extensions if you have a good reason. He checked in on me personally multiple times to make sure I was caught up.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I hated Physics 1, not because of Dr. Wetzel, but due to the way the class is structured. Every period, you go in, do an activity, while relying on an extremely short lecture video that all Physics 1 classes share. These activities did not help, and you have to learn most of it yourself.

All of the physics professors use the same slides, so it really doesn't matter who you get. Wetzel was a decent lecturer, usually got through the lectures pretty quickly so that students could work on the lab activities. Very accessible and reasonable; easy to talk to about grades or missing papers.

The way I didn't learn a single thing in this class <<< You couldn't pay me to take this class again. This man was so hard to understand, not because of his accent just because he makes everything more complicated than it needs to be. If you don't understand anything within the first few weeks, drop the class. Switch to Kim instead.

Tough curriculum, although this appears to be the fault of the department and not the professor. He occasionally jumps through topics without talking about them much and assumes everyone understands it. Doesn't explain some things very well.

His lectures are dry even though he tries to make jokes, so I want to sleep in every class. His expectant tone of voice makes it hard to ask for clarifications because he expects us to just know physics and makes you sound stupid. And if you make a mistake, you can tell he disguises his annoyance and is passive aggressive.

Wetzel attempts to make jokes in class which generally fail. He teaches as if we all understand physics at his level, and make fun of students in front of the whole class who do not understand. Does not attempt to show how an answer is obtained. Spends much of class texting while the TAs are overloaded with questions.
A fun teacher, who is very easy to listen too.  However, he does not go over material as well as I would like.

Wetzel is generally a nice person, though I've witnessed harsh comments towards his TAs, probably out of frustration that the class is quite lost. The tests for all Physics sections were made by Ciolek this semester. Wetzel's section fared badly, with average scores ranging from 55-70 on each test.

If you don't have a solid background in physics, I don't recommend taking his course.  He is very smart and doesn't realize that physics is not as easy to everyone as it is to him.  He often calls the entire class lazy if we don't know how to solve a problem rather than realize that he probably didn't explain things so well.

He might be best physics teacher as he speaks english and examples well. But he is a hard grader. you will learn if you pay attention and go to class. but physics is all about tests, so take him and pay attention. no slacking
No Comments
I certainyl enjoyed his class a lot. I felt like he was pretty good at explaining the material. Plus the grad TA that I had was excellent, so I learned a lot from my TA as well.

A smart guy who has trouble understanding why physics is difficult. Also, his accent is a little less than "charming," native German speakers may have difficulty understanding him when he tries to say words like "Tangential." Or "Joules."
No Comments

He is such a helpful professor. His lecture is very interesting, so I never fell asleep in his class. He explains everything very clearly;making sure that we understand the concept visually helped me a lot. Plus, his German accent is so charming.
avoid him!
No Comments
He tried to get us to use our own knowledge of physics, which was tough in the beginning.

As long as you're not entirely incompetent and pay attention while he lectures (read: don't stare at your laptop all class), he's very helpful and very explanatory.  Compared to what I hear about a lot of the other phys 1 professors (aside from Bedrosian and some others), he's certainly one of the better ones. Plus, he actually has a sense of humor

Wetzel was okay in lectures and activities. He tries to help students out, especially if you make an appointment and go see him he gives you advice and some comments on your work. (Its good to go see him) He was a nice guy
lectures are helpful, keeps them interesting
No Comments
All he does is talk to himself in front of the classroom, instead of teaching!!!!!!!!!!!!
Not great, but not horrible. Nice.
I thought he was a good professor?!  He's very friendly and willing to help.  I think that he is clear and his examples are helpful.

Agree w/ rating @ bottom of pg. Bring your laptop to class! Boring + Confusing. U're better off ignoring him + learn on own. Ask for help on a hw prob, and he'll spend 10min on it, realize he'd messed up and just move on. TAs helpful. Don't skimp at the beginning. Not same as highschool phys.

the guy truly is 100% terrible.   subs were SO VERY much better than wetzel.   and i told the subs that....specially prof cummings.   he was great and i told him i wished he was teaching our class.   wetzel just didn't want to help or answer questions or be of any sort of use to the class.

He's awful. He was absent twice in my class and the subs were so much better. One of the subs was Cunnings. He, along with Bedrosian are awesome. They don't tell you which professor you have (it says Bedrosian for all). If you do get Wetzel, try to switch. Really, anyone is better than Wetzel.

Freshmen need to stop whining and realize what exactly a bad professor is. Compared to others at RPI, Wetzel is a decent professor. The class is set up badly in general (especially the useless lecture slides) and that is not Wetzel's fault. A decent guy and much better than many other RPI professors
worst prof ever

He gets the homework problems wrong in class if you ask him. Then when the TA corrects him, he gets flustered and trys to explain why his way is still correct, even though it isn't. In summation, he's a big ****. He doesn't prepare you for the tests at all.
This module didn't give anything like example before we start the group project, also there's no guidance for writing, please improve
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very frustrating course. Workload is excessive and split into many low-weight tasks that mostly feel like busywork. Class content often does not match the assignments, and almost no concrete examples are given. Grading is harsh and non-transparent, with vague criteria and little useful feedback.😅
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
unclear in-class guidance and instructions
poor links between lectutre contens and presentation assessments
time-cost and grade-recevied are unfair
requirements are too strict as a minor module
lack of good examples
usually release grades via email at late night (i.e. 11pm)
you gonna spend a a lot of time on it and most likely to get a 60+ grade.

Taught this grad course with Prof. Garde. You could tell Coppens knew his stuff but he didnt explain things quite as well as you wanted. He wrote one of the tests and half of the take home final. The test was fair but the part of the final he wrote was pretty brutal. Usually put a lot of effort into helping out outside of class though.

Professor C-K is a sweetheart, more than willing to accommodate students experience difficulties as severe as housing insecurity or just mental health recovery days. With a good depth of material and a hearty sense of humor, Brandon makes all classes enjoyable.

This is not your typical professor, Brandon is a younger, passionate, funny and realistic guy. He doesn't believe in our culture's grading system, he believes to teach through group bonding, participation and self discussion. He is as chill as they come. He participates extensively in climate change protests, sustainability efforts and being chill

Very eager to hear students' thoughts and opinions. Never shoots down an idea, even if it is bad.  With Environment and Politics, you have to write essays, which is never fun. Lectures can be kind of boring, and he takes attendance. We watched quite a few movies though, too. Easy A if you get the right TA. I didn't.
A little vague sometimes in what he expects from his students, but extremely willing to work with you on a case by case basis.
Provided very little grade feedback during the class (Only two assignments)

By far the worst professor I've ever had. He does not check his email. He is impossible to reach. He will not provide information. He does not post resources in a timely manner. I consistently asked him to do something four times before seeing results. He is not a good professor and doesn't understand why his students don't do well. Good luck.

Emailing Woodcock means you're yelling into the void. Do not expect a reply. It takes months to receive a grade, and it depends on the semester whether your exams will be easy or not. You also need to tell him to post the lecture slides and homework solutions, or they will not get posted. He will like you if you ask questions.
He is just bad.
good teacher

Hear me out- if he literally only lectured then his class would be great. He's just really not good at responding to emails and grading in a timely manner. For context, I took an exam mid-October and just got grades back 4 days ago. He's super frustrating at times but he really does know course material and if you can catch him in OH, he's great
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Worst professor at RPI. Had 4 tests, test 1 took 3 MONTHS to grade!! By the end of the semester had only gotten 2 out of 4 test grades back. Ridiculously slow grading and would be extremely snarky to students asking questions. Maybe he needs some more energy drinks in the morning.

Although he definitely knows the content, he is not a good person. He was very rude and arrogant towards the students and if someone was asking a question he would often just cut them off. Some of the exams did not reflect what we were learning in class at all. He doesn't respond to emails. He takes forever to grade exams... like 3 months.
Took 9 weeks during arch to grade our Exam 1. Completely unavailable outside classes. Doesn't respond to emails.

He's always so behind on his work and the pressure reflects on us especially when he forgets (consistently!) to post homework for the class for a week. Additionally, he did not grade our exams for over 9 weeks in a 12 week semester. Overall, avoid him as much as possible.

He's a terrible professor shows no respect to students nor other professors. He's always shows that he cares about us but at the same time it takes him 3 exams out of 4 to finally grad our 1st exam. If only there's another professor for this class, I would never want to take his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If he has a whiteboard and a classroom full of not mouthy students, he's pretty good. He is awful with emails and webex messages, so finding him somewhere in person is usually the way to go. GO TO OFFICE HOURS and talk in class as much as you can, even if you think you understand all the material. He had homework groups for us this sem, so beware.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Show up for attendance, there were a few lectures where he gave an optional question you could answer related to the lecture, and if you did it, then you got points back for an exam, one of my top 3 favorite professors at RPI
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great professor and person. If you show interest or participate, he brightens up and is much more willing to help. He really helps and tries to answer questions when they come up and will use interesting analogies and applications to explain the concepts. Also great person to get to know outside of class as an advisor and mentor.

Prof. Woodcock is a very good lecturer, I would recommend attending as many of his lectures as possible. He is both entertaining and knowledgeable. He isn't consistent with assigning homework, so some weeks will have a lot more work required than other. He has also has been known to get annoyed at students and over-assign HW, so don't annoy him.

Woodcock is very generous & explaining professor to have for TP1, especially with him making it mandatory for us to do HWs in groups, which makes me less likely to struggle and understand more of the class. However, there will be times where he forgets to upload lectures, grade hws and exams (he curves exams) until the end of the semester.

Dr. Woodcock's course was unpredictable and difficult to follow. He would give out assignments and grades seemingly randomly and often seemed disinterested in lecture. Outside of lecture, he is helpful in person.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: All exams were take-home and curved and overall a great guy. Outside of class would teach you whatever you wanted to learn. Helped with Capstone projects after finished his class also.

He seemed to care about students but had a weird way of showing it. He would tear groups apart when they presented for it seemed like an unusually long time. His remarks were a little beyond constructive criticism. Nice guy to talk to outside of class. Terrified to present to him.

Despite Fluid Mechanics being cut down to 3 credits, Professor Woodcock tries to pad out his online lectures to make it feel like you're in a 4 credit. I always end up doing all my learning out of the textbook, which, for the first time, manages to teach the material MORE concisely than the professor.
great guy!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Corey is a chill guy, but he seems like he doesn't care a lot of the time, and on occasion even makes students feel kind of dumb for asking questions. I think he just gives out grades based on what he feels like the student should get, because I assure you I did not do well enough on tests to earn a B+, but I guess he went easy on us due to COVID
Cares little about students and their work. Randomly gives out grade.

Solid professor. Very charismatic. Definitely seems like he wants the students to understand everything and do well. That said, he does try to make the tests somewhat on the harder side so that he can determine a proper scale so that you get a normal bell curve with an average around a 75 - 80
literally my favorite professor ever
Corey is nice and always available, but yet another test heavy class. The curves he gives are very generous but this is a class that you either get it or you don't. Good luck.

Dr. Woodcock is relatively new to teaching, but he received his bachelor's and PhD degrees at RPI, so he understands the student experience. He has an "open door policy". His lectures can be boring and seem very theoretical, but his examples are helpful. His grading is fair and exams are generally curved. Make a solid effort and you'll do well.

MMM contains interesting content and DTC is passionate about the content and student's learning. Content is detailed, therefore participation is important to understand where you might be missing something. 6000 level don't let the oral final deter you, if you participate in class it is basically practice for the final. Very nice guy one-on-one!

Very intelligent and has commanding knowledge of the material, but boy is this class hard. Completely different than other mechanics courses, heavy focus on complicated symbolic math that is unlike any other course I've taken at RPI. The material is pretty interesting if you can wrap your head around it, but get ready to work. Few hws but very hard

I have learned nothing from Corr's lectures. He is an interactive teacher but thinks we all know what is going on when we absolutely don't. Is rude to students when they answer his questions in class and talks down to students. Not very nice man. Would not take MMM with him either. 0 out of 10 would not recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: The evaluation includes an oral test.
Biomechanics 2 is incredibly tough, but interesting information. Dr. Corr grades mercilessly though. The jumping simulation competition at the end is pretty fun. Take at your own risk!
He simply reads through slides during lectures, which makes the lectures super boring.  His exams are all stupid memorization.

One of the worst the professors I have ever met. His tests are stupid memorization staff. You will get 90 points in the exam if you just remember the slides without understanding anything. Select the other professor Tacy in fall semester if you can. That section is easier to get an A.

Tests are by the bok compeltely! He requires very detailed answers and TAs tend to make mistakes. Just write as much as possible on the exams. I got an A- in the class because you needed a 95 on the final for an A and the final was RIDICULOUS! 20 pages of long answer questions worth 2-4pts.

Grading system is based off of deviation from the average so the majority of the class receives a C. He basically reads off of the slides during class and follows the book very closely. The information isn't very hard but small mistakes on exams are graded harshly. Hes nice if you talk to him.

Very good teacher, the class structure was a little unorganized but he is very helpful and kind. He has plenty of resources online which make the tests pretty easy. Interesting guy. The labs arent bad if you have a good group who is willing to work together.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Had him for Fields I, and as an ECSE advisor.  Very helpful and clear.

Great guy and a good teacher, but a moderately difficult class.  The homeworks do take a lot of time (second only to signals) but the exams are fair and with some studying most do fairly well on them.  Most "lab" sessions are really open shop to work on homework and the 2 projects for the semester.
Very thorough and intelligent guy.  The homeworks and tests are pretty damn hard, but he's extraordinarily helpful.
Took Fields 1 and II with this guy. Very bright...

Nice guy, lectures are thorough, but his HW are impossible. It's like doing a graduate research paper. You have to scrounge all over the place for answers. It may be hidden deep in the lecture slides, or in the book, or something that you just should know. He really pushes you to the limit. You really learn a lot when you get through his course.
Good guy, tons of knowledge
Keeping EE's sane for yet another semester. SWWEEEET
No Comments
tests are long but straightforward and fair, very low exam averages, homework helps for exams, office hours help if you go
bad lectures

Prof Collins is very intelligent and challenges students to answer their own questions, but she is unclear when teaching topics and does not emphasize what will be important to the laboratories.  Attendence at lectures is mandatory due to regular quizzes.  She becomes emotional about unprepared students, yet her disorganization does not prepare us.
Dr. Cramer does talk really fast during lectures and it's sometimes hard to understand the material in class. But the homeworks did help a lot and he was really flexible with office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Cramer is a genius in the field. Nice person and helpful, if you can keep up with the topics and with him. Moves very fast and skips over some of the basics. Will ignore questions he already answered or that are self-explanatory (check the textbook, its usually there) but if you ask good questions he will start to ease up on the whole class.
Shows little respect for his students and TAs. I went to office hours three times and he commented on my looks each time. Talks really fast and dismisses questions if they are not good enough.

He's all over the place in lecture and I rarely knew what he was talking about.  Speaks really fast and often skips over derivations.  Prefers to give you the equations and let you figure out where they came from.  He's more helpful during office hours.
No Comments
No Comments
No Comments
very energetic!

She is knowledgeable in architectural theory and open to any ideas. Half of the class is like a seminar and discussion. She cares about everyone's opinions. I am not so active in her class, but she always encourages me to speak out.

I have Jillian as my IDS professor. She is very wise and knowledgeable. She takes time to understand your idea and project. She gives advice at your design point. She is also approachable out of class time and always gives really detailed markup for your drawings.

Jillian is for sure incredibly knowledgeable in this area of study. She has a lot of experience in the professional field and this knowledge translates well to helping her students in developing their projects to a more realistic resolution. Jillian also cares a lot about the well being and mental health of her students, which is I respect a lot.

I think Prof. Crandall is great!! She knows what she does and her lectures had such an amazing impact on me every class. They were so interesting!! I would take another class with her without any doubt. There is a LOT to do, but the knowledge acquired makes it worth it.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Group projects

reviews.comment: Gives a large amount of work with short amounts of time to complete. Not very respectful of students personal issues. Wants us to use techniques we don't know. Tells different students different things about the same assignment.
Amazing professor. Kind and always willing to help. Lecture heavy, but if you try hard, getting a A is not hard. 100% the best professor in RPI.

Amazing teacher, passionate about the subject. Lots of content so going to class and paying attention helps. If you do so you will succeed. Homework is easy, you get two tries and best grade is taken. 100% would take the class again.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Crone is great and so far my favorite professor at RPI! I took both 4620 and 4630 with her, got an A in both. It's lecture heavy, but homework in both classes are easy and interesting. 4620 is basic homework and exams, but in 4630 there is a fun group project and paper; exams also have take home components. Crone is super caring and friendly!

Worst class I've ever taken, and I've taken Data Structures. None of the questions on her homework or take home tests can be found on google, in the textbook, or in her lecture slides. The class consists of Crone's understanding of useless current events in Molec Bio. The necessary information can be found nowhere except in Crone's brain.

Homework is EASY. 10 mindless multiple choice after every lecture, and you get two attempts if you didn't get a 100 the first time. The tests should be no problem if you do your reading. The final is a joke. 100 multiple choice from old homework and tests, and it replaces your lowest test grade.

Covers a lot of topics very quickly without any particular order. The class could be restructured to flow better and focus on the big picture rather than memorizing protein names and specific bits of information.

Cell and Dev lab is a straight forward class, but if you do not put in the hours or pay attention to what she says, you will be lost in the class. She clarifies anything you have a problem with and ALWAYS willing to help students. She's helped me immensely in the course, giving me a B was more than generous. Very understanding and nice to talk to!

Dr. Crone is a lovely person!  Although she does recite off the ppts, the exams are mostly based off the slides.  She may become angry sometimes but only when justified.  She dislikes it when people ask unnecessary difficult questions.  She also strongly dislikes it when people with grades already in the A range try to get points back on exams.

Crone is a horrible teacher. She basically recites her powerpoints in class and if you ask her any questions she yells at you. Don't bother going to office hours, she only complains about how much other work she has and does not do her job as a professor.

Donna Crone is a lovely person and a great teacher. She teaches through PowerPoints, which constitute most of the exam material. Course is 80% tests and 20% homework. Many of the homework answers come directly from the book, so it is beneficial to read it. She is willing to answer any questions and is great if you go to office hours.

Dr. Crone knows who is trying and it matters to her. She is also great one on one. I failed the first exam, went and talked to her. We worked out a better time for me to take the next exam and my grade pulled a 180. She is not the easiest woman to follow in lecture but she's very approachable and will help you if you ask.

Dr. Crone is an excellent professor. Some students didn't like her because she often had to yell at the class for talking over her at the beginning of class which shouldn't be happening anyways. I always found her to be very pleasant and helpful. The homework is relatively easy and the exams are even easier if you look at back tests. Great class.

Dr. Crone is an excellent professor. The homework was relatively easy and the exams were even easier if you look at back tests. Some people didn't like her personality because she often had to yell at the rude students who thought it was acceptable to talk over her at the beginning of class, but I always found her to be very pleasant and helpful.

Not a good teacher;she stutters all the time while lecturing.Her office hours are okay,but if you ask a question that's on the test,she won't answer your q's.She yells at us like we're children and keeps saying how she's stressed out and has many things to do.Her tests are okay,just memorization no understanding.

Class is interesting. Gave only one test, which is not much of the grade but easy, and gives lots of help. The rest of the class is readings with short responses and a few short papers and presentations. She is hyper but passionate about subjects covered.
Very easy. Tests are usually 70% back test. Online homework is straight forward. Her exams are based one what she teaches in lecture. So know her lecture notes and the back test..and you're golden.
Class was fun to take. Homeworks are from the text and test are mostly the same as the back test. The class can get boring at times but it is an easy A.
I have had the pleasure of taking Donna's classes and serving as her TA twice.  There is no one more helpful at all of RPI.

Dr. Crone is one of the most enthusiastic, helpful teachers I"ve ever had!  The work we did in her lab during the last summer of my grad work there was thrilling! As a teacher, I appreciate all her hard work, her thorough knowledge and her kindness!
Boring ... talks like a research paper.
She taught great last year, knows her stuff and loves to teach. Doing lots of great research, she's the hardest working part-time member at RPI
Good teaching technique

Professor Craig is a great dynamics professor but when it comes to his classes in mechantronics and control systems his passion for the subject matter becomes his weakeness.  He is unable to teach any of the material it is simple presented.  This class was perhaps the biggest waste of my RPI tuition since i gained nothing from it.

This is a good professor. If you go to class and pay attention to the problems he gives as examples, you will not have a problem. I got a C in Dynamics and that was because I didnt do the homeworks. Do the homeworks!

Prof. Craig is fantastic! He will help you learn Dynamics like none other. If hea is teaching it, take him. Go to class, pay attention, do the work and you will be rewarded. Anyone who says he is obnoxious just found themselves on his bad side. And he is always around for office hours to help his students out.

Professor Craig is the best professor that i have ever had. If you have to take a dynamics (even though its not in your major) take it with Professor Craig. He explains it in a way that anyone can understand.
Most likely the best professor at RPI and a heck of a decent guy, too.  If you put forth some effort, he will go out of his way to help you understand difficult material or even try to find a JOB.

The comment below is ridiculous. Professor Craig is the only reason I passed Dynamics, with his review sessions and going to his office (since I was stuck with Li). If you find this guy to be a bad professor, well, you're completely out of luck at RPI. A really great guy.

Professor Craig was a very arrogant and obnoxious professor. He showed interest in teaching, but was rude when you asked for help, even if you showed an initative to know WHY you couldn't figure it out. Overall, he is an overconfident individual who truly shows an interest in teaching, but only to feed his already oversized ego.
You can tell he's really interested in teaching.  Always interested in helping you out.  We got a lot of hands on experience in this class.

He really cares about the students. The first week of class he said "I really want to give you all A's and I think thats very reasonable."  I missed some classes due to illness and he told me to forget about his class until I made up the other classes.  He also gave us his home phone number and told us to call him whenever we needed help anything.

this guy is the best teacher i have ever had. he is extremely energetic and very captivating about what he teaches, making it very easy to learn the material. he has his students use industry standard equipment regularly in class, so that his students have a concrete background in their field instead of just hours of lectures. prof. craig is among the best in the field of engineering in the nation, and certianly one of the very best here at rpi.
No Comments
He is brawlic, very nice, easy going..
Not so great!  Very hard class!
Prof. Craig is the man. He really cares about learning and it was always a pleasure to work under him. I wish there were more prof's out there like him.
BEST PROFESSOR EVER!!! I WISHED I WAS THE IN THE MECHANICAL ENGR DEPARTMENT. HE KNOWS THE MATERIAL IS HARD AND DOES HIS BEST TO EXPLAIN..I LOVE YOU CRAIG. I HOPE I GET AN A. LOL

the course isn't as easy as a 4, but with craig it seems that way.  his teaching is by far better than any other dynamics professor.  holds extra help sessions, encourages students to do homework and learn from it, even allowing them to hand in late if necessary.  if you get a chance, get craig.
Kevin Craig is my hero!!! he is such an awesome teacher, and i was very lucky to have him as a dynamics instructor
West Pointer.  Brilliant.  Uses color-coded markers like a madman.  Teaching effectiveness is unparalled.

The man is genuinely interested in helping students and seeing them succeed in their courses and new careers.  You can really tell that teaching is a 'Calling' for him rather than just a job. I wish more RPI profs were like him !!
No Comments

Best teacher I have ever had. He is helpful. He cares about the individual student. He'll devote any amount of time needed. He also runs his own class in such a way where he shys from lectures and just works homework problems. He's as good as they get.

Great professor, hands down.  Emits a genuine interest in each and every student's success in his class.  More than willing to help and will respond to emails at 5AM.  He's done some very interesting stuff for industry too.  I highly recommend him.

Gets a high easiness rating because he's very helpful and thorough with difficult material (Engineering Dynamics), even encouraging students to call him at home.  Don't talk smack about West Point or he'll crush you with his dangerous forearms of justice.
One of the best professors on campus
He's a very friendly guy, but sometimes he seems lost and like he doesn't know what he's doing.
Very friendly and caring professor. Knows his material well and has a sense of humor. Answered all my questions without being condescending and responded to all my emails promptly.

I suppose it's not really fair for me to rate this guy as I never actually went to his class. He put me to sleep in the first two lectures so I figured might as well stay home in bed if I was going to sleep.  With that said the curve in this class was awesome, I had a B with a 48 average.
Breneman is a really helpful professor. Easy to contact if you had questions.
No Comments
No Comments
Since I like this subject, it's quite easy for me to understand him. Enough said.
No Comments
He can sometimes go off on a tangent during lectures, telling stories about his grad work and whatnot, but most of them are funny.
Friendly. Replied to emails quickly.
He is ok, but he is very unclear in what he wants.  He has 3 TAs!!!  What a jerk.  He assigns a lot of hw and asks questions on tests that are unreleated to class dissucsions.
No Comments
Breneman is very clear & helpful, willing to give students extra atention
Tough class but he does a good job of explaining the concepts. Gives out candies to those who answer or ask questions.

Professor Cusatis really really cares about the students in his class. He is not really that great of a professor, but he does everything in his power to make sure that students learn something in his class. Some of the techniques are obnoxious... When you see him in office hours he is very nice and good at explaining the material.
He really wanted to make sure students LEARNED. He was extremely helpful during office hours. Class was boring, but he did his best to help students learn material.

Made every effort possible to reach out to all students, and help them understand the material.  Tests were very straightforward, he made the homeworks himself (as opposed to assigning numbers from the book) so they looked a lot like the tests.  Lastly, he gave everyone the opportunity to move up one letter grade or more if they did well on final.

Well he started off very poor.  Very hard to follow and really fast.  He did make up for some things by offering more points.  Should have focused more on the course itself instead of penalizing for lack of statics. Needs alot of work.
Got off to a rough start but made up for it in the end.  I think he has a lot of potential to be an excellent instructor, look for good things to come as he gains experience in teaching.
Worst teacher ever.  Introduction to Structural Engineering

He is a very nice professor however I feel that the lectures are much easier than the homework, which makes it very difficult to figure things out on your own. Labs don't really seem like they apply that much to the tests. However, if you email him a question or ask in class, he is super responsive and friendly.

He was very helpful. When the TA's would not respond and fix a grade that was input incorrectly he did immediately and fixed it right away. He's also a very nice guy, great to talk to and definitely wants you to succeed if you're trying.
He understands you and wants you to succeed. He would give you full credit for a late work if the reason is valid. He also explained questions in detail as well.

Prof. Michael doesn't add much to his lecture slides, but he'll do demos sometimes. Not much lecturing each class, time is taken up with labs (which are useless). He gives formulas but there's not enough focus on understanding concepts. He still might be one of the better professors, but that's not saying much. He is flexible w/ office hours.

This professor pretty much just reads off the slides but he will always help when you are confused with something. I think I only did well on physics because of the crib sheets and the fact that exams are reused questions from back exams.

NOTE: This is for PHYS2350

I do not understand all the negative feedback about professor Michael as I really liked him. He goes over the syllabus on the first day and sets his expectations very clearly immediately. If you ask for help during the labs he will gladly help. Only is rude if you are rude first/disrespectful first. He is straightforward

(for phys 2350 but the option isn't available)

Class is almost exclusively self-taught, with the professor only coming in to fix experiment equipment problems.  Fairly disrespectful to students, has a huge ego, and is very disconnected with the students' knowledge about the course (mostly because he's not teaching).  Amazing TA's though.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Horrible lecturer. Literally reads off of slides for 30 minutes ON WEBEX while IN PERSON. Forced you to attend class with activities even though they could easily be done outside class. Does not teach physics in an engaging nor inspiring way.

Prof. Michael is a solid teacher. His lectures often lack enthusiasm, but he does a good job of explaining concepts. My main issue with this class is that no practice problems were ever done in class. This is not helpful, and I feel like we were never taught how to approach problems. I often relied on my high school physics experience for exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Tough grader

reviews.comment: One of the nicest professors I have had so far, the exams are kinda difficult, but overall, good class and his lectures are pretty good, If you have any questions, ask, also he genuinely cares about his students. I asked him questions on other physic work, and he stayed like 15 minutes after class to explain it to me. overall, amazing person
He's a great teacher but the course overall is pretty difficult. You can't miss class since there are in class labs every class. He does what he can to help and is always available for office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: He prefers we call him Darryl and isnt the best lecturer. He wouldnt give me credit back for a grade incorrectly put in the system, so I got a 0 for a homework i actually got a 100 on. This was the difference between a B and a B- I would not take him again.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: IED can be a frustrating class so make sure your project will fit the class requirements by communicating with Lander early! Good communication with your team is key and Lander is a fair grader, just pay attention to the rubric!

Dr Lander clearly understands what his students do and don't understand and can articulate complicated concepts well. He is very accessible during office hours and is willing to move deadlines if too many things are overlapping. Even though I don't particularly enjoy the content of the course, having him as a professor has been a pleasure.

While there is no attendance, it is imperative to go to lectures. He has a great character during lectures and wants to make sure you're understanding the topics. Very caring and gives good feedback on assignments. His syllabus is clear and understandable. It is important not to brush this class off, as it gets very tough.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Lander is a straightforward and effective professor. Expectations are explicitly laid out at the beginning of the semester, and grading is fair. Recitation-style office hours and activity on Webex makes it easy to ask Dr. Lander questions outside of class. This course also contains an Engineering Ethics Seminar. Optional Final.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Has a clearly defined schedule in the syllabus from the beginning of the semester, and grading criteria is always well-explained, particularly on lab reports. Always on top of his responsibilities as a professor (holding extra study hours, responding to emails, etc.).

Was a great class, and surprisingly the best intro course by far. Don't be afraid to take this class with Lander, great guy and very to the point. Also, he may come off as a bit sassy at times but this isn't anything to worry about. Accent is the best too, fits the class perfectly.
He is a nice guy but he can be pretty disorganized at times. For labs he is very specific on formatting. I liked that final was optional.

Great man love the accent too
Easy-to-follow lectures and exams are fair. I also like that the final was optional.
This man is an absolute G. You can tell he was raised by the streets and is respects the code. He will never cross you and will always take the time to explain things better.
dan lander is undefeated

Surprisingly nice and understanding guy, class is engaging despite occasionally dull material. He realizes that some of the concepts are very confusing and does his best to address students' difficulties. Not a pushover, will make sure you actually do the work but it is in the interest of making sure people actually learn the material.

He loves the material, he is funny, a little snarky, and actually cares about you learning the material (Hint, he is obsessed with triggering turbulent flow). He is passionate about climate change, and the homework reflects the material well. The homework can be supported by chegg, however, the numbers/exact details will be different.

3 Tests, weekly homework, 4 quizzes, and a group project will define your grade for his thermals and fluids class. He's a very knowledgeable guy but has no idea how to pass on that knowledge. Very boring lectures and unless you've got previous background on the subject, you probably aren't going to follow along very well.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Lander is easy to be impatient when someone asks simple questions in class. The lecture notes are a little bit messy. His tests are quite tricky including conceptual questions and extended answer questions. The time for tests is really limited. About the homework, we have at least one homework per week.

Dan Lander is an excellent IED professor! He is a very friendly and approachable person. Also, he appears to be one of the most generous grading IED professors. Despite two of our subsystems not working properly, my group was still able to pull a B+ on the demo. We also got an A+ on the final memo, and many other professors simply dont give A+s.

Terrible teacher. The averages were almost always below 50 and he liked to point out how we should have done better because a small percentage of the class got A's on the Test, while never addressing the fact that over half the class failed the test and tried to say it was our fault that the grades where bad.

Took ochem 1 and 2 with him, and did fine.  GO TO CLASS! it really does help.  Reading the textbook clarifies lots of points that he often circles around, but you have to do the problems.  They are the most important part of the class.  Cutler is really good with explanations for how difficult of a subject ochem is.
If you enjoy being insulted on a daily basis, little to no out of class help, and tests that do not reflect lectures, this class is for you!

He definitely cares about his students.  He has many office hours where asking questions really helps! In the beginning of ochem I, I thought he was a bad teacher, but then I had Michael Aldersley and realized how much of a BETTER teacher Cutler is!Tests are hard, but if you work hard, it's fine.  Took ochem I with him and now in ochem II ;)

Prof Cutler is a very good lecturer. The trick to O Chem is keeping up with the reading /problems.  It helped me to READ every word of the text and do all in chapters problems while reading. Doing prep before the course helps especially Klein's Organic chemistry as a Second Language. Exams are hard, but not impossible, generous curve. I got an A-.
terribad

He's tough and expects students to put in a lot of work on their own, but he's not the horrible person these ratings make him out to be. He does care, somewhat, about students if they ask for help. Also, you leave this class with a ton of knowledge if you put in the effort.

material on tests is barely covered in class meeting with cutler one-on-one is mildly helpful..he is less rude but still doesn't help very much writes test questions exactly like he speaks..not with proper english not easy to understand

This is the worst professor I have ever had. He does not know how to write questions and his tests take most of time to just decode the questions. EMD is the 2nd class I've taken with De, IEA was the first. He was a great IEA professor - very clear and fair. I think its the way EMD is setup, but it seems scattered. His teaching is still pretty good, grading is fair, and he makes sense when you listen to him. He's intense so people might find him intimidating. Overall, I would recommend De.

I really don't know what people see in this guy.  He is the only professor I've ever had who will go through a slide show and skip the examples.  He'll do a useless derivation and skip the examples.  If you're someone who learns by seeing how things work and not from theoretical explanations I'd stay away from this guy.
Clear and intense.

One of the best professors ever.  Very clear and thorough in lectures.  Helpful in office hours.  Book not very useful, but he makes up for it.  Go to class, and you should be fine.   The TA was not a nice grader.
Best prof. he makes everything clear

De was a great prof, by far the best I've had. His lectures were clear and he was very helpful during his office hours. He really cares about how his students are doing in the class. I highly recommend him for an IEA prof.
De was the best teacher I had so far. I'll recommend him for IEA.
Excellent teacher! Very helpful, kind and caring. Made IEA a really fun class.

De is a cold human being who only cares about his CV. He doesn't care about his students. He doesn't communicate, and just isn't honest at all. He is just about the worst advisor you could hope to have. He shows students no respect, ignores emails, yet expects you to show him the utmost respect. If he says 6 hours, he expects 30. STAY AWAY FROM DE!
Very scary and intimidating.  Goes over material quickly which can make it hard to learn the stuff you need.

The guy is a moron. He doesn't care about his students, if you go to his office hours and ask him a question about the test even if it's not about your grade he tells you to see the TA. He never starts class on time and we always get out late. it sucked.
A very good professor. Sometime goes through lecture too quickly but is excellent for 1 on 1 help. I would recomend him for IEA.
Good professor.  He is helpful at his office hours.  He lacks the ability to motivate the students, but it is IEA.  He did seem to care about our grades.
He's my advisor but has never returned my emails.  I would recommend a different advisor if he's your's.
De isn't a bad guy at all. I mean, how interesting can you make IEA?
umm...he was alright...he did an OK job...could have done better
he was always willing to help. he cared about his student's test scores. lectured from power points that were very helpfull when it was time to take a test
Horrible teacher, thick accent, nasty to students, poor time management in class.  TA was much more useful than Suvy D.
not a bad prof, but only reads off power point without enough example problems, never had enough time to finish the activity and were always at least fifteen minutes late getting out of class
Excellent professor. Clearly knows his subject. Make sure you really prepare for the tests. Don't use the solution manual.
Excellent professor. Clearly knows his subject. Don't use the solution manual.

Shaver is a good professor for understanding the material that is being presented.  That said, he hand writes all his notes and his handwriting can best be described as terrible.  Expect to have to ask the person sitting next to you for clarification on what he actually wrote.  The other problem with Shaver is that his tests are merciless.

He lectures from the book, which is excellent, and has everything you need to know for the course. He also can answer any question you might have. He knows his stuff. That said, he makes up his own exam questions and they are DIFFICULT. Averages in the low 50's. Tests concepts and understanding with abstract problems. Highly recommended.

Shaver is a great professor who genuinely cares that students understand the material. He didn't post his lecture notes online (even though he had them typed up for lesson planning) but hand-wrote them every class. I actually really enjoyed this because although his handwriting kinda sucks, he is very clear and makes the material easy to understand
The project was very interesting and we learned a lot about iteration and design
Project was interesting learned a lot about UX
Learned a ton about design. Reading was a lot but really good class.

More work than a communication intensive class!!! Attendance is required and he spends at least 10 minutes at the start of class (8 AM) calling out names of ~100 students... If you are late (come in after your name is called), he lowers your attendance grade (even if he is still calling out names of other students and you come in late...)
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Highly do not recommend
Tough quiz, easy exam.
No tests besides the final, but have to give two presentations on cases. Not difficult. Graded generously

Genuinely one of the worst professors I've had at this school. He is extremely unaccommodating for uncontrollable/unplanned circumstances. I was doing work for 3 people in a group because they didn't do their part and when I expressed my issues with him, he basically told me to deal with it because he didn't want to because he doesn't care.

His lectures are not very useful when it comes to the testing material. Memorize the test book because lectures only cover about half of the exam material and lecture slides contain minimal information so take notes on what he says. Your standard teach it to yourself class. Grading by the TA's are very inconsistent.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Rude, arrogant, condescending, inappropriate, unprofessional, and awkward. He is not even competent with material: disorganized, unable to answer questions, and constantly confusing himself. He acts as if students existing is an inconvenience to him. Almost your entire grade is three exams. If you have to take him, focus on his lectures 100%.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: EACH test is 20% of your grade and covers 8 chapters! Higher expectations for students than himself. Confuses himself constantly and can't answer questions. EVERYTHING comes from lectures that are read from disorganized, misspelled powerpoints. Acts annoyed if you talk to him. He needs to leave this position or gain some empathy.

Powerpoints are TERRIBLE and make no sense so you actually have to go to class and take word for word notes to understand them. He also teaches stuff thats not in the textbook so even though you read EVERYTHING- only some of it is on the test. Powerpoint are also random things about physiology- not the most important concepts. Studios were annoying

He mumbles and his powerpoint slides are very difficult to understand. Says "right?" about every 10 seconds. When you ask questions, he doesn't seem to know the material well and it's better to ask the TA. Watch videos on Khan Academy to learn the material.

Overall, I found him to be a pretty decent professor. The tests are fairly graded and mostly based on backwork, and the lab reports take a while to complete but are not very difficult. I definitely learned a lot from this class and consider it a very useful course.

He is a bit of a timid professor, but he knows what he is talking about and is actually very nice. Overslept for a test once and he let me take it anyway. The book, his lectures, and the labs work well together to teach physiology cohesively, but the lectures were probably least useful of the three if you are going to skip one.

He's a terrible lecturer, but if you can somehow pay attention to what he says you'll be fine.  I never used the textbook, and just tried following his slideshows and did well.  The studios seem pointless most of the time, but a few of them are actually useful to know whats going on because they make the lectures make more sense.

You basically have to teach yourself the class.  He is very quiet and nervous and most of his slides make very little sense, if any. Studio is a complete waste of time, but the corresponding sections in the book are what he will test you on.  There are only two exams, so keep up on the material because there is alot of it...

I didn't have him as a teacher for very long. Unfortunately, he died before the midterms in 2021. From what I gathered being in his class, he was caring but he was a hard-ass. A was a great math teacher and an even better person. Talked a lot about his family. He was very understanding. A good teacher that was unfortunately taken from us too soon.

Prof. Drew is a very nice guy. He enjoys teaching however he sometimes cant be helpful, specially in office hours. The material he taught was more his than Holmes' but the homework assignments were from Holmes' book. Overall he is good.

Professor was a clear but slow lecturer - I spent most my time pulling my hair out because I knew where he was going. Ocassionally makes mistakes and gets confused making bits of lecture confusing. Exams are pretty easy and very evidently based on material from recitation/lecture.

The materials covered on his tests are easy. The only problem is that he and his TAs are hard graders, and you might end up losing a lot of points because of small careless mistakes. Overall, he is quite funny, he tends to prove things, and his test focuses on lecture material, so pay attention and try to understand the concepts.

He's funny as hell during lectures!  He kind of stinks at arithmetic, but he does a pretty good job of explaining the concepts he wants you to know.  The tests are easy if you do the (non-required) practice homework, but I didn't realize that until the last third of the semester :(
He doesn't know how to explain anything.

Not exactly a bad guy, but STAY AWAY FROM HIS CLASS.  You have to write essays on every test with him in calc II, and his tests are pretty tricky.  If you're stuck with him, do all of the HW probs (even though they're optional) because the test questions are similar.  I would've bombed if it wasn't for our grad TA.
I went to two classes, drew is a nice guy and real smart, but not good at teaching, i dropped is class took kiehls class and got an A no prob, DREW is the WRONG choice
Only does proofs, the only reason i passed was because of our TA that had terrets.... ps Grades like a Swanz (that means not good)
He's an okay guy and makes the material relatively clear.
He's cute and always smiling..i like him!!
If I hadn't already taken Calc in high school I would have failed.  Don't take Drew.

He taught the material well and made sure to tell you what was going to be on his tests. The graders however were very harsh, although by the 3rd test they loosened up a bit. The class seemed to be harder than all the other calc sections, but those that earned there grades got them.

I'm sure he cares about his classes deep down inside, but it doesn't really seem like he's able to get across exactly what he's trying to do. BEWARE: He has this really hard grader FOR SPRING 2005. AVOID CALC II WHILE THIS GRADER IS STILL EMPLOYED... he is infamous. I got a B in the class.
By far the worst teacher iv ever had.  Basically he sucks.  He teaches us nothing and expects us to know everything
He just goes over problems and doesnt really bother to teach any thing.  and the tas are no help

I found this class very complicated, and although I thought Prof. Drew was friendly and all that, I just didn't understand what was going on. Our first exam was failed by most and took several weeks to grade. Aaagh!
funny and knowledgeable, will end class early if the topic is something easy. lots of practice material availible if you need it
funny and smart.
best teacher I had at rpi my freshman year hands down
Amazing teacher! I would definitely recommend him. He is very nice, and keeps you interested. He is clear and helpful.

Knew his stuff and went out of his way to make sure we knew the material. Accent's not a problem, random tangents on his favorite movies & books made an awful class somewhat bearable-we once watched his 10 favorite movie moments at the end of class. He would solve the in-class problems himself rather than use the solutions manual

IEA is a terrible class.  That said, it's required for all engineers.  Dobry was a great guy and a pretty good teacher.  Never went to his office hours (IEA is REALLY EASY) but his explanations in class were clear.  Big fan of movies, one class we even watched his top 10 movie quotes of all time.

might be hard to understand at first but you do get used to it. and he does like to say "substraction" instead of "subtraction". he randomly talks about movies which is a nice tiny break from the class material. but he teaches well and is really nice.

Great teacher! The subject sucks, but he keeps everybody awake with jokes, and a funny accent. You'll get used to hearing "soob-straction" instead of subtraction. Once we took a break from work, and watched a quick movie.
Good teacher, probably my best in my first semester at RPI.  Tries his best to help you out, it's just really up to you as to whether you want to take advantage of this or not.
He is the human form of Strongbad.  Really funny, not my favorite class for sure but he made it bearable.  It sucked when he left the TAs to teaching though...
no child left behind!
i don't really like his way of teaching...
No Comments

doesn't speak english well but you get used to the way he speaks.  Its hard to get an A in this class unless you put a lot of time into it.  Sometimes he is funny.

Dr. Drazan is an amazing IED prof. Sure, he's harder on his students than most IED profs are but the skills he teaches in IED are more valuable than anything written on the syllabus. I've gotten much more out of IED than I would've if I had any other prof. It's a ton of work, but if I had to do it over again, I'd be sure to take it with Drazan.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Class starts very easy as a review of Physics 1 all through the first test. Second test was also mostly easy if you knew how to solve problems symbolically. Gave extra credit on exams for proving that you got together with a group to study. Third exam is challenging material, but completely doable as exam questions are drawn FROM HOMEWORK.

I had him for Engineering Dynamics and I dont think the class average was ever above a 70, the standard deviation for the first two exams ranged from 15-18. He does an awful job explaining how he came up with a solution during lecture. If a student isnt doing well in his class, he just says this is basic kinematics and says you should know it.

Worst IED professor at RPI Expects way too much for presentations and memos and will just give you an 80 regardless of the effort spent You are graded on his personal opinion of you rather than your performance Prepare to cater to all of his personal interests if you want to deviate from the 80% box

A very complicated figure and the most annoying person I know. I'm all fine with a professor with great sassiness, aggressive requirements, and tendencies to give frustrating critique to alter your design but not this one. This guy may know a thing or two about architecture, but is also a down right hypocritical manipulator with little good heart.

Has a lucidly defined interest for his studios, that is, expects his students to rigorously tackle the issues foregrounded, which tend to be rather intriguing contemporary ideas. Maya & Rhino wizard, all his students go on to be highly proficient.  Sometimes, frustrating to deal with his demands, but I’ve come to appreciate how hard he pushed us

Snooty elitist irrelevant waste of time.  Can't butt-kiss ... can't pass here.  Name-dropper, fragile-egoed typical case of someone unable to make it in the real world, so opted to hide in academia.  Avoid this guy if you can

you can take the man out of harvard, but you can't take the harvard out of the man. This guy is one cocky mofo. Loves it when you kiss up, and often grades unfairly. Doesn't realize that we do have other classes to work on, and we aren't made of money to spend on models. But yes, he is pretty hot, especially since he's trimmed down a bit.
Hes not the best but hes not the worst either.

Be prepared to kiss his ass and if you dont then be prepared to fail. He is not really a very useful professor and he plays favorites. great teacher and cool guy.  lets you have alot of design freedom, and is really interested in everything, really cares about his and your work and takes pride in the work of his students
