Pretty nice guy, he can be a bit vague at times, but overall, I think he's a good designer and a cool professor. He's not the person thats going to baby you through everything, so part of the learning you have to do yourself.

Very arrogant person. Does not know how to teach, very disorganized, and unaware of the financial limitations of his students. Talks way to much about Harvar... like we give a damn. Serious butt kissing and ego stroking needed to pass his course, or you have to do a project you hate to please him. I don't recommend you take his course.
He definitely makes you do your work, but the tests and quizzes are pretty straight forward. As long as you do the homework, you'll be fine.

I love Professor Schoch! I read a lot of scary things on here before I took his class, but he's actually an awesome teacher. He's really nice and will work with you if you need help. He sticks around during studios to help. He works at a fast pace, but it's not too hard. BUY THE BOOK! All the quizzes and tests are open book so make sure you have it
No interest in the students, leaves lab shortly after assigning studio. Powerpoints are short and incomplete, no repetition. Do not take this class

Professor hardly teaches. Completely unclear in wording questions/expectations, rude to students and TA's, assumes people already understand programming, many students have to the take class multiple times to pass, tests do not reflect the course material, you can know how to code perfectly and fail the tests. avoid him unless you already know VB.
Very good professor. Yale Ph.D. Knows what he is doing

Bases lectures on very clear and helpful slides which he elaborates on and clarifies very well. Is extremely knowledgeable and can clearly answer any question. The work is difficult, but fair, with no surprises. Seems like a nice guy and has an awesome (but easy to understand) accent. Favorite class in CS so far (doesn't say a ton but still...)
Professor Drineas' lectures are both clear and exact.

Very good at portraying information. Slides online for entire semester, and writes the notes then goes through the slides for double reinforcement. Strong accent, but easily understandable. Very approachable.

He's great at teaching the material, but he teaches a subject that's really hard for most students, and he doesn't give much leeway with grading.  His accent is crazy, but easy enough to understand.  Some semesters he assigns less work, try to get one of those: the homework isn't very helpful, and the projects are worthless.
A very good professor. Attractive, too.
Lectures were pretty good - questions answered during office hours - tests were reasonable except there's no partial credit! The TA's grade way too harshly and the homeworks are impossible.
hotttness  :o)
sometimes hard to understand because of his accent, but, other than that, a pretty good prof

Course material presented well, but professor took a hands off approach to grading, and left it to incompetent TAs. Exams were rather difficult compared to HW's and material actually taught (applied mathematics). Result ...a MASSIVE curve put on the class at the end of the semester.

Very clear lectures, good at teaching the material. Always seems kind of angry though when people get things wrong, but he will take time to explain things and answer questions well. And his accent is fun
He looks like a Greek older version Jimmy Fallon.

This class can be pretty confusing but I found that actually paying attention in lecture made it alot easier.  Its a hard class but he teaches it pretty well.  I had more problems with the homeworks than the tests.

His tests are rediculously difficult and he doesn't give partial credit on exams.  He does, however really know how to teach and knows how to get the material across to the class, unfortunately labs and homework don't reflect the lecture.

Teaches well. Learned a lot but the tests are hard, so be ready to study. You learn a lot from lecture, so don't skip. Hw is difficult but feasible. Overall, a good professor.
Good Professor, he knows his stuff. Easy to understand.  Difficult, but not impossible.  Homeworks took a considerable amount of time but covered the material well.

An excellent professor overall.  Its not exaggerating when I say I learned more from him in the first lecture than in the entire year with Prof. Hardwick (CS 1).  Tests are hard, but curved, and the homeworks/labs truly help to understand concepts.
Definitely has an accent, but does a good job presenting the information clearly. Tests are difficult, but looking through his lectures prepare you pretty well
His undecipherable Greek accent, poorly-written homework instructions that leave you wondering what the hell he wants you to do, and his difficult tests are all reasons he was never meant to teach.
Good Teacher. Does an awesome job of explaining in lecture and, if you attend his office hours, he will give you tons of help. The tests are difficult but if you study, you'll be fine.
He is a demanding professor, and yes he does resemble a lizard. Most people come out of his exams brain dead. But he's cool guy.

I love this professor. He is nice and kind.
Best professor evaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaar.  Open book tests.

This class was a total joke.  I did 30 minutes of work for the mini project and our team project was half done and he accepted it.  Still got an A-.  Deadlines are flexible and he is happy as long as you put in effort for it.  Has high expectations to start then lowers them.

Completely incomprehensible. I don't understand 2/3 of the words he says, and the other 1/3 is useless information. Like the other users, I recommend avoiding at all costs (even if you graduate late, you will still thank me).
The worst.  What a waste of time.  You'll wind up teaching yourself the entire class.  And you'll still have the pay for the class, of course.

AVOID AT ALL COSTS!!! Will lecture for hours on the most useless info. Quizzes are based on things that were never discussed in class. If the quizzes aren't bad enough, you can get NEGATIVE grades on them. Homework is mostly jokingly easy, but the quizzes kill it. He even said he gave a 50 question TF quiz where every answer was F! Stay away!

HORRIBLE!!!!!  you can't understand a word he says, and spends the whole class flipping through power point slides.  Is very unclear about what is expected of the students.  NEVER TAKE HIS CLASS!!!!!!!!

thorough and hot
Absent minded at best!

A very smart and experienced prof, wish he was teaching more often. Has some weird jokes too.
Great to listen to.  Makes any class fun yet intellectually engaging.

I took her Ecological Economics class, and I liked it.  She's interested in everyone's opinion, and is willing to admit when she's wrong, or if she doesn't know the answer to a question.  She mostly teaches upper-class and graduate classes, and she grades as such.  As an underclassman, I felt a bit overwhelmed by her expectations, but I had fun.

My experience in Global Economics was wonderful. A lot of the class was spent in discussions, and professor Duchin really helps to foster debate. The class itself was not overtly difficult if class was attended daily. A plethora of videos kept the class grounded in reality.

One of my most favorite classes my freshmen year. I loved her global econ. class! I got the chance to know her a bit better over a scholarship dinner at my fraternity and she's pretty much the coolest I met my first year of college. The class is good, but it would be nice if the book was easier to read. She describes it pretty well during class tho
Insightful on topics of discussion.  Interested in students' comments.

I didn't have the greatest time in the class, you work for the grade you receive. Midterm and Final exam questions are very subjective. A lot of movie presentations and discussion in class, so you definetely cannot sleep through it. She has a lot of personal experience in the field so know what you're saying.

Excellent class if you are interested in what's going on in the world. The prof. has exceptionally rich knowledge in global issues. Her in-depth analysis on every topic is very helpful in organizing and developing your own view.
It's just a bad class.  No prof could make it interesting.  Just don't take the class, even if you are interested in econ (like i was), because it makes you dislike the subject :(
An excellent professor. Exceptionally helpful, and amazingly knowledgeable.

If ever there were a completely useless class, this is it.  The material taught in this class consists of things any educated person should already know.  The workload for this class is enormous, the grading is strict, and it is almost completely uneducational.
Assigns a lot of readings, but these are not required to do well in the course. Pretty objective about controversial material. Highly values attendance and participation.

Anna is an amazing academic; not only does she comprehend meticulous scientific knowledge but pushes theoretical boundaries to a new level.  She has advised me as a graduate student for over three years, and I find her insights and guidance invaluable.

Anna Dyson is one of the most brilliant professors I've encountered.  Her continuing dedication to students? intellectual growth and enthusiasm has made her one of the most inspirational mentors in my life and career.
Immensely influential, she has been an inspiring figure for my career and life goals.

Anna is a dedicated teacher and brilliant individual.  To appreciate her intelligence you must have a legitimate understanding of the topics at-hand, or else a writing utensil to jot down references and look them up later.  She expects much from students and certainly won't entertain individuals unwilling to engage in upper level discussion

Amazingly intelligent woman, but should never have gotten tenure. Constantly bites off more than she can chew and is very disorganized. Her comments are wishy washy... (e.g. "Third graders could've done this work" one day and the next "Oh my god this is like Alvar Aalto"). Excellent w/ theory work, but bad w/ implementation into design.
Anna is definitely flighty but amazingly intelligent.   Its almost like too much is going on for her to sort it out.    She's such a hottie I spent my class staring at her and fantasizing-- if only--

Anna Dyson is a disorganized mess.  She is not on top of either her schedule or her subject.  She is very unprofessional and plays favorites.  There is only one right answer: hers.  That is no way to run a studio.

Anna is a good teacher, but like all good teachers, she does not baby you and hold your hand all day. You have to take the initiative to open the book and apply the knowledge to your design. She gives you the basics and what you need to know and leaves the rest up to you. For those of you with a bad design sense...well...you're not going to do well

I couldn't understand a word he said and he could be very disrespectful towards his students. Also, he did not teach at all; he basically expected his students to know everything without him teaching it.

Although I know several people who couldn't follow his lectures, I enjoyed them and got a lot out of them.  It took a while to get used to his humor and accent, but that wasn't a problem after the first week or so.  Very helpful at office hours, and he offers extra credit for going.

Has a thick accent that takes some getting used to, but his explanations of physics principles are awesome. He's extremely enthusiastic in class, which can come across as corny, but is really pretty hilarious. Best teacher I've had, hands down.
He knows what he is doing, but is just not a good teacher.  Really smart, really funny, knows what he is doing, but does not relate them well to students, which is, unfortunately, his job.

He's really hard to understand and the homework is impossible. I used the answer key for every hw. But if you can complete the assignments and write a decent cheat sheet for the test, you'll have no problems.

He makes his lectures entertaining and helpful in office hours where there is candy. Exams were hard to prepare for, but all the lectures and materials are online for review. MATLAB is important for the course but the programs were easy. Taking the class I felt like I wasn't learing much, but in retrospect I understand the material much better now.
Sang-Kee is the man! He made science exciting and entertaining.  If you're looking for the best Physics I professor at RPI, Sang-Kee is your guy.  Gold nanoparticles!

Really goofy and enthusiastic, which sometimes took away from the class. Like a lot of the faculty, his accent is a little tricky at first, and you really need to pay attention. Extremely helpful though.

I had a great time in physics I thanks to him. He is passionate about what he does, and will help you if you need it. Very pleasant to talk to outside of class, even though his accent may get a little getting used to for some people.

Funny guy. Definitely a people person. If you don't understand something then go to his office hours. Has a bit of an accent, but if you're from RPI then you know everyone has an accent. This course is pretty standard. It's not easier nor more difficult than any other physics I course.

He is very interested in his teaching, he is one of the few teachers who actually looks like he cares about the subject he teaches.  His jokes of the day are the best.  He sometimes wastes a lot of time on random tangents though.

Very entertaining professor. He may be difficult for some to understand because of his accent, but I didn't have any issues with it. He works hard to keep his students interested in the lectures with jokes and demonstrations and has a genuine interest in seeing them succeed. Homework is more difficult than in class work, but the exams aren't.

Hard to understand, wastes time trying to sell the fact that he hands out candy. But does seem really interested in getting to know students and teach. But this enthusiasm sometimes draws back on learning.
Seriously tries to teach.

Professor Eah is not that bad.  He is tough at times to understand, but if you pay attention hes not bad at explaining things.  Hes also  very willing to help, and entertaining in lecture as well. Just do the work, and remember he is not even the one writing the tests, quizes, labs, and homeworks.   And he says he gives out candy at office hours!
very friendly. he gives out candy at office hours.
Class was fairly entertaining, but he expected the class to be able to do problems about new material rapidly.
he sucks, plain and simple. if you want to pass, don't take him. p.s. he can't speak english either.

Scott is an awesome teacher i had him for ma 060 and i would recommend him to anyone that is struggling in math or wants a good teacher that actually cares about you passing. The homework is normal as any math class. Don't skip class in order to understand yet if you do he will post notes or homework online.  Great teacher.
Great lecturer

Professor Dwyer's lectures are very fast paced and can be hard to follow. Make sure you go to office hours though because he is very helpful there. Tests are tough. Labs are difficult because the material is only taught that same day so there is not time to learn it. Dwyer knows his stuff and is concerned with helping students learn the material.

First, I admit he is a great professor. But there are many downsides his course, due to the limited space I'll just be brief: fast pace in lecture; offer quizzes at lecture which Persans don't this semester; if you need to take this course, make sure you place the lecture and lab at least 2 hours apart so you can work on lab before, lab is a lot

Dwyer is a great teacher. He lectures very well and explains things really well. Each lecture he goes over material learned in the previous lecture which is super helpful. You definitely want him for Physics 2.

Prof. Dwyer is one of the best I've had so far at RPI.  He's a great lecturer and uses lots of real-world examples and applications to explain concepts.  In Physics II, you can't find anyone better, and I'd recommend him wholeheartedly.
Very good prof, he also writes labs that making fun of MIT and liberal arts colleges

Prof. Dwyer is great in that he is actually a TEACHER, not just a guy who talks at you about his subject. His explanations are thorough, his lecture experiments are practical applications to course material, and he is extremely personable. Plus he has an awesome mustache.

Dwyer is a no BS prof;however if you're willing to learn he will go out of his way to help you.Physics II is a hard course and if you're not willing to put the work in, you won't do well(unless if you're a genius).I got a 63 on the first test and a 97 on the last test-Dwyer helped me quite a lot;he helps you if you take the initiative.Great teacher

Awesome professor. Even if you're not a big fan of physics, Prof. Dwyer's lectures are entertaining, highly informative, and interesting. His use of written notes will help you learn much more than Powerpoints will teach you. He is very approachable and friendly, and will gladly answer any questions you may have.

Worst physics teacher I've ever had. You have to copy projector notes otherwise you only have the textbook to review, so you don't have any time to understand physics! Activities were also meaningless. Even I got them all right I don't know what's the point of it. He didn't reply emailed questions, and usually just disappeared during the activity.

Professor Dwyer keeps attention during lecture by taking commercial breaks to give awesome demonstrations.  He tells stories that make the material memorable.  And he explains difficult course material concisely.  Although Physics II is still a difficult course, Professor Dwyer keeps it straightforward.  He is an amazing teacher.

Dwyer is a great teacher. He knows his stuff and loves to answer your questions. Magnetics and electricity aren't my strongest suites but he still made it good going through and learning them. He's great to talk to out of class as well. He'll help clear up anything you need as well as be a great person to talk to in general.

Dr. Dwyer is a wonderful professor. I can't stand Physics yet I enjoy class with him. He's very helpful, very smart, and very open to questions. He also likes to have "commercials" where he gives real-life examples of how things work. Great guy!

Dwyer's really cool, really knows his stuff, and really enjoys teaching students. He chews you out pretty hard if youre ever late and he's got some pretty high standards but he makes sure his students reach them.

He was a great professor. He really tries to make everybody understand the subject. If you ask him questions he will answer them. He loves the subject matter and enjoys teaching. He does a great job at describing the topics and their relevance.
horrible person, bases every student on any one single person who might have done something wrong. Dont even try to talk to him because he is a rude snob
Dwyer is tied with schmidt for the best professor at rpi.  He's extremely clear and his notes are excellent.  Goes out of his way to help you.

Amazing professor, no other way to put it. Unlike other professors too caught up in their research hes JUST here to teach. He writes all the notes out for you every class period, and gives great review packets before each exam. His teaching skill is reflected in his tests averages being almost 20 points higher than other sections.
Great Professor. He will help you get the grade you want. His class is slightly more demanding but you will do well in the tests if you listen to him
Scott Dwyer was one of my least favorite professors at RPI.  If you are a nerd and love physics that you'll probly love him.  but for the average student... try to avoid him.
It's more important to Dwyer that you get a good grade than your actually learning the material.  This could be a good thing depending on your preference.
Simply put, he is the Man.

Very good teacher, presents the material well. The rest of the sections use prepared powerpoint, while Dwyer writes all the notes out for you in class. His classes have the highest average of all the sections.

He makes the class fun and is a overall great guy, and most importantly, he really knows how to teach.  The only drawback to his class is that the homeworks are graded very hard.  I probably would have gotten an A in his class if the homework rubric was the same as the other classes.

Dwyer absolutely blew me away with how amazing of a professor he was. After an absolutely horrid physics 1 experience, Dwyer completely redeemed the physics department as a whole. Never has a professor gotten my interest in a class, conveyed the material so well, and been such a good guy. RPI needs to use him as a model!!!
The best Physics II prof. Had the highest exam scores out of all the other sections.

I don't have enough words to convey my satisfaction and impression of Dwyer. He does an awesome job with the lectures and exam prep- it makes learning pretty easy. One caveat: he is pretty tough on grading homework but this is a tiny price for what you get for signing up for his physic sections.

Excellent professor. I actually learned the material IN CLASS for once. He explains things perfectly.  Top 3 profs I've had. There is one downside tho. His class grades the homework like crazy. I've gotten a 100 once on a HW assignment, and I try very hard on them. In Physics I, I used to get 100s on all my HW w/out trying much. Still amazing tho.
If you want to do well in physics 2 definatly take it from this professor!  He cares about his students and their gtrades...and he does everything possible to help you do well!
Awesome teacher

Dwyer is great.  Get him, seriously.  A little more work that the other professors, but totally worth it.  He's a really nice guy and an EXCELLENT professor, one of the best at RPI for sure.  I wish he taught physics 1 too.  Prepares you for the exams really well, gives out study packets.  A little bitter about IBM, but it's ok.  Totally rules!

far and away the best teacher I have had at RPI.  He cares so much about students understanding material, and shows it with the best tests scores of all sections consistently. He makes a serious effort to  get to know his students,and he is an extremely out going nice guy and an excellent teacher.

Dywer is a great teacher.  He steers away from the powerpoint and that helps students immensely.  He also knows students names and knows their difficulties.  Execellent in class demonstrations.  Made me like physics again after a terrible physics 1 class.
Seek this guy out for your pysics classes. He is the most helpful prof i've ever had. He'll care more about your grades than your parents
This guy is freakin amazing.  Extremly helpful, easy to understand, clear notes, makes the class somewhat interesting.  Plus he give a well detailed packet before the exam to study from.  Excellent.

this guy is the man. hes had the highest test avgs in his classes for a couple years in a row.  hes english and speaks it well.

what i can say is that his sections had the highest test average overall
An awesome physics professor.  He learned my name, that's a big thing to me.  He really cares about you as an individual and wants to help.
Cool guy.  Tough to get an A but his review packets are amazing.  He'll know your name if you go to class.
Nice guy, great teaching and goes out of his way to help you.
Possibly the best professor at rpi!

Scott is the best professor I've had so far at RPI (2 yrs). He explains all concepts and presents material in an understandable fashion. Gives out great review packets, and MAKES HIS OWN notes, in addition to the powerpoints. Gt his section for an A!!

Dwyer was by far the best teacher I've had so far at this school. He explained things thoroughly, but clearly. Plus he's a funny guy and has some great stories about the people at IBM. Definitely sign up for his section if you can!!!!
Great Teacher...best one to have.
awesome teacher. easily the best i've ever had. went out of his way to help the students.
he's easily the best physics professor here. very helpful, knowledgeable and genuinely cares about his students. thanks prof. dwyer.

He's an overly opinionated leftist and gets preachy in class. That being said, the homeworks are easyish...and all online. The papers are all graded by the TAs so it depends. My TA was cool and just gave you an A if you met the length requirements.

Class is very boring and he talks in circles. Your grade in this class mainly  has to do with your TA. The class is not too hard, just showing up and participating gets you pretty far and then it was just regurgitating what he said in class into an essay and I ended up with an A

no man has ever made me hate their own opinions so much.  the class is 99% opinion based with terms and concepts that are largely imaginary and subjective.  this class will not be a class you enjoy.

Woodhouse is an interesting teacher. Take this course if you would like to learn about the intricate web of connections that are woven within Science, Technology, and Society. Very helpful and knowledgable.

She is very kind and knowledgeable. Always willing to help students improve understanding. Easy to reach outside of class, responds to emails quickly. Professor Ecker is one of the kindest people Ive met in the teaching field. He knows that there is no point beating around the bush with what he expects us to know for upcoming quizzes and exams. Kindest professor I ever had. He cares for the students, understands their situations, and gives fair difficulty exam. He is awesome!

He is one of the best teacher in the whole school, very nice and kind. On exam, he would not try to make the questions hard. The thing that he consider is whether students understand the knowledge or not.

Our grades are made up of two parts: quizzes and exams. Homework is not mandatory, but make sure to do your homework, study for your tests. He is the best professor!!!!!!!!!!!
I'v e heard this is his 52nd year teaching and his last year teaching in RPI. Best wishes for him.

Joe Ecker is one of the nicest people you will meet at RPI. Great guy, lectures are good, and plenty of teaching experience. 50 years teaching at RPI! Quizzes are based directly off of HW problems, tests are fine if you study for them. HW not required. If you have the option to take him for Calculus, do it! Can't say enough good about this man.

He was honestly the best for Calc 2. I feel like I learned everything clearly with out having to worry about hard tests (they are very similar to examples in class and back exams) . He is such a nice man, and you can tell he genuinely cares about his students.

When I took him it was his 101st semester at RPI. He is a funny old man but a great caring guy that takes the time to try and learn each of his students names. He is very reasonable on what exactly he will cover. He explicitly explains what cases he wont test you over. He isn't that good with technology so he sometimes cant figure it out.

Hmmm... this is basically a calculus class for Business, Arch, and Liberal Arts (HASS) students. Much much much easier than regular Calculus I. Attendance is not mandatory, and notes are emailed after each lecture. Weekly quizzes which are basically free 100s. The tests are also exactly like the backtests (EXACTLY). Easy A, even if you suck at math

Demonstrated kindness to his students and I wasn't really expecting to encounter such a considerate professor during my college years. And, he made the effort to memorize the names of his 100+ students.

Joe Ecker is the true full package of professors. He is incredibly sweet and truly cares about his students. He makes a usually very challenging course extremely digestible (arguably easy) and actually exciting to learn. If you're considering taking a course with Joe, don't hesitate.
They don't make professors like this anymore. Other professors can learn from his delivery and dedication.

Chill professor but material was not that easy. However, I missed half of the lectures, but still got an A because he sent all lecture notes through email. The TA was also extremely nice and an easy grader, so the class was a lot easier. Test questions are basically given the lecture before the exams so you can memorize them and get a 100.
cool guy, emails the notes to all students everyday after class so you don't have to worry if you miss a class

This guy is an absolute legend. If you can get a class with this man teaching it, you have struck gold. Quizzes are easy, homework is helpful (but by no means necessary), tests are straight forward. Cute old guy, he emails you all of the slides from his lectures, and all of the quizzes are questions from the homework that you get the answers to in recitation
Best professor!
Ecker is hands down the best prof in RPI. He remembered everyone's name in the first week. Tests looked very similar to the back exams. Final was easy too. Very nice guy!

Ecker made an effort to get to know all the students personally and tried to remember all 250 of our names.  It seemed successful, too, as every time I saw him outside of the lecture hall he addressed me by name.  All the quizzes consisted of questions from homework assignments, and the final was made up of questions from previous unit tests.
He is so kind and good, even if sometimes do not have very clear mind to teach some things.
Joe Ecker is the bomb. Favorite professor at RPI.
Ecker is a very fun teacher who posts the class notes every day.  I would definitely recommend him as a teacher if you need to take calc 2. It's been a blast with him.

Great man, I hope he recovers from his stroke. He has photographic memory, and remembers everyone's name, its quite amazing. He is sweet and you will like him immediately. He also emails lecture notes and back tests that he has made. There is no final.

Best calc professor ever. Really makes an effort to know the students (he will remember EVERYBODY'S name) and is very clear on all material he teaches. He also emails everyone the notes after each class.

Ecker is easily the best math professor I've ever had. He connects with the students and genuinely wants his student to succeed. He's easy to understand and doesn't trick students. I wish I could take more classes with him!!

Very helpful and easy to understand. Some might find class slow-moving if they've already taken Calculus. Makes an effort to know everyone's name, even in classes of 80+ students. Exams/quizzes not difficult - picks most questions directly from homework/practice tests.

Ecker's an awesome teacher. He is friendly, unassuming, and very easy to ask for help, if you'll ever need to. Best teacher I had this semester. The class was both easy and informative - not something I can say about a lot of classes here.

As he says himself all the time: "what a guy". He is easy to understand, tells you exactly whats going to be on each test. and is super funny.

Ecker is awesome. Super nice, super peppy. Lectures are clear and understandable, makes powerpoint drawings during lecture explaining everything and emails them everyday. Exams are just like the back tests. Exams are also relatively easy, just study a bit.

Joe Ecker is hands down the man.  He learns everyone's name and is extremely helpful with whatever you need.  He wants everyone to succeed and he outlines the curriculum as such.  He makes his own tests cutting out the middle man.  Get into his class!!!
Joe Ecker is the man.
Easiest A earned at RPI hands down. His backtests are almost identical and he emails you the notes from each class.
Easiest Calc 2 class ever. His test are super easy and he is really nice.

Dr. Ecker is great. He explains everything and gives you the back test form the previous year, then just changes a few things around. He is very helpful during office hours, too.

Best teacher I have ever had at RPI.  I love Joe Ecker! He was personable, learned everyone's name, engaged students and taught easy material very clearly.  Take calc with him if you can!  Great TA Adam went over every problem before quizes.  Used maple for labs and tests.  No final!

EASY A..however, you should go to class. Two-hour lectures are very boring but going is very helpful. He goes over every test  with you, and some of the questions are the same ones you will find on the test.

reviews.comment: Easy class and optional attendance. Most classes are lectures (which were streamed on WebEx). The weekly readings could get heavy but you could skim them and still get a good grade.

prof schaffer is very caring and accommodating towards students. while most assignments are not graded, if you want to stand out, you should do the readings and participate in class. they are very encouraging of students' ideas and perspectives.
Very respectful and understanding towards students and the readings/lectures are very interesting and insightful.

Guy is an extremely caring person who prioritizes the needs of his students first. His lectures are interesting and make use of a large variety of multimedia. STSO 1110 has a lot of assigned reading, but if you at least take a look at all the readings and take some notes during lectures, you will have no issue succeeding in this class.

He talks about very odd philosophical topics and will agree to anything a student adds even if it makes absolutely no sense. His class is an easy A and the only reading that matters is before presentations. If you want to learn, this is not the class

Really nice guy, he's young so he relates to the students well. Very reasonable with absences; usually doesn't take attendance and is very willing to give extra credit if you miss lots of classes and want to make up your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Group projects

reviews.comment: Very political and he makes it clear at the start of the class that that's how he will be, but he also makes it clear that you do not have to agree with him and he likes when students push back on his ideas in respectful ways. He's chill and laid back, lectures are kind of boring, but can also be very weird and interesting.

Guy is one of the best professors I have had at RPI! He really cares about students and strives to be the best instructor he can be. Guy is also just all around a very nice person that wants you to be successful. Guy also focuses more on inquiry, which helps you grow individually in the subject being taught and focus on your own professional goals.

He is an amazing professor who actually cares about what you say. Lectures are not mandatory, recitations are. If you talk during recitation, show you are paying attention and show some kind of interest and time investment in your project you'll get an A. Queries are a pain in the ass, though. But overall, he is a fair grader.
Guy is one of the most easy-going people in RPI! He cares about his students much and gives us great chances to show off our abilities during group projects and presentation.
Guy is one of the BEST professors I've had at RPI. He's funny, caring, and puts lots of effort into teaching his classes.

He's actually an adjunct at SUNY Albany as well, I took his International Economic Relations class and it was super easy. Very knowledgeable professor, great guy, easy to understand if you pay attention.
easy easy course.

Great Instructor. Knows his stuff.

Exams go beyond class content, including conceptual questions not adequately covered. The course pressure is unusually high due to perceived unfairness in exam questions and the dullness of the content. Professor Wertz focuses heavily on formula derivation, neglecting the explanation of physical significance and interesting anecdotes.

Her lectures were basically just reading off the slides, and she can't really explain concepts in any other way - if you didn't get it the first time, she won't be able to help. All of the grading was done by the TA (who was actually really cool). Tests (for all of phys I) are all multiple choice, the rest of the grade is in-class activities + HW.

It was an online course during the covid era. She simply did not give any lecturing and asked us read textbook by ourselves. Besides, she would straight give you 0 out 5 participation points if you not talking in "5 min feminism" (which was usually 30 min btw), which capped your overall grade at 95%, making it extremely hard to get an A.

Be very careful of the participation!!! You not only need to attend the class but actually answer the question. I got good grades in all exams, quizzes, and homework. I only got 1 out of 5 of participation points just because I didn't answer questions during the class.

I came into this class with such high hopes only to be utterly disappointed. I literally feel as if I learned nothing in this class. When I tried to ask basic questions, Wertz could not even answer really. She gets so nervous. She is so out of touch with difficulty levels so hw assignments are long and beyond difficult and the exams are cruel.

Exceedingly tough class. The exams aren't all that bad, and the quizzes are also fairly ok, but the homeworks... god, the homeworks. Also home of the infamous five minutes of feminism. People might say they disliked it, but imo it is one of the most important parts of the class, because you talk about things physicists need to think more about.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I have had Wertz for EM theory and nano optics. She's OK but slightly below average. I learned my stuff in EM theory but honestly can't say I learned any nanoptics. She doesn't always know EM as well as she should and is very self conscious. She can grade surprisingly harshly and for nano optics assigned way to much(unrelated) work for 2 credits.

Professor Wertz is very nice and if you ask her for help she will gladly give it to you. She also heads Women in Physics. EM Theory is tough as anything but Professor Wertz makes it accessible, and the tests are tough but survivable. I enjoyed having class with her!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Electromag theory was probably the worst class I've ever taken. Unfortunately, Prof. Wertz is extremely out of touch with what students need more time on, which is partly the students' faults for never asking questions. Explanations usually rather non-intuitive. Tests not that difficult. DEMONICALLY difficult and long homeworks from the get-go.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Great course...best HASS I've taken at RPI. Grades are based on papers and a final performance project. Fun class.

She's a philosophy major teaching non-philosophy courses. Has no idea how to perform the most basic tasks on a computer, which would normally not be an issue in a literature class; however, she likes to take up class periods with presentations on the background of a book or on surrealist art. Grades easy, but class is boring.

Horrible teacher. Scattered in style, doesn't know what she's doing electronically, and constantly goes off topic for no reason. She's boring, monotonous, and generally just not a fun person to be in the room with.
Easy class, but hard to sit through--she's pretty scatterbrained and has a habit of going off topic. Overall, not horrible, but I wouldn't recommend it unless you love the subject.

Visual Culture was originally 4000-level, but got demoted to 2000-level during this past semester. That was probably a good idea. Though I learned a lot, and though Esrock is knowledgeable, class discussion relied heavily on student participation. Also, for too much of the time we were learning straight from the text. That's not how culture works.
Boring class. Read a lot of books and a presentation. She's sometimes unfair with her grading. But, otherwise, it's a fairly easy class to take.

Worst class I have ever taken!!!! She is flippin crazy!!!! She spent atleast 2/3 of the class reading aloud. This was a graduate course, normally we are expected to read for ourselves. She was rude and disrespectful to students during private meetings. In class she was unable to answer basic questions, and unable to lead a discussion.
Scatterbrained and totally out there. Avoid her at all costs. She thinks she knows what she's talking about but just ends up running herself in circles and half the time she's wrong.
No Comments

She always tries philosophizing during class time, and just ends up going in circles about nothing. Doesn't let you think for yourself. A relatively easy class, but the material covered was awful, and she just presses her own opinion on you, even on debatable concepts such as surrealism and abstract performance. Cant spark discussions for anything.
Ellen is great!  She is really laid back, flexible, full of crazy stories, and makes class really enjoyable.  She's quite an interesting character.

I took solids with him at NC State, the class is fine with the exception that he doesn't respect his students. Completely wrote off our concerns about a test question nobody knew a formula for, wrote off the fact that we didn't think the formula sheet was helpful. He doesn't take feedback into consideration at all. KNOW YOUR REVIEW, he tests you.
Do the homeworks! Exams are normally old homework problems/the method is the same. Ferede does a good job explaining problems in class and accommodating for most issues.

This was for Strengths (ENGR-2530). Kind of mid. Not the easiest to follow during lecture, although his slides were decent for later review. Do the homework! It's 20% of your grade and will help you with the exams. I'd probably consider taking this with someone else if possible.

ENGR 2530, (Not in the drop-down menu for some reason)

Great professor who knows what he's doing. There are in-class assignments so go to class. Also, HW is worth 20% of your grade so do it religiously since there are only two tests and a final.

Has some of the most unclear grading criteria of any professor. He will specifically tell you to include one thing, then will doc points for it the next day. Very rarely gives grades above an 89. During presentations, be ready to get severely criticized. So hard to understand and would not reccomend

Professor Ferede is very articulate and puts a lot of effort and detail into his lectures. Great at teaching and explaining things, and always takes questions from students. BUT ENGINEERING DYNAMICS IS SO BORING THOUGH. It's a shame I have such a great professor for such a dull class because I'm actually in a coma for like 90% of these lectures.
I'm a fan of Fan

Great professor and person in general. Clear lectures and the grading was lenient enough to not be stressed out over the class but still be able to learn the material. Also loves to talk to students about any work/research/side projects they are working on. Highly recommend taking her course.

Probably the best prof I've had.  Clear lectures, great at explaining concepts and using examples.  She will reference current day events and papers, often with humor included!  The class felt easy but I know I was learning a lot at the same time-- thats the true mark of an exceptional professor
Shes a really good teacher. You can read her slides and get the gist of all of the material and during lecture she makes them all really clear and easy to follow if you pay attention.

Prof. Fan is my favorite econ prof. She really cares about her students and you can feel her passion on what she's teaching. Her slides are neat and clean and her teaching is explicat and useful. I can tell you the contents in this course is pretty helpful when you have a quant BA interview. Will take her others courses(4580 and 4590).
A very reasonable professor who puts her students well beings into mind all while teaching a very interesting class. I would highly recommend her to anyone interested in taking Econ classes at RPI
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: ECONOMETRICS is INTERESTING
Videos and uploaded notes are very high-quality.  Teaches this class like a well oiled machine.

Very knowledgeable about the course. He can be very condescending towards students, and hard to find in office hours. If you are able to learn everything through lectures and do not have to talk to him directly, you shouldnt have a problem.
No nonsense professor who covers material thoroughly

Nightmare professor. His lectures aren't too bad; fairly slow-paced and easy to follow if you pay attention. But he regularly belittles/is rude to students, and is very inconsiderate/dismissive in office hours. Finally, his grading philosophy is a mess; tread carefully.

I only last a month in Multi-Rotor with UAV Systems with Gandhi before dropping the class. This is his first time teaching the class and the structure was terrible. There is no textbook and the course is based on memorizing and deriving millions of equations. Homework graded very harshly and takes on the order of 12-15 hrs IF you can code well.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Gandhi is super clear in his explanations. Even when he subs for other professors, students leave the class wishing he was their professor all the time. No book, so only his notes. And tests are open notes as well. I fall asleep in his class sometimes, however.

Outstanding professor. His passion for the material is as clear as day. He gives very clear and interesting lectures, which contain much material the textbook does not have. Professor Fajen is one of the first professors of mine who I feel is great to have beyond simply reading the textbook to understand the material.

One of the best professors at RPI.  The only professor that I have witnessed to be capable of teaching extremely complex and difficult course material in such a manner that a novice can follow.  As a student, you cannot be lazy in his class, or you will do poorly.  If you put in the effort though, you will learn an immense amount.
Do not take this class if you want an A. The class material is very interesting and Fajen knows what he is talking about, but the way the grading is structured makes it hard to get an A.
I aspire to his greatness.
Great teacher.  Material can be challenging but everything is completely FAIR.
Really good teacher, lectures and course content are interesting, which is rare at RPI. Very helpful, and cares about his students.
Good guy, very well run classes
Do the reading and you'll be fine.  Get involved in class.  He's a good guy, and a decent lecturer, and the material is actually very interesting.  An all-round awesome experience.
He knows his stuff and not too bad on the eyes either.

She is awful at explaining things and answering students' questions. Good luck using her lecture notes to study, they seem super organized but are terrible at guiding you in the solving process. Take with CSL if possible so that you have access to notes from the lab

Lectures are terrible and she forces you to show with in class assignments. Your best bet is to use lecture notes from other professor's classes as her notes often are unreadable/don't have the info necessary to do the homeworks.
Literally the worst professor I've had in my 4 years at RPI. And that's saying a lot

I think she gets bad reviews b/c students put in no work besides in lecture: if you put in work on your own to understand the math, her lectures are extremely clear and office hours are very helpful. ModCon can seem abstract and she does a great job of explaining real life applications. Favorite class at RPI and one of the best professors I've had.

Somewhat new teacher. Lectures are very poor, but forces you attend with in class assignments. Gives homework with some problems on topics not covered yet, so you can't complete immediately. When I reach out for clarification on homework she tells me I'm wrong, but it turned out I was correct. Diverges from textbook methods, gl making out her notes

She seems to struggle as a lecturer, she is a very good lab professor. She seems to be more comfortable with that. I have had her for both CSL and MODCON (in her first time teaching it) and can attest to her being helpful and cared about the students passing if you went to her for help. Would recommend for lab(CSL) as she is very knowledgeable

Good luck!
She is a very new teacher and has a hard time teaching material. She has not yet found a way to relate her industry experience to class material. Lectures are often unclear and don't include many relevant example problems. The goal of specific problem solving methods is often unclear.

The class was incredibly easy, but the way she taught and lectured was abominable. You would probably get more lost and gather the wrong information if you paid attention to her in lecture. I suggest just reading the next book and doing back exams, and you'll get an A. Take the class with Hurst if you can.

Professor Felix teaches well and clearly. The previous raters clearly didn't bother showing up to class, because I did and received an easy A by just applying what she described in her lectures to the homework and exams. She was very accessible by email and offered clear feedback on my grades when I asked for it.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Do not at all costs take Mod-Con with Felix. If you do, find someone who is in CSL to give you Joshua Hurst's recorded Mod-Con Lectures. (If she realizes that really cannot teach the class a semester, then she will even post them as well to the Mod-Con LMS). If she is the only option, take it next semester. Need to graduate? Take them at same time.

About to take the final tmm, learning and reviewing solely from another prof's lecture vids/notes, just like for previous exams throughout the semester. Her in-person lectures were poorly communicated, and exam content didn't match what was taught or given from the lectures/homework. If I have to take again, it'll 100% be under a different prof
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Sarah Felix is by far the worst professor Ive had in my 3 years at RPI. In lecture, she has no idea what she is talking about, and posts past professors' lecture notes instead of her own. The back tests and homework problems she gives have little to no relevance to test material, and doesnt even post solutions. Also cant use methods from textbook
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I am not sure she really knows what she is talking about at all, lots of inconsistencies with lecture notes, homework solutions. Very difficult to tell what material will be on tests
If the prof knows what she is doing, she does not communicate it well.
strange class
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Required to purchase textbook then told expressly NOT to use textbook methods, exam material does not reflect material covered in lecture or homeworks

Professor Finger doesn't seem to take any interest in her students at all and it comes off that she thinks her time is more valuable then ours. She basically just reads her lecture slides and leaves. Thank god the material is somewhat interesting. If you read the book and do the homeworks, its not that hard to get a good grade though.

Posts her powerpoints, which were actually very thorough, making studying for tests much more reasonable.  Tests are not that absurd if you do study.  The weekly homeworks are a bit intense, but they are the same type of problems that go on the test so its definitely worth knowing what you're doing then instead of just copying.

Definitely a challenging course, but doable if the effort is put in.  Homework helps out your grade.  You can work with other people during in class quizzes.  Tests weren't bad after a lot of studying.  I went in thinking it was going to be hard but I pulled off the A.  Definitely better than Ochem.

I don't know...I thought her class was easy (though I relied on the textbook a lot). I mean the stuff is straight-forward, but she obviously has no interest in her students! Her office hours are at a completely useless time and she just rattles from the textbook...she also confuses herself sometimes and has a HUGE habit of saying "um" all the time!

She completely changed the course.  You've homework and in class problems that count for a grade as well as three exams and the final.  She comes off a bit snobby, but go to her office hours, they help.
Ummmmmmmm....
The hardest biology class and a lot of work. Make sure to read the chapters and be thorough with her lectures. Her exams are very detailed and challenging. Good luck!

Her lectures are very far from stimulating as she just repeats what the book says.  Neither is she seemingly interested in her students.  Definitely not one of my favorite classes here, and it wasn't due to the material covered.
Very knowledgeble but has difficulty explaining. Quizzes are easy and so are the first 2 exams. Tip: know the whole textbook!!

She changed the course. It's easy now. Rd ch's b4 class, then get EASY 5-? qzs everyday. 2hrs for tests - plenty of time. Tests pretty easy. Lectures straight from txtbk and boring. No hw. Competent prof, but not the best.

Boring. Not very good at answering questions. Tests were very long but not necc difficult. They did require thinking; some questions were pretty clever. If you could finish her test you were usually fine, but very fw people actually finished.
One of the worst classes i've taken! i'm guessing it was because it was her first time teaching, but at any rate, she could have been much more open to suggestions.
Don't bother to ask questions in class, she'll just tell you to read the book. She clearly does not enjoy teaching at all.

Worst professor I've had at RPI. Does not know how to teach, does not know how to explain problems, and can not answer half her own questions herself. She even has trouble reading off the slides which are word for word from the textbook. Should be removed from teaching position in my opinion.
Doesn't teach. Learn by yourself method.

She is genuinely a nice professor, but to be honest if I could have switched out of her class I would have. There is way too much work for a 2000 level class and here grading is entirely too harsh. She likes if you write the way she wants you to and if you don't you'll lose points. I should have taken an STS class like I normally do....
Dr. Jan was awesome!

WAY too much work for a 2000 level class, more work than some of my 4000 level classes. You will spend more time learning rhetoric than anything else. She has almost no knowledge of Web development, students wound up teaching technical classes for her. She is helpful outside of class though, and she's kinda hot. Take it with Grice and get the "A."

Assigns way too much work for a 2000 class. Unclear about topics and isnt experienced at with web design. I didn't find this class helpful and would recomend Grice. More than half of the class dropped out.
Too much work for a 2000 level writing class. Grice is much better and actually teaches what the course description says.

Great professor. Unit 1 started off weird with counterpoint and tons of rules/regulations which I found challenging to enjoy. After that though, I really started liking the course and I began to appreciate the skills that Christopher was instilling in us. Can't wait for ARTS4380!! Very approachable and loves participation
Easy class but you won't learn as much things as expected for a 2000 level class
History of Hip Hop was great, F-L is truly an amazing man.

Nate is a great professor. He really cares about his students and provides thoughtful, individualized feedback. He's additionally very knowledgeable about STS authors and cyberbullying. Lastly, I wish I could give him more than one chili pepper, bc Nate is the HOTTEST professor I've had at RPI.

The load of coursework can be a lot to handle, especially because there is a large amount of assignments to cover all at once, but the conversations and topics we get to cover in class are varied and interesting.
Great Professor with a wide breadth of knowledge regarding social issues.

Extremely easy class with one big group writing assignment and presentation at the end.  Reading assignments are long and heavily worded but you can totally get a good grade without reading them.  Prof. Fisk took a class I had no interest in and made it fun.

Fisk himself was good teacher, although he gave too much authority to his section instructors, and they weren't that great. I mean, they were nice people, but they didn't do much teaching, or much of anything, really.

Professor Fisk is a great professor who is very passionate about his research and really wants us to understand the material ("Artifacts have politics"). His lectures are intriguing and explore topics which are crucial to our ability to make informed decisions about IT and Society.

Great professor, had him for IT&Society. I don't know if I would have been interested in STS before, but I very much am now thanks to him. Material is kind of difficult, but he helps you through it very well. Just hope he doesn't use Reddit for your class...
Great professor!! Very intelligent and interested in providing students the best learning experience possible. He made this class a lot more interesting than I thought it would be.

Professor is amazing at making the class useful and relevant to each student. He works with you on anything, including scheduling issues. He may be pretty laid back, but the class was very helpful and he intelligent.

Great professor! I had little interest in the course when I signed up for it, but he made it very interesting and entertaining. Homework includes reading short chapters from the textbook as well as articles he finds relevant, and about one paper a week.
He uses real world examples in his lectures which makes things interesting. Not too harsh on grading. Would take another class with him again

Foundations - It will be Required for all Civils by 2012. Useful class when you talk to all civil professionals. Class is awful though. Floess uses Powerpoints and does not explain the examples well. Reccomend working in groups on the 6 HW's and 3 projects. 3 tests, no Final. Tough class, need to work to get an A. hard class but you should take it

Good teacher, but it sucked that he didn't have office hours.  Very responsive to email.  Class was pretty hard, but definitely useful.  The projects were real-world examples.  Probably would recommend the class and professor.
AMAZING
Carsten was a great teacher.  Class was boring at some times, but he gave real world examples and projects that proved to help in the long run.
Carsten rules!

class wasn't too bad, sorta boring, just read off slides, gave some real world examples. Projects weren't too bad. 2 of the 3 exams were take homes and fairly hard. the inclass exam was insanely hard.

I came into this class, basically no understanding of strengths and no idea how to use MATLAB. Prof always helped, and is very fair and understanding. If you TRY you will pass AND DO WELL. It helps that this is a certificate based class. Do all the hw, try for all the certs that you can. Prof is always willing to help and watch students succeed.

Took Fotis in the Spring '23 in the last semester he implemented the "certificate" grading system. If you did the work, and understood the content, you'd get an A. I definitely learned a lot not only through homeworks, but through projects related to my interest. Very good professor, unfortunate he does not teach any other courses.

I had Fotios back in 2018. He ran through practice problems with me after class and carefully and patiently explained to me what I was doing wrong. I still remember the smile he gave me when he handed me back the next exam with an A letter grade after nearly failing the previous exam. A truly inspirational professor, I cousins ask for a better one.

Fotis is hands down the best Professor Ive had during my time at RPI. He is extremely interested in actually teaching, rather than being an inaccessible research prof. He spends a lot of time working to create an interesting class, is extremely understanding, and a completely fair and reasonable grader on assignment, exams, and projects. 11/10

I had his class online over summer 2020. On day 1, he said if anyone wasn't in the country and couldn't attend regular office hours, he would adjust his schedule, even if it meant having to call in the middle of the night. I have tons of really great stories about his teaching (character limit) but he's very dedicated to helping students learn.
Very caring and inspirational professor.
Reasonable professor.

By far the best professor I've ever had. He's extremely chill about due dates and if you do the work, which isn't an extreme amount by any means, you'll likely finish with a B+ at minimum. He's extremely accessible for any needs you have, related to the class or not. He knows a lot so definitely do what you can to learn from him.
I got C in her class while I had no clue about it. I was a PhD student at RPI. She never teaches in her undergrad classes, She just shows movies and then TAs lead the class. She does nothing!

I really enjoyed her class and her teaching style.  She is laid back but expects a lot from her students AND she's fair.  Plus, she really cares about the class topics and students and it shows through her teaching.  I highly recommend her.
She is assertive, which might lead some of the other students to not enjoy her teaching style, but I found that it aided in the presentation of the material.  I learned a lot in her class.
Very intersting class, very clear about assignments, not too much written hw, mainly reading.  Classes are in debate format, makes for good discussions and class involvement.  Def recommend.
No Comments
No Comments
Hated her.  Always thought she was right and no one else had an opinion.  TAs were terrible.
No Comments
Amazing intellect -- knows something about everything

The amount you are supposed to read is very high, but to be honest I never read all I was supposed to, only enough to make his slave Colin give me credit. His lectures are very boring and usually, he ends up talking about some "Ouroboros" philosophical crap and looking for a way to seem thoughtful and unique. Colin doesnt read, OnlyWordCountMatters
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I have no idea how he is so highly rated. In the class I took with him, he was universally hated. From his smartass quips to students who disagree with him to his expectation for us to agree with his viewpoint on a contentious issue. Everyone hated his class, though the grades were generous.
Great guy, class is easy, just do the readings and do well on your final projects.

Professor Fortun is one of if not the best teacher Ive had here. He is so passionate about his work, and a truly outstanding guy. The discussion is awesome! Although the lectures can be a little long-winded (he'll admit to that the first class). I had him for both the century of the gene and biofutures. he is truly awesome.
Great professor. Very passionate about the subject matter and really makes you think about it! One of the best professor's I've had.

The best professor ive had at RPI, a cool guy and really understanding and interesting, actually has a personality which is hard to comeby here, overall the man, especially when he wears his all purple outfit including purple alligator skin shoes
Excellent professor

The lectures can be a little on the dry side, but overall tolerable. Dr. Fortun is a good professor in the sense that he tells you what it is that he expects and it is your choice whether you do it or not. Only advice is be involved with the discussions if you want to know the material for the test.
OK I guess

He cares about you LEARNING, not you passing tests on memorizations.  His class was interesting and was 1 hr discussion and then 1 hour movie/him teaching.  He's the most understanding guy I've met here, definitly take this class to learn alot and for an easy A.
The coolest Prof at RPI!
Very helpful and insightful Professor. Very research oriented and really cares about his students. Lot to learn from the course and extremely well structured.
Most awesome Prof. ever !!!
Incredible Professor, I'm an alumni and still use the learnings to this day many years later!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Very supportive and encouraging. He would challenge you but you would grow a lot faster than you would with any other professor.
Everyone should take this class from Prof Wright!
A lot of work but not hard. Best professor I had at RPI.  If you put in the work and show effort you will get an A. Take Frank Wright and you will learn a lot but be prepared to work for it.
This course demands a lot of focus and time. The team you join in the beginning of the semester can make or break you. I would take this course again.
Terrific Professor.
cool dude

Dr. Spear is a great professor; as long as you take notes on the slides (which he uploads online), you should be fine. He isn't the best at explaining content, but as long as you ask him questions, he'll answer and break it down for you! He grades based on how much background knowledge you have as well. Overall, he's very kind and understanding!
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--So many papers--Caring

reviews.comment: To understand the class content, you have to participate and go to classes and listen/take notes during lecture. He's not the best lecturer and isn't the best at explaining content, but he's knowledgeable and knows his field, and you just have to ask the right questions. He's very kind and funny, and is a relatively easy grader. Highly recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes--So many papers

reviews.comment: Frank Spear is both a caring and very knowledgeable professor, who is willing to put in one-on-one time when needed. He is the head of the Earth Sciences Department and is well respected. You cannot go wrong with taking his classes, as you learn a large amount and there is a lot of hands on work.

he has good moments but he is really not a good teacher.  he seems more interested in sounding good but is clueless if we are following him or not. he gave me a good grade but i am not sure i learned anything that will stick. avoid.
Hard to reach outside of class as he is very busy being the head of the department, but very approachable in class and easy to learn from with any effort.
Yuck!Regret paying for this course, don't recommend even if offered for free! One of the worst at RPI - a perfect example of how a professor can end a student's interest.
Completely stuck in the 1960s, unapproachable and never around for extra help.  Don't take a class with him if you can avoid it.
No Comments
Best thermodynamics (MANE 2710) professor in the department. He is really good at explaining difficult concepts in an easy way. Highly recommended.

MANE 27210, (Not in drop-down menu for some reason)

Very good lecturer who makes sure his TA's are generous with grading. Attend class since there are in-class assignments.
Good experience with him for IEA. Class always ends early which was nice. Knows and communicates the material very well.

Prof. Han is not a native speaker. But he is very knowledgeable and explains the course materials very well. He is also very accommodating. My favorite course and favorite professor for the first semester. Would like to take his other courses in the future.

As a B student, I enjoyed Prof. Han's class very much. He very appreciated students' difficulties in understanding and has been trying to introduce complicated concept in a way as simple as possible. Highly Recommended.
Excellent instructor. Knowledgeable and down to earth.

Constantly makes mistakes and lecture notes are illegible; is still using a mask, which would be a problem if it were not for the fact that his English is rough and he barely speaks up. Nice guy, but he should not be teaching this course.

Professor Han is fairly hard to understand and basically only reads off lecture slides. I had to do a lot of learning on my own. 3 exams plus a final. Exams give a lot of partial credit. Not crazy hard topics, just not a great teacher with the material

This is Prof. Han's first course at RPI, but he did an excellent job explaining the content despite some occasional grammar mistakes. Prof. Han is very knowledgeable. He is also very approachable and he had many additional office hours. He is caring about students.

Professor Han is clearly not a good teacher for this class. He strictly reads off the slides given to him making going to class of little help other than completing the in-class assignments. Professor Han also frequently makes mistakes and does not clearly answer the student's questions.
Ridiculous no technology policy for the Consumer Behavior and Product Design class. Will act beyond dramatic if he catches you using one in class. Doesn't give any clear instructions for projects.

I absolutely love prof Jain!! His ways are def different compared to other profs but that is the best part! I have taken all of his classes, and his lectures are so entertaining and engaging to listen too. You can tell he is very knowledgeable in what he teachers and it is really hard to get a bad grade in his classes so I def recommend him!

I would highly recommend taking any class you can with Gaurav. I took his Marketing Principles course in the spring and the course work was easy, but you will learn a lot from him as he has a lot of business experience and uses real world examples. Tests were fun and take-home, and the questions make you think hard.

Expect zero guidelines, instructions, or feedback when dealing with this professor. He will outright refuse to give directions for assignments and will deconstruct points and evidence fed to him all to demonstrate his worldliness and position above you as a professor. Assignments are almost always busy work he will never even open up or care about.

Class was ridiculously easy and Prof. Jain is an awesome guy. I think he knows the class is kinda a joke so it is really laid back, both midterm and final are take at home and there was maybe 3 homework assignments all semester plus one 6 page paper at the end. Also helps he is a very reputable and experienced person in the field of marketing.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is a really great guy. He definitely cares a lot about his students. He answers his emails pretty frequently. You need to go to class because attendance is mandatory and for his exams he gives the a lot of the answers to the questions in class. He provides a lot of real world examples. I never once said when am I ever going to need this.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: His lectures cover the content well, but can be unspecific at times. He is very helpful answering questions at the end of lectures. He also allows an infinite amount of on-paper notes, so take notes physically rather than digitally.

Small class. Gao is very friendly and has passion for the topic.
Interesting course material. Gave me an appreciation for the breadth of applications for network science.
He can be a little hard to understand at times but is a talented professor who is patient with students.
One of my favorite courses at RPI.

Gao's lectures are very difficult to understand; you'll have an easier time learning the material from YouTube. In addition, homework would take an extremely long time to be graded, to the point where feedback would be given only after you were tested on the topics.

Gao is a very nice guy who I can tell genuinely wants his students to succeed. Tests weren't absurdly difficult, HW was fair, and I enjoyed his lectures.

My biggest gripe with this course was with its management—grades took forever to come out, TAs were very unresponsive, and Gao himself was often not available online. This needs to be improved.

No review for the final(unless you think the 270Pages PDF has any meaning),and the hw and exercises are almost useless for the exam2.Since most of the code and specific implementation are not involved, you must use LC to learn DP,or it is hard for you to learn DP by reading book. Im not mean that Prof is bad,but there are big problems course design
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: pretty solid professor. i didn't really like this class or the textbook at all, but his lectures were well-explained and he went at a good pace. the tests were pretty fair even though I don't think they were my best performance.

Professor Gao is truly the "Luigi wins by doing nothing" of professors. There is nothing below average about him or his course, and that on its own makes it the best (or at least least polarizing) course that you'll take in the second year of your CS major.

He's a decent lecturer, but the exams do not reflect what is taught in class and the assigned homeworks.  This is a major problem because your final grade will either be the homeworks or the exams, and it will be the worst of the two.

Issue is grading & final grade policy. Final grade is based on "min of ExamAvg&HwAvg", so, it doesn't matter if you do well on hws, bc your exam avgs is what your final grade will really be based on. RG doesn't reflect the weighted totals, so until you calculate the min of the two avgs, you will think you are doing much better than you really are.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: You need to read the book to get a good grade since the method taught in class might not be the correct one to be use in test since they're only examples but not general solutions.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Take this class with him. You won't regret it.

I took Introduction to Network Science, he is really passionate about this field and is eager to share his knowledge in an extremely digestible manner. Despite the material being the state of the art models concerning network science and very focused on research papers he neatly distills the information to a clear and deliverable lecture. Amazing!

Gao's courses on Network Science are great. He is an expert in this subject and makes the material understandable to undergrads. He uses quizzes/tests as a way to gauge student's ability so he can teach to their level, but they do not incorporate as much into the final grade. Grading can be vague, but you just need to demonstrate effort.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: Very goooood professor, nice and friendly. His class has many interesting points and little practices which I love the most. He is a professor who really consider students' feeling. All in all, one of the best prof I have ever met

Intro to Algorithms can be a nightmare with other professors, but Gao presents the subject matter in a pretty straightforward way. He's not patronizing when you ask questions, and will work with you to make sure that you understand the material if you're struggling. 10/10 would take a class with him again.

This class is VERY hard, and Dr. Ramanath knows that. He is understanding and makes sure that his lectures are clear and the concepts are understood. He works with us to see how we can learn more effectively. Sure, it's all straight from the textbook and you can learn that way, but Dr. Ramanath's lectures are still very worthwhile. Bubbly guy too.

A great guy. Really helpful in the office hours. But the assignments are quite difficult. So are the tests. Grading is very tough. A very difficult course indeed. One needs to spend a lot of time to properly handle the different aspects of the course.

He knows the material well. I personally wouldn't recommend taking this course with him if there is an option. In my experience he is not fair & consistent in grading at all. This course requires a lot of work which is fine, there are lots of techniques to be covered. I personally learnt mostly from the textbook. Good book, some typos though.

I'm doing well in his course, but it's not his doing at all. The textbook is excellent. His weekly quizzes contain material he never did in class, and when a student in our section commented on how we were only to be quizzed on material taught in class, the student was told his point was not valid. Smart, but not personable, doesn't care about you.
Very mean, does not care about questions from the class or explaining the material because he thinks it is easy. i do not recommend

Very good lecturer.  I don't know why others don't like him. I think he was a pretty good professor.  His teaching style is good.  He doesn't linger on stupid questions if no one is going to answer.  He gets all the material done, mostly on time, so you don't get too behind.   Also, the Mat Sci book is a good read, so read it.
obviuosly nothings changed since he got tenureship. He's still a bully.
Very unclear and not interested in students as people.
No Comments
he doesnt like to share his wireless with others in the MRC
I was in the hospital and he refused to let me make up the work
good but tough

Knows his stuff and also teaches it well. But he also expects you to know it well (nothing wrong with that). You walk out as a different person from his course. Gives a deep insight. But be prepared to work hard or else drop the course.

He was my IED professor, and he did less than the minimum asked of him.  He provided no help when we were designing our project, and did nothing but criticize us on our work, even though we worked very very hard on the entire course.
No Comments

Knows his stuff.  Helpful, but boring and heavy accent

Tough on the outside but if you actually show up, particiapte, and perform, he is a great dude. Lectures made sense, he constantly would ask if anyone needed clarity and would explain anything further. Didn't just tell us concepts/equations/reasonings, he actually explained the process to land on a conclusion/equation.

Prof. Georg is extremely knowledgeable about Physics, however expects his students to be the same. He blew through lecture notes, thinking everything was self explanatory, and left the remaining time for "questions". The problem with that is nobody knew anything, so there were no questions, and he did not go in depth of the lecture notes.

If you are a physics major taking an upper level class, I highly recommend. His lecture style helped me learn better than any other class. 

If you are a freshman taking physics 1, he will probably be too intense, especially if you are just trying to get your science credit out of the way. Avoid.

He does do cold calls.
