reviews.comment: Prof. Georg is an excellent professor. His lectures are very clear and engaging. He is also accessible and helpful during office hours.

An absolutely Insufferable Professor. While he has a good explanation during lectures, his attitude kills the mood. He is strict and very heavy during lectures. During office hours he refuses to explain material. His catch phrase is “What's your question?” While knows his stuff, impossible to approach. The course is very hard
Please don't take him.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: He definitely is intense in class but as long as you show up on time and pay attention everything will be good. Definitely visit office hours, he's a lot less intense there and will take the time to explain concepts more thoroughly if needed. He is strict but also cares a lot about his students and wants them all to learn.

Absolutely fantastic professor. Seems scary but as long as you show up to class on time and pay attention you won't make him upset. Going to him after poor test/homework performance is really useful and he takes his time explaining things to you. A pleasure to learn from.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: I took group theory with professor Georg. the class was very difficult, and Julian is very intense, but he wants his students to succeed. If you don't ask stupid questions, and pay attention, and don't let the course work overwhelm you, you'll be fine. Get him talking about cosmology or something he's passionate about and he's a new man.

Professor Georg is an intense guy, but if you keep your head down, do the work and GET TO CLASS ON TIME, the class is a breeze, very simple if you took Physics and calc in High school. The man can teach difficult topics well, and he started to lighten up towards the end. make sure you do lots of back tests the questions are almost exactly the same.
If you know physics before this class, you'll do fine. If you didn't, you have to work hard. His lectures are really good and entertaining to watch. I also recommend doing bac exams before tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Best physics professor I have ever had! I love his lectures and he always makes learning fun in class.

Many say you should take responsibility for your learning and not blame the professor. But oh my goodness, I honestly don't see how this professor got a job in education. He is just plain awful. If condescending, rude, unhelpful, and ignorant was a person it would be him. It made being in class unbearable and learning the material seemed pointless
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The professor is the biggest bigot and pretentious person on the campus. He disregards the student's questions and claims any slightly excessive questions as "stupid". He has subpar teaching skills and his class is absolutely not enjoyable.

Bros actual thingy was straight up visible through his pants that were very clearly three sizes too small. Mans doesn't know how to shop for himself. The class itself would've been helpful if he didn't spend it being the most insufferable, pretentious man I have ever had the displeasure of meeting. Only blind and deaf people should take this class.

This class is 75% exams and nothing else. He needs to stop teaching. Clearly does not care and didn't even show up for class one day and made the TA teach. Genuinely terrible. Content wasn't terrible but the last exam was like 600 lecture slides of material. Ur cooked if ur taking any other content heavy courses with this. Back exams are useful
This class is bad. Real bad

I had him for biochem and he was eh. It was a major required course and I unfortunately was stuck taking it with Makhatadze than with Fraser. If you have the option take it with Fraser, it will be a lot easier and Fraser is a better professor.

Dr. Makhatadze, while very smart, clearly does not want to teach this course. He is fairly dismissive of questions in lecture, and when asked for help he tells students to ask the TA. Every class is just a lecture for 2 hours; it is quite boring. He doesn't show up to exams. You will do 1000 HW questions. Exams are a bit difficult but reasonable.

reviews.comment: Exams are difficult.

reviews.comment: He is a good guy who knows his material, but the material and tests are badly structured. Makhatadze teaches Biochemistry as if it is not a science, but something akin to History. Instead of helping you understand the biochemical processes and mechanisms he wants you to learn random details about them by heart. Lots of unhelpful homework too.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He doesn't take attendance but he requires WileyPlus ($140) and has homework due every class, ranging from 30 to 100 questions each time. The book is useless and his lectures are dry and awful. Only plus side is most of the test questions are from back tests

The class was ok.  He is passionate about his area of expertise and is not that interested in teaching.  Brilliant biophysicist,  would have rather taken a more specific course with him, he would have been better.

Boring class. Just goes through the slides provided by the textbook publisher. Very smart guy but doesn't care about students unless they show an active interest. Uses WileyPlus for online homework which is the most annoying part of the course. Exams are all multiple choice and change very little from year to year. No final exam.
Don't need textbook but highly useful. Lectures boring, study from the slides and book. Responds to email quickly. Really a self-teaching class.
No Comments
Took his intro to MGMT class as a freshmen. By far the best MGMT professor I've had. You have to put in the work, but he will make you improve.
Best professor at RPI. If you get the chance to take this class do so. You will not regret it.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Overall, an excellent professor. No tests or quizzes, just constant assignments where you apply everything you learn. Assignments are a lot of reading and will take outside research as well. Beginning of this class will be super confusing on what is expected of you. Asking Wright questions to clarify and working with classmates are major keys.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: I'm writing this review as a senior and I can say that this course is easily in my top 3 favorite courses across engineering and management.   Don't skip class and be ready to improve.  If you just want an easy A, don't take this course. Mr. Wright will make you work for your grade and if you take the time to improve you will be rewarded.

My favorite professor I've had at RPI. It has been one of the most useful courses I have taken because he provides insightful life lessons. The course is a lot of work and will challenge you to put thought into the assignments. However, it is very rewarding. If you have the chance to take a class with him, do it!

You need to talk. If you do not participate your grade will suffer harshly. Intimidating teacher who is very knowledgable. A wrong answer is better than no answer. You will spend many hours on the homework. You will need to apply yourself, but you will learn much. He has a lot of experience and makes you work like you are an adult.

Greatest, wisest and most helpful as well as difficult a professor you can have. One of the few that will CHALLENGE a student with material that requires thought. Chegg will get you absolutely nowhere in this class, you must actually engage and come up with your own (correct) answer that is perfect in its own right.

Wright is one of the best professors I've had at RPI so far. He goes beyond teaching management by providing insightful life lessons. If you're not interested in a business degree, then another teacher is better. It's a hard class but if you put in the effort and communicate with him, you'll get an A. If you get an A+ he gives you a letter of rec.

Professor Wright helps facilitate learning in different methods that any professor I have ever had. His class has a lot of work that takes a lot of effort. The most work that i have ever done for a class, and I'm a senior! I would recommend anyone to take his course, it inspires learning unlike any other class I have taken at RPI.

Frank Wright is awesome! Best professor I had that semester. The class was very engaging and felt very relevant. His teaching style is phenomenal. The cases are pretty simple and is an interesting way to teach the topic.
Asked for help, got none; was told I had to find out on my own. I'm fully expecting to fail, due to complete lack of communication as to what he expects from each case study.
Class has a lot of work, but it's all worth it in the end. You learn so much and get to know a great guy.
Mr. Wright is fantastic. Although he is kind tough, his course will definitely be a part of helpful experiences.

Everyone says he's hard, and the reality is, he is. But if you put the effort in, go to class, take everything seriously, do your work, and don't slack, the rewards are well worth the effort. He doesn't help individually much and he mostly leaves you to figure out stuff yourself, but that's just his way of getting  you to do stuff yourself. Great.

Mr. Wright was my first experience with a professor at RPI, and he was fantastic. He challenges his students, and makes his classroom an awesome interactive learning experience. I gained a great deal of applicable real world knowledge from him, making the lack sleep completely worth while.

If you ever have an opportunity to take Frank's class, DO IT! Especially if you're not a Management major! He's one of the most helpful, insightful people at RPI, and you owe it to yourself to interact with him. He's served as a mentor and friend to me ever since I took his class...four years ago. A real asset to RPI.

What a class! This class is a lot of work, no one will deny that.  The class is very rewording. He does not return work which is very frustrating. If you go to his office, he will  give you your grade.  He will say, "If you exceed your expectations, you will exceed mine." He gives you life tips and hints. He loves his job and it shows through.
Strongly recommend his class

Wright is one of the most outstanding professors I have ever had. Do not take this class with him unless can put the work in. You would do both everyone a favor. That being said, the quality of your work MUST rise with every assignment, or else you will do badly. Also, the standard for an A changes each term depending on the brightness of students.
Wright is a great professor. Although you think he is insane sometimes, it is all for a purpose in the end. I would recommend this class to anyone, but you will have to put in the work to do well
Intro to mgmt: Easy peasy class as long as you participate and are confident. Wright himself is no help and doesn't return your work back.... No way to know how well you're doing.

I did not find lectures incredibly helpful in learning anything about business.  However, this class teaches you how to learn for yourself, work in a group, deal with a lot of stress in a small amount of time, think (or ****) on your toes, and be prepared for anything. You won't realize how much you learned until later, during, it's hell.
Phenomenal professor.  I will always be grateful for Mr. Wright's help and advice.
Best all around course @ RPI; everyone there should have this course.  highly relevant, no matter what you're there for. contagious enthusiasm for material. inspired & inspiring.
Great

This is a class that you will only realize it's helpfulness down the line. He is a great teacher who intentionally makes assignments vague and tough to prepare you. He cares to much about his students to hurt them(GPA wise). Overall nice guy, great person to ask for advice from. Live by: "prior preparation prevents poor performance".

Lots say he's the 'best professor ever.' I find that he rambles on a lot about pointless topics. I only found the final presentation to be relevant; other than that I did not think I learned much in his class at all. However, it's  not hard to get at least at A-; he's an easy grader.

Prof Wright is a cool guy. He's eccentric, but he also knows what he's talking about. If you have to take Intro to Management, take it with him. He'll make class interesting, and he'll connect what you learn to real life.
Everyone says he's wonderful, but class isn't that interesting, I don't think.  Just rambles on about non-important things in the front of the class sitting in his little chair.
quite possibly the coolest prof ever.  he is basically the man and you need to take this course with him, you will have alot of work, but it is worth it.
He is one of those teachers that you will never forget. Best teacher I've ever had!
No Comments

A great teacher. Notihng prepares you for the ambiguity that may arise in the work world, as well as the work load. You can learn alot about business from his course. No teacher has ever motivated me to do the work as much as him.

Had him for both Intro to Mgmt & International Business over the course of my rpi career and he is extremely intelligent and well versed.  Learned a LOT from both classes and was very interested throughout both.  He's one of the best teachers I had at RPI.
Best teacher i've ever had. Learn as much as you can from this class.
good god there was a lot of work. also, he is definitely crazy. now that i'm not taking the class i like it a lot more.
Easy A, guaranteed B.  He gave 18 A's in a class of about 30.  Great guy

sooo over-rated. Wasn't what I expected. he tries to be your "shrink" or something. maybe appealing to other rpi people but not to me. found him boring and he constantly repeats himself.his class only teaches you how to dress well in the "business" world and how to "present" well. but after 5 wks, there is no need for him anymore.

The best professor I've had thus far.  Amazing at getting student involvement and still allows the student to decide how much he/she will put into the course.  Awesome, awesome, awesome.  FXW fo life!
Best Teacher first semester... got me really into it... and im not a geek... you learn a lot and the presentations are fun!

GREATEST TEACHER I'VE EVER HAD!!! FXW 4 LIFE! Taught everything with great detail and the class was amazing. BEST PROFESSOR AT RPI! You'll never regret taking the class with him. Amazing man and great professor who cares about students and material and life in general. Amazing in and out of class.

The best professor i ever had. He's fun.. understanding.. fully engaged with students.. he has that stern look but dont let it fool you. class is a lot of work, but you get used to it pretty fast. i wished prof wright teached every class in rpi cause i simply adore him!!!

Going into my senior year here at RPI and still no teacher like him....He has the ability to entertain and educate you all at the same time.  What you learn in this class goes far beyond the four years of college......Thanks Prof. Wright!
lot of work, but u learn a lot. Easy A-B
awesome class, very usefull!

Best professor there is!  He is beyond intelligent, and truly cares about the students. He is teaching for all the right reasons, unlike many of the Engineering professors. Find the time to take introduction to management.  Wright is the best!!

Took this class 5 years ago as a freshman and he shaped my work ethic at RPI from there on out. Allows you to push the class as far as you want, and i learned the most out of such a basic class! Awesome awesome guy!!!!

awesome awesome dude.  i learned more in his class than probably any other class here.  hard but worth it.
stop whining.  This guy is the man, definitely my favorite teacher ever.  Those who complain should just grow a pair.
Great Prof...Should be at a much better school
Best MGMT class i've had at RPI, Yes u work, and half the assignment is figuring it out but u will learn more in this class then accounting, eeb, and a handful of other classes combined
awesome class!  great view point on business
took his class twice dropped it mid way once and once in 2 weeks .and i am going to take it again ...can u guess who i am?
excellent teacher. likes to confuse the students, but in the end he helps everyone out to the best of his ability.
Definitely one of the best teachers I've ever had.  He has such a unique way of teaching.
Very passionate towards teaching.  Very iteresting methods.
awesome professor

He is very arrogant and has a big ego. People make the class seem very hard when it is not. He picks his favorites also. He comes up with stories that are just ridiculous.

franks incredible. i almost went to RPI because of him.  i took his course when i was in high school and he taught me so much more than i expected.  how good is good enough? frank sets his standard high and it pays off to work hard.

Good class to take. You learn a lot even if it is a lot of work. Lots of team projects, so make sure you have a good group. He acts like he is grading everything very very critically, but then he gives half the class A's.
Frank Wright is the man. He does have an ego and he speaks cryptically at times, but overall he's one of the best professors I've had so far. Taking Intro to Management with anyone else is unwise.
Third highest workload in the MGMT school, but soooo worth it.  You will learn a hell of a lot.
No Comments
Frank wright is very pompous and makes himself out to be gods gift. interesting class but bad personality
Best teacher at this school.  Lot of work in the class, but he is the best teacher.
more homework than their should be but a phenomenal course
No Comments
Frank Wright is the man, and don't you forget it.

Intro to management with this guy was the best class ever.  I am an EMAC major and I plan on getting a minor in management just so I can take all of the classes he teaches.  He is the best proffessor I have ever had.  If you can take this course, do it!
No Comments
One of the best Mgmt professors  at RPI
I felt he was one of the brightest and most fair professors in all of RPI
Best professor I've ever had.  Looked forward to class.

Frank Wright's class is the only one I look forward to.
Take Intro to Management with Frank Write
He was very hard to understand and the presentations had formulas with many pictures and no explanation. The exams are very specific so study more than what you think you need to. Try to avoid.

reviews.comment: Hard to understand, made worse by the fact that the lecture slides have 0 words on them, so it is impossible to know what he is saying. Better off going to lectures given by the other professor.

He doesn't understand that 99% of us have little to no knowledge of the topic (it's an introductory course). Graded based on 3 exams and homework that does nothing to prepare you for the exam, but it comes down to what he wants to give you. Exams are long and pointless, not fair compared to the exam given to other section (different professor).

He has a heavy accent, that I unfortunately never got used to, but the books he listed in the first class saved me. His presentation slides aren't useful unless you attend lecture and the grading is 2/3 exam and 1/3 homework with some MATLAB activities. He gives a good amount of time to do work.

Chronic rambler and as a thick accent. Aimlessly goes on tangents and not good at explaining topics at all. Presentations are completely incomprehensible, just pictures that have little correlation and very little notes. Makes you use his own book that he's still in the process of making and grades using ChatGPT. Avoid at all costs
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Lectures aren't mandatory but are good to go to because the lecture slides are bad and hard to study from. Some think he's hard to understand, but you'll get used to it. Always would ask for feedback on his teaching, he cares about student's success. Overall good teacher, very respected and has great knowledge of medical imaging.

I remember him from the mid 1980s. He was funny and interesting. Yes, the class was his podium. He was interesting but of course you needed to learn the material on your own. He did tell you what to expect on the exams, etc.
Be prepared to teach yourself the material and the mathematics behind it.  He spends most of class teaching broad concepts with little depth.  Homework and exam solutions are given in class only.

His classes are interesting. He has a really good grasp of the subject, and could relate very well with real life examples. Gave great feedback on homeworks and exams, it showed that the grading was done carefully. Homeworks can be a little hard. You have to attend his classes though as he does not put things up online. Genuinely cares for students

DON'T take a course with him. Very egotistical and doesn't teach very well. Expects you to learn all material on your own. For the final, he gave us the option of doing a project or taking a test. I offered 4 proposals to him, he rejected all of them. His interactions and approach to teaching made me feel bad about myself every time we had class.

If you get him as a grading professor for capstone switch projects or drop the class. It's impossible to please him and he arbitrarily issues grade based on 30 second meetings he has with you. Awful teacher, worse person.

He's funny, and really enjoys what he's teaching.  However, he tends to ramble and not really teach much during lecture.  He'll mention something, and then tell you to investigate it yourself (if I just wanted to investigate things myself I wouldn't be going to college).  I tended to learn everything during the lectures Prof. Radke gave.

He makes the class fun but he doesn't teach you most of the material that's on the tests or homework nor does he tell you what the tests will cover so you can study it yourself. He manages to talk a lot, though.
hilarious man. Mel brooks watch out!

Nice guy, but tends to not teach anything that is going to be on the homework, tests, etc.  Expects you to learn everything on your own.  Class is just him saying  This is amazing!  It really works!  and not really teaching much.

You have to keep up with the reading and videos or else you are screwed. Stuff that he goes over in lecture will most likely be on the test, so don't skip! He may seem like he doesn't care about you, but if you show interest and go to office hours he will care. Make sure he knows your name.
Very willing to help if you go see him for office hours but his tests are incredibly difficult. Lots of material to learn all at once but he makes it interesting. Just do not fall behind.

Dr. Plopper is an amazing professor. The only reason he gets a 45 for clarity is because he tried something new this semester. I literally learned so much from his class. His tests are very difficult, but he will help if you need it. Favorite class so far. Amazing lecturer. So inspired to continue my path as a biology major.

His class is hard but fair. He is an excellent professor, very willing to help students. BUT, the topic he teaches is a hard subject in and of itself, so work is mandatory. Lectures are great and very helpful as is the textbook.

Dr. Plopper wants you to pass his class and he cares that you learn the material, but you will have to work for it. His course is not easy, but if you truly work hard you should succeed. He gives you everything you need to pass, from past exams to real advice from former students on how to pass his exams.

I do think that Prof Plopper wants his students to do well, but he doesn't make that remotely easy. Not that it SHOULD be easy for students to do well, but it shouldn't feel impossible. If you work hard and put a lot of time in, you'll do well. But with other difficult courses and some personal issues, it was too hard to succeed in the class.

Plopper is the worst person ever existed on planet earth. He tricks you into thinking that he only want to help you learn, but really all he wants is slay you with no mercy.I went to all classes, took notes, studied the book, but the tests seemed like they're in a foreign language. SAVE YOU LIVES AND DO NOT TAKE HIS CLASSES!

Easy class if you take notes in lecture, read the textbook thoroughly and practice all the drawings. The only people who complain are the ones who don't put in the effort and are unprepared for exams. Dr. Plopper wants you to succeed and get an A.
Dr. Plopper is a great lecturer that cares more about sharing the material than doing busy work assignments. Hard class but very rewarding.

Dr. PloppG is the best. Down-to-earth but insanely smart, & incredibly helpful. I was intimidated upon registering for the course, hearing of its high demand; one of the top classes I've taken during the course of my academic career. Work IS demanding, & attendance is required as participation is valued highly by Dr. P.

This class was ridiculously difficult. No amount of studying from the back tests would prepare you for the exams. HOWEVER, the book was very informational, he was available everyday for office hours, and the UG mentors DO know their stuff. He is always willing to clarify, even set up a Facebook account to hold questions for students!
Very hard class. Very hard tests.
He was a good professor and taught well. But his tests are impossible and that made up 65% of the class grade (35% was lab).

Dr.Plopper is by far my favorite professor. I would love to TA for Cell Bio to relive the experience. Cell Bio is NOT hard. Everyone is studying hard,but is everyone studying the right way? By now,students should have set study techniques that they know work for them. If not,then such classes will seem difficult!

GO TO LECTURE, and office hours are helpful too. Tests are difficult but the amount of your grade they count for starts low and increases so if you aren't prepared for the first, it's not a huge deal. Everything stacks,info-wise. The final project takes up a huge amount of time, so be prepared.

This class is HARD. Keeping up with the lectures is a must, and reviewing the notes, especially the drawings, is very important. Plopper makes his multiple choice questions very, very difficult, so be wary of that. Lab also takes a lot of time out side of class (I came in every day for 2 hours, three weeks straight)

Between studying the material and keeping up with your lab, this class takes up a lot of time outside of class time. However, it's worth it because I did learn a TON about cell biology. Just keep with the reading, and for the love of god, DO NOT MISS LECTURE.
His tests are really hard and the class takes up a lot of time
Tests are super hard. He's good at teaching the material, but can be very pompous and somewhat inconsiderate at times.
Very good professor. He is able to explain everything in an explicit way.
He knows what concepts are difficult for students to learn and takes the time to explain the subtleties of the concepts
GREAT teacher. His testing style is a little funny, so BE WARE of answer A.

Best Professor I've ever had.  He truly cares about his students learning and doing well.  He uses novel approaches in teaching which work very well and make it easier to learn.  He writes challenging but fair exams.

Dr. Plopper is an excellent professor. The podcasts are awesome because sometimes the lectures are hard to keep up with. He does five office hours a week. . . no one else does that. If you can go to at least 1 or 2 a week it will help you tremendously. I got an A but it was not easy. Go to office hours!! He has that many for a reason.

Dr Plopper is a great professor. He really does care about cell biology and relates everything he can to real life applications. The tests are difficult but not impossible. I suggest you do what I do-- listen to the podcasts and take notes on EVERYTHING. It's impossible to get all the pertinent information in lectures. Keep calm and you'll do fine

Awesome teacher but the material and class is hard.  very helpful with office hours 5 times a week is unheard of.  He tells you what you need to do to get a good grade and that it will be hard.  Very upfront and to the point best prof thus far at rpi

One of the toughest classes I have ever taken.  Plopper really cares about the subject and tries to relate everything to real life circumstances such as cancer.  He is an excellent professor but your going to need to work in this class even for a B.  I loved this class and it really showed me what studying is all about
Tough class, but he seems to enjoy teaching and devotes a lot of time.  Questions require memorization and working knowledge of subject matter.

professor plopper is definitely one of the best teachers here at rpi. he explains everything thoroughly in class, if you dont understand anything at all, you can go to his office hrs which he holds almost every single day. he really truly cares for his students, the tests are very hard but they're completely based on lecture + modules we read.

He has the bad habit of oversimplifying his lectures and then overcomplicating his exams.  He is still excellent at explaining difficult principles in lecture, but he doesn't go in depth enough for you to go to lecture and do well on the test.

He'll always stop if people have questions, even if it makes the class go ridiculously slow, so thats a bit annoying.  But that makes him really helpful, and his tests have material straight from his lectures.  Often says specific things during lectures that you need to know for tests, so they are clear and fair. Don't just read the book though.

Took this class a year ago. Its hard and he DOES NOT post lectures. You need to take excellent notes. When he says to memorize a figure, do it, it'll probably be on the test. GO TO HIS OFFICE HOURS! He really does try to help the students and cares about how they do in his class and their overall academics. Don't be shy, ask him for help.

His class is hard and he definitely wants to keep it that way.He doesn't post his lectures online(even though he said he will;he always has some excuse)and he doesn't really say what's going to be on the test;so you just have to guess. Personally, I did not like his teaching style and the fact that he makes you read the section around the pictures.
Material was difficult but he is hands down the best prof. I have had so far and arguably the best at RPI
He is nice and knows his stuff well. He also readily accepts new ideas and comments.

I could have gotten away with taking BIOL 1010 instead of this course, but my academic adviser encouraged me to take cell bio. At times I hated her for it, but overall I believe the class left me better than I came in. The class is fast, complicated, and intense. Plopper is awesome though and he's there for you. He can really get you through it.

Professor Plopper has a very hands off teaching style that will take many people a few weeks to get used too. He jumps around in the text and covers TONS of material in just a few lectures. He leaves it up to you to figure out what will be on the tests. He's an awesome guy outside of class! Get to know him and he'll help you out a great deal.

I love Dr. Plopper and I loved this course. He's an awesome teacher and an excellent mentor. I know how to go about the rest of my academic career because of him.  This course is much more enjoyable than Bio-1010 (bio majors don't give up if you didn't get/like that class). Study a lot, care about the material, find the good in your accomplishments

Get ready to study like you've never studied before. There will be times when you'll question why you took the class, but in the end ITS WORTH IT. You will accomplish things you never dreamed you could. Yeah, I learned lots of cell bio, but really I learned I can do anything if I put my mind to it; those are lessons I'll keep with me my whole life.

This is the best class I have taken so far. But you have to work. Go to the lectures so you know what to study and because Plopper's lectures are good. Office hours help a lot even if you think you know the material. The tests are hard and you must study. The lab section is easy as long as you stay organized.

He's the nicest most caring and best professor I've ever heard of but he's absolutely terrifying. You will NOT get through his class unless you study EVERY SINGLE DAY. Go to his office hours. Theyll save your life. He'll do anything to make sure you understand the material, but you can't take this class lightly. Brace yourself. Isnt High school now

Easily the best professor I've had at RPI.  Intelligent, enthusiastic, always willing to help.  You can tell he loves to teach.  His tests are hard because he expects a lot but he will always do his best to make sure you understand.  Go to office hours, study, work to understand the concepts instead of memorizing.
great teacher. but course is easy, never read a page nor went to office hours nor asked any question and still got an A.

Everything everyone else has said is true.  Plopper is an AMAZING teacher.  If you do not understand something, TELL HIM and he will go to every end to make sure you DO.  He retaught an entire lecture because he felt no one got it.  Tests are hard, but that's the nature of the beast: YOU HAVE TO THINK ON THEM.  Just be ready to connect some dots.

amazing teacher. lectures are really detailed but interesting at the same time. his tests range in terms of difficulty, the 2nd being the most difficult. GO TO OFFICE HOURS!! and stay on top of your reading. all in all the best class i've taken so far here.

One of the best teachers I've ever had. Very articulate and engaging in the subject matter that helps you not only learn but also appreciate cell biology. The exams are tough but rigorous preparation is required. Professor is very helpful, so ask him questions.

Intro to Cell in his class is a hard class, but he teaches it REALLY WELL, I actually enjoyed his lectures to an extent, and the class was overall excellent.  He tells you his class and his tests are hard in the beginning, and he's right, but he works with you to help you get things right.

Really nice guy. Holds review sessions on Sunday afternoons just to clarify things before tests. The multiple choice questions have some ridiculous answers, but overall the tests are pretty fair.  Definitely the best professor I've had so far.
saf
Amazing teacher, though possibly unbalanced - cut his arm with his fingernails to demonstrate how intermediate fibers give cells strength. Go to office hours, they help a lot.
GO TO OFFICE HOURS! ASk QUESTIONS. IF he gets to know u he will be very elpful
Good teacher. HARD tests. Study a lot and don't fall behind. GO TO OFFICE HOURS!
Great Prof
HORRIBLE teacher
very thorough! and entertaining most of the time

Plopper is a good teacher, but get ready to work like a dog! Sell your soul to cell bio, quit drinking,and become close friends with the smartest biology geek that you know. You're going to need all the help you can get.Stay on top of things or else you're a goner. Don't take shortcuts...suck it up and read the material.

Plopper is awesome.  Concerned about the students understanding lecture material.  His analogies are amazing and help non-bio people to understand even the most complex biological processes. Ex - "Think of transcription and translation as a Xerox machine..."
Excellent Professor, very helpful and interesting / funny lecutres
Awesome lectures. Outlines everything and is interesting to listen to. I haven't fallen asleep once.
Super chill, exams/quizzes were online & open-note, very knowledgeable about the topic and explained things very well in lecture
One of the best proffessors I had in RPI. Classes are really interesting. Exams are open notes and open internet. Really good prof

Every lecture he emphasizes real world relevance to the material we're learning and mentions companies past students now work for. Quiz and test questions really make you think, but everything is open internet. Offers extra credit too. Probably the most applicable-to-internships BME class I've taken so far.
Great professor, just do the work and it is the easiest A in college!
The exam was unreasonably hard. I memorized the lecture notes and study guides. Still not able to answer the exam questions.
Makes class interesting

Honestly, the only professor at RPI i have actually learned and understood the material from..  Definitely take his classes.. He is incredibly helpful and really prepares you for exams/quizzes. Also a very involved learning environment.

Honestly, the only professor at RPI i have actually learned and understood the material from..  Definitely take his classes.. He is incredibly helpful and really prepares you for exams/quizzes. Also a very involved learning environment.

I really enjoyed Biomaterials with Dr. Gilbert. He promoted a good classroom dynamic, encouraging participation and ensuring he was clearly understood. Reading is a must for this class (at least to do very well) as the lectures supplement the text. If you hate reading, you could still easily manage a 'B' so long as you pay attention in lecture.
Dr. Gilbert was a good lecturer.  His class notes were very clear and he prepares you well for the test.  I found him a bit intimidating when I went to his office for help though.
Professor Gilbert is super cute! Woof! I took his class for the eye candy, but learned a lot! Great class!
Dr. Gilbert does a great job of finding the baseline of information that everyone knows and then building on it. This makes is lectures very clear and engaging. Excellent Professor!
If you actually want to learn the material, take his class. Best professor at actually teaching teacher I have had at rpi
Great teacher.  Really makes things simple and then he adds in great Case Studies to make you think.   Personally, I think he is the best BMED teacher.
His teaching style is very similar to that of a high school teacher.  He actually posts the lectures after class and uses them for the quizzes, so studying is easy.

He teaches directly from the textbook. There is little understanding of what is expected on exams and quizzes. His homework is just to perform textbook problems. His notes are copied 1 for 1 from the textbook. He does not clear up uncertainties and his lecture ability is overall awful

get ready to teach yourself relativity

Quizzes are nearly impossible to ace. He does not go over helpful material, just the examples from the book. I feel like I lost knowledge taking his class. Just stick to the book and try to do well on homeworks and activities. One open book final, but doing well on it doesn't really bring your grade up if your quiz average is bad.

The course material is extremely challenging but the best thing about him is that he understands this, so his homeworks and exams are pretty straightforward. Understanding the concepts is much more important than solving crazy amounts of problems

Her lectures are just her reading off her slides. The slides often have too much information on them and it seems like sometimes she doesn't even know what is going on. She is really nice, but when it comes to the lectures, it is near impossible to sit through them and actually understand what is going on.

Fundamental concepts were not clearly explained, rather focusing on a few specific examples. Tests were more memorisation of people, dates, etc. than anything else. Clearly knowledgeable and passionate about the subject but doesn't know how to teach at an introductory level

Very professional and collected, she clearly knows her stuff. Enjoyed her teaching style as well. Subject material was very interesting and she did her best to tie the relevance of the material into our daily lives. Recommended.
Tests too hard and flows through lectures too fast and they're a little hard to understand.

He was usually behind in lectures, but he always caught up by the time an exam came around. If you stay after class of go to his office hours he is genuine and tries his best to explain everything (he also gives out answers to HW and exam questions all the time)

The class is challenging, but Professor Korenowski tries to make it more manageable. While he can get sidetracked, his review sessions are very helpful. unstuck study was a great study tool alongside the textbook.
pretty average RPI teacher. wasnt too great but definitely wasnt bad, definitely better than other alternatives (Tysoe)

He tends to go on random tangents leaving us behind on the material. There were a couple times I had to teach myself material to get through the homework because we hadn't reached it in class. He's very willing to help students.
Was consistently behind the other professors by at least a week.

Dr. Korenowski is a very smart person, but he is also a professor that is uninvolved with teaching. He reads off the slides that someone else gives him, and it's obvious that he is seeing the slides for the first time in class. Additionally, he will sometimes not show up to his office hours. However, Chem 1100 offers a lot of other great resources.
Take Ma if you can, Karnowski is okay, I like his personality but sometimes he can be behind in the material.

Choose Dr. Ma for Chemistry 1100 if possible. Dr. Korenowski is not a bad lecturer, but Dr. Ma makes the exams for every Chem 1100 section, so you are better off being in his class. Dr. K hosts very helpful review sessions for exams and often gives away questions. The class is very difficult, but he does try to make it easier for his students.

Korenowski doesn't progress through slides as fast as they were already designed to. This might matter if your lab is right after his lecture, meaning info you need for the post-lab hasn't been covered yet. Other than that, I enjoyed his small tangents. Just in general though, this class WILL be a lot of work no matter which lecturer you get.

The professor is frequently behind the other two chemistry professors, meaning that the already decently difficult tests are made even harder by having less time to review material. Homework load is also very high compared to most other first year classes, and much of it is busy work. It is easiest to simply read through slides during lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: As other students have already mentioned, he just parrots the information on the slides. He is also behind schedule on the content in his lectures making homework as well as review for exams that much harder as you must teach yourself what he is supposed to teach.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: The professor brags about his students needing to spend 60 hours a week just on his class. The class average has most people at a D or lower just from the first exam. He just reads of the slides and does barely a few problems during lectures. You're better off reading the textbook. Dr. Ma and Tysoe are way better are at teaching the course.
Having Korenowski as a lecturer makes a tough class harder, he's often behind the other professors and the tests themselves are very difficult.

I would not recommend anyone take professor Korenowski for Chem 1. He absolutely cannot teach and does not explain anything. He just goes through concepts and says oh yeah this is easy, flies through an example and moves on. He never covers the material in depth enough for the exams. Take Dr. Ma if you can, but he's not great either

He seems like a really great guy. I think he would be an awesome parent to have (I know that's weird, but that's beside the point...) ANYWAYS, we are always the most behind in lectures and he gets a bit off-topic, which makes homework (which has the same deadline in all classes), much harder to complete as well as lab quizzes.
Great professor, only complaint was the structure of labs. If you show up to most lectures and answer the online questions you will get a good grade. Loved all of his stories

Lectures consist entirely of him reading off the slides, which would be fine if he wasn't blatantly using other professors' slides. It's apparent within lecture that he is viewing the slides for the first time. His genial attitude does not make up for what he lacks as a professor.

Korenowski is funny and nice but his lectures aren't great. I just show up to class for the participation credit and teach the stuff to myself by reading the powerpoints later or watching Dr. Ma's lecture.

He is a really good person, and has a good sense of humor. He definitely knows his stuff, but for me, personally, he went very fast in lecture and it didn't benefit me going to lecture as much as it did just reading the textbook.
Completely reads off the slides and teaches a lot of unnecessary information but he's a great dude if you actually ask him stuff and he brought candy for Halloween so. It's what you make of it.
Very generous with homework points. Often cancels class due to weather. Lectures are recorded, class attendance is not mandatory. TA can be hard to find. Tests similar to homework and back exams.
All around good professor. Is passionate in subject and really wants students to understand the concepts.

He is overall a pretty good professor, but he always goes off topic with his lecture and falls behind with other classes taught by a different professor. This is a problem when you are in a lab section with students who have already learned the material you haven't.

Dr. Korenowski tries his hardest to make sure everyone understands the material and gets the best grade they can possibly get. He's extremely helpful if you go to his office hours, and takes your feedback very seriously. Great guy and great teacher.
Super nice, gives lots of extra credit. Tests are open book, and you can regrade them for up to half credit back. Get the solution manual for the book.

His lectures were interesting, but totally optional. He loves Physical Chemistry and is passionate about it during his lectures. The tests were open-book, cheating was easy, and the questions were from book problems. Make sure to get the text book solution manual. Overall, easy class.

I really enjoyed Dr. Korenowski's class. He's very smart and is always willing to help during office hours. He tells you exactly what to study for the exam, so as long as you're prepared you'll do well. I would definitely take another class of his.

I had Prof. Korenoski for Chem 1 and Physical Chemistry. He was MUCH better in Pchem than he was for Chem 1. I didn't think he went off on as many tangents as other reviewers. Pchem is a whole nother story; it's his field. He did a good job at explaining things, was very clear about exam problems, and made a hard subject more relatable.

Hard to figure out the important parts of his lecture. A very boring lecturer and goes on tangents. Not a great teacher for students who need clear-cut facts for retention. Exams are only 25 multiple choice questions.
Goes off on too many random tangents, and is very hard to glean any useful information from lecture. His tests are difficult but manageable.
If you enjoy sifting through what appear to be the scribblings of a homeless schizophrenic the night before a test, this is the guy for you!

He is a very positive and friendly professor, and is always looking for ways to help his students. Chem requires out of class studying, but all the test questions are available through class or outside work. He likes to include stories in his lectures, and think about how anything in life relates to chem. Overall great Professor, always friendly!

He's lively, funny, and down to earth.  However, his ability to convey not-so basic Chemistry over a period of 80 minutes leaves a little to be desired.  It's not hard to follow with him, but in the end you realize what you've learned isn't so clear, and it's hard to get a big picture.
It is absolutely impossible to learn from him.  He just rambles on and doesn't actually explain anything he just adds more information that ends up confusing you even more...
At least half of every class is him ranting about some completely unrelated tangent.

He does not present the material in an organized fashion. He starts off with examples but never explains thee concepts behind them. He goes off on tangents most of the time. Honestly, I gave up on learning anything after the first couple of lectures. I looked at Alvaro's notes and everything became crystal clear.

He goes off on tangents and i just couldn't follow what he said. I felt like he made things more complicated than they are and taught things we didnt need to know. after a few lectures i stopped even trying to pay attention, i just read the book and did the homework on my own and was able to learn the material that way.
Good Professor, Very helpful if you need it
I had him for Eq Chem and quantitative analysis, not the clearest professor I've had, but he is wicked nice
Easy A if you study. And thank god he goes off on tangents, chem isn't that interesting.

He goes off on way too many tangents! You can't tell what to filter out because everything seems unimportant. I suggest reading the textbook over listening to him. Barely anyone in class listened to him. People were either playing games on their laptop, doing hw for other classes, or sleeping. The only reason to come to class was for iclicker.

Easy to understand, goes off on tangents quite a bit. Easy to forget everything you learned. Works through almost every problem he shows, sometimes while you are supposed to answer it with the clicker
He seems like a smart guy but he doesn't know how to teach. I come to class just to get credit for attendance but I do other work in class and read class notes from other teachers online later.
Great Prof! Easy to listen to, and informative
Great teacher but you must read the text book.  If you listen he teaches everything you will see on the test.  Classes are huge so sit in the front if you can't stay awake.  Funny stories
He will teach you what you need to know, but it's up to you to understand it.  Do the homework to reinforce and reteach concepts to yourself.

Overall decent professor.  Though it was sometimes easy to zone out during his lectures, he nonetheless kept it light-hearted and often cracked some jokes (some less funny than others).  If you listened to his lectures and did all the work, you got the A like I did.  Nice guy outside of class too; he is the professor that colleges need more of.

He seems to be a nice person to get along with, and in the beginning the class seemed interesting, but he just cannot possibly figure out how to keep everybody's attention, and the Lab TAs are forced to pick up the slack. Everybody in the back half of the lecture hall completely zones out.  Keep an ear out for his tangents -- they're pretty funny.
He is very unclear and not much can be taken out of lecture, no matter how much you pay attention.  He is too brilliant a man to be teaching such an elementary course.
No Comments
i honestly don't pay attention to him

Dr. Korenowski may seem a little disorganized at first, but if you concentrate hard on what he says, he will teach you everything very well. Tests are only hard if you do not do the homework. If you have trouble with online homework, he will spend as much time as it takes to help you. Approach this guy when you need help: he is kind and easy going.
Very unclear teacher! Doesn't stay on topic, wastes lecture time then gives tests with material we haven't seen.
The class has a lot of work, but it is fair and gives you an Indication of what it will be like in RPI
good teacher, maybe not the best but didn't do a bad job, if you take notes and pay attention you'll do well
Final questions are taken directly from previous tests, and most multiple choice questions on tests are taken from clicker questions, so start memorizing. A breeze compared to Gillies.
clear and helpful on an individual basis but goes quickly through difficult material in class. clicker questions rule all, learn those and youll pass.

He isn't that bad as long as you pay attention.  His tests are difficult, but study clicker questions and you'll be fine.  Trust me you may hate him at first, then Gillies takes over and you miss him.
At first I did not like this professor... that was until Gillies took over, then I missed him! Not too bad at teaching and his tests were reasonable. He really wanted students to do well.

I hated him, until we switched professors and i realized id taken him forgranted.... he is a pretty good lecturer, even though chem 1300-1100 sucks.... his tests are pretty fair, MEMORIZE THE CLICKER QUESTIONS!!!! easy points!
I found him to be really clear.  His lectures are well laid out, so that he goes in a logical order.
Makes time available to help out students
THIS CLASS SUCKS THA BIG ONE!

Talks way too fast, and doesn't explain equations to understand them. Always late for class and never explained a test that 1/2 of the entire class failed - and the average was a 58%. Overall, a horribe teacher, but since he's the only one, theres nothing to do!
He's very hard to follow and wastes a lot of time during classes
The exams are difficult, but the lectures are animated and amusing.

Said I couldn't do logarithms in front of the whole class.  Not me specifically, but after we submitted an answer with our faulty RF transmitters, we heard that "59 people in class had better learn how to do logs."  Heck, I can calculate logs of NEGATIVE numbers!  (They're complex.) Questions we answer in class are often quite ambiguous.

This class is really easy.  It's basically a review of high school chemistry.  Korenowski's lectures are pretty straight forward, and he talks alot about the online quizzing thing, so that takes up a lot of time.
I didn't have a good chem background so I found this class tough.  He has good intentions but his exams are brutal.  The final was easy though, so I managed a B.
Useless teacher. Class is easy so its not a big deal. Online assignments are junk. Back tests are all that are needed.

Awful lecturer, very disorganized.  He would confuse himself when explaining anything; he was often late or he wasted lecture time talking about his kids or PRS receivers. His exams contained lots of errors, his grading on partial credit was draconian, and he generally sucks.  SUCKS.
Lectures were informative and enjoyable.  Knew his stuff and even blew stuff up in front of everybody once in a while.  I especially enjoyed his anti-DeBeers rants midway through the semester.
He spent fifteen minutes of lecture talking about random nonsense, and the rest of lecture was not clear at all.
No Comments

He's a great guy and all, and he's funny, and he obviously knows his stuff... but his way of getting it across is a little muddier than it has to be. I learned more in chem principles by just having a friend reteach it to me. As for the class, it's not hard as long as you put a TINY bit of effort in

Easy class IF you study.  An 85 is the lowest A.  Very easy to get that if you put your mind to it.  As for Korenowski, very helpful whenever I needed it.  Overall a great guy.  Good sense of humor too!

Class was hard and unclear. Simple material presented in such an unclear fashion that it was awful. Too much material for too little time. Good guy though, just totally slaughtered every kid with the test material and awful grades at the end of the year.
he sucks

Very nice guy but moves through material extremely fast and assumes that students know much more than they do.  If you didn't take AP Chem 3 times in high school you could be screwed.  Tests range from managable to impossible without warning.  Only savior is final.
No Comments

For those of you below who are taking the time to write a review, maybe you should be using that time wisely and studying for whatever is to come. The material is not that difficult, though there is a lot, so take off the diapers and go study, just have to review the material and pound it in.

Indeed this class has alot of material, but Dr. K. is the man. He is trying his hardest to teach and that's what counts. He did not create the course so he should not be blamed for all the hard work. Overall, he is a clear lecturer and great man!

I hate him.  Way too fast.  Too much information.  Tests are impossible.  My test average is 42% after getting A's in high school.  Do the lab reports and homework (if you can figure it out) and you should still be able to pass.  I hope I can.

Nice guy with some good humor, but teaching is too fast and over my head, even though I had High School Chem Honors. Too big of a curriculum with tests being pretty difficult to most. Many of the kids were lost, even though some kids did really well. Very high and low grades on tests.
This guy is way too fast! The Course is too advanced to be called a intro course.  Very tuff if your highschool chem class was as bad as mine.The guy thinks the student know as much as him.
sux balls, horrible teacher. cracks horrible jokes
Too much info for an inroductory chem course, and it seems like he thinks that everyone in the class already has a Ph.D. in chem
Great person knows his stuff BUT goes way too quick and needs to elaborate. It feels that he thinks everyone already knows what hes talking about.
After a year I still want to go into his office and break things.  Worst professor EVER.
ALOT OF MATERIAL ON EXAMS! Great person. The curriculum should be shortened...too much info...not his fault. He teaches well. Go to his office hours and you will do fine!

This class covers way too much info. for an intro. chem. class for people who are not chem. majors. Be careful on exams.  The first one is cake, but don't get comfortable. The second exam will kill you.  READ THE BOOK.  He doesn't necessarily teach everything on the exam to both sections.

Chem mat I is not a hard course at all because it's mostly chemistry from high school plus some new stuff from chemistry AP. Prof Korenowski is a great lecturer, much better than other chem mat I professor. And the exams and fianl are not hard at all.
I'd rather read the book than go to lecture.
Easiest class I've ever taken.  Even though their is alot of material covered in every exam, they were all doable and straightforward.  Easy A.
Difficult course... far too much information for an introductory chem class for mostly non-chem majors. However, he is a decent guy who teaches the material pretty well. Very available and fair.
HORRIBLE, thats all I have to say
I had him for Chem mat 1 and thought he was very good. Better than the other Chem mat 1 lecturer.
Loser! Worst Teacher Ever.
Boring, inane, and totally unhelpful. Had him for chem Mat 1. He would bring his kids to class, not know what he was teaching about, and not care about the students. Worse chem class I've ever had.
Very, very hard course.  Way too much material for one semester.  Good teacher though.
Excellent lecturer.  Very approachable after class, always open to questions.  He cares about his students and enjoys teaching.
He's very nice and makes lectures interesting but his tests can be exceptionally cruel and unusual. For such a difficult course, he does a great job.
Too many anecdotes and info he mixes up and then doesn't bother to clarify. I can forgive lecture mistakes as long as u make sure the class knows what the real info is but this is a weakness of his.
No Comments
good professor, but the course was retardedb
Very good Lecturer.  Concise Clear
No Comments
definitely the better chem mat I lecturer, very approachable
Great lecture, clear instructions, and grading criteria. Happy to take this course!
Benj is great and wants you to succeed. I've made a great connection with him as my professor. He is kind with criticism and recognizes your strengths quickly and will encourage you.

The class mostly consists of critiques on both projects and "Formal Focuses" where you read a chapter of the textbook and take + edit a photo based on the concepts of that chapter. If you participate in the critiques and can explain why you made design decisions, you will likely get a good grade. He is not a very harsh grader on projects.

Benj is an amazing professor who cares about all of his students equally. He always tries his best to make the class entertaining and engaging, making learning art for a stem-centric institution insightful and eye-opening. His grading policy is extremely fair and he is the most understanding professor at RPI. Benj is the GOAT.

He is such an easy professor. He doesn't give  multiple choice tests, but they are straightforward. He is an awesome lecturer and will tell you the most important stuff to know. Labs are easy. All you have to do is go to lab to get an A in it.

Best Biology Professor at HVCC! He is very helpful, his lectures are very clear. Conducts very helpful exam reviews prior to all exams. I wish the guy were teaching General Bio II instead of the tenured folks at HVCC who could care less if you pass or fail. I think they enjoy watching students fail and charging them for a re-take!!!
I have him for Biology at Hudson Valley Community College and he's a really great teacher.

Really humorous and charming professor. Very smart too on top of that! His Ethics in Bio class was so engaging that I actually looked forward to attend it. Never wanted to miss a single class. Does have a lot of presentations though.  Never presented so much in once class before.
He cares about teaching; very clear & well-prepared.  Nice guy.
Fundies with Kang was super approachable. Lectures can be a drag but helpful, occasionally very funny. Make a really great crib sheet and you'll be okay.

Kang for Fundies is chill. Some say his accent is bad but it's not really. Wouldn't take again cause lectures can get kinda boring but hw is chill. Be prepared cause Fundies picks up a lot at the end.

This was kind of a double whammy. MAU is a difficult class, and Prof. Kang isn't the best at communicating the material. His lecturing style was somewhat monotone, and I found myself struggling to pay attention. Class attendance went from 35 to 12 students by the end of the semester. I'd say: take the class with a different professor if you can.
N/AAAAAAAAA
I took Seminar class with her. She's definitely caring and motivational but more of a guidance rather than actually teaching. She is accessible outside of class and is willing to help at any time.
She does not teach. Occasionally will waste class time to ramble. Needs to retire asap
not recommend

Cultural Anthropology was such an interesting class! I learned so much, and thoroughly enjoyed the content, as well as Prof Gordon's passion and humor. Definitely be prepared for the (only 2) pop quizzes based on key words from the readings. The tests were fair, and the group project was an interesting experience. Overall, I learned a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Doc Film is a fun class and a good choice if you need a HASS elective! There are three 5-6 papers, which are easy to write if you stay on top of the readings. Send her a draft before the deadline or go to her office hours so you can get some feedback before you turn in the final draft, she's very accessible. Go to class- the documentaries are great
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Language and Culture had a ton of super interesting material if you have any remote interest in sociology. She knows a lot about what she's teaching and brings in plenty of personal research. Class is easy to get an A if you're willing to write 3 papers, do 3-4 small presentations, and show up to class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Documentary Film itself was an enjoyable class. 3 essays with an optional 4th. Go to her for help on the essays and see what she's looking for. A well-written essay won't get a good grade unless it incorporates everything, and disagreeing with the text is not good.
Really boring class, not helpful at all.  class dropped immediately. Religion in Media

Not a bad professor, but writing the essays for Documentary Film is very laborious. Must include many sources and quotations from the assigned texts, or else even very good papers won't be graded well.
Really friendly, informative and makes the class interesting. Would recommend!
Great teacher. Fun and lively. You can tell she loves her work. So much fun to be away, keeps things interesting.

One of the best profs at RPI. Dr. Gold is very real in terms of her worldview, and understands students have lives. Class is relatively easy as long as you attend a bulk of the lectures and study a few hours for the exams (online). I finished all the homeworks online in the first month of classes which made everything so light for the rest of sem.

Professor Gold is a great professor and you can tell she cares if her students learn. The class itself isn't very difficult but make sure to study for the final as I found it to be significantly harder than the quizzes.

Prof Gold has a lot of knowledge in the subject and likes to provide stories as example. She is really nice. Classes are an hour long. There are weekly quizzes, midterm, short paper which is easy, and a final. Before the midterm and final, Prof Gold goes over the study guide item by item in class.

Her class is quite interesting, though easy. There were only two tests, the midterm and then the final and the final thankfully is not cumulative. There is one paper in her class, only about one page long, and weekly quizzes with the lowest scoring one being dropped. Professor Gold is pretty funny during lectures too and she is super nice.

Super easy professor.  Lectures never last more than an hour.  LMS quizzes every week but all the answers can be found online.  Definitely has an interesting personality but is really likeable.  Gives out a midterm topics sheet which is all you need to study.

Prof. Gowdy is someones who actually knows things beyond the boring standard textbook stuff. His projects are amazing and often real applications compared to most other professors, who research theoretical stuff from the last century. His smaller classes are the best if you like to discuss and learn about current issues.
Takes the interesting bits and makes them boring. Makes the boring bits tortuous. Doesn't seem to want to be in class himself.....
His voice trails off during lectures, making the ends of his thoughts difficult to understand.  Otherwise, is an easy professor since the exam questions are given out ahead of time.
Excellent professor.  A little difficult to understand sometimes, but he tries to keep your interest.  This was the only class I actually looked forward to going to, and it was mostly because of him.
Hes Way easy! Does nothing but lecture off of power point during class, gives you the test questions before the exam and rarely gives homework.... easiest class I have taken so far... have fun!
Lectures are useless in studying for tests, but it doesn't matter because he gives you the test questions ahead of time.
easiest class at rpi...no hw, gives questions and answers to mult. choice questions before tests.  let us out after an hour in every class when we should have had 2.
Gives you all the questions and answers to the test beforehand.  He does mumble a lot however, but I still love the man.
he's pretty kewl. kinda freaky too. do the work and get an easy A. Thas all dat matters!
Pretty leniant for Humanities courses. Good teaching style, but antagonistic with students who disagree and don't support their arguments.

"Casey" is very helpful when a need arises, and has quickly provided our team with needed materials. However, he will also be very quick to point out your every misstep, which can make him feel more like a critic than an educator.

Casey was extremely helpful as an advisor to my capstone team.  He is very knowledgeable in several technical areas and can be a great resource if you need to hammer out the details of a design or procedure.

Goes on tangents, rarely knows what he's talking about and absurdly harsh grading. Semantics can be grounds for huge deductions, if by some miracle you get him to help you, he'll make you start again from scratch; he'll accuse you of 'not following the design process' if you don't follow his insane instructions to the word.

Took forever to return things, didn't follow rubric on LMS for grading them and did not explain grading criteria/rationale. Hard to get a hold of, and not helpful even if you do-he'll basically make you rewrite/redesign your memo/project to his own standards; narrow-minded & very preferential towards students who come in sharing his worldview.

I do not agree with the previous rating. let me separate truth and fiction here:  He does not return things in time- yes, does not explain clearly what he wants- yes, but he is willing to go above and beyond to help you.  Really harsh grader because you dont know what he wants.... all you have to do is ask.

A grad student with no business teaching. Rambled endlessly & answered questions with useless tangents, so we never got in-class work done on time. He didn't tell us when class got moved to another room, gave us little to no guidance on writing the mini-project reports and never held office hours. Picked on the gay student in our class.

Casey was our group's project engineer for our senior Capstone project. Talk about the hardest person to work under. He is a great guy - when he is not there (which happens to be 99% of the time). Don't bother emailing him because he won't respond. Don't bother asking him questions either, because he'll turn it into a yelling match. Worst guy ever.

Made IED HELL when i took it. mini project reports were returned AFTER the first draft of the final paper was due. He failed to mention what he wanted in the papers and graded harshly for not meeting the unknown reqs. what could have been a great class became a nightmare.

He was my Project Engineer for Senior Design Capstone.  Unfortunately, Professor Steiner selects him to be in charge of our group, so I can't suggest you select him. Casey supports his teams the best, by being very devoted to our success, and definitely kept us in line with our decisions. You may be able to choose him as an IED professor.
She is a very nice person but her grading can be hard to understand sometimes because she always seems to change the scales for everything. I liked her class Writing for classroom and career though.

Professor Gordon is a really nice person and genuinely cares about her students. Creative fiction writing was a fun class, positively impacted my writing style, and was a really nice, low-stress break from all of my engineering classes.

You should only take Creative Fiction Writing if you have a strong interest in writing fiction. That said, it was an awesome class. You spend much of each class period writing, and there's only an hour or so of homework per week. Basically, if you put in the work, you will get a good grade, and the class is very low stress.

Funny guy, but talks more about his own life than what we need to learn. Easy to cheat on exams but homework is a different story as they're graded harshly. He doesn't really explain how he does the math portions but expects you to catch on right away. I'm not great at econ so I found myself always confused and overwhelmed.
Easy A+ If you cheat on the test so easy anyone can do it its online and just look up answer

The man.  Great presenter, but make sure you know how to do his math portion for the exam! Excellent at keeping your attention, recommend if you like a personable person who is down to earth and interesting, and teaches you as well!
Awesome guy. Knows his stuff and presents it well while keeping you entertained with hysterical stories. He's like a frat guy trapped as a professor.

Greg is one of the most down to earth, knowledgeable Economics professors I have ever had at RPI. He keeps Managerial Econ interesting by relating some of his crazy life experiences with economic topics developed in class. Yes, there are a few class days devoted to the math behind Cobb-douglass equations, but it is well worth it in the long run :D
A little vague but the class was kept interesting. Does some interesting things to keep you entertained. Would recommend.
Roger is a real nice guy but I didn't get a whole lot of out of this class. May be the easiest college course I have ever taken
I like Roger

Roger is the kind of professor who really cares about the well-being and progress of his students.  While his assignments, even in the HCI capstone, were pretty straightforward, the course was a decent amount of work and well organized.  Talk with him outside of class and he'll become a good friend and mentor.
Awesome dude.  very easy no matter what class you take with him.
Great professor. Very laid back will allow excuses not to have class. Not heavy work intensive, just keep up with work and you'll get a good grade. Try to get him as a professor.
Take whatever you can with him. Most laidback professor, comes up with excuses to not have class (its too hot, the hockey team won, etc.) Do the 5 projects (that aren't difficult) and the A is yours.
good sense of humor, very easy on grading. do the assignments and u'll be more than fine
very easy grader... cool/fun teacher.. understands students
His lectures bored me to death, but he allowed AIM in class so it wasnt so bad. You didnt need to pay attention to do well, just keep up with the assignments.

I had Grice for Writing to the WWW, but I knew who he was before I took the course.  He's a great guy with good sense of humor.  His classes are always fun and that makes them a lot easier.  Great professor and an asset to the school.

Great teacher.  Funny, energetic, creative and a good teacher.  He may be easier than some teachers, but who cares?  As long as you learn the material, you're getting what you paid for.  And with this guy, you have fun in the process.
Very Approachable outside of class, made a subject I thought was dull very interesting and fun
No Comments
Its a grice class

This is a good interductory class into the area of Human Computer Interaction.  The teachers is also very easy.  I recieve a 100% in the class.  The only problem with the class is that is has a lot of animations that do not stream well over the Internet to the distance students.
Roger is the best professor ever.  Bring him a Diet Pepsi and win an A.
Roger is as easy as he is friendly.  He is a great guy, and although his classes are not the most extensive at RPI, you do learn something.
Roger is the best professor at this school by far.  He also loves hockey and coming up to his fraternity house to hang out afterwards.
ROGER is the man!
This professor is one of the elite at RPI.  Other professors should be honored to hold his coffee cup (just to sip from it once)!    ROGER IS THE BEST!!!!!!

roger's class is certainly easy; almost impossible _not_ to get an A.  however, the material he presents is not exceptional if you're truly interested in human-computer interaction.  that you're supposed to read norman's 'design of everyday things' is it.
a distance class that you could 'attend' anywhere I went to as many of Roger's Lectures as I could.
Simply the best professor at the school hands down.  Not only helped me in school, but helped me get the job I have today.
One of the few classes I would always look forward to - always made it interesting
I played volleyball for an A.  Doesn't get much easier than that.
I enjoyed his class. I dunno. It was fun & easy.
Best HCI Professor. Ever!
Very relaxed classroom atmosphere, flexible teacher,
funny guy, laid back, cool class

His lectures often have minor mistakes, so they might be difficult to follow for some. He also assigns unfathomable amounts of homework worth 30% of the grade. However, the two exams are somewhat easy and very straightforward. This semester, 35% was a passing grade and 83% was an A, so don't crash out if you're not doing perfect.
The class was easy. I stopped attending after the third lecture. Gregor makes the class basically a joke because of the leniency on exams. I have no passion for this degree…..
Just very easy test, good for your GPA. His exam total is 60 and with 10 extra points! If you just spend some time before his exam, you should never worry about your grade on that.
The TA Francis carries the entire course, as the teacher isn't really good at his job...
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's so, SO funny. But, his lectures are slow + in the end half of the course the logic is hard to follow re formula derivations. Weekly recitation quizzes clarify concepts as TAs review problems before quizzes. Exams are plug-and-chug, similar to quizzes. You're allowed a crib sheet, and e/ exam offers ~16% EC that can boost other exam grades.

The professor isn't the best lecturer and his handwriting is a spectacle. However, the homework in the class is very nice, and as long as you do proficiently on the test and quizzes, you can obtain a reasonably good grade.
Kovacic if you're reading this, why tf do you use "n" as a variable in your classes? The way you write it, it could be mistaken for an r, u, a, h, v, or m. Why. Why

He may not be a great lecturer but his personality is great. And tests are 70% of your final grade but you are allowed a crib sheet and he offers  bonus question so you can earn 10 extra points on an exam out of 50. Content is difficult but not unbearable so just study and go to office hours if needed as he is helpful (just tell him you are coming)
The lectures are confusing and hard to digest. The notes are illegible, and there aren't really any office hours. The TAs are helpful and honestly the only reason I passed this class.
If you want get a high GPA. No! NO! NO!
Lots of extra credit and a big curve.

Good and nice professor. 
He offers a lot of extra credits and useful office hours. 
Also, with a nice curve on the final grade.
Good professor. Lots of extra credit. Gig curve.

Very nice and hilarious person to talk to.
However, his notes are terrible and not legible at all. Homework is notoriously difficult, especially for the extra credits.
Tests are fine, actually, very easy compared to hw.

His notes are awful and nothing can be learned from them as they are so disorganized. Often on example questions he skips steps making it impossible to understand his process. He often bashes the textbook he assigned for the class for being awful, which it is, and not much can be learned from the textbook.

Prof. Kovacic is a really nice and funny person. Unfortunately, this did not come through with his lectures, which were not engaging. This class can be very difficult if you are not comfortable with Calculus. Some of his tests are very tough. To keep up, do all optional HW assignments and seek out help when you need it. It also helps to read ahead
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He's a real sweetheart who genuinely cares about students. His lectures are easy to follow and he lays out how quizzes and tests will go.
