After they grade they give you the rubric so you can challenge and potentially get points back. The quizzes are easy and the tests are either easy or impossible. (look out for test 2) (hw not checked/required)

Linear algebra this summer was great. Professor provides clean, parseable lecture notes, and the lectures are good. Doesn't reign in harshly grading TAs, however, so be very meticulous in your assignments to make sure they see everything they could possibly be looking for.
Those were the hardest homeworks I have ever done but the curve is very generous.
No exams. Homeworks are insanely hard. Gives good lectures, though. Make sure you buy the book by Sanchez, it actually helps a lot; start the homeworks early!!!
He's a little hard to understand but its manageable if you pay attention. Tests are nothing like the homeworks and the homeworks are quite difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Dr Kovacic gives a lot of homework which is really hard, plus the lecture notes only help sometimes. Beware you have to mainly do a lot of work on your own. On the first test he gave in our class a lot of our class failed so be careful.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: The homework is hard. The class is daunting, five people walked out on the first day. But it's incredibly worth it. I came out understanding calculus better than ever before, and for the first time in my life, I actually UNDERSTAND the fundamental theorem of calculus. This class was amazing.
This guy is a straight up G! Hes absolutely hilarious, though his lectures were a little hard to understand through his thick accent.

Easiest class I took my first semester here. I stopped attending lectures after the first week, and skipped a few recitation session. Instead,I watched khan Academy and PatrickJMT and went over the class notes online days before the test. Only had to take two test all semester. (Quiz average can be used as the 3rd test grade) Easy A!

He writes down the lecture notes on a digital format and posts them online. These are a good reference for the homework. The learning process is done while doing the homework as there is not much learning from lecture. Easy exams, no final, and he's very approachable for questions. The homework works you a lot, but you will learn. Overall, good.
Homework is extremely hard for students. And do not expect his class note to be helpful while doing homework.

Very friendly and funny. His general gaiety is almost infectious. Great professor for math majors or anyone interested in seriously pursuing mathematics; has a lot of advice about the culture of academia. His Analysis homework is astoundingly difficult and time-consuming, but it pays great dividends for your understanding. Tests are almost trivial.

Gregor Kovacic is a pretty good professor. He presents the material well and assigns homework problem that are very similar to test questions. His tests can be a little hard since he has a hard time understanding what students find difficult. Still, not a bad experience.
This guy is the man. Multiple choice tests, no homework, no textbook. He even co-authored a paper on the practical challenges of creating an invisibility cloak.

Don't expect great instruction, and you'll need to get several of the textbooks listed on his webpage to refer to (he uses material from many sources).  The homework is a challenge, and is where the learning happens, just don't expect it to be graded, make and keep a copy to compare with posted solutions.
Lectures are horrible and boring, his English is terrible, and his notes are illegible and don't really explain a single thing. I also had an awful TA which didn't help.
Kovacic works you hard, but it ppays off in the end. He is also a funny guy.

Very intelligent professor. Knows his stuff. Has trouble explaining exactly what he means, but extremely knowledgeable. Rarely makes mistakes on the board, and can answer difficult questions immediately. The homework load is a lot, but not impossible. Over all good teacher.
my favorite professor, homeworks are longer but are deeper than plugging numbers into formulas

Kind of hard to explain this man.  He's a really good guy, and he teaches the material and tests on the material as difficult as anyone I've heard of, but class averages are generally low.  He has huge curves at the end though, so you'll probably get the grade you want even if you are expecting the worst.
No Comments
Really easy grader, tons of extra credit on tests, good TAs, take it with him!

Interesting person.  Hard to understand sometimes.  Doesn't care if you attend lecture and his notes are on line anyway.  At the end of the couse there was a 5 point curve so getting a good grade shouldn't be much of a problem.  Knows his stuff but has trouble explaining it.
Nice guy. Lectures are fairly unorganized and often contain mistakes. Suggested homework is nicely organized.
Very unorganized lectures, and not very clear as to what needed to be known. my TA was terrible too
Tends to push so hard in the beginning that students start the semester behind and can't catch up.  Intro to integration is really advanced integration techniques.
"Say you walk into a room and you find a corpse..." Great professor, funny and taught the material well.
Best teacher ever.  He reminds me forcefully of Goldmember.  His laugh is infectious and he loves gold.
Even though there is an accent you get used to it. Very good class,some lectures painful at times. Great TA's.
Really nice guy, knows his stuff.  Always willing to make sure you understand a concept if you ask him.  Excellent boardwork.  Makes the classroom atmosphere friendly, if a little corny.
No Comments
I'm repeating diffeq, it's 10x easier with Kovacic than it could've been
Differential Equations. Difficult subject, but he made it a bit clearer. Has a thick accent. Is often giddy, which can be contagious. Laughs at self frequently.
not so easy, but not utterly impossible
Very thick accent, not available.  No req-ed final tho.
While the class is hard, and a lot of work is given out, it is very rewarding.
This guy is a baller. He helps out noob freshmen such as me and is very approachable. I breezed thru this class like a boss
You won't find a better professor than Greg Hughes in your time at RPI.
Awesome Professor. Crystal clear concepts.
awesome & interesting

Professor Hughes is both an awesome professor and a person.  A very fun guy to hang out for a few minutes and chat once in a while.  He offers tons of real world experience from his years at major companies and knows many people working at other companies.  Sometimes frustrating course work but overall challenging and definitely a worthwhile course
No Comments
IT Capstone.  The class is a good culmination to the IT major, but there is too much emphasis on weekly case studies. There is freedom to go after any project you want, but beware of the final paper!
Fantastic! The best professor ive ever had! Simple amazing!
Professor keeps classes extremely interesting. This was my favorite class at RPI so far.

it's refreshing to take class from someone different than other profs here. grandeau is no scholar. he's a professional who teaches on the side. that's why the intellectual content is simple. a break from th demanding classes taught by profs

Still recovering...  I learned a lot about contracts which I now think about all the time.  I think that is a good thing.  I suggest recording every class and bring a pocket constitution to class, he will appreciate that. I liked going to class everyday.  Don't worry about the points thing, just earn as much as you can whenever possible.
This class was always interesting and for the people who said he doesn't teach anything, they obviously just did not understand the concepts; I learned a ton.
He is a very interest guy. Show up all the time and be careful with the game he plays and you'll be good.

Whoever says Grandeau teaches nothing in this class is clearly too big of a moron to understand the whole underlying lessons to what may seem like idiotic babble. This class really gets you into the mindset that you need to learn the principles and Grandeau makes it engaging. This is a great class and a lot of fun. I would definitely reccomend it.
Hated this class..he doles out points randomly. I couldn't pay attention ever in this class. Your grade fluctuates a lot..you are never sure if you have an A or not.

One of the worst professors at RPI.  He is not qualified to teach, and RPI decided to have him back since the tenured professor for the course retired.  He uses no textbook and there is no homework.  You are graded on the little quizzes and tests he has as well as the random points he gives out.  If you are not on a team he likes you will not get a
A BLAST. I loved every second of his class.

This guy is a freackin character.  We dont use any textbooks.  He makes up crazy stories and has the class determine whether someone can get sued, or whether its illegal, etc....Grading:  If you are within 50 % of the highest point total you get a B, 80 % of the highest point total you get an A.  He didnt follow this and gave half the class A's
Funny as heck... great class... learn a lot and didn't mind getting up at 7:00 to go to his class

Good professor (and a very sweet person) though a little tough to understand with the accent sometimes. Labs are not too lengthy, and exams are very similar to homework, use your reference sheet wisely and you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Despite what the rating says, Professor Wang is an energetic and kind lecturer despite the minor accent. From taking this last fall, it was very chill: just show up for labs (they are easy) and do homework. Tests are challenging, but she gives a class for review and almost always the back exams have similar types of questions. Lecture slides help!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Wang is a very good professor. She is very energetic in lecture, frequently demoing little experiments for the class. Her voice can quiet, especially as she wears a mask, but she is still understandable. **You DEFINITELY need to attend class tho. In-class activities are a LARGE amount of your grade.** Tests aren't too bad; do back exams.

I had Dr. Wang for Physics 1 this semester, and she was very kind to me! She was hard to understand in lectures due to her accent, but she seemed to care about students with the way she explained concepts and reminded us to understand the material. I have problems with the way RPI teaches physics, but her office hours were helpful when I went.

While hard to understand in lecture, Professor Wang is very good at giving 1 on 1 help.  If you're not someone who pays attention in lectures (you can just read notes and/or read the textbook, but still go to lecture for activities), she's not too bad.
lectures are hard to follow and doesn't always answer student's questions very clearly. she will make you work for a good grade.
Doesnt explain things well during lecture but when you ask for help explains things really well and drops lowest test score
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Wang is very friendly and knowledgeable in the subject. She will help and almost baby you until the answer is found. Lecture slides are clearly laid out with a recap of important formulas at the end. She does not create the tests but a formula sheet is allowed. There is a significant HW but it boosts the grade. Once past her accent, EZ dub.

difficult to understand through think accent over Webex and bad speakers because our class was split into two rooms because of covid restrictions (fall 2021) so she teaches from one room one day and Webex meets with the other and vis versa depending on the day. She is a somewhat decent professor though actually at least tries to help if you need it
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: Very poor lecturer in my opinion, paired with her  accent makes the class very challenging. A lot of homework in this class, two mastering physics per week and two written problems. She is very intelligent, but not good at teaching. Avoid if possible.

There's a lab twice a week and they're always graded very easily. The average lab grade in the class is a 94. Homework is usually 2-3 hours per week and is only sometimes difficult. The tests are appropriately tough, although it's worth noting that Wang does not create the tests. Wang is hard to understand, but not too terrible.

I was more confused after lectures then I was after reading the book.  She had more powerpoint slides than there were pages in the book and would jump back an forth between them a hundred at a time.  This unorganized style mixed with the lights being off often put half the class literally to sleep.

Wow.  Really nice in a grandmotherly sort of way, but very hard to understand (accent & poor wording on tests).  I dropped her class just because it was so rediculous what she wanted us to memorize.  She had in-class quizzes to make sure people came to class, but they were difficult to understand.  She had 100's of pages of notes!
Loved her accent!

Very knowledgeable and helpful.  She has a strong accent, but she manages to convey the fundamental ideas better than most native English speaker professors.  Her tests are very fair and to the point.  She is interested in teaching and having the students learn and she strives to achieve that goal.

Most ridiculous class taken at RPI. Class is useless except for the Worksheets/Quizzes she hands out (Answers for which can be copied exactly from the book). Book is almost as confusing as her unintelligible accent. Reads directly off PP slides. Aviod Wang; even if it means waiting another semester.

Hard to understand, uses terrible analogies. Ex:When talking about energy bands, she asked if anyone in the class was in a rock band.  She then commented on the difference between rock and energy bands.  Tests are impossible, HW takes a while.  There's a reason she only teaches every few years...

Made QPhys way harder than it should have been. Classes consist of powerpoint slides of equations with little explanation. Thick accent. Impossible tests. Tends to create extended metaphors of grandchildren to explain wave equations instead of math.  Very willing to help, but not actually helpful.
Very caring professor. Genuinely wants you to succeed. Makes the content easy to swallow and easily understandable. 10/10 no notes; would take very class with him if I could.

Professor Hasan is honestly great. He is very knowledgeable about accounting and gives lots of examples in class. The class is fairly straightforward, and as long as you show up and participate, you'll do well. He's also available after class to help with any homework, and he is free during office hours if you need extra help.

Professor Hasan is a little disorganized, but overall a good professor. He is very knowledgeable about accounting and wants students to succeed. He provides the resources to make this happen. Sometimes lectures can move slowly, and he will backtrack on himself, but if you show up to class and pay attention it's nearly impossible to fail.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: His lectures are not very helpful in learning the material for the second half of the course. The homework's do not align with the course material. You have to do the hws and activities to get an A. The tests are easy if you do the provided back exams. Overall if you do the classwork, it is very possible to get an A

The lectures were math-heavy. If you're good with calculus, you'll have no issues, although the thermodynamics section felt rushed. Attendance is mandatory for both lectures and labs. There are two in-person exams with questions similar to previous years, and one take-home online final. It's an easy A if you attend lectures and practice past exams.

Homeworks often don't align well with lecture material, need to attend class to get lecture activities, the back exams he provides are basically the exam with different numbers, you get a front/back crib sheet for exams too.

Overall there is way too much emphasis on the math portion of the course and not enough on the actual intuition behind the concepts. The first half of the course if manageable if you've done Physics I in high school, however the second half is a train wreck, doing thermodynamics in 3 days and rushing through all of it. Korniss is a nice guy though

Had him for classical dynamics. Have to go to class to get activity worksheets which are due 2x/week. Nice TAs and mentors. If you do all HW and labs perfectly, you roughly need an average minimum of an 80 on very exam. +10 point extra credit on exams. Lectures are just doing multi.. I don't know multi. Have an A so far but subject to change.

His lectures are literally just calculus. No concept.

If you are able to grasp material by merely looking at an equation: your solid.
If not: have fun buddy, I know I sure didn't!

And some real talk: All he does in lecture is go through each step of the math as though it's not sitting there in front of you. Not helpful.

He is very nice though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Korniss is the most caring and understanding professor I've ever had and it's nearly impossible to fail his class. There's a lot of multivar/diffeq, but he explains its connection to the formulas very clearly and conscisely. He even went out of his way to make the material extra accessible when I was out sick. Cannot recommend him enough!

Normal Physics 1 looks like middle-school content to me. His Honors Physics 1 was a complete nightmare. He taught so many concepts, such as general relativity and thermodyn. What made things really hard was the level of Mathematics involved. Diffeq and Multivar were used heavily in his lecture notes. Anyway, generous grader. Exams weren't hard.

Lectures can be very dense(lots of calculus), tbh I don't understand why calc-1 is a co-requisite, partial derivatives and line integrals are used often, students must be able to understand calc-3 if they haven't studied it yet. Far more in depth than a standard AP class, definitely don't skip as a physics major.

Learned everything from the textbook. His lectures were actually useless, but I still had to go because he handed out assignments during the lecture breaks. On the bright side, he is very willing to help.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: This man is a god. Physics major or not, take his intro physics class. Back exams are posted on his website and very much resemble the real thing. There are often a large number of conceptual questions that are directly from the back exams. Study the back exams, and you'll have no trouble in this class. HW is from book, can be downloaded online.

Lectures are upper level math heavy with triple intervals and partial derivatives but you usually won't need to use them on the homework or tests. Tests don't have any surprises, they're very similar to the backtests and the problems gone over in class. Korniss seems to care about his students and can offer a lot of help if you need it.

He throws line integrals and partial derivatives at you in the first month. He is a very personable guy. He is okay with you turning in activities late with a semi-valid excuse. His TAs grade labs and that is toss up whether they are reasonable or not. My friends would make sure every persons labs were close to failing, while mine was okay.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Lectures are very math heavy and he uses Diff EQs and Multi Var so if you haven't taken calc before be warned.

Professor Korniss is a great teacher if you're interested in physics. He doesn't spare you on the mathematical side of it, and therefore when you understand things that he teaches or the problems that he assigns you can feel extremely accomplished. He is caring and willing to help if you ask.
Really nice guy, the class is challenging as are the tests but if you use the notes and the provided back tests it isn't so bad.

Very interesting material, and Korniss covered it very well. Tests are essentially the questions covered in lecture/in-class problems with the occasional problem that is similar to a homework question. Oh and once you get used to him you'll find that he's hilarious.

Lectures almost always consist of long, complex derivations that will make your head explode. Homework is much less challenging than the lectures and the tests are a downright joke. Korniss is a bit quiet but is always willing to help 1-on-1 if you're confused. It's easy to get a good grade but the material itself is very deep.

The class was ridiculously difficult for absolutely no reason at all. Lecture was useless. Everything I learned was from reading the textbook. Lecture barely matched what the homework did, and the tests railed everyone every single time.

Brilliant man. However, we are young and therefore not so brilliant. Expects a level of intellect that as freshman we haven't obtained yet. Extremely difficult material, combined with accent and speed of speech makes a bad combination. Made me sad =(

Korniss' brain is lightyears ahead of everyone's, but he has the humility to walk you through material you don't understand. Oh, and he's Hungarian, so he has an awesome accent. He probably killed a man once.

The hw was easy, however the tests are pretty difficult so pay attention in class, also he is not super forgiving on tests.  He teaches mostly from the book and is pretty clear.  Lectures were a little dry but that has more to do with the material than the teacher.  Overall he is a nice guy and I would take another course with him.
I'm sorry but he was horrible. I still learned everything I had to learn because I completely relied on the textbook.

? second that he is the man! easy tests, but sometime the homework is challenging. his lecture covers a lot about physics and he showed the process of how physicists derive the formulas brightly. Thought his accent could be a pain and sometime he talks too fast?
Gyorgy is THE MAN! Attend his lectures, you'll fall behind fast if you skip.
cool dude, good teacher
Excellent professor.  Very helpful and approachable inside and outside of class.  The class notes and homework were challenging.  The exams were straight forward and the grading was easy.
Great guy, good teacher.  He practically gave us the answers to the tests the class before, and they were open notes/open book.  He's pretty easy to understand if you get past the accent.
Korniss is smart and thoughtful.  He cares whether you get it.

He would read the notes he handed you. He knows what he is doing, but it is still a rough class that requires a lot of time to understand. His homeworks are hard, but the exams were very reasonable, especially the grading
He is an understading guy, helpful if u ask questions, and keeps stuff brief, very knowledgable, phys I is pretty easy

One of the smartest profs I've had, but hard as nails; doesn't suffer fools gladly. Make sure you have a good overall understanding before you ask him any detail related questions. Expect homeworks to take a very significant amount of time - find/organize a group. Very possible to get an A, but you must put the time in.
difficult class, but he's extremely helpful if you go to him for help. HW is really hard, but exams were very reasonable.
Good teacher, very helpful if you ask questions.  Nice guy.  Lectures are read from powerpoint, but are very short.  I get out early every class.

Tough class, but he can be very helpful. Make sure you take down ALL notes in class, as he'll usually slip in a solution to one of the hw problems. Go to office hours, hw will kill you if you don't keep up. Tests arent too bad, as long is you make it the the class prior (he gives you the answers).

8am in Carnegie with a chalkboard. Does a few very long problems in class. Boring, but more helpful that the book. Very helpful after class. Does "sample" problems in class that are almost exactly what's on the test and lets you use notes/book on test. Good soccer player.
Boring class....equation after equation that took up the entire front wall.  Handwriting a little hard to read, but he reviews for his tests - and usually uses the questions he does in class.
class was at 8am... boring as hell to listen to him lecture.  Very helpful, sends email to students who do badly on the first exam.

each class is basically a lecture for whatever topic is being covered, hw's every week or so, 2 take home exams (should do well if you go to class and look at ppts), 2 short presentations on papers relating to class, one short written report on second paper. not a hard class just have to do the work

Everything will be done in a small group, which is kind of annoying. Otherwise prof is a really nice and understanding guy who does care about his students. Attendance isn't mandatory, two take home exams that are pretty difficult if you don't go to class, but doable if you can teach yourself. One homework a week typically.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I loved going to class, even though it was pretty late at night. sometimes lectures can be hard, but that is true for almost any 3 hour class. HW was easy and relevant. class work was focused. my favorite were the 2 simulations. this class really introduced me to supply chain, which i now love

He has a strong accent and makes odd pauses in the wrong place of a sentence which makes it difficult to pay attention and understand. He has a monotonic voice and it's easy to zone out especially since it's not the most exciting topic. Homework is due on LMS every week, a short 1-2 page term paper with a 5 minute presentation with a group of 4

Fantastic professor, super good at explaining things, sacrifices his time to help students well after class ends. Is not afraid to admit if he doesn't know something, and does his best to figure it out with you. Loves to connect topics with industry work to show that we're learning with purpose. Absolutely recommend Tom for NuMPE.
He is an amazing professor and makes me happy.

I love how energetic he was in lectures! Very helpful and understands the difficulty (and reputation) of this class. Homework can take 12+ hours but he warns you about that. Quizzes are brutal but not unfair or anything. Extremely hard, time consuming class but with a professor this good I still loved it.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The HW in Numpe can get rough but Haley makes what is normally a dreadful class into something managable, dare I say fun? He really is a gem at RPI and I think the first post on this thread from 20 years ago says it all.

Haley is the most caring professor I have ever had. Helped with any question. Every week his office hours would go on for hours longer than their official length so that he could help every students. NumP will kick you, but Haley does an amazing job at explaining the reason of why you need to go through it. If you have to, take it with him.

Haley would explain and break down even the hardest NuMPE problems for his students. It seems like he really does cares about his students and want them to succeed in this class. It isn't an easy nor well structured class but Haley makes it easier by telling his students what to expect for those quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: came to this guy to ask a question and he stayed after class and made me a 4 year plan for engineering. extremely patient, cares about teaching, the goat. take every one of his classes if you can.

I had him for MANE 1961 and he was an amazing professor. If you miss a class its quite hard to fully understand the material since he mostly explains it in class but is the best professor I have ever had so far.
the goat

Haley is truly a gem. As long as he's the professor, I'll take any class with him. Numerical Methods is a TOUGH course but he did well with what he was given. Yes, tests were brutal and HW's were quite deadly BUT Tom was always there for help, just ask! He knows how to explain concepts but be prepared to put in the work and start on HW's early!

Haley is one of those guys who could lecture on paint drying and would still find a way to make it interesting. He admits he is not the best professor, but he really tries his best to make sure people understand. His long-winded nature does tend to confuse some, though. One thing to watch out for: his tests can be BRUTAL. Still a great prof.

Professor Haley really cares about how students do. He will fight to make sure you understand the material, so long as you ask for help. Even in things completely unrelated to class, if you ask for help he goes the extra mile to make sure you do well.

Great class. Can be verbose, but his lectures are informative and entertaining; I learned a lot. Tests were tough but fair, he would post a list of potential questions ~1 week before the exam. Rewards and encourages original and creative solutions to the open-ended homework problems. Very available through email, etc.

He will talk your ear off, but you sit on the edge of your seat drinking in every word. Makes going to class interesting and fun. You can go to him for any question, related or unrelated, and get all the information you need. The best professor I've had in 4 years at RPI.

Dr. Haley isn't a professor, he is a god and the rest of us are lucky to be here with him. Entertaining lectures, fair grading and very clear on expectations-goes out of his way to provide examples of good presentations/tech memos. Cares about students, he personally tutored me in PNR and gave career advice in addition to helping w/IED.

Has a good sense of humor. A self-described "man of 1000 words." Relies heavily on the text-book for homework problems. Expected to read assigned chapters before you come to class. This is important, as a big part of the lecture is straight from the reading. Exams are hard, but if you do all the HW they won't be a problem. Grades more than fairly.

Professor Haley was a great teacher for Thermals and Fluids 1. His real world experience was very helpful when giving examples. He has a good sense of humor. And he is always willing to go above and beyond to help students. His test are kind of tricky, but I think he had a small curve at the end of the class. Most importantly, I learned a lot.

Haley was overqualified to teach IEA (intro to engineering analysis), but that made the class so much more better. He'd tie in material from other courses to show us how practical statics analysis can be. Overall, great guy. He can think in 10 dimensions, but he only requires you to think in 3. that's fair imo.
He is not very organised, but knows most of the material. Will be quite hard to get in touch with. Always wants you to do well and will try to make the class fun

Awesome professor.  Excited to teach the material, and is more than willing to use his own time to help you out.  Sometimes gets off track during lectures, or tries to explain absolutely everything, but great to listen to regardless.  Has plenty of experience in industry to help you make good career choices.  Take whatever class he's teaching!!!!!!
Haley completely rules.  The class is hard, but he makes going to class fun.  Unfortunately the course format is ridiculous but what can you do.
Great professor.  Wish I could have taken more classes with him.
Haley is the man :)

Dr. Hahn is clearly very smart and qualified to teach the class. However, she's very disorganized and chaotic, and often lets her personal issues affect the class. This improved throughout the semester but she lost the attention of most of the class in the beginning- so stick with it! Pay attention in lecture, take good notes, and READ THE TEXTBOOK

She is a much better teacher than she thinks she is. I enjoyed the class and she is clearly knowledgeable about the subject material. Wish she would prepare for lecture a little more, often crosses out her notes and has the class start over. I would take her again and respect her as a teacher very much, although she takes getting used to.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Boring lecturer. Berates students for asking questions. When asked about final grade, was told to calculate it myself. I did and she got mad at me that it was different from the grade she calculated. She didn't understand why the textbook made simplifications. All of her knowledge came from textbook. Very dispassionate about the subject.

Dr. Hahn is a great person but mediocre lecturer. The jokes she told took away from the learning and talked a little too much about her personal life. Tests were not very hard, studied book for most of the information.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Lots of materials were covered. Lots of studying. Lots of work. But in the end, not much  substance was learned.

Dr. Hahn is great. Makes the material really interesting. She does make a lot of dumb jokes but they're kind of funny. Grading is hard but fair so you have to study pretty hard for the tests. Going to class is not only part of your grade but pretty much the only way to pass as the book doesn't match the class very well. So make sure to take notes.
Dr hahn is brilliant. Shes also the sweetest prof i've ever had. Would take the class again if I could. Interesting material but you've got to study pretty hard for the exams.
She's a good teacher, but has very low confidence.  She tries to make up for this by making stupid jokes and putting herself down.  Overall better than Gilbert for materials though.
The worst professor

Not sure why this guys rating's so low, I really liked him. He doesn't take his class too seriously and leaves a lot of room for interesting discussion. He doesn't get offended if you disagree with him. I NEVER go to class, and I ended up going to this one. Very little work, and the grading is forgiving. One of the better classes I've taken overall
One easy Assignment for the whole semester, but the tests are harder than expected
Really easy to get an A in the class, can re-do assignments and he gives you all homeworks at the beginning of the year. Only has Satisfactory/ Unsatisfactory grading system.
this class is very easy, he used a satisfactory/unsatisfactory grading system, but he is a horrible teacher and i think i feel asleep at least three times every class

Managerial econ is supposed to be a huge stepping stone to the harder econ classes.  He skipped over many of the important topics that are suppose to be learned for the future, and one of the things he worked with the most, the XGame, did not even affect your grade.  Easy as hell though if you just need an A.

This guy SUCKS!! I took this class b/c it used to interest me.He failed a bunch of people in the class, and no one knows how and why!!He compares RPI students and talks bad about the RPI administration all the time.He always talks about beer, his kids and his SUNY Albany students, I hope to never see him again. Take Prof. Julia, she's the best.
He is quite possibly the worst professor.  He gave us no tests and only pop quizes so if you dont like going to class you are screwed.  He is very full of himself.  Stay away from this professor.
Professor Hadsell is very strict and gives us a lot of work. He expects you to know details from the lectures and readings when you take the quizes and tests. Be careful.

Most Useless teacher of Economics Ever! Class could only be better if experienced with a hangover. He is soooo boring &a pain in the ass who doesnt let his students sleep in his boring class. He expects more from his students that go to RPI & makes you redo,redo,redo your papers until they meet his standards. Economics Sleepfest!
Best professor at RPI, too bad he's gone now, would love to take any class w/ him since his lectures were great and he taught very well, hw and exams were fair

One of the best professors of EE. He would stay more than 30 minutes after class to help students, and he would record a video to explain some difficult problems, or you can schedule an appointment with him. The most caring professor I've ever seen. He is passionate about his stuff and explains it well. His exams are also well designed.

Dr. Hameed is always the best in ECSE department. He is very caring and pays attention to the questions proposed by students in the lecture. He always explains complex concepts and problems in a way that is easiest for students to understand. He also gave lots of resources for test review. Definitely the best of best professors in RPI!!!

Spring22: Best professor I've ever had! Lectures are engaging, entertaining, and teach you exactly what you need to know for the tests, future interviews, and your career. He is caring, fair, and inspiring to his students, and I'm legitimately sad to see him leaving because my two classes with him have by far been my favorite part of school at RPI!

Fall21: Can't recommend him enough! Great lectures, very engaging, entertaining, and effective at teaching the content. Test questions are exactly what you're shown in the lectures and exactly what you'll see on interview questions in the future. Sad to hear he's leaving RPI, but definitely made his way onto my list of professors I'll never forget!
Introduces the material in a very clear manner! Always willing to help
Cares about his students on the individual level. Very helpful if you ask for it.
very approachable

Professor Hameed is probably the greatest educator I have ever had. He really cares about each and every one of his students and will take the time to make sure everyone understands the content of the course. I had him for both Intro to ECSE and CoCO, and he was excellent in both classes.

Hameed is the best professor I've ever had. Had him for CoCO and CANOS, both online. He's a great lecturer, they're typically easy to follow. He really cares about his students! Having the book helps, but really isn't needed as Hameed's lectures are pretty thorough. Just be aware, he likes to give a lot of small participation assignments.
Really cool guy, you can tell he cares for each and every one of his students and will try his best to make sure everyone understands what's going on.

Hes a good professor for teaching. But the worst professor for time management. Dont take his class during summer or take more than one of his classes at the same time. Because he always behind his schedule, and you will have tons of homework and labs to do during the final.
He really cares about the learning experience of his students and is always eager to help if you are having trouble. Very friendly and approachable

Hameed is awesome. He truly cares about each and every student in his classes more than most, and is such a nice guy. Additionally, he tries his best to make sure to convey the material as best as he can. If not, he is more than willing to help via office hours or in class. Overall, a super knowledgeable, down to earth, chill guy.
Great professor. A bit tough on grading, but a lot of partial credits. Attendance is a grade. New lab every class block unless there is a quiz, but quizzes are open notes.

Professor Hameed is hands down the best professor I've ever had at RPI. He really cares about his students and wants you to do well. He always asks after lectures if there's anything he can improve upon. His tests are challenging, but fair and he is helps out a ton with the labs. He knows the topics really well and can clearly explain questions.
He's great to chat with

Awesome lecturer, nice guy! He wrote a lot in class to help us understand and inspires us to ask questions, in any way and at any time since he would like every student to master the course material better. Also he always give us hints for preparing the exams. You will learn a lot from his class!

The best professor you can have for Signals and Systems! His notes are clear and concise. He answers all questions quickly and thoroughly, even at odd times. Genuinely cares about the students. There is a lot of homework but the tests are fair. Dr. Hameed is a real gem, I wish I could take more classes with him.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Good professor go to lectures he makes them entertaining and they are very helpful
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Definitely knows what he's talking about. If you ask a question, he will answer it right away. With proper explanation. If you ask a question in his office hours, he will not only answer it, but provide diagrams, proofs, formulas, etc. His back tests include video solutions from a previous instructor and are almost identical to the real test.
very nice guy. good lecture.
Great guy, very helpful if you talk to him.
fun course
Very fun class, a lot of reading for the homework but test are fair and light. overall great
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: fun class

Teaches the class like a 4000 level. Doesn't understand the meaning of INTRO class. there is a homework every single week and a reading quiz every single week and lecture quiz every single week, to much to keep with. dont not take if you are not a physics major

Teaches the class like a 4000 level. Doesn't understand the meaning of INTRO class. Don't take the class with her unless you want to either PNC or lower your GPA. My interest level decreased significantly after taking this class.
She's an awesome lady. If you want to know more about astrophysics/astronomy shes willing to tell you anything she knows. Yes, shes tough but shes trying to mold future bright, quality scientists.
She is one of the best teachers   I have had so far at RPI.  The class was very interesting and I highly suggest anyone takes it.

First of all, I've had this professor for 3 classes so far-- in the field of astronomy and astrophysics she is one of the most respected researchers in her field.  Anyways, that said-- you need to do a lot of outside work in her class. She's of the mentality that YOU are the primary source of your education. If you cant handle that, try Managment

I took a one credit P/F very basic Astronomy course with her:  when the material in lecture was interesting, I paid attention and she seemed to know what she was talking about.  On the nerdy side, and a little patronizing, but I suppose that's to be expected.

Given how much WileyPlus sucks, I didn't mind the new policy for homework this semester.  I know the new coordinator thing causes trouble, but that doesn't excuse how boring class is.  She spends too much time on homework and doesn't do enough with the daily lecture, leaving the activity up to the students.

her grading policies are wierd.  wiley plus counts for nothing.  hw grade is determined solely from hw quizzes which are based on the wiley hw.  she doesnt do lectures.  she just goes over the wiley hw and then goes either to a quiz or straight to the activity.  overall  avoid if possble.  her ability to actually speak english is not worth it.
introductory astrophysics, pretty good teacher, entertaining classes

I've taken a few classes with Newberg, and she's not that great.  Doesn't seem to understand half of what she's teaching or talking about and interrupts people to talk about minor details that are irrelevant to what questions/discussions are happening.  Overly sensitive if corrected.  Just avoid her.
A little weird, but good teacher anyway.

This was one of the worst classes I took at RPI.  It actually made me dislike astronomy and astrophysics. In this class, actual math knowledge is completely worthless, you could make up better stuff than she teaches you to use.  Test are hit or miss
Total grading Nazi, don't ask for partial credit because it's not worth your time. Also, if your homework answers look even a little like the given solutions, you'll get accused of cheating.
awesome professor, cool lady too.  definately recommended
Ok, Heidi isnt a great physics professor, but then again, none of them are.  If you ever want to wrok for JPL though, kiss her ass and kiss it good, because she has some pull there.

Actually this comment is for ECSE-4030, she has no plans for her teaching and she does not care about all the students but just the top students. If you are not confident with your academic ability, don't take her class.
Dr. Hella really knows her stuff. My only complaint is that she lectures really fast in class so it is difficult to take notes.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Goes way too fast in class. Tests are super hard but fair. Can't say the same about homeworks or labs though. She teaches some material after the lab session or after the homework is due with that same material on it
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: I really liked this course. Her teaching style was all about in-class examples. For 110 minutes straight, she would solve problem after problem. The repetition made the tests pretty fair (for the people who showed up).

Great teacher. Gives a bunch of examples and I was always able to take good notes. You can pretty much turn on autopilot in class, copy everything she writes, and than figure it out later. Book was really good too, even though it was huge. Extremely hard tests, but HW was pretty straight forward.

Prof Hella does an excellent job teaching the course. She works through plenty of examples and reviews. Most negative comments are a result of the fact that her tests are extremely difficult. If you pay attention and keep up with the work, you will get a lot out of the course.

The only professor teaching the course, so not much choice in the matter, but she does a pretty good job.  Lectures make sense and the work's not overly hard.  Exams are on the tricky side, make sure to study and write a good crib sheet or you'll be up the creek without a paddle.
she's an idiot ... enough said
I'd agree
Basically, she's not good at teaching.  Basically, she can't answer questions you ask about the labs in class. Basically, she says basically too much.

I took Data and Society - CSCI 4370. This is the type of class where you get what you put into it. The course structure is created to align with what is going on in the current world and allows students to explore the ethics of new technology. No other computer science course at RPI explores the same type of topics and it is quite frankly a need.

The best professor I've had at RPI.  Took Data and Society, and now my life is irreversibly changed.  This course was stupidly easy but also incredibly interesting and applicable to the computer science major and my social life at large.  Take a class with Jim Hendler - you won't regret it.

I had Professor Hendler for my very first CMSC class at UMCP.  He was awesome.  I loved every single class session.  I was already very familiar with programming and software when I started at UMCP, but he was a good first professor to have.

I really like him, so I was surprised to see lots of poor rating for a few years ago. It was obvious he was passionate about the subject, and was really accommodating and friendly. I do think some assignments were vague, but he was easy to get a hold of with the class slack and was there for clarification

Syllabus, homework, and labs were very vague, and were graded in a perfunctory manner. Hendler is a terrible professor who was of absolutely not help throughout the entire semester. Hendler is the kind of professor who is simply interested in himself, not students. He is quick to dismiss students and I advise you avoid him at all costs.

Explained IEA topics clearly and understandable! He's really passionate about teaching and helpful during office hours.

Taking Dr. Warner for IEA was easily the best choice I made in my first semester. He has very flexible office hours, even sometimes on holidays, and always is willing to answer any question you ask, no matter how basic. He covers the content thoroughly but still manages to make lectures light-hearted and fun. Absolutely worth the 8AM.

Dr. Warner is a very good choice for IEA! I had him this Fall, and although the coursework can be quite grueling, Warner has so much care for his students and wants us to understand the material. He also cracked so many jokes and is very fun to talk with at the Union when we're studying for exams. Highly recommend him for IEA!

For being his first time,, he made MEEBal somewhat tolerable. His assignments made no sense sometimes, mostly due to the fact that he knew as much software as we did, but is generally very knowledgeable about the textbook type problems. He his chronically unable to respond to emails for some reason, but if you pester him, he will be very helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Warner taught IEA in a very understandable, well paced, and thorough manner. His office hours are super accessible, and he is always willing to help students understand the material, which can be somewhat challenging at times. Always made lectures interesting and was a very fun professor.

I had Dr. Warner for IEA, and it was hands down my favorite class out of freshman year. We had no issues with pacing and lecture content ALWAYS mirrored what was in homework and exams (even when other professors began to lag behind). Dr. Warner was also extremely kind and able to help with problems during office hours, even on the weekends.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Shelley is one of my favorite professors I've ever had at RPI. He is extremely understanding of the course's content and its difficulties and is always willing to help his students learn. If I could leave him a 10,000 star rating I would. I highly recommend taking any class taught by him! Dr. Shelley you're the BESTTT

Though Intro to Mass Spectrometry is a hard subject to get into, Dr. Shelley makes each concept digestible and easy to understand. The quizzes are helpful to keep you on track throughout the semester and his homeworks are few. He is accessible at office hours and always makes time for his students. Mama! Don't sleep on this class!

The mass spectrometry lectures from Prof. Shelley were amazing! The lectures are like story to capitivate me. The in-class quiz motivates me to review what I have learned. He is an excellent professor to delivery knowledge clearly and concisely. I really enjoyed his lectures. Highly recommend students to take his class.

He is very disorganized. He does not properly communicate changes in schedule with his students, and is oftentimes unreasonable with the time commitment required. I like him more now that I'm not taking a class with him. I think he has an interesting perspective to give, but I'm not a fan of his teaching style

Impressive professor. His class always consists clear and interesting explanations. He is both kind and inspiring. He would always be there to solve your problems. I view his class as a primary introduction, and it raises interest a lot. Feel free to discuss with him if you are interested in art. Wish I can take other classes taught by him.

Great Professor, highly recommended. He helps us nail the test. Amazing lectures. If you do your work, you will get an A. There are extra credits. Good stuff. The material focus more on Art than History.

Best professor ever had in RPI! He is really knowledgable to the course materials and is always able to inspire the class. He is more like a good friend, who would always be there to help you. Definitely would like to take other courses taught by him, and if you 'd like to explore your interest on art history, you should definitely take his class.

He is very interesting and passionate about art, but he is unclear about grading criteria and often doesn't seem to know the best methods for our projects. I think he doesn't realize how difficult other classes are at RPI, and it's more important that we learn and be creative rather than produce a perfect product.
The papers and presentations are graded very easily. Tests are no partial credit. Get ready to talk about about vag every day for the last month of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Kielwagen is awesome. Super cool guy and great personality. Tests were pretty straightfoward as he goes over important pieces during the lecture before the test date.  Had to write two papers but they were not hard to do. Do the required work and show up to class and you will get a good grade. Highly recommend if you enjoy History or Art History.

Jefferson is among the most interesting people i have ever met. He is young and feels almost more like a friend or older brother than a teacher. The class is a real time sink as it is a lot more work than i had expected to sculpt but it is a great time. One of the few classes to express oneself at RPI.

It's A LOT of reading. Basically you have to read the whole textbook and know the main points of each chapter. The tests are ok-ish. He points out the important parts in class. Extra credits are also very helpful.

Great professor with a lot of energy! Her classes are engaging and she uses changes in her voice to communicate. It was an 8:30 class, but she was kind even though I showed up 5 minutes late. She is available to help and her office hours are very helpful. Very kind and makes me smile. If you have the opportunity to take her, do. You will learn.

This class was super heavily group project-focused (her other classes aren't necessarily like this). But she does an amazing job of making sure you learn, without leaving you floundering and confused. I feel like this is one of the few classes you get real-world IE experience! 10/10 <3

Her class has exams with open book and closed book sections. Recommend to pay attention in class and understand the content. Her content on exams is based on the homework and whether you understand the concepts. Her lectures are engaging. She cares for her students and is willing to help you. I would take another class with her again.

Prof Kemp is an incredible teacher and such a caring person. Keep in mind attendance is absolutely essential to pass this course. She gives good feedback on projects but grades more on effort than quality. Definitely recommend her course.
Amazing professor, cares a lot about each student and their work, and I genuinely improved my drawing skills. Will be continuing to take classes with her. She's very kind and understanding as well.
Very sweet and kind, could give more feedback and be more harsh, considering it is an art class

Amazing professor. I came in with no experience and came out knowing how to draw. She is really caring and wants all her students to succeed. Each of the major projects are designed to help grow certain skills. The class was a lot of work but it was very rewarding.

He clearly knows what he is talking about content-wise, this class was really just a question of if you could understand his explanations. He is very nice and is definitely willing to answer questions, I just never really knew where to start. I would recommend taking this class with LaGraff (he filled in once for my class and was way better).

Professor Shi has a bit of an accent so don't be afraid to ask him to repeat what he said. TAs lead most labs and activities, the workload is very light for the class overall as long as you pay attention to the material. Tests are mostly based off the homeworks due every week, so an easy way to prepare is just through reviewing slides and notes.

Professor Shi was a good professor. He had a thicker accent but it never stopped from understanding what he was saying. Sometimes his explanation of the course material was confusing, but feel free to ask questions since he'll always try to clear any confusion if you ask.
Overall decent professor, but there are better.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Materials Science for Engineers was straight forward for the most part. However, most stuff in the lectures were not presented clearly and I learned most of the material from the text book. Teacher has very thick accent and just read from power points.  Weekly short quizzes were pretty straightforward but longer quizzes tended to be tougher.
Great professor for DIS Studio 2! The hardest thing was doing all the CAD projects on time but they're really easy once you get a hang of the software.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Jim clearly really cares about his students. Having him as a Studio II prof was amazing; I learned a lot about both rhino and unreal. If you're doing something dumb, he's surefire to call you out, but in the best way. I can honestly say that I learned a lot in his class, and I'm more than happy I got to run my designs by him. Work is tough tho.

Incredible game design professor with a clear passion for games and his students' work. He actively brings students into discussions and makes sure that students excel in their work, especially in creating interesting game designs that use the medium and materials as well as possible.

Had some pretty great discussions. I never actually did any of the reading; I'd just skim their synopsis during the lecture and then talk during the discussion sections. If you're at all interested in the course content, he'll love you and you'll get an A. I enjoyed the class but didn't have to work at all, really.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Would take again

reviews.comment: i had taken him for both IT and Society and Open Source, Art,music, and Culture: not too bad. Just make sure you do your homework, and just be prepared to write two essays for an assignment. He gives a lot of time to complete the essays, and is normally available to answer questions. I would recommend taking his class.

I went into this class thinking that it would be an easy HASS class because that's what I was told. 2 BS 2000 word essays. A group project/essay/presentation that will count for about 45% of your grade. Busy work to hand in at the start of each class. Overall not too hard, but extremely annoying. I'm sorry if you're an IT major who has to take it
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: There was a ton of online HW, it is not supposed to be like this for a hass course that is 1200 level, this course requires a lot of effort if you want to get an A.

The majority of the material you learn outside of class via your textbook, and online learning activities and ZAPS labs. In lectures, he literally discusses the types of questions that would be on the exam. Buying a textbook was a pain, but is expected from a college-level course. I was satisfied with this course and increased my interest in Psych.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Class was changed from years past and not for the better. Very stubborn old man who doesnt see that nobody is taking this class because they are generally interested in Psych. 80% are engineers. We took this class because it was supposed to be a lighter course as pushed by the admin but it didnt end up that way

reviews.comment: A lot of work, but really funny professor. Lectures are unnecessary.

He is really kind and nice old man. As nonnative speaker I should say I cannot follow everything he said but still you should attend his lecture if you wanna get A in this class. If you wanna A in this course you should get at lease 168/180 in four tests. Each test has 45 questions in total and 5 of them are stated in class. And he will not tell u

Took for General Psych. No homework other than reading. Tests are almost completely based on the textbook, going to lecture isn't super important. When you do go to class, he's a funny joker and isn't afraid to be profane or talk politics. Grade is completely based on the four tests and if you get less than a C+ then your grade is rounded up.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Do the study guides, and go to lectures and you'll get an A.

In his class, you MUST REVIEW THE QUESTIONS he gives to you by glancing over the Textbook. Also the questions after each chapter and those on PSYC Lab are also significant. If you fails to get good grades in exams? Don't worry, participate in his research program. You will find he is very generous in giving extra credits to students who helps him
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: In the spring, you're guaranteed a C if you just fill out the Scantrons. If you want more, that's easy too; just come to class or get a friend to take notes for you, skim the textbook, and study for the tests. He doesn't usually change the test questions significantly from the ones he provides in class, so pay attention and you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Gen Psych with Hubbell is about as straightforward of a course as it gets. Show up to class, copy down the questions, and skim the textbook. Congratulations you get an A.
Get the study guide, do the practice problems on the textbook, join in some research programs for extra credit and you will get an A.

If you have Hubbell for psych 1100 you are basically guaranteed at least a B-. Going to class is optional but if you want an A, you'll have to earn it. Tests make up 100% of your grade so make sure to read the textbook and take those end of the chapter practice tests
You will pass this class. He curses in lecture and goes on funny rants. The class is extremely easy to pass with a B- but getting an A will require a lot of work.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Hilarious--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: He's awesome. Alot of times he goes off on a tangent or just rants but its always interesting. If you want a class where you just sit and read and are bored all time time this isn't for you. Most test questions can be found in his study guides. He's not like the other professors here who try and trick you, he wants you to do well.

Hubbell is knowledgeable, however rants and swears constantly. The entire grade for the course was based on four 'quizzes' where all questions are from a test bank. The study guides are all based off the prompts from the test bank and are often useless because they don't correspond well with our textbook. Hubbell was not available and didn't care.

He needs to use up time during the two hour lecture, so he spends a lot of time ranting about topics that aren't really relevant. He tries to get students' attention by swearing a lot and telling stories about his crazy times in college haha
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Most irresponsible professer

When I took this class, it was fairly easy. Everything was straight from the book and test bank. Class attendance was not required. Extra credit through volunteering for experiments. Has strong views. Can rant.
It's Gen. Psyc. It is not that hard. Tests come straight from the test bank and most times follow a pattern from the test bank. No need to go to class.

Great professor. He is funny and very entertaining. On top of that, he makes his class unbelievably easy. If you show up a week before the test, he gives you a study guide that is word for word the test. I didn't take notes, read the textbook, or study (besides doing the study guide) for the first and second test and I got a 94 and a 104.
Such a funny guy! I really enjoyed his lectures!
He's alright unless you aren't a bleading heart liberal. It's an easy A if you do what he tells you. The tests are a joke.
easiest class ever to get an A.  Read the book, do the study guides, and take surveys to get more points.  THe more points you get the higher your grade gets, couldn't get any easier than that!
A terrible teacher who just reads you his power points.
This class was extremely easy. Tests are a breeze with the provided study guides, and there is lots of extra credit.
the perfect professor and course. you can't go wrong with general psychology.
the perfect professor and class. you just can't go wrong with general psychology.
Funny
Great teacher

Straight forward.  4 tests, no final.  Don't take 1 test, you pretty much fail the class.  A lot of extra credit (outside surveys, experimetrix).  Listen and remember to what Hubbell says in this class and you'll score about 115/125 on the tests.  Add some ECs, and you're golden in the class.

Very entertaining. Gives four exams with plenty of opportunities for extra credit. He gives out study questions which help you greatly for the exams. Attend class to guarantee the A although it's not necessary.
Awesome, one of the funniest professors ever. Study for his tests though, I didn't and bombed one but the ones I studied for I got in the 90's

It's just like any other Hubbel course. Make sure you come to class because pretty much all of the tests are based on lectures. He will say exactly whats on the tests though. Back tests are also really helpful for the true/false and multiple choice.

"General Psychology" and "Intro to Sport Psychology" - grade based entirely on multiple-choice tests. All you need to do is read the book and it is definite A on the exams. If you do go to class, you get to hear bonus question, which is not worth it.

Easy classes, took both GenPsych and SportPsych.  Tests are straight out of textbook and/or backtests, just straight MC, and can be memorized easily.  Attendance is not mandatory at all, but I'd suggest going because his rants are fun to hear; just bring other work as well.  Overall he's a very chill guy with fun classes.

Gen Psych is the easiest class to get an A in. Just read the textbook, and you'll do fine on the tests. Going to lecture is almost a waste of time. Very helpful if you ask him questions after lecture on "difficult" material. Swears a lot.

Very easy course. He teaches straight from the book. I suggest going to lecture because test questions and bonus questions are directly from lecture. He is kind of obnoxious but most students find him funny so it works. He acts mean in class but is very kind in person. He tries to stress that Psychology is REALLY hard, but its not..at all.
The class is an easy A.
He is awesome. I recommend showing up to lectures doing other work, writing down his notes because they are test questions, studying back test and its the easiest A you ever got

Learning is much less laid back than Gen Psych, but if you work for your grade you should do well. He expects you to work hard, and although attendance is not mandatory, you will need to be in class if you want to pass. Remember to look for back tests, they will help you. If you need help, go to his office hours immediately..he will help you.
Great guy. I've taken 2 of his classes now. Interesting to talk to. Theories of Learning is a lot of notes, so don't skip class. One of my favorite professors at RPI.
Hubbell is the man!

Very good teacher. You will learn the stuff. But terrible person. He would swear in class just to make students laugh. Told disgusting stories of his personal life. I could have just skipped class, read the book, and done the same in the class. But if you go to class, you won't have to read the book as thoroughly.
m

Hubbell is awesome. Gen Psych is a very laid back class, and even though attendance is technically mandatory, most people choose not to go to class, which is ok since you can still get an A. Just do the reading and you will get a good grade. Oh, and be prepared to get made fun of a bit if you sit directly in front of him.
give you answers for quizzes
He's honest. He's interesting. And he teaches us about how things work. Oh, and he speaks English. That's rare at RPI.

Hubbell is pretty awesome. I had him for Gen Psych & I'm taking Learning with him next semester. Basically, all you have to do is readthe book & do back tests. Easy A. But if you get a chance, go talk to him. He's probably the most normal professor at RPI & isn't a total nerd (like MANY other professors). I recommend him.

This is not gen pysch. And he warns you and people drop out pretty quickly. Learning theory is a good class though and he teaches it well. If you need help he will give it to you if you ask. I did not want to talk to him because i was afraid to approach because he comes of arrogant but he is helpful and one of my favorite teachers.
The Learning class is much less laid-back than Gen Psyc, but it was a good and interesting class nonetheless.  Getting an A isn't easy, but it's doable.

Prof. Hubbell is ignorant, his test reviews are BS, and he doesn't know how to motivate students. Some of the info you need for tests is hidden deep in the text. His tests are hard and detailed - contrary to what others (nerds and cheaters) say. If I was to fire a professor of my choice, i wouldn't hesitate to chose hubbell.
teaches straight out of the book.  tests are format as gen psych.  come to the class before the test to get his study guide.  the questions are straight from there... no ifs, ands or buts.

gen psych, super easy class. teaches right out of the book, which is fine. doesn't care if you show up to class, 75% of people don't. just read the book, do the practice problems at the end of each chapter, memorize definitions and there you have it! show up on the 4 quiz days and you'll get your A, or at least a B. Final is optional.

Ditto.  Easiest class I've had at RPI.  Read the book, do the practice tests, you shouldn't get less than a B, worst case.  Although from what I understand from people who have taken his 4000 level class, he's only arrogant to the gen psych people and does know what he's doing in his Psych of Learning class.

this professor is the largest bag of **** ever, obviously very insecure with himslef and feels the need to take lecture time to make sure the students like him through swearing and other ****ry.  according to himself he is one of the highest certified professors in the world....i say certified shmertified he reads to you straight from the book.
Hubbell is an arrogant ponce, but classes don't get much easier than this.
Other than the fact that he is always hitting on all the hockey girls, he seems to be very passionate about teaching.

easiest course on campus.! funny and entertaining lectures too if u choose to go
I don't like him, but the class was easy.

Gen psych=easiest class ever. If you take learning though, you need to go to lectures.  If you read the book and copy down all the notes, he makes it pretty easy to get an A.  Btw... who said he was hot?? HAHA.
never went to class, never studied, showed up for tests, got a B, easiest class i've ever taken
best part about this class is you don't have to go... hubbell's pretty cool, a little crude, but okay... read the book before tests and it's an easy a
Easiest class ever.  Don't need to go to class, he reads from the book anyway.
Easy class but Hubbell is really stuck up and refuses to help at all.  Don't go to class, just read the book.
how the hell do you spell it?  This guy is awesome, for General Pscychology you will get an A if you do tons and tons of extra credit

Easy class but he's very arrogant and the lectures are dull.  You get a guaranteed A if you just show up the day before the tests to get the answers to the questions he's going to ask on the test and then read the book.
His lectures are boring and he gets everything from the book.  Just read the book and get the practice quizes for the book since he gets 80% of his questions directly from the practice quizes.

We had a new book, so he was adjusting. Antedotes came straight from book. Mostly memorization. Read the book + study guide (end of chapter), and just come to class the the day before the tests. He tells you what's on the exams, and gives answers to bonuses. Easy interesting class.
I don't know what anyone else is talking about but Hubbell is the man.  He has interesting lectures with funny jokes and statements.  His tests are fair and easy if you read the material.
Presents the material clearly and competently.  Takes time to address all inquiries.  Helpful both in and out of the classroom environment.  Straight-forward, honest, funny, and knowledgable.

Great guy. He's funny and if you show interest in his class, he'll show interest in you. Gen Psych is not hard at all as long as you read (or at least read the study guide...) It's not exactly an *easy* A, but its easy enough. He offers you credit for participation in psych studies around campus.

Great teacher.  You can go to class or not go, as long as you study before each test.  For the people who do go, he keeps you entertained with anecdotes, and he has a very 'colorful' vocabulary.  He's a great Scuba diver too.
read and ur set, don't bother goin to class...

A weird, stupid fat man.  He cracks some funny jokes in class...once or twice a semester.  An easy A, you've gotta be a total moron to get anything else.  The tests are all multiple choice and stupid.  Buy the book with all the questions, you'll be fine.
Hubbell is the man!!!
Very easy.  Interestingly, there are quite a few jocks in class (when they show up) looking for an easy A.  But so was most of the class.

Absolutely worthless and boring as hell.  Class is absolutely meaningless, and his worthless multiple choice tests are beyond crappy.  He couldnt care less about what he does, just stands in the front and babbles on about nothing.  Hubble sucks.

Hubbell is ****ing hilarious. I often found myself writing down great quotes of his during class, such as "I may be a little fat guy, but I'm a rugged ****." The class was so easy that you'd have to be dumber than a dead fetus to not get an A.

After 4 Hubble classes, he's still the guy to get. Make to take at least 1 hubble class, i recommend more! dont go to class, but make sure to study for the tests. Back tests are the way to go. thanks for the 4 A's, Hubble!
Great professor gives clear notes of exact questions. Funny guy and lets you out early alot esp when its nice out.  Go to class and everyday and you will be absolutly fine.

You really don't even have to go to class.  I spent 4 hours studying the day before each test and got an A for the semester in Gen Psych.  Just learn the bold and italicized words in the text and do the practice tests from the study guide.
Read the study guide and do the practice tests and old tests from old students.  Do that and it's an easy A.
if you can read and take the practice exams that come with the book bundle at least 2 days before the test then you should be fine, not an 'easy' A, but a B isn't a very hard task
Same as everyone else...either go to class or read the book, they both include the exact same information.  Very easy A.

Decent guy, can be funny at times. The text and review books are the most useful resource. Unless you have nerves of steel, the class is far too boring to be able to learn everything from it. Hubbell is fair and very approachable about everything.

Theey say it's an easy course but it's not unless you carefully read every page of the book, which to me means it's not an easy course at all.  Don't take it expecting an easy A.  Maybe I just don't like his style but I think he's a d*ck. Class = useless.

Great guy and reasonable professor with multiple choice tests. Read the book and you should get a well earned A. Don't go to lecture without a distraction and something to write embarassing quotes on. You're an idiot if you don't get an A in his class.
Easy A, if you get back exams and read the text.  However, the lectures are as boring as hell.
You've heard it from everyone...Don't go to class, study 2 hours for each exam and get an A.
Very easy course.  Either read the book or go to class, no need for both.  Funny guy if you like his type of humor.
Extremely easy course if you read the material.  He was very helpful, but you have to go to him for it.
He read the class out of the text book.

number one rule... read the text... after that the class is a breeze
This class is way too easy, but what do you expect at a tech school. Read the book and you are fine for the tests (which are all multiple choice, plus bonuses)
Easy grades. He spends a little too much of his free time with rats. Will spend a whole class on foot-shock if you let him.

Prof. Ji was helpful and enthusiastic.  The biggest drawback to taking one of his classes is that he has a thick accent, and is a little hard to communicate with.  His classes are hard, but if you can handle it, I certainly recommend him.

great lectures + intelligent professor. his lecture notes are better than any textbook. he's a tough grader but outside of class he's extremely nice and helpful. i'd say he's one of the best teachers here in RPI.
Nice guy who knew his stuff, but boring & quiet in lectures and a tough grader. Accent's not strong, and he really warms up to anyone who tries to get to know him  outside of class.

Avoid him if you want to grow in your career. He is very selfish and he will treat you like a slave through constant belittling. His exams were extremely tough and he is a tough grader. Better stay clear of him or your career will be ruined by him.
He is knowledgeable, but has no interest in imparting that knowledge to his students. He looks down upon his students and many leave him for that matter.

Jian Sun is very smart and you will learn a lot.  However, his leadership style is horrendous.  He berates students and deems them as slaves. A well-known professor in his area, but avoid him unless his class is critical to your research focus.  He set unclear expectations, didn't use the required text at all, was difficult to reach, and has a way of berating and denegrating his students. Incredible learning experience. Professor Ji is one of the best in the NLP game and it was a privilege to take this course offered by her. Assignments and homework were fun. Based on latest NLP research.
Can't say enough positive things about Dr. Ji. Her class is designed in a way where you get out what you put in. Very research focused if you're interested in purusing research.
