reviews.comment: Caring and Inspirational. Reading materials are pretty helpful for finding interests in NLP. Final project is a good way to test yourself if you are a good fit for research/PhD career. We received a lot of hand in hand help and instructions for choosing topic, refining models and selecting reference literature.

I took two of her courses, and really enjoyed all of her lectures and suggestions she gave during her office hours. She was always available during office hours and appointments made in advance. I even visited her during some weekends.  She did have high standard on assignments though. Extra reading was required to complete them well.

The professor is accessible outside class.   Otherwise, things are pretty bad - lectures are insipid with too many slides and people dozing off, HWs do not have clear requirements, late day policy is a joke etc.

reviews.comment: The professor always picks up most up-to-date modern techniques and explains them in clear manner with lots of examples. I learned a lot of interesting and useful methods. This is the best part of the course. Based on my observations, late assignment submissions were never allowed. It's the best course I've taken .

reviews.comment: The Professor is really awful at explaining things.  Saving grace: Easy A-s and relaxed late day policies. The only caveat is that these things are never stated explicitly.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Like others who stay in the class I really enjoyed both of her NLP course and AI course. I plan to take her other courses in the future.  Her lectures are always extremely informative and up-to-date.  All of the assignments are challenging and fun. She offers many extra office hours and always makes herself available upon request.  Take her!

What happens in this class: You sleep in the class or you don't show up. You do the 5 HWs whose requirements are not clear. You do a final project (often trivial) on a topic of your choice. The professor offers little help.  Silver Lining: Whatever is mentioned in the class policy section of this course's website, none of that is followed!
Extremely disorganized class, lectures are mostly filled with useless material with 200+ ppt slides. Homeworks are spent deciphering what to do rather than actually doing it

I had Professor Milanese in the fall of 2025 for minds and machines. I would highly recommend this class as it was very interesting. Along with that, Professor Milanese is a great guy and truly cares about his students. Only thing I will say is that the class is graded on only a few assignments.

Professors Bram and Milanese are so kind. I would be happy to have them again but did not enjoy the class in a content perspective. I thought it would be technology impacts on the world but it's a philosophy/critical thinking class. If you enjoy that I recommend the class, it just isn't my cup of tea. Class was also 5 assignments, all groupwork.

John is a great guy who cares a lot about his students and understands that they have a lot going on. If you have issues, he will make it work with you as long as you are straightforward and show up to class. He's very knowledgeable about the subjects he teaches and encourages student input in both class discussions and how the class is run.
Great Professor, very passionate about the subject and genuinely cares about students well being and success in and out of the classroom

I had him for Critical Thinking, overall the class was fairly easy, however with the weight of the quizzes one bad one could really hurt your final grade. If you show up and somewhat pay attention you'll do fine. If you actually try to understand what he's teaching you can learn a lot.

Nice guy, but very frustrating. Feedback on assignments takes an inordinate amount of time, and he places too much emphasis on group projects. Hour-long weekly plenary lectures are complete wastes of time and lack meaningful content. My advice: choose a different HAAS Inquiry class -- this one is worthless.
Ok

This was Dr. Reilly's last semester before retirement. What a great guy! Lectures were a little drawn-out, but the in-class assignments helped with concepts, and homeworks and exams were fair. No final, but the 4 midterms were worth a large chunk of the overall grade.

Going into the last months, I was in a bad spot on this course, but Prof. Reilly helped me out a lot. He's very reasonable and personable, and he lays out everything on the table. His assignments and tests aren't too hard, and although his lectures leave something to be desired, as long as you complete the HW and ICA's, this class will be a breeze.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Im going to get an A in the class. Regardless, I would not take again. He demeans me at every turn, and he brags about his availability, but it takes forever for him to respond. He's personable but calls all his content easy. I feel dumb and angry in his class, two emotions I don't usually feel. Refuses to answer my "simple" questions.

Professor Reilly is great, but you dont learn that much from him and its all dependent on how hard the TA's grade you. Go to him and regrade every test and you'll get points back. Hes an amazing guy and outside of class, he really does care.
reviews.rating_tags: Hilarious--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Do not use textbooks, mass transit is easy, a few hw and two take home tests, and final 10 page paper thats it.
you need to depend on you own and group for your capstone project
Professor Reilly was one of the best Professors Ive had at RPI. Very accessible outside of class, super personable, and always there to help students in anyway possible. Overall great guy

He was one of my favorite teachers I have had. He genuinely wants his students to learn and if you have trouble understanding, he will give you the help he needs. Great lectures and cares about his students. Tests were not super hard, but definitely tests that you know what has been happening in the class. You do need to study and learn excel.
Reilly is a good guy. He is not here to trick you like most professors. His homework and exams are very straight forward. I highly recommend him as a professor. Just wants everyone to do well.
Cool professor, makes jokes and talks to students outside of the class. low voice, have to focus to hear what he is talking about during lecture.

Mass Transit - Jack loves Mass Transit as he was big shot in CDTA. Class includes analyzing NYC MTA and international systems. Very Easy class! 2 HW's and 2 take home tests. 1 10 page paper due last day. Jack is an easy grader. Very interesting class and we went on field trips. Highly Recommended for easy A, interesting and he is good prof!
One of the best Professors at RPI.  Is very approachable and is always around to help students.  Genuinely cares about students

Slow teacher, doesn't like to deal with 'nonsense'.  Doesn't answer student's questions in class, rather asks them to ask him after class 'off-line' which isn't helpful to the rest of the class who might be wondering the same thing.  Definitely holds theory X about students, always first to assume that the student is trying to BS him.
One of the best professors at RPI
Can drag lectures on sometimes but he's not a hard teacher.  If you pay attention in class you should get an A in the class.  He is really helpful if you go to office hours and a nice guy overall.
Not understandable.
Jack is a great guy and runs a fluid class.  He encourages students to learn from each other and encourages his teaching staff to help.  Interested in students on a personal level also.

I wouldn't recommend taking this class if you don't love the topic. However, I survived through it with a B+ even though I feel like I didn't learn anything. The lectures aren't taught in the standard definition-theorem format, and you have to figure out yourself what the important takeaways are to prepare for the exams. He posts back exams.
Feels like you're drowning all the time
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Very high amount of work and a lot of studying required for tests only for him to throw curve balls randomly. Test was a completely different format than all the previous year tests that he provided and had several different subjects added that weren't gone over in homework. Avoid class if at all possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Very poor instruction and very harsh grading. Unless you already knew the topic you're in trouble.

This class is likely fine for MATP majors. However, there are cases you can be forced to take this class even if you are in another major. If you're in this situation like I currently am, the course is near impossible as he assumes you have significant background information and you're probably going to be spending >20 hours per weekly hw.

He is one of the best professors I had. The class material is not hard, but you need to work on it for exams. hws are very helpful in exams, he will have one question from hws in each exam. He is also very helpful, and he is very patient as well. There is a programming project involves, great in simulation practice.
Best classes at RPI.

Extraordinarily smart man, but he wouldn't let you say that about him. Taking his NLP course was one of the most challenging experiences in my academic career, but well worth it in the end. The homework is difficult, but enlightening if you see it through. John's extremely accommodating and his door's always open if you need help - super nice guy.

I found Professor Mitchell's Models of OR class to be less interesting than his Discrete Structures class (which was awesome), but it is probably a worthwhile course nonetheless. I haven't personally conversed with him outside of class, but from what I heard he is very approachable and really wants you to do well.
He sounds like a teacher straight out of Charlie Brown's world, but if you can manage to pay attention, he does actually seem to be a sart man.
Brilliant man. Not very socialable. Dull lectures. Great guy. Teachs a lot of material. Do not take if you are look for easy A. Only take if you want to know the material.
Prof. Mitchell teaches the class Intro to Discrete Structures very well. Take his class.

He does enjoy teaching, but his style is a bit bland.  Proving things out is essential for understanding things like Discrete Mathematics, which means it's hard to follow at times, but he provides enough examples that it's easy to see what he's looking for.  This was his first year teaching Discrete, and I think he did pretty well.
Prof. Mitchell loves teaching and it shows. He cares about his students and he makes himself available for help.

You don't even go to class with this guy. Everything is DIRECTLY from the book. He doesnt even make his own review sheets. He uses Prof. Schmidt's. Come on guy, get motivated and show some interest in what you're doing or no one else will.
Very boring professor, was not motivated to go to class.  I wouldn't recommend him unless you want a class that is straight out of the book.

Mitchell's good, but nothing to write home about.  He teaches the Multivariable Calculus portion of the course really well, but since he actively researches in applied programming, he tends to go off on confusing tangents wrt Matrix Algebra.
His lectures are interesting and his policies are very fair. He makes his tests difficult, but he's nice and more than willing to help. He's one of the best professors I've had so far.
John Sturman is the goat of everything. He is so attractive and such a good professor!

Great class - useful lectures and topics. Not much work outside of class. A lot of writing and papers, but all software focused. Genuinely useful class and you can tell he likes teaching it. Highly recommend, grading is also very lenient. Professor is very kind and willing to help
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--So many papers

reviews.comment: Great class if you are interested in CS. Definitely need some background in coding. Great lectures - if you attend and keep up with lecture exercises the class is easy. Exams are graded fairly and homeworks can be completed in a few hours. Professor is great and tries to make class engaging. Those who don't do well are not prepared for RPI courses.
Awesome class and professor. SDND isn't too much work if you keep up with deadlines ahead of time, just make sure to start the final exam early.

Prof. Sturman is ok, I came into the class not knowing how to code and actually learned a decent amount. The homeworks arent too bad except hw 8 which took forever. Tests are hard and the class is extremely hard to get an A in, especially if you have no coding experience. The average in the class was around a C so a lot of people definitely fail.

CSCI-1100 at RPI is going to be very difficult if you don't already know how to code, as Sturman does not do an amazing job explaining material. I would recommend learning Python and/or reading lecture notes before taking the course (they can be found online). Sturman himself is a pretty nice guy, but can be slightly difficult to talk to.

Be prepared to spend a ridiculous amount of time doing the homeworks. If you have some background in coding, you don't really have to go to the lectures (they are very boring and all the notes are posted to the website). The class kinda sucks, but after you're done you know how to code pretty well.

The homework assignments are ridiculous. The tests are on paper so the code must be handwritten-- why? He refuses to answer student emails or questions about grades. Why can't a school that costs so much money find a better instructor for this course?!?

Don't bother going to lectures, it's easier just to read the notes. Homeworks are impossible and count towards a third of the grade. Instructions are never clear, but grading is super precise. Tests are on paper for some reason, so get ready to hand-write your code. Unless you're a CS major, you will only use about 1/4 of the info from this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Avoid at all cost because he will ask the students what his bugs are.

He doesn't show his mastery of the CS material in my opinion. He will trip on things in the lecture and doesn't know where the bug is. His format on HW and files posting are sometimes off. Students have a question on a practice exam question but he wasn't able to answer it.

John Sturman upsides:
- Good lectures and tries to keep the class engaged through activities and discussion
- Can be understanding (sometimes)
John Sturman downsides:
- He is very nit picky about silly things 
- He is not a software developer!
- Expectations for assignments/tasks are not clear 
- Prepare yourself to be writing a lot of papers

Assignment instructions are extremely vague, but he's very particular when grading. Not a software developer and fixates on silly things. I'm a big OOP and agile guy but he's dogmatic. Do not use functional programming patterns, he will dock you into the ground on your diagrams and writeups.

Sturman is wholly unqualified to teach the course and seems to be clueless about modern software development. Much of the course is an exercise in futility and needless tedium. This course is set up as if all software is an object-oriented CRUD application in Java. I would not recommend the course.

I thought this class was going to suck but he made it about as interesting as it could be. He seems to know a lot and is a great lecturer. I thought he was funny, but his sense of humor is a bit of a taste thing. Pretty easy grader but very rubrik-based so just make sure you satisfy the rubrik and you'll be fine.

I don't know why people are being so nice to this guy. He's completely clueless. Absolutely clueless. I'm just glad I quit caring about paying attention and began playing chess instead. At least this way I got some practice with the Queen's Gambit.

John is one of the friendliest guys I know. He made class fun and full of life while explaining material well. Answers e-mails promptly and is a joy to work for. He goes out of his way for students to ensure that they understand the material and have a fun time in the course. Highly reccommended class and teacher.
Tied for worst professor ever with his co-instructor.
Was open to questions to make sure everyone could understand what he was talking about, willing to repeat things again.

Sturman is an excellent speaker and explains what hes trying to explain very well. Many of the topics he speaks on are terribly boring. Also, they waste a great a portion of the class doing Design Pattern presentations when they should really just do them. Doesn't help with coding, but this class is about doing things yourself, so get over it.

Lectures were extremely boring and didn't learn a thing, but the class itself was easy. He's willing to help. For the classwork, I just asked him to look over what I did, and he would simply tell me all the changes I needed.
No Comments
loud and can be obnoxious while students are presenting - grading is stricter on the first parts of the project and on presentations - i've had worse profs for a required course, but eh...
No Comments

Sturman's technical knowledge is limited but Pearce's guru status makes up for that.  He tends to grade earlier project deliverables harder than later ones.  Don't be afraid if your project average is a 75 and you have three deliverables left.  Your grade will go up.  A fair grader and a good guy.

He is very dumb. He does not know the material, and isn't very good of a teacher at all. Takes forever to grade tests and never gives feedback in anything close to a timley manner. But his class is easy (for SDD)....
Although his knowledge on Software Design is limited, he teaches his material well. He gives easy homework too.
Kuchera's partner.  He at least makes an effort, but I consider his knowledge of the subject so minimal that he shouldn't be teaching.  Adjunct lecturer, not represenative of RPI's usual quality.
One of the most interesting people you'll meet and you'll find out why after the first exam. So worth

If you do the homework and attend every lecture, you'll get an A. Quizzes and tests are normally homework questions and he curves pretty well. He's pretty strict on attendance so just make sure you go!

Homework's were optional, but if you don't do them you most certainly wont be prepared for the exams. I found the exams to be very fair, usually the questions on the exam were modified homework problems. He's a great guy, very nice, but I didn't learn that well from his lecture style.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The professor's lecture notes and homework solutions have many typos in them. He tends to change the layout of the problem. When he does this, I can't really tell what's given by the problem or something that you have to figure out. His quizzes and tests aren't horribly difficult as they're remarkably similar to problems done in lecture.

I don't know how Tichy has such great reviews in other classes. Fluid Mechanics has been a mess. His notes are all over the place and gets annoyed when the test averages are lower than what he wanted. Everything is extremely confusing and I would not recommend him.

Tichy's a solid choice for Dynamics. The first half of class is notes, the second half is examples. Just go over notes and the examples before tests or quizzes and the class should be a breeze. He also has really cool life stories, you can learn a thing or two from them.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Pretty good professor, willing to help anyone out. He's very old, and getting the projector to work / doc cam to focus was an every-20 minute ordeal. Makes class interesting because most of the class is working through examples, and usually lets us out early. Fun Fact: he was in Commander Cody & His Lost Planet Airmen in the 70s-80s. Cool guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: You should definitely try to take a class with Tichy at some point at RPI. I took dynamics with him as an elective and learned a lot. There were never any surprises on tests, so it's not too hard to do well if you put in just a bit of work. He gave weekly quizzes, and is also pretty strict about attendance and phone usage though.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Show up to all the classes, do the homework (or at least copy the solution), study a little for the tests and you should get a relatively easy A. Quizzes every other class. Test 1 was easy, test 2 was hard, and the final was medium difficulty.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: The most interesting teacher and one of the best guys, will miss him after classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: very straightforward with quiztest problems  - very very similar to homeworks. tons of examples to work off of. don't buy the textbook!!!!!!!!!!!
Overall a good professor, but could be moody at times. Explains things well, but too impatient to listen.
Fairly easy class. Good at teacing / explaining. Strict on policy such as no cell phone/ no sleeping/ attendance...Has weird grading system and also funny history(he used to be in rock band).

DOWN SIDE-has an attitude. no phones, can't be late. can't talk in class.UPSIDE-crystal clear methodological approach to dynamics, follow his steps and you can't go wrong. fair grader, generous curve, and really helpful outside of class. tests are awefully similar to the homework/class examples. so do your part, and   ace this class!

Prof. Tichy was one of the best teachers I have had at RPI.  He was very helpful outside of class and his teaching methods were very straight forward.  He does tons of example problems, which are very similar to the HW and tests.  More professors should teach like this.
Great Prof. Will help you if you need it although the class is straightforward if you go to class. Tests are extremely similar to practice problems in class.

Uses methods different from the book and other professors that seem more roundabout and difficult. All problems on tests are directly from class and homeworks so if you study there is no reason not to get an A. Pesky quizzes make attendance mandatory which is annoying especially at 8 am. Decent professor though a nice. plus tichy's a rock star!

He was a good professor.  Went over theory then problems during class.  He was clear and understandable in class.  Tests were over in class problems of homeworks, so if you studied those you were fine.

If you go to class, you basically get an A for quizzes.  If you study the problems he goes over in class and actually try them again at home, you can't do poorly on the tests.  If you even slightly make an attempt at this class, you will do pretty well.  Good class and good prof.

I don't know what these other people are talking about because Tichy is a great teacher.  He made the class interesting and did many example questions to help you learn.  No graded hw and some pop quizes that were mad easy.  As long as you do the hw on your own and study a little for the tests from his example problems in class you'll do good.

Tichy is one of the worst professor's I've had at RPI in 3.5 years.  He treats his students like middle schoolers and demands they learn the way he wants to teach them - or you will be penalized through attendance/participation and quiz grades.  He makes up for his lack of teaching ability by grading exams generously.

doesn't follow the book's notation.  you will get screwed when it comes to common exams because of his non-traditional ways.  realtively easy though once you get the hang of his teaching style.  very laid back, maybe has a lazyish attitude but wouldnt say he doesnt care at all.  a bit of a clown sometimes.no confidence in him lecturing.

Strengths isn't the hardest engineering class, and he made it even easier.  Did an OK job of teaching his way and for his particular tests, but once the general final comes from other professors, you'll get killed.  He skipped over some of the more difficult concepts in the class, which may hurt you if your a civil.

Great professor.. His teaching style takes a little while to get used to but he does a really good job.  Always goes over what's going to be on the tests unlike other professors (according to friends). Has a slide set about his rock band.  If you have to take strengths, this is definitely your best choice. He checks ratemyprofessors.com.
No Comments

What he went over in class, was learned. The hard part of the class was when other professors made the tests and used different notation. Great at explaining the material espeically since he hadn't taught dynamics before.
Tichy isn't great at teaching but the material was easy to learn, and he grades really generously.  Put a few equations for like 85%.
easy grader, not too clear on class notes, but goes over problems similar to the homework. gives lots of helpful handouts.

Great guy and very nice. Ask for help and he'll always help you until you fully understand, or he'll just give you the answer if you want the answer. Lectures are very boring because he reads off slides from a different source, so you have to read the textbook on your own to learn the material. Read the textbook before quizzes to get an easy A
Cool guy, I dont get why he's getting all this flak. I think I liked his class! Would take again. Dedicated to his job, once seen him talk all lecture till he lost his voice!

A good teacher, would be arrogant to say he teaches badly. He looks after the whole spectrum of students in his class and paces it accordingly. Something I've seen few RPI profs do. Simply has a different style of teaching, likes to use visual aids (videos etc.) to make learning simple, trivialise difficult problems and maintain interest.

The lectures may not be the greatest; however, he will help you understand what is troubling you during office hours. Doing this & reading the textbook will earn you a decent grade. The homeworks are simple unlike the quizzes. During breaks, he plays videos the students suggest to relieve stress and show how the concepts we learn are applied irl.

Really disorganized. Uses other peoples powerpoints and focuses on random information such as CPU performance from 10 years ago instead of teaching. Some of the homeworks do not actually have a prompt and you basically just have to figure it out. Stops lecture so people can have conversation with each other. Its not too hard though.

Incredible amount of class time is wasted, course is poorly taught and designed. Homework assignments and quizzes are not clear. Takes long breaks in class. Lets students speak about irrelevant material, which is incredibly disruptive (common theme at RPI), but must CS profs will tell the particular student to speak with them after class.

Homeworks/labs are a week ahead of the material he's teaching. He reads off the powerpoint slides, and quizzes focus primarily on applied CS, which isn't ever covered. Every 4 class sessions has a quiz, and wastes time watching youtube (15min) in class. Homeworks/labs instructions are incredibly vague. Submitty doesn't go up until last minute.

Homeworks and labs are easy to do. Quizzes are pretty hard because the questions are poorly worded. Takes a really long time to grade assignments. Likes to take breaks in lecture to watch club penguin videos.
worst class I've taken at RPI.  Interesting content but the professor teaches class very poorly and makes it difficult
He has no idea on what he is talking about in class.  The explanation is unclear.  and the planning of the class is absolutely BAD.

Terrible professor. Very poor planning of both individual lectures and the overall course. His explanations are meandering, confusing, lacking in detail, and boring. The biweekly tests can be tough, but only because the questions tend to be so unclear. My advice: try to get by on the textbook alone; lectures are too excruciating.

If I understand correctly, he's a postdoc student teaching Comp Org so that his advisor doesn't have to. He is very passionate about the material, but he really doesn't explain anything well because he hasn't yet figured out how to teach properly.
Dr. Ke is knowledgeable about transportation systems. The lectures connect theory with real-world examples, which made the material more interesting and practical.
Dr. Ke is an awesome professor. I admire how much he cares about his students, and the time and effort he puts in to help us understand the content.

Dr. Ke is a great 1-on-1, but is a poor lecturer. Is very engaged and helpful at office hours, but is shy and doesn't seem confident in the lecture material. The textbook is much more helpful than the lectures. The exams are worth 50% of your grade, so don't brush them off. I believe Dr. Ke will improve immensely as time goes on. No final.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great Professor. Bio lab was super interesting and I enjoyed his class. My only complaint is that most of the assignments were not graded until the end of the semester but grading critieria was super easy to follow so you should be fine. Would definitely take molecular bio lab with him again.
Had him for BIOL 2125 (lab). Good stuff. Just remember to keep up with lab reports since they're due at checkpoints.

I had Dr Cheeseman as my Intro to Cell and Molec Bio lab professor, and he's very helpful! He's always willing to answer questions and his instructions are pretty clear! He's also pretty easy to talk to and get along with, and his grading is very fair.

I took molecular biochem with him as a 6 week class during the summer arch. It was a solid class, and he was very understanding that we were all very busy and that 6 weeks is not a long time. He would always discuss what to expect for an upcoming test (and often give some important hints) during the previous class.

He knows his stuff and makes it relevant to students. The students who complain are the ones who honestly arent trying. He works with you if you are struggling. Theres really no reason to do poorly if you really put in effort.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: This professor was quite possibly the worst I have ever had. His tests were unnecessarily difficult and long, the TAs graded differently depending on which one you had (they alternated), the homework was long and had little to no test correlation. He was very unresponsive and slow on responding to emails. Thank god for generous test curves.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Shamz can't teach at all.  He loves to be lanky and eat terrible food.  It's astounding.  Sometimes I walk into class and he preaches excerpts from the bible, basketballs flying everywhere.  It's astounding.  I can't help but get bruised. I hate playing defense. The oreos, gamecube and dirty laundry is everywhere. Someone help me. It's astounding.
Easy class, don't even need to come, teacher doesn't show up either sometimes

Don't need to come to class, all homework online, taught me that if Teemo stands still and takes no action for 2 seconds, he becomes stealthed. Taking any action will break his camouflage, granting him 40% attack speed for 3 seconds.
Easiest professor ever, never came to class, just play league of legends for homework
PLEASE READ TEXTBOOK
THE CERTIFIED GOATTTTTTTTTTTTTTTT!!!
The course is pretty straight-forward--if you do the homework and in-class assignments, it's an easy A. TAs are easy to access and there's a lot of help available if you're struggling.

Lectures are essentially read from a script; if you ask a question that isn't explicitly answered in a slide somewhere, don't expect to get a satisfying answer. Nothing really negative to say about Professor Kim, but nothing really positive either. Perhaps the best teacher for the class, but didn't leave a lasting impression.
cannot understand him at all. Nice guy though
Professor Kim is a great physics professor. He always took the time to answer student questions, making sure everyone understood the topic. Very friendly and helpful.

Prof. Kim was easily one of the best professors I've had so far, although I generally don't like physics and only took it as a major requirement, he made the class much more tolerable. If there is something you don't understand please just ask during activities and he will explain it very clearly without any room for misinterpretation.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Kim is FANTASTIC! He makes the content clear and he's a very kind professor. Everything is clear, concise, and well-stated in the syllabus & class notes. He's also head of the department, so he truly understands the concepts. I will be taking him for Physics II if he's teaching it. Best professor in the department by far.

One of the few professors at RPI that goes out of his way to ensure success for his students. He is personable, knows all of his students by name, engages everyone into class discussion and activities. He really goes the extra mile to help each student individually and put time into making extra practice and study material for those that need help.
He lectures well and really cares about students. Usually got out of class pretty early, his lectures are pretty straight to the point. He does have an accent you may have to get used to.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Fantastic professor, ALWAYS kind to students. His smile gave me so much confidence, and made me feel guilty not getting good grades in his class. The class goes pretty fast because there's only 2 lectures a week. If you are not certain about something or need help, ask him right away.

Professor Kim is THE BEST physics 1 professor at RPI. He is very knowledgable and even takes on helping students he doesn't have in class. He will go over the same problem with you however many times you need until you fully understand. He was always available in office hours and would stay late just to answer questions. He is a true gem!!!!!

He is definitely the best teacher. There is a lab every class which takes about 30 minutes so you leave early, but that means you have to come to class. There is no curve on your grade, or tests or anything. Whatever equations he writes down write them in your notes and on a separate sheet of paper to use for your crib sheet or else it'l be a mess
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Young is incredible. I did poorly on the first exam and he sought me out and asked if I wanted to come in for extra help. Cares about his students. He scheduled separate office hours every week with me to review. I'm also a student athlete and he was more than accommodating. He also would keep up with my stats! Really great professor!
He is the best choice for Physics I. Do all the homework and you will get an A
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Kim is the best. Classes are quick and interesting. High expectations, but willing to help when things don't go quite as planned (which is common for freshmen in physics 1). He even tutored me and one of my friends once a week outside of his office hours to help us improve our grades. Definitely try to get him for physics 1!

Prof Kim is very good at teaching and making sure that students understand. Personally, I found the labs hard and occasionally frustrating. I didn't do very well in the course as I would have liked, but I learned so much from him.

Kim is an amazing professor. I had originally failed the first two tests and began getting tutoring from him and it totally turned things around, I actually began to understand the concepts more in depth and it made it a huge help for when I aced the third exam. 100%  would recommend this professor to ANYONE taking Physics 1.
I loved Professor Kim. He spent a lot of time during labs helping students understand the concepts we were learning
Helpful professor, nice man. Willing to make some meaningful discussions with his students.
Super chill and knowledgable!

Professor Kilduff is the backbone of the ENVE track. He truly cares about academic, professional, and personal growth. I recommend taking notes on key things said in lecture, doing the in class problems. Do not worry about taking notes off the slides (he goes too fast) & you have access to them on LMS. Exams are similar to exams from past years.
Excellent.  Difficult class and teaches at a high level.  Very accessible and always willing to help you learn.

He's always a few minutes late, but you get over it once you realize that he's an awesome professor.  The material is pretty difficult, but he is very helpful and flexible.  His office hours are usually pretty busy though, so it is a good idea to get there early or make an appointment.
Taps teeth and chews on overhead markers usually a few minutes late.  Otherwise a great teacher, very clear and accessible. Made material clear in class.
Awesome
Best professor I had at RPI.  Tough classes but he will work with you individually to help you learn.  Outstanding.
I think he is a great professor, definitely very helpful. All you have to do is ask!
Too Smart for himself.  Good luck to you seniors!
No Comments

Lewis is a nice person, but she's too heavily rooted in research and doesn't understand how to teach students who know nothing about Physics. She also didn't respect that many students in the class were Archies and had other priorities. Overall, you can definitely pass this class, but avoid her if possible; you won't get an A unless you really try.

Replaced Dwyer halfway through the semester for unknown reasons. Big mistake. Nowhere even close to how good he was and tests were even harder. Uses bad powerpoints to teach and the rest is on your own. Test average was 70 the whole semester with no curve. Not sure how that is ok

Professor Lewis has no interest in the education or well being of her students, not that she has the proper ability to educate them even if she did care. She copies directly from her notes which are a more confusing version of the textbook and is horrendous at answering students questions. Avoid this professor at all costs.

Not a bad professor, but doesn't stand out. Her handwriting and speaking is clear, but her lectures were mostly just book material and if you asked a question that she hadn't explicitly prepared for she often got tripped up and couldn't answer satisfactorily or until the next class.  Tests were generally easy, and had large multiple choice sections

I would disagree with most of the comments here.  Tests are hard, but if your prepare for them using the book, class notes, and homework examples, you can be successful.  You can't just memorize the formulas; you have to know how and when they are applied.  I have gone to her office hours to ask her questions and she has been helpful.

I'm sure Dr. Lewis was a great professor in a phys 2 where she did not have to develop her own course materials. She is terrible at preparing this class. Her lectures are just quotes from the book. Tests are hard, homework is harder. Doesn't give good study material for tests and could care less about her students. Avoid this professor at all costs

We thought she would be a good step up from the professor that taught last year. Unfortunately, she does not care about her students at all. She recites the book to the class during lecture, using no unique notes or examples. She gives tests that cover subjects not covered during class. And she is rude and uncaring toward her students.
No Comments

Physics II for non-physics minded people will be difficult.  The course is hard, however Professor Lewis is a good professor.  The labs and exams are all standardized through all of the sections.  Lewis is very helpful in office hours;  this is where I learned most of the material on the mandatory homework and of course this helped greatly on exams
Clear and concise. Her in-class examples did a good job of reinforcing the material. Presented everything to us in a down to earth fashion that made a difficult subject easy to understand.
She's a good teacher. Go to her office hours, she's really helpful with homework. And study alot and you'll get an A.
Excellent teacher, likes to help. She cares for her students a lot.

She is a great professor and really tries to learn your name and make you participate(but not required). Which really shows me that she cares about her students. The only tough part is that even though she is a great lecturer, your grade is fully on tests and no final.

Dr. K is an amazing lecturer, shes very funny and makes an effort to learn everyones name, (and remember them), her practice tests are great preperation so make sure to complete them thoroughly. Most of the time the homework is much harder than the test, and shes a fair grader Her office hours are amazing so take advantage when you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Klyachko is a great professor and I can't recommend enough to take f her for calc 1. She teaches exceptionally well and her tests are extremely fair. She is also very caring of her students and will help you if you need it.

She is incredibly kind. She learned everyone's name. Yes, she will randomly call on you, but there is no pressure to correctly answer the question, as you can always skip it. If you're afraid of her calling on you, I would just recommend that you sit in the back. She is an amazing professor, and I would totally recommend the course.

Professor Klyachko is honestly one of the best professor that I've ever had. She NEVER makes students feel stupid and the "there are no stupid questions" is actually real with her. She is amazing and I would have loved to be able to get her for Calc II. I wish she taught more math courses because her lectures and genuinely amazing.

Dr.Klyachko is a very amusing professor. I had her for Calc I and Calc II. She will randomly call on students in class but will hint and help you with the answer if you aren't sure. Calc II is difficult, but she is patient, a detailed lectured, and provides review questions that are almost identical to the exams. I would definitely recommend her.

She actually has a personality, and she makes lectures as entertaining as possible. If you sit in the first three-four rows she will call on you randomly, but it's beneficial. If she calls on you and you don't know the answer, you can pass and she doesn't hold it against you. She teaches you material that is harder than what she puts on the test.
Engaging lectures, fair tests and fair grading. Highly recommend this professor. Attend lectures and use the review sheets.
She lectured very well and clearly while making sure everyone understood. Her exams were fair and I thought she was a fair grader too.
She was a good lecturer and actually cared about the students. Tests are fair

I had her for Calc 1 and loved her and I took her again for Calc 2 and she was equally as great! Calc 2 can be challenging but she goes above and beyond for her students so go to office hours! No final which is great but all 4 exams will count so study hard! She will cold call. if you don't know the answer be honest and she'll help you through it

This is a review for calc 1 but she is one of the best Calc professors at RPI. She is super caring and really wants her students to succeed. I had her for Calc 1 and her teaching style was easy for me to understand. Also No final if you get her

I had her for both Calc I and II and she was incredible both times. She was always really understanding and always did whatever she could to try and boost any grade. Shes very open and happy to laugh to take a quick break during lecture while staying on task. If you get the opportunity to take her class definitely do so.

One of my favorite professors at RPI hands down. She is very approachable and easy to understand. Her exams are very similar to the review questions she provides(however there are no back exams). There are 4 exams and no final, the overall grade is pretty test heavy, however the exams and quizzes are very reasonable.

Tests are worth more than 75% of your grade. Buckle down, study, and good luck. However, some pros include no final at the end of the year, Test structures that exam 2 is 1 and 2, and exam 4 is exam 3 and 4, so when you are done with series, it becomes easy(like a pre-multivar). Best instructor for 1020, just prioritize her tests over anyone else.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Easy to reach outside of class, clearly cares about all of her students. Very good lectures, and minimal homework. She will know your name whether or not you speak to her at all. Klyachko didn't give us a final, but we had an extra exam. Doesn't drop scores or curves grades. Exams are graded harshly, but not unfairly.
she is so sweet and nice, and I love her even though I did poorly on exams; her lectures are very efficient and well-rounded, and she is so smart

best math teacher at rpi. she has office hours and she actually gives an f. She has exam reviews which other rpi teachers do not have btw and also has bunch of things to help you pass the test. P.S every math teacher is very test heavy at rpi it is just how it is but I wish I could take her for every semester.
Really clear and concise during lectures. Responds to emails promptly and never EVER rude.
She is great. She's a solid lecturer and her smile and jokes are so cute. I think I have a girl crush on her.
Cold calls atleast 20 times a class, makes the hardest exams out of every math professor, extremely test heavy
Homework is optional and not for credit. He's a pretty good lecturer, explains a concept then teaches by examples. Nice guy, would take another diffeq class with him in a heartbeat.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Klobusicky is freaking amazing. His lectures are easy to understand and his homeworks cover the material well, are easy to understand what is expected of you, and are graded fairly. I can't recommend him enough
No homework + tons of examples

Data Systems is an easy A with a light workload. All the work and exams are online. A couple assignments have extra credit. The lecture slides are posted. The content of the course can be confusing sometimes, but Rosty is a lenient grader. Rosty tries to make his lectures interesting and funny, and he almost always ends a half hour early.

Definitely the easiest professor you will have at RPI. Very little work and extremely light grading. Lectures are impossible to follow, but attendance is not mandatory (nor is it required to do well)! Super funny guy, be prepared to not learn a thing though.

Arguably the worst professor I have ever experienced here at RPI. Not only is he lost within the content he is teaching, but he teaches and preaches the wrong information. I was able to comprehend him through the thick accent, but the illegible handwriting on the projector screen was unacceptable. I will not be taking any future classes with him.

Rosty is amazing! This class wasn't hard in comparison to other classes at RPI but it was actually fun. You'll learn SQL, R, etc and the extent to which we learned wasn't a lot but was basic and efficient. Grading is so so lenient and is practically graded off on effort. I had to teach myself out of class but from the slides and it wasn't hard!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Slides are helpful, grading criteria is not strict so long as your logic is sound. Fun class overall.
Super chill and nice guy, and is very lenient with deadlines.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: One of the easiest professors in the IE department. Even if you do not show up to class, his lectures are easy to follow and he is accessible 24/7. If you can take any class with him - take it!

Favorite IE professor. He's very accessible outside of class, and lenient on grading EVERYTHING (late work, assignments, take-home tests, etc). If you stay on top of your work and occasionally ask him for help (& know what you're talking about) you can get an A. His slides are also straightforward and you can easily do assignments from those.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Korolov has probably been my funniest teacher yet though I don't believe it was intentional. He is very knowledgable, but he often lost control of the class and let students disrespect him which would sidetrack the entire class. He's a solid choice for IEA and was always flexible with absences and make ups as long as they were rare.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I took MAU his first semester EVER as a professor. Somehow ended up with an A because he was lenient of redoing assignments, and tests were take-home or open-computer. Lectures are extremely confusing though, and he's a little hard to understand. A little condescending when you ask for help as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Lecture intensive class, and while the material can be difficult, Korolov's open-everything policy helps mitigate the tediousness of the material. He tries to test understanding rather than memorization in quizzes and exams. Homework is easy, group projects can be difficult though, there is little to no instructions on how to use statistic software
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Course was definitely on the easier side of ECSE courses, and overlaps early on with both ECSE 4670 and 4560. Was lab work heavy with sometimes buggy/lacking setups. However, final creative project allowed for a lot of freedom but seemed to be difficult for a lot of other students to complete.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This course was exceptionally interesting for those looking for a course in communication systems, although a bit theory heavy. Professor Kar provided all materials online and was easily reached for help and feedback. As a senior, homeworks were more difficult than average, with heavy focus on Signals & Systems math and MATLAB demos.

Professor Kar decided to make the cutoff for an A absurdly high (95) without warning at the end of the semester, after we already submitted course evaluations. Lectures were useless for the labs and final project, so you could do this course on your own. No one would have attended his mumbling lectures if there weren't quizzes due after each one.

IoT doesn't have exams but has labs, homeworks, and daily in-class quizzes. Professor Kar is always willing to help for any questions you may have and is very flexible on due dates. Lectures were interesting.

Easy class, material is well explained. Professor has a bit of an accent/stutter but it's not severe. Excellent notes provided. Exams were open everything. There was a semester project, but options were pretty much unlimited.

The class was not bad as I thought it would be and I was really nervous about the probability stuff but it was not difficult at all and overall an easy class if you are used to do your stuff on time and also if you do understand the homeworks you should be fine.

I don't know what everyone is talking about...Kar is a good teacher.  He does stutter, but his examples are straightfoward.  The homeworks really weren't that bad and the tests were a little long, but comon, it was curved (not to mention open book open notes).

The assignments from this professor are very long and difficult to finish.  I would aspend 8 hours working on any given assignment.  Furthermore, the tests are way to long.  Many people in the class including myself were unable to finish many of them.  Though we did finish class a week early.
Way too much work, tests too long....even if you know all the answers you can't finish them. Hard to understand, stutters more than porky ****..Nice guy....but bad teacher

15 weeks felt like an eternity.  Hard to understand.  Usually unprepared for class.  Never finishes examples, most likely because he doesn't know how.  Has no clue how long a test takes. (Nobody ever finished them.)  Shouldn't be teaching graduate courses

One of the best lecturers I've had at RPI. She explained things clearly and did her best to make sure the class was keeping up as she taught. One of the best things for lecturers to do imo is to make sure everyone (more or less) understands what you just taught before moving along, and she did that without going too slow
She is self-centered and tends to elevate her image above that of other students. I have personally experienced her criticism, and she often makes harsh remarks.

Great professor overall, notes are clear and concise and if you pay attention in class, everything should make sense. Very open to questions and will answer them well. Homework is very similar to what's covered in class. There are outliers here and there but they're specific cases you won't really see in exams. Homeworks are very similar to exams.

She gives you what you need on the slides and that's about it. Lectures often boring. Skips through example problems leaving you lost. Homework will only get longer and most times does not correlate to what was taught. Tough exams, although sometimes generous partial credit. Only 2 midterms; you must study for these, as anything can show up.

- Lectures are very well organized and easy to understand. - Graded in-class problems every lecture that are graded so come to class. - Exams are reasonable regarding difficulty and material. - Homeworks take a while so start early. - Highly recommend this prof and I'm taking a class with her again this semester.
Very good lecturer
Professor kraft passed out during class and proceeded to fail everyone since he was mad. Stay mad bruh.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: LITEC is the worst class you will probably take at RPI. Kraft is a decent professor but isn't aware that most of his students are mechs who can't code. The labs will take up 20 to 30 hours a week and are barely worth a quarter of your grade. The tests are ridiculously long and hard. Basically a 3 hour test in a 2 hours Avoid LITEC at all costs

Nice professor! He cares about his students a lot and never shouts or yells to his students. He always smiles to you and explains things patiently. As this course is relatively difficult, choose this professor might be a wise way to get a satisfying grade finally.

This is a rough class for most, pick your team wisely. Professor kraft is a good guy to deal with, he responds to email promptly, will help you if you get behind, but if you wait too long trying to fix it yourself, you'll be chastised for it. Typically far less lenient with reports or projects than other professors. Be on the dot or else -20pts.
Excellent professor. Will go far out of his way to help you if needed.
Great professor and a pleasure to work with.

Not a very good teacher. He may be OK if you are an Electrical Engineer or Computer Systems Engineer, but if you are a Mechanical Engineer or something similar he teaches at too high of a level. He expects you to have too much experience with programming when you enter the class.
Professor is outgoing and fun. LITEC always sucks but he is on top of things and always willing to help. Glad I got him

Go to lecture, she goes over a lot of incredibly key concepts there that she tests on. Overall, I thought she was a great professor - the material isn't the easiest to take in from lecture. If you go see her outside of class she will sit through it with you until you understand it. Good luck!

Probably for her first teaching she was a bit shy but also very patient. I went there a lot and she could always wait to fully understand my question(ESL student lol). Sometimes lectures can be dry at times but her very well organized ppt could save the time for you from reading . boring textbooks.

There are very few factors that contribute to your grade. This class is not easy. Homeworks and exams graded very harshly. She is very nice but very monotone and grades hard. Take classes with other professors if possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Group projects

reviews.comment: Her lectures can be a bit rambly, but she genuinely cares about her students. I recommend attending all lectures if you're new to calculus, though you can get away with only attending those with in-class quizzes. Homework is fair, exams are not curved, and practicing is very important to do well in this class.

Professor Kiehl (while being a very kind and thorough professor) definitely demands competence. Attending lectures and actually doing the optional textbook problems are the best ways to ensure you pass her class.

- Overall, she's not a terrible lecturer, the lectures are just extremely fast paced and not clear at times.
- The exams are incredibly fair, just long. Quizzes are also quite fair, just nitpicky, but homeworks were graded with the most nitpicky-ness though.
- During class, she will call on students and then berate them for not knowing the answer.

I pay so much in tuition, yet ended up with a professor who couldn't explain the material or grade fairly. Lectures were confusing, feedback was meaningless, and effort didn't matter. I've learned almost nothing. It's unacceptable for a required course to be taught like this.

Very in depth and easy to understand lectures. Her tests make sure you understand the concepts and are mixed with true/false, multiple select, multiple choice, and open ended so that you can make up your points somewhere. Would definitely recommend!

Dr. Kiehl is a great lecturer, but her office hours are what really made me like her as a professor. She is extremely helpful one-on-one. In class she can seem intimidating but during office hours she is very respectful. The work can be a lot since there's homework and a quiz every week but overall it's not super difficult. Her exams are very fair.

The exams were fair, with partial credit questions. The course was organized and predictable. The lectures were content-heavy and not very helpful. Students can be passive-aggressive when answering questions. Homework (15% of the grade) was an easy A with multiple attempts and dropped scores. Your lowest exam score is dropped.

A great professor, Dr Kiehl makes her lectures thick with content. A little too thick for me, but she does a great job at teaching the material as the semester goes on. 4 Exams is a little much, giving you about three weeks between each at best. Definitely one of the easier classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures optional, but you should go. She teaches very efficiently and explains things well. Homework 2x a week. There's graded online work and then unchecked textbook work that she says is mandatory, but don't do it. Instead, use it to study for the test because there aren't any back exams. Tests are easier than the HW; there aren't any tricks

Professor Kiehl's lectures can be fast-paced, but engaging if you stay focused. While she can seem unapproachable at times, unstuck AI proved helpful for supplementary practice and reinforcing concepts outside of class.
Very rough professor. She is very passive agressive with student. Not clear of what she wants on the test. Examples are terrible

Amazing teacher and one of the few teachers at RPI that I admire. Her lectures give a lot of examples that really help you out during the exams. She was very caring and considerate to me when I was having family issues; she seemed like she actually cared about her students. I would love to take other classes with her.

Dr. Kiehl is very knowledgable, offers great notes during classes. Great lecturer, goes really slow on concepts and break down everything in details. She does not have regular OHs but you can always book appointments with her, she offers great help on HW probs and exam prep. Most back exams at APO are from her class so use those to study!
I like Kiehl. Grading can be quite pedantic but for the most part exams and homeworks were fair. Never had much of an issue with her for this course.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr. Kiehl is the only reason I passed Calc I&II. I came from a school with a severely lacking curriculum and students and teachers who didn't care--I was far behind from the start. If you reach out to her for help, you'll immediately see her clear care for her students. I don't think there is any RPI math professor more understanding than she is.

Good notes and clear grading criteria. Fair exams, homework's and presentations. Feedback on assignments is good, and provides hints/steps for proofs. Grading tends to be nitpicky, but that's just the nature of the course. Solid professor.

Professor Kiehl easily had the best lectures out of my freshman classes. Tests offered a lot of partial credit on open-ended problems, and homework was given via Achieve, allowing you ten attempts to correctly answer each question.

It really feels like Dr. Kiehl wants you to do well in her class. If you put in the effort to do the homework and go to office hours you will do well. The material can be difficult but her grading system gives room for mistakes. She is great at explaining concepts if you ask for help and ask questions. Highly recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr.Kiehl is a very good professor, she is not harsh on grading, and if you ask her questions she answers them to the best of her abilities and if she can't then she will find the answer for you.

Her notes are very easy to read and look back on. Some lectures are heavier than other and the only downside is that she will just power through the heavy lectures and cram it all into the 2 hours of class. She tries her best to answer your question during/after class. Fairly easy class and also easy to find her back exams.

Dr. Kiehl is a wonderful professor. She knows exactly what she expects from her students and makes that very clear in lecture. She may seem impersonal during the class but she is extremely kind and helpful during her office hours. Would definitely take a course with her again if I could!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Mathematics has always been my favorite subject and my strongest suit, until I had class with this professor. I hated each single class. She scolds people very harshly and is very strict, and she makes you feel stupid by answering your question and staring at you. I did not have a fun experience, and her exams are the hardest of them all.

Professor Kiehl lessons are quite good, she can move very fast throughout the lectures. Kiehl is one of those professors who tends to want to make there lessons  perfect. In my opinion, I don't know if it was just me, but she seemed really unapproachable and unfriendly, to the point where you couldn't ask her anything without feeling stupid.

Does a lot of example problems during lectures and typically does a good job explaining the content. Her tests do tend to be a bit more difficult than other professors but if you find a good way to study or have taken calc before they are fine. Is very kind and great to go to with questions during office hours and review sessions.

Dr. Kiehl made Calculus I a very enjoyable experience. I am absolutely horrible at math, but her exams were very fair and she was always willing to stay after lecture to explain topics to confused students. She hosts exam reviews one week in advance of exams, and exam questions are usually similar to the ones shown in the review.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She was pretty good, I liked her teaching style. My main problem was that notes and homework were not posted in a timely fashion and sometimes I was surprised with homework. Overall, I liked her and her class.

All I can say is that in my opinion Dr. Kiehl was a really hard Calculus professor. I swear some of the exam versions are harder than the others and the TAs are told not to give brownie points for showing work. Calc 2 is hard enough as it is, so if you're looking for extra credit take another prof.

Professor Kiehl did an amazing job teaching Calculus.

It certainly helped to have a little background but calculus can be confusing for many.

Not accessible outside of class and will ignore emails. Rude and condescending in class. In the first class I attended with her she publicly humiliated someone for asking a clarifying question. As someone with anxiety, it sucks that she yells when she proctors tests making it harder to focus. The actual class material is not difficult.

The lectures could get boring at times, but overall I think she is a great professor. She covered everything in depth, I thought the tests were fair, and she gave good feedback on work. She does have a low tolerance for disrupting class though, so if you're going to talk or sit on your phone, she might give you a hard time.

Her class is structured such that you watch the lecture before the in-person session and then do a worksheet. It's more work, but you're guaranteed to learn the material. I found learning under her to be an extremely pleasant and inspiring experience. I highly recommend taking a class with her if you get the chance.
She is a good professor overall. I found some of the lectures long and boring especially towards the end but, I learned the material well and her notes were very useful.

If you're the type of person to go above and beyond you will love her. She provides a lot of example questions and lectures are detailed/well organized. I didn't go to lectures because I already took calc I. You should go to lecture to know how she wants you to write your exam answers otherwise you could lose points. Personality is strict.

Her lectures are fine, except she chooses the most bright, hard-to-read colors to write notes with. If her color choices were more normal, I think I would've actually gone to class more often. Can sometimes be snappy if she's having a bad day, but otherwise a kind person and is concise in lecture.

The flipped classroom is actually the most vile invention known to mankind. Having to watch lectures + do the HW outside of class created an immense amount of work given that the work done in class consisted of struggling through a worksheet whose answers were never posted and were therefore no help at all. Class was mandatory but a waste of time.
Detailed and to-the-point lectures! Not the best at technology.
Good Prof

Gives relevant examples of material, along w/ examples found in the textbook. 50% of each test being multiple choice questions and definitions makes it easy to do well as long as you study and do the HW. HWs are pretty easy if you do the worksheets. Worksheets are pretty easy if you watch lectures and ask questions when confused.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: If you ask a question in class and don't understand it by the 2nd time she explains it she will condescendingly tell you that you're not doing it right & that you should get it. Takes points off of quizzes and homework but won't tell you the correct way to do it. 72 theorems & definitions must be memorized word for word..... that's just for Exam 1.
Amazing clarity and depth in lectures; assigns a generous amount of homework, but specifies what parts to study for exams.

Kiehl is okay, though she's not particularly accessible outside class and isn't the best at explaining the material. She does care about how well you learn the material, but she's nothing special. The TA on the other hand... If Dan is still the TA when you want to take the class, avoid that section at all costs. He's awful and an awful grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Tough grader

reviews.comment: A lot of work from webassign but shes a really good lecturer and a sweetheart. She gives lots of examples for each topic. Only negative thing I have to say is that her handwriting is sometimes hard to read. Extra credit for getting iClicker questions correct in class
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Absolutely get her  if you have the option
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Kiehl is the best technical lecturer I've had RPI. She takes amazing notes and posts them online. That came in clutch if I missed a lecture. I probably should have gone to class more as she gave iClicker questions, but even when I missed, I was alright because of her notes. She's amazing. I took Calc 1 & 2 with her and I highly recommend her!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: One of the best professors you will have. She has the best notes ever. Much better than the book.
Easiest class I've taken, A+ without bonus quizzes. Great help if you have issue, which isn't likely
She's super nice and easy to talk to and has very clear expectations for every test. All you need to know is on her website, including all of the hand written lectures.

Took Kiehl for Calc 2 last semester. She was very clear in all her lectures and I understood all the material. Never opened my textbook the whole semester. She gives extra credit too. 1% on final grade for participate with I-Clicker. Great professor.
Easy Calc I and II teacher

I have her for Calc 2, and while my test average right now is an 88, my average in the class is just under a B, because the full-or-no credit skills quizzes are weighted so heavily. They're worth 20% and after our first test most people had a skills average under  a 50% (myself included), and a 50% means a straight 10% loss from the final average.

Professor Kiehl is probably the best instructor for mathematics that I have ever had to this point in my life. She organizes her class lectures very well, and has a clear understanding of the course content. Professor Kiehl's class notes are also easy to follow along with, so if you study them for the tests, you will do well in the class.

There extra credit quizzes that help boost your grade. She writes clearly all steps like a high school teacher. There are suggested homework problems and  test problems to study. This is not mandatory to complete and it is not graded. Overall, one of the best math teacher I had in RPI.
Great Calc I professor. Easy Tests. Great notes, posted online

The material can be challenging, but Kiehl structures the class in such a way that it is very difficult to do poorly. It's also refreshing to have a professor who happens to be a human being and not an academic robot.
Very kind professor who actually explains the material well in class.  Course is very manageable if you stay on track and study at all.
A well taught and well organized class. An enjoyable experience overall. A good teacher that I recommend.

She does a great job of explaining things and her test are really straight forward. She bases her test from hw problems in the textbook, so if you do your homework you'll have no problem acing the tests.
Amazing woman. Great teacher. Lessons are very clear and to the point. Come ready to take notes she doesn't pause. If you miss something notes are immediately posted online. Highly recommend.

Professor Kiehl did a solid job teaching Calc II.  Granted, the stuff can get terribly dry, but she teaches it, and won't leave you in the dark on anything. She also clearly explains how you will be tested, which is a +.
She is a good teacher, and she is a nice teacher, but as a person she isn't so nice.

Kiehl is definitely my favorite professor here. Concepts are explained extremely well, there's no homework, and tests are pretty easy (and there's a lot of extra credit). Kiehl often gives very big hints about what is going to be on the test and I always felt very prepared going into them. Kiehl is also very nice and helpful as a person.

Calc 2 has changed its structure. There is in-class material and quizzes, as well as "skills" quizzes that cover material at a different pace (a little confusing). She teaches integration well and the quizzes were easy. Lines and planes were hard to understand. Does a lot of in class examples and is helpful during at office hours. Go to class!
She's an amazing professor and gives a ton of extra credit.  Super easy if you go to lecture and do the homework. Tests are a lot easier than the homework

She's probably the best professor I have this semester. She covers the material thoroughly in class but still finds time to explain things further if you have questions during lecture. There's never any HW but there are always optional practice problems online. We've had two tests so far and I felt very prepared for both.

She is really nice. The way she teaches her class is great. It is a very simple class and only requires out of class studying. Honestly, she does her part when it comes to teaching. I highly suggest going to office hours. This course is mostly memorization, but also about seeing proof processes. The best thing to do, is practice. Go to class!

Great teacher!  This course was easier than AP calc.  Set up problems but do not solve.  She went through everything very thoroughly even when kids asked dumb questions.  You'll have to use maple for labs.  Optional final.  Easy A if you could handle AP calc.
Very friendly, I attended most classes and she made an effort to learn my name. I would recommend her.
incompatible, goes too fast, does NOT explain herself ... leaves you in the dark; very difficult to wrap your arms around this teaching method

Had her for both Calc I and II. Get her if you can. Ignore those who say she goes too fast, she doesn't at all. She tells you the exact kinds of problems that will be on the exams, gives study hints and problems, and explains things crystal-clear. I got an A in Calc II. Easy class, and she is easier to listen to and understand than most professors.
Had for calc 1 and 2.  She covers more material than some of the other professors but she goes in to less detail and tells you exactly what is on the exams.  Awesome teacher
Posts practice problems on website that are identical (except #s used) to exam problems and tells you in lecture before exam exactly whats going to be on it
She's an amazing prof. She goes fast and it's very easy to understand. Do the homework and do all the problems that she gives right before the exams. Easy A.

Goes pretty fast and doesn't do much to explain the material. Pretty much pulls all of her lecture notes from the book. Will occasionally give helpful tips, but usually goes too fast for you to get all of them and the notes at the same time. I wouldn't recommend taking this course if you don't have a head for math.
Awesome. Maya Kiehl is the best teacher. Have her if you can!
awesome

About as straightforward of a teaching style as you can get. Almost as good as Schmidt in terms of clarity and easy tests. She drastically narrows down for you what you need to study for the final. You won't learn how to do extremely difficult calculus problems, but you'll still leave with a good basic understanding.

This course is very easy, and everyone knows it. Don't tell your Calc 2-taking friends that you're in "Contemporary Math". But make sure you still give the assignments your best shot, or you *will* receive a bad grade. As for the professor, she's nice in and out of class, and in general cares more about the course than you probably will.

Kiehl is fairly clear with teaching, but is on the easy side as far as exams go.  There are quizzes every week, but it comes in handy with the basic skills stuff.  One may or may not learn much, depends on how much effort is put into it.
Very good prof, clear, helpful, fun

Kiehl is totally uninspired and too bureaucratic. She acts like a highschool teacher and an overprotective, annoying mom. Has a quiz every week and FOUR midterms, one of which is a week before the final. She basically tells you the exam questions the day before and grades very leniently. Easy A, but you won't learn anything from her. Good luck!!!!!
Easy class gives u all the problems on the test beforehand, if u know calc u should get an A pretty easy

She's such a boring teacher. I guess she's perfect for those who miss being in highschool. She's far too bureaucratic and uninspired. It's teachers like her that make learning seem like a painful process.

Great teacher.  Easy to understand and learn, and her tests are very easy.  She's a nice person and cares about you understanding the material.  If she isn't available she tries to have her TA be available so you always can get help.

Kiehl was a great prof. Her lectures were very clear and organized. She posts practice questions before each exam so you know exactly what you need to study. I would deffinitely recommend Kiehl as a prof.
She's great, easy, and nice!
Excellent Calculus professor. Spells everything out for you and walks you through each type of problem. Extremely helpful and understanding.

Excellent professor; lectures are clear, organized, and to the point.  She teaches you what you need to know, and doesn't waste your time with anything else.  Despite the fact that calc2 sucks, she did a great job teaching it, and it's fairly easy to get an A.
This class wasn't exactly easy...but Kiehl gave great notes and gave very fair tests.  From what i hear about some other Calc II professors she is extremely good in comparison.  I'd recomend her!

Had her for both Calc 1 and 2 and she tells you exactly what you need to know and how to do it.  When you don't understand something in the class, she personally goes out of her way to make sure you understand it.  Highly recommended, provided you get a good TA.
easy to get an A, just sort of pay attention and study what she tells you to. the only reason you should ever get less than an A is because of gateway
