Good lecturer who can give you a lot of information very clearly.  Lots of opportunities to do well in the class.  Her only drawback is that she runs the Gateway, which is Satan's **** child risen on Earth.  But besides that, highly recommended.
Very nice... big class kind of hard to pay attention... but easy to get an A if you took calc before in high school
Class was very organized, always knew what would be on our exams and quizzes, lectures very informative and useful.
Had her both semesters, slept through class. Shes teaches very well, no HW, maple labs done in resus. and is very nice

She goes way too fast.  I asked her questions about what I didn't understand, and she tried to help, but I didn't understand what she was saying.  Maybe I'm too dumb.  I have a D in there right now.  I haven't gotten less than an A in math since probably sixth grade, if even then.  I don't like it.
Teaches well!
she cuts straight to the point with her notes
The class is very informative.
good teacher, yea, go to class day before a test, she tells you what to study, not hard to get an A at all!

Excellent teacher.  Gave clear examples.  Tests are no surprise.  Moves at a good pace so you don't get bored and zone out. My advice don't skip class the day before an exam because she basicly goes over exactly what to study especially for the final.
she is the best teacher I have had at RPI (not daying much b/c i am a freashmen) but she is really clear
not a bad teacher, though if you miss one class you get screwed because she goes so fast. worth taking from her, her exams are awful though.
She's a good teacher- explains things clearly and gives good notes.
Totally incompatible teaching style for me...I didn't understand a single thing she taught.
She makes everything seem easy when it isn't
I repeated calc 2 and I understand this subject much better than the professor i had last year, heavily recommanded.

Good teacher. Very clear. Easy as long as you study. I got A's all through the class then slacked off before the final and ended up with a B in the class (after spending 8 hours in the gateway to get a 10).
Excellent.
I had an A going into the final but she wouldn't give me one afterwards even though I was like .000001% from it. She's pretty easy to understand though, and does explain the topics pretty well.
Decent lectures, fair exams and pretty fair homeworks.  Doesn't tend focus on any particular thing for long.  That helps sometimes but makes the class move really fast.
went so fast i had no clue what was going on the entire time. managed to get a D in her class after getting a B in calc I. couldn't understand a thing. go figure.
Very easy exams and no homeworks. Extremely clear in her teaching and very helpful in all aspects.  Quite simply, TAKE CALC I AND II WITH HER!!! You won't regret it, trust me.
Very clear and organizes material very well.  Also very reasonable about grading and preparing you for exams.

Her final was interesting. She tends to rip through difficult material and have no bearing on what the class sees as hard, even after using the placement exam. Willing to throw out points to make anyone pass; makes it harder to get the A though...
Good professor, very friendly and easy to understand.  Do the suggested problems and use office hours...they can save you.
Took the time to make it easier and clearer for someone who's strong point is not Math...
She was terrible at explaining stuff a few years ago.  Heard she's gotten better, but dont know for sure.  Asks if people understand and if they dont, she still moved on
Sometimes she goes really fast especially with difficult material.  Not really bad, not really good either.
she is simply awesome...must say she one of the best math teachers ive had EVER...shes awesome...loved calc 2 with her...
Good teacher.  Makes sure everyone understands things before going on.  Always willing to answer questions and wants students to succeed.
Very helpful teacher.  Very clear.  Highly suggest to take Calc 2 with her.
always willing to answer questions, very nice.
She makes sure that everyone understands before going on and is always open to answering questions
Good explanations, makes sure she doesn't lose too many people before she continues
Really takes the time to ensure that students get the material. Putting forth the effort will result in an A.
No Comments
No Comments
great teacher
good teacher... easy class, very helpful
No Comments
No Comments
No Comments
easy course!
No Comments
Terrific teacher
excellent teacher!
One of the best math teachers I've had, very consise and informative
Great Teacher!  Very clear!  Very good!

He seems like a great man throughout the semester just with the fact that he was not care about my project. In the end he gave bad grades which I never get from any other professors. Worst is that he never tells why :(

I first interacted with him in IDS. I wasn't the best in his studio, but I genuinely appreciate the way he teaches. His Tai-Chi desk crits are so effective that all I learned became unforgettable. His own works are infused with the air of avant-garde, and he's way more open-minded than most faculty members in this school. He deserves a lot of love.

Indeed, ‘overly confident in his own knowledge and intelligence’, but then again, he is an architect. Ted tends to use his experience to teach his us. Very helpful…will stay as late as possible to help you during desk crits. Gives freedom and insightful feedback, only if you work hard and seriously towards developing your idea.

He seemed overly confident in his own knowledge and intelligence to the point of a limiting cynicism that precluded other valuable pov and led to critical errors in assessment. Brilliant people remain open minded and curious, enjoy seeing things from different perspectives. Ted lacked any of that. Also plays unnecessary games that were concerning.

Ted is best for intrinsically motivated students. Pursue what you're interested in, and he'll be intrigued by your interest. He lets lazy and/or unsure students fall by the wayside. He would be great to talk about architecture with over a cup of coffee, but as his student I was often left frustrated and wanting actual guidance.

Cool guy, awful professor. Not present for about 1/4 of classes. Very unclear. Like the Cheshire cat. Seems to speak in riddles. Very good trait for, like, the equivocating narrator of some Shakespearean play. NOT for a professor.

Be clear about one thing: Ted will not issue any clear formula for "good design." He will offer insight/criticism (and some tangential anecdotes) to help you find yourself as a designer.  Don't aim to please him - first pursue what interests you. If he senses you're wrestling with issues and engaged, you'll be fine. Great guy - take his seminar!

Ted is a genius, he really is...the bad comments left on this board a probably from incompetent design students who expect professors to hold their hands and baby them through everything. For many of you that do not know, Ted has taught all over the world including some very now famous architects.
Ted doesn't lie or pretend -- that makes him worthwhile in my book.  His perennial question "why is that a good idea" is an honest one. Helps you get over your bad self, if you take it seriously.
he is an extremely knowledgeable professor. There are few like him at rpi. however he may not be the best for 1st - 2nd year studios. Really great guy if u get to know him.

Not helpful in a Studio Environment!!! Never once got a straight answer from him. Great guy to talk to but not a professor. I can deal with criticism and even pushing myself to produce better work but "you need to start over if you can't make this work" after a month of developing as the second desk-crit that i got from him just made me furious.

Seems like a great guy when he's your teacher... then it comes time for your grade.  He'll sneeak up on you and nail you with your grade out of nowhere.  It's not too pleasant.  Also not a very clear guy in what he's looking for; kind of indifferent towards whatever you're doing, and then he'll just agree with whatever your critics say in review.

Ted was one my best teachers.  He always finds a way of understanding your research and giving you a world of possibilities.  It's too bad that arch undergrads are not ready for criticism and give him such bad reviews.  They're not ready for the real world.
Good criticisim if it interests him.  It your idea isn't his cup of tea you get pretty much nothing. Not much help to those who are unsure.  Great juror.  Not so good teacher. Good guy though.
completly unhelpful, very arrogant
sarcastic; disinterested (often absent from studio); unapproachable; antagonistic at reviews.  bitter that he has to teach at all and can't just follow his research whims.

Ted is wasted on the undergrads. He can come across as being snooty but is approachable. His book "Mosquitoes" is a refreshing satire on architecture and I reccomend everyone to read it if they are to learn more about Ted. As for his behaviour at reviews, I do think some students need their feathers ruffeled as the school is a little too polite.
so inappropriate, he is surely headed for a lawsuit or dismissal.

Clearly, Ted has contributed to this website (see last comment) since I can't think of any student who would actually say that. Definitely a victim of the "failed architect lashing out on students for fun". Doesn't understand the concept of constructive criticism. Really, he should be ashamed of himself.
No Comments

laid back easy going prof. casual teaching style. Be careful the "open end" project could be a trap. He won't push you. If you are self-motivated person, take his class to broaden your idea about architecture and design.
Ted is God...
Demands hard work and creative thought.
No Comments
No Comments

Really nice guy, a bit hard to understand and doesn't explain things well but I took intro to open source so he wasn't lecturing most of the time. The class suits him well, definitely recommend. Genuinely cares about students and inspiring open source creation

Moorthy is a very passionate professor. If you can get past his accent (Which is a problem for some people) then he is a great professor. He knows the material and is always ready to help. He is invested into his students.
Professor Moorthy, overall, was pretty good. He is a very entertaining lecturer and presents the material well. Sometimes the tests could be quite difficult, but that comes with the territory.

I had him twice: once for Algorithms and once for ModComp. In Algorithms, the TAs ruined that class as some TAs didn't give partial credit so a lot of is TA-dependent. Moorthy is helpful, he has a facebook you can even use to ask him questions. However, his lectures are fast-moving and hard to understand.

Moorthy is the best professor at RPI, aside from R. Grice.  His lectures are hilarious, but only if you pay attention.  He is ALWAYS willing to help and loves to teach.  His accent isn't too difficult to understand.  I think he is a bot though, he responds to all E-mails in roughly 29.7 seconds flat....

He's knowledgeable and has a good sense of humor, but I really had a lot of trouble understanding him because of his accent. I skipped most of the lectures but luckily you can learn most of the material from the textbook.

Professor Moorthy's Models of Computation class was very enjoyable. I've heard very mixed opinions about him coming into this class, but there really is nothing to complain about. He does have an accent, but he's very understandable.
Moorthy's a great teacher.  He knows his stuff, but the accent does provide some trouble at times.  He's very helpful if you seek him out, pay attention and go to his office hours if you need help.

Good teacher.  His accent was a bit tough to understand at times, but he was good at explaining, and cracked an occasional joke, in his own kinda way.  Very helpful too.  He went out of his way at one point to meet me for extra help late evening because I had such a busy schedule.

Projects were difficult, and he spent lectures teaching us "magic tricks" (which was really just math).If you had questions he recommended you use google. He did curve tests though, but the projects were very time consuming and frustrating
Very intelligent.  Provides interesting examples in class.  Almost always in office.  Has a thick accent, though.

The course material is difficult and demanding. The projects are very difficult and should be started on immediately. He's very helpful if you seek him for help. Class is only semi-useful. He can be difficult to understand, especially when he gets excited about a topic.

Can't understand a word he says in lecture and he has poor organization and teaching skills. He makes things more complicated than it seems.  I was really looking foward to taking this course, but he made this course hell for me
Can't understand what he says.  He jumps from point 1 to point 5 without explaining how he got there.  Hws are graded pretty tough but the projects are ok.

Lectures are tough, but if you go see him to get help he will basically walk you through anything you have trouble with.  Gives projects which are involve little more than cutting and pasting code together.
Accent was a bit tough, but once you get past that the material was not hard at all except for the last 2 weeks.

Good teacher.  In his class you can learn as much or as little as you want to really.  He makes the tests and projects pretty easy.  Tries to get the class involved in discussions.  His accent isn't bad at all compared to many other TA's and professors.
Yes, he has a thick accent, but it's not that hard to undstand.  He's always happy in class and he smiles a lot and will always answer questions.  A nice teacher.
Excellent teacher.  Easy class.
Fantastic teacher.  Very funny.  Made computer science fun again...
Good overall.  At his best when improvising demonstrations of the material rather than summarizes the textbook.  But I had to buy a book on network programming to do one of the assignments.
No Comments
Funny guy, really bright.  Ask him to juggle and recite Pi, as this is one of his many talents.  Hard to understand but his final was incredibly simple.  RTFM!

The man is funny to watch, but thats about the only amu****t you will get from him. He is totally and utterly incomprehensible. The homeworks started off easy enough but out of no where they became totally impossible to understand.
He is very hard to understand, has a thick accent and just reads off of powerpoint lecture notes another professor made.

Wow, if you ever have any trouble with homework or projects, go to his office hours (not the TAs). He sat with my partner and I and helped us fully complete the project.  He is funny and a great person to talk to.  The Pi man!
Great teacher, lots of extra credit, took about 2 weeks of sitting up front to get used to his accent.
No Comments
He's not really a bad guy, but he's not really a good professor.
Nice Guy,  Indian  (I think) accent, but not too hard to understand. Funny, and interesting too.
No Comments

I have taken two classes with Professor Kupferschmid and they have more than exceeded my expectations. He puts 100% of his effort into making his classes effective, fun, and fair. He is probably the most organized professor I've ever had, cares about his students, and constantly improves his classes based off student feedback. Amazing professor!
Great Professor. Enjoyed taking his class.
Professor Kupferschmid is the most organized person I've seen.
An excellent teacher. Helpful professor. The course was very well structured. He is just perfect in all.

Although the course material was complex, Professor Kupferschmid showed a strong understanding of the material and presented it in lecture in a manner that made learning fun, easy and engaging. He was always happy to help with any kind of question and made doing well in this class very achievable for any student willing to participate.

Mike (he prefers to be called Mike) is the best professor I've had on his campus. His attention to detail in his lectures is impeccable. Ample opportunities for extra credit and he makes going to class enjoyable. I definitely recommend taking any class with him if you can!
He is the best Professor I have had at RPI so far. He is extremely caring and puts a lot into his lesson plans. If you can take a course with him!

I love Mike! He makes operations research a lot of fun and engaging. His grading policies are extremely fair. Extra credit is given by handing in assignments early, and the further along you are in the class, the more credit you get! One of my favorite classes and professors to date.
Wonderful teacher! Explained everything clearly, was super organized, and made sure you understood the material. Available at office hours. Overall, one of the best teacher's i've ever had.

This is a quite easy class, even for students who are not math major. The professor will illustrate all the things slowly and clearly in class, all you have to do is to spend no more than half an hour a week to finish the homework. He gives a lot of extra credits, it is really easy for you to get an A if you attend class.
Yes

This professor is excellent. He explains everything in class just about as clearly as could possibly be. He makes a point of calling on specific people in class to make sure everyone is keeping up. The grading is very merciful, with extra credit being given for work turned in early. He's most interested in you actually learning the material.

The best professor I have ever had. He gives crystal clear notes, and explains things until every student understands. He wants you to do well and understand the material at the same time. No exams - just homework and quizzes that you are allowed to retake if you bomb one. TAKE THIS PROFESSOR!

Absolutely one of the best professors I've seen at RPI yet, right up there with Prof. Schmidt and Holmes.  His syllabus and lecture notes are very organized and easy to follow.  His grading system is very lenient and he is more than willing to help students in and out of class.  Lastly, you actually learn the material and get something out of class
The assignment work is heavy but as long as you get it done, it is alright. The class activities are innovative. Professor makes each lecture interesting and relevant.

She is so funny and tries to make every lecture interesting. She does look for attendance but her coursework is super easy as long as you try and actually attend class. She is super nice as well and caring. She is also hilarious and has a lot of dad jokes. There is pop quizzes but she lets the students decide when they will take place.

Typical classes are lectures followed by easy mini group project that you work on with an assigned group for 10 minutes and then present. She gives notice for pop quizzes that are just one short answer question. Hw assignments are just readings that you write a page on which are fairly easy to do but you need to remember when they are due.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: TONS of homework. Hard to get an A, but most people can get an A-.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Great class. A little too much to read and I missed the first assignment (my bad, it was already posted). The project was interesting and the class had a lot of activities to keep it fun. Learned a lot and used it in a job interview
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Very cool examples. Really easy to approach!
super easy and caring if you get to know her. show up and participate in class and she'll love you.
Langdon is my best memory of RPI. What a great experience. Favorite teacher!
He is an excellent teacher, and very engaging as a professor.  Extremely helpful and understanding, and I look forward to taking my lass HASS elective with him :)
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Had him for American Politics in Crisis. Fantastic class. Class discussions motivated by weekly readings that were extremely interesting. Winner had great discussion starters that made for great conversation in and out of class. Also, out of class, he is one of the most interesting and personable people I have ever met.

Winner is a very smart man who will tell you exactly what he thinks.  He's very good at getting people to think about and discuss the subjects at hand.  His classes have a good amount of reading and writing in them.  Also, he'll sometimes use lead-in questions to try to put words in your mouth if you don't agree with him, so be careful.
Langdon is a task master but he also takes the time to be extremely helpful and engaging with each and every student in his class.

Winner is a really good professor and caused me to become interested in politics and how terrible they really are.His grading on papers can make doing well difficult if you are a poor writer. Not the biggest fan of technology...may lead to our downfall. STSS and PDI courses are good with this professor.
No Comments

Langdon is an extremely conscientious professor and is now the Thomas Phelan Professor by that very merit. He neglects noone in class and brings out peoples strengths so that everone feels included in discussions that turn into conversations.

the big winner of science and technology studies is an extreme technology sceptic. hes really liberal and postmodern and i bet his political beleifs get int the way of product design. if you wanto help 3rd world countries and poor people and stuff with engineering go for PDI

Winner isn't fantastic, but he's better than most professors I've met here. He's very clear and useful for everything outside of the class. In class stuff (design as in this) he's decent. He actually has a designer point of view instead of the engineers that we had. Just a tad better than average.
No Comments
American Politics and Elections was the perfect elective for freshman year, first semester. Interesting class, interesting and intelligent professor.
this guy knows nothing about design. he needs to stop talking about hair care products and start teaching.

Intelligent, humerous, fair, open minded, a good teacher.  Respectible and responsible as a person.  Knows what he's talking about.  RPI asks "Why not change the world?" He asks "Is that change for the better?"
Excellent professor, fairly laid back
Very ineffective professor who ends up being forced to give large curves, did not learn much, don't recommend. VERY stressful course
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lai is one of the worst professors. The grades are built off of 2 tests and the average score of 10 homework assignments. Each lecture is unorganized and lecture notes are just variables and symbols which are confusing and vague. Often he skips steps because he is rushing through the content creating more confusion and sounds like a rambling child.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Great lecture! Not very easy exam. But still get A.

Professor Lai is very clear in his teaching. He gives students plenty of opportunities during his lectures to ask clarifying questions, but this is often unnecessary as he reiterates important points.  His HW problems sometimes use his own notation, so go to lecture. My only complaint is his heavy weighting on 2 exams; 30% midterm and 40% final.

I took Dan's class for ENGR 2050 (Introduction to Engineering Design, or IED). Dan is one of the most caring professors I have met at RPI. IED is known as one of the scariest courses. Dan flipped that paradigm on its head. Rarely did I ever feel like the environment created by Dan was hostile, and overall, IED with him was a super fun experience.

Finishing up my 5th semester at RPI and Dan is the most impactful professors I have had here. Dan truly sees and treats his students as future engineers, which is reflected in how he lectures, assigns work, and grades students.

2nd class w/. Initially comes off arrogant but genuinely cares you are learning. Assignments, poorly communicated but open-ended. You can submit a lot or a little so long as you show improvementv. easy grader. This class is tangentially MTLE but the topics/skills are very useful. Highly recommend but LOTS of work (10-20 hr/wk) for quality hw.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Unclear assignments and lots of reading, lectures are not very helpful
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: His attempt to explain things in a simpler way makes the material more difficult to grasp. The book doesn't help either as the book goes not helpful material. The book chosen does a poor job preparing students for homework problems in the book. Students end up spending a lot of time in homework but not really learning. His class is also unorganized

He is really passionate about materials science and cares about teaching his students. He makes class interesting since he is so into what he is teaching.  He is definitely willing to meet with students to go over any confusing concepts.  Tests and quizzes are fair.  If you read the textbook, go to class, and study a good amount, you will do well.
Lewis was rude and unprofessional.  He has almost single handedly ruined this school for me.

You need to read the book for his class. What he says is interesting and fun, but not always entirely relevant. Each professor makes his own weekly quizzes with the exception of 4 cumulative quizzes. Prof. Lewis' quizzes are hard, so the cumulative quizzes shouldn't seem that bad.

Passionate teacher who would make a good lab assistant.  NOT a teacher.  He can't convey simple concepts to students because gets too excited and goes off on crazy table-standing tangents.  Also, hes kind of a jerk.
Quizzes are hard but good professor

Even though the subject material was not something I really cared for, Prof. Lewis presented it in a way that made me enjoy attending the class (even at 8am on Mondays.) Prof Lewis always put 110% into teaching this class. His passion for this material really shown in his lectures which is something one does not see often at RPI. Since I am not a M

Very good professor (at least for Mat. Sci).  Showed a genuine interest in his students' learning.  Knows his stuff and is good in getting the material in lectures.  Also, very helpful outside of class.  I'd recommend him highly to anyone taking this course.

Prof. Lewis is an excellent professor. You need to really know your stuff to do well in his class and on quizzes, but he makes the material interesting, and sincerely wants to help you understand things. Recommended for MatSci.

He is the only IEA prof. to use webCT and he has all of his powerpoint presentations online so you can look at them while you are doing homework. Me almost gives away hw points by giving you the answer to the hw questiosn, no other iea prof. does that. if you want to do well and learn, prof. lewis is a great teacher

His lectures would be 20 minutes at most since he knew we wouldn't pay attention if it was longer. His lectures never matched up with tests but tests were easy enough that this wasn't an issue. Course became online and asynchronous about halfway through the semester so it became even easier. Want a GPA booster, take with Larry Reid.
Goes on tangents, and doesn't really teach, but it's an easy psych class.

I'm sure Dr. Reid was great once, but I can't give him a good rating. He's very old, can't hear 90% of what students say, and you won't hear/understand like 50% of what he says. Class "discussions" are embarrassing as he goes on tangents then blames students for not talking. Content is interesting and if you put in any effort at all you'll get an A
If youre upset about InfoWars being removed from social media, you can attend this professors lectures instead.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: It is literally impossible to receive anything less than a 100 in his Abnormal Psych class. The first half of the semester are hour long lectures and the second half is retaking tests and researching . You retake the exact same test until you get everything right. He won't let you turn it in otherwise. You do a final presentation on any disorder.
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: My favorite professor I've ever had.  I would jump at any chance to take a course he teaches.  Not only is he extremely intelligent and knowledgeable, but he is also very wise and pretty funny too.  He demands respect of his students, which I highly admire.  Anyone who is on their phone during his lectures is really missing out.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Thoroughly entertaining lecturer and easy enough tests. Go to class, you'll learn something and its worth his antics alone.

Professor Reid is a very knowledgeable man and a great professor. He makes learning the subject of psychopharmacology really interesting. He's also a really nice guy as long as you're never late to his class!
Extremely intelligent.  Learned tons in his classes.  Be respectful; on time, come to class, don't text, or else he'll call you out.

Will supposedly randomly take attendance and drop everyone's grade a letter who's not there, but never did so all semester.  All tests are cumulative and contain some questions that were on previous tests, so its easy to redeem your grade after a poor start.  Lectures don't correlate to tests, but they are sometimes interesting.

He gives interesting lectures and his tests aren't particularly hard, but the curve is brutal. He's very reasonable with fixing grading errors on the tests as well. Don't fool around or be late to class or you will regret it.

This class was easy and very interesting. Is an easy A if you read the text, come to class and study the back test. Just don't fall asleep in class, for he will make fun of you. Also don't get caught doing other things in class....he can throw you out with no questions asked. He can come off as a little creepy at times but is easy going and funny.

I took his class in Spring 00. He gives A's easily and is easy going. For engineering students, you learn to be responsible adults when dealing with drugs. For psychology students, you are missing out! Other schools require their students to work much harder than Reid does which puts you at a disadvantage because you do not learn much.
Clear and knowledgeable but slightly pompous.
The best psychology professor in this school! Very interesitng lectures, attend them, do the reading and you will deffinetlly get an A.

keep to his rules and you will be fine. he occasionally takes attendence and might lower ur grade a full letter for one miss. the scalin is also diff than most classes an A starts at 92, and 69 and below is an F, believe offhand that a B starts at 85. also saw him throw a kid out of class for sleepin and he told him to drop the class.
Easy A... and one word: Obedient. :P
Borderline crazy, but an interesting class regardless, or maybe because of.  Don't disagree with him, he'll chew your head off for the entertainment of others.  Really easy A.
Interesting lectures.  Funny guy who knows alot.  Alot of reading is required for tests, but they aren't so hard as he gives you back tests.

the guy is incredibly interesting, class isn't a drag to go to.  not hard to get an A, but don't get caught sleeping or doing other stuff while in his class.  he threw a kid out of the course for doing other homework in his class.  but if you sit there and listen, the class is very interesting.

Back tests make things easy. Lectures are interesting and he knows when to cut it short. He can come off as an **** sometimes but he wears sweater vests so he can't be a real hardass. Overall the class is fairly easy and very worthwhile.

Good Class.  Interesting Stories.  The room is in Sage and it's a 6pm class.  Get's as hot as balls so it's really easy to fall asleep in.  So take the class get an easy A or B and catch up on your sleep.
EXCELLENT entertaining speaker, very clear, nothing is tricky in this class but tests do take studying.
One of the more entertaining lecturers on campus.  If you learn the basics you can very easily get a B from him.  One of the best profs at RPI.
He is one of the most interesting lecturors out there, loved the class.  Knows a lot and teaches it well
I don't know where you draw the line between strong-willed educator and hard-ass traditional academic goat is... but larry seems to tread this well. Boring, memorization, wierdo... whatever.
Lecture tends to get boring, but tests are predictable from a series of questions he gives you ahead of time.
Class is easy, but the guy is very condescending toward the students, always trying to push his code of morality on you which gets annoying.  Not hard to get an A though.
Very nice man.
Definitely one of the best profs. I have had in this school.

this guy is THE MAN. he is the best prof i have had yet. 80% of the tests are the practice questions and the rest are from the reading, so if you do practice tests you can get a B without a lot of work.  the class was fun too.

lectures were a waste-his tests were a scattershot collection of prior tests and practice questions he gives out. and a lot of the questions were based on the 4th ed of the book(we had the 5th!!!!!). nice guy, but class could use more integrity

Good guy and all... but make sure you NEVER look up during one of his tests or he'll say you were cheating and threten to throw you out of his class... happed to me... wasn't very happy at all with him from that point on.
No Comments

Prof. Reid is an excellent teacher, probably one of the best at RPI.  He certainly had a huge impact on me, in fact taking this class almost single handedly made me change my lifelong career goals.  Yeah, I really liked the class that much.

What a great class and a stand up professor. Do not cross him and go to class. He is old school and will embarrass you every chance you give him. Speak your mind and ask questions. One of the best classes I have ever taken. Great Professor, do the work.
good sense of humor

He is a very nice guy tbh, but not a good professor for CoCO. It is not a very hard course but it still contains some new materials that can not be understood easily. If you are good at self-teaching go ahead with his course but if you really want to learn all the stuffs well you had better aviod him.

Dr. lecoz is very chill but not a good lecturer. He always fails to explain all the materials with concise and probable words. He spends some time talking about things not related to course materials... But his tests are not so ruthless and he gave sample quizzes for us to study, except Quiz 3(many questions not mentioned in class appeared...)

His lectures are interesting most of the time and he really respects questions. He comes off as impossibly reasonable but he really is a reasonable guy. The homework can be hard, as you are expected to read the textbook, but just look ahead in his lectures. Quizzes and tests are straight-forward and he tells you what is on it in class.

Decent lecturer. Respects students that ask questions and politely correct him. Nice guy, but has a stubborn personality. When asking questions, you need to be very specific and assert yourself or he will dominate the conversation and answer all the questions you never asked. Little to no partial credit and no credit back on propagation errors

Great person and a cool guy. Knows his stuff. An old-school style of professor so the lectures aren't too exciting for this lower level class. Do every assignment, study the slides and back examples, and you'll do well.

Awesome class, right up until the final.  Everything before the final is open book/open notes, and he practically gives you the answers to the studios and parts of the take-home midterm.  And then the final is closed book, no crib sheet.  All you get is your calculator.

Lecoz is great. Digital is super easy because of his teaching style. Very thorough. Give's you the questions and the answers for the final, and the mid term is a project just like the labs... Go Lecoz!
Very thorough and speedy.  He gives you a note packet that you basically just follow through.  The studio sessions are very helpful.
Good Design Advisor...understanding and is willing to help anytime...
No Comments

Real good guy.  If you have a problem, he's there to help you.  If all profs were like him and Wozny, I'd go to class more often, and probably have a better opinion of RPI in general.

Knows what he's talking about, but sometimes does not want to be there.  The midterm is take home and he goes over a sample final the last few lectures.  Make sure you go to get your name on the attendance though.
he doesn't seem to like teaching very much. Likes to skip classes or get out of it as much as the students do.
One of the best Profs at RPI.  Took a boring class and made it as pleasing as possible.  If you get an opportunity take a class with him.

makes digital as interesting as it could possibly be... which is still boring but it's a good effort

I wish Dr. Liu taught more Nuke classes than just Phenom. She is so sweet and so nice and if you like the content of the class it will make the class genuinely something you look forward too. Never heard someone say something negative about her.

Dr. Liu is the sweetest lady lectures are so enjoyable. Sometimes it does feel like it goes forever but she provides breaks and snacks during exams. Overall very good professor, sucks that you will never see her after Nuclear Phenomena lol.

I really enjoyed Nuclear Phenomena and I really enjoyed having Professor Liu. Very kind, engaging, and approachable. Lecture slides are clear and accessible. Textbook is basically irrelevant. Do the back exams and the actual exams will be easy.
She's very nice, and the material and grading is not too difficult. she does have to leave class occasionally for business that she does outside of teaching

Professor Liu is the best professor I have ever had. Her accent is understandable and her course material is clear concise and easy to understand. All is available on LMS and test are super easy to prepare for, just do the back exams and you will be fine. The homework is a little challenging but she can in office hours or by email.

Prof. Liu is extremely nice, and she knows what she's talking about.  Her accent isn't particularly strong either.  Her Power Point lectures aren't the most helpful, but the book is very informative and useful.  Her tests are fair, and she lets you use a crib sheet on them.

The sweetest lady you'll ever meet at RPI. She cares so much about her students and truly wants to see them succeed. Homework 1/week, tests similar to backtests, few quizzes, lets you use laptops in class, and everything you need is on lms. her anonymous online question forum is excellent for asking questions when you've missed a class or two
She goes through the powerpoint in class, then elaborates on key points. The book is a good read and can be helpful if you get stuck on the homework
She's an OK teacher and is very helpful in office hours, but the book is completely superfluous.
She didn't use videos this time. And she is very concerned about our questions. It is a nice taught class.

She's nice and fair, but relied on LMS/WebCT more than I would have liked. I did NOT like how the video lectures were the primary lectures for learning, and the classroom was treated as a supplement. It should have been the other way around.
She is nice. She cares about students and is easy to be found.

She's basically worthless. Gives "on-class" questions, which she makes us sit there and work on for 40 minutes, then doesn't explain how to actually solve it. If this class wasn't mandatory, you could bet half the class wouldn't be here.
I liked her. She has a different style of teaching but once you know what to do and appreciate the knowledge she is sharing it can be very beneficial.

Probably one of the most usless professors at this school. I felt like I was back in not high school, but friggin middle school. anyone with a high school diploma could teach this class and probably better. I found myself constantly pointing out her errors. Bottom line  the students are better at the subject then the professor. Pathetic right?
Avoid
Blah blah blah… a lot of mumbling over nothing. What is she teaching anyway??

Bad bad bad

QPI is pretty tough, especially if you don't have diff eq experience. He is aware of his accent and it can be rough sometimes but he tries to help out students. The TA my year was really bad, so if you have a better TA it might work out better. The tests are fair but can be tough if you don't study.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Required attendance with in-class exercises making up a sizable chunk of the grade. He's fine. I feel less like I've learned physics and real world things and more like i've learned how to solve specific types of exam problems. :/
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: QP1 is a tough class regardless of your teacher, but you can't get much better than Lu. He's a great lecturer (getting used to his accent takes a week or so) and is clear about what he expects of you. Tests are hard but fair, and there's no curve so you have to do a lot of work. Read the textbook, go to class, and ask for help and you'll do fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I can hear from his words that his mind is full of knowledge, but he fail to consider the average level of students, it is very unwise to take his class directly after you took PHY 2 honer or PHY 2, if you want to do well, you better read some book or ask some experts about quantumor your life will be hard. also he did not give curves.

Few reviews so cramming into char limit. Super nice. Clear lectures w example problems. Gr8 @ explaining, ask questions! Makes tough QP material easier. HWs graded very tough by TA. Tests well-made & fair. Best quality is his enthusiasm. Loves what he does, smiles a lot, very inspirational. Pay attntn, bring pos attitude, & QP will b ur fav class.
If you get used to his accent, he's not bad at all.

He has huge accent which makes his lecture unclear and pointless. He never explained the details about how to solve the problem. The most used words by him are 'this' and 'that'. He never gives any clear and complete notes to students. He always assumed students can easily follow him and make the homework and exam too long and too hard.

Prof Lu is a harsh grader that expects perfection without specifying what perfection is. His accent makes him difficult to understand. He relates stories that are not really related to the subject. He doesn't take the course evaluations seriously.
Professor Lu is very nice and caring.

Prof. Lu was one of the most caring and helpful professors I've ever had. He starts every class by asking good morning and knows everyone's name and face. We cover a lot of complex material in a short period of time, but even so he strives to make sure that everyone gets the material.

Can be a little hard to understand at times, but is always clear and concise with advice. He is also very involved with student projects and as long as you put in the work, you get do well on projects.

I love Lupita!  She's always been extremely helpful in everything- advising, independent research, class material.  You can tell she really cares about her students and does her best to improve her courses to suit student needs.
OMG, are you kidding me?  Really, I am certain she doesn't understand half of what she is teaching.  Very narrow and everything gravitates to her research interest.  Not recommended.
Tough professor. You can really tell she cares about the students and is passionate about what she is doing. Dont take this class if you dont want to put in above and beyond effort
No Comments

Its too bad there's no language department anymore, but Lucien was fun while he was here.  The class was really easy, I came in at level 3, but still felt like I learned very little new that semester.  It was often difficult to stay awake through all the videos, and the quizzes were direct memorization, since he gave the answers the previous class.
I took his classes in Fall 00 & Spring 01. I still remember a very understanding, friendly and kind professor. He was very interested in his students. I wish I can keep in touch with him.

I really like Prof. Gerber. He really cares about his students and is always very willing to help, is more like your grand-father teaching you French. He is very knowledgeable and energetic. The only downside to his class is that he teaches through videos which sometimes can be a bit boring.

Class is extremely slow-paced.  Quizzes are based on memorizing minute details instead of understanding fundamentals of grammar.  Does not respond to e-mails, but is very willing to let work be handed in late.  Shows up late for class sometimes, which in and of itself isn't a huge offense, but acts disgusted if anyone else is late.
Best Professor I've had at RPI. Too bad RPI doesn't offer majors in french. If you work, you will learn so much from him. His classes, however, are not for people who have never taken french before.

Great professor if you make an effort to speak correctly and learn instead of being a loser who's afraid to pronounce words in front of their classmates.  I would have gotten an A if I turned in my final paper.  Whoops! :)

Amazing professor- does everything he can to make you understand, very enthusiastic and wants to help his students...a clear passion for his language- very impressive english vocabulary- my favorite professor at RPI-easy A, just read the text and memorize
Very energetic professor
He's good-humored and funny.  Youi probably won't get below a B if you do all the work.  Consider reading over the lesson before quizzes because their mostly memorization.
Monsieur Gerber is a very cool guy. He tries very hard to help you and makes the stuff very clear. Do the HW and you will be fine. Bon journee tout le monde! Bon journee monsieur!
Professor Gerber is the cutest little French guy. If you want to know about the language and the culture, this class is perfect. He is very helpful and very fair when it comes to grading.
Je n'aime pas les francais
Very knowledgable and enthusiastic

Like others said, he's very ambitious in what he wants to accomplish with the class, specifically the semester long design project. Absolutely great mentor, but a terrible teacher. His tests aren't too bad, study lecture notes online. He allows 1 full page of equations - NO diagrams for the tests. Daily activities and about 15 HW's from the book.

A really ambitious and enthusiastic teacher. Be prepared for a design project. His tests are not that bad, pay attention in class and review his lectures that are posted online. He is a fair teacher, just hard to reach through emails sometimes.

Castillo was on point with his lectures and made sure everyone understood him at all times. He made the material simple to understand and was always encouraging the students to participate in class. If you had questions you could always catch him right after class or even at his office. Overall it was a great course with a great professor.

Prof Castillo is one of the nicest professors I have ever met in the department. He DOES care about students and their performance unlike what many people claim. Best recipe to get an A in the class: review lecture notes, ask questions and start the hw early not the day before!

Has difficulty explaining topics clearly. Frequently diverts to other topics. Has online "lecture notes" that are largely ignored. Gives HW due the day OF the exam, provides no help on how to solve problems like those on the exam. TAs were just as useless. Substitute lecturers were better than him. Doesn't follow/use book. Nice guy, but can't teach

The lectures range from decent to awful.  The Book is AWESOME. Buy it & read it.  This class is pretty straightforward, but he is a big fan of putting things on the exams that have not been discussed in class or in the book.  HIGHLY RECOMMEND TAKING ENGR 2250 (Thermals and Fluids) at the same time as Fun Flight. Makes undiscussed questions doable.

I hate to say this, but he doesn't explain concepts in details. He is unorganized and his lecutres are useless. You have to rely on your textbooks for studying; Although it didn't help me much anyway either.

Class is utterly disorganized. last month of class seemed to be a waste other than to give him a soap box to talk about his research. never really received any grades back and therefor couldn't challenge final grades.  his heart and enthusiasm is in the right place but he shouldn't allowed to teach at the 4000 level.

I agree with the previous comments. He has good intentions but has a definite inability to present topics in a logical, encompassing, and concise manner. Confusion has accompanied every test, with him having to interrupt often with notes he should have mentioned on the exam itself. I purposely tried to avoid taking this class with him.

As a person, he is pleasant. However, as a professor, he is awful. He is highly unorganized and has difficulty explaining himself well. He will give you homework on certain topics that were not discussed in class. Exams are highly unpredictable...do not only prepare for what he tells you will be on them.. and can either be very easy or very hard.

Castillo sums up his teaching style best with this quote: "I wont go out of my way to make sure everyone understands the material."  He makes up random stuff in class, only cares about his research, and doesn't comprehend how much his students know or don't know.  If you can avoid this professor, do so at all costs.
he literally just makes things up and then when you make something up on a test you are wrong

I actually liked him. I thought he was funny and I thought he seemed to care about what he was teaching. I don't really pay attention in classes anyway so him being, or trying to be funny, at least kept me somewhat interested. Class was not that hard, but it looks like he may have changed his tests from years past.
awful prof. ended up giving A's to everyone but the class was bull. I never knew what was due and he gave us an impossible project.

Very difficult class but he mustve been told how bad he was teaching in the past since he made things very clear and the TA said his first test was easier than usual. Hes helpful in office hours but you have to go to class and pay good attention

Worst professor i've ever had in my life. Did not clairify the things he taught. Would accuse you of not paying attention when you went to office hours. Didnt clairfy anything in office hours by responding "i did that in class". His exams a haphazardly put together. Expects you to know everything he did not teach. Cares too much about his research.

Castillo is the worst professor ever.  He shows up only when he feels like it, seems not to care about students needs or thoughts at all.  Tests are absurd.  Required regrade and extra questions.  I was originally interested in thermal as a field, but castillo has made me HATE IT!
Never update his website. Take a long time to respond to students. Won't be in office hours at all. He sucks.
keep sighing in class....keep saying he is tired...he is such a lazy pig........

unorganized in general... very unclear in lectures and is not helpful when approached with questions
The things he explained in class, and the things we did on the homework weren't even close to being related.  The class was redicusly unorganized.
gives lots of homework

Caffeine addict.  Likes to talk about his ex-wife, his son, and his hot girlfriend.  He talks trash about Shirley Ann sometimes, but says we have to be careful, 'cause her office is right above our classroom.  Overall, a pretty crumby teacher.
boring n really sucks
bad professor, his class had the worst exam average out of all the classes. he doesn't teach well at all
Kicked a lot of ass.  Probably my favorite teacher in two years.
was easily sidetracked. didnt fully explain concepts. difficult to get help from. his one plus was his emthusiasm towards the course
wicked hard
This guy was hilarious.  Accents not a problem, it sounds awesome.  Great teacher too.
I had taken a few physics classes before I took his IEA class.  I realized he knew little to nothing and wound up explaining most of the course to the other students.
He gives too much homework and doesn't explain anything.
This guy is the real man.  He likes to talk about his ex-wife.  He is very fun although a little unorganized
enthusisatic but unorganized

he was cool..the energy was very exciting...buuuut very  very unorganized. my only gripe

He is the most energetic professor that I've ever had. It was nice to be in a class that professor wanted to teach and wanted us to learn, he was not just standing up in front of students and talking. But. . . he did talk REALLY fast in a carribean accent
She's a gem! I love her. She's a very sweet professor and very understanding
Really Good! Make sure every one learn basics on ML. I came from Engineering background and learn python from basics to code a ML model. Highly encourage to take the class
She was really sweet. I really enjoyed her!

Sometimes seems like she doesn't know what she's talking about when lecturing. Someone asks a question and she replies with "it's just like that" or "that's just how it works". There are 2 exams for this class and she did not give exam 1 back for us to review until after exam 2. Also uses Piazza instead of LMS so you don't get notis

He's amazingly knowledgeable of loads of useful information about software engineering but the problem is that he rambles. It's a real shame because often times I feel like I have no control of the conversation whatsoever and that I can't steer it where I want.

i was hoping for an easy humanity but this was something else.  hes good about extending deadlines but terrible at correcting quickly. he admitted the class was harder than he wanted so hopefully its better now. can be helpful but sometimes gets on long tangents.

I took History and culture of games....in my opinion, the easiest humanities class at RPI..it requires some work and occasional projects/papers, but it sure beats other classes like Minds and Machines...No tests, lecture is basically a napping session...some stuff was interesting...Lynch is pretty cool
Good professor...know's his stuff (and many interesting things beyond what he teaches in this class).  Labs are fairly easy and useful. 30 page paper isn't really that bad.
Dry, yet mildly informative lectures.  Seems more like a survey style of teaching.  Not very good about communication outside of class.  Overall a fairly average professor.

History and Culture of Games is the easiest humanities class ever.  If your a freshmen in first semester take this class.  There are no tests or quizzes.  The most you do is write small one page papers on games.  And the lectures, don't pay attention, do homework, because he doesn't care.

Very nice guy and knows his games.  The class is easy do teh assignments and your fine.  Class might change and have tests but in the fall 2005 semester there were none since it was the classes first semester.

Never responds to emails. Tried repeatedly to contact him about problems in class. Ended up with an F, which was my fault, but he never gave grades or talked to students EVER so I had no idea until I saw the grade. Rambles off topic constantly, teachers STRAIGHT from the book. Avoid.
Boring class lectures... no reason to go... just go to labs
very boring but very easy
Excellent Professor who definatly knows what he is talking about. He definatly could use a TA though, he doesnt seem to have enough time.
Needs to put more emphasis on making sure his 'technology' functions correctly in his classroom.
At least he's a libertarian...
Dr. McDermott is a great professor. Her lectures and in class activities are engaging and enjoyable. She gives a very manageable amount of homework, and the quizzes are not too difficult.

This is one of the best types of classes, you will learn so much but as long as you put in basic effort you will never be stressed about this class. She makes lectures focus on real-world applications of knowledge to better prepare you for the business world. Definitely recommend taking this class even if it is just an elective!

MGMT 1100 is one of the hardest classes in the business program in my opinion if you are taking it with Dr. McDermott. There are three 'quizzes' that are 50 questions each it really is an exam. There are homework's she doesn't tell you about and they just appear. Good luck, and show up to class. Whole letter grade gone if you don't.

Very kind and clear professor, class is very easy since it is into to managment so all you have to do is show up and do minimal work. Attendance is required but I was very active in class and asked her a lot of questions so even though I skipped half the classes she didnt penalize me.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: We would watch prerecorded lectures before class and then she would elaborate in class and we would have activities relevant to what we learn. As long as you show up and put in the effort you'll be fine. She's really caring and gives good advice so you can always go to her.

AWESOME. Highly recommend. This class does have a lot of work but she tells you exactly what she is looking for. She also takes into account peer evaluations for group projects (most professors don't) If you do the work you will get an A no problem. She'll even check over your cover letter and resume if you ask her
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: I took her class last semester. She teaches well, provides useful materials, and lets you learn with real world cases. A lot of work but you learn a lot. A lot of team work and presentations but not very hard if you try, but they do take a lot of time. Study for the tests, and you will do good. Definitely recommend her for Intro to Management.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Kinda boring. Her idea of "fun" is giving us 3 riddles on Halloween and taking 20 minutes to go buy a breakfast sandwich and document the process.  Presentations and/or group write ups every week, and huge (50-90 pages) paper at the end of the semester. Overall, eh. A lot of work.
If you take Intro to Management at any point, take with her.
A lot of work including a 50 page paper and presentations every week.
No Comments

The material is pretty stupid, and you'll feel like you're in high school again. Group discussions are on such simple topics that it's painful to raise your hand to contribute, unless of course you're a dumb jock and need constant validation that you're not a complete moron.

She showed up to none of our exams when half the question had typos and the proctor was an art student (no hate on art just new nothing ab Econ). You have to show up to class because she does not share in class notes but when you do show up 90% of time she is reading off of slides made by the textbook company. Not a real one.
really bad
This lesson wasn't that difficult, but it was extremely mood-ruining.
The exam is very trick nobody want to get a good（96） grade unless you are genius
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She purposely makes the exams hard and words the multiple choice questions to trick students even if you studied and understand the concepts. She's a very hard grader on the free response homework assignments. The class slides are useless and you must be in class to take notes everyday. DO NOT pick her as a prof unless you want to tank your GPA!
I didn't wear a seatbelt on the drive to her class.

She doesn't allow students to take pictures of her lecture notes, nor does she upload them for the class. When I asked her for some guidance on preparing for the test, she simply told me to "read the book," which is actually just a very brief PowerPoint presentation.
So hard to pass.
Don't pick this professor.

Also, this professor doesn't care about your grade, she lets the TA do everything for her, if you go ask her about grading issues, she lets you bother the TA instead. In addition, I would say I would rather watch a 10-minute YouTube video instead of watching her entire lecture.

I've learned a lesson from her: Do not trust your professor or lecture that we don't have a quiz or test in the upcoming class just because they didn't announce it in the previous class. If you take this professor's class, remember to read the syllabus because she won't announce anything in the class and didn't include anything in the lecture note
Not a good teacher, rushes the lectures, hardly any back exams, difficult tests. Would not recommend it. Material was very fun tho, but again not a good professor.

Sometimes nice and makes jokes, sometimes rude af. Your grade basically depends on how she is feeling at that moment. Only thing I can say as a pro is that she never singled anyone in my class out. Participation is mandatory... sometimes when she feels like it. She is also very against taking pictures of notes. Overall rating: Yikes.
She doesn't teach, we self-learned the whole semester. Tough grader, no accommodation for exams
Avoid this professor for ur grade and future

Overall well taught class. Prof. Mahmoudi would always be prepared and was pretty engaging during most lectures. Generally let the class out early for 1-1 questions. Does expect participation. A lot of time ahead given for HWs and the presentation for which is given a lot of freedom in when you present and what you want to present about.

Dr. Mahmoudi can be lively & lovely in class, but blase on other days. While she clearly has a passion for Econ, she only occasionally explores material outside the PowerPoint lectures, perhaps because of RPI's perceived underinvestment in HASS disciplines. Strict to the syllabus, but still accommodating, she's a nice member of faculty.
Terrible teacher, difficult exam, just stay away from this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She always says that things are extremely easy and when the class average is a 50% she gets confused as to how we could do so terribly without considering the fact that she may be an awful professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She's friendly, I had her twice, spring 2021 for international macro, and fall 2021 for macroeconomics masters level. both classes were online, lots of examples for the exams in the notes, and she goes over what you need to know, she curves the grades, honestly, you can't fail unless you're an idiot, she cares about all her students

RPI teacher in Albany class. Absolute the horrible professor I've ever seen. homework does not make any sense and grade is very bad for the whole class. No connections with students and zoom lectures are bored. I don't think the RPI professor all like this but she really gives me a bad experience.

This professor needs to not teach this class anymore. Reads effectively word for word from a graduate level FEM textbook without explaining the concepts any further. You can ask any student in this class, and they would say the only time they actually learn anything is from the practicum sessions. He seems nice but he should not be teaching.

Not engaging during class, no lecture slides, go to his office hours if you want help although I never did. Two exams totaling 60% of your grade. This class would be okay if all of the content wasn't theory, practicum was good though. They should have used real world application of FEM more. 95% of students stopped going to lecture after day 2.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: falls asleep during lecture. changed notion for everything so you cant even read a textbook when his lectures fail you. lecture notes are riddled with errors; had 86 revisions in the first week of classes alone.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
He is not an evil man. He is just an older professor who is used to lecturing to grad students. If you go to his office hours he does a great job explaining the problems and concepts.

HOWEVER
his lectures this semester have been ROUGH. He basically just reads a textbook. They are trying something new this year, and most likely will fix in future
He just read his 200-page note that changed 14 times in a month

For FEM, lecture notes consist of summarized notes from textbook which are basically just all theory and very hard to understand. Homework questions are then given with limited examples to pull from, and expected to derive the needed equations based on weird notation and expressions given in notes. Would not take again after just three weeks.

The lectures are unhelpful and leave you more confused than when you walk in. Said lectures consist of reading a glorified parallel version of the textbook, no examples, extreme amounts of poorly explained notation and no written work. Dictionary definition of a LECTURER.

FOCS is not an easy course, and Malik does not go out of his way to make it easy. He does however go out of his way to: Make lectures entertaining, make the textbook accessible, give you endless practice problems, and always answers on Piazza. Out of all the CS professors I've had in my time at RPI, Malik is one of a kind. Take his class.

Malik is the best professor I have ever had. I constantly wish he teaches every course I take. Learning under him is the best part of RPI and should be front and center on the website. His explanations, while passionate, leave no room of confusion or doubt. His calling is teaching, and he does it better than everyone else. I love him! 100/10

One of the best professors I have ever had the pleasure of learning from. He is the type of professor where tests mean everything. Just DO NOT use AI, you'll be fine. Rely on TAs and keep a good connection with the professor, as his office hours were SUPER helpful. If you ever get the chance to take this class with Malik, I HIGHLY recommend it

By far the best professor i've had. Fantastic, well prepared lectures. New topics were explained very clearly, and even topics I have already learned were still exciting to hear about from his perspective. Pay attention and quizzes and the final are easy. Homeworks are tricky but helpful.

Great professor, if you take his class YOU WILL LEARN! However that comes at the cost of him making his class HARD, average of the exams was 60% in the beginning, which went "up" latter on. However at the end he did do quite a big grade curve which no one expected, so he does care about the students. 90% of our grade made up by exams btw

This was not a light course, but you'll truly learn ML. You really need to pay attention and know your math.

With that said, he constantly gives pop quizzes and doesn't offer any make-ups whatsoever. He also gave us a final for the first time in years, which was much more difficult than the back exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Engaging lecturer and definitely knows his stuff. Only two complaints were that you have to go his OH to see your graded exam and he switched the duration of the final exam from 3 hours to 2 hours the morning of the exam without letting anyone know.

I don't want to judge his skill, but he is very disrespectful to students. He was unhappy during the last class because 50% chose not to participate in the final exam. However, he had said that if you choose to go home early and get a 70% final, that's fair. He should reflect on why so many people are unwilling to take the exam instead of sulking.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Magdon has very clear and productive lectures. Although the class has 3 Exams, 1 Midterm, and a Final, it gives you room to get lower scores on an Exam or two. Above all the professor cares about growth in performance, so if you get above a 90 on the final you're most likely to get an A in the class.
Very animated. Knows his stuff well and is pretty great all around.
In essence, what you've heard is true. Absolutely brutal grading and difficulty, but excellent lecturer-- you *will* learn FoCS.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Lectures are very engaging which is pretty rare, only time I've seen people show up to class when the lectures are recorded. The tests require studying but back exams are provided and they are pretty similar to the tests. Wrote the book himself so it's very relevant to the class. Difficult course but good professor.
Tough grader. He forwards most questions to the TAs instead of answering them himself. He might raise the A line again depending on overall performance — I heard that last year his A cutoff was 96.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Professor Malik made me excited to attend each lecture. He cares that students learn and frequently pauses the lecture briefly so that everyone can try to finish the calculation on their own and make sure they understand it. I love his chalk-on-blackboard style which is so much better paced and engaging than Powerpoint slides.
My pronouns are he, not him. Because I'll never be him.

One of the most amazing professors at RPI, his lectures are so enthusiastic and he knows what he is talking about.

He gives pep talks in class about how to do well in life and for our future, he really CARES about his students.

Professor Malik is an enthusiastic man with passion when teaching. I love his pre-recorded lecture as it teaches me so much and I can review things I don't understand immediately. The quizzes and tests are not that hard tbh; if you study hard on the homework you will get a good grade.

Prof. Malik teaches amazing lectures. You can feel his passion even it's on the screen. Personally, FOCS is a kinda easy class for me. The first half-semester is pretty easy and the second half is just a little challenging, especially about TM. The quizzes and the midterm are really easy except the final is a little hard.

Very knowledge teacher, he is trying very hard to make this hard course interesting. Feels rewarding if you do your work but its really really hard. You will learn a lot. Don't drop the course, I know you want to.

Professor Malik is a brilliant Professor, incredibly smart guy. The lectures are crystal clear and the concepts presented with no logical gaps and theory from the ground up. But when you ask Malik questions, he tries to stop the conversation instead of expand on them and it stifles more curious students who would benefit from conversation with him.
Great lectures and be prepared for hard tests
Exams are impossible and no curve despite a D- average
Really great lectures, super helpful and passionate, homeworks were hard but graded easy
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures--Graded by few things--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Good

He's definitely got the enthusiasm and he's pretty good at explaining certain concepts, but it's harder to understand his explanations for the harder concepts and he just throws really hard problems at you and expects you to not seek external help to solve those problems. I think he should provide more examples of where the concepts can be applied.

Malik is my favorite professor at RPI. The enthusiasm that he brought to FOCS despite it being online made me excited to attend the class every day. I genuinely cannot express how much of a pleasure it was to take a class taught by him. I highly, HIGHLY recommend taking FOCS or Machine Learning with him specifically. Those who don't are missing out

Professor Ismail is impressive. He gives amazing lectures and you can actually learn a lot from his lectures. His exams are kind of skills based but as long as you put effort in his homework, you should be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Phenomenal professor. Makes you really work to get the grade you want - but with lectures as engaging as he offers, if you put in the effort, you'll get a lot out of the class. I know I did.
Absolutely fantastic. FOCS is not an easy course under him, but you feel very rewarded when you do well. He clearly cares and puts effort into his teaching to make the content interesting.
don't cheat.

His lectures are decent, but the tests are kind of bad. It was basically a math class and a ton of points came from multiple choice questions that didn't have any partial credit. That being said, if you put in more work, it would probably be a solid choice.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Very good lecturer, and YOU WILL LEARN. He doesn't make it easy, though. In fact, he makes it hard. You'll really have to work for a decent grade.

Honestly, one of the best professors I've ever had at RPI. I have yet to see a professor as passionate as Professor Malik about the material he teaches. While this class will definitely make you work for the grade you get, it is a phenomenal learning experience and I hope to have Malik as a professor again.

His class was one of my favorites. His lectures are very specific and you can really tell he wants you to learn. If you're having trouble he is there for you and will make sure you leave happy. If you put in the work you will definitely see the fruits of your labor as he is a great professor. Also there is extra credit if you just go to class!

I took FOCS with Professor Malik, and he is extremely knowledgeable. He's very patient with students who don't understand and will take his time to walk through problems for them. He also uses easier problems as an example to help students understand the more difficult ones better. He is by far one of my favorite professors at RPI!

Dr. Malik is so funny, engaging, and passionate. When you ask a question, he makes sure to turn around and check that you're following. His quizzes are fair in my opinion, most questions are similar to back quizzes and all the homework assignments and such are relevant. Not to mention, he wrote his own textbook which he gives for free. Love him!
Good Prof

Grading scheme is awful and does not promote "trying." Exams are multiple choice with work being required, but no partial credit for this work. Homeworks are long and worth little. Your entire grade is pretty much determined by your answer on the few "hard" (non-gimmie) questions on each test. This has been my absolute worst experience at RPI.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Fantastic lecturer, one of the best I've ever seen. He has super high expectations, the class will be difficult. But you will learn a huge amount of material that is all very useful in CS. Malik is super intelligent and if you listen to him you will learn more in his off comments than in some other entire classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: One of the smartest professors in CS. Very challenging course and homework. It's not easy to understand everything, but at least I'll always remember some basic concepts in machine learning that would be very helpful if I'll use them one day.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Inspirational--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Great guy, engaging lectures. Course is paced well, but a bit challenging.
TOUGH GRADER... NOT RESPECTFUL FOR STUDENTS

One of the best professors at RPI. He is a very good lecturer and is clear and easy to understand. His courses are not the easiest, but very much worth it. Very knowledgeable in his research field and is a funny guy.
The hardest course in RPI I've ever experienced. Got an A, which soaked up all my spare time last semester.
Mind-crushingly difficult professor. Dauntingly intelligent. Sometimes expects too much of students who learn slower than others.
Malik Magdon Ismail's CSCI 4100, Machine Learning, is by far the best course I have ever taken. It was an eye-opening experience, hard as hell, and enjoyable to take.
It's tough, but you can learn a lot from this course. Prepare yourself for the peculiar discrete math world.
knows what he's talking about
Excellent professor, but merciless in his homeworks. Helped write the book for his Machine Learning class.
His method of teaching is very effective. He is overall a good teacher.
Probably my most influential prof, actually challenges students. Uses real math in compsci courses which many profs in compsci don't. Very smart insanely good memory.
Went from teaching us cin and cout to file input, arrays, and sort in a week.  Definitely not a CS1 professor.

I am a CS who took CS1 with him. I ended up with a 106% grade in the class. For homework you choose a level of difficulty 1-5 and if you complete the level that you have choosen then you get that level*10 number of points. Most of the level 5s  required previous CS experience. Beware of Word Ladders. Grades were given on a full/half/none basis.

A note to anyone who reads his rating from here on out- he is not going to discuss how to solve all of the homework problems he gives you. But there is this funny aspect of Computer Science where the question is not what you know but what you can figure out. Thus, he is doing what he should. Get used to it.

Homework assignments were either very easy, or very difficult (or impossible; Malik assigned problems that have yet to be completely solved [NP problems]).  Lecture was useful, Lab was not.  Tests aren't bad if you know the material.  Known to confuse other professors on campus with his intellect.

Homework projects ranged from being too easy to absurdly hard. Ways to solve harder project questions were NOT discussed in lecture. Lectures were  very repetitive and downright useless by the end of the semester. Tests were fairly easy overall. I succeeded in the class (A-) by reading the book and Google searching the material for more examples.

Class was very difficult especially if you don't know programming before taking this course. Labs were easy and Projects not bad. Lots of opportunity for bonus points, but at some points I felt as though we were programming Google. Not a good teacher for a low level course, but he does know his stuff.
