tough for an intro class, but if you apply yourself and think about the projects it's not as bad as some will say. he tests you with the projects and labs, as a result exams (provided you did the projects and labs) are much simpler. no half credit but bonus points galore, which helps make up for it. kept me entertained, funny guy, cool accent.
Class wasnt that hard, Pleanty of bonus points on every thing, it wasn't an easy A but atleast we learned something
wow, too hard of a class. I wish I knew how to program before I took this class...
Teaches way too fast...he doesn't teach in sync with the projects/labs. Class is funny though....

He doesn't quite know how to teach Comp Sci 1; he flies through the material and often what he's teaching doesn't sync up with the assignments he gives us (he teaches us how to do something after we have to do it). His grading policies are way too harsh for CS1: any mistake at all, no matter how minor, means half points. He's HILARIOUS though.

terrible professor. he is going way too fast and deep for comp sci 1. i have heard that this course was easy in the past. we passed comp sci 2 material within two weeks of class. his grading system is HORRIBLE. full, 1/2 or no credit... i fyou make one simple mistake you get HALF of the answer wrong!! doesn't teach most of the material on his exams

He treats the class like it were DSA which means really really hard but it's a lot better than the last csci 100 professor where the students didn't learn anything. I recommend Malik since he's a really good teacher.
too hard for just an intro to comp sci and c++

This is a very hard course, but keep up with all the practice problems and you should do fine.  Malik is an interesting person, I love it when he finishes explaining something and says "BOOM".  But yeah, the course is kinda hard.
if you can keep up with he's a good professor otherwise you're screwed
This is one person who can lecture and lecture and lecture, but you don't get sick of listening.  Was extremely clear; I could always follow him.
Good Lecturer but gives us the answers.  That's how learn.  I mean I'm not going to go to your office hours for every answer on the Final question Sheet.
Good lecturer, very tough grader. Not much of an accent.

Excellent lecturer. Very hard grading, but has available pool of test problems. Gave decent curve for the course grade, but it was certainly needed. One time, took off 7/50 points on project for not having something that wasn't asked for.

Abysmal professor. Projects were ludicrous, everyone failed the midterm. 1 of my friends was 1 of 4 people he gaves As to, and only because he memorized all the answers from the pool of final exam questions. Most people couldn't do them at home (incl. me)
It was all a game ! a very useful game.
He is able to explain the material so that i can have an understanding of what is going on but then he expects expertise almost immediately after
Impossibly hard course.  Malik obviously understands the material very well, but can't understand how to measure the difficulty of his own problems.
I've never considered killing myself, before taking this class.
Amazing professor, one of the best at RPI, and the best Comp Sci professor I've had to date.
Good Teacher, one of the best here.
Don't regret having him.  He is energetic and funny, not bad on grading.
Very good lecturer. HIs lectures are phun

Taking MATH 4090 from him online. He doesn't reply to student emails. None of my classmates know about their grades 3 months into the semester and no feedback on assignment. Homework expects you to apply definitions, which he doesn't teach you in lectures. This class is also latex heavy but he doesn't teach how to use latex either.

Doesn't share lecture recordings, answer emails or give back any grades whatsoever. Nobody knows how they're doing in the class at this point. He's a nice guy and cares about the topic, but an awful professor. Wish he would use a textbook because his teaching is incomprehensible. (He's also my advisor and has never, in 3 years, answered an email)
He Speaks of his notes rather than showing the student how to complete the work. the TA help more than him.

Professor McLaughlin is super passionate about math and truly cares about his students. Homework optional (test questions pulled from HW), quizzes are extra credit (can only help you), notes given in class. Not hard to do well if you go through the problems and see him for help. Also, get to know him in office hours. He is a great guy all around.

Prof. McLaughlin loves math; his lectures, lecture notes, and textbook are all filled with intricate math theory. If you are more interested in the practitioner's perspective, it can be hard to decipher the often unnecessarily complex mathematical justifications. His tests are completely based on the worksheets, so it's easy A.

One of the best professors at RPI. Lectures are fantastic and McLaughlin is charming. Even if you don't go to lectures, you can read his thorough and easily understood lecture notes that he sells for $25 at Market Block Bookstore (he claims that he usually doesn't profit off of them). He is very caring about his students. His class was a privilege.

I like to call him "Grandpa Calculus." His lectures are thought-provoking, and they often lead to discussions which help his students to understand the material. I think this name suits him because he is a great calculus teacher, whom I feel truly cares about his students. He doesn't want you to just know things, but he encourages you to think!
Mclaughlin seriously cares about his students. Make an effort to go to class, study, ask questions, and visit him in office hours. He wants you to pass, and it's easy to do so.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Very intelligent Mathematician, and good professor.  His notation threw me off my first semester freshman year in Calc II, and I quickly found that I learned the material better on my own simply reading his excellent provided lecture notes.  Go to class for the first while, then you can stop going if you read the notes and do the worksheets.

If you like tests that do not resemble the backtests and that consist of topics that aren't covered in lecture, then you'll probably enjoy this course. Although he tries to be helpful, he covers almost none of the material that will be on the test, in lecture. I would recommend against taking MultiVar with MacLaughlin. Save yourself; take Schmidt.

Every practice exam question provided by McLaughlin in my semester had no answer. He would tell you "come to lectures to get it" but it was never there. If you miss the lectures, you will never find his class note online. Also his class is not very friendly to foreign students.
His lectures are confusing sometimes. Mainly because he talks about theories a lot. The tests are based on homework and textbook  questions. Go to office hours.
Takes test and final exam problems straight from his worksheets  and example problems in his lecture notes. Doesn't use an actual textbook and you buy his lecture notes instead.

McLaughlin is a very smart man, but not the best prof. I found that his course notes were excellent to learn from, so I didn't go to many lectures. Quizzes are very easy, and he gives a ton of partial credit on exams. This course shouldn't be a problem if you study. Do the worksheets, as the test questions are exact copies from the worksheets.

Some dislike the level of mathematical rigor that Harry employs. I consider my use of mathematics more practical than artful, so this aspect of his class was not initially enjoyable to me. However, he is a fantastic teacher and has taken my understanding of mathematics to another level. Highly recommend. (P.S. there is a steep learning curve)

Complete theory, poor explanations, and absolutely no examples in class. His exams are very easy but I had already taking Multivar when I went into his class, so I could ignore most of his confusing notation. Be prepared to teach yourself Calculus.

Goes into WAY more detail than anyone who isnt a math major needs. Uses his own textbook instead of the one every other prof uses, and his is practically useless.  He also randomly changed the test format halfway through the semester, making half of it no partial credit.  uses formal notation, and never explains any of it, just expects you to know.

I attended every lecture, took diligent notes and did all of the homework assignments. Got 100% average on the skills quizzes and a 60% on the exams. The exams are all problems you have seen before but I have only meet people who were successful in his class by memorizing all of the problems presented in homework and class work.

I had Mclaughlin for Calc II (Math 1020). The course consists of 4 exams, skills quizzes, and a final. The exams are not difficult; only 4 or 5 of the 6 questions per test are graded (generously, I might add). I only went to recitation to collect quizzes andor exams. The recitations lagged behind lectures in terms of content. Do the worksheets  A

Harry is an inspiration. He is the embodiment of pure commitment to what he teaches. Of course, taking Analysis II with him has a much different flavor than Analysis with Kovacic. That being said, I thoroughly enjoyed both courses. Harry structured the course in a way such that he felt like more of a colleague than a lecturer, which was nice.

He's a good professor for Math majors who want to know every detail and beyond what we're supposed to learn for Multivar Calc & Linear Algebra.  However, for any other major who just wants to pass and move on, he says a lot of unnecessary stuff that makes it all confusing, especially for Linear Algebra.  He's a super nice guy though.

This instructor writes his own lecture notes which he goes over and talks about during lectures. At first, they seemed unfamiliar but I come realize that I took away so much more from his notes and lectures than any other texts I've used for any class. I would recomend this course to those who seek a 'higher' understanding of mathematics.

Awful. Did not use the textbook most of us already had (since its the same text for Calc I) and most of us would need later (for MultiVar). Instead he told all of us to *buy his notes*! If you're looking to just pass Calc II instead of actually LEARNING anything from it, go ahead. But if you want to actually know the material, stay away.
Professor McLaughlin is the most experienced lecturer and kindest professor at RPI. Being part of his lecture has been a privilege.
Wants you to succeed, but is so smart he is unable to communicate effectively with his students
Very steep curve on all tests, designed to help people get 100%.  Quizzes are extra credit and lectures are clear and worthwhile.
Professor McLaughlin is by far the best professor I have had at RPI.

McLaughlin is a really nice guy and tries hard to make his students do well. I really wasn't a fan of his teaching approach, though. He skips the theory and jumps right to examples because he thinks that's a better way to learn the theory. Only 4 out of 6 test questions are graded, so tests aren't bad.

Not a very comprehensive teacher. His tests are supposedly easy but not when his lectures are like decoding the Rosetta Stone. His lectures have absolutely no transition. The hieroglyphics he writes during lecture are seen as so because he nose dives into topics. His classes are based off of doing problems and not the theory of the math.

McLaughlin is undeniably one of the esier A's to get at RPI. Go to recitation and his office hours and memorize all of the worksheet problems, then you will get an A in the couse, he uses the same problems. He's also a great guy to talk to, especially if you have a few minutes to hear from an experienced guy on pretty much any subject.
Tests are very simple. It's easy to get 100 as long as you have a decent grasp of the material. Harry is friendly and enthusiastic about the material.
Great teacher gives you the lecture before hand so you can read up on your stuff

I liked him as a professor, you could tell he really cared. He has examples in his lectures and sends out lecture notes that are really helpful and clear and have loads of examples. Homework in this class is optional. Your grade is entirely your test scores. Tests were set up so you answer 6 questions and your best 4 make up your grade.
Had him for calc I and II one of my favorite proffs of all time good guy words things kinda complicated but tests are identical to inclass problems/worksheets so do them

Dont go to lecture, the only way you will be able to comprehend what he is saying is if you have a phd in math.  Tests are really easy compared to what he teaches, on top of that he is an easy grader.  I would take calc II with this professor, just dont bother going to class.
He wrote his own lecture notes, I still kept them in my mailbox because they're so helpful

It depends on what kind of students you are, but unless you are an unthinking, blind-memorizing type, you won't like this professor. He expects you to memorize every theorem he taught in his class word for word. He is not a true mathematician and he would excell at it if and only if he were a biology professor.

Professor McLaughlin is a very good professor.  He is very helpful and will answer all questions in class.  His lectures could be a bit complicated and confusing, but PDF lecture notes clear everything up.  Exams are comprised of questions from lecture notes with different or exactly the same numbers/solutions.  Never used the text book once.
He is a genius in math and sometimes goes over concepts way over your head. He is extremely fair on grading and allows the final to be your final grade if you do very well.
Best Professor I've had yet.
Harry delivers a great calculus curriculum. It isn't easy but it'll prepare you for later classes, which an easy calc class won't necessarily. Go to class!

Harry knows what he talking about. You as a student might have an issue following it, but Harry tries real hard to interact with the class and have the class grasp the material. If you are having trouble stop by his office. He is a really nice guy who love mathematics. If you are a math major take all your courses with him. If not, go to Schmidt...

Excellent professor. He sets up the course so that you pretty much get the highest grade possible. Really passionate about calculus. I took Calc I in high school and he taught me the same stuff from different angles. This I really enjoyed course from him.

Harry is the man! He has a real passion for mathematics and teaches the class in a unique fashion. For those that have taken Calculus already, Harry provides a new spin from a geometry point of view. I hate geometry, but he makes it interesting. His exams are straight forward and he e-mails detailed lecture notes for studying.Might be confusing tho

Real nice guy. Discrete isn't the best class in the world. Gives pretty good test references, and his tests have a nice grading scheme. If you don't do well in this class it's because you aren't putting the work in.
nicest guy ever.  the class is hard and hes very persistent on making you figure everything out but he lets you know what will be on the test and grades pretty easy.
Very good
No Comments

This is my second course with Harry and he met every expectation I could ever have. Harry is not only one of the brightest guys on campus, he is also one of the most effective teachers I have ever seen. His style is unique, intriguing, and most of all it will grab your attention. Highly recommended!

He waxes a love for mathematics that is really hard to find.  The work is nowhere near easy, but he makes you want to learn the material.  Taking Fund. of Math. in preparation isn't crucial, but I'd recommend it.  Harry's one of the most interesting, eloquent, and capable teachers I've ever had.

Best profesor I have met at RPI. Truly an amazing teacher and an extremely interesting person. Take his class if you have the remote opportunity, and definitely DO NOT miss going to the office hours, you'll get more out of them than just a good grade. The work is hard but do-able.

Honestly the best course I have taken in my time in college. Harry has an amazing teaching style and allows you to discover the answers on your own which really makes it stick. You could be tired entering the class and you'll leave it awake and energized. If you have a chance take a course with him.

I must admit that having Harry for Calc 1 was quite difficult. Having never taken any calculus before, he jumps directly into it on the first day. However, he is always willing to help, is a very nice guy, and has very fair grading schemes.
No Comments
He's truly a great professor! He really knows his stuff, keeps class interesting, and knows how to communicate difficult concepts to others. Great grading methods too =D.

I had a class with Harry last year. He was great. Encouraged developing objective and creative way of thinking. Put emphasis on understanding of material, not grades, and was available for help. Without a doubt, one of the best profs in this hell-hole.
Harry is the best.
This guy is the man.  He is the best math professor I have ever had, but don't take a classs with him if you don't care about the subject.

Dr. McLaughlin is by far one of the best professors in the Math Department.  He expects you to put in a lot of work, but you will end up learning a lot more because of it.  He has the best grading scheme ever and is always ready to offer help.

Excellent professor, as long as you like math. He makes the learning experience very interactive. The course is a nice break from the normal process of going to class and falling asleep. He gives good feedback as well...
on numerous occasions has reffered to math as an artform.  and when asked how he got to an answer responded with because smarter people before us figured it out and we just accept it.
Don't sign up for him unless you're a total math wiz and have taken Calc AB/BC before.  He teaches randomly and will put you in Chapter 9 in the third week of class.
He was Great!!

An odd character, but a good teacher. Sticks to his word. Be prepared to learn. Very informative and ran the course well. Understood that Multivar and Matrix Alg are two courses combined, and taught accordingly.
He's a nice person. I took all the courses he taught and get A in every course. If u can get used to learn everything by yourself, he's a great Prof for u. BTW, he's the only Prof who teaches CHD.
Smart man, still a terrible class and so disorganized. Avoid.
Terrible Prof!!

I had him for both Computer Hardware Design and Advanced Computer hardware design. His course is very out of date so his lectures are useless but I liked the course. He rambles through lectures and there is almost nothing worth writing down.

He knows his stuff. The course itself requires many skills to be successful. You need to think beyond what he writes down or says. It is not suppose to be an easy course. It should require you to ponder in deep thought. He is fair.

Definitely agree with all other raters...AVOID HIM AT ALL COST... but in fact he's the only one who teaches the computer hardware design and advanced computer hardware design. He will NOT hand out notes and he will just go through a little bit of things you will need in class. The other stuffs you will have to look it up online.
Extra hard grading policy, no help where it was really needed.

Besides the fact that he is old, mumbles a lot, scribbles at times, and chuckles to himself all the time... his notes start nowehere and go nowehere, his homeworks make no sense, and I'm in week 14 out of 15 and we're having our first test.  Washed up.

Abysmal.  4 weeks into class and we've only learned some equations which were learned in prerequisite classes.  Misses class regularly for research, leaving the TA to do software tutorials.  No class notes provided, no website, no course schedule, no direction to the class.  He takes material you've already learned and makes it seem impossible.

TERRIBLE PROFESSOR.  AVOID HIM AT ALL COSTS, HE IS EXTREMELY CONCEITED AND LOVES TO HEAR HIMSELF TALK.  YOU WON'T LEARN ANYTHING.  HE SHOULD BE FIRED BUT IS STILL AROUND BECAUSE HE GOT HIS TENURE YEARS AGO.

He is not very helpful when I went to him numerous times about the course work. The were only a couple of homework assignments, a midterm, and 2 projects. The homework was straight forward from the class notes. The projects took a huge amount of time but mainly due to the learning curve of the software package. Plan to spend many hours in the lab.

Prof. McDonald's lecutres are torture...it's the worst punishment ever. This man has NO communication skills..absolute worst class you could ever take...I have not learned one thing from this man...i'd rather have my eyelide hairs pulled out ONE BY ONE than sit thru another one of his lectures.
most egoistic a prf can get

CHD is definitely one of my favorite classes here.. McDonald seems to get negative ratings, but he is one of my favorite professors here.  CHD was not difficult, especially with no tests and class material only being an add-on to the labs.  Labs are time consuming but so is the average class here...
I thought he was great.  Oh well.

This guy is the absolute worst professor i've had in my undergrad studies. All he talks about is how he his research is doing this and that and blah blah but never teaches about the course. A rock could teach better then him. Visit him during office hrs.

He gets a bad rap unfortunately because he's conservative and old-fashioned.  His knowledge and teaching is spot on, and mixes hands on projects with classroom lecture.  A++++ if you get a chance take CHD and ACHD with him.
Warning: Beware of McDonald
Ruin my senior year!
Computer Illiterate
Ruined my entire senior year and my capstone.  AVOID AVOID AVOID!!!
No Comments
No Comments
rambles all the time about stupid side stories more than he actually teaches (which he does pretty poorly)
No Comments
does not answer email
totally incoherent, clueless
No Comments
Doesn't teach, unorganized, may as well not be there. AVOID HIM.
Dr. Alvaro is definitely the best professor I've had at RPI. She's easy to talk to and really wants you to learn
She's willing to help whenever you have trouble.  Her notes are clear and concise which makes the tests much more bearable.  Best chem teacher I've had so far at RPI.
FABULOUS FABULOUS TEACHER!!!!!

I had her for both (Chem I &II) last year and she was an awesome teacher.  It's obvious she tries really hard to make the material understandable and interesting (demos, videos, sounds effects).  If you study her notes, you should be fine for the tests, since the test questions are really similar to the questions she goes over in her notes.

no point complaining about the tests because she DOESN'T WRITE THEM. all chem exams are given in the same time period. same exam is given to all sections. out of the three possible professors she is absolutely the best. very easy to talk to. she's young and therefore she understands where students have trouble.
In continuation with the previous post, the tests can hit you hard, so make sure you study and know the material! Good luck! :)

Sara is an awesome professor! She's really approachable and willing to help her students. The lectures can get boring at times, but she does her best to make things interesting with demos and videos. The material is pretty straightforward...if you put effort into learning it, you can do well in this class.
Really good teacher, gives good examples in class. kinda hot

Her lectures are boring, her notes are impossible to read, and she skips over the clicker questions. The worst part of her class though, are the tests. Simply knowing the material cold is not enough, because she goes out of her way to write questions that will trip up even her best students. Not sure which McIntosh everyone else is talking about.

Lectures can get boring after a while, but they are helpful.  Take notes even though she posts them online.  I don't like the iClicker quizzes, but they are an easy grade boost.  Don't wait until the last minute to study or do the online homework!
Tests can be challenging, but you'll do well if you go to class, go through the examples, and study.  Sara is a really great and approachable prof.  One of the best I've had at RPI!

She was pretty good, nothing special in my opinion.  Her lectures are nothing more than an outline of the chapter and her lectures are almost verbatim from the textbook.  She tries to be funny but fails hard.  She has poor handwriting, but if you can read it then you could try and skip her EXTREMELY boring lectures.
Probably the best core science professor I've had so far.  Her lectures were really easy to follow and she made sure to outline what would be on the test.  Very nice too!
Good teacher - probably the best for Chem 1.

The best way to describe Dr. McIntosh is FAIR.  She has strict guidelines but makes them clear at the beginning of the semester.  She WANTS us to know the material and makes us work for it.  She is always there for you and willing to help any time.  She is also VERY cute!  I'd like to ask her out!

Sara is great.  While her lectures are generally far too long and if you have her too early in the morning it's especially bad, she tries to keep things interesting.  If you go to lecture and actually listen, you'll do just fine on all the tests.  WARNING: The first test is a hard one, especially if you aren't the tyep to study.
She is a very good teacher and is funny, but has some of the worst hand writing i have ever seen. If you can decypher it though, your golden
Very good teacher. She's easy to talk to and get help from. tests reflect what she teaches and aren't too hard. i enjoyed taking her class and look forward to having her in future classes.
Very good teacher. She's easy to talk to and get help from. tests reflect what she teaches and aren't too hard. i enjoyed taking her class and look forward to having her in future classes.
Truly fantastic class, a bit bad with feedback but amazing lecture notes.
Great man and he makes it easy to study physics by presenting different approach to study the same material. I am really grateful for his life

Amazing professor, and amazing and engaging lectures. One of the best professors I've had. He goes above and beyond to create great content for the course and to help students understand the topics. My only criticism would be that some homeworks are a little plug-and-chug.

This is my second semester with Professor Meunier and I am extremely lucky to have been able to take his classes. Not only does he care about his students but he goes above and beyond what could ever be asked of a professor to ensure his student's well-being. Attend the lectures, not because it's mandatory but because Prof Meunier is hilarious!

Truly cares about the students learning the material, and attempts to reach all students by displaying the material in various ways: through the screencasts, lecture, and quizzes. Always there to help!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This is the best professor you will ever have. I took his in person IQM course and his online Thermo/Statmech Course. The quality of his in person lectures were beyond the quality of any other I have ever had. The content in the recorded screencasts are superb. His courses permanently changed the way I engage with physics. (for the better!)

I took the course over the summer. Professor Meunier did more than an excellent job, he helped everyone get the most of the material. There were (and still are) screencasts available on YT, so that everyone could watch them at their own pace, and live class where everyone could participate. A feeling of normality during the pandemic.
Fantastic
Screencasts are too long.

The most genuine and caring professor I have had the privilege of meeting. He is flexible and has no problem delaying deadlines. He asks students for feedback on his course and uses that feedback to change the style of his course. His courses were innovative, informative, and pleasant to take. I highly recommend you take any class he offers!
Professor Meunier ('moon-yay', not 'moon-ear') is a real gem. You'll probably have him at some point if you are a physics major. Look forward to his class!
Exceptionally skilled lecturer. Like most professors in the department, cares a great deal about his students and his class. He will tease you. Do not use your phone in his class.
Amazing professor. One of the best I had at RPI. Good sense of humor, and managed to make a complex topic understandable.

I want to be this guy. He is honestly one of the best. He has a lot too add while still not deviating from the book too much to bear. He's funny and cares a lot about the students. Ask him a question and you'll get some serious insight. He's a crazy hard worker, wakes up at 5, publishes more than anyone in his field at RPI and runs the department.
One of the best classes and professors at RPI.

Prof. Meunier is the best professor I have encountered at RPI so far. His lectures and powerpoints are engaging and entertaining. He enjoys interacting with students on an individual basis, and at the final project he interviews students one-on-one. Watch out though, he is very mischievous with his jokes, teasing, etc.

Prof. Meunier genuinely cares about his students and education! The assignments are designed to teach students practical skills and ways of thinking. It's strongly suggested to have some background in programming (c++ specifically), but even if this is new to you he has a tutorial session for those starting off. His lecture style is very fun.

Prof. Meunier genuinely cares about his students and education! The assignments are designed to teach students practical skills and ways of thinking. It's strongly suggested to have some background in programming (c++ specifically), but even if this is new to you he has a tutorial session for those starting off. His lecture style is very fun!

If you are taking this class purely for Inquiry Credit, it is easy but BORING. If you have an interest in code, or have taken prereq's this class is better suited for you. It is project-based and group-heavy. As long as you complete the assignments you will pass. No need to attend lecture, as it is boring like I said.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Rough Class. She doesn't know how much her assignments are worth/how difficult they are and seems to assign due dates arbitrarily. She's done none of the work for her class, so she expects students to be guinea pigs, at the expense of their grades. Unity experience highly recommended beforehand, as the tutorials given are lackluster. Do not take.

Very disorganized and unprepared for class. She didn't grade any of the important assignments till very late in the class so I had no idea how I was doing. By the end of the class we were over 2 weeks behind schedule, making it so we had to crunch once she finally assigned the final project.

Pretty fair class, the grading criteria could've been clearer but pretty much everyone got an A. Really interesting subject material. Mainly homework and projects which where group oriented. Probably should have more prereqs but if you already have some AI/code knowledge you should be fine.

I took Dr. Si for AI and society, which was, by far, the most disorganized class I have ever taken. At any given point, 60% of the class had no idea what was going on. There were also ridiculous coding assignments which mainly involved changing variables and had little to do with learning about AI.

Incredibly disorganized and uninteresting. She is VERY hard to understand due to her broken English. She turned a 1000 level HASS into a class where you needed to know how to code at a high level (or have someone in your group that did) to do well.
reviews.rating_tags: GRADED BY FEW THINGS--GROUP PROJECTS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Si took a class that was supposed to be on the moralities and implications of Artificial Intelligence into a "JV" Intro to AI Class. There was no coding Prequisite, but our Final project was heavily code-based. She also did not have a good foundation in English. This class was the sloppiest last-minute put together class I've ever taken.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Fun, fair grader, makes at times dry material interesting, has great fashion for a professor

Can be difficult to access outside of class, often has trouble interpreting students' questions. Engages with students in class. Can come off as abrasive, but he's super nice. Emphasizes actually understanding the material's real-life applications and shortcomings (this is a HUGE boon). Provides great mix of casual and formal vocabulary. Really fun
Great guy. Really great classroom experience. Makes the effort to get to know each student!

Everyone in class loved Merrill. It was one of the best classes I took in RPI. Merrill is exceptional at teaching. I learned a lot from the class and I will always remember this wonderful experience. I felt sad when the class ended (so was my undergrad at the same time).

This class was definitely one of the most helpful I have ever taken. Prof. Whitburn gives excellent feedback for improvement and is very generous for grading, as long as you put in a sincere effort. I thoroughly enjoyed the class to provide feedback for my peers and saw strong improvement in my public speaking skills. Excellent class overall.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Great class

Great course and an outstanding professor! Merrill cares about the success of his students and really pushes them to succeed. His course was the most useful I've taken thus far, and I wholeheartedly recommend it to all RPI students.

Merrill is the best professor at Rensselaer!  I had to put many extra hours into this course and I was stressed at many points in time about giving speeches but he structured the class so that it made it easy to succeed. 100% would recommend!  I feel confident about public speaking and it is a great tool to have for the future.
One of the best classes and professors at RPI
The class is hard, and if you have problems speaking publicly it will be extra hard. But you will learn more in this class for your career than many other classes.
I learned so much about public speaking. I really got to know the professor and my classmates. Fun, interesting, easy, and you'll never get critics like in this class!

Greatest professor at RPI. He expects a lot, so you'll need to work hard but you will learn a ton. Very friendly and comical class environment. Textbook reading not too important, practice and improvement determine your grade. Painful at first but you will see yourself gain confidence and become a much better public speaker. Take this class.

I took public speaking from this guy. He has a commanding presence, and knows a lot about the subject, but he doesn't know nearly as much as he thinks he does. Attendance is mandatory and his grading is brutal. If you don't eat up every bit of his dogma like the religion he thinks it is, he will hang you for it. I did A level work, it got me a C+.

Easily the most useful class I've taken to date, and his advice has helped me in every single presentation that I've given since then.  Merrill keeps the class fun and interesting, and I hated all public speaking coming in.  Grading is not too bad as long as you put in the effort, he judges you on your improvement over the semester.
Came into speech communication with zero public speaking ability now i feel much more confident and prepared to make a public speech.  great professor

Merrill is awesome! Take speech communication and you will ace any and every single speech, oral presentation and interview you encounter for the rest of your life. Oh, don't buy the textbook for this class, its a waste of money. Just go to the library or borrow a friend's to do what little reading he assigns at the beginning.
Merrill is the man! Best professor at RPI!

This is one professor you definitely want to have.  His class starts out hard; you will have to practice a lot to meet his high expectations.  However, he is very knowledgeable, and will help you however he can. Your class will come together and you will feel like you have all been lifelong friends.  I will definitely take more of his classes.

Amazing prof. who deeply cares about students. Hard if you haven't spoken in front of people before but well worth the effort.  He's scary the first day but don't worry he really does care, and it's not as much reading as he says.  as long as you try your best and dont just blow it off you will not just get a good grade  but learn great life skills

Merril was by far the best professor I've had at RPI. He's so awesome that my class made a Facebook group for him.  "You just got Whitburned!"  One of the only classes where the whole class actually felt like a group and learned something.  Odd, I know, learning something from a class, but Merrill manages it perfectly.

As I'm going into my last semester of RPI, I can honestly say that Merrill has been my favorite and best professor I've had.  He's a bit scary at first but he truly cares about you succeeding and is incredibly supportive.  You can truly take what you've learned and use it for the rest of your life. Wish he taught more classes! Amazing person.

I took his class in my freshman year at RPI, and now--even as a second-semester Junior--I can safely say that Merrill is the best professor I have had at the Institute to date.  I felt like I grew as a person by taking his class.  He may seem tough at first, but if you put in the time to excel, his class will be an amazing experience.
Great Professor! Down to earth and hilarious. Grades extra hard in the beginning, but if you progressively work hard you should get an A in the class. But working hard is the key.

Simply the best professor at RPI.  Merrill challenges students to perform and makes class extremely enjoyable.  Though the class seems intimidating at first, hard work and determination pay off in the end.  Speech Communication with Merrill is the rare course that helps you develop as a person and not just gain experience in a particular subject.

Merrill is one of the best professors at RPI. Lessons you learn from him will help you immensely in the future. Don't be intimidated by him in the first few classes, he really is one of the most genuinely kind and caring professors on campus. He is also hilarious, but makes you work, he wants you to grow into a great communicator.
Merrill for President... Loved him... Loved the class

TAKE THIS COURSE! Merrill is the best prof I've had at RPI. Everyone in the class works to help ppl recognize areas that need work to make you a good speaker. Don't let his speech the 1st day scare you off.

The best professor at RPI hands down. The only class where I have actually developed as a person and not as a studying machine. You would be wasting four years at RPI if you did not take this class. This man is the type of professor your dream about. I definitely will miss this class :'(.

By far the best professor I have ever had, his charisma and humor creates an amazing atmosphere for students to interact in.  Learned wonderful life skills from his class.  I reccomend this class to anyone who enjoys learning and having fun while doing it.  Thanks Merrill!
He's hilarious! Made a class that could have been nerve-wracking really fun.
The Novel was one of the most enjoyable classes that I have ever taken!  Merrill is an incredible teacher, and you can learn a lot from him.  More of the professors at RPI should learn from him!

After having so much fun and learning so much in Speech Comm. I decided to take The Novel as well.  Without a doubt, the best teacher I have ever had.  He keeps the class engaged and has an incredible wit and sense of humor.  Take a class with him before you graduate!  Keep up the good work, Merrill
I learned so much from this man in the subject.  He made you work hard for your grade.  Kept the class always excited in what was happening.  Take his class if possible.

Merrill is one awesome teacher.  He's really organized and does a great job at understanding each and every person's problems with their speeches.  He's also very helpful, and has a great sense of humor.

Terrible professor. Always went off topic in lecture, gave impossible tests, impossible homework and tough grading. When asked for help, he would always refer us to his useless textbook. Hull was also equally bad. He has made me hate anything to do with materials science. Do not recommend.

Thank God Dr. Steinbruchel taught this for the 1st half of the semester, 'cause I learned nothing from Messler. "Lecture" was mostly tangents; lectures didn't follow the syllabus & quizzes weren't based on lecture or the book so studying did nothing. Forgot about labs, changed grading rules in MAY. Got nasty if you asked him for help.

Not as bad as people are saying. I went to class, read the book, did the homework, and studied for quizzes/tests. Ended with an A in the class. If you do whats expected, you can do as well as you want.

Even by RPI standards, Bob Messler is a horrible teacher. As others have said, class was mostly him going on a tangent, with hard quizzes on things that weren't in lecture or the book. He never prepared for lecture, ao his attempts at teaching were just as useless as his tangents. Had to teach myself the material in this class.

Spent most of class on irrelevant, boring tangents; quizzed on material that wasn't in lecture or the book; cumulative quizzes(which he didn't write) tested on stuff we never learned. Horrible teacher even when he lectured on relevant topics; wrote almost nothing down and skipped major topics. Useless, rude & arrogant during office hours.
Very little class time spent on subject matter. Often goes off on tangents that are irrelevant. Extremely difficult quizzes on topics not covered in class.

Material on quizzes wasn't in lecture or the book, he said it didn't matter when we called him out on it. Class time was mostly spent on tangents; actual discussion of the relevant material was rare, full of mistakes and very light on notes-the only way to learn in his class is reading the book. Office hours non-existent. Extremely hard quizzes.

Avoid his class or any class that uses his text book(Messler).  His textbook is very light on information, full of reference and spelling errors, making things very confusing. Some material on the cumulative tests(same for all sections) are not covered in his class or textbook at all.  As others said, he goes off on a tangent A LOT.

Didn't give time for labs, brutal quizzes. Didn't prep for class, spent more time on tangents than 'lecture', which was him thumbing through & reading from the book. Often dismissed us early & told us to read the sections he didn't cover. Class ON GM DAY, reviews were useless. Changed how grades were calculated with about a week left in class.

Avoid him if possible. Goes off on random tangents and barely teaches. Uses his own textbook which is almost as useless as he is which is unfortunate since reading is the only way you can learn in his class

I cannot stand him as a professor.  Very little notes, and material that was never covered in class will be on quizzes and assessments.  Teaches a lot like Professor Hubbell from RPI PSYC, but isn't as funny.  I find it difficult to tolerate the demeanor it which he teaches and discusses topics.

He talks about the material only half of the time.  Of the time he talks about other things, very little is relevant.  He comes off as conceited and unless you are okay with listening to that, then it's not as bad.

Appalling. Can't actually stay on-topic for more than 10-15 minutes before he goes off on a tangent, including tons of promoting a textbook he wrote, and doesn't know/care that some of the stuff on quizzes never showed up in lectures. Office hours are appointment-only, thanks to him I'm now best friends with the book and TA.

Messler tends to go off on tangents a lot during lectures but he still somehow manages to cover all of the material. He doesn't believe in giving easy tests though, so if you don't take good notes you can easily find yourself getting under 50% on the weekly quizzes.

Professor Messler frequently veers off course to talk about his days at Lockheed Martin or his love for Corvettes.  His lectures can be exciting, boring, long, and informative.  He is a smart guy who knows what he's talking about.  I learned a lot from this class, but my grade didn't show it.

Funny professors that sometimes go off topic with his jokes. While his lectures may seem boring and pointless to some, his quizzes are very hard. That's a good thing considering that you become more prepared for the final and experience a best curve usually of all the Mat-Sci classes.
He goes of on some weird and strange topics in class. but hes a fun teacher. his quizes are extreamly hard

Messler is a difficult professor in the way he designs his weekly quizzes....He has good stories usually during class which sometimes do and sometimes don't help you remember the material...it can feel like a waste of time to go to class, but I would suggest attending every one.

He was a very good professor who intentionally made his weekly quizes harder than other professors.  This may sound bad, but it proved profitable come test time. Tests were created by him for all sections or he collaborated on most tests, so while other classes did horrible, ours did well.  I guess you could say he was the dwyer of the mat sci dept

Rather interesting professor, but goes off onto tangental stories whose connection to the subject matter is tenuous at best. (Case in point: Stress Strengthening to his working as a bouncer??) Stories keep you interested, the only reason I kept going to the 8 am classes. Gives the class material, helps you until you understand it if you have a problem, real funny teacher. Only problem is the course material is sorta hard, but hey, it's college. Suck it up.
Excellent teacher
Very knowledgable and gave practical/clear examples as illustration of concepts.  I disagree with the people below.  this guys is funny.  Keeps you interested during lecture.
you learn nothing in class.  He is very unprepared for class and goes off subject way to much.  A lot of extra work because class is useless.
horrible, just horrible

Started the first class with "I normally teach Java, but..." Yeah, not so great when most of the class involves low abstraction. Relied heavily on the textbook. The next year, I had him for Java. Thought it would be better until he opened lecture with, and I quote: "I haven't actually written Java in over 5 years." Avoid this one.

He's good guy, but knows nothing about the course material. He tends to reference Java when asked a question. The problem is that Java and MIPS or x86 ASM have very little to do with each other.  Quizzes and homeworks are absolutely murderous, mostly because he doesn't teach the material.  I would avoid this guy for class CSCI-2500.

This class was easy, but it was not at all fun. And that's because most Java apps from textbooks are not fun. Mehta made lemonade, so to speak, and I commend him for that- but the homework, which makes up most of your grade in the class, was pure drudgery.
Good guy and professor. Tries to make lectures interesting by showing random examples of java-related things.  Online lectures and use of Google will get you an A in this class.

Very clear, and teaches everything well. Well prepared for his class and homeworks are reasonable. No one shows up to class and participation is very low, but it'll teach me Java and it's a very easy 2 credits.
He's a nice guy, but you have to know a bit about the subject material to keep up with his lectures.  Talks fairly quickly, so taking notes is difficult.

Not a hard class, not a hard prof.  Gives good lecture material for you to reference.  Also does plenty of in class examples for those that bother to show up (~10% of the class).  Easiest CS class I've taken since CS2.
No Comments
Very into his own ideas

Professor Murray is an excellent professor. The class is very manageable, with ample time for assignments. He gives extensions on deadlines if you ask. I especially appreciated the emphasis on group discussion rather than lectures, which makes the class engaging and interactive. Instead of exams, you'll complete projects for the midterm and final.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Super sweet guy, very understanding of the fact that he teaches Literature at a stem school. Contributing during in class conversations makes the class much more interesting and he is overall a pretty good professor.

Morris taught one of my favorite, and most practical courses at RPI -- optoelectrionics. He comes from decades of industry research and is an expert's expert in practical and applied optics, which shows through in his lectures. I found him soft spoken, but fun to listen to and very knowledgeable. His course was tough due to the challenging content.

Great guy. The lecture is structured very well. Constantly checks to make sure everyone understands the content and happily goes over it if someone doesn't quite understand it. The class itself has a lot of work outside of class, but if you do the readings and homework you should be fine (Go through back exams before test).
Worst professor ever. He gives horrible explanations and argues students about their grade making it always lower than it should be!
Prof. Washington is a very clear and concise professor.
Terrible. Doesn't really know what he is talking about. Can't answer questions that well.

Good professor for physics 1. The course is really determined by the coordinator, but Washington teaches the material clearly. Other students complained about their grades, but if you look around half the class is on AIM on their laptops. Speaks clearly, which you would think would be a requirement for a professor, but sadly is not.

He was one of the best professor I ever had.  He always tried to make sure everyone understood what was going on, and encouraged people to visit his office hours.  Very easy to understand.  Definately Recommend him.
really nice guy, best course i have ever taken
I like him... but not the class or the way it's taught
Explained the material pretty well.

For upper level classes, he is pretty good.  He knows what he is talking about from industry experience, and is very helpful.  Gives reasonable, though long HW.  His grading during the semester is weird, especially tests, and he then curves all the grades at the end to make some sense out of them.
No Comments
A 20 min lecture each 2 hr class full of unclear concepts + a terrible activity = no learning.
No Comments

IED Pilot is a great class (if you have a good group), and Dr. Mucci is a great professor! Approachable and gives great feedback, and is very clear with his standards/expectations. Regardless of your skill level, participate within your group as much as you possibly can.

Mucci did a great job with the course. He was very personable and approachable if you needed any help or clarification, was consistently available outside of class, and understood very well what students tended to struggle with and could offer suggestions or alternatives when you got stuck. Great professor and overall cool guy
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great professor cares a lot about students and is always ready to help your team.

Professor Mucci is a great professor and very smart. He gave great feedback and was helpful with any/all questions. He has some fire fashion sense and a goated lecturing style 🏀. 
society

Professor Mucci is an inspirational figure in higher education. Assignments are naturally difficult because of the design of the course, but Prof. Mucci makes sure design groups are up to speed and motivated to change the world.
Great professor to have, gave us good leeway on our group project - super understanding and kind. Would 100% take again.
Really nice guy, but the entire class was pretty much review from the previous ITWS class, and I don't feel like we learned anything.
Best professor I've had at RPI. Cares for students, lectures are fun, and makes the class easy. Pretty sure it's impossible not to get an A.
Professor Munasinghe is the best professor I've had at RPI; He's caring and ensures you feel respected. He provides excellent professional opportunities through conferences and publications.

I took Prof. Thilanka Munasinghe's Data Science course in fall, 2021. He conducts valuable guest lectures facilitated by renowned professionals and authors. (NASA/Google etc) He is an ethical lecturer who teach students with dignity and empathy, and he receives respect in return from the students. He creates a friendly learning environment.

Very passionate about class material and group discussion.
Amazing lecturer - he used no slides or teaching aides but still came across effectively.
Genuinely just an excellent teacher.

Professor Chari is one of the best at RPI's Lally School of Management. He's energetic, clear with expectations, and deeply knowledgeable. The class ties business and corporate strategy frameworks to real business news, which makes it engaging and useful. Workload is fair but challenging. Highly recommend if you want a practical, insightful course.
Greatest professor I had at RPI, taught a different class but if you have the opportunity to take his class do it.
Top 3 professor in the business department at RPI if not the best.

My favorite professor at RPI thus far, you learn a lot from him and can stay after class to talk to him. Class was very interesting and we would start each class discussing current business news which I found pretty cool.

Lectures were just filling out the handouts from the textbook, which was very boring, but I can't say that didn't prepare me for the exams. She was very responsive on WebEx if you had any questions. Weekly quizzes were very annoying especially because they were on Wednesdays when most classes have exams, though that is a course-wide problem.
Class was fine as long as you show up and pay attention. I was able to understand the material from her by just doing that

Her lectures felt like a waste of time and takes up majority lab time. Main problem with her lecture is that it felt very vague and surface level, you will be more lost than before by listening to his hard to follow lectures. Exams are also so ridiculously hard and barely resembles HW. She comes off as cold and uncaring, even for emergency cases.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: She expects very much out of her class but does not provide quality instruction. Be aware, pop quizzes are not excused if you miss class even though attendance is optional, and she has assigned hw due AFTER reading days and on the days of finals. Lectures are not comprehensible but hw is a guaranteed 100.

I take BMED2050 with Dr. Maldonado. I do not want to outright say that she is the worst, however, she teaches this class with very high expectations. Majority of the class never had any programming knowledge but she teaches as if we are CS majors. She does not explain clearly, and there are many pop quizzes where none of them are excused. Avoid her
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Worst BMED2050 prof. Lectures aren't useful and you cannot learn anything from them if you try to look back on them. She gives unannounced quizzes whenever she pleases and does not let you make them up for any reason, even though this is an attendance optional class. Does not explain how to code or why a program works and expects you to learn.

Her lectures take up half of lab time and are poorly structured. The heavy accent makes it impossible to even attempt to follow along. Tests are ridiculous, homeworks confusing, and there is way too little time to finish the labs. I haven't found anyone in the entire class that knows what's going on, or, bluntly, cares anymore. Find any other prof.

The group projects are great, and you can get pretty good grades on the experiments and projects, but the exam. HER EXAM IS SO HARD. It's not like the back exam, where she expects you to know based on lectures and experiments. She's nice but very hard

Very unhelpful. Generally gets tuned out when lecturing, as her lectures are hard to follow and unrelated to the course content. Her lectures take forever and cut into lab time, while providing no useful information and leaving students more lost than before they walked in. Don't dare ask questions, she is condescending and won't help.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Maldonado is nice and understands to students' difficulties. But in MAU, I believe she didn't do the best just because of the structure of the class itself. Id sooner see the class be individually taught by professors instead of standardized because its unfair to students. She taught very well in office hours, just not perfect in class.

I dropped out of her MAU class early in the semester. There were no phones or computers allowed and I couldn't understand what she was explaining. She speaks a bit fast and when she's showing her work, the camera was either never focused or half of what she was writing was off the screen so no one could see. I don't really recommend her.

Dr. Martinez led MAU lecture at an extremely slow pace. She forced all students to put away their laptops and phones which made her lectures even more insufferable. 1 month in, most of the class would skip. She would often make mistakes when doing problems, even forgetting how to do them. I feel she would be better served to teaching HS students.
tries to be engaging during lectures and checks in to make sure everyone understands the content. lectures content is usually very similar to homework assignments.

This professor is a understanding guy who's actually a great teacher and lecturer. Unfortunately, his exams are extremely difficult even though they are open notes. I do feel like I learned a lot in his class, but he is certainly more difficult than other professors.

He's a very thorough lecturer, taking time out of class to ensure everybody there understands the material covered. Tests are hard, but graded kindly. Weekly homeworks take a long time but provide a good grade boost. Overall solid professor, don't let the amount of work dissuade you, all thermals classes give tons of work.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: He was very good if not the best

He is the best prof. that I have ever had.  His lectures are clear.  He is smart and he cares.  He is tough, but those who don't like him are people who do not try.  Anyone who is willing to work and learn loves the class.
Nauman is easily one of the worst professors I have had.  His text book is beyond terrible, and his lectures are useless.  I felt like the class was a waste of time.
This man wrote one of the worst textbooks in the world!  He has little or no interest in students - why is he still a professor?
No Comments

He's clear and to the point in his textbook and occaisionally in class when he's explaining the material. The problem is that half the time he goes on long-winded tangents, not explaining the material.

Professor never really seems terribly prepared, nor does he demonstrate mastery of the material. He reads directly off of the slides, which he posts online; paying attention is almost a game. His exams way exceed how he presents himself and the material in lecture. Wait a semester and take it with a different professor.

Biomaterials with Tacy is actually not that bad... he seems to be knowledgeable and interested. There is a lot of focus on the monstrous textbook, but you can easily get good grade in the class by just studying the lecture slides and skimming the textbook. Only reason I go to class is for quizzes and the sporadic attendance taking.
Not a very helpful professor. Reads verbatim off the sides and does not know much about what needs to be done for class.

Prof Tacy is a great professor. He really cares about his students and is very easy to talk with. He has a great interest in the topics of this course, despite it sometimes being boring. Highly recommend taking any class with him!

Has good intentions, and knows the material well (as hard and annoying as it is), but his lectures are kind of boring because he tends to speak in a monotone.  Very helpful in office hours though.  If you have questions, make sure to go to him and/or ALAC tutoring.  Tests are almost always medium-difficulty problems right from the homework section.

I had Tacy for Strengths, and he was horrible at expalining the material. In class examples, we would spend half the time doing basic arithmetic, making it impossible to stay engaged. He also refused to use units in examples, making them hard to follow.
One of the better professors at RPI. Clearly explains concepts and answers questions well. Uses the same lecture slides as everyone but he explains them well and engages the class.

Good, straightforward, easy to understand professor. Lectures are directly from the slides, but he does a good job explaining concepts. Most importantly, all the test material is covered thoroughly and effectively.  Always helpful in office hours or after class. Recommended.

Prof. Tacy was great. Helped students when needed. Material was presented on PowerPoint that was awful but not his fault given to him by department. He displayed a amazing understanding of the material and a commitment to the students.  Before test reviews were the most important class. This s where prof tacy excelled!
Reads off a powerpoint, go to SI sessions to learn the material
This proffessor repeats himself many times during class. It seems as if he does not read the slides before class. He has a very boring presentation style.

Awesome guy.. "Call me Neil".  Computer music was great, and he's the perfect guy to teach this material, as he's been a part of developing that scene. he commutes from NYC, and brings energy and fun to what could be a solely technical class.
I found rolnick to be the most condescending professor I have run into thus far at RPI. The class is really easy, and as long as your TA is helpful everything will be fine.

Neil knows what he is talking about but had a hard time keeping everyones attention for 2 hours. You never really get to work with him in this class, only the TA's. That was OKAY by me, they were much more helpful. If you are into music, especially ambient stuff, you'll like his class.
Booooooriiiiingg.All he talks about is stupid sounding music.
Excellent & experienced professor.  Give good critiques and helpful.
Neil really knows his stuff, he can do music programming, he can compose, make aesthetic judgments, critique and theorize. His voice is a little on the quiet side.

He must have some sort of complex internal bigotry, because he consistently picked on me every studio. He had to audacity to curse at me and tell me I had no work and he was going to fail me in a week, halfway through the semester. I am not a slacker by any means. This man has a reputation for making students cry in his studio. (he's fired now)

Extremely bright professor and brutally honest studio critic. His stance on technology in the context of architecture is unique at RPI, and he will open your eyes to emerging materials, processes and ways of thinking.
smart guy but can't teach. Would have been  helpful if studio was more structured and if given more time than a couple of weeks to develop it.

Ted is the****!  He's very clear in what he's looking for, and a great guy!  Funny as hell, too.  Pushes you as far as you're willing to go; different personality than most studio professors, but it still definitely works.
No Comments

Push over. He's useless. I have no idea why hes working as a Studio professer, maybe his inside friends Jefferson Ellinger and Andrew Saunders got him the job. I guess they figure that if they load the Greene Building with their buddies that they could all get away with poor behavior.  He doesn't do a damb thing.
Worst studio professor I've ever had, by far.  Very unhelpful, and does poorly in setting a schedule to get projects accomplished in a timely manner.  His behavior is very inappropriate at times.

Lectures are intensive.
Labs are demanding.

reviews.comment: Gives pop quizzes at the start of lectures. Made the 3-time lab into an 11-week lab with a lab report with no direction of what is expected. Hw given at any time, even if it is due the next day. There is a project (not on syllabus) & no hw schedule. Professor consistently cancels office hrs last minute every time they are supposed to be available.

reviews.comment: she is very knowledgeable, but you need to be good at taking note and write everything down to succeed the class
Her lectures are very informative and relevant, though a bit dry. She grades fairly gently and gives a lot of opportunities for extra credit. She's also very patient and helpful if you ask for help.
Excellent professor - keeps lectures relevant and materials very appropriate to curriculum

She is the only professor I've had for an engineering course at RPI who actually teaches the material well.  I learn more from her than my textbook.  She is a pretty easy grader, doesn't try to trick you on exams, and she's very approachable.
Super Approachable, really friendly.  Enjoys teaching.  Hard class because many levels of knowledge required

Untrustworthy and unprofessional. If you have the unfortunate experience of having him as your academic advisor, he will do nothing for you. In fact, he will go out of his way to sabotage you and sit by ideally while you figure things out on your own.
Excellent Professor! He actually cares about his students.
ever since he got ten-yr he's stopped showering and brushing his teeth.  It was hard to take him seriously before but now it's just impossible

eh. if he doesn't like you then good friggin' luck trying to do well. he has these team meetings though that are really helpful. he's an amazing artist and very inspiring but sometimes loses sight of the fact that we have 4 other classes to worry about too.

Seems like hes lacks communication skills. When he crits my work it seems like he lives in a different world. Does not understand that drawing is not the only class that students take and requires too much (quite pointless at times) work.
gotta love the Oat-man
I hate this class!! Im an engineer and no artist! I hate to draw, this guy and his assignments are a PDI nightmare, 26 drawings of styrafoam anyone??
His popularity is unwarranted.  Anyone who studied art before will not be impressed.  Dumb assignments with no point and no development.
What a cool dude, never a dull moment with him, gotta love his jokes!  Bit then again, his drawing assignments are ridiculously long and usually pointless and he normally doesnt even collect them.
Awesome Oatman. Absolutely Awesome.
Oatman. Gotta love him. Love to hate him.
Bring ear plugs - the man cant stop talking!
he is really cool, has great ideas and a great sense of humor.  sometimes talks too much but if you listen youll always learn or open your mind
No Comments
No Comments
Oatman is pretty cool.  He's a typical art teacher.. kinda out there.  He gives some weird assignments but he's always willing to help out or just chill with you in studio
Wack job, he is a cool guy with crazy ideas, but he needs ot be a little more down to earth, nad be a little less flighty/unrealistic
You will learn nothing. He will rant about random topics ranging from his opinion of corporal punishment to borderline discriminatory musings.

This professor is incredibly goofy, he would show up late to every class and then go on huge tangents about essentially nothing, then give you a group project with the vaguest instructions I've ever heard. As long as you show up to the presentations and somewhat participate, he'll give you an A.

You probably won't learn anything valuable in this class, he basically just goes off on rambles about his own personal beliefs and views of the world. If you show up and nod your head and smile you will get an A. Don't question it, just got along with it.
I literally dont know what he is talking about.

Professor Noble tried to be a good professor in Future of AI/HCI, however, his class ended up being more of a coding class, instead of a HASS, due to Professor Si. I would probably take him for other classes because he makes class really engaging and a good speaker, but the answer here is to never take Future of AI.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Absolute amazing professor.  He's so funny and unlike some of the classes I've taken previously to this class, his textbooks, lectures, and assignments are perfect for helping the students understand the course. Sometimes randomly calls students, but more for opinion input. Weekly journal entries and a "cool" prjct is all you have to do to get an A

He is not a good professor. The class is beyond simple, but I'm a month and a half into his Motivation and Performance class and have learned close to nothing about motivation or performance. He just sits in class and rambles for two hours while the class sits on their computers. Take this if you want an easy A but not if you want to learn anything

Come to class, listen to him talk about anything and everything (including Food, how he feels he is entitled to a percentage of your first million for his retirement fun and anything else) Go home, write a paragraph about the class, do a project on almost anything and that is the class. Fun to take this class to get a break from harder courses.

A cool guy. Likes food a tad too much, but that's not important. He's friendly, can't remember anyone's name, and doesn't require you to come to class. Class consists of sitting there listening to him talk about whatever, and the grade is entirely based on two projects. Easy projects. Fun times overall.

great professor. makes you think more than read...and thinking teaches more. he's very intelligent, interesting and understanding, but don't take advantage of his kind understanding nature - it's there to help you.
"A good teacher doesn't teach"
great teacher,very insightful and makes you think,the hardest work you will do sometimes is just thinking, work is on the low side but he keep the class awake and intrested
Took Psychology of Motivation with Prof. Noble back in 1987.  It was the most useful elective class that I took at RPI.  And, he was, by far the best professor at RPI.
noble is a funny guy, he likes to joke around and keep class interesting. class is decently easy as long as you keep up with your work, it's a nice break from the typically rpi class from hell.

He raises some interesting points, keeps your attention, and does not bog you down with meaningless work. He makes you think and gives you the opportunity to dive into the subject matter, but does not force it down your throat like some teachers do.
Awesome guy, taught an awesome class
This class is a good break from engineering core.  Dont learn too much but if you pick a good project, you can have fun with it.
Cool guy.  Classes with him are very laid back and interesting.
Totally awesome.
Great professor. He makes lectures interesting and material relevant to life. If you're going to take a psychology course while you're at RPI, take one with Noble.
Awesome professor.  Convey's his point clearly and effectively.  It was a joy to have experienced his class.
He tries to make the lectures fun and interesting and imparts some very useful tips along the way.

Relatively easy class, some group projects that end with a final project but no real homework.  Noble has endless personal experience and his lectures are often more like anecdotes, but the class is a pretty easy 'A' and it's better than the other IT reqs
Strange man.  But it's psych, so it's easy.
Odell is pretty chill. Owns some cool hats and doesn't assign too much homework. If you figure out what he wants in his essays, you will do fine.

Not too hard to get an A if you do what he tells you. A bit of work outside of class on the papers, but he's willing to read through your writing and help you. Really nice guy, could be a stressful class/ a bit more work if you aren't so good at writing.

As a freshman I enjoyed professor odell's class and I learned so much on how to write. This class will be helpful through rest of career because it improved the way I used to write (horrible writing) dramatically. I wish I can always be taught by him. I recommend this course personally because it is not difficult to get high grade if you try!

Took his class freshmen year as a requirement. All reviewers are correct that "his style of writing is the only way to receive an A in the class". On the first paper when I questioned my grade, which was written in his format, he told me, "You wrote this very aggressively, and that's not how women get ahead in life." I wish I could make that up.

Writing for Classroom career was straightforward for me, which was due to Odell, and being a good writer. I thought his methods were easy to follow. However, I knew many others in the class who did NOT understand his methods and as such got Cs when I was getting As. He goes out of his way to meet with and help students. He was funny, too.

He does not deserve all the bad comments.  Honestly his grading is pretty straight forward, do what he asks you to do and put a lot of work into your writing, and get an A.  However, if you decide you know how to write and he does not, just drop the class since it is a waste of your time.  He taught me how to write (one way granted) very well.

He's never clear on the assignments and he wants you to print multiple copies of assignments as if we have we can print infinitely. He doesn't care about the class and he is a snot. Even after a rewrite, he can give you a worse grade if you put in a lot of effort. AVOID HIM. AVOID HIM. YOU HAVE BEEN ADVISED.

Ok. Let me rewrite first essay and accepted late even then. Not sure how grading will go yet. Unfair with grading at times (first group to present given short notice; graded harshly imo considering work and painstaking care to follow his guidelines). Ditto below otherwise.

Useless. Seems to only know one style of writing. If you're looking to write for magazines and infomercials, consider this. Looking to write to write for classroom and career? Try something else. He's used a plethora of student samples and seems to be easily swayed by class opinion.

More than half my class dropped after the first paper.  His writing style was the only correct way.  He once told me I could rewrite a paper for a better grade.  I went to 2 meetings with him to talk about the guidelines of what he wanted, rewrote it and he refused to change anything, just encouraged me to go to the Dean of Students to complain.
One of the worst professors I've had at RPI.  Very unhelpful to students and gives very hazy feedback.  Avoid having him like the plague.
No Comments

You will actually learn how to write in this class. Before I took Writing for the Classroom & Career with Odell I wasn't very confident in my writing skills. After taking this class, I have recieved all A's on my papers.  There's a not a lot of work (only 4 papers and presentation). Just do what he says in your writing and you'll be fine.
A very dedicated professor. After every class he sends each student a bunch of very useful comments.  He will definitely improve your writing ability.

Worst professor I have ever had. Demanded ridiculous things and if your writing wasn't just like his, he would grade it poorly. Didn't learn anything about writing, just learned how to write more like him. Take this class, but not from this professor!!

Good prof, but too demanding from engineering students. Grade hard, but guranteed to learn a lot from him. Take his class if you are a good writer. Expect to get more work than any other writing class.
Great professor, teaches well, really helpful and funny.
Looked forward to every class :)
Very good teaching. Great class

Taught the material extremely well.  He doesn't tolerate cell phones, tardiness, or talking during lecture, which kept everyone pretty focused.  He was extremely helpful during office hours and more laid back than he was in class.
Good :)
Great professor, teaches very well and tests on what he teaches, just a good guy as well.

He sounds like a jerk on the first day. Once the semester starts, however, he's very jocular and helpful. Easy class, imo, and the worst treatment you'll get is if you're late, and he asks for your excuse.

She's changed the class. Now, not only is 4 tedious hours a week of annoying noises and dull anecdotes, there's also an amazing amount of repetitious and ultimately pointless homework. The meditation was somewhat relaxing, but if I want to sit quietly for ten minutes, I can go do that somewhere else. I would not recommend this course.

Pauline is quite an interesting person and is friendly and helpful inside and outside of class (as long as she's around). Her class provided an escape from engineering, in part because it was extremely easy and laid-back.
what do you say about an old hippy who wants to wrap a copyright around listening ?
Lots of insights... 4 hours isn't always easy to get by but A is almost certain in that class.
Easy, but very deep and spiritual.  Kind of tedious, being four hours, but a very easy A.
Her class Deep Listening might seem like a joke to some but take it seriously and you'll hear the difference. As a musician and composer I gained a lot.

Pauline Oliveros' class came at a good time in the middle of the week (in '03). You just relax, forget about everything else, sleep if you're really tired.  Her unorthodox way of teaching can be strange, but it doesn't hurt anyone -- quite the opposite.

Pauline is one of the most amazing women I've met.  The only people sleeping through the class are those that do not take the inquiry seriously.  If you choose to rise to the difficult challenge you will leave the class with new perspective.
u have to take this class....hahaha ...DEEP LISTENING IS THE ****...all u do is sleep in class

Knowledgeable but poor at actually teaching, avoid if possible. Lectures are not useful: he reads off the slides, has few example problems, and does not delineate testable, necessary content from extra graduate-level content thrown in for fun. Exams are badly designed, with unclear wording, nonsensical point distributions, and curveball topics.
