awesome professor. if you ever have to take the class take it with him you'll actually learn.
A great class! Really taught the material well and showed an interest in helping us learn. Awesome guy, really funny.
A vey lazy guy....the grades are only based on tests.  If you study you'll get a good grade.
great teacher, enjoyable, and a isnt a communist.
kind of a boring class... read of of powerpoint slides online
Easiest class ever
great professor, very energetic and funny. explains the subject very well.
awesome prof. second time i am in his class and i am enjoying it... very clear, very energetic, helpful and funny...
awesome prof. great guy.

Had Jones for Intro and Money and Banking.  Great professor!  Isn't a firm believer in final exams during finals week.  Tests aren't the easiest things but they're more than fair.  Funny and applicable stories in lecture.  You'll learn the stuff too.
best prof ever
Easy, funny guy, has a story on every topic. Lectures were pretty much out of the book.
Awesome prof, he's cool and funny. Always has great stories.
No Comments
One of the best professors I have had at college.
No Comments
Bob Jones is a super prof. His classes are well taught.
Decent. Does not explain well.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Overall great professor who is super knowledgeable. The homeworks can be time consuming and tough to get and the project at the end of the year isn't easy. Made SFM very interesting and I am looking to do research with him in the future as a result.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: This was his first semester teaching SM and it was one of the best classes I've taken at RPI.  Professor Singh is very knowledgeable, has very well-prepared lectures, and is very helpful during office hours.  Highly recommend this class and professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: In his first semester, things started off a little rocky after the first exam, but after taking in feedback the course became much more manageable. There were some growing pains but Professor Singh was very understanding to everyone and by the end the class was much better. The lectures were a drag and the project was difficult, but overall not bad

Spends too much time on simple things then not enough time on harder things. Still learned what he taught in class, but he doesn't cover the information with enough depth to do the homework. You should definitely read to understand the material well.

Really terrible lecturer. We were always behind and sometimes we didn't even cover all the material before the tests. Half the time he's talking to himself and not lecturing, so it's really hard to learn anything in his classes. some people show up to the lecture for attendance and watch videos of other prof's lectures. It's the only way to pass.

Dr. Ryu should have a high score because he is one of the best lecturers I've had. You have to go to class for clicker questions, but it's actually helpful compared to Ma's lectures because it's all practice problems, which are similar to what the tests are comprised of. Good idea to read the textbook, you'll ace the exams. Cute little guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: Heavy accent. Boring lecture.  Too much time on basic topics-falls behind other lectures quickly. Doesn't hit main topics of lectures that are usually on exams.
He was a horrible teacher, for some reason he would laugh all the time for no reason.  He also changed his grading scheme at the end of the semester. I remember nothing from his class

I didn't really learn anything from his class, out of our 3 exams, 2 of them were take home so in the end, I ended up not really learning anything.  He laughs a lot, even over stuff that isn't funny...the test questions are the ones from past exams that he posts online..good thing, or else Phy chem at RPI would be as hard as it is at other colleges

Dr. Ryu was an excellent teacher, his problems were of the correct difficulty to maximize my learning, and his tests were as expected, challenging, and of a correct length.  Overall, he was an excellent professor.
SO EASY. tests were just like homework. he made certain to repeat the important stuff so you had no excuse for not knowing it.

he spends far too much time on simple subjects. his tests have not followed a pattern (1st was multiple-choice, 2nd was open-ended, 3rd remains to be seen). difficult topics are not covered in sufficient detail. i wish i had a different professor

Spends too much time explaining simple concepts and not enough time explaining hard areas. Tends to ask at least one question on each test that cannot be studied for. Fairly easy on grading, though, can be convinced to give somewhat generous curves.

Picking her for PD1 was probably the best decision I've made here. She is super understanding, kind, and accessible outside of class for things unrelated to course material. She redirected lecture to prep us for the career fair, and has made me feel like I've gotten something out of the class. She pushed me out of my comfort zone enough to succeed.

She is a fantastic professor and very reasonable person overall. If you email her about absences, she will be extremely understanding. As an introverted person. she pushed me out of my comfort zone enough to be challenged, but not enough to be uncomfortable and not want to come back. Will be trying for her PD 3 class

Professor Schierenbeck is really caring and understanding toward students. In PD3, sometimes she scared me with her lectures about interviews and professionalism. She "cold-calls" you and makes you stand up in front of the class to speak. Even though the class was anxiety-inducing, speaking with her privately is a dream. Such a nice person.
Best PD3 professor you can get!

Tracy is passionate + provides keen insights. Be forewarned that PD1 lacks structure + involves many surprises; an intentional move to take students out of their comfort zone. As a result, you will either embrace the ambiguity + see it as a chance to grow, or you will remain uncomfortable + spurn the class. I recommend the former; it's worthwhile.
really nice and enthusiastic

Worthless. She's not in class a lot, never learns students' names and actually believes that PD1 isn't a joke. Would put us on the spot with absurd demands, harsh grading and inane, nonsense comments-apparently those of us who are bad at public speaking shouldn't try to talk in front of groups. Ever.
a charismatic speaker

I know that the instructor is Prof. Staff when you sign up for it, but do your best to get this lady.  She will have an interest in your team and project.  I do not really like the PD-series aka the BS-series, but comparing her teaching on Wed to Murtuza's on M&R, I preferred actually LEARNING in PD1.
Tracy was an AWESOME teacher!

Gives obvious help on the quizes like doing a "review" right beforehand so you know the answers to some of the harder questions.   Makes you stand up in class whenever you speak, and has the class critique your speaking style. At the beginning of each class, she picks some note cards you fill out before, and asks you interview question based on i
No Comments
Easy class and she tried to make this boring class interesting. Although some of the material sucked she did her best to make it interesting.

Sawyer's lectures are very unorganized and hard to follow if you aren't paying attention/don't go to class. However, she is very clear and thorough when answering questions. The questions asked in lecture tend to be what exams are focused around, and she intentionally makes the exams are extremely difficult.

Sawyer is a great professor who cares about her students and pushes them hard. Some of her lectures were pretty fun as well which I haven't seen any other class so far. I think my only complaint with this course it felt like I was putting more than 4 credit hours in for my labs.

I love Sawyer as a person but her lecture style just isn't for me. I find the lectures in this class to be too tangential and disorganized.

However, she very obviously does care about her students. There are tons of resources available to you on the course website and plenty of office hours available with student assistance. Difficult but doable!

Sawyers lectures are great, and she cares a lot about her students. Exams are usually difficult, especailly if you don't do the homeworks (which are very long). Doing omega labs can get you out of the final, but they could definitely be organized better. In general, the class is a lot of work, but Sawyer does a good job helping students through it.

This class was much better than expected with sawyer. There are a lot of resources to make sure you do well. I learned a lot about myself as a student and this class has definitely prepared me for the rest of rpi.

I really enjoyed Sawyer's lectures, she is very in touch with the students in her class and there are lots of opportunities to get points back on homework, projects, AND exams. Not the horrific class everyone says it is if you use the resources given to you and care about the subject.

phenomenal professor, phenomenal engineer and an even more phenomenal person. she challenges her students and tests make you think outside the box, but she gives opportunities to help you improve. she cares about her students and truly wants them to become better. one of the best professors i've had, i wish more were like her.

Circuits with Prof. Sawyer is far from the easiest class I've had in terms of grading, but the workload's not too unreasonable. HW is 2% of course grade and the labs aren't difficult as long as you choose the Alpha option (I pity you if you go for Omega). Lectures are hard to follow, but study material is posted online, including practice exams.
This class needs some better organization. Assignment guidelines are inconsistent and confusing. However her classes are fun and she does a great job at allowing creativity.

Great professor! Very knowledgeable and good at teaching, but: HW is 2%, so it's only worth doing that to study for exams. Labs are a huge time sink, 80% of the effort in the class, but only worth 15%, but getting 80s makes the final optional! The communication and assignments on the website+webex+gradescope makes everything chaotic and confusing..

A charismatic, engaging teacher, but infuriatingly disorganized. Uses a difficult to read website to 'organize' course information. Due dates change regularly and grading is done at the last minute. TONS of group work, so don't get stuck with freeloaders or your semester will be miserable. Stresses communication skills despite her lack thereof.

Sawyer's one of the few professors at RPI who grades hw for completion, which really allows her students to  practice problems instead of fitting a grading criteria. You really feel that she's trying to get you to learn things; She provides plentiful resources, is extremely responsive and reasonable, and brings great energy to every lecture.
This class is very difficult so ample study time is needed. Professor Sawyer is a great lecturer, and teaches the course better than the average professor could.

I really appreciated how Professor Sawyer helped me with my group projects throughout the semester. She was always willing to help and gave good advice. This is a new class structure so this was the beta testing semester and I think it went well. Show up to class and participate and the tests should be quite easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: At the beginning of this course, everything is good, and I could understand almost everything in the class. However, after the second test, the time is not adequate, and she did not teach everything in the class. Instead, she just let us do the examples .. Especially for the last section, she just use 1 week to teach everything....
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Too many tests. She taught nothing on her class, so you should figure out everything by yourself. All her resources are even not written by herself. ECSE made a bad decision on letting her to teach this important class.

It's a tough class, be prepared to put in time with a lab group. You learn a lot if you pay attention, and you definitely should if you want to stay on top of this class. Definitely don't slack off and start your labs early, they're pretty long-winded. Great professor, keeps things interesting during class!
Sawyer is the goat. The class is tough, but you really learn a lot from her.

Professor Sawyer is by far one of the best professors at RPI! I was a student struggling in her class and she was more than helpful in helping me catch up with the material and understand the concepts behind what we were learning. She makes learning circuits really fun and gives lots of opportunities to improve in the course. For exams do backtests

Expect a heavy courseload, but great professor. She really cares about her students and bases things off each individual class that semester (based on lecture questions/discussions, concepts most students are struggling with, etc.) She gives chances to get some points back on tests and offers other extra credit assignments! Overall, LOVE HER
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: A respectful professor but with lots of work.

Professor Sawyer was uncaring, condescending, and assigned more work than all my other courses combined. Her lectures were not particularly insightful and she expected students to come to class having taken notes on 20-30 minutes of videos which were subpar at best. I would avoid Sawyer as best as humanly possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Seems cheery until you realize she is completely unsympathetic to your troubles in the class. Says things aren't mandatory, then they are. Obtuse test grading; bi-weekly labs take 20-30 man-hours each and are barely worth anything. Believes in reversed classroom model despite significant negative feedback. This class is SO MUCH WORK! Never again.
Extremely unprofessional and unfair. Tests are written poorly. Rude to students.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She expects us to know every little movement she does
Terrible lecture notes.
Exam is hard, also no time to work on exam. The lectures are bad, she has ppt but never use it. Only few class problem.

I learned a lot in this class. I put in the work during labs and homework to understand the material and it really showed on the tests. The tests are straight forward and very similar to the homework. There is "class problems" which is mostly what I learned with and are a great resource for studying.

Dr. Sawyer is really nice. She is always willing to help us in many ways to improve our performance. The lectures may not be super-helpful but the supplemental videos can still be of great significance of understanding materials. Tests are not very difficult, try to study hard to push for a good grade!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: The average is really high this semester. Dr. Sawyer gave us cutoffs mid-semester and the cutoffs were a 98 for an A and a 68 to pass. Everyone got anxious, particularly alpha lab students because we have less extra credit opportunities. Seeing the anxiety, she then moved the cutoffs again to reasonable ones. I don't know how I feel about this.
I appreciate how Dr. Sawyer is receptive to student input and actively tries to make ECSE Enrichment Seminar engaging. Plus, her seminar about her own career was wonderful! Would listen to again.
Professor Sawyer grades very fairly. The option between Alpha Labs and Beta Labs was a huge plus.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Electronic Instrumentation was painful for me. I found the experiments/projects conceptually easy, but tediously long and vague. Since there were no in-class lectures, Sawyer was basically a TA. What really made me respect her was when we filled out mid-semester surveys and she took time in class to go over the responses. She actually cares.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: One of the best professors Ive ever had. Homework can be challenging but the team assignments and optional class problems prepare you for them. Cares about her students and wants them to succeed.

If you miss class, it's not the worst thing because of the videos she provides. However, if you fall behind on the material, catch up fast. The homeworks can range from easy to challenging, and may take a good amount of time. Overall, just put effort into the class and you should be fine

Tests are not hard, but homework is quite difficult. You need to watch the video before class to have a good understanding of what she talks about. In class problems are pretty helpful in understanding the complicated concepts. Generally a good teacher.
Not specific about course material. Didn't even explain the main concept of calculation

Good professor. The additional video lectures were incredibly helpful, there was a ton of extra credit, and her explanations during lecture were pretty solid. Make sure you try for a regrade on each test, she's very generous with points and the TA's usually grade them pretty harshly.

She spends a lot of time on the little math and stuff, including in the video lectures (and I mean spending a lot of time to write out the problem... I would prefer not waiting for a problem to be written out and to have more examples that I can go back on as to why something happens). It makes it easier to let your mind wander and then get lost.

Pros:  She's generous with regrading for tests.   Cons: Lot's of formatting errors and typos in assignments and tests. Often will not do a problem all the way out. Review sessions before exams are a waste of time. She doesn't get into detail with the difficult topics because she tries to touch on everything.
She is really nice, talking about her child a lot. Videos are helpful. I don't like the Team Assignment part, kinda hard to do. Be sure to be prepared for class.

Took mathematical physics with him, and it was the most ineffective class I've ever taken in my entire college career. Schroeder will stare at his notes for 2 hours straight, ignore the class, and cancel class with less than an hour warning due to health. Over a month into the course and no hw or syllabus handed out. Class is not his priority.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Avoid him, and you will still do well in the course. His voice is low and hard to hear clearly. He seldom helps his students understand the course materials. All this kind of work is done by his TAs.

I did not take this course but I was a TA. I would highly recommend to NEVER NEVER take a class with him. He's old, mostly deaf, unorganized, and doesn't seem to comprehend the material that he is teaching. I would give him a 0 if the scale worked that way.

Excellent professor, doesn't hold your hand.  You'll have to do a lot of outside reading (think textbooks), but he cites most of his sources and is very approachable, though you'll quickly learn to figure things out for yourself.

Schroeder is a really nice guy. And very trusting of his students. But he is a horrible teacher. I learned absolutely zero optics and practically fell asleep while he recited the words from the power points. On the plus side, he sounds just like Christopher Walken. That's amusing at least.

Well, he's not a bad guy and if you go up to him to ask a question, he'll do his best to explain the answer.  But really, he doesn't teach you much.  For the most part, he reads off of the powerpoint slides.  I can do that myself.  Maybe it was just he way the class was structured, but I didn't get too much from him being my professor.
Assigns difficult homework problems, but grades easy. His exams are fair. He's always willing to help if you can find him. Tells awesome stories.
had him for fundamentals of optics, didnt really learn much from class, he tried to teach us too much.  suppose hed be fine in other classes
He knows what he "teaches," but he doesn't really teach...he just uses power point presentations. He doesn't have office hours this year either... Boring as hell class...ahhh!!

Truly a nice guy, takes time from class to tell stories of World War II, and how his sense of hearing was destroyed by falling bombs, etc. However, he can't teach for his life. He knows the material, but only reads powerpoint, so you might as well just stay home and read the text. Easy class for me, because I had a good background of physics.
Terrible teacher.  He is very boring, relying solely on PowerPoint, like many teachers here.

class was bad. its all derivations, with no turning to look at the students. and the notes didnt help do the homework. very old school. if you go talk to him about a problem, he'll help you, but then you get pulled into long conversation. which is nice unless you're in a hurry. But he's very genuine and nice. Got HW back.. a semester later!
No Comments

Dr. S is an exceedingly nice guy, but boring as all hell.  He has accomplished so much in his life that I guess it doesn't seem worthwhile to keep the (undergraduate) class engaged.  Talk to him at colloquia, but DO NOT TAKE HIS CLASSES.
Hard to understand.  He just reads lectures from the slides provided and could not really tie the lecture notes in with the presentations.
He's a nice guy, but you cannot understand him!
He just reads directly from the slides.  Seems like he doesn't know what he's doing half the time
He is a REALLY nice guy. But, he can't teach. If you take A.Mech., get the Leung notes from an older grad student. He reads directly from them. The tests aren't too bad--open book/notebook.
Nice guy, but couldnt teach physics to Sir Isaac Newton himself! Someone please get this man towel.
one comment: grrr
No Comments
No Comments
Made me hate physics 1 with a passion
overly tardy returning HW and exams, lecture redundant and non-interactive

I took IED with him. It's his first time teaching this course so he tried to show himself off by lowering students' grades and asking unreasonable requirements. This resulted in the average grades of his sections being roughly 10% lower than all other sections.

Great professor. Highly suggest taking IEA with him. He understands the material and understands student's weaknesses which are the most ideal qualities you want in a professor. If you don't understand something, go to office hours. That being said, don't skip lectures and do pre-readings from the textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Too hard
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Great professor for IEA, so dedicated to everyone and makes sure you are all caught up with the material.

Very good prof. Tests are straightforward and overall a good estimation of your apptitude in thermals. He drops the lowest of 3 tests, with each on counting for 25% of the grade, and has a final worth 40%. He covers everything he will test and gives out very useful review. I highly reccomend him unless you struggle with test heavy courses.
Actually horrific- boring, unengaging, rude- even his TAs have no idea what's going on. Save yourself!!

This is the first time I've gone here to rate a professor because I genuinely like his professor really much. He's really nice and I think all his exams are a lot easier than what it could've been. Although he's not very lenient, he makes his course easy enough so that you shouldn't have trouble despite that. I enjoy his teaching style a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: (ENGR-2530) I don't get why everyone is so hard on him, he's a great professor. His setup is good: Lecture, followed by walk-through problems and then a participation/attendance in-class assignment. He understandably gets upset when people aren't paying attention, so no computers in class. He preps you well for exams and wants you to do well too.

I took ENGR2530 (Strengths of Materials), which is not a selectable option.  While he had a rough start, I believe he got better as the semester went on, making less mistakes and giving better explanations.  By the end of the semester, I was perfectly happy in his class.  Occasionally needs to be reminded to center his notes under the projector.
Save yourself and DO NOT take his course. His course is just a disaster.

I took Shenogin for ENGR 2530 (Strengths of Materials), and it didnt help that this was his first time teaching the course. He reads directly off other profesors' slides, focuses more on theory rather than going through examples and makes frequent mistakes when he does do examples.

I have had this professor for both strengths and MAU. He just reads off of other professor's lecture slides and solves problems on his own, often asking the students if he is correct or how to solve something. He makes many mistakes and often has to be corrected. Please do not take his classes unless you want to learn everything yourself.
Please save yourself and take another professor.

He often can't solve problems because he himself doesn't know what he is doing as he is just copying off an answer sheet and blames the students for their low grades. Both of his sections had the lowest class average and still believes it isn't his teaching. Do not take Strength of Materials with this professor as you won't understand anything.

Hard to even understand him and at times has no idea what he's doing, asking students for help multiple times and taking terrible notes. Really no point in attending his lectures, please switch your professor unless you have no problem learning all the material yourself
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Shenogin is an absolute nightmare. He's completely incompetent—can't solve problems, struggles to explain anything, and often asks students for help. I barely scraped by in his MAU class, thanks only to friends with a different professor. Do yourself a favor and stay far away; he made my semester a total disaster.

I had this professor for MAU and he constantly had no clue what he was teaching. Many days he had to ask students for help solving in-class examples. Many people just straight up didn't show up to lecture and I used his lecture time to study other lecture notes. I almost wish I failed this class so that his average class rating would be lower.

I have taken a short intro course at a different college for strength of materials so I was familiar with the content of the first few days but the way he teaches is way too overcomplicated for the content and he is bad at explaining things which makes it impossible to do the homework without going to a TA or another professor.

Professor Shenogin is by far the worst professor I have had at RPI.  He uses the wrong edition of the textbook, ignores his lecture slides, scribbles notes all over messy sheets of paper, and admits he can't solve example problems.  There are no grading criteria for anything, and some of his solutions are incorrect or end with "too complicated".

Easily one of the worst professors I have ever taken at RPI. Lectures are useless, and half the time it doesn't even seem like he knows how to solve the problems. Very messy hand writing and notes. Tests are completely random, in the same section there will be different versions with some easier than others. Would not recommend.

He has absolutely no clue how to solve the example problems, teaches from a textbook different from the one in the syllabus, and grades by writing a score on the paper without posting a rubric or any grading feedback. I went to another section's professor for help with a problem and he said "What is this guy even trying to teach you?"

Took MAU, not IED with him. Awful handwriting and scribbling all over the page. Never posted lecture notes so if you didn't show up to class you had no clue what was going on. Constantly admitted he had no idea how to solve examples and had to get help from students. Also had no idea when/where exams were so had to ask other sections. Avoid. Him.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The IED Pilot course has many flaws and Sergei is the most incompetent person to be teaching it. Yes, he's passionate about teaching and an easy grader but multiple times I've had to remind him when assignments were due and rubric criteria. However, he'd always ask the course coordinator my questions and have extended due dates multiple times.

She was the most empathetic teacher I ever met at RPI, and she really took into consideration every student's individual struggles. Oftentimes my classes were so packed I wouldn't have time to each breakfast or lunch during the day, and one day I legit cried real-ass tears because she let us go early and I was able to grab food. I'll miss her a lot

Seeley is a phenomenal professor. She doesn't care necessarily if you're a "bad" writer; what she cares about is that you improve over the course of the semester because she genuinely wants your writing skills to grow. There aren't many hard deadlines for this class, so it's easy to juggle, and she's very accessible to go over drafts and questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: A caring professor who loves to provide outside assistance when students need help. The course material help my communication skill a lot. Would defnitely take her class.
Great guy, caring and flexible

I found his lectures fascinating. He doesn't just teach from the textbook, but he also tries to incorporate new and up-to-date information form research in the field. The class discussions were incredibly thought-provoking, and even though the class wasn't "difficult" per-se, it was an environment that encouraged and fostered learning.

Had him for PSYC4370 - such a great class & prof. Lectures were interesting & was very fair with grading. He is such a kind & charismatic person, & wants you to succeed. There was pop quizzes almost every week, but as long as you go to lecture & review the slides, you will do fine. Not a lot of assignments but the ones given required time & effort.

prof sims is a great prof. lectures can feel long, but he is really interested in what he is teaching and it definitely helps time go by. quizzes are all open note, but he doesn't always tell you when they'll be (this is how he tries to make sure people go to class). i'd be happy to take another class of his!
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Sims is a good teacher and cares about you as a student. If you have any questions he is easily accessible outside of class. The lectures feel long sometimes but he knows that and tries to make them shorter. He is truly interested in the subject. Would definitely take him as a professor again.
Prof. Simons is great. I highly suggest taking Econometrics for any major- it is a lot of work, but you will learn the material very will. Favorite class so far at RPI.
Do your routine work and get an easy A
Brilliant. I highly recommend any course taught by Prof. Simons.

econometrics is a tough class, a lot of work but if you put the effort in it then you can get an A. he's a really nice guy and really helpful. going to the lectures is not mandatory but STRONGLY recommended. you will get decent amount of in class work and a lot of homework so be prepared. overall it's hard but you will learn a lot of useful stuff
I love industry shakeouts
No Comments
Great professor, really easy to understand.  You definitely want him for Diff Eq
Yes, you want him for DiffEQ.  Clear, and actually teaches very well.  Watch out for flying candy!
Very clear to understand. Goes through the proof of all the equations that you need to know. Also, very clear to understand.

Professor Siegmann is without doubt a genius at mathematics He is funny and really enthusiastic. (He gives out candy!) At the beginning of each class he reviews the previous lesson, which is very helpful. If you get lost, you can ask questions during class or during his office hours. Just do the hws and read through the notes to ace the class.
very clear and personable

The genome and you: great lectures and we had interesting discussions on the class topics. Small amounts of pre-class readings and two exams but she grades them very fairly and they are exactly on the topics she emphasizes in class. Very understanding as a professor and she cares about her students, still waves to me around campus a year later.

Professor Smith was incredible for Science Misconduct. Her course was engaging, the workload was fair, and Professor Smith led great class discussions. Her passion for the subject rubs off on the class, and she gives fantastic advice with your presentation and papers. I suggest everyone take this class, as science ethics are important to learn.
If you read the books, go to class, and participate in discussions, you will love Dr. Smith. She is by far one of the nicest professors I have ever met. Her reviews speak for themself.

Amazing professor who really respects and cares about her students. Would always bring interesting and applicable news/additional info to class and always understood if students showed up late/needed extensions. Overall just amazing course that felt super useful for critical thinking of science and an amazing prof. 100/10 recommend.

Susan gives high school teacher vibes- always checking in with you and genuinely caring about you. She is great for the Genome and You inquiry class and I hope to have her again in the future. Make sure you study for her exams but if you put effort in, she will reward it!

She is extremely caring about her students and always asks how we're doing. The class is extremely easy and before tests just look over the lecture slides. Sometimes the lectures were a little boring but there was a lot of interesting material! Would definitely recommend her class!

Dr. Smith is the most caring professor I've had yet, repeatedly pushing deadlines back if she learned that her students' other classes had a lot going on. Her course is highly engaging, and I never struggled to pay attention in class. All assignments are fair and reasonable, and her grading is not harsh in the slightest. Highly interesting course.

This class you are going to learn a lot about hard topics, but this is a class I would recommend to anyone. Tests are easy as long as you show up and participate in class, open note so make sure you take some. Otherwise there were a few assignments the big kicker is the final paper. As long as you do a draft like she asks you'll get it done.
Great lectures. Super fun and easy to understand. Will be more classes with her later.

Not only is Dr Smith very knowledgeable, but she really does care about her students. She always checks up on us at the beginning of class. Her feedback is very helpful, and she makes every lecture interesting. I also don't think she's a tough grader at all, and she's definitely willing to help out if you need it!

She is the absolute best! She did an amazing job, especially considering that she wasn't even meant to teach this class and got dropped in as the prof 2wks into the semester. She's smart, honest, and incredibly caring - she genuinely wants you to learn and understand the material, and she makes sure you know how to apply the info to the real world.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Her Genome and You class was very fun and professor Smith is very good at what she does. The class taught me a lot ethical problems surrounding advancing technology and the human genome. Very informative class and I look forward to taking her bioethics class in a later semester.

Easily the best professor I've had at RPI. Genuinely cares about her students, is flexible with deadlines, and is a moderate grader. Is full of information and will definitely give interesting lectures about relevant material. 10/10
Absolutely amazing professor, best professor I've ever had. Cares about students wellbeing in and outside of class. Learned so much, incredibly interesting lectures.

i love dr. smith. the material she teaches is fantastic and is definitely needed at RPI. she is super caring, understanding, and her classes are easy to engage in. you'll have to be able to write a good paper, but i recommend her classes to everybody.

Dr. Smith is fabulous! What a great course. Lectures cover a lot of information but are very interesting. Attendance not required but I often looked forward to coming to class so I went. Tests are of average difficulty, pretty easy if you study, and she has extra credit questions. Some writing and reading.

It is clear that she loves what she teaches and has a real passion for the subject. I would describe her grading as tough but fair. If you don't know the material, you don't know it. She assigns a few books to read some chapters from. It is not mandatory that you read them, so don't stress. But reading the chapter will help with participation.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Sotoudeh is very nice person, but during class she doesn't look that way. She gets upset that people are not participating in class. All you have to do to succeed is pay attention during her lectures and do the homework. Everything is done in WileyPlus. The tests are very similar to the homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: She is a very good professor. She is flexible if you have special circumstances outside of class. You will earn a good grade in her class if you do your homework. Her tests are very similar to the assigned homework. She is even better during office hours. I wish I could take her for more classes. I took her for 326,327 and 329

I honestly don't know why Dr. Sotoudeh has bad ratings on here. She is by far one of the most caring professors and all she wants you to do is succeed. I don't think people understand that her teaching style is active learning, meaning you do HW, figure it out, or ask for help. Lecture is only there to introduce the concept to be applied.

She is very caring and makes sure you know the subject but you will need to participate. She is very very academic and her lectures are dry. the first half of the subject is actually easy to understand. After chapter 4 if your on wiley(online txt book) then the subject gets very difficult to understand. I highly recommend going to SI.

Yells at her class, asked her friend to ask our class what she could improve upon, then purposefully sabotaged our class by changing the entire structure of the class and told us "well you guys wanted this right?"She likes math more than dynamics, so instead of teaching you a simple procedure, she spends too much time deriving everything in class.

She explains concepts very well and cares if you understand the material or not. For homework, she only assigns about 4 problems or less. This quarter we started turning in hw online. Also sometimes she has class activities for a few points. In the class activities you try to solve an example on your own but does not care if it is right.
Easy A

She's OK. Here grading criteria is very specific. What I mean by that is that you need to follow her solution to a T. She is a bit unclear during Lecture and doesn't explain the whole picture behind a problem. That said her exam problems are fairly easy. She uses linear algebra in her class. Overall I barely learned anything from her.
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Her lectures are good but she grades very harshly on the exams. A simple mistake can be detrimental to your exam grade with her. She tries her best, the main issue is the grading. Good prof but discourages students with her grading.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: I took a few classes of Dr. Spina-Caza's and she's honestly an amazing professor. She really looks out for her students and genuinely cares about each of them. As long as you demonstrate effort and learning then you'll be fine in the class. She gives good feedback and guidance too so I'd take advantage of it while you can.

I took Professor Spina-Cazas Writing for the Screen course Spring 2020. I really enjoyed the outline of the class and all the work we were assigned. She is very understanding, coherent and truly teaching something that is very interesting. In this day and age, we are constantly surrounded by screens. I learned a lot and had a great time.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Group projects

reviews.comment: I took 3 classes with Prof. Spina-Caza and I always enjoyed them. She is understanding and goal oriented, and easy to talk to. I do think sometimes the assignments can be a unclear, but it's easy to ask for clarification. Most classes with her you'll be working in groups to some capacity... which can be the most frustrating part. Good practice tho
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--So many papers

reviews.comment: Really really nice woman, gives lots of constructive feedback in a really positive way. Not too hard of a grader either. Class as decently entertaining, but the projects were the heavily-graded part of the class, which required a fair amount of outside work. Overall, great choice of professor and class.

There isn't an overbearing amount of writing. I wrote 3 journals, each 700-800 words. The most time-consuming work you'll do are group projects. I presented twice with my group, and each presentation was 20-25 minutes long on theories that you find in the book. Spina-Caza is nice but her lectures are dry and a bit boring. You have to read to pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Professor Spina-Caza is generally pretty lazy with her course construction. She creates arbitrary guidelines for presentations and a lot of the course has to do with busywork. Primarily, the course follows the trend of having the student do the reading, and then the professor tests you on it and covers the content again in class. Very frustrating.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: The content is easy and she's a nice person. However, the class is terrible. This was my most-hated class this semester and I'm a comm major. The work never ends, and basically all of it is stressful and has a ton of requirements that are difficult to meet. It felt like busywork rather than actual learning material, and I was burned out by October.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: She does an amazing job teaching. I have taken COMM 1510,  4550, and 4960, all of which have been largely group-based. This tactic allows you to build valuable skills regarding working with others. She is extremely open to talking with students, whether it is about saying hello or about grades. The courses also apply to real-world applications.

Course involved a lot of reading&discussion, w expected amounts of writing. Interesting content - assts allow you to take control based on your interests. With careeffortrespect for materialquestions you'll do well. Prof SC is passionate & knowledgeable within video comm & crisis comm; also kind-hearted. No "bs" humanities w SC you will LEARN!

For a professor of Communication, she sure SUCKS at it. Assignments are pretty vague, and then she gets pissed that she didn't get what she wanted from you. Also, she's irritatingly condescending. Oh, and she doesn't teach. She makes you read the text and then has the TA do the rest.

Professor Spooner was one of the better professors I've had at RPI. He really knows what he's talking about, so his lectures are really informative. His class is also pretty easy which is a nice perk. Be aware of the 30 min solo pres you give at the end of the semester. Overall, he's a great guy who knows how to teach effectively. Would recommend.
Great sleep therapy class.
average. his lectures put me to sleep.
Very nice guy, helpful.
very good explanations
Decent professor but kinda boring and that unfortunate lip problem he has is distracting.
His lectures are quite good, but it seemed to me that tests weren't quite matched to them...  He always seems to have a whitish something on the left corner of his mouth.
No Comments
No Comments
No Comments
good professor ....but puts me to sleep
No Comments
No Comments
Helped me when I needed it, very prompt, courteous, pleasant, and clear.
easy course and very clear teaching method
No Comments
Fair professor, good teacher, easy exams
Really helpful.   Relatively easy.  Exams are fair.

The class can get a bit dull at points.  It seems like a lot of the information could be left out to get to the main point.  But overall it's a decent class.  Tests aren't too hard because you get to make a cheat sheet.  The projects are so vague, take forever to finish, and are graded ruthlessly by the TA (who is no help).  Homework is a pain too.
Nice guy. Pretty good teacher. Explains things pretty well, answers questions in class. Tells you pretty much exactly what to expect on exams.
No Comments

Spilker's IEA class is fairly boring but only because it is IEA.  I think he is a good teacher and he covers the material very in depth.  Seems like a helpful guy although I have not visited his office hours.  Unfortunately IEA is really boring.  Bring your laptop and do other homework during class!

He's very clear about everything he explains, but he doesn't really teach you how to fend for yourself -- he definitely treats you like a freshman (good or bad? You decide). I could do everything well IN class, but he did easy examples. As soon as I was out of class, different story. Do the homework sooner than the night before or you'll lose it.

Helpful guy, in advising as well as in class time.  Tried his best not to read too much from IEA slides, helped students as well.  Didn't even collect class activities.  However, if you're not interested in IEA from the get-go, he's not going to make it especially interesting.  You do have to keep your own.

Its not his fault the class sucks and is boring... once we got started he tailored the class to fit our needs,.... its just not an easy class.... i thought he was a pretty good teacher teaching crappy material.... GO TO THE EXTRA HELP SESSIONS IF YOU WANT TO PASS THE CLASS!!!
not recommended if u plan to absorb anything in class.  outside class he's nice.  but strength is just not his thing...
Lecture is boring, tests aren't horrible
Seemed to be a pretty nice guy, but had boring lectures.  Having the class at 8 in the morning didn't help.  If you do have him, make sure to go to his office - he's a lot more helpful there.
he jumps around the lecture and can easily confuse you... but is very open to helping you outside of class.... has a funny and great personality... take it for who he is and have fun....
He's a mess.  Class is hard to follow b/c he rushes through everything.  He is approachable and a nice guy, however IEA isn't that hard and he makes it seem like it is.

Spilker is overall a good guy.  He gets a little frazzled at times, so it gets a little confusing.  IEA isn't difficult to begin with though so it's not bad.  If you need help with anything, just ask.  He's good at explaining specific things to one or two people.
I agree -- he was very approachable and also friendly.
Spilker's really helpful, approachable, and clear. He is concise and easy to understand. IEA really isn't that difficult to begin with but Spilker makes it even easier.
No Comments
He's the best nuclear engineering professor at RPI.
(Fuel Management) Very interesting class, very easy if you pay attention.
Can't say enough good things about this Professor.  Extremely helpful and wants students to learn. Laid back, relaxed and extremely intelligent.  Take his classes!
easy materials taught not understandable way. hardly understand his lecture.. sorry

Amazing class. The homework made me think and helped me understand everything I'd learned up to that point. Sreepada is a great teacher; he knows everything there is to know about nuclear and draws on a wealth of real-world experience. Available and friendly in office hours, he's a great resource for all nukes and loves discussing nuclear stuff.
God tier professor at rpi if there is such a thing.

Taught this course straight from Podowski's notes, but it was still awesome. Very intelligent, gave clear examples and fair exams & HW. Related topics in class to real-world applications. Very helpful in & out of class. Only complaint is that he listed a $91 textbook as 'required' and then never used it.
Sastry is the man! I don't know how he got stuck teaching MODCON, but he is a wealth of knowledge and very approachable with regards to his nuclear classes. Highly recommend if you're a nuke.

Great teacher. Could tell when I couldn't understand something in class, very smart and very good at explaining material. Kept class lively with jokes, didn't mind it when you pointed out his mistakes. Zero tolerance for late homework, but otherwise laid back & a fun guy to talk to. Posted HW solutions and lecture notes helped a LOT.

Fuel management was a good class and fairly easy if you took good notes. He did a good job getting to the main points of the material as well as alluding to all the different directions you could do further study in.

Interesting class and fairly easy. Practice tests are almost identical to exams. Textbook was used for about 3 homework problems the whole semester- essentially worthless. Kind of quiet and hard to understand, but writes lots of notes to cover the concepts.

Very understanding of your troubles.Teaches relavent information and relates it to real life application. He is very good with thermal hydraulics and could probably teach it to a level as advanced as you would like it to be. He is also very good with answering your questions in person or by email.
Hard to understand...

Schmidt felt like a really easy professor, yet I always left his classes and tests feeling like I knew the material. He makes mid-level undergrad math about as approachable as it can be, fun lectures and well made tests, that are easy if you get how the concept works. There's also room for bonus points on tests. One of the best RPI math professors.

All I did was show up and pay attention. He conveys the material in a way that is clear and easy to understand. Only downside was Covid cutting us off, to which he posted his lecture notes online. While instruction was still clear, losing the lectures was disappointing, to say the least.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Solid lectures, easy tests that are like the same as the backtests. One of the few professors I felt was really fair with students.

If you're taking Multivar, Schmidt is the way to go. His lectures are pretty interesting, but the only thing that matters is if you can get back tests -- exams are almost identical to previous semesters.

Lectures are very good and clear, both in content and in terms of speaking. The exams are very similar to old exams and the quizzes are generally pretty easy while teaching you how to do the math. Can be a little theory heavy and does not post notes or homework solutions online.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Lectures are like youtube tutorials on multivar, tests are easy, just like the homeworks (and similar to what is discussed in class). The final is just test questions from previous exams. No required homework. Easy quiz in recitation. Learned a lot and very easy class.
Schmidt has very clear notes and lectures. Homework is not mandatory. Quizzes and Tests are very straight forward.
Learn how to do all the back test questions and you will get an A easily
Straight out amazing. One of the best professor you get in RPI.

Extremely clear lectures. Gives lots of examples and will always ask if people have questions to make sure nobody is confused. For tests, go over one or two back exams and you're set since he keeps the same problems and equations but just changes the numbers

Probably the best/easiest RPI prof. for any MATH course. Tests are easy and simple but he doesn't give back exams, so study. HW is optional, but if you do that and show up for recitation you should be good. Do go to class and take notes, his notes are on the overhead projector so not posted online. Gives a review before exams too.

He is such a nice guy that I thought he might be the best among the math department. A really good lecturer and really kind to his students. The tests are not very tough and I don't think you will get a bad grade after reviewing all the questions he gives to you!

Overall, great professor. The initial lectures before a test are more conceptual and intangible in nature but as the test gets closer becomes more concrete with problems appearing straight on the exam. DEFINITELY check out the backwork before taking the tests. Blue matrix algebra book helpful for the final.
Prof. Schmidt was the best professor I ever had at RPI. His lectures were easy to follow, his course was well designed, and he genuinely seemed to care about his students. I highly recommend him.

He focuses on the "why" a little bit more than the "how." He wants to make sure you have a full understanding of the class, and why everything operates in the way that it does. Excellent teacher who makes sure everyone understands the content before continuing to more complex concepts.

Stupidly good, plain and simple. Lectures are insanely clear, extremely well organized, and well-suited for any lvl of student. Very willing to answer questions, and always gives a thorough answer. Focuses more on intuition than formulas, great for those looking for a deep understanding, even for applications beyond the course material.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Schmidt's lectures are insanely clear, he asks questions to ensure no one is confused, and holds a class prior to exams to just work through problems. If you do more than 2 backtests before an exam, you're guranteed to pass. Wish I had him for every math course.

Schmidt is a real gem. I would have taken his Multivar class this semester but his class was filled before I could register for it. Also he's very friendly and super chill. One of the best professors I've ever had. Explains all content very clearly, and always sticks around after class to answer questions
Bless this amazing gentleman. The real mvp.
He is a caring professor and explains the topics lucidly. Taking notes in that class is essential if you want the A

Professor Schmidt is by far the most articulate professor I've had so far. He's the only math teacher/professor I've ever had that explains topics clearly, but more importantly he wants to make sure everyone understands WHY a particular theorem is the way it is. I would DEFINITELY take another class with him and I highly recommend him.

Schmidt is a good guy, but beware because he doesn't use LMS, so it might be difficult to balance focusing and note taking. I've heard this class is easier with another prof if you haven't taken Calc AB. Quizzes are no partial credit which sucks, but the exams are pretty straightforward. His handwriting might be one of his most redeeming qualities

Dave Schmidt is one of my favorite professors I've had so far. I've taken classes with him twice now (Calculus 2 MATH1020 and Multivariable Calculus) and I find his lecturing style very easy to follow. Plus, he's very accessible outside of class, and it's obvious that he cares deeply about his students.

It's probably okay if you don't want to show up to lectures--the only things you're graded on are your tests and quizzes. But going to the lectures makes things simple. Course material is clearly presented and explained, homework questions are provided for practice and questions are always answered.

In my 3 years at RPI, no other professor came close to Schmidt's clarity. He answers any potential questions you may have before you can even ask them! His exams are fair. He doesn't try to trick you. He cracks jokes in lecture from time to time and does not acknowledge them. His swag knows no bounds. I wish I could take this class again.
Excellent instructor! Very clear during lecture!
Great professor. Lectures are clear and understandable.

Professor Schmidt was a good professor for Multivariable CalcMatrix Algebra. Found the matrix algebra portion of the class to be somewhat more difficult but will vary for each student. Lectures are fast paced but he is very helpful in office hours and very approachable after class. Tests and quizzes are the only graded work.
Great teacher! Very clear and uses straight forward examples!

It might be surprising but you cannot float on prior knowledge of the material. Homework is optional but don't skip over it. Class is kind of dull but overall he really is not bad. Don't take him for all calc i, ii, multivar though unless you want to. Mix it up and see how the other professors work too. He is a good professor

Lectures are boring.  He's the most monotone teacher I've had and it's hard to stay awake if you go to class.  Tests are 80% the back test which is good but I still wish I took the class with khiel because i learned nothing.  I've heard he's much better for mutivar.

Great professor.  Possibly the best lecturer I've encountered, giving crystal clear proofs and explanations.  Also very good at answering questions asked by students in class (I find many professors don't answer the question asked.  Homework is optional, but also is very helpful for test preparation.  Highest of recommendations for this professor.

Schmidt is the bomb.  Like a nuclear bomb.  Or like a hydrogen-cobalt bomb.  Either way, he is a great teacher.  To succeed in his classes, at least in multivar, do the optional homework, do the quizzes, and go to his study sessions before each test.  He has got his stuff together and annihilates any weak points math students may have.  Praise Dave
Schmidt is great. Easy to understand and breaks things down into very simple ideas. His tests are fair and representative of what you do in class and for homework.
Schmidt is amazing and the best professor I've ever had. alsew hot
Great explanations of topics. Sometimes too in depth but always teaches thoroughly. Tests are slightly difficult but if you do homework well you will do fine on tests.

I've had Prof. Schmidt for two consecutive semesters and to tell you the truth, his lectures are boring. (he doesn't let you play on phone/electronic devices too), but his tests are really easy once you do few hw problems from the textbook. He also know what he's talking about, but might seem confusing or boring to some. He's awesome!
No submission of homework

Excellent lecturer, homeworks are extremely useful for studying. Tests are somewhat easy depending on how well you know the material (no absurd amounts of work for a question), but he's a harsh grader.
It's the best math teacher I've ever met! His lecture is clear and the homework is really helpful to gain an A!

To teach a class such as calculus,such a crystal clear professor is essential.He explains things so well in class,with a great number of examples,that I didn't exactly have to study outside of class.I really liked how instead of just giving the students formulas to use,he explained how to derive them.This way,I was able to remember them better!
Great guy.  After sleeping through a test, I went to office hours and he let me take it no problem.
Crystal clear lecturer. Runs a great class. Personable. What else are you looking for? Actually that brings me to another point, girls think he's hot.

I had Schmidt for Calc II, and he was pretty much the best thing that could have happened for me.  He has a gift for explaining things in a way that most people can understand.  His level of clarity is far beyond any other professors I've had here.  I would recommend him for any math class you're taking.
Very helpful in class, answers are very detailed. However, when he is sick, he tends to be very loud about it; be warned! Seriously though, he is a great professor.
Awesome Discrete prof
Professor is probably one of the most knowledgable math people I know. Is very smart and enjoys teaching. Tests aren't too bad either.
Great teacher, easy to understand, approachable. No curving though.
This is by far the best professor I had in RPI. Had him for Calculus and DFQs back in the day and when I am in town I go to one of his lectures just for fun... Kudos for Schmidt...
Great for Calc II, boring for Discreet. That might not be his fault though, that's just a terrible class.
Great teacher. Very clear on how to solve problems, tons of in-class examples, and having frequent quizzes with no required homework was better than the opposite.
I like his class ;)
he is amazing
A freakin math yoda. Very clear, step-by-step, and good handwriting too. The best.
This man is a living math GOD. He is perfect to learn from and other professors wish they could be him. :) Schmidt is the man!

very awesome teacher. he knows his math, AND he knows how to teach to students, two qualities that often do not come together. He actually answers your questions in class, rather than just re-stating what he has just said in lecture. very, very, very, good, especially if you are not doing so hot with your math grades.

Took calc 1 and IDS with him...  I have a general dislike for math, but Schmidt clearly explained everything and where it came from. I passed the class no problem by attending and paying attention. tho doing the optional homework would most likely have improved my grade  Best teacher I've had at RPI. would take his classes anytime

Calculus II was an interesting course. Schmidt is an awesome teacher, and his TAs were awesome too (Joanie and Kai at the time). I learned a lot in his class, though at times I felt like things were coming out of left field (like when we were expected to know L'Hospitals). I think doing the optional homework would have helped a bit though, lol.
Best prof ever,even though I hate math.
I felt that he was very clear when explaining new topics in a way that I understood them. It was not an easy class, but if you want to learn then this is the class that you can excel in.

His lectures are easy to follow and he explains the material very clearly. The homework is optional, but does a good job of preparing you for the exams, which are pretty straightforward. As long as you attend lectures or work the homework problems, it's a very easy class. I took two courses with him and would be happy to take another.
Although classes are very boring, he knows his stuff. The tests were fair but the final was much harder than the class ever was.
Fantastic teacher. Clear, helpful, and a little bit funny. his videos are the best study tool ever. When you're in class you don't realize that you're learning, but you really are.
Awesome professor, really easy to understand and his tests aren't that bad.
Best professor by far. Easy to understand. Tests are easy.
I dont think he liked me much, but I still have to admit he was a fantastic math teacher, probably the best one at rpi.

Is the second best professor I've ever had... even through my master's degree. I have never seen such a man in academia with that dedication and knowledge of the material and the way he is able to project himself to the class and deliver the material in a clear, understandable way. I wish I could go back and sit in one of his lectures.

I had Prof Schmidt during my undergraduate degree at RPI for Calculus I,II, and Discrete Structures.  He is an excellent teacher and seems to enjoy it.  I highly recommend his courses.  Top 5 RPI professor.

Schmidt is popular because he gives straightforward tests and explains everything clearly and concisely, even though he takes the time to prove some equations which can be a bit tedious.  He is excellent at math and has an above average vocabulary.  For me, Schmidt is the epitome of a great teacher.  He knows where many student's difficulties lie.
Discreet structures; I wouldn't buy the textbook, you wont need it.  Prof. Schmidt explains everything quite clearly.
WOW... best math teacher i've ever had. I thought i knew calc before taking his class but I was wrong.  His videos for diff eq. are also extremely helpful.

Definitely the best teacher at RPI. My weak background in Calculus strengthened exponentially (pun intended) after taking his course. His test problems are very fair. No monkey wrenches or tricks thrown in. I don't advocate skipping recitation and skills classes, but his lectures are all you need. Very systematic and clear. Thumbs up all the way!

I came into Schmidt's class without ever haven taken Calc and a weak base in Precalc. In class, I feel he skips steps a lot. I learned more easily from tutors, but overall, his tests are A LOT easier than the other Calc teacher's. Problems on his tests are pretty much similar if not exactly the same as the backtests.
i'm using his DiffEQ videos because my DiffEQ prof is aweful at life
We wish, One day every professor will bacame a SCHMIDT !!.

I took his classes in the Fall 00 & Spring 01. I can still remember the HOT prof! He provides clear notes. His exams are super easy. Once I didn't go to his class, and he was okay with it. He explained things over again to during office hours. But the question is, are easy exams good for students? Will students learn much?
Goes slow, clarifies even the simplest points. Tests are decent as long as you understood what was going on in the class.
Professor Schmidt is amazing. I'm taking my fourth class with him now. The man's a god.
Professor Schmidt is a whiz at providing exceedingly useful, informative, and clear lectures and fair exams.  He is a model for RPI math professors.
SCHMIDT = GOD.  Enough said.
WOW..best math teacher on campus. Hands down.
WOW! Best math teacher here...perhaps the best teacher here in general.
With all the hype, I think you can see hes a good professor. He's very clear and thoughtful in his presentations.

He is hands down the best calculus teacher in the world. He teaches super basic and easy stuff; he's really REALLY good at explaining it. AND he posts videos of him doing common problems online. So you NEVER have to go to class and you can still get an A. All I did was watch the videos before each test and I averaged a 100. Praise be to Schmidt. :)
Prof Schmidt is the best teacher i have ever had...ever!  He explains everything clearly, and has really nice handwritting too. I recommend him to anyone who has an opportunity to have him! : )
The way he teaches makes you understand.  Even if you don't think you get it, you really are learning.  He's amazing like that.

Excellent teacher! Very clear lectures and fair tests. Homework sheets list problems on the book that are generally doable without a calculator. EXTREMELY helpful during office hours--he caught me up on three weeks of material in half an hour. Highly recommended overall.

Schmidt is the man! He is very clear, and explains things very well. Also great to listen to him talk... if you watch his lectures, he talks JUST like that in class. It's rather soothing. He has perfect handwriting, and writes out everything so you have time to take good notes. Exams are tough and tricky though.

He is the best teacher that I've ever had. He clearly explains everything and does great examples. His videos are great too. If you have the option to take a class with him, do it. He not only makes it easy to learn and really understand the material but he also makes it interesting.
great prof! knew what he was talking about and he KNOWS HOW to teach it too!

I didnt have him but Schmidt videos saved my life.  I thought my friends were on something when they were excited about watching a prof. work out porblems online but there is reason for excitment.  They somehow are interesting and very very very helpful
Schmidt is the man.  Seriously, he teaches well, exams aren't hard, and he doesn't put people to sleep in my experience (unlike other professors here) and knows what he's doing.
SCHMIDT IS SIMPLY THE MAN
Seriously, this man is the best teacher I've ever had. Very clear and organized. His classes may seem easy, but he explains the material so well that you just have to know what you're doing.
Schmidt = God

Quite possibly the easiest class I've taken at RPI, yet I still feel I learned a great deal of information.  He organizes his lectures well, is fair with his tests, and gives optional homework.  Recitation complemented lecture perfectly.  I recommend this class for all engineers to take to enhance their math knowledge.
BEST MATH TEACHER EVER. Clear.
a wonderful teacher, makes everything easy to understand. If you can manage it in your schedual take theis prof for as many math classes as you can!!
Awesome prep before exams, makes sure you know how to do every type of problem, no suprises on tests. Explains as much as necessary to make sure you understand, best math prof around
He's really hot and good. AND 110/100.
No Comments
awesome teacher
The tests are pretty easy, he does lots of examples, and everything you need to know is in the notes.  Just go to class and do the homework!  Some of the TAs are a little difficult though.
schmitty is the man!  he's the best math teacher ever.  his lectures are super clear and easy to follow... take his classes!  i wish he taught diff eq

Schmidt is the best math professor at RPI, it's as simple as that.  I got an A in diffEQ with a totally horrible professor after taking Calc I and II with Schmidt because he prepares you well.  Very very fair.  Also, if you need DiffEQ help he has long distance learning videos online that are a total godsend.

Prof Schmidt has a voice that put me to sleep,but his class isn't bad. Be respectful in class. Turn off your cell phone, don't come in late and DON'T TALK. Having a good or bad TA can make a difference. Stick with the hw and you are golden. Most people blow off the lectures and get behind. Don't do that! You'll have a HUGE advantage.
Great at explaining things in a way that makes sense, and not at all boring to listen to.  The classes (Calc 1 & 2, and MultiVar) are pretty easy, too.
explains everything in a simple way , easy to follow and understand, tests are reasonable, mostly on what's done in class. nothing dramatic

take schmidt for any math class that you need to take that he offers.  best professor for math at the school, hands down.  some call him boring, but its just cause he does his job and you learn the information.  clear as that.
had him three semesters in a row- calc 1,2, and Diff Eq-- and he was the most amazing professor.. very awesome
Simply amazing.  Fair tests for all.  Fair grading.  Very easy to understand.  Great professor.  The best math professor at RPI for Calc II
Didn't realize how much I liked his class till I took Diff Eq with another professor (Kovacic). I would give anything for shmidt! The best applied math professor at RPI!
great explanations
Schmidt is as good as they get. He was excellent back when I took Calc 2... and his online videos saved me from certain doom in Diff Eq. Thanks Dave!!
Simply the best. Fair test and grading system.
He did alright. He really is a walking textbook - he knows his stuff. Probably the best prof if you are looking to learn the material.
He will blow your mind with made-up math words.  Excellent.
Awesome professor.  Highly reccomended.  Very soothing voice, if he wasnt a math teacher, he would def. be reading audio books professionally.  Peace!
d-schmidt is the man...he is a walking textbook!
I didn't like how he speaked at first, but you start to appreciate how he orders things as time goes. Plus he saves lives in Diff EQ
He's not that good!
No question, he is the best!

There's just something about him. He is the clearest, most even-toned individual you will ever hear speak.  It's almost to the point of being creepy.  You will never miss a word he says.  He does do a wierd flick think with his pens though.  I found that distracting.
He is a great professor, as clear as they get and is more than fair on his exams. Taking him will be a good investment in the money you put into RPI
One word AWSOME
Best Prof at RPI (a school filled with horrible professors)
dave is the man.  had him for both calc one and two and if it wasnt for the goddamn gateway wouldve easily had A's in both.  he is very intelligent and is a great teacher.  grades fairly as well
Hard to find a better calc I teacher.  Good notes, easy to understand.
Great professor, easy to understand.
The nicest and most organized professor at the institute.

schmidt is the man.  best math teacher at rpi.  simple, kinda funny, smart, and crystal clear in every single lecture.  if you get a chance to have him as a teacher, dont pass it up.  schmidt you the man.
Best math teacher at rpi.

Compared with other professors at RPI, Professor Schmidt is amongst the very best at teaching. His lectures are crystal clear, the format of the course is very straight forward, no tricks. Tests are fair and follow the lectures very closely.
Great guy. Explains stuff clearly and taught very useful material. Get him as a prof. if you can.
Prof. Schmidt is great, his tests are fair and he covers the material in multiple ways so you are sure to understand it.
"He has one of the most soothing math voices you'll ever hear." >>>>>> He's helpful, clear, and he sounds like he should be on the radio.
Is extremely clear in his lectures. If you go to class and study your notes his tests will not drop many surprises on you. Great teacher.

Best professor there is at RPI, exams are more than fair, and he covers material very clearly.  If you need help he can teach help you learn anything during his office hours.  Very good at teaching!  and a very nice guy on top of that
very clear, the best teacher i've had at rpi
Good teacher, lectures are interesting.  Fair tests.
good teacher, no bullsh*t, very fair tests and grading
Great professor, teaches very clearly, good dry sense of humor, very reasonable tests that are easy if you pay attention in class, highly recommended.
Very easy for calc 2, very nice guy too.  Explains things very well.  Best math teacher I've ever had.
Very good teacher. Explains everything very clearly in lecture; altough sometimes seems so clear can lead to false sense of security. Highly recommended!
Great teacher, explains well without rushing, little bit of a boring voice but does many examples and is very helpful. one of the better teachers at RPI.
Monotomic voice at times but he makes sure you understand what your learning.  Very good teacher, you learn alot but it doesn't seem like he's rushing through it.
spends a lot of time on un-important topics

Very good lecturer. Explains the material clearly and concisely. I thought multivar would be hard, but he has made it seem easy because he's so good at teaching it. Also very friendly and grades leniently.
dave schmidt is the coolest guy in the world. and also the only one who has ever been able to teach me calculus. he is nice, understanding, and very helpful and will go out of his way for you.
Professor was helpful.
AWESOME prof! So clear
very clear, does proofs for everything
I recommend Schmidt for any Math course. Believe me, if you can't get a good grade in his class, you wouldn't in the other ones either. Speaks so clearly and softly in lecture I'd often fall asleep.
i studied a lot and still didnt do as well as i wanted to... it sux that most ppl who do well r taking calc after taking ap... ppl like me get screwed occasionally
Had him for calc I and II and I can honestly say that I hated it.  Bad Prof, no matter what anyone else says.
He is awesome....i took 2 classes with im...Calc 1 and Diff Eq....he is very personable...very approachable...if u are good to him hes good to u ...
Yes im one of the few schmidt grads. Two semesters with this guy, and it was well worth it, teaches what u need to know and a great guy. Stop by his office hours good guy to talk to.
TAKE MATH CLASSES WITH SCHMIDT!!! If you put any effort into the class and do homework, you WILL get an A. Its not that the material is easy; he is a really good teacher.
The best teacher in the entire department.
best prof ever. made freshman year way easier. if you do really bad in its class its your own fault
He was very clear in explaining the material, and the tests were never a surprise (and fairly easy).

This class was simply TOO EASY. All his tests are out of 105 so you have 5 points to mess up with and still get a 100. Not hard material at all. He explains things very well and is just an easy prof in general. Best math prof I've had by far.
never showed up to class and still got an A just from reading my buddy's notes

Great Prof.
Nice Guy. Excellent Teacher. Great Attitude.
Hands down the best all around professor at RPI.

got in A in calc 1 with him, now i'm in his calc 2 class. hopefully i'll get an A or B. gives good notes and helpful review problems before exams. an A or B is possible in this class, unlike with most classes here.
by far the easiest class I've ever taken, mostly because it was schmidt.  actually, he was a little TOO easy - my test avg was above 100 which is about 30 pts higher than most classes
SCHMIDT-Y BABY!!!! Dude is awesome. The bomb math prof...man I got As because he conveyed the material oh so well. I say we nominate him for Math Dept Chair!!! Gooood guy. Has a heart. FINALLY!

I don't know what everyone's raving about, he's OK, but I've had better teachers.

Schmidt is awesome. A really good teacher and he says weird funny things all the time.
