My favorite professor on campus. Genuinely cares about his students.

The stuff we went over in Writing for Games was immediately applicable to my Game Dev 1 class, which helped me feel like I was helpful even as a writing concentration. You basically do a project for each step of the game writing process (pitching, beat sheets, and scripting) and you learn about industry tests, aka how you would actually get hired.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I hesitated between 3 and 4 because the class was very good but way too easy. Some students got very good despite their lack of work. But apart from that, Professor Suckling knows what he is talking about, he is on my top 3 at GSAS.

Maurice's Intro to Game Storytelling is great. Easy A. I took it during a tough semester and it gave me a nice break from my other classes. He assigns several short essays throughout the semester and pretty much your entire grade is based on the quality of your writing. He's a pretty chill dude. 10/10 would take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Caring

reviews.comment: Had Maurice for Intro to Game Storytelling and Game Narrative Design. Very nice professor, his classes are mostly based on essays and as long as you stay on topic (focusing on the narrative), then you'll get good grades. Game Narrative Design you literally just play board games in, probably the best class I've ever taken.

She was so nice at the beginning. Then she started to give us so many assignments/projects/essay at the end of the semester. There was one time that she gave us two presentation in three days...... But easy exams. She basically gave all the answers in the review documents.

One of my favorite professors. She is understanding and cares about her students. Exams and assignments are fair. Study and you will do well in this class. Professor Freeman is very knowledgeable in human resources.
Very nice and wants everyone to do well, overall easy class and gives extra credit if needed

She's very unorganized. Her explanations are all over the place. Most classes are useless. Don't expect to take much from her lectures. Don't buy the textbook cuz you are never gonna use it. It's a waste of money.

Professor Sanderson was unclear about every aspect of the class. Long boring lectures regarding her personal research, with little to no tie back into course material. Students are very unclear of her expectations, which lead to much confusion about projects and assignments. Take with someone else if you want to learn something. Easy class, though.

Dr. Sanderson is very opinionated and grades based off of her understanding of the idea, and rarely grades the overall process. You can hit her with cold-hard facts, but she refutes them with her feelings of concepts and business ideas. She believes 9.5 out of 10 businesses fail and that we need to start them for social welfare or else they are bad

She was very vague in her feedback and her directions for assignments were very vague. I would have to say constructive feedback from professor, which was such a critical factor for this class, was almost nonexistent. Easy class though.

you will not want to go to class, because she repeats everything over and over again. very unclear on assignments and projects. Does not care about timelines or syllabus at all. she thinks she is a product design teacher, but she knows nothing about design or production.

Class was very easy, and Professor Sanderson didnt mind when work was not done on time. The assignments themselves were vague and unclear, but because she was so nice, whatever was turned in ended up being ok. Making the business plan was the best part of the course.
I'm sure that she means well but its like she doesn't take the time to make things organized and understand what she is doing

Consistantly gave unclear assignments/directions. whenever you had a question, the answer was always 'do more research' and if you came back with research, she would tell you that you were wrong. was unable to take control of the class, no one ever showed up. unclear grading. if you are respectful and somewhat apply yourself, you might do well.

I'm glad I had Professor Swalla for 1600 too.  She always made sure we were on top of what we needed to do well on exams, we did lots of in class problems, and she was always available when I had questions.

Professor knows alot about design.  Our team was able to get help on every aspect of our project.  She gave good feedback on reports.  Everyone's project worked this semester.  I give her alot of credit for that.

I took Material Selection with her and feel I learned a great deal and will do well in Capstone.  The final project was awesome.  I heard she busted a couple of people for cheating.  I am glad to have a professor who is tough about that.
She is very knowledgeable in her field. Some people dislike her, i found her very helpful. She also gives you a lot of industry application of course material.
Worst professor I've ever had

Her style is different. Now that I'm doing a co-op, I can see why she teaches this way and glad I took her.  She doesn't make you participate in class, but in class work is worth alot.  She showed us a plot linking in class grades and test grades.

Her lectures are good if you do the reading assignments.  If you dont you will have a hard time. Her methods are different from other professors but i think that comes from knowing what employers want.

Prof. Swalla is extremely knowledgeable, but that doesn't necessarily translate to being a good professor.  Her Thermals class is pretty tough, but that's normal for the subject.  She tries to make people participate in class, with limited success.  She's also a pretty quiet speaker.  Her tests are open-book and of appropriate difficulty.
In the capstone class Dr Swalla really helped us stay focused and helped us complete a project that our customer was very happy with , she is a great capstone professor.

She not only teaches in a way that makes the problems understandable but brings real work experiences to the class. I have gone to her office many times and she Dr. Swalla makes it clear that this is no longer high school and that she is here to teach us advanced skills that will help us to be great engineers. She expects the best from us.
Extremely boring class, legitimately reads straight from the textbook at times. A nice curve from the start though, get a 50 and you pass

I cannot stand her! I wasn't able to understand the material well at all, and it took about 6-8 hours to do the homework due each week. A's and B's were also not to be expected in her class, because although some of us might be used to it, this is because of "grade inflation". Probably not the worst professor I'll ever have, but still, I'd switch.

Dr. Swalla was my favorite teacher this semester!  She takes students out of the high school 'plug and chug' and gives them skills they will need when they graduate.  She's tough but fair. That is how it is supposed to be. I'm looking forward to taking her TF1 class.

Dr. Swalla sometimes has difficulty organizing a lecture. She has alot of experience from industry that makes the material interesting. She cares alot about students, always answers emails, and is willing to spend extra time when needed.
Has good intentions, but is a terrible teacher. Doesn't explain things well, and kept changing the homework system every week. Overall, not a good experience.

This professor describs Strength of Materials as her "bread and butter". While copying derivations out of the text she still manages to mess up. I would recommend taking this class with someone else. You can end up with a test average above 90, and a final exam grade of 94  and still manage a B+ with her grading system. Puts herself on a pedestal.

Terribly annoying teacher. She really understands the material but isn't too great at conveying it to a room of students.  As a Mech E major who really enjoyed statics, I dread having to go to Swalla's class. I highly advise you to take the class with someone else
Do not reply to any emails and no responses.
Great teaching skills to penetrate deep inside the subject. Exams are a bit tricky but easy if you understand the basics.
He presents the material in the driest way possible. I was very afraid to go to him for office hours because he was very unapproachable.

Avoid if at all possible. Boring lectures followed by tests that he likes to nit pick at to find every little mistake and will check for more errors that you did if he makes one on tests and homeworks. Takes too many pauses and makes you fall asleep.
Symans is a good professor. He takes care to clarify his lectures and provides all the slides from the lecture afterwards. He is very helpful, especially regarding test/grading

Uses slides made by another professor and edits them for his own use. Flounders in class and seems very disorganized. Confuses a lot of the students with his flipflopping, but with more experience in teaching the course, could be good. Plays REALLY CRAPPY celtic music and Enya during in class problems, but sometimes plays 80s.

I've heard my classmates talk about how awful this subject was but Aniket makes this class very engaging and I came out of it understanding Thermal and Fluid Dynamics like a pro. I believe Aniket is the best professor in this subject and you should make sure you sign up for his section! The tests will be a challenge but there's usually extra credit

Professor Tekawade, although new, is a great professor. Thermals and Fluids 1 is a difficult course, and Professor Tekawade was able to present the course material in a concise, understandable manner. He is very approachable, and will always help you if you email him with problems or go to his office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Would take again

reviews.comment: Professor Tekawade is a new professor, and I took Thermals and Fluids his first semester teaching (Fall 2017). That being said, he does an excellent job explaining concepts and doing examples in class, and is very accessible during office hours if you need extra help. The tests and homework are challenging, but doable.
Dr. Tessier is a great professor and a great guy. His classes are difficult, so take his lectures seriously. He is very willing to help students if they seek it out. Awesome facial hair.
i china student can't get him very well. but good proffosor.

This man is amazing. If you want to do well in the class, he will put forth all of his energy to make sure you do so. Very helpful. Absurdly difficult exams, but he makes sure people don't fail. He connects with students and changes the class to fit the needs of the students. All around great guy. His wife bringing in desserts was a plus too!!

Where to start? Congrats to RPI for taking a hold of Tessier. Amazing Professor with plenty of passion towards his profession. It gets better, Tessier is brilliant. He is extremely devoted to teaching, prepares his lectures and students incredibly well. He also rewards his class by encouraging them and praising those who participate and are active.
One of the best professors I've met at RPI.  If you show interest in the class, he will like you and help you.
very very helpful. at the same time, the test is very very difficult
Very nice guy. He tries very hard to help you out when you need it. Exams can be difficult but he does curve them to a B- average. Lectures are very useful and necessary.

Very good professor. He wants his class to be challenging but makes it so that if you don't understand at first, you get many chances to get a grasp on it. Wife's a great cook, review sessions he gives the test out. ADORABLE little girls! One of the few professors who actually knows your name! A nice alternative to the typical professor.
Great professor.  He really tries to make sure you understand what he's teaching.  Changes his style to fit the class needs.  Just all around a great guy.
Would give everyone a A if he could! He is laid back and amazing and will give his tests out in review sessions

Extremely good teacher.  You learn everything you need to learn and he gives excellent examples in class.  Lots of opportunities to get essentially free points and test questions are given during the review session.  Excellent Professor!!

All I have to say is nice guy but as a teacher, terrible. I learned more from my tutors than from him. He doesn't care if you understand, he's moving on to the next topic. He needs to retire honestly.

By far the worst professor I had freshman year. Dr. Teresco talked down to us like we were infants. Lectures were incredibly slowly paced, and featured very little information that was relevant to either the tests or labs. Luckily, he won't be back next year, as from what I understand he was not re-hired.

Computer Organization. You learn everything about how computers work, from "there is current going through this wire" to coding in c in painstaking detail. He made us code in mips and ssh into unix shells and all of that annoying junk. He imparts knowledge well, but he delves too deep into the monotonous material, and you stop paying attention.
So much time is spent going over homework in class that you hardly learn anything new in class which makes the homeworks difficult.

Very good professor. He knows what he teaches quite well, although he does not always have an answer to specific students' questions. He is good at lecturing, always ready to help, answers questions online pretty fast. Homeworks may be hard at times, but usually, they are not. Quizzes and tests are always fair.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Thompson is really nice and friendly. I've taken his courses and he did so much better than previous instructors. He is indeed an educator.

Engaging lectures are definitely not  his strong suit. He tends to over explain things frequently, and will move through the lectures very slowly. However, he is usually quick to respond to questions, and is much better at giving a direct answer to a question than standing and lecturing. His homework submission with an svn is annoyingly redundant.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He's a dull lecturer who frequently gets lost in the details of implementation than getting the main idea out there. However, his tests are fair and he curves very generously. He provides questions from back tests that give a good idea of what he wants.  Leave plenty of time for HW, labs, and back tests and you'll do fine considering the curve.
Very nice guy, but woefully unengaging lecturer, and absurdly hard grader. (There's a reverse curve on a few of the assignments in PSoft where an A is  95 and a C is  90, seriously who does that?)
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Data Structures was the second hardest course I have ever taken. Long lectures were un-engaging and better explained a google search away.  Averages on tests were generally low(50 with 63 the cutoff for an A). Homework was challenging but more so the submission system and automatic grading.  Policy and instruction vague. Shaky on course material.

Despite the fact that he often doesn't have enough time to cover all of his notes during lecture, I would still recommend going to lecture. The example problems in the notes are very helpful when it comes time for the homework. Prof Thompson is incredibly helpful in office hours, though I would recommend getting there early as long lines can form.

His lectures barely cover any solid materials, often he would just make us perform "activities" for his personal entertainment (that included singing and dancing). Having spent a long time in the tech industry, I can tell you that he doesn't know anything about Information Systems, Business or Technology. An extremely racist and egotistical person.
So full of himself.  Projects were good in building soft skills but taught you zero hard skills or quantitative methods for solving business problems.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--SO MANY PAPERS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Would take any and all criticism incredibly personal and would argue with students in class to make his point.  Never lectured, but assigned unclear group projects throughout the semester.  His tests were incredibly easy because of this lack of actual instruction.  Learned nothing but did boost my GPA.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: One of the better management professors at RPI. He really knows his stuff and challenges you to better yourself. I'd recommend taking any class with him. Plus he assigned a project that was a HUGE resume booster.

Many students did not like for the reasons I liked him, actually. He brought us down to Downtown Troy and had us consult with local business owners utilizing the quantitative models we learned in class. He did not lecture that much which was fine with me. He is a practitioner and brings his experience to the classroom. One of my favorite at RPI.

Taking his MSA 640 at Central Michigan University - He must be different guy than these previous comments - found his examples in class as good practical personal experiences that gelled with lessons for practical learning.  I think previous raters on here were a little less apt for learning the real lessons he is teaching.  Very good professor.
DO NOT TAKE HIM
Dedicated to his work, make learning so much fun!!Respects everyone in the class. THE BEST OF THE BEST!!!! A true Professional

This professor is very easy but completely full of himself. His homework assignments are all about his previous experiences and how he single handedly saved the military millions of dollars or his uncle's business etc... Also unless you are a woman, he won't usualy give you much attention.

A wonderful professor who thinks outside the normal curriculum box.  Focuses on challenging projects, tests are easy.  Turns boring math into real life scenarios which are both practical and interesting.  Take a course with this professor if you like to think outside the box!
real life application of concepts taught
No Comments
No Comments

One of the coolest and most practical teachers I've had here at RPI. More time outside of class is required to do better on tests, but it's not impossible. Will go the extra mile for you. You'll actually find out what IT is about in this class. ;)

Spends most of class time talking about himself, and when he was in the army. Doesn't really teach any of the course material, which makes it hard to study for tests. Has a way of making you feel stupid if you don't know the answer to his questions.
No Comments

Very Interesting, gives great real life applications and example of classroom material, harder to study for tests (since he was not course coordinator). Great if you're looking to get more out of a class than just an A or B.
Prof Sharkey is awesome. He is a great teacher and is willing to help students provided you go to ask him for help. Almost always curves HWExams if the average is below an 80ish.
Good at teaching. very clear. If you pay attention in lecture then the materials are fairly easy. Tests can be harder than expected but there are curves.
He is comprehensive with his notes. He makes class interesting as well!
Awesome professor.  Relatively new to the department but teaches better than anybody.
So, this is a very hard course, regardless of who teaches it. TAKE TIANYI CHEN. I have not seen a better grader than this professor. Very fair and gives a lot of extra credit.
A well-organized class with clear grading criteria. The pace of the lecture is a bit slow at the beginning, so some advanced material does not be covered at the end.

This is a math-heavy course for me. But Prof. Chen did a great job in explaining things well. He is also a caring person that can accommodate diverse student backgrounds and individual needs. Recommend to students with the weak mathematical background to catch up on the probability foundations.

Prof. Chen's course covers all the important topics in ML, an excellent start for students from different background. The lecture are clear, homework are practical. He also includes some ideas in research, very inspiring. Prof. Chen is a caring instructor. He is patient, helpful. You can get support easily. Grading is kind if you spend enough effor

Prof. Chen is a junior professor in RPI. It is first time I attended his course. The lecture is clear, well-prepared. He is very approachable after the class as well. High recommend for ECSE students who want to learn ML.

This class was probably the worst class I have taken at RPI. The professor taught a lot but when it came to homework and tests, it was likeI didn't even attend lecture. The test average was a 40 but he added 20 points to everyones grade to make it look like we did better. Test 2 wasn't better. He assigned homework during finals week.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Presentations and essays are easy assignments but beware of class "discussions" (basically Brian talking about his thoughts on the weekly readings and shooting down students who disagree). You can definitely get away with not doing the readings.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Even though I enjoy discussion & humanities based classes, the same can't be said for Design, Culture, and Society.
Prof Tolle was really difficult to work with. He regularly (and loudly) interrupted students during discussions and gave zero guidance on grading criteria (despite grading harshly). Some topics in class were interesting, at least?
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Course is entirely based on in-class discussion.  Brian is a very knowledgeable, caring instructor.  He does have an annoying habit of cutting students off right after they begin talking, but otherwise he is great.  Overall, this is a super easy course where you can learn a lot.

Politics of Design is a fairly easy and straight forward class, but is very reading heavy. Tolle is an easy going and sociable professor, but he can come across as full of himself. He often cuts students off to insert his own opinion and he does not like granting extensions. The course is very thought provoking & supports a cooperative atmosphere.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dude does not know how to use technology and I'd rather watch paint dry than hear him lecture. He is that boring.

This class was good overall. You have to fully understand the pre-print he has for the course, the lecture slides, and the homework. Exam questions are always related to what he talked about in class/lecture/pre-print. But he is a tough grader. I once lost 10/100 points for units typo despite my solution being correct and carrying correct units.

A very kind and intelligent professor. He doesn't give partial credit, but his exams are straightforward if you pay attention. Sometimes he'll go on cool tangents about materials, which raised my interest in the subject greatly. Sit as close to the front as possible, though, to absorb his wisdom.
His lower level classes are often very similar to previous years in regards to tests/quizzes/homework. Can be hard to understand and has poorly structured lectures.

Get backwork!!! Quizzes are exactly the same as previous years. Even the numbers are the same. Far superior teacher compared to other MatSci professors. HW is on Wiley and there are no prelabs. Easy A.

he's ok.  Hard to understand sometimes. Uses the ready-notes and is all over the place with them.  The partial credit thing people keep referring too depends on the TA for your class, they do all the grading, I get a fair amount of partial credit.  He gives you a list of the material that will be covered on every quiz/test the class before.
No partial credit ever.

Awesome professor! He is fun and really seems to care for his students. He wants you to understand and goes out of his way to make sure you get it. Quizzes were difficult with little partial credit, but overall the cumulative averages were higher. definitely get him if you can.
He always talks about his research, which is glass.  He writes on his overhead slides over and over again, with the same thing.  He is alright, but his quizzes are really hard.

I agree with what many people have already said. No partial credit. And a lot of it is luck. I don't really know what I'm doing in this class, but I beat the average on the first exam, by making some educated guesses and being lucky. Unfortunately, he's the only guy who teaches this course, otherwise I'd suggest getting someone else.

Overall I liked this prof. Very intelligent, has somewhat humorous anecdotes. Accent can be hard to understand. Class is a bore, but tests are VERY straight forward. Yes, he doesn't give partial credit, but if you know your stuff you shouldn't need any. One caveat: I'm probably in the minority, as most of the people in class  weren't fond of him.
interesting guy, tests difficult and a bit unclear, but he seems reasonable about adjusting grades accordingly.  Will spend 1/2 a class explaining techniques for forging a sword

He offers no partial credit and is a little bit hard to understand because of his accent. However, if you go into office hours he is extremly helpful and tries to think of new ways to explain things to you. Also for this class he understand that its really hard and that hes a strict grader so he curves it very nicely.
Excellent professor, extremely intelligent but very had.  Gives little to no partial credit on exams, but his cum. quiz grades are much higher than that of other professors.  Highly recommended.
the tests are so unfair and he is not a good teacher and no partial credit
No Comments
my quiz grades were all over the board, but he's decent guy.
no partial credit at all for tests. if you want a better grade, switch to another professor!

If you don't make a mistake on the exams you are golden (basically no partial credit).  The exams are extremely straight forward however. Other than this, he is an excellent professor who you will learn from as long as you tune in.
AWESOME teacher

Out of all of the professors I've had, he is absolutely the worst one by far. He creates homework that has very little to do with the in-class assignments or lectures for that week. His quizzes can (and usually do) contain questions from the lecture that class. At least he responds to emails quickly and is easy to understand.

Very unhelpful and discouraging professor. Perhaps he did not enjoy teaching this course because it was for engineers who had a weak background in MATLAB, and he prefers to teach  the higher level computer science courses. But he showed little interest in helping his students, definitely take Beginning C with a different professor.

A good teacher who assumes no prior knowledge of Matlab, he gives clear examples, and puts his example programs and lecture notes on LMS.  HW and inclass assignments are easy, but quizzes can be tricky and frequently have multiple choice questions worth 15% each.

He thinks everyone knows at least some C programming, which makes it tough for students who have never programmed before.  It is not impossible to get an A, but you have to do your fair share of work and utilize all of your resources.  Professor Todd is easy to reach and his website is very helpful.

Beginning C was a rather easy required class.  Todd's assignments and quizzes weren't hard, but you had to have read his slides or the book to have known what you were doing.  Most people just zoned out or played games during his lectures; may help to listen occasionally.  Final project was difficult considering material taught, but graded easily.
No Comments
Can't miss class, confusing lectures, relies heavily on TA's. Not accessible outside class whatsoever. Good luck.

He was a lot of fun in tour of the solar system. We mostly watched movies and did some activities and everyone got As. He's extremely enthusiastic about astronomy and if you are too you will enjoy his astro classes. But I've heard he should be avoided for physics classes.

His "lectures" prior to the activities are very broad and he expects you to know the material already. Compared to other professors, his teaching is minimal and as a result our class average on tests was significantly lower than those of other classes.

Great guy, realistic, just need to get to know him. He was next door class teacher at Shaker High, and then "moved with me" to HVCC. I always could come to him after class to have clarify material that I did not understood in my class. He was able to explain in easy and way the concepts so it became a common sense. - bohdan

This guy is a nut job he gives crazy examples about stuff nobody can understand, he smiles when he is nervous and when nobody wants to answer his questions. He is a very nice teacher and really smart but he just cannot get his points across. Do the homework and you will do well in this class.

The Trink is the man! He's a great professor that will teach you above and  beyond what you need to know for the test. He will often give you derivations of equations and explain to you why things work instead of just throwing material at you. He gives a lot of the mathematical background to physics as well. Also he is a great help one-on-one.
No Comments
No Comments
expect homework inspirational amazing lectures would take again
best class ever at rpi

Prof. Tracy is a great professor. He keeps up to date with all news and incorporates it into the classroom. We studied old and very current cases, so much so that our strategy memos would change based on current news. The class is challenging (he grades pretty hard on memos) if you don't read cases and do not open your mind to strategic thinking.
Very smart guy who makes the class very interesting. Make sure you do the reading, the majority of the grade is based on class participation and a couple of group projects.
Interesting Class. I like his way of teaching. participation counts so go to class. Keep up with the readings and you will do well.

Every exam/quiz question is taken directly from assigned homework. Questions were selected from the simpler/exemplary type homework problems. Calculator & crib-sheet were allowed in all exams but not in quizzes. Use the solution manual. No attendance, no graded homework. 3-exams, a cumulative final & a weekly quiz from the previous weeks homework.

Honestly hes probably one of the better DS profs out there.  Subject material can be challenging but most of his test and quiz questions come straight out of HW problems that he assigns.  Lectures can be somewhat boring but hes clearly trying his best to teach it.

Every time I show up to lecture, I regret it. The lectures are not helpful, just read the book. If you stay exactly where the syllabus says you should be, you'll be ahead, because he is ALWAYS behind in his lectures.
He was a terrible teacher. I'm so lucky I took Calc 1 in H.S. His exams questions come exactly from the homework problems so make sure you do those. Don't go to class. It's definitely not worth it.

Extremely easy for Diffeq, we could use a crib sheet to put all formulas so tests essentially came down to copying the right equation and doing some algebraic simplification. Lectures were boring, yet somehow useful.  Weekly quizzes not hard if you do even just a few of the suggest problems from the book.

Dont bother attending class. Just teach yourself and go to office hours and you are pretty much guaranteed an A... Going and listening to him for 2 hours is the BIGGEST waste of time. Do yourself a favor and go have a beer instead.
By far the easiest differential equations professor. Questions on the tests are straight out of the practice problems assigned to you. Easy A

Makes absolutely no sense in lecture. Sometimes you can get lucky and get a qualified TA who can translate his two hours of nonsense for the past 3 classes into an easily understandable 20 min review. Then again, you can get a TA who doesn't speak english very well and is equally unorganized. Avoid him if you can, and if not - do the optional hw.

No homework, class attendance is optional, only tests and quizzes, and he drops the lowest test(aka. no FINAL!!!). Study homework problems and you should do fine. His lectures do get long and boring, and he has trouble explaining things, but eventually you'll understand, maybe if its not the same day of class.
He does not give homework or projects. There are just tests and quizzes. His lectures can get a little long but overall he teaches well. The TA is very helpful.

I also took Professor Turiel for Calc 1 during the Fall 06 term.  I think this was his first semester at RPI, so I gave him some slack.  Even taking that into consideration, it was painful to try and focus on the lecture.  Fortunately, I took both Calc 1 and 2 in high school so it was all just a review.  Some topics weren't covered before exams.
Had this guy in Fall 06 for Calc  1.  He was pretty bad and hard to follow in lecture.  I had taken Calc in high so I knew everything he did.  He was pretty bad too.  Painful to listen to.

Lectures are geared to math majors more than a general class. Sometimes didn't cover something before quizzing students on it (the TA would cover it in recitation before the quiz) Do the homework and you'll do fine. Didn't understand students' questions in class without being walked through the students' problems, which took like 5 minutes each.

Dude was useless...  He used "lemmas" which are kinda like theorums...  but not...  and everything he said made no sense...  i was extremely lucky that i had taken calc in h.s.  I leanred more in Schmidt's review of calc I in calc II than anything from this guy...
Professor Turner cares very deeply about RCOS and really does his best to ensure student success. He creates a very welcoming and collaborative environment in which open source projects thrive.

Overall great experience, wrote my first line of code in this class and it really developed my love for the discipline as a whole. Homeworks can be time-consuming, but nothing out of the ordinary for a cs course at RPI, level of rigor is just right imo. Prof Turner is also a great guy, pretty engaging during lecture, would recommend.

I have only had Professor Turner for RCOS, so I cannot speak on other classes, but he has always been an excellent professor who is very nice, caring, and respectful. He runs a very fun class while also having it be very useful and informative for students
A lot a lot a lot of reading the textbook to understand
Lecture wise probably the best I've had so far at RPI. Assignments and exams are pretty fair if you put in the work. Not much to complain about. Solid guy.

Professor Turner is a cool dude. He tells dad jokes every class, and they're awful yet funny. CS is hard, but he does his best to make it better. He is really good in office hours and in online replies on Submitty. The course content is boring (naturally, not his fault), but his explanations are good.

Firstly, this class is NOT an intro class. As someone who came into RPI not knowing a lick of code, it was extremely difficult to grasp this class, theoretically. Prof. Turner is a cool guy and all but the speed of his teaching is not easily adjustable. ALAC tutoring is available but always crowded and provides limited help
Never, ever take this class! It's homework > rest of homework
love em
Failed to teach me anything substantial

The class I had with Prof. Turner was meant to be a class you can take if you've never coded before however I don't believe this is the case. The class was challenging even for someone like myself who has been coding for a few years. The tests are very nit-picky and it is almost impossible to get a 100 even if you are near perfect in other sections
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: CS 1 with Prof. Turner can be tough. For my year, he used pre-recorded video lectures in place of live classes, and it created a major disconnect between him and the students. Often, explanations of concepts were not very clear or engaging. Prof. Turner is a nice person, and he cares about this class. He will not hesitate to help you if you ask.

He is a horrible professor. I recently just finished taking his class, barely passing, and feel that I have learned nothing useful or valuable from him. He used pre recorded lectures and used his actual lecture times, in which he was supposed to be teaching, as Q&A, which were not helpful at all. Failed to teach me anything substantial

Honestly this was the hardest class I have ever taken and it wasn't like I was not putting in the effort. I was spending about 30-35 hours from monday-thursday just on Comp sci alone with 0 progress/learning anything. The lectures didn't help and notes barley helped. Overall this is one of those classes that students have nightmares about. Horrible

I had Professor Turner as both a student and now a TA for the same class. He is honestly still one of my favorite professors. Lectures can drag if you have CS experience, but he tells jokes. Once in class I asked a question and didn't understand his answer, so he found me after class and reexplained it for me. All-around caring guy.

I took Comp Sci 1 P/NC as a science major just to get a taste for it. Prof Turner seems nice and caring and has a great sense of humor, but I got NOTHING at all from lectures or labs. Homeworks were difficult and time consuming. Tests were hard when I took it, so we were given massive curves. Overall, I probably would've taken this course elsewhere
So far the best lecturer I've ever seen. the exams and homework are not easy, but they all look far from tedious.

Lectures were useless for me. Taught myself pretty much the entire class. Best part about the class is the homework. There's a lot of it, but it's helpful and, unlike the tests, useful. Tests are hard, and they use weird, arbitrary examples. Poor tests of programming ability, imo.
Very flawed course. Exams are very hard and everything is toughly graded.

Wish I was exaggerating by saying he is the worst instructor I have ever had. Has no idea what he is doing half of the time, the wordings of homework and test questions are terrible, and no useful instruction is given. Sometimes he literally just posts he wrong thing. Anticipating an A-, but terrible experience getting there. Nothing good to say.
CS 1 is pretty easy. Not the best lecturer but got through the content. Homeworks were regular but pretty easy.
Professor Turner is the best CS1 prof! He stayed well past his posted office hours on numerous occasions to help this lost freshman debug their code. The mentors and TA's are wonderful.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: A lot of work, get ready for 12 hours a week for homework, lab, lecture exercises, and studying for exams. He is funny though and good lecturer, and knows the material.

Turner is an extremely caring professor and is always trying to help students. Lectures are decent. You should review them first if you want to have a better grasp of the material. They can and should be boring if you prepared for them. Turner provides all the necessary materials to succeed you just have to put the work in. Tests aren't the easiest

Hes not a terrible lecturer, but the problem overall with the class is that its hard to take notes about coding. A lot of times he will use things in examples that people who have never coded before dont know.

He was my favorite professor ever. I completely respect him and his teaching style. he is funny and caring. If you ever need help his door is always open and he will help to the best of his ability. If you can take his class you should. 100/100 :)

He's pretty funny usually his jokes are really corny but he tries. He gives great examples and he even provides print outs of the notes at each class so you can grab a copy. He's super nice. Realizes the class is hard if you don't have prior experience and gives lots of examples.

If you've done programming before, especially Python, this will probably be easy for you. I struggled the whole semester, but Turner was extremely helpful. I visited him a few times in office hours and he was able to explain even the most difficult concepts I was having trouble with. He cares a lot about his students. Take in the spring for curve.

He is a overall decent professor. His lectures are okay, but, similarly to most CS classes, the majority of the material is learned through homework. Tests are kind of difficult, but they don't count as a lot relative to other classes. He also can't seem to get through a lecture without at least one corny joke.
Straightforward lecturer with coding examples and tangential intro to higher level programming topics. Usually tells 1-2 corny jokes in the beginning of each lecture.

Dr. Vastola is a fantastic guy with funny, engaging lectures. Unfortunately, you get almost nothing from class. He simply reads from the slides,  and a majority of his examples and explanations are not very intuitive. I understand that the subject matter itself is not very intuitive, but online sources were far more helpful.

I've had Vastola for 3 classes now and I have to say he is the worst professor I've ever had. He's a nice guy, but he is an awful teacher. He just clicks through power points and reads them verbatim. Half the time he gets confused by his own slides so I'm not even sure he wrote them.

The worst professor I've encountered at RPI. He may not have an accent, but his teaching style doesn't foster learning. Hard, long assignments. TAs were mildly helpful. Very deaf to student feedback and over-all not the most popular teacher.
I can not think of words horrible enough to describe Kenneth Vastola. He steals his lecture slides from other professors and if you ask a question and the answer isn't on the slides, he doesn't know.
Worst class I've ever taken. Ever.

Most worthless professor i have ever had. Lectures are stupid and pointless. Have to teach yourself everything as you do in-class activities. Old Prof had open book/ open notes tests designed with that in mind, Vastola takes the same tests but without open book/notes because 'he doesnt believe in open book tests' and expects encyclopedic knowledge
This guys joke are just so bizarre. I mean I actually laugh at them because there so bizarre. I mean there bad but just odd. Anyways great guy, did well at teaching.

Wasn't an outstanding professor, but he was very clear and helpful when you asked for assistance and did everything he could to work out issues with grading. He's really a good guy with a not-so-hot sense of humor.

Vastola is a bloated man-ball of a professor, whose ego somehow surpasses even his incredulous girth. Vastola finds it an unfortunate accident that he has students in his class each semester and treats them accordingly with general disdain.  The concept of answering questions or encouraging discussion is clearly far below him.
No Comments

Social Psychology. Good lecturer, but you don't need to go to class if you don't want to. There are a good bit of essays but he grades them very lenient. No tests, only online quizzes. One of two "memorization" assignments but you actually just read off a paper. Overall easy comm intensive class, and pretty entertaining if you go to class.

VerWys is the best professor at RPI. I was Aeronautical Engineering until I took his course. Go to office hours! I had a heart-to-heart with him and switched into a career path that I love. The course isn't difficult, but he makes it interesting. Very self-aware and conscientious professor!
Good class, lots of papers and its very interesting, he will randomly take attendance.

Super easy. We did one presentation over the FBI motivational model and wrote a paper with a group of 6. Very knowledgeable if you talk to him in a small setting doesn't lecture enough to figure that out during class
Easy class. Don't buy textbook. Attend class for majority of classes to get attendance. Finish essays. Not need to attend class for last two weeks of semester

Lax deadlines on easy assignments make this one of the easiest communications-intensive classes out there. Promises 3 tests, there's actually just 1, which is literally impossible to fail. Class gets cancelled a lot, when it doesn't you'll watch videos most of the time, or he'll read off his overhead slides. Class usually ends early.

forensic psychology, interesting course, and the professor teaches about classic serial killers as well as current serial killers (serial killers or spee killers who are active when you take the course)

This guy is as useless as it gets. Easiest A I have ever gotten in my life, which I guess is good, but I didn't learn anything about psychology. I don't think we even discussed anything relative to psychology. He spent most of our class lectures reading us news stories out loud. Another excellent use of tuition at RPI...

i had him for social psych the class was real easy, as long as the essays are the right length you get hundreds,had enough points by the beginning of novemeber and didn't have to do any work for the rest of the semester to get an A

Basically the coolest professor at RPI. So long as you can fathom SOME form of insightful, introspective thinking, his classes are the easiest in the world, and rich with enlightenment for those who seek it.

Good teacher, but his assignments were a little excessive. Expects you to write 20 page papers like it ain't no thang. At times, it seemed like they were graded based on length alone rather than content/quality.
no enthusiasm was not prepared for class ever.  rarely taught actual material
Best prof @ rpi.  The only one that knows how to give information at our level of study as opposed to phd level information.

His grading system is absurd.  If you've ever heard that quality is more important than quantity, well forget that now.  He requires 60 pages of writing by the end of the year and doesn't think anything of it, not to mention the course isn't considered "writing intensive."
had him for social psych, basically the man, work is easy, he grades essays on how long they are
He slaps the projector A LOT, can get kinda annoying at times.  Otherwise, easy A if you come to class and pay attention.

This is the easiest class EVER! He gives out 25% bonuses on all the tests so you don't even need to study or read (or come to class, since social psych is all common sense)! Don't buy all the books either, since he never assigns reading, only "recommends" it. Easy A.
No Comments

He's a really good lecturer and has interesting projects or paper. Sometimes I wish there was more structure to the class but this allows him to experiment with us and it's fun so eh... It's overall very enjoyable.
i agree. an all around excellent professor regardless of what class he teaches. i've had him in social psych, forensic psych, and im taking his psych and the law class.

Very nice man, and not a bad lecturer either. i always enjoyed the videos he had for class, and it was a little unnerving how the entire grade was based on one huge paper, but it turned out not to be so bad.
If you love sarcasm and you find psychology interesting, then take anything you can from him!  It is a lot of fun and really interesting.

VerWys is one of the best professors on the RPI campus regardless what they teach. Forensic Psych with him was an extremely interesting class and the presentations you have to do actually help you improve your presenting skills for other classes. He is an easy grader and I would suggest everyone try and take at least one course with Prof. VerWys.

A 35-40 paper is easy?  I wrote almost 50 in the end and it challenged me the whole way. Class is not mandatory, but if you go to class, you learn the topics you're going to write about.  If you don't, then you do it on your own and that's your choice.  The class was great and the prof was funny! :)

I don't think I learned a single thing in this class. It sounds unbelievable but I'm serious. I never once needed to open the textbook. We watched movies half the time, and the other half was Prof. VerWys making stuff up and not teaching. Your only grade was 8 BS essays about how you feel.
I am also in personality.... it's 30 pages, not 35.. and he gives you the whole semesters.. it's pretty easy.

I have him for social psych and personality.  Many classes are devoted to watching movies or TV shows.  Entire grade in both classes is a 35-40 page paper--which he refuses to meet with students about.  Take him only if you want a grade for doing a 35 page independent research project.
Very easy to understand, and really wanted students to be interested and excel.
Somewhat entertaining and the tests are really fair, they test you proportional to what you learn.
So easy yet so boring.  Tests are direct word for word from the notes that he posts online.  Some interesting videos but when he speaks bring your pillow.  An easy A.
His lectures were boring.  He didn't seem like he wanted to be teaching.  However, the course was fairly easy.  Make sure you attend class because he tests you on videos you watch in class.
Easy class.  Frequently cancels classes, especially in winter months.

I've had him as a professor and I've worked with him.  He's extremely knowledgable.  He insists on students being able to recognize classroom concepts in the everyday world.  His workload and ease varies, but work had and you'll get an A.

Great classes... He's very straightforward about the non-manditory attendance.  Tests are multiple choice and no real HW (just a few "worksheets" in some classes).  Big Lebowski movie clips defiantlty a plus.
Frequently blew off class, spent most classes listening to a monotone lecture or watching a movie.

Psychological Tests and Measures ... the class writes the tests (all multiple choice).  The course material is mostly about testing making and what tests are actually testing.  Easy A, does require some work
Took personality with him.  Wants his students to pass, opinionated, but honestly tries to teach material.

easiest class by far.  He is not afraid to talk to us about whats really on every college kids mind... SEX.  what other topic in this world could get 250 college students to pay attention all at once.. and we are actually learning, bc his lectures r great

I have taken every class he has offered since my freshman year, he is the best teacher I have ever had, Period. You learn massive amounts of information easily, you do well, you have fun, AND you actually use it. Prof of Decade material.
Easiest class I've taken so far.  Only class I haven't taken notes in.
Best professor ever... and I've had Hagerup and Li
No Comments
No Comments
we watch lots of FOX on TV during class
No Comments
pretty cool guy...
No Comments
No Comments

As a person, Dr. Tysoe is very nice and does a lot to entertain his students. He is very knowledgeable on the subject and helps a lot during office hours. However, it is very hard to learn much during his lectures. He goes on so many tangents that most people find it beneficial to just skip his lectures and go over the lecture notes.

Tysoe's lectures are a waste of time. He keeps going on tangents about other things unrelated to the topic. He keeps bringing up the history of chemistry. He is a great person, and will bring candy and other fun things to lecture, but he is just not a good teacher.

Cares about the subject matter and students, but isn't the best lecturer.
Tried to make class engaging by encouraging participation with prizes, but spent most of the lectures just reading the slides.
I learned the material best by studying it on my own time. To his credit he is very accessible online to answer questions, particularly before exams.

There are lots of mixed thoughts on Dr. T, personally I had no problem with his style of teaching and I found the textbook reading and labs to be particularly helpful in learning content. He's always on WebEx and is willing to help anyone that asks.

Doctor Tysoe is a great guy, however could improve upon his time management and general teaching skills. His lectures were often unpredictable, which usually provided some form of entertainment happening at some point or another, but also took time away from actual learning and lecture. Always willing to help and has a positive outlook on life.

Tysoe constantly wastes time in class talking about unrelated topics. Most students in my class would sit in the hall and watch Ma's lecture during class (just so they could get the attendance points by being in the building). I taught myself all of Chem 1. If you have to take him- still go to Ma's office hours!

He goes on tangents and rambles for most of the class and before labs. This means he's always behind in lecture and labs start late. He also gets way too close to incoming freshman that it's just weird. Always asking us to DM him something at any possible opportunity. He tries to seem like a nice guy but he just makes me uncomfortable. Stay away.

I really enjoyed Dr. Tysoe, very approachable and will show you around his 3D printer lab if you go to his office hours. But he does tend to go off on tangents which are funny and interesting but for a class that requires attendance via IClicker, it sometimes made class fall behind. Very knowledgable and nice though so all a round a great professor

Dr. Tysoe's a good professor &helps out his students a lot. It's very easy to reach out for help. He often cuts into lab/lecture time with off-topic rants & music. If you read the slides & textbooks before lectures, you should be fine. Overall, a great person but I wish he spent more time in lectures explaining topics rather than telling stories.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Tysoe is a very empathetic person. He gets distracted in lecture easily, assigns mandatory homework with old questions, and usually makes attendance graded as well. He is very easy to reach, be it by email or webex, he'll respond very fast. Despite the harsh opinions of him held by students, he genuinely wants you to succeed.
He was a great person. He really cared if we passed and wanted us all to pass. However he wasn't a good teacher. His lectures weren't exciting and usually consists of a waste of 20ish minutes.

Don't take his class!!! He doesn't know what he's teaching, and he wastes time going of tangents in his lecture. He does only 3 practice exam questions in an hour, which is extremely inefficient, and he did those 3 questions using unnecessary complicated methods.

He makes his lectures mandatory but teaches for barely half the class. He goes on random tangents that make taking notes nearly impossible, as to where it's more time-productive to read the entire textbook before trying to participate in his class. He wants to be the fun, "cool" professor but is just annoying.
DO NOT TAKE TYSOE!!!! He wasted the first 10ish minutes of class playing random rock songs from the 80's and does not teach well at all.

Dr.Tysoe is a good person who wants the class to do well, but the way lectures are structured and presented are not enough to fully understand the material. The pacing and content of lectures are inconsistent sometimes we spend a whole class on 15-20 slides or we go through a full slideshow in another. He really cares but outside study is necessary

Super caring guy who really wants you to succeed. Chem in general isn't a super interesting topic and has a lot of memorization involved. He makes it engaging and will go out of his way to host quality review sessions and long office hours. He does tend to speed up throughout class and go a little too fast to wright the example problem down however

After spending almost 90 days with him, I can say for sure that he is a professor that you don't come by easily. He is very approachable, has a great sense of humor and humility, and very much so wants students to succeed. He did read some of the comments on here, but did a poll in a lecture to feel out where he could improve. He cares 4 & about u.

Holy this guy is actually insanse, what pissed me off is the fact that he tries to manipulate us into thinking that he is trying his best and that he constantly says he only wants best for us, but doesn't give us the resources we need during lecture to be doing well in the class, absolutely dissapointed.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr. Tysoe is a great professor. In other lectures, professors just read from slides, and it gets extremely boring. However, Dr. T provides real life examples, questions, and overall, just keeps the class engaged whether it be by experiments, music (before lecture), 3D objects, candy, etc. He is also very caring and wants success for everyone.

Spent the first 1/4 of class time less than a week before our exam making us take a survey on how much we liked him. It was true/false, and included questions like "Dr. T should retire. He's not an effective educator." We are also so far behind that the entire biochem unit was dropped from the curriculum. Need I say more?
Terrible, awful, useless. Avoid at all costs
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This guy pisses me off so much, he has no prioritization at all, instead of teaching during lectures, this guy plays games and plays loud music for 10 minutes while throwing 3D-printed toys at students, the worst part is that attendance is required where you don't learn anything until the last 10 minute when he realized he wasted to much time.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: learned absolutely nothing in class, going to lecture was a waste of time, does not explain the topics and just talks about them, does not walk through example questions clearly

Dr. Tysoe is one of the best educators i've ever had the privilege to have. He can be polarizing to some but in all honesty i don't really get it. He brings a lot of life and character to what would otherwise be dull material. If your an incoming freshman, no one on campus will make you feel more welcome and help you while your struggling.
Professor Tysoe is literally the only professor I have had that WANTS every student to pass his class. Most aca

Wholesome dude. Tries to make his lectures not boring and for the most part it works. Not the greatest chemistry professor at RPI but overall he's funny and does a good job teaching the material. Pay attention in lecture and go to other professor's test prep and you'll be alright.

In a brief statement, Professor Tysoe lacks the professional maturity to distinguish between being a lecturer and another person in the room. His lectures are almost incomprehensible between the countless tangents he goes on in the middle of class. He's a very nice individual, but your learning will suffer if you rely solely on his lectures.

Tysoe is literally insane. He got reprimanded for inviting students to his house and although nothing happened, he remains weird. Also if you're looking to take general chemistry with him, I highly recommend a different professor. He's most commonly the professor with the lowest test grades and he'll go on random tangents about his personal life.

Only had for Chem Lab, not lecture. Took over an hour every week to actually begin the lab, and frequently had to rush/ran out of time to submit lab data by end of class. Lab grades were not returned for weeks if not months.

Some people like him, most people don't. He mumbles thru every lecture then goes off and plays a random video. His exam review sessions are useless and all he does is joke with students. Do not take spring sem chem he basically tried to change around everything bc everyone was failing (everyone is still failing). Be prepared to teach yourself.

Steven Tysoe is a dedicated RPI teacher known for saying, "Once a Tysoe student, always a Tysoe student." He goes above and beyond to ease the transition for first-year students. like movie and video game nights and remains a lifelong advocate. It's surprising he isn't tenured yet, given his commitment to the parents, and students alike.

Dr. Tysoe is an amazing professor. He cares more about his students than the school does. He gives everybody the opportunity to have fun and cares about his teaching. In lecture, he tries to make it fun and upbeat so that people pay attention. He is also very funny and personable. Chem 1100 isn't that hard if you try outside of lecture.

This review is strictly on the teaching/lecturing efforts by Dr. T. He is a very nice person and this is not a personal negative review. I have problems with the total and complete lack of any lecturing going on during class time. No teaching is going on during lectures and I do not feel I am learning anything from class. I want to learn Chem :(
He's a great person, super easy to get a hold of outside of class but his lecturing is somewhat lacking. If you keep up with the reading, you'll do fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He's a bit of a rambler but incredibly kind and accommodating. He tries his best to ease the stress that comes along with such a difficult course. Definitely choose Dr. Ma for lecture if possible, but Dr. Tysoe is not a bad professor by any means.

Dr. Tysoe is a fantastic person who clearly cares a lot about his students, but has a tendency to waste lecture/discussion time on tangents or playing music, having to compensate by going extremely quickly during the last few minutes of lecture. Altogether a good professor for a very difficult course, but could do with staying more on-topic.

I had Dr Tysoe for both Chem 1 lecture and lab. I liked his lectures a lot, I found his jokes and tangents nice and kept my attention for the whole block. He also plays music at the beginning and end of class and hosts events around RPI for students. For lab, his tangents can sometimes cut into time actually in the lab or post-lab time.

The course is challenging but organized well, and Dr. T does a decent enough job at giving us the information Dr. Ma wants us to know. Dr. T messes around and goes off on tangents a lot, which make his lectures not the best if you want to get something out of it. Cool guy and very reachable outside of class, not the most effective lecturer, though.

Dr. T is a person that everyone needs to meet at least once. He really does know his stuff, and he does a great job explaining things in rudimentary ways when you don't understand. Sometimes his lectures are a little unserious, but that breaks up the monotony. Take his section of lecture to learn and have fun in chem 1.

Dr. Tysoe is wonderful!! He's always available to answer questions or just to talk. He hosts many events outside of class which are fun to go to and he really cares about his students. I also took his History of Chemistry class and really enjoyed that as well.

Dr. Tysoe loves to help students in many ways for them to succeed and explains things in a way that is clear to everyone. Despite what some have said, he won't go off topic for more than a minute and will not waste time on playing music. He reads the reviews about him on this site too and will improve his performance from the feedback if possible.
I feel like I learned nothing you really have to teach your self to get through the class he is a nice person but not so great at teaching he is off topic all the time

Dr. Tyso is an awesome professor. He cares a lot about students learning and goes out of his way to answer questions on Webex especially before a test/exam. He's brought candy to lectures and printed hundreds of custom stickers for students.
RIP his old car "The Beast"
(he also holds a retro game thing once a year that's awesome)

Awesome professor, you can tell how much he loves to talk about chemistry in his lectures. Goes on many tangents which some stupids complain about, but I never saw them as an issue. He is very willing to help students and take the time to meet with them if they need extra help.

Dr Tysoe is literally one of the sweetest people I've ever met. He really cares about his students. I had him for my Chem 2 lab, and his explanations during the discussions are really helpful and in-depth. I haven't had him for lecture, and I hear he can go off on tangents sometimes, but it's definitely worth it to take him.

Prof Tysoe is a great guy, cares a lot about his students. Goes on many tangents about the most random things instead of teaching, but very passionate! Brings in snacks sometimes. Relatable guy, cares about ethics. Lastly, one of the tangents he went on was telling us to never hesitate to call him if we're in a hard place. (In terms of depression)

Professor Tysoe is a great lecturer and a kind man. The chemistry one curriculum can be difficult at times, and he is expected to go through the lecture slides fast, but regardless, Professor Tysoe is understanding of his student's abilities. He also cares for the success of the students. He plays music and hands out stickers too!

He's the kind of professor that will answer your last-minute questions about tests the next day at 3AM. I found his lectures not as useful as the textbook, but it was more of my problem because COVID kept me from finishing HS Chem.
Overall, he's the bubbliest professor I've ever met who really enjoys spreading his knowledge and love of chem. 
10/10
Overall fun and engaging teacher. He doesn't make the exams though.

Although he tends to go on tangents, Tysoe is a really funny professor and cares a lot about how you progress and learn. Chemistry is one of the toughest subjects I've ever taken and he's definitely the reason I passed. Thank you Dr. T

Professor Tysoe does his best to keep class entertaining and interesting. Sometimes he can go off on a bit of a tangent, but he absolutely cares about his students. I've seen him open his office doors for people with questions 3 hours early to do whatever he can to help his students succeed. While the class can be difficult, Dr. Tysoe is great.

He liked to get off topic at the beginning of the semester and it was BAD, like 30-45 minutes of the lecture sometimes were random crap. But he did get better later in the semester. Great person just not the best professor

He's a fun guy but if you show up to a lecture looking to learn, you might have a hard time.  I ended up scrolling through the slides outside of lecture to learn the material instead of paying attention in lecture.  It's fun but I wish he concentrated more.

Chem1110 is more work than my other classes in terms of homework and studying

Even though he is a very kind and smart person, his lectures tend to be very unproductive. Learned most of the material myself, and only attended lecture for the iClicker points. If your major is chem-based, then I definitely  wouldn't recommend his lecture, but he can be helpful outside of lecture in his office hours or during lab.

Dr T cares for the Gen Chem students so much! He always will spend extra time out of class to help you, whether it be during his very flexible office hours or on Webex. He brings his jokes and songs to every class with him, but uses them well. He is very knowledgable about chemistry and loves to spread his knowledge and see kids learn! Love ya Dr T

Very caring and funny guy. Gives you lots of mnemonics to help memorize what you need to. Gets behind in lecture, though, so sometimes homework assignments will be on material not covered yet. He used to play music for the first part of lecture but I don't know if he's still allowed to do that.

Dr. Tysoe showed his love for chemistry every lecture and would go out of his way to make the class environment relaxed and fun. He would buy us stickers and make jokes to try and help us stay positive and it made all the difference. This and his clear understanding of chemistry made the generally difficult course not as bad.
spends 20 minutes blasting music at the beginning of lecture and blasts through 200 pages of slides through the rest of the hour and 30 minutes remaining, good guy but not the best teacher

Dr T's lectures are as useless as watching TV. Always talks about unrelated things MID-SENTENCE while teaching. I hardly learned anything useful
If you are in RPI for learning and paid a lot of money for it. Do not waste your 10k on his class

Good guy but often rambles in lectures and gets off-topic. Does hold review sessions the weekend before an exam which helps. This year one exam was scheduled the day after the Superbowl, and another was scheduled the day after Easter. Does give chances for extra credit; understanding when it comes to your grade, sometimes helps to increase it.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Although Tysoe is super sweet, funny, and caring, he almost always goes off on tangents and never ends up covering material needed for lab quizzes or otherwise. Sucks that you have to be there for iClicker because I would skip and attend Ma's lectures instead.
Difficult to pay attention in lectures. He gets distracted very easily.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I had Tysoe for chem lab. He's terribly nice and wants his students to do well, but he literally does not stop talking ever. I would trust him as a wacky uncle, but the constant chatter just bugged me.
Very knowledgeable but Tysoe's lectures were not very helpful, and I had to use a lot of outside sources to learn the material. Often times we would be behind the other chem classes

I did not find his lectures super helpful, and had to learn the material on my own outside of class. HW and pre labs took quite some time. He checked attendance by having in class questions that we would have to answer (but not have to get correct), for credit. If taking Chem 1, Id recommend Dr. Ma, as he writes the tests.
Dr. T is a great guy. He does go off on many tangents but usually relates them to the lecture. Tests are not hard if you go over notes and labs are easy.

While the online learning format has been a challenge (in my personal experience), Dr. Tysoe always went above and beyond to make sure his students had ample opportunity to get help with chemistry. He spent a good portion of his weekends holding live review sessions which not a lot of professors are willing to do. Very caring and kind person.

Dr. Tysoe loves chemistry. He really wants you to understand the material and offered extra tutoring sessions before exams. He may go on tangents sometimes, and plays music before and after class (he mainly listens to songs from the 70's-80's). Talking to him would only help you, as he loves knowing his students.

Dr. Tysoe is a good professor, although he's like a valve that doesn't close. He frequently goes off on tangents but usually makes them relevant to the material... His aim is to get everyone to love chemistry as much as he does. He's fine at lecturing, but is especially helpful when you have specific questions. He likes to know his students.

Tysoe is funny and knows a lot about chemistry, but O Chem lab is generally a very difficult course. It's easy to lose many points of pre-lab and post-lab reports, but he gives feedback so hopefully you can avoid mistakes in the future.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: I love Tysoe. He is amazing. I am excited to have him for Chemistry 1200.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Honestly, he's an all around amazing professor.  He cares not only about his students' success in the classroom, but also in their everyday lives.  His lab is filled with great jokes, good music, and an easy to understand breakdown of the material.  He's a fantastic professor who goes above and beyond for his students.

I had him for a chem II lab.  He likes to tell a lot of stories during the "question" portion, and he objectively wastes a lot of time in this regard.  There has been labs where we could have finished the post lab that day, but started the lab late because of tangents he went on.
Very well involved in lecturing. Is really sweet and will help you with anything you need in chemistry.

Dr. Tysoe is one of my favorite professors at RPI! He clearly cares for each of his students and genuinely wants you to learn something in his class. He's very funny and a great lecturer! His careful explanation of the discussion questions really helps to clear up difficult topics.
His jokes can be funny, and he's a good teacher and explains everything well

Dr. Tysoe is one of the funniest people I have encountered. He is a lab professor so his job is basically to do discussion questions which he explains thoroughly albeit a little slowly. His jokes are hysterical in the cringe-worthy pun way. So glad I got him as a lab professor though!

Truly cares for all of his students, and while his lab lectures may take awhile, he does it to ensure that his students have all of the information that they need in order to do well on exams. He keeps things light and engaging with goofy jokes, that are somehow always chemistry related. I had him for CHEM 1&2.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: A great professor! He is always doing his best to engage the class in different ways and is super helpful in office hours!

Lab instructor for CHEM 1100-07; he is a bit goofy but you can really tell he genuinely cares about his students. This is a rare quality to have in modern college education setting. If you like bad puns and dad jokes, he is the guy for you. He takes his time on problems, so if you need it to go slowly then his lectures are perfect. Really nice guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Lab instructor for my CHEM 1100-07 and he makes boring chem lectures worse. Everything gets dragged out and he goes on a irrelevant tangent every problem. It took us 1 hour to make it through 4 example problems. He makes the boring material unbearable with his awful puns and jokes. The work load is equivalent to all of the other lab blocks. Um, No.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Chakrapani is teaching T&F for the first time this semester since 2018. This class took a lot of hours for me to do well in. Funnily enough, the hardest part about this course is using English units. The dimensional analysis gets really difficult and most of her exams have more problems with English units than SI. She lectures very fast.

Professor Chakrapani, for courses in her focus (electrochemistry), is incredibly enthusiastic. She loved the material; making the course much more enjoyable. She is very understanding and approachable.
She knows what shes talking about but the class is mad hard. Not the worst TF1 professor but definitely not the best.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Material gets more difficult as semester progresses. Final given in class.
He does not help. He does not respond to emails.

His class is very difficult, and the grading systems makes you really work hard if you want an A.  He gives very difficult homework assignments, but he is more than willing to help you out with it if you ask or email him.  Going to him for any needed help is key.
Worst Professor ever.
I took two of his classes this semster.He is helpful in some aspects, but he usually gives back our homework at the end of the semster.
He just copies everyting on his notes. He doesn't give feed back on time. I learned everything in this class by myself like other students in my statistics class do.

He is impatience to help students solve problem, sometimes he even get angry when students asked him for help.He just read everything on ppt in class.Also, he gives back our hw at the end of this semster, so we have no idea about our progess at all. He grades the homework basically depends on his self-interest, no fairness at all.

I had him for Discrete Event Simulation.  His lecture slides are very good and he tells you pretty much everything you need to know for the hmwk.  He is very helpful in Office Hours. I found his English to be quite good compared to most professors at RPI, and I did not have trouble understanding him.  I would recommend him, at least in this class.
simple,naive
Actually, the professor needs to improve his teaching skills and oral English. At the same time, the grading policy is unfair.

The professor spends most of the time in class just copying down his notes without any clarification. The lecture is by no means useful; I learn almost everything from reading the textbook by my own.Besides his oral English is poor.

The Statistics course is required for PhD students by the school. I think it's unfair to rate the professor with the school's problematic policy. (A side note: the first rating at the bottom was done on Feb 2, which was only few days after the first lecture.)
No Comments
he admittedly teaches this UNDERGRAD course as if it were PhD-level... cant speak english, he sucks in all aspects

Took him Fall 2024, not bad of a professor. Almost never uploads any of his written lectures. Never holds office hours, so you may have to barge him when you see him. His quizzes had “true” or “all of the above” as the answer. Also never showed up on the exams and almost everything is straightforward except 1 question that is impossible to solve.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is the best professor I have had at RPI. He is extremely helpful and will explain concepts in many different ways to ensure understanding. The tests are very easy if you do the homework yourself. His lectures are engaging and relevant. Great person to get to know!

Prof. Bequette teaches what you need to know for the industry. You get time to work on homework in class and some MATLAB code and Simulink files are provided to lessen the coding pain. Exams are fair. He tells stories about his experiences in process control and tries to make lectures relevant and short. Put in a moderate effort and you'll be fine.

He's a great lecturer, because he teaches you what you actually need to know for the working world instead of flooding your brain with tons of math and useless equations. HW tends to be much harder than exams.  He loves MATLAB too, so don't be surprised if he puts it on tests.
sucks
